title: Deciding in the shadow of the state: when regulatory logic collides with market logic
abstract: Purpose Capital allocation models treat planning inputs as market-governed, even when they originate from political authority. Written for The Practice of Making Decisions section of Management Decision, this paper develops a three-phase response: classify each input, stress test it against a change of authority and design commitments that can move if the answer changes. Design/methodology/approach The process is built from the tasks the decision involves, not from theory. A constructed vignette of a wine producer entering Mendoza runs through the argument; three documented situations (utility privatization, wine internationalization, EU digital regulation) serve as retrospective illustrations. Findings Standard tools presume a judgment they do not perform: which institutional logic governs each input; tagging inputs by source, durability and evidence confidence comes first. In Mendoza the commitment changes form, not direction: purchase becomes staged entry sized to survive the incentive's loss. Research limitations/implications Retrospective illustrations show compatibility with documented responses, not conscious use or performance effects. Practical implications Each phase specifies questions, participants, outputs and revisit triggers; a decision matrix and a pre-commitment checklist support its use. Originality/value The contribution is a managerial task rather than a the…

title: How do green market orientation, green innovation and leadership styles interact for green new venture creation among family-owned enterprises?
abstract: Purpose Drawing on stakeholder theory and leader-member exchange theory, the study examines how a firm's tactical green market orientation – the implementation of eco-friendly marketing tactics – influences green innovation and, in turn, results in successful green new venture creation under different leadership styles. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from family-owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) involved in green initiatives in Oman using snowball sampling and analyzed to test the proposed model using partial least squares structural equation modeling in Smart PLS version 4.1.1.8. Findings The findings revealed that tactical green market orientation positively influences green innovation, and green innovation positively influences green new venture creation. Green innovation significantly mediates the relationship between tactical green market orientation and green new venture creation. Finally, the study found a positive but insignificant moderating impact of leadership styles on the associations of tactical green market orientation, green innovation and green new venture creation. Originality/value The results highlight the crucial interplay among tactical green market orientation, green innovation and hybrid leadership styles in promoting sustainable new venture creation in the unique context of family-owned MSMEs. title: Enhancing Community Resilience Through Disaster-Safe Market Preparedness in Kelud Volcanic Hazard Zone
abstract: This community service program aimed to enhance disaster preparedness among market traders and stakeholders in the Kelud volcanic hazard zone through education, skills training, and evacuation simulations. The activity employed a participatory action research (PAR) approach, involving Wage Market vendors, market managers, the Blitar City Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD), and the Blitar City Disaster Risk Reduction Forum (FPRB) as technical partners. The program included planning, action, observation, and reflection to develop a sustainable Disaster-Safe Market model. Initial outreach sessions provided basic disaster education, self-evacuation procedures, and first aid using counseling and audio-visual presentations. Knowledge gains were measured through pre- and post-tests, while practical skills in evacuation and first aid were trained via demonstrations and hands-on exercises using Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and evaluated with an SOP skills checklist. A miniature Wage Disaster Preparedness Market was used for table-top simulations to visualize market structure, evacuation routes, and assembly points. The final stage involved a full-scale evacuation simulation, resulting in the establishment of a Wage Market Disaster Preparedness Team. Among 30 participants, knowledge scores increased from 54.3 to 88.7, 82% achieved skilled competency in SOP-based procedure…

title: Do Big4 accounting firms affect foreign individuals’ investment decisions? Evidence from an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This paper focuses on an emerging market and investigates whether a firm’s audit engagement with a Big4 accounting firm is associated with foreign individuals’ investments. We hypothesize that Big4 accounting firms’ reputation may function as a heuristic trust signal for these investors. Design/methodology/approach We tested our hypothesis by utilizing 225 non-financial firms listed on Borsa Istanbul. The dataset covers 2005 to 2023 and contains 3,590 firm-year observations. Findings Our empirical evidence indicates that foreign individuals are more likely to invest in BIST-listed firms audited by a Big4 accounting firm (AF). Our results are consistent with prior studies showing that accounting firms’ reputation is associated with investors’ decisions. Our robustness analysis suggests that Big4 AFs’ reputation may lose importance when public governance declines. Research limitations/implications The primary limitation of this research is that investor-level data are not publicly available. We also did not incorporate audit-firm-level variables such as expertise and number of partners. Practical implications Our study has implications for managers, policymakers and accounting professionals. Managers seeking to signal trust to foreign individuals may consider the positive association between Big4 AF engagement and foreign investment. Social implications Policymakers shoul…

title: FX market connectedness during the Israel–Iran 12-day confrontation: evidence from minute-level data
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how volatility was transmitted across global and regional currencies during the June 2025 Israel–Iran confrontation. Design/methodology/approach Using minute-level FX data covering 12–24 June 2025, we apply a TVP-VAR connectedness framework with APARCH-based volatility modelling to track how shocks moved across currency pairs in real time. Findings EUR/USD and GBP/USD generate large outward spillovers, while USD/CNY records the strongest positive full-horizon NET position. Regionally exposed currencies are predominantly net receivers, although transmitter and receiver positions change across short intraday horizons. EGP/USD, ILS/USD and SAR/USD mainly absorb shocks from dominant global pairs, while SAR/USD shows more limited volatility, consistent with its pegged exchange-rate regime. Connectedness also increases sharply on 18 June despite the absence of a single discrete major event in the study's chronology. We interpret this as heightened market repricing during evolving geopolitical uncertainty, while recognising that the connectedness measure does not identify the specific information responsible. Several currency pairs also switch between transmitter and receiver roles within 2–5-min intervals. Originality/value The study provides new evidence on how geopolitical stress is transmitted through the FX network at minute-level frequency. Its main c…

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS AND ASSESSMENT OF THE CURRENT STATE OF MARKET SEGMENTS IN AZERBAIJAN'S FOOD INDUSTRY
abstract: This article presents a comparative analysis and assessment of the current state of market segments in Azerbaijan's food industry. The study examines the level of development of the main product market segments, consumer demand, the competitive environment, pricing policies, and marketing activities within the food industry. It also evaluates the competitiveness of domestic products against imported goods, the key factors influencing consumer behavior, and the current positions of market participants. The findings of the comparative analysis indicate significant differences among market segments in terms of development, innovation adoption, and competitiveness. Based on the research results, the article offers practical recommendations aimed at improving the efficiency of market segmentation, strengthening the competitiveness of food industry enterprises, and supporting the sustainable development of Azerbaijan's food sector.

title: Climate conditions, financial uncertainty and market resilience in African equity markets: an event-driven probabilistic deep learning approach
abstract: Purpose This paper examines stock-market volatility in Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa and Tunisia under geopolitical and financial uncertainty and physical climate conditions. African evidence rarely integrates event-time shock analysis with full-distribution forecasting while distinguishing physical climate signals from climate-related financial risk. The study develops an event-driven probabilistic framework grounded in a Climate–Market Conditioning Framework (CMCF). Design/methodology/approach The study combines cumulative abnormal volatility (CAV) analysis with Mixture Density Network–Long Short-Term Memory (MDN-LSTM) volatility and return-density models. Daily market data from January 2015 to April 2025 are combined with Geopolitical Risk, Financial Stress Index and National Aeronautics and Space Administration Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources climate indicators. Forecasts use a strict chronological holdout and are compared with Generalised Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH)(1,1)-Normal, GARCH(1,1)-Student-t, Exponential GARCH (EGARCH), Glosten–Jagannathan–Runkle-GARCH (GJR-GARCH), Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting. Distributional performance is additionally benchmarked against probabilistic GARCH using the weighted interval score (WIS). Findings Shock responses are heterogeneous across markets. The four fixed global events provi…

title: Governance modes and their applicability boundaries in compensated rural homestead withdrawal: a control-rights comparison of organization-led and market-coordinated governance
abstract: Inroduction Rural land restructuring must reconcile asset reuse with household security and accountable governance. Methods This conceptual-comparative study examines compensated homestead withdrawal in China using documentary analysis, a narrative literature synthesis, and four structured cases. Results The analysis separates compensation instruments from governance structures and distinguishes administrative coordination from member-authorized collective autonomy. It specifies control-rights closure across decisions, subsequent use, benefits, accountability, and risk bearing, alongside qualification-right buffering through credible household safeguards. Verified source evidence shows that stated willingness, withdrawal scale, and compensation preferences cannot substitute for durable land-use and welfare outcomes. Case contrasts identify conditional coordination and protection requirements without establishing causal effects or performance rankings. Discussion International comparison connects these propositions to dispersed-rights coordination, livelihood reconstruction, and post-transfer accountability while preserving institutional differences.

title: Improving Posyandu Cadres’ Skills to Support Primary Care Integration
abstract: Posyandu is currently undergoing health-system transformation through the integration of primary care services targeting all stages of the human life cycle, with Posyandu cadres playing a key role in service delivery. Cadre regeneration remains necessary; however, some newly recruited Posyandu cadres have not previously received information or training on Posyandu management. This community service activity was conducted as a training program for newly recruited Posyandu cadres to improve their skills. The participants were 42 newly recruited Posyandu cadres from Kepanjen Kidul Subdistrict, Kepanjen Kidul District, Blitar City. The training was conducted over two days, 22–23 July 2026, by healthcare professionals from Kepanjen Kidul Community Health Center and community service team members from Poltekkes Kemenkes Malang. The classroom-based training included Posyandu management, simulation of effective communication using the SAJI model, and simulation of Posyandu services using the five-step procedure. The results indicated that the cadres had good perceptions and knowledge of Posyandu management and were able to simulate the five-step Posyandu service procedure. The training improved cadres’ knowledge, self-confidence, effective communication skills, and ability to provide Posyandu services. Therefore, training for Posyandu cadres should be conducted regularly.

title: Inside the service work ecosystem: a lived account of young workers
abstract: Purpose Existing service work ecosystem research primarily examines how systems are structured and managed, offering limited insight into how they are experienced by workers. This study addresses that gap by providing the first empirical, worker-centered account of how the service work ecosystem is lived, interpreted and navigated from within. Design/methodology/approach Five Lego® Serious Play® (LSP) workshops were conducted with 80 participants aged 18–26, all with frontline service experience and originating from Global South contexts (Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos). Visual, narrative and observational data were analyzed using an abductive, iterative approach, examining participants' interpretations and recurring visual patterns alongside transcripts, with Psychology of Working Theory (PWT) as a sensitizing lens. Findings Findings reveal a systemic pattern of constraint rather than opportunity. Work is experienced not as a pathway to mobility, but as a site where all three PWT needs (survival, social connection, self-determination) are persistently compromised through macro-level forces, organizational practices and relational dynamics. Pursuing self-determination carries a moral cost, conceptualized here as the guilt of aspiration. Navigating these conditions is itself invisible, uncompensated labor that depletes the very resources on which service quality depends. O…

title: Family-Based Tuberculosis Prevention Through Self-Management Education (SME) for Community Health Workers in Rural East Indonesia
abstract: Pulmonary Tuberculosis (TB) remains a significant public health concern in Indonesia, especially in East Nusa Tenggara Province. This community service program aimed to strengthen the knowledge and skills of community health workers (cadres) in delivering family-based TB prevention through a Self-Management Education (SME) approach. A pre–post descriptive design was implemented involving 35 active Integrated Service Post (ISP) health cadres in Manusak Village, Kupang Regency. The intervention included cadres training, developing and distributing educational materials (modules, posters, and leaflets), conducting structured home visits, and implementing monitoring tools. Cadres’ knowledge and skills were measured using a structured 15-item questionnaire and a skills observational checklist before and after the intervention. The results showed an increase in average knowledge scores from 57% before the intervention to 94% after the intervention. Cadres’ skills also improved markedly, with the proportion of cadres categorized as having good skills increasing from 6% at baseline to 94% after the intervention. This program demonstrates that SME is a feasible and effective approach to empowering community health cadres to deliver family-based TB prevention in rural settings. Each family affected by TB received four home visits over an eight-week period. Post-intervention observations …

title: Development and Validation of a Multidimensional Gen-AI Competence Scale for Pre-Service Science Teachers
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) into education is transforming the competencies required of future teachers and creating a need for a robust multidimensional measure of Gen-AI competency. This study developed and validated a six-dimensional framework comprising output evaluation, use appropriateness, prompting & operation, technical integration, model literacy, and responsible practice among pre-service science teachers. Data were obtained from 426 biology, chemistry, and physics education students at Universitas Jambi, Indonesia. The responses were randomly split into EFA (n = 256; 60%) and CFA (n = 170; 40%) subsamples. An initial 84-item pool was evaluated through ten experts’ judgment using CVR and CVI, resulting in 63 content-valid items. The data were suitable for factor analysis (KMO = 0.972; Bartlett’s χ² = 20430.533; df = 1,953; p < 0.001), and EFA retained 33 items across six dimensions, with factor loadings of 0.502–0.811 and Cronbach’s alpha of 0.765–0.909. CFA supported the six-dimensional structure with acceptable fit (RMSEA = 0.063, CFI = 0.913, TLI = 0.904, SRMR = 0.052). The dimensions demonstrated satisfactory reliability and convergent validity (α = 0.754–0.909; CR = 0.752–0.910; AVE = 0.505–0.611), while HTMT values of 0.586–0.874 supported discriminant validity. The resulting measure provides an empirically supported bas…

title: Human Resource Management Strategies for Improving Work Effectiveness and Service Quality: A Case Study
abstract: This study aims to analyze human resource management strategies in improving work effectiveness and service quality at Mubarak Tour & Travel. The study employed a qualitative approach using a case study method. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, direct observation, documentation, and literature review. Informants were selected purposively and included the director, employees, marketing staff, mutawwif, and pilgrims who had used the services of Mubarak Tour & Travel more than twice. Data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification using the interactive analysis model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings indicate that Mubarak Tour & Travel faces limitations in its human resource structure, resulting in overlapping responsibilities and increased workload dynamics, particularly during periods of high pilgrim numbers and departure schedules. These challenges are managed through the optimization of available human resources, flexible task allocation, coordination and collaboration among employees, and competency development through briefings, direct guidance, experience sharing, and work evaluation. These strategies contribute to improving productivity, timely task completion, and employees’ ability to adapt to changing workloads. title: Smart Pregnant Women Movement: Education on Danger Signs and High-Risk Pregnancy in Blabak Village, Kediri Regency
abstract: Limited knowledge of pregnancy danger signs and high-risk conditions may contribute to delays in recognizing complications and seeking appropriate healthcare. This community service program aimed to improve pregnant women’s knowledge of pregnancy danger signs and high-risk conditions through the “Smart Pregnant Women Movement.” The program was conducted on November 10, 2025, in Blabak Village, Kediri Regency, and involved 18 pregnant women in the first to third trimesters. The intervention consisted of interactive health education, discussions, and question-and-answer sessions supported by PowerPoint presentations and educational leaflets. Knowledge was assessed before and after the intervention using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Before the intervention, 6 participants (33%) had good knowledge and 12 (67%) had moderate knowledge. After the intervention, the proportion of participants with good knowledge increased to 16 (88%), while only 2 (12%) remained in the moderate category. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated a statistically significant difference between pre- and post-intervention knowledge scores (Z = −3.742; p < 0.001). The Smart Pregnant Women Movement was associated with improved knowledge of pregnancy danger signs and high-risk conditions and may serve as a practical community-based strategy to strengthen maternal h…

title: AI-mediated teacher learning in Chinese lesson study: regulating cognitive demands in EFL pre-service teachers
abstract: Purpose This study, guided by the cognitive theory of multimedia learning (CTML), investigates how multimodal large language models (MLLMs) mediate the professional learning of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) pre-service teachers within Chinese lesson study (CLS). It aims to elucidate the cognitive and dialogic mechanisms through which AI-supported mediation shapes teacher learning processes and participation. Design/methodology/approach A three-month intervention integrating MLLMs into CLS was conducted with 50 EFL pre-service teachers at a Chinese normal university. Adopting an interpretive qualitative design, data were collected from longitudinal reflective journals, MLLM interaction logs, field notes and two rounds of semi-structured interviews with 5 purposively selected focal participants. Data analysis combined deductive coding based on CTML (intrinsic, extraneous and germane cognitive load) with inductive thematic analysis to capture emergent patterns of AI-mediated learning and interaction. Findings The findings reveal that MLLMs functioned as cognitive-dialogic mediators in three key ways: (1) reducing linguistic and organizational barriers, thereby lowering extraneous cognitive load; (2) redistributing cognitive resources to support meaning-making and pedagogical reasoning; and (3) enabling deeper engagement in collaborative knowledge construction and reflective …

title: Counseling on Household-Scale Pharmaceutical Waste Disposal at Talise Public Health Center
abstract: Improper disposal of pharmaceutical waste can harm the environment and public health. Public knowledge regarding appropriate household-level drug disposal remains limited. This community engagement aimed to improve the knowledge, attitudes, and behavior of residents regarding the handling of expired and damaged medicines. The activity was conducted at Bumi Roviga Sub-Public Health Center, a unit under Talise Public Health Center, Palu City. A total of 24 respondents, selected randomly among parents attending child health checks or antenatal care, participated in the program. The counseling was delivered face-to-face and supplemented with printed educational flyers. A pre-test was administered at the location, while the post-test was distributed via WhatsApp using Google Forms one week later. Shapiro-Wilk normality tests indicated non-normal data distribution. Paired t-tests showed significant improvements (p<0.05) in knowledge (p=0.000), attitude (p=0.000), and behavior (p=0.000) scores, indicating the effectiveness of the intervention. This activity demonstrates that brief counseling supported by print media can effectively enhance public understanding of safe drug disposal at the household level. As a recommendation, household-level pharmaceutical waste education should be integrated into routine health promotion activities at community health centers, with periodic follow-up…

abstract: This study examines the development of Uzbekistan’s public service delivery system using secondary administrative data for 2017–2024. Descriptive statistical, comparative, and dynamic analyses were applied. From 2018 to 2024, the number of services offered through Public Service Centers (PSCs) increased from 63 to 403, while services available via the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (UPIPS) rose from 83 to 717. By 22 October 2024, automated services had increased from 10 to 186 and BPM-based services from 24 to 494. The findings show broader service coverage and greater automation; the article compares these trends by delivery channel and automation type

title: Universal design for learning in general chemistry: a pre-post study of inclusive teaching competence in pre-service teacher education
abstract: Abstract Inclusive STEM education places distinct demands on prospective chemistry teachers, owing to the discipline’s high cognitive load, the need to organize practice-oriented activities safely, and the requirement to ensure fair assessment in the context of diverse learners’ educational needs. The present study examined changes in inclusive chemistry teaching competence during a semester-long intervention grounded in Universal Design for Learning (UDL). A single-group pretest-posttest intervention design was implemented in the General Chemistry course (6 credits; 180 academic hours) at Zhanibekov University. The sample comprised 106 first-year university students. Over a 15-week semester, the UDL approach was embedded into the course through a sequence of design-based assignments targeting multiple means of engagement, representation, and action and expression. The course instructor served as the intervention implementer (teacher effect). Data collection included pre- and post-measures using self-report scales (knowledge, self-efficacy, attitudes, and intention to implement UDL), a case-based knowledge test, and the evaluation of student-generated pedagogical artifacts at two time points (T1 and T2) using a study-specific eight-criterion UDL design rubric (0–3 per criterion; total score 0–24). Data were analyzed using paired pre-post comparisons, effect size estimation, and…

title: Esco2 restrains pathological endothelial-mesenchymal transition through hidden isoform regulation in a Roberts syndrome model
abstract: Roberts syndrome is caused by biallelic ESCO2 pathogenic variants, but the mechanisms linking ESCO2 loss to embryonic endothelial failure remain poorly defined. Endothelial cells must maintain identity and resist endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), yet conventional transcriptomics measures gene abundance rather than isoform composition. Here, using endothelial-specific Esco2 deletion in a mouse model relevant to Roberts syndrome, we show that Esco2 loss causes yolk sac vascular remodeling failure, pathological EndMT, diversion from hemogenic endothelial fate, hemogenic endothelial depletion, impaired hematopoietic output, and embryonic lethality. Short-read single-cell RNA-seq revealed broad endothelial reprogramming, whereas single-cell long-read isoform sequencing uncovered a hidden layer of isoform dysregulation that conventional gene-level analysis failed to resolve. Esco2-deficient endothelium exhibited transcriptome-wide isoform switching, disruption of a multi-tier splicing-factor network, and predicted broad loss or rewiring of protein-coding output. Chromatin occupancy profiling localized Esco2 to exonic regions near alternatively spliced loci, supporting a cotranscriptional route to spliceopathy. Enhanced output voltage regulation in a seven-level inverter with minimal active power switches for renewable energy applications
abstract: Smart inverters are a prevalent solution in renewable energy applications due to their capacity to provide output voltage with minimal harmonic distortion and ease of control and operation. This trend has driven the rapid growth of power converters in various renewable energy applications. This research aims to design a strategy and implementation technique for a single-phase seven-level (SPSL) inverter that can control output voltage accurately. This research is innovative because it constructs an SPSL inverter with six active power switches and a new control strategy. This inverter comprises two active power switches that operate as a three-level direct current (DC) voltage shaper and four active power switches for polarity inversion. This inverter is controlled using advanced sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) methods. The inverter SPSL was selected because it can produce smoother sine waves with a total harmonic distortion (THD) less than the IEEE standard. The SPSL inverter's power circuit is controlled by a microcontroller-based control system, which enables the inverter to dynamically adapt to changes in load and operating conditions. This study performed simulations and verified the design performance via hardware implementation. abstract: Метою статті є дослідження механізму імплементації міжнародних стандартів у сфері регулювання віртуальних активів, з’ясування його адміністративно-правової природи, характерних ознак та особливостей функціонування в умовах технологічної динаміки цифрового фінансового середовища. Методи. Методологічну основу дослідження становлять загальнонаукові та спеціально-юридичні методи пізнання. Формально-юридичний метод застосовано для аналізу нормативного змісту стандартів FATF, рекомендацій FSB та Регламенту Європейського Союзу про ринки криптоактивів (MiCA), Закону України «Про віртуальні активи» та законопроєкту № 10225-д щодо врегулювання обороту віртуальних активів в Україні. Порівняльно-правовий метод використано для зіставлення доктринальних підходів до розуміння категорії «імплементація» у працях вітчизняних дослідників. За допомогою системно-структурного методу виокремлено й систематизовано визначальні ознаки механізму імплементації міжнародних стандартів у сфері віртуальних активів. Методи аналізу, синтезу та узагальнення застосовано для формулювання цілісної адміністративно-правової характеристики досліджуваного механізму та підсумкових висновків. Результати. title: Digital leapfrogging or digital divide? Internet penetration and structural transformation in Africa
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether digitalization accelerates structural transformation in African economies or reinforces existing structural inequalities. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data on African countries and a rigorous fixed-effects framework, complemented by dynamic System GMM estimation, the analysis provides a direct test of the digital structural transformation hypothesis. Findings The results show a strong and robust positive effect of internet penetration on structural transformation, even after controlling for key macroeconomic and demographic factors. Sectoral evidence reveals a clear mechanism: increased internet access reduces the share of agriculture while significantly expanding the services sector, confirming that digitalization actively reallocates economic activity across sectors. Crucially, interaction results show that the impact of internet penetration is stronger in slower-growing, less advanced economies, providing compelling evidence in favor of the digital leapfrogging hypothesis rather than the digital divide. Originality/value These findings establish digital infrastructure as a central driver of modern structural change and suggest that expanding internet access can serve as a powerful policy tool for accelerating inclusive development in Africa.

title: Regulations, infrastructure and financial efficiency: evidence from 101 economies
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether regulatory quality or information infrastructure better predicts financial system efficiency and investigate the pathway through which regulation translates into operational outcomes across 101 economies. Design/methodology/approach The World Bank B-READY 2025 data set is used to separately measure regulatory framework quality and public-service infrastructure as predictors of operational efficiency. OLS with HC3-robust standard errors is estimated across eight institutional variables and four income groups, with formal mediation analysis and robustness checks including region fixed effects and principal component digital infrastructure. Findings Payment interoperability rules and credit registry accessibility are the institutional variables most robustly associated with efficiency. Information infrastructure transmits approximately 29% of the total regulatory effect, consistent with partial mediation. A steep income gradient persists after controlling for all institutional variables. Decomposing efficiency reveals distinct channels: credit registry accessibility is associated with credit efficiency; payment interoperability rules are associated with payment efficiency. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design prevents causal identification. The sample is dominated by Europe and Central Asia, limiting generalisabili…

title: Decoupling growth from degradation: a fractional frequency Fourier analysis of India's aviation sector and the environmental Kuznets Curve
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India's aviation sector from 1970 to 2021. Using the ecological footprint as an indicator and a novel fractional frequency Fourier approach, it tests the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. The results reveal a U-shaped relationship, contradicting the EKC, and highlight the negative environmental impact of increased air freight. However, financial development supports sustainability by enabling cleaner technologies. The study aims to inform policy by proposing strategies such as carbon pricing, renewable fuel adoption, and green logistics to decouple aviation growth from environmental harm. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a fractional frequency Fourier approach to examine the long-run relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India from 1970 to 2021. The ecological footprint is used as a comprehensive measure of environmental impact. This advanced econometric method captures structural breaks and nonlinearities more effectively than traditional models. By testing the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis within this framework, the study provides nuanced insights into the dynamic interactions among the variables. The methodology e…

Factors associated with severe COVID-19 among children aged <12 years in Fuzhou, China: a frequency-matched case-control study
abstract: Background Evidence on social, preventive, and clinical factors associated with severe pediatric COVID-19 remains limited in regional Chinese surveillance settings. We evaluated these factors among children aged <12 years in Fuzhou. Methods We conducted a frequency-matched case-control study of 347 severe cases and 694 non-severe controls identified from sentinel hospitals and the China Disease Prevention and Control Information System between January 2020 and August 2025. Controls were sampled at a 1:2 ratio by broad onset period, geographic sampling stratum, and parental education level. Group differences were assessed using Pearson&apos;s chi-square test. Given frequency matching without individual matched sets, unconditional multivariable logistic regression was used. Concurrent clinical manifestations were interpreted as warning indicators rather than antecedent etiologic risk factors. Results The selected sample comprised 1,041 children (347 severe cases and 694 non-severe controls). Severe disease was positively associated with male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.897, 95% CI 1.451-2.481), age <=5 years (aOR 1.578, 95% CI 1.209-2.061), home-based/preschool care (aOR 2.771, 95% CI 2.033-3.776), rural residence (aOR 2.470, 95% CI 1.858-3.283), delayed consultation of &gt;2 days (aOR 1.902, 95% CI 1.388-2.605), obesity (aOR 2.028, 95% CI 1.398-2.941), chronic…

title: Розвиток емоційної саморегуляції майбутніх викладачів вокалу як засіб подолання сценічного хвилювання
abstract: Дослідження присвячене теоретичному обґрунтуванню ролі емоційної саморегуляції у фаховій підготовці майбутніх викладачів вокалу та висвітлення методів подолання сценічного хвилювання. Було використано комплекс теоретичних методів дослідження: аналіз науково-методичної літератури, синтез, порівняння отриманих даних, індукція, дедукція. Конкретизовано сутність понять: «регуляція», «саморегуляція», «емоційна саморегуляція», «хвилювання», «сценічне хвилювання». Подано авторське визначення науковій дефініції «емоційна саморегуляція майбутніх артистів-вокалістів». На думку авторів, емоційна саморегуляція майбутніх викладачів – це інтегративна професійно значуща якість, що виявляється у здатності усвідомлено керувати власними емоційними переживаннями, контролювати рівень сценічного хвилювання, мобілізувати внутрішні психічні ресурси та підтримувати оптимальний емоційний стан для успішної вокально-виконавської діяльності й художньої інтерпретації музичного твору. Теоретично обґрунтовано роль емоційної саморегуляції у фаховій підготовці майбутніх викладачів вокалу у закладах вищої освіти мистецького спрямування. title: Process optimization of spray-dried buffalo milk Bubalus bubalis bubalis (Linnaeus, 1758) using response surface methodology
abstract: Buffalo milk has higher fat and solids-not-fat contents, consisting mainly of proteins, carbohydrates, and minerals, making it more nutritious than cow’s milk. However, its composition also makes the product more perishable. Thus, preservation techniques like spray drying must be employed to extend its shelf life and facilitate efficient transportation and distribution. Spray-drying conditions for cow's milk have already been established. However, because of differences in physicochemical properties and composition, these conditions may not be applicable to buffalo milk. Therefore, optimizing the processing conditions for buffalo milk is necessary. This study aimed to optimize the spray-drying conditions for buffalo milk to produce an acceptable milk powder. Response surface methodology was used to evaluate the effects of three key variables: maltodextrin (10-20%w/w), feed pressure (8-12Hz), and inlet temperature (190-210°C). The goal was to determine their effects on the response variables, including moisture content, water activity, hygroscopic moisture, and insolubility index. The optimal spray-drying conditions were obtained at a maltodextrin concentration of 20% (w/w), a feed pressure of 12 Hz, and an inlet temperature of 210°C. The Calculus of Quick Commerce: Demand, Pricing, Elasticity and Profit Optimization in India
abstract: The fast-paced evolution of digital retail requires the enhanced application of quantitative analysis of decisions related to pricing, demand forecasting, inventory control and fulfillment. In this paper, there is a mathematical treatment of the modern business model of quick commerce and how the tools of calculus and business mathematics can be employed in order to analyze the decisions related to it. For this purpose, a linear inverse demand function is constructed that sets the connection between price and quantity. Using this connection, a quadratic function of revenue is developed and then marginal revenue is found out via differentiation. Further, a nonlinear cost function that reflects the fixed operating cost, variable costs and increasing marginal cost is constructed. Using the profit function, its first derivative is found in order to find out the stationary level of output and the second derivative helps in defining the characteristics of this point. Moreover, price elasticity is computed in order to measure the degree of sensitivity of demand to the price change. The numerical values are fictional and are used for the purpose of demonstrating the process of mathematical analysis. The study is contextualized within the context of digital commerce within India, which entails the emergence of quick commerce and an open digital commerce infrastructure like ONDC. Calculu…

title: Integrative bioinformatics and drug response profiling identify MEK/ERK inhibition as a strategy to overcome venetoclax resistance in AML
abstract: Background Drug resistance remains a key barrier to durable remission in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). A central but poorly resolved question is whether AML cells resistant to mechanistically distinct drugs converge on shared downstream survival dependencies, and whether those dependencies can be exploited therapeutically. Methods We compared transcriptional reprogramming across 3 independent resistance models derived from the FLT3-ITD-positive MV4-11 cell line: midostaurin-resistant cells, sorafenib-resistant cells, and a novel venetoclax-resistant line generated in our laboratory. Differential expression analysis, protein -protein interaction network analysis, hub-gene prioritization across multiple network centrality algorithms, and pathway enrichment analyses were performed on shared upregulated genes. Functional validation was performed using the MEK inhibitor selumetinib, and drug combination effects with the mTOR inhibitor PP242 were quantified using the Chou-Talalay combination index method. Results Despite the distinct mechanisms through which each drug exerts its effect, differential expression analysis identified 328 upregulated genes shared across at least 2 resistance conditions, with a meaningful subset common to all 3. Ketone monoester supplementation during a live high – train low training camp does not yield an additional adaptive response
abstract: Recent evidence indicates that oral ketone monoester (KE) intake acutely increases blood [EPO] following exercise in normoxia and improves endurance performance following an exercise training program. Therefore, we investigated whether post-exercise and pre-sleep KE supplementation may improve performance and hematological adaptations to an altitude training program. Eighteen recreational cyclists (9 male, 9 female) performed a five-week, live-high, train-low (LHTL) program, involving progressive normobaric hypoxia (2000-3000m) and 4–7 training sessions per week, followed by a one-week tapering period under normoxic conditions. Throughout the six-week period, subjects received either 25g KE (n=9) or an isocaloric placebo (CON; n=9) both post-exercise and pre-sleep for a total daily dose of 50g. Experimental measurements were performed before (PRE) and after (POST) LHTL, and after the subsequent taper (POST + 7), and included a 30-minute time trial (TT30), maximal oxygen uptake rate (VO 2 max) test, determination of gross mechanical efficiency, repeated sprint performance, measurements of hemoglobin mass, blood draws and muscle biopsies. In both groups, mean power output during TT30 improved by 9% (p<0.001) alongside increases in VO 2 max (+8%, p=0.001) and absolute hemoglobin mass (+8.77%, p<0.001) from PRE to POST + 7. A weight loss fibrotic response in visceral fat is driven by defective lysosome-dependent collagenolysis
abstract: Obesity induces pathological remodeling of white adipose tissue (WAT), including chronic inflammation and fibrosis, which drive metabolic dysfunction. Although weight loss (WL) is the cornerstone of obesity treatment and improves systemic metabolic health, its effect on WAT remodeling remains incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of diet-induced obesity followed by nutritional WL, we show that visceral WAT (vWAT) failed to fully recover despite normalization of body weight and marked metabolic improvement. Notably, vWAT fibrosis persisted and continued to progress after WL. This occurred while extracellular matrix (ECM) production by adipose progenitor cells was markedly reduced following WL, explaining why pharmacological inhibition of ECM synthesis fails to prevent fibrosis during WL. Instead, we observed impaired collagen degradation by both progenitor cells and macrophages, along with lysosomal dysfunction, during WL. This suggests that defective ECM degradation, rather than continued ECM production, underlies fibrosis persistence and aggravation during WL. Together, these findings identify impaired collagenolysis as a critical barrier to adipose tissue recovery after WL and suggest that enhancing ECM clearance, rather than inhibiting ECM synthesis, may represent a more effective therapeutic strategy to restore adipose tissue function.

title: Aerobic exercise for depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms and perceived stress in university students: a systematic review and dose–response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Abstract Objective To assess the effects of aerobic exercise on depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms and perceived stress in university students and to identify potential exercise prescription and dose–response patterns. Methods PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, PsycINFO and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception to August 15, 2026. Eligible studies were English language, peer reviewed RCTs in university students (≥ 18 years) comparing aerobic exercise with a control condition. Random effects meta-analyses used standardized mean differences (SMDs) based on change scores. Subgroup analyses examined baseline depression, intensity, session duration and intervention length. Dose–response associations (METs·min/week) were modelled using restricted cubic splines. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, and publication bias was explored using funnel plots and Egger test. The review was retrospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261473381). Results Fourteen RCTs ( n = 982) were included. Aerobic exercise reduced depressive symptoms (13 RCTs; n = 717; SMD = − 0.88, 95% CI − 1.35 to − 0.41), anxiety symptoms (10 RCTs; n = 579; SMD = − 0.59, 95% CI − 0.92 to − 0.26) and perceived stress (7 RCTs; n = 353; SMD = − 0.68, 95% CI − 1.20 to − 0.16). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested variations in pooled estimates across exercise characteristics. For depression, sessions < 60 mi…

Assessing demand-side policy impacts on US urban passenger transport
abstract: Abstract Demand-side policies could significantly mitigate energy use and carbon emissions of urban passenger transport. However, previous integrated assessment modeling studies often failed to fully evaluate their mitigation potential in the absence of explicit representation of urban transport dynamics. Here we adjust the global integrated assessment model GCAM to disaggregate passenger transport in the US region into the urban and inter-city subsectors. We analyze the impacts of transformative demand-side policies on US urban passenger transport service demand, mode share, energy use, and carbon emissions. We consider six demand-side policies (compact urban development , speed limit, shared mobility, remote working, fuel tax, and congestion fee) as well as a technology policy of vehicle electrification. We find that all demand-side policies could collectively reduce urban transport energy use and carbon emissions by approximately 60% from the baseline in 2050 by shifting and reducing transport demand. We also find that demand-side policies could deliver strong synergies with electric vehicle (EV) deployment. Under ambitious EV deployment, although most direct urban passenger transport emissions are mitigated, electricity demand would increase by 718 TWh from 2021 to 2050, as much as 16% of current US total electricity consumption. title: Beyond the basics: how digital transformation, orientation and competence fuel SME performance through resilience in the manufacturing sector
abstract: Purpose In emerging economies such as Pakistan, SMEs have a high failure rate, underscoring the need to understand what drives SME performance. This paper fills a knowledge gap by considering the impact of digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and entrepreneurial resilience on SMEs' performance. Entrepreneurial resilience serves as a mediator between digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, environmental dynamism (ED) is used as a moderator between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 453 managers of manufacturing SMEs in Punjab, Pakistan. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling is used for hypothesis testing. Findings Digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation and entrepreneurial competencies have a significant and positive influence on entrepreneurial resilience and SME performance. Entrepreneurial resilience significantly enhances SMEs' performance. Additionally, entrepreneurial resilience significantly mediates the relationships among digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, ED significantly moderates the relationship between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Practical implications SME manag…

title: GenAI dependence and team innovation in construction projects: moderated mediation analysis of knowledge integration, team reflexivity and learning goal orientation
abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly embedded in construction project work, yet its implications for project team innovation remain insufficiently understood. Moving beyond a simple adoption or use perspective, this study examines how perceived team-referent GenAI dependence is associated with team innovation in construction projects. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on information processing theory, this study develops a moderated mediation model linking GenAI dependence, knowledge integration, team reflexivity, learning goal orientation and team innovation. Based on survey data from 257 construction project professionals in China, the model was tested using structural equation modeling, supplemented by hierarchical regression and bootstrapped analysis. Findings Based on survey data from the Chinese construction industry, the results show that GenAI dependence is positively associated with knowledge integration and negatively associated with team reflexivity. These two team processes account for opposing indirect associations between GenAI dependence and team innovation. Team learning goal orientation further attenuates the negative association involving team reflexivity, along with the corresponding negative indirect association with team innovation. Originality/value By examining perceived team-referent GenAI dependence as an information-proc…

abstract: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perspectives on institutional governance challenges affecting the implementation of Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) in Indonesia under Presidential Regulation Number 38 of 2015. It further identifies stakeholder-informed policy reform needs to strengthen the national PPP framework. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using semi-structured interviews with nine high-level purposively selected participants representing government institutions, private sector entities, and financial institutions involved in PPP implementation. Data were analyzed through thematic synthesis involving open coding, category development, and interpretive theme construction. Findings The findings identify four institutional governance dimensions influencing PPP implementation: regulatory adaptability and institutional continuity, project preparation quality, financial structuring and risk allocation, and lifecycle governance. Across stakeholder groups, participants consistently highlighted policy inconsistency, limited feasibility study credibility, rigid contractual arrangements, disproportionate risk allocation, and insufficient operational oversight as priority governance concerns. Optimization of a Laccase Biosynthesis and Mediator System: A Potential Headway for Sustainable Microplastic Degradation
abstract: Abstract The global accumulation of microplastics has become a critical environmental challenge due to their persistence, widespread distribution, and adverse effects on ecosystems and human health. Although enzymatic degradation has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional physicochemical remediation methods, the practical application of laccase (Lac) remains constrained by low enzyme productivity, limited stability, high production costs, and insufficient activity towards recalcitrant non-phenolic polymers such as polyethylene and polystyrene. Furthermore, current studies are often fragmented, focusing on either enzyme production or degradation performance, while lacking an integrated assessment of catalytic optimization, mediator systems, scalability, and environmental sustainability. This review provides a critical and comprehensive evaluation of recent advances in optimizing Lac biosynthesis and laccase-mediator systems (LMS) for microplastic degradation. Unlike previous reviews, it integrates developments in strain engineering, heterologous expression, protein engineering, omics-guided process optimization, enzyme immobilization, mediator selection, and techno-economic considerations within a single framework. Particular attention is given to how LMS expands the oxidative capacity of Lac towards resistant plastic polymers and to the evidence required to distin…

title: Primary care staff and health policymakers’ perspectives on the Israeli special team management program for complex patients and its further enhancement: a qualitative study
abstract: Abstract Background/aim The healthcare of complex patients is challenging, requiring holistic multidisciplinary teamwork. The targeted Team Management for Complex Patients Program (TMCP) was therefore initiated in Israel and implemented by Leumit Health Services. The aim of the current study was to examine the perceptions and insights of healthcare stakeholders regarding the program implementation and its further enhancement. Methods A descriptive qualitative study using semi-structured remote videoconference interviews was conducted. A purposive sampling of primary care practitioners, managers and policymakers, with operational experience in the TMCP, was employed. Interviewees were categorized into three levels: field staff and service providers, mid-level management staff and high-level policymakers. Results Five main themes were examined amongst the 22 interviewees: detection of complex patients for inclusion in the TMCP; quality and access to healthcare; team function, governance and accountability; and provider experience. These themes were extracted from the three levels of interviewees, all of whom endorsed a broad definition of complexity that integrates clinical, functional, mental and social dimensions and emphasized the critical role of multidisciplinary teamwork in complex patient care. title: Conservation of heat in the Coupled Arctic Prediction System (CAPS v1.1): comprehensive model evaluation based on the MOSAiC observations
abstract: Atmosphere–sea ice–ocean interactions are vital for understanding past and future changes in the Arctic climate system. Consistent heat-flux exchange across model-component interfaces is essential for investigating these interactions with coupled models on longer timescales. Here, we present the improved version of the Coupled Arctic Prediction System (CAPS), in which heat-flux exchange between the atmosphere (WRF) and ocean–sea ice (ROMS–CICE) components is made consistent across coupling interfaces. A set of pan-Arctic simulations covering the period of Multidisciplinary drifting Observatory for the Study of Arctic Climate (MOSAiC) were conducted with the revised CAPS. The revised coupling substantially reduces interfacial heat-flux residuals and improves the simulation of Arctic sea-ice conditions relative to the original coupling, which produces enhanced winter ice growth and reduced summer ice retreat during the 14-month simulation. CAPS was further evaluated against comprehensive MOSAiC observations of the atmosphere, ocean, snow, and sea ice. The model reproduces the broad evolution of Arctic conditions along the MOSAiC drift, although biases remain, partly associated with errors in simulated synoptic systems and unresolved polar physical processes. Austrian pine site indices as a basis for adaptive forest management in southwestern Serbia
abstract: Introduction The site index is the most commonly used indirect indicator of forest site productivity, based on the height-age relationship. The objectives of this study were: (1) to develop a dynamic site index model and (2) to create a site index map for Austrian pine (Pinus nigra) in southwestern Serbia using the Generalized Algebraic Difference Approach (GADA). Materials and methods The modeling was based on data obtained from stem analysis of 56 dominant trees (990 age-height pairs) and was validated using an independent set of 2,835 age-height pairs. In the initial stage, eight nonlinear models were tested, while the subsequent analysis employed the GADA approach to four selected models. Parameter estimation was performed using the Generalized Nonlinear Least Squares (GNLS) method with corrections for autocorrelation (ARMA (2,1)) and heteroscedasticity. The final model selection was based on a combination of statistical and biological criteria. Results The results showed that the Chapman-Richards, Hossfeld IV and Weibull models achieved a high goodness of fit ( R 2 adj ≈ 0.98), while the Gompertz model proved to be less suitable. However, only the Hossfeld IV model within the GADA approach fully satisfied the biological and theoretical assumptions, providing realistic asymptotic values and a biologically logical pattern of height growth. title: Less effort, less meaning? Authorship ambiguity and impostor-like experiences in GenAI-mediated knowledge work
abstract: Purpose This study examines how knowledge workers make sense of GenAI-enabled co-production, with particular attention to authorship ambiguity and its implications for competence attribution, self-evaluation and meaningful work. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative approach based on in-depth interviews with 32 knowledge workers who work directly with GenAI tools, combining inductive coding with abductive interpretation. We used the Gioia methodology to analyze participants' reported experiences and interpretations of human–AI collaboration, with sensemaking informing the interpretation of emergent themes and aggregate dimensions. Findings The findings identify authorship ambiguity as a central interpretive challenge in GenAI-mediated knowledge work. When GenAI contributes to ideation, analysis, drafting, coding or other knowledge-intensive outputs, workers may find it difficult to distinguish their own contribution from that of the technology. Participants responded to this ambiguity differently. Some reconstructed their expertise around judgment, validation and contextualization and experienced GenAI as extending their professional capability. Others struggled to internalize successful outputs as evidence of their own competence and reported impostor-like experiences and reduced meaningfulness. title: Legal Culture and Pandemic Management: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: Abstract This article compares the COVID-19 responses of four selected jurisdictions through the lens of legal culture. Legal culture is defined in this article as the interplay of legislation, the infrastructure and behaviour of legal institutions, and the behaviour and legal consciousness of the general population. The four jurisdictions are New Zealand, Taiwan, Germany and mainland China; they bear cross-cutting similarities and differences in terms of legal system, political system and cultural tradition. This article examines how legal culture was revealed in COVID responses and how it in turn shaped COVID responses. It illustrates the legal culture of the four jurisdictions as revealed through their respective pandemic responses. It argues that the three dimensions of legal culture interacted with each other to produce distinct pandemic responses; in other words, pandemic management is to some extent the product of legal culture.

title: Experts' and AI perspectives on the environmental sustainability of tensile membrane structures
abstract: Purpose With increasing demands for sustainable construction, there is growing interest in enhancing the environmental performance of tensile membrane structures (TMS). This study aims to investigate the environmental sustainability challenges and opportunities of TMS across their lifecycle stages by integrating expert insights and advanced AI-generated perspectives. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative methodology was employed using semi-structured interviews with 16 experienced professionals including architects, engineers, contractors, builders, environmental sustainability experts and researchers. To enhance the reliability of findings and address potential gaps, the study also utilised artificial intelligence (AI) tools (ChatGPT and DeepSeek) to compare human expert insights with AI responses. Thematic analysis was conducted to categorise the results into core environmental sustainability themes. Findings Five interrelated themes were identified: (1) material innovation and environmental sustainability, (2) structural efficiency and lightweight design, (3) construction techniques and environmental sustainability alignment, (4) life durability management and (5) accessibility, inclusivity and waste management. title: Integrating ecohydrological modelling and participatory processes to co-design multifunctional forest management
abstract: Mediterranean forests are becoming denser, drier, and more combustible because of natural and human-driven factors. Forest managers report that managing them is increasingly costly relative to its economic returns and requires informed decision-making supported by appropriate tools and dialogue. This study couples the Decision Support System (DSS) CAFE (Carbon, Aqua, Fire and Eco-resilience) with structured participatory processes across four Living Labs in Spain, Morocco, and Italy, representing distinct Mediterranean socioecological systems: semiarid Aleppo pine forests, traditional argan woodlands with goat grazing, and cork-oak silvopastoral systems. The aim was to evaluate whether management co-designed in this way is resilient to climate disturbance while improving ecosystem services (ES). In three rounds of co-design workshops, stakeholders identified priority ES, agreed on the management actions to enhance them, and evaluated alternatives generated by the DSS. Their priorities were remarkably consistent across sites, focusing on wildfire risk, water availability, and biomass extraction. Preferred interventions were ecologically sound and consistent with field evidence. To this end, CAFE was expanded to quantify locally relevant ES that had not previously been modelled, including argan fruit production, cork extraction, fodder availability, and bark regeneration. title: C-suite incentive conflict and firm efficiency
abstract: Purpose This article provides empirical support to a long-debated theory in behavioral and organizational management literature regarding how the incentive conflict of firms' executives affects the firm's efficiency. Design/methodology/approach The study employs panel regression techniques, using efficiency measures derived from data envelopment analysis (DEA) and stochastic frontier analysis (SFA) as dependent variables, and a novel measure of C-suite incentive conflict as the independent variable, based on annual data from US companies covering the period 1992–2018. Findings Our results show that incentive conflict improves firm efficiency and thus support the constructive impact of C-suite conflict on firm efficiency. We find that the positive impact of incentive conflict on firm efficiency is weakened when the CEO is more powerful. Our findings provide support to agency theory by documenting that a more diverse board of directors reinforces the positive relationship between incentive conflict and firm efficiency. Research limitations/implications One limitation of this study is that the dataset is restricted to the period ending in 2018, which may limit the ability to capture more recent developments in corporate governance practices and executive incentive structures. Although the findings provide important insights for corporate executives and policymakers, extending the …

title: Do financial analysts improve the quality of earnings forecasting? Evidence from Central Europe, 2014–2024
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether consensus analyst forecasts for annual earnings per share (EPS) are more accurate than a standard random walk (RW) model for companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, the Prague Stock Exchange, the Budapest Stock Exchange and the Bucharest Stock Exchange during 2014–2024. Design/methodology/approach Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS from EquityRT are compared against RW model predictions using mean arctangent absolute percentage error, mean absolute error and mean square error. Wilcoxon and permutation tests assess statistical significance. For the Warsaw Stock Exchange, which provides the largest sample, the analysis is further stratified by analyst coverage intensity, firm capitalization, industry classification, corporate governance structure, institutional ownership composition and dividend orientation. Robustness checks employ alternative error metrics across multiple dimensions. Findings Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS demonstrate no statistically significant differentiation from RW predictions for Poland (excluding 2020), the Czech Republic (excluding 2020 and 2022), Hungary (excluding 2020) and Romania (excluding 2019 and 2022). This finding holds with respect to ownership structures and dividend policies. In the Polish market, for which detailed multi-dimensional analysis is provided, the absence of analyst a…

Artificial neural network-assisted prediction of Ti3C2-GO hybrid nanofluid flow over a curved surface
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the hemodynamics characteristics of nanofluid and hybrid nanofluid over a curved surface. The analysis focuses on momentum and energy transport in the presence of nanoparticles and compares the numerical results with artificial neural network (ANN) results. Design/methodology/approach A Casson blood-based nanofluid (nf) and hybrid nanofluid (hnf) flow model over a curved region is considered. The nf consists of 4% MXene (Ti3C2) nanoparticles dispersed in blood, while the hnf contains 4% MXene (Ti3C2) and 4% graphene oxide (GO) nanoparticles dispersed in blood. The flow is influenced by magnetic forces and Darcy–Forchheimer porous effects, whereas the energy field is affected by radiant heat, ohmic heating and uneven heat-source/sink conditions. The mathematical model is solved numerically by the MATLAB bvp5c problem solver. In addition, an ANN model accomplished with the Levenberg–Marquardt backpropagation procedure is used. The random data split is 70% for training, 15% for validation and 15% for testing to predict the heat transfer rate, and the predictions are validated against numerical results. Findings Results show that hnf significantly improves the heat transfer rate compared with nf taken in this study. Also, the relative change in the magnitude of skin friction is approximately 10%–12% for nf and 22%–25% for hnf when compared wit…

title: CurvEdgeNet: edge feature integration with Ricci curvature for circRNA-disease association prediction
abstract: Introduction Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are important regulatory non-coding RNAs involved in diverse pathological processes and have emerged as promising candidates for disease biomarker discovery. Systematic identification of circRNA–disease associations can help elucidate disease mechanisms and prioritize candidates for biological validation. However, existing computational approaches often rely on conventional similarity networks or node-centered feature learning, which may inadequately capture the non-Euclidean geometry and edge-level interactions of biological networks. Methods We propose CurvEdgeNet, a geometry-enhanced computational framework for predicting circRNA–disease associations. CurvEdgeNet constructs a heterogeneous circRNA–disease network by integrating multiple circRNA and disease similarity measures with known associations. A discrete Ollivier–Ricci curvature-based edge descriptor is incorporated into a curvature-enhanced graph attention mechanism to characterize local network geometry. In parallel, a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) module captures global feature dependencies, while multi-head attention integrates complementary local geometric and global representations for association prediction. Results CurvEdgeNet was evaluated on three public benchmark datasets: CircR2Disease V2, CircRNADisease V2, and CircFunBase. Under five-fold cross-valida…

title: Interpretable linguistic features for multi-trait prediction of english essay scores, and what they do not license a feedback tool to claim
abstract: Automated writing assessment is increasingly proposed for language-learning tools, but the feedback offered is often loosely connected to what the underlying model supports. This study examines multi-trait prediction of English essay scores from interpretable linguistic features, and asks what a feedback tool built on that model may legitimately claim. Working with the released 3,911-essay training partition of the ELLIPSE Corpus of English-language-learner writing, whose six corpus-provided score variables (cohesion, syntax, vocabulary, phraseology, grammar, conventions) are scored 1.0–5.0, we computed 77 linguistic features and evaluated models with nested cross-validation (5 folds × 3 repeats), compared using the Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t -test with Holm–Bonferroni adjustment. Because fold dependence leaves an effective 3.16 independent folds, effect sizes are mean differences with corrected intervals, fold win rates and essay-level probabilities of superiority rather than standardised d z . Ridge regression over these features achieved a mean columnwise RMSE of 0.5271, a 19.3% reduction against a constant-mean baseline, with no detectable difference from TF-IDF representations. Four further findings emerged. First, dimension-specific modelling outperformed a holistic model, but against a base-rate-ranked constant strategy neither single- nor two-variable identific…

title: Reservoir-Scale Heterogeneity in CO2 Geological Storage: A Review of Characterization, Mechanisms, Prediction, and Management with Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract The large-scale deployment of CO2 geological storage imposes stringent requirements on injectivity, subsurface space utilization, and long-term safety, making reservoir-scale heterogeneity a critical constraint on engineering feasibility and storage reliability. However, existing studies have primarily focused on individual heterogeneity elements, localized storage processes, or specific spatial scales, while systematic understanding of the coupling among multiple structural types, cross-scale transfer, and their impacts throughout the storage lifecycle remains limited. Therefore, this study synthesizes experimental, modeling, field, and ML studies, distinguishing their evidence sources and validation limits, to summarize the origins, types, characterization methods, and quantitative indicators of heterogeneity and to compare approaches for geological modeling, probabilistic prediction, and engineering regulation. The reviewed literature indicates the influence of geological architecture and connectivity on preferential migration and plume distribution. Quantitative effects on pressure, capacity, and trapping remain dependent on site conditions and model assumptions. Based on the identified limitations, recommendations are proposed in eight areas: evaluation standards, multisource data integration, structural fidelity, scale correction, probabilistic prediction, dynami…

title: 3D convolutional Dimension Preserved decomposition model integrated with Fourier Transform for traffic data prediction
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to overcome the limitations of traditional deep learning architectures in processing missing and noisy spatio-temporal streaming data. It aims to develop a robust spatio-temporal forecasting framework that can directly utilize incomplete inputs to achieve accurate predictions, thereby preventing catastrophic performance degradation and gradient collapse. Design/methodology/approach An innovative framework, termed FTI3DCDP, is proposed for traffic forecasting with incomplete data without requiring prior imputation. It establishes a dual-domain learning mechanism, where Fourier Transform extracts robust periodic patterns from incomplete signals in the frequency domain, while Dimension Preserved (DP) Decomposition captures low-rank spatial structures. A 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) adaptively integrates these complementary features for end-to-end spatio-temporal forecasting. Extensive experiments on five real-world traffic datasets under varying missing rates demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of FTI3DCDP across diverse traffic scenarios. Findings The results demonstrate that the proposed approach not only maintains forecasting stability under high sparsity but also consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baseline methods. This offers a highly resilient and deployable tool for supporting edge-intelligence solutions in…

title: Hydraulic conductivity and prediction models for clays in Tailan River Irrigation District
abstract: This study examines the permeability mechanism of cohesive soils using the Tailan River Irrigation District in Xinjiang as a case. Laboratory hydraulic conductivity tests and scanning electron microscopy were conducted to analyse the effect of dry density on hydraulic conductivity from both macro and micro perspectives, leading to improved hydraulic conductivity calculations. The results show that: Hydraulic conductivity decreases with increasing dry density, and the strongest correlation is found between porosity and hydraulic conductivity. Four commonly used empirical hydraulic conductivity formulas are modified by incorporating the concept of effective porosity ratio. The modified Kozeny–Carman formula performs the best with an average relative error of 28.16%, which is significantly lower than that of the other modified formulas. Further validation with independent test data from arid cold irrigation districts shows that the error of the modified formula is stably below 35%, indicating sound cross-regional applicability. It can provide reference for the calculation of clayey soil hydraulic conductivity in similar groundwater level regulation projects in arid cold irrigation districts.

title: Effects of egg source and extraction method on physicochemical properties, volatile profiles, and in vitro antioxidant capacity of egg yolk oil
abstract: Egg yolk is rich in lipids, phospholipids and other fat-soluble compounds, which are generally considered to contribute to its nutritional and technological value and have supported its use in flavor bases and functional-food formulations. However, the quality and flavor development of egg yolk oil (EYO) depend on egg source and preparation method. Here, egg yolk oils from conventional chicken eggs and Taihe Black-Bone Silk Fowl eggs were prepared by traditional thermal extraction or ethanol extraction. Physical properties, volatile compounds, and in vitro antioxidant activities were compared to define their flavor characteristics. Both egg source and extraction method influenced oil quality, although extraction method exerted the greater effect on the overall odor profile. Ethanol extraction increased extract yield and reduced viscosity. Thermal extraction produced stronger browning, and aldehydes and furans were the most numerous classes in its volatile profile. In total, 33 volatile compounds were putatively identified across the samples. Ethanol-extracted oils contained relatively higher levels of esters, ketones and pyrazines. Electronic-nose analysis further distinguished the odor fingerprints associated with the two extraction methods. Ethanol extraction of Taihe Black-Bone Silk Fowl egg yolk produced a relatively high extract yield, strong in vitro free-radical-scavengi…

title: Temporal changes in self-reported noncommunicable disease prevention, surveillance, and management capacity among primary care nurses in Binga District, Zimbabwe: A pilot repeated-measures implementation evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims: This pilot implementation study described temporal changes in self-reported noncommunicable disease (NCD) prevention, surveillance, and management capacity among primary care nurses in Binga District, Zimbabwe. Materials and Methods: A prospective repeated-measures implementation evaluation followed eight matched primary care nurses. Baseline data were collected from January 23 to January 24, 2026 after ethics committee approval, followed by midline and endline assessments. Program records listed 36 primary care nurses in the initial concept note and a final target of 40 nurses; exact invitation and refusal counts were unavailable. Study-specific domain scores and an equally weighted self-reported NCD capacity index were expressed on 0–100 scales. Friedman tests with Kendall’s W were exploratory and Holm-adjusted. Results: Five participants were female (62.5%), and the mean age was 40.6 years. The study-specific self-reported NCD capacity index changed from 81.9 at baseline to 89.6 at endline (+7.7). Facility and community readiness changed by +19.8 points, surveillance knowledge by +11.7, prevention knowledge by +8.3, essential medicine availability by +9.4, and nutrition counseling by +5.6; guideline availability changed by −30.0. No comparison remained statistically significant after Holm adjustment. Conclusion: The findings provide pilot descri…

title: Teacher charisma as a mechanism for transforming performance anxiety into creative energy: a case study in vocal education
abstract: Purpose This study explores the potential role of teacher charisma in transforming performance anxiety into constructive creative energy, and identifies strategies of charismatic pedagogical facilitation in vocal and performative arts education. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative pedagogical case-study design, combining conceptual analysis with in-depth, longitudinal observation of two contrasting cases in the vocal classroom of a Ukrainian university specialising in performative arts, over one academic year. The theoretical framework integrates humanistic pedagogy, charismatic leadership theory and the psychology of performance anxiety. Findings Two case-based patterns of performance anxiety were identified – physiological-panic and cognitive-perfectionism – each associated with a different facilitation strategy. In both cases, the teacher's charismatic presence appeared to be one salient factor, alongside other concurrent influences, in the students' movement from anxiety towards greater performance freedom. A preliminary four-mechanism model of this process is proposed as a hypothesis for further, independent empirical verification, rather than as an established finding. Originality/value This study contributes to a still limited body of work by offering an illustrative, case-based account of charismatic pedagogical facilitation as one plausible mecha…
