title: Explainable machine learning for predicting kidney disease progression defined by changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate in type 2 diabetes: a single-centre retrospective study
abstract: Background and objectives Routine clinical data may contain information on the future course of kidney disease in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study assessed the predictive performance and interpretability of seven machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to baseline measurements. Materials and methods This single-centre retrospective study included 382 patients with T2DM evaluated between January 2024 and December 2025. Progression was ascertained at a fixed three-month reassessment and defined according to KDIGO criteria as a decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) category with a fall of at least 25% from baseline or an increase in albuminuria category. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression selected 22 of 52 candidate predictors before repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation, and a sensitivity analysis repeated the selection within training folds. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) were used to interpret the models. Results Progression occurred in 162 patients (42.4%). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.682 for the radial-basis support vector machine (SVM) and 0.671 for LASSO logistic regression; when feature selection was repeated within training folds, the AUCs were 0.603 and 0.640, respectively. Lower reward-based reinforcement learning underlying explore-exploit decision making in non-kleptomanic theft recidivists
abstract: Introduction Larceny imposes profound societal and economic burdens; however, punitive judicial measures frequently fail to deter recidivism. The neurobehavioral mechanisms driving habitual offending, whether instrumental or kleptomanic, in theft recidivists remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, we investigated explore-exploit decision-making and underlying reinforcement learning architectures in theft recidivists with a four-arm bandit task while prefrontal cortex (PFC) hemodynamics were continuously monitored using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Results Model-free behavioral analyses revealed that non-kleptomanic theft recidivists (NTR) accumulated significantly higher cumulative regret and made fewer optimal choices compared to control individuals without criminal records (CT), whereas results for the kleptomanic theft recidivists (KTR) remained inconclusive. Model-based analyses through Variational Bayesian Analysis identified Q-learning with decay model as the optimal computational fit. Parameter extraction using the model demonstrated that the NTR group exhibited a lower learning rate than CT and KTR groups, indicating a learning deficit in updating action values following environmental feedback. fNIRS tracking of trial-by-trial latent reinforcement variables revealed that while PFC activity was modulated by these variables, group differences we…

title: ПОНЯТТЯ ПРАВОВОЇ НЕВИЗНАЧЕНОСТІ: ХАРАКТЕРНІ РИСИ ТА МІСЦЕ У ПОНЯТІЙНОМУ АПАРАТІ ТЕОРІЇ ПРАВА
abstract: Мета. Здійснити комплексний теоретико-правовий аналіз поняття правової невизначеності та розкрити його зміст у понятійному апараті загальної теорії права. Методологічну основу дослідження становлять діалектичний метод, структурний і системний підходи, методи аналізу та синтезу, порівняльно-правовий, формально-юридичний та логіко-юридичний методи. Їх застосування дало змогу проаналізувати наукові підходи до розуміння правової невизначеності, виокремити її характерні риси, дослідити співвідношення з правовою визначеністю та сформулювати авторське визначення. Результати. Обґрунтовано доцільність використання терміна «правова невизначеність» у межах загальнотеоретичного дослідження. Встановлено її характерні риси: об’єктивну зумовленість, багаторівневий характер, біполярність, динамічність та контекстну обумовленість. З’ясовано, що правова визначеність і правова невизначеність взаємопов’язані у процесі функціонування права, а певний рівень невизначеності може бути сумісним із вимогами правової визначеності. Запропоновано визначати правову невизначеність як об’єктивно зумовлену характеристику правової реальності, що виявляється у відсутності достатніх підстав для однозначного встановлення змісту правового припису, вибору єдиного правомірного варіанта рішення або достатньо точного передбачення правових наслідків. Висновки. Правова невизначеність не обмежується недоліками нормативного…

title: Uncertainty analysis of sphere parameter estimation from NMM-1 point cloud measurements
abstract: Abstract The reliable estimation of sphere parameters is important for precision metrology, calibration, and uncertainty evaluation. This study investigates the effects of the number of measurement points and the sampled region on the uncertainty of sphere parameter fitting using the least-squares (LS) method. Contact surface topography data of a high-precision bearing ball were acquired on the NMM-1 platform using two scanning strategies. Repeated subsampling was applied to evaluate the uncertainty of the fitted parameters under different sampling conditions. The results show that the fitting uncertainty depends not only on the number of measurement points, but also on the geometric coverage of the sampled region. Although increasing the number of points generally improves fitting stability, the gain becomes progressively smaller beyond a certain range. This study therefore provides an experimental basis for the design and selection of sampling strategies for reliable sphere parameter estimation under non-ideal measurement conditions.

title: A Tensorized Systematic Short-Time Fourier Transform Optimization Framework with Lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
Numerical Solution of Optimal Feedback Control for Finite Horizon Optimal Control Problem with Growth Condition
abstract: In this paper, we study approximation of optimal feedback control for the finite horizon optimal control problem with growth conditions for control systems and cost functionals. The optimal control problems with growth conditions are usually applied in practice. In reducing the boundedness for the dynamics function to the growth conditions, we have some difficulty in proving the convergence of the approximation scheme by the Euler scheme. First, we prove comparison principle of unbounded viscosity solution under the growth condition for the dynamics function and prove that the value function is the unique viscosity solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. We then construct a new approximation scheme using Euler implicit scheme for the finite horizon optimal control problem and prove that the approximation value function converges to the viscosity solution of the HJB equation as the discretization step goes to zero. Based on the approximations of the viscosity solution, we construct the optimal feedback controls for the corresponding discrete control systems. We consider an example to show the efficiency of the time-space approximation algorithm by the Euler implicit scheme through computational results.

title: I–V characteristics and optimization of the electronic performance of a GaAs/AlGaAs resonant tunneling diode under the combined influence of geometric parameters and hydrostatic pressure
Optimization of oil production rates under geomechanical stress constraints: a coupled reservoir–geomechanics approach using cascaded artificial neural network surrogates
abstract: Abstract Geomechanical constraints can limit oil production from deep carbonate reservoirs, because depletion raises the effective stress and, with it, the risk of compaction and rock failure. Enforcing such a limit inside a production optimizer is costly, since every candidate rate schedule produces its own pore-pressure field and one coupled reservoir–geomechanical simulation takes about 3 h. This study develops a cascaded artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate to maximize oil production from the MB21 unit of the Mishrif Formation, Buzurgan Oil Field, while keeping the effective mean stress below 11,200 psi. A Pressure ANN predicts the pore-pressure field from the well rates and geomechanical inputs, and a Stress ANN converts the predicted field into effective mean stress. Unlike single-network stress surrogates, which need pore pressure as a known input, the cascade evaluates the stress constraint for the depletion that each proposed rate schedule would itself cause. The networks were trained on 2,446 high-fidelity CMG-GEM coupled simulations and coupled with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to allocate the rates of 18 producers. On independent test scenarios, the Pressure and Stress ANNs reached coefficients of determination of 0.95 and 0.94. PSO produced 42,799.02 bbl/day against 42,592.96 bbl/day for GA (+ 206.06 bbl/day, 0.48%) and reache…

title: Smart Kitchen Counter Innovation for Elderly Users Based on Quality Function Deployment and Internet of Things System
abstract: This study aims to design and develop a kitchen counter product for elderly users by applying the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) technique to address user requirements. The study began with a survey of elderly users’ needs, including design, facilities, usability, product quality, and materials. The collected data was analyzed using the QFD product planning matrix and the design deployment matrix to translate customer requirements into technical design specifications. The results indicated that the participants reported a mean perceived satisfaction score of 4.42 out of 5.00 after observing a demonstration of the prototype and its functions in an actual kitchen environment. The five product attributes with the highest satisfaction scores were lighting within overhead cabinet storage compartments, operational safety, ease of maintenance, structural strength, and electrical outlet safety systems, with mean scores of 4.62, 4.57, 4.56, 4.54, and 4.53, respectively. These findings demonstrate that Quality Function Deployment (QFD) is an effective approach for translating user requirements into product design, particularly in the development of kitchen counter products for elderly users. The resulting design was perceived as having the potential to improve safety and convenience for elderly users during kitchen activities. However, further hands-on usability and long-term field te…

title: MULTI-ACTOR SUPPORT SYSTEM SHAPING UNIVERSITY STUDENT ENTREPRENEURSHIP – A CASE STUDY AT HANOI OPEN UNIVERSITY
abstract: This study investigates how the Multi-Actor Support System (MASS) affects university students’ entrepreneurial skills, motivation, intention, and actions. Using survey data from 2,271 students and a PLS-SEM model, the results show that business and mentor support primarily enhances entrepreneurial self-efficacy. In contrast, support from universities, media, and financial resources tends to boost entrepreneurial motivation. The strong connection between motivation, intention, and behavior shows that motivation is crucial for translating support resources into entrepreneurial activity. The research broadens the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) framework by adding insights from human capital and the university entrepreneurial ecosystem. It also highlights the need for coordinated stakeholder efforts to improve the effectiveness of student entrepreneurship support in Vietnam.

title: FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION IN THE PROCESS OF CONVERGENCE OF THE LEGAL SYSTEM OF UKRAINE WITH THE EU ACQUIS: EUROPEAN STANDARDS, ECTHR PRACTICE AND CHALLENGES OF THE DIGITAL AGE
abstract: Purpose. The purpose of the study is to provide a comprehensive analysis of European standards for protecting freedom of expression in the context of the convergence of Ukraine’s legal system with the European Union acquis. The study also examines the case law of the European Court of Human Rights concerning the exercise of the right to freedom of expression in the digital environment and identifies the main challenges and prospects for improving Ukrainian legislation in the context of digital transformation and European integration. To achieve this purpose, the study pursues the following objectives: to analyse contemporary approaches adopted by the European Court of Human Rights to the interpretation of Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights and to systematise its case law concerning freedom of expression in the digital environment; and to identify the specific features of the convergence of Ukraine’s legal system with the EU acquis in the field of freedom of expression and the implementation of European standards. Methods. The methodological basis of the study is a comprehensive interdisciplinary approach to freedom of expression as a fundamental human right undergoing transformation under the influence of the digitalisation of social relations and Ukraine’s European legal integration. The research draws on human rights theory, constitutional law, European Uni…

title: Effectiveness of Integrated Neuromuscular Inhibition Technique Compared with Local Vibration Therapy on Iliotibial Band Tightness as an Adjunct in the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis
abstract: Abstract Background: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative disorder of synovial joints, leading to knee pain, stiffness, reduced mobility, and impaired quality of life. Iliotibial band (ITB) tightness and associated myofascial pain may further aggravate symptoms in individuals with knee OA. Conventional physiotherapy commonly includes stretching and strengthening exercises. Local vibration therapy (LVT) facilitates muscle relaxation, enhances circulation, and reduces soft-tissue tension through the tonic vibration reflex. Integrated neuromuscular inhibition technique (INIT), which combines ischemic compression, positional release, and muscle energy techniques, has been shown to deactivate trigger points and reduce muscle tightness. However, limited evidence exists comparing the effectiveness of LVT and INIT for managing ITB tightness in individuals with knee OA. Objectives: To compare the effectiveness of INIT and LVT on ITB tightness in individuals with knee OA. Materials and Methods: Forty-six participants aged 50–70 years with knee OA and ITB tightness were recruited and were randomly assigned to the LVT (Group A) and INIT (Group B). Outcome measures included Ober’s test, the visual analog scale (VAS), the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC). Assessments were conducted before and after the interven…

title: A physically integrated GNN surrogate for microbially-mediated kinetic reactive transport: PHYGNET
abstract: Reactive transport modelling (RTM) is essential for subsurface environmental management but is fundamentally constrained by traditional geochemical solvers. These solvers incur prohibitive computational costs and frequently suffer from numerical instabilities such as convergence failures, particularly in microbially-mediated kinetic reaction systems. While machine learning surrogates offer acceleration, they often lack physical consistency when dealing with stiff biogeochemical dynamics. Here we propose PHYGNET (Physically GNN Network), which maps microbial reaction networks into a directed graph by representing species and reactions as nodes and edges. It embeds Monod-type kinetics within a differentiable physics layer that enforces stoichiometric mass conservation and thermodynamic hierarchies, and incorporates a residual corrector that refines the final outputs at the cost of small deviations from exact mass balance. By successfully coupling with COMSOL, PHYGNET demonstrates the capability to execute full reactive transport simulations. Benchmark tests reveal that, in contrast to the severe super-linear time penalties faced by traditional solvers at engineering scales, PHYGNET maintains stable sub-linear scaling via tensor parallelism. At a scale of 10 5 grid nodes, PHYGNET achieved an acceleration (up to 3588-fold) without numerical crashes. Furthermore, its escalating spee…

title: Harmonious and obsessive passion, cultural identity, and mental health in Chinese students of traditional versus Western music: a national multi-institutional comparison
abstract: Background University music students carry an elevated burden of depression, anxiety, and performance-related distress, yet the motivational processes separating adaptive from maladaptive engagement remain only partly understood, and little is known about how they differ between the traditional Chinese and Western training tracks that coexist in Chinese tertiary music education. Drawing on the dualistic model of passion, we compared the two tracks on passion, cultural identity, and mental health, and tested identity as mediator of the track differences and as buffer of the obsessive passion-distress link. Methods A cross-sectional online survey recruited full-time music majors from 32 institutions across seven regions of China. After attention-check exclusions, 546 students remained (266 traditional, 280 Western; 59.3% women; M age = 20.63 years, SD = 1.33). Participants completed the Passion Scale, an adapted Multigroup Ethnic Identity Measure referencing Chinese cultural heritage, the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21, the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-being Scale, and a brief music performance anxiety scale. Group differences, moderated regression, and bootstrap mediation analyses were estimated. How Resilient Green Logistics drives Sustainable Environmental Outcomes: the multi-mediating role of governance, leadership and work ethos
abstract: Purpose This study looks at how Resilient Green Logistics (RGL) affects Sustainable Environmental Outcomes (SEO) in the Indian dairy sector. It focuses on the roles of Sustainability-Driven Governance (SDG), Eco-Transformative Leadership (ETL) and Pro-Environmental Work Ethos (PWE) as mediators. The research also aims to show how governance, leadership and employee behavior collectively contribute to environmental sustainability in dairy supply chains. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey design was adopted, covering 189 registered dairy companies across Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab and New Delhi. Purposive sampling targeted key supply chain professionals, including senior managers, logistics/supply chain managers and sustainability/environment officers. Of 567 targeted respondents, 407 provided valid responses. The data were analyzed using SmartPLS-SEM 4.1 to examine the proposed relationships. Findings The analysis strongly indicated that RGL directly improves environmental outcomes through business and behavioral mechanisms in the dairy sector's supply chain. Furthermore, the mediating roles of SDG, PWE and ETL have been established, and these mediators strengthen the relationship between RGL and SEO. Among the above-defined mediators, SDG emerged as the strongest, followed by PWE and ETL. Practical implications Adopting and implementing sustainable logistics …

title: Mapping a Quarter-Century of Forensic Nursing Research: A Multi-Database Bibliometric and Science-Mapping Analysis (2000–2025)
abstract: Background Forensic nursing spans interpersonal violence, correctional and forensic mental health, and death investigation, yet its research base has been mapped only in fragments. Aims To map the indexed literature of forensic nursing published between 2000 and 2025, and to identify where its evidence base is thinnest. Methods Performance analysis and science mapping of 1,221 documents (2000–2025), retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science by a 30-term topic query within three defined journal sets, analyzed in bibliometrix. Results Output grew 7.66% annually; one journal carried 47.8% of documents. The United States led production (51.0% of resolvable corresponding addresses) but was the least internationally connected major producer (3.3%), against 9.2% overall. Interpersonal violence dominated the indexed vocabulary; trafficking, exploitation and forensic mental health were concentrated in recent years. Global and local citations identified different documents. Discussion The literature is concentrated in one journal and four countries. Whether its dominant topics define the specialty or reflect uneven research infrastructure cannot be settled bibliometrically; the distribution shows where capacity is thinnest.

Dynamic capabilities perspective on successful technology commercialization: a meta-analysis
abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms' dynamic capabilities shape firm performance in technology commercialization contexts, focusing on the interplay between higher-order dynamic capabilities (sensing, seizing, and reconfiguration) and lower-order dynamic capabilities (technological and marketing capabilities). Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 54 independent samples (N = 16,099), this meta-analysis develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework examining the direct and indirect effects of dynamic capabilities on firm performance, as well as the moderating role of country development. Findings The findings show that sensing and seizing indirectly influence firm performance through technological and marketing capabilities, whereas reconfiguration has both direct and indirect effects on firm performance. Furthermore, country development moderates the relationships between sensing and seizing and technological and marketing capabilities. Originality/value This study advances understanding of dynamic capabilities in technology commercialization by distinguishing the roles of higher- and lower-order capabilities in shaping firm performance. It demonstrates how higher-order dynamic capabilities contribute to performance through technological and marketing capabilities and identifies country development as a boundary condition for these relationships.

title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem and Female Entrepreneurial Growth: Thematic Analysis
abstract: This study evaluates the influence of the entrepreneurial ecosystem on female entrepreneurial growth. Female entrepreneurs face restricted access to finance, growth-oriented capital, venture capital, and business angel funding. These impede the ability of female entrepreneurs to scale up and innovate. The thematic analysis methodology involving the use of juried textual data, from scientific literature was applied to analyze the entrepreneurial ecosystem and female entrepreneurial growth. Findings were extracted using the qualitative analysis of both theoretical and empirical literature in line with the main objectives of this study. The research revealed that female entrepreneurial outcomes are not exclusively based on individual traits. Instead, female entrepreneurial growth reflects the nature of its entrepreneurial ecosystems as it relates to institutional logic and structure, governance, financial networks, dominant values, and social capital within entrepreneurial ecosystems. The entrepreneurial ecosystem is structured and operates in a manner that logically constrains female entrepreneurial growth opportunities. The study recommends that financial institutions within the entrepreneurial ecosystem should deliberately tailor themselves appropriately with the necessary financial tools to assist in the growth of female entrepreneurs. title: The Structure and Evolution of China’s Green Finance Policy Instruments
abstract: China’s green finance policy system consists of many separate measures, and most studies examine them one at a time. This paper describes the system as a whole. It asks which instruments the system contains and how their relative weight changed between the 2016 Guiding Opinions on Building a Green Financial System and 2025. The instruments are grouped into five categories: green credit, green bonds, green insurance, green funds and carbon finance. The description rests on three public sources: green loan statistics from the People’s Bank of China, green bond issuance data from the Climate Bonds Initiative, and the text of the policy documents. Green loans grew faster than total loans over the period, and their share of total loans rose from 6.7% at end-2020 to 16.2% at end-2025. Green bond issuance peaked in 2022 within the period covered and was about 18% lower in 2024 than in 2023. Both patterns need to be read with care, because the green loan statistics were redefined in 2025 and the bond figures come from report editions with different database cut-off dates. Read together with the policy documents, the evidence suggests that direct financial support has been joined by project standards, institutional assessment and risk management requirements. title: COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF THE FINANCIAL EFFICIENCY OF TOURISM INVESTMENTS IN AZERBAIJAN
abstract: The study assesses how fixed-capital investment in tourism-characteristic industries in Azerbaijan is transformed into value added and identifies mechanisms for improving the performance of tourism finance. Official annual data for 2014-2024 are analysed using dynamic and comparative methods, investment intensity, a conditional financial-efficiency ratio, a post-pandemic recovery index, compound annual growth, coefficients of variation, and current and one-year-lagged Pearson correlations. Value added increased 2.48 times to AZN 5,973.8 million, while the sector’s share of GDP reached 4.7 per cent. Investment flows were substantially more volatile than value added. For 2016-2024, the correlation between investment and value added was 0.67; with a one-year lag, it was 0.63, indicating that investment outcomes emerge over time. The scientific contribution is an integrated framework combining current financial flows, value added, volatility, time lags and recovery from external shocks. The study recommends performance-based financing, regional project portfolios, a digital investment registry, risk-adjusted financial instruments, public-private partnerships and systematic post-investment monitoring.

title: Contextualizing True Knowledge: Oral Transmission in Balinese Tembang and Hindustani Classical Vocal Traditions
abstract: In classical and traditional vocal music, oral tradition remains a vital epistemology where knowledge is transmitted through direct interaction between teacher and student rather than through written notation. Hindustani classical vocal and Balinese tembang represent this paradigm, where knowledge is understood and sustained through oral transmission within the guru-shishya, or teacher-disciple, relationship. This study aims to understand how oral transmission shapes the meaning of "true knowledge" within the vocal pedagogy of Hindustani classical and Balinese tembang traditions, and how this knowledge is inseparable from the context in which it is taught and practiced. This study uses a qualitative literature-based approach to explore how oral transmission influences teaching, memory, and understanding in Hindustani classical and Balinese tembang vocal traditions. In both traditions, musical knowledge is not simply transferred but developed gradually through imitation, attentive listening, and a trusting relationship between teacher and student. Hence, oral transmission does not merely transmit musical information; it cultivates embodied musical knowledge. This study suggests that sustaining oral vocal traditions requires attention not only to the songs themselves, but also to the relationships and contexts through which musical knowledge continues to be taught, understood, an…

title: From knowledge transmission to competency formation: pedagogical innovation in investigative studies education
abstract: Purpose Competency-oriented reform is a central priority in higher vocational education. This study examines the direct association between pedagogical leadership commitment (PLC) and staff-reported student competency formation (SCF), the mediating role of practice-oriented learning culture (POLC) and the moderating effect of PLC on the POLC–SCF relationship. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to teaching staff and programme leaders involved in the education of investigative studies at higher vocational institutions in China. A total of 312 valid responses were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with WarpPLS to test the proposed direct, mediating and moderating relationships. Findings PLC was positively associated with SCF and strongly associated with POLC. POLC was positively associated with SCF and partially mediated the relationship between PLC and SCF. In addition, PLC significantly moderated the relationship between POLC and SCF. The model showed moderate explanatory power for both POLC and SCF. Practical implications The findings suggest that higher vocational institutions should strengthen leadership support for practice-oriented pedagogy by aligning resource allocation, professional development and curriculum implementation w…

title: Equity Research and Fundamental Analysis of Reliance Industries Limited: Financial Performance, DCF Valuation and Portfolio Relevance for the ABSLI Maximizer ULIP Fund
abstract: The study evaluates Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) using fundamental equity-research techniques and examines the relevance of the company as a core blue-chip holding in the ABSLI Maximizer ULIP Fund. The research problem arises from the need to assess a diversified conglomerate whose businesses differ materially in growth drivers, capital intensity, risk and cash-flow characteristics. Four objectives were addressed: analysis of five-year financial performance and ratios; construction of an FCFF-based DCF valuation; assessment of RIL’s strategic portfolio relevance; and application of practical wealth-management workflows such as goal discovery, risk profiling and consultative product communication. The study uses a descriptive and analytical research design, a purposive single-company case-study approach, and secondary data from RIL financial statements, investor disclosures, regulatory sources and financial databases. Analysis covers FY2022–FY2026, with DCF projections through FY2031. Results show revenue CAGR of approximately 10.6%, PAT CAGR of about 9.0%, OCF CAGR of about 14.8%, improving ROE and ROCE, moderate leverage and strong cash generation. The base-case DCF estimates intrinsic value at about ₹1,080 per share versus an assumed market price of ₹1,275.90, implying approximately 15.3% downside. The study therefore concludes that RIL has strong fundamentals but requir…

Financial risk and health insurance utilization among older adults in an urban informal settlement in Pune, India: a prospective community-based study
abstract: Background Older adults living in urban informal settlements are vulnerable to financial hardship because of chronic morbidity, repeated healthcare visits, and financial dependence. Longitudinal evidence on healthcare expenditure and financial risk protection in this group remains limited. This study assessed health insurance utilization, out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE), catastrophic health expenditure (CHE), and associated factors among older adults in one urban informal settlement. Methods A community-based longitudinal study was conducted among 116 older adults aged ≥60 years residing in urban informal settlements under an Urban Health Training Center of a medical college in Western India. Participants were followed for 1 year (June 2024 to May 2025) with quarterly assessments. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, morbidity, healthcare utilization, health insurance utilization, and healthcare expenditure were collected using a pre-tested questionnaire and expenditure recording sheets. CHE was defined as OOPE exceeding 10% of household income. Associations were assessed using chi-square, Mann–Whitney U, Friedman and Cochran’s Q tests (pairwise comparisons were Holm-adjusted), modified Poisson regression, multiple classification analysis, and concentration indices. title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN RIGHT ATRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND PROGRESSION OF RIGHT HEART FAILURE IN PULMONARY HYPERTENSION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS AND PRIMARY STUDIES
abstract: Introduction: Survival in pulmonary hypertension (PH) is determined by the capacity of the right ventricle (RV) to adapt to a chronically increased afterload, and the right atrium (RA) is the chamber that buffers RV filling during this transition. Phasic RA function can now be quantified with speckle-tracking echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance feature tracking (CMR-FT), but individual cohorts are small and use heterogeneous metrics, units and endpoints. We aimed to quantify the association between RA dysfunction and progression of right heart failure in PH, to characterise RA dysfunction relative to healthy controls and to determinants of RV failure, and to evaluate whether RA function is modifiable by afterload-reducing therapy. Methods: This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov and Semantic Scholar were searched from January 2011 to 3 November 2026, complemented by citation searching. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), comparative studies, cohort studies and case series were eligible. Hazard ratios (HRs) were harmonised to a 1% absolute decrease in RA reservoir strain and pooled with DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models, with Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman (HKSJ) intervals and 95% prediction intervals. title: BUDGET PLANNING, ORGANIZATION SIZE AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF THE TOP 100 SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN KENYA
abstract: Budget planning is widely promoted as a foundation of sound financial management in small and medium enterprises (SMEs), yet the strength of its payoff may depend on the scale at which an enterprise operates. This study examined the effect of budget planning on the financial performance of the top 100 SMEs in Kenya and determined the moderating effect of organization size on this relationship. The study was anchored on Incremental Budgeting Theory and Activity-Based Costing Theory and adopted a descriptive research design. A census of the 100 SMEs on the Ministry of Trade 2021/2022 list was attempted, with the Chief Accounting Officer of each firm as the respondent. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale, and 83 questionnaires were returned (83.0% response rate). The instrument was reliable in a pilot study (Cronbach’s alpha: budget planning 0.810, organization size 0.731, financial performance 0.713). Data were analysed in SPSS using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and regression with an interaction term. Budget planning was moderately practised (mean = 2.81, SD = 1.054), with strong strategic alignment and budget reviews but weak forecasting accuracy, departmental participation and contingency planning (means below 2.00). title: Climate reporting in public sector organisations: identity construction and changes
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to explore climate change reporting by public sector organisations. In particular, the analysis draws attention to how public sector organisations represent themselves through climate reporting practice to construct and reproduce their identities over time. Design/methodology/approach A comprehensive content analysis of 164 annual and stand-alone sustainability reports produced by 15 public sector organisations listed on the Australian National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting register over an 11-year period from 2014 to 2024 was used for this study. The analysis is informed by Tregidga et al.'s (2014) identity framework of sustainable organisations. Findings The analysis reveals an unbalanced pattern of identity construction in public sector climate reporting, characterised by a strong focus on compliance-oriented reporting, followed by reporting on climate leadership and limited engagement with strategically “good” practices associated with legitimacy seeking. Despite evidence of more substantive climate reporting, disclosures continue to focus predominantly on metrics and statistics reflecting regulatory and policy expectations. The longitudinal analysis reinforces this identity structure, although their climate reporting has developed into a more complex communicative space through which public sector organisations simultaneously constr…

title: Right versus left donor hepatectomy in living donor liver transplantation
Impact of built environment in mountainous aging communities on spatiotemporal behavioural differentiation among older persons: a geospatial analysis
abstract: As demographic aging deepens, the conflict between efficiency of public space resource allocation in mountainous communities and the diverse needs of older persons becomes more prominent. Understanding the adaptability between space and behaviour is crucial for identifying the built environment characteristics associated with the older persons’ outdoor activities for targeted environmental interventions. This study focuses on 42 public spaces in Chongqing, a typical mountainous city in China. From the perspectives of spatial layout and design, it establishes a connection between the public space environment and the characteristics of the older persons’ outdoor activities. Spatial clustering is used to explore the spatiotemporal aggregation of the older persons’ activities, and multiple linear regression models are employed to quantify the associations between environmental factors and the older persons’ behaviours. The results aim to match spatial environments with the activity requirements of older persons, providing evidence for optimising age-friendly built environment upgrades.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Urban Design and Planning

title: TPACK Readiness, Innovative Learning Design, and Digital Entrepreneurship Skills among Indonesian Business Education Students
abstract: Background: Digital entrepreneurship skills are increasingly important for business graduates, but evidence remains limited on how technology-integrated pedagogy is associated with their development. Objective: This study examined the structural associations among TPACK readiness, Innovative Learning Design, and the latent construct Digital Entrepreneurship Skills, including whether Innovative Learning Design carried a significant indirect association. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling. Of 119 responses, two cases met the prespecified extreme-score rule and were excluded, producing an analytic sample of 117 students. Nineteen dimension-level indicators represented the three constructs. Results: The retained measurement model produced standardized loadings of 0.459-0.812 and composite reliability of 0.738-0.863. Model fit improved after two theoretically justified within-construct residual correlations but remained below conventional benchmarks: chi-square (114) = 308.66, p < 0.001; CFI = 0.808; TLI = 0.771; and RMSEA = 0.121. The three direct paths were significant: TPACK-Innovative Learning Design (beta = 0.861, p < 0.001), Innovative Learning Design-Digital Entrepreneurship Skills (beta = 0.451, p = 0.044), and TPACK-Digital Entrepreneurship Skills (beta = 0.464, p = 0.048). Visual Question and Answer Educational Game Design for Natural and Social Sciences Learning
abstract: Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) learning in elementary schools is still dominated by lectures, which makes it difficult for students to understand abstract concepts. This study aims to design an educational game based on Visual Question and Answer (VQA) as an IPAS learning medium for fourth-grade students at UPT SD Negeri Papungan 02 and to determine its feasibility. The study employed Research and Development (R&D) with the Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) model consisting of six stages: concept, design, material collecting, assembly, testing, and distribution. The game was built with the HTML5-based Construct 2 engine and integrated with an Express.js backend connected to the Google Gemini API to generate adaptive exam questions based on students' practice scores. Feasibility was measured through black box testing, media expert validation, material expert validation, and a student response questionnaire. The results show that all 22 black box scenarios were successful, and the feasibility percentages were 87% from the media experts, 100% from the material expert, and 91.43% from the student responses, all in the very feasible category. The VQA educational game is feasible as an IPAS learning medium. Future work should add more learning materials, audio narration, and an offline version.

Sol-gel based design of lead-free yttrium-doped barium titanate nanocomposites for advanced functional materials
abstract: Abstract Nano-structured pure BaTiO 3 (B-T) and BaTiO 3 doped with different concentrations of yttrium ranging from 1 to 10 mol.%, coded as [BYT-x (x = 0–10)], were prepared using a modified sol-gel process. The study utilized X-ray diffraction (XRD) to illustrate the tetragonal structure of the perovskite BaTiO 3 . The persistence of the tetragonal phase was further verified using a mathematical derivative-based investigation. High resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) were used to examine the morphology of the doped samples. The results indicated that the crystallite size estimated using XRD ranged from 23.36 to 37.84 nm. Two complementary precision impedance measuring instruments were used to properly assess the dielectric characteristics across a wide frequency range (42 Hz to 1 GHz), guaranteeing good measuring accuracy across various regimes. Dielectric characterization of the yttrium-doped BaTiO 3 over such an extended frequency range remains scarcely reported. The dielectric measurements were carried out using a 3532-50 LCR Hi-TESTER and a network impedance analyzer (KEYSIGHT-E4991B), respectively. The pure sample (BYT-0) exhibited a significant permittivity ( ~ 770) and a tangent loss ( ~ 0.076), whereas the doped sample (BYT-9) showed a reduced permittivity (ε′ ~ 95) along with a significantly lower…

title: In Search of Identity: Rethinking Balinese Product Design through Cultural History
abstract: Balinese product design is often recognized through visual signs such as ornament, material, craft technique, and references to tradition. Yet these signs do not fully explain how a design identity is formed or maintained. This paper revisits the history of Balinese product design through a cultural-historical perspective to examine identity as a process rather than a fixed style. Using literature, historical documents, manuscripts, colonial records, and visual documentation, the study traces recurring relations among local knowledge, patronage, external influence, tourism, and professional design practice. The findings suggest that Balinese design identity has developed through continuity and adaptation: new functions, materials, technologies, and markets have been incorporated without entirely displacing established systems of making and cultural reference. Balinese product design is therefore better understood as a historically negotiated design tradition than as a stable collection of visual attributes.

title: From Transit Space to Third Space: A Critical Regionalist Study of Bus Stop Design in Bali
abstract: Bali has experienced a significant increase in the use of public transportation in recent years. Public transportation systems require supporting infrastructure that functions as transit spaces for users transferring between modes of transportation. Bus stops are understood as transportation infrastructure that serves as temporary transit and waiting spaces. In Bali, bus stops exhibit diverse forms and design characteristics that extend beyond their primary function as transit infrastructure and have the potential to generate varied spatial experiences for users. This study aims to analyze the diversity of forms and design characteristics of bus stops in Bali and to identify their potential as third spaces through the perspective of Critical Regionalism. The study employs a qualitative approach using field observations, visual documentation, interviews with the Dinas Perhubungan Provinsi Bali and document analysis. The collected data are analyzed through three main stages: data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings are expected to demonstrate that the diversity of bus stop designs not only produces variations in architectural form but also contributes to different spatial experiences for users. Bus stops are therefore not merely regarded as transit facilities but also as public spaces capable of fostering aesthetic and social experien…

title: Cost reductions in total hip arthroplasty after DRG payment reform and volume-based procurement in China: a difference-in-differences study
abstract: Background: Between 2021 and 2022, China's health system reforms deployed two overlapping cost-containment instruments in quick succession: diagnosis-related group (DRG) bundled payment and a nationalized volume-based procurement (VBP) programme that cut orthopedic implant prices by 70%−90%. Disentangling their independent contributions to hospitalization costs is both methodologically challenging and policy-critical. We examined whether the January 2021 DRG roll-out in Wenzhou was associated with a differential change in total hip arthroplasty (THA) costs and adverse discharge outcomes across insurance groups, and whether the observed cost reductions are consistent with a larger contribution from either reform. Methods We analyzed 2,518 consecutive THA admissions at a tertiary hospital in Wenzhou (2015–2025). Patients were classified as Social Insurance (NRCMS, URBMI, and UEBMI; n = 2,046) or Other Payment (self-pay, full public-service, miscellaneous; n = 472). A difference-in-differences (DID) framework with year fixed effects and HC3-robust standard errors estimated the group-specific cost change associated with the reform. An event-study design assessed pre-reform parallel trends and traced the year-by-year trajectory of any post-reform divergence. Does environmental judicial reform influence audit fees? Evidence from China's environmental public interest litigation
abstract: Purpose A careful study of the impact of the environmental public interest litigation (EPIL) pilot policy on audit fees would not only make the economic costs of judicial innovation in environmental governance but also the study would make a strong empirical statement about improving the environmental practices of the business community and audit policies. Design/methodology/approach We are working with a quasi-natural experiment in China based on its EPIL pilot program and we apply a difference-in-differences framework. Findings We find that firms in pilot regions pay 4.7% higher audit fees than non-pilot peers, a result robust to parallel-trend checks, placebo tests, propensity score matching and controls for concurrent policies. Mechanism evidence indicates that the EPIL pilot policy elevates auditors' perceived litigation and regulatory risk, leading to higher risk premia in pricing without commensurate increases in engagement hours. Effects are stronger for firms with weaker ESG, greater information asymmetry, higher auditor specialization, lower auditor workload pressure, or strong regional environmental policy enforcement. Further analysis shows that the increase in audit fees associated with the EPIL pilot policy does not lead to an improvement in audit quality. abstract: В статье рассматривается влияние цифровой трансформации на финансово-кредитные механизмы предприятий сферы услуг Республики Узбекистан. Предприятия сферы услуг, как правило, располагают небольшим объемом материальных активов, пригодных для залога, поэтому традиционная модель кредитования под обеспечение для них малоэффективна. На основе данных Центрального банка Республики Узбекистан и базы Global Findex Всемирного банка за 2017–2025 гг. показано, что число учетных записей в системах дистанционного банковского обслуживания выросло примерно с 20 млн в начале 2022 г. до 79,3 млн к декабрю 2025 г., а доля взрослых, имеющих счет, увеличилась с 34% до 56%. При этом юридические лица и индивидуальные предприниматели составляют лишь около 2% пользователей. В исследовании предложены модель цифрового контура кредитования предприятий сферы услуг на основе электронных счетов-фактур, онлайн-ККТ и эквайринговых данных, а также направления совершенствования финансово-кредитных механизмов.

title: Predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer via artificial intelligence: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND For patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), achieving a pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) creates an opportunity for organ preservation through a “watch-and-wait” strategy, thereby avoiding radical surgery. Artificial intelligence (AI) models applied to medical imaging offer a non-invasive way to predict this response, yet the landscape of available predictive tools remains fragmented. Importantly, pCR is a histopathological endpoint that can only be confirmed after surgical resection, whereas clinical complete response is assessed clinically and used to guide watch-and-wait decisions. AIM To evaluate the diagnostic performance of image-based AI models in predicting pCR (ypT0N0) for patients with LARC following nCRT. METHODS We searched PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL up to May 17, 2026. Studies developing image-based AI or radiomics models predicting pCR were included. Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool, Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-AI, and Radiomics Quality Score were used to evaluate methodological quality, while Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation-Diagnostic Test Accuracy assessed certainty of evidence. A bivariate random-effects model was used to pool sensitivity and specificity, and a hierarchical summary receiver operati…

Managing Students' Physical and Spiritual Conditions Through Classroom Management in Islamic Education: a Study of Coastal Elementary Schools
abstract: This study explores the impact of both physical and spiritual classroom conditions, as well as the accessibility of educational resources, on students' motivation to learn within Islamic Religious Education (IRE) in a coastal elementary school environment located in Lamongan, East Java. Existing research extensively covers classroom management in urban and suburban areas. However, few studies investigate how the socio-cultural dynamics of coastal communities interact with classroom management. Specifically, more research is needed on how spiritual and physical classroom environments operate in rural coastal elementary schools. This study adopted a qualitative field research design. Data were collected through non-participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and document reviews. A total of twelve key informants participated, including the school principal, IRE educators, classroom teachers, and upper-grade students. The key innovation of this investigation is its cohesive framework that connects spatial and physical organization, play-based learning tools, and spiritual practices, specifically designed for the socio-cultural circumstances of coastal learners. The results reveal that a tidy, inviting, and thoughtfully arranged physical environment has a positive effect on students' concentration and emotional health. title: Experimental Evaluation of a Hold-State Fuzzy Supervisor for P&O–PSO MPPT in an ESP8266-Based Standalone Photovoltaic System
abstract: Rapid irradiance variation exposes a practical trade-off in photovoltaic maximum power point tracking (MPPT): perturb-and-observe (P&O) is inexpensive to execute but oscillates around the maximum power point, whereas particle swarm optimization (PSO) can recover the optimum after large operating changes but requires more computation. This paper develops a hold-state fuzzy supervisor that assigns duty-cycle calculation to either P&O or PSO according to the normalized power error and its change. Fuzzy logic is therefore used only for mode selection; it does not act as a third MPPT algorithm or directly generate the pulse-width-modulation duty cycle. When the operating point enters a prescribed convergence region, the controller retains the last accepted duty cycle until the measured error indicates a material change. The method was first evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink and then implemented on an ESP8266-based 50 W standalone PV prototype subjected to the same 25 s stepped-irradiance profile. Under the reported test conditions, the supervisor achieved a convergence time of 0.12 s, a settling time of 0.16 s, a tracking efficiency of 99.78%, a steady-state power ripple of 0.48%, and a peak overshoot of 0.82%. The corresponding values for P&O were 0.35 s, 0.42 s, 98.95%, 1.82%, and 2.60%, while PSO achieved 0.18 s, 0.24 s, 99.42%, 0.91%, and 1.35% respectively. The results indicate that…

title: Design and Development of an Information System to Improve Services at Posyandu Dharma Wanita Rawajaya, Palembang
abstract: Posyandu is a community-based maternal and child health service in Indonesia, yet most Posyandu still depend on paper record books that are prone to recording errors, while information on schedules and services reaches parents only through conventional channels. Existing Posyandu information systems are mostly single-platform and do not give parents a view of the data that cadres enter. This study designs and builds an integrated Posyandu Information System for Posyandu Dharma Wanita Rawajaya, Palembang, in which a PHP/MySQL website for cadres and the community and an Android application share one centralized MySQL database through HTTP endpoints that exchange JSON, so that a record or schedule saved by a cadre is available to parents on their next request without re-entry. The system was developed by custom programming after observation and interviews. It covers toddler, pregnant-mother, immunization, and activity management, online activity registration with a unique registration number and a printable proof, and a date-filtered reporting dashboard. Black Box Testing of 26 scenarios in 14 feature groups, run on a pilot dataset of 21 community members, 18 toddlers, 12 pregnant mothers, 33 immunization records, and 12 activities, produced a 100% pass rate (26/26). The results indicate that a shared-database, multi-client architecture is a feasible way to digitalize Posyandu ser…

title: Artificial intelligence in functional gastrointestinal disorders: From symptom recognition to personalised management
abstract: Functional gastrointestinal disorders, now termed disorders of gut-brain interaction, are heterogeneous conditions shaped by psychological, physiological, microbial, and environmental factors. Diagnosis and treatment remain difficult because symptoms overlap, trajectories fluctuate, and no single objective biomarker exists. This minireview synthesises human evidence for artificial intelligence (AI) in symptom classification, digital phenotyping, microbiome and multi-omics prediction, treatment-response estimation, wearable monitoring, and language-based care. Targeted PubMed searches were updated through September 20, 2026. Current studies show feasibility, but most use small, single-centre cohorts, retrospective designs, or internal validation; calibration and prospective impact evaluation are uncommon. The most plausible near-term role of AI is therefore clinical augmentation: Identifying longitudinal patterns, supporting shared decisions, and detecting changes that require reassessment while preserving human oversight and patient autonomy. Large language models may improve education and communication, but disorder-specific evaluations reveal imperfect diagnosis and treatment recommendations with marked overconfidence. Translation requires representative cohorts that include overlapping organic disease, explicit endpoints despite the absence of a diagnostic gold standard, ext…

title: Clinical Supervision in Teachers’ Professional Development: An Integrative Framework
abstract: Clinical supervision has increasingly been positioned as an approach to support teacher professional development; however, previous studies have examined its stages, implementation mechanisms, contextual conditions, and professional outcomes from relatively fragmented perspectives. This study aims to analyze the role of clinical supervision in teacher professional development and to synthesize the relationships among the supervision cycle, developmental mechanisms, implementation conditions, and professional outcomes. This study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with thematic-narrative synthesis following the PRISMA 2020 framework. Relevant literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026 was identified through Scopus, ERIC, Google Scholar, Garuda, and SINTA using keywords related to clinical supervision and teacher professional development. Selected studies were assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Tools and analyzed through thematic coding and cross-study comparison. The findings indicate four interconnected domains: clinical supervision cycle, developmental mechanisms, enabling and constraining conditions, and professional development outcomes. Coherent radio emission at 45 MHz from the nearby planet-hosting star GJ 725A
abstract: Ultralow-frequency (ν<100,MHz) coherent radio emission from exoplanet-hosting stellar systems carries information about planetary and stellar magnetic fields as well as the space weather environment -- information that is difficult to obtain at other wavelengths. We carried out the circularly polarized LOFAR LBA Sky Survey, the most sensitive circularly polarized survey in this frequency range, using the LOFAR low-band antenna system. As part of this untargeted search, we detected a signal in a 1,h observation that is coincident with the quiescent, planet-hosting, solar-neighborhood M,dwarf GJ,725A at a distance of 3.5,pc. The signal has a high circular polarization fraction of 74 =135 between 42,MHz and 50,MHz. It was undetected in the 50--66,MHz range, with a 3σ upper limit of and a peak brightness of B_ I,46 -1 I,58 <48, , corresponding to a drop of at least a factor of ∼3 across 12,MHz and indicating a strong spectral feature or cutoff around 50,MHz. Our detection represents the lowest-frequency confirmed detection of a stellar system. Based on its high estimated brightness temperature (∼10^ -1 14 ,K), transient character, and polarization fraction, the emission is most plausibly attributed to the electron cyclotron maser instability. The available observations are not sufficient to identify the astrophysical origin of the emission. We consider three plausible scenarios: au…

abstract: Kelompok Wanita Tani (KWT) Lebah Emas di Kalurahan Guwosari, Bantul, mengelola sekitar satu hektar lahan produktif, dua puluh petak budidaya, dan beberapa kolam lele. Pengembangannya menghadapi keterbatasan integrasi pengelolaan air dengan budidaya ikan, belum konsistennya perhitungan biaya produksi dan pengemasan, serta belum optimalnya promosi digital. Program pengabdian ini bertujuan memperkuat kapasitas teknis dan usaha melalui pendekatan terpadu yang menggabungkan perencanaan irigasi tetes, budidaya lele, diversifikasi produk, pengemasan, dan pemasaran digital. Pelaksanaan menggunakan metode partisipatif yang mencakup koordinasi dan pemetaan kebutuhan, pelatihan, pendampingan lapangan, pengembangan produk dan media promosi, serta pemantauan. Data diperoleh melalui observasi, diskusi kelompok, dokumentasi kegiatan, artefak produk, dan media digital, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Program menghasilkan pemetaan kolam, jaringan air, dan petak budidaya; pelatihan harga pokok produksi, pengemasan, pembuatan konten, dan promosi daring; penguatan identitas serta kemasan Lele Roy; aktivasi konten Instagram; serta inspeksi teknis kolam buis beton dan jaringan air. Hasil menunjukkan meningkatnya kesiapan mitra mengelola sistem produksi terpadu dan memasarkan produk, sementara pengukuran kuantitatif dampak masih memerlukan monitoring tahap akhir.

title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Low-Cost Autonomous Medical Rescue Robot for Hazardous and Conflict-Affected Environments
abstract: Emergency rescue operations in hazardous, unstable, and conflict-affected environments expose medical teams and first responders to serious risks, including structural collapse, fire, debris, toxic exposure, communication failure, and restricted access to victims. Robotic systems can reduce direct human exposure by performing early reconnaissance, detecting possible human presence, transmitting visual information, and supporting rescue planning. However, many advanced rescue robots are expensive, complex, and difficult to reproduce in low-resource settings. This paper presents the design, implementation, and experimental evaluation of a low-cost autonomous medical rescue robot developed for simulated hazardous-environment rescue support. The proposed prototype integrates an ESP32 microcontroller, HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor, PIR motion sensor, Neo-6M GPS module, ESP32-CAM video-streaming module, L298N motor driver, differential-drive DC motors, servo-actuated robotic arm, and rechargeable battery power system. A reactive autonomous control algorithm was implemented to enable low-speed autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance, human-motion detection, GPS coordinate reporting, live visual monitoring, and basic robotic-arm activation. Experimental testing showed that the robot achieved an average obstacle-response time of approximately 50 ms, distance-measurement accuracy of approx…

Impacto de la educación virtual en el aprendizaje del inglés en estudiantes de básica ecuatoriana [Impact of virtual education on English learning in Ecuadorian basic education students]
abstract: La educación virtual llegó a las escuelas ecuatorianas en marzo de 2020 sin equipos suficientes ni docentes preparados, por cuanto el aprendizaje del inglés quedó sujeto a la conectividad de cada hogar. Es así que el estudio se planteó como objetivo analizar el impacto de la educación virtual en el aprendizaje del inglés en estudiantes de básica ecuatoriana. En este sentido se empleó una metodología descriptiva, documental y comparativa, teniéndose como corpus 25 fuentes (2012-2025) contrastadas mediante matrices por país, nivel, tecnología y resultado. Entre los resultados se obtuvo que las herramientas digitales producen efectos positivos en condiciones planificadas, mientras en Ecuador la falta de dispositivos, la conexión irregular y la escasa interacción limitaron la práctica oral. Entre las conclusiones se estableció que el impacto depende menos de la plataforma que del acceso, la mediación docente y el acompañamiento familiar.

title: Women's Participation in Peacebuilding: A Study of Selected Areas in Taraba State, 1991-2023
abstract: Violent conflicts arising from ethnic, religious, political, land-related, citizenship, and resource-based disputes have shaped peacebuilding needs in Taraba State, Nigeria. This study examined women’s participation in conflict resolution, reconciliation, and peacebuilding in Jalingo, Wukari, and Sardauna Local Government Areas from 1991 to 2023. Using a qualitative approach grounded in documentary and historical evidence, the study analyzed the nature and consequences of violent conflicts and women’s contributions to peacebuilding in the selected areas. The findings indicate that women and children were among the groups most severely affected, experiencing the loss of family members, displacement, property destruction, livelihood losses, economic hardship, and disruption of social relations. Women also played important roles in promoting peace through religious mobilization, including prayer and fasting; community mobilization; women’s associations; peace marches and protests; interfaith engagement; advocacy; dialogue; and informal reconciliation initiatives. Despite these contributions, patriarchal norms, institutional bias, and limited access to decision-making constrained their participation in formal peace and security structures. The study demonstrates the importance of women’s community-based and informal peacebuilding contributions while identifying persistent barriers …

title: Post-Meal Walking as A Strategy for Postprandial Glycemic Control After High-Carbohydrate Meals in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Literature Review of Timing, Duration, & Intensity
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterized by impaired postprandial glycemic control, a condition of particular concern in Asian populations, including Indonesia, where rice serves as the dominant carbohydrate source and carries a high glycemic index. Postprandial exercise, particularly walking, has been proposed as a practical, low-cost, non-pharmacological strategy to attenuate glucose excursions after meals, yet no prior narrative review has specifically synthesized evidence on post-meal walking in relation to high-carbohydrate, rice-based diets. This narrative review aimed to synthesize existing evidence on the effectiveness, optimal timing, duration, and intensity of post-meal walking for glycemic control in individuals with T2DM, and to evaluate its relevance to high-carbohydrate meal contexts. Literature was searched through PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2016 and 2026, yielding ten randomized controlled trials that met the inclusion criteria. Findings showed that post-meal walking consistently reduced postprandial glucose excursions, peak glucose, and area under the curve, with the most consistent benefits observed when walking was initiated within 15-30 minutes after meals, for 10-20 minutes, at light-to-moderate intensity. These effects are physiologically explained by insulin-independent GLUT4 translocation induc…

title: Playing to Teach: SPED Teachers' Experiences in Using Physical and Traditional Games in Teaching Learners with Special Needs
abstract: Background and Aim: Game-based learning has emerged as a promising pedagogical approach in special education, yet existing research has largely examined strategies, challenges, coping mechanisms, and support systems as separate lines of inquiry rather than as an interconnected process, particularly within the Philippine SPED context. This study explored the lived experiences of SPED teachers in using physical and traditional games to teach learners with special needs, examining how their strategies, challenges, coping mechanisms, and support systems interrelate in practice. Materials and Methods: Using a qualitative case study design, this research employed in-depth semi-structured interviews with five SPED teachers from selected schools in District 6, Oroquieta City Division, Philippines. Purposive sampling was used to select participants who had at least one year of experience in special education and actively used game-based instruction, with the sample size guided by the principle of information power and confirmed through the attainment of thematic saturation. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework. Results: Four major themes emerged from the analysis: (1) adaptive game implementation strategies, including game modification, multisensory engagement, and differentiated instruction; (2) multifaceted challenges encompassing…

title: Pan-Cancer Classification in Clinical Applications: A Comprehensive Analysis using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Cancer affects millions of people worldwide, and accurate, timely classification of cancer type is closely tied to treatment selection and patient outcomes — particularly in metastatic disease or Cancer of Unknown Primary, where identifying the tissue of origin directly informs site specific treatment. Multiple clinical and genomic variables, including mutation count, tumor stage, diagnosis age, tumor purity, smoking status and sex are individually associated with cancer behavior, but whether their combined use improves classification across a broad range of cancer types — rather than within a single cancer type, as in most prior work — has rarely been tested directly. This study evaluates four machine learning classifiers — Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, and Artificial Neural Network — on a clinical pancancer dataset spanning 20 cancer types (6,110 patients; 1,222 held out for testing), using ten routinely available clinical and summary genomic covariates. XGBoost achieved the strongestperformance (accuracy 87.0%, 95% CI: 85.0–88.8%; F1-score 0.869; ROC AUC 0.993), with Random Forest close behind; both outperformed SVM and ANN by a margin confirmed as statistically significant through 5-fold cross-validation. Rather than assuming that the selected variables jointly contribute to classification performance, this study tests that claim directly…

title: Exploring Teachers’ Practices in Advocating Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Background and Aim: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education creates opportunities and challenges for teaching and learning. As AI tools become accessible, teachers are essential in guiding students toward responsible, ethical, and effective use. Yet, teacher practices supporting responsible AI use remain underexplored, particularly in the Philippine context. This case study examined how teachers advocate responsible AI use in their classrooms. Materials and Methods: A qualitative case study design was used. Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with fifteen school teachers at Tabina National High School, Tabina District, Division of Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. Purposive criterion sampling selected participants who: (a) taught in basic education, (b) integrated AI tools or AI-related discussions into teaching, (c) demonstrated advocacy for responsible technology use, and (d) had at least three years of teaching experience. Interviews were conducted in Cebuano, transcribed verbatim, translated into English when necessary, and thematically analyzed following Merriam and Tisdell’s (2016) case study procedures. Data were collected from January to June 2026. Results: Four sequential themes emerged: (1) challenges involving student overreliance, absent institutional policies, limited teacher training, and academic integrity; (2) coping mechanis…
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews

title: Vivekananda's Educational Philosophy and Its Relevance to Twenty-First Century Learning
abstract: Background and Aim: India’s education system in 2026 is mid-implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, even as the Indian classroom grapples with digital distraction, uneven policy rollout, and fast AI adoption. Questions remain about the effects on students’ concentration, values, and overall development. This paper examines whether Swami Vivekananda's four core educational concepts — man-making education, concentration of mind, universal access, and character-building — offer a workable framework for analysing this learning crisis, read against NEP 2020 and NCF 2023. Scholarship on Vivekananda’s views on education and the academic discussion on contemporary Indian policy discourse have developed quite independently. There has been very little discussion of the relationship between Vivekananda’s ideas, formulated a century ago, and modern empirical work on attention, equity, and character formation. Materials and Methods: This study uses qualitative, conceptual, and comparative textual analysis and not primary data gathering or statistical testing. The main sources are the speeches and writings of Vivekananda in the Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda. Secondary sources include Indian government documents (NEP 2020, NCF 2023) and articles about policy implementation, digital attention, digital divide, and SEL. Recurring themes in Vivekananda's writings were id…

title: Students’ Perceptions of Homework as a Support for Improving Learning and Knowledge Retention in Vocational Engineering Education: An Action Research Study
abstract: Background and Aim: The inclusion of homework in the engineering vocational curriculum is uncommon, and its effects remain underexplored. To address this gap in the literature, this research focused on students' perceptions of homework to better understand its impact on learning and knowledge retention. To achieve the aim and objectives of this study, both quantitative and qualitative data were collected from 10 learners enrolled at a college in a socioeconomically deprived city in Northern England. The hybrid data collection technique was adopted to ascertain extensively the design and extent to which homework influences learning, based on participants' lived experiences. Materials and Methods: A participatory Action Research (AR) approach adopted in this research began by identifying homework as an intervention to support learning and knowledge retention. This was followed by an evaluation of learners’ perceptions of how homework supported learning and knowledge retention. The evaluation process involved assigning two sets of homework to the selected cohort. Feedback from completing the first set of homework helped redesign the second set. Tasks in both homework sets were problem-based and involved applying and memorizing formulas. The feedback collection method involved both quantitative and qualitative approaches, using survey questionnaires and open-ended interviews, respe…

title: Negotiating Grade 12 English Textbook Implementation in Nepal: Lived Experiences of Teachers and Students
abstract: Background and Aim: The textbook plays an important role in institutional curriculum policies, in providing a systematic sequence of topics and a logical progression from simpler to more complex concepts. Listening activities, speaking tasks, reading passages, and vocabulary development activities correspond to learning objectives and cultural representation in contemporary English language education. This study explored secondary-level English teachers’ and students’ perceptions of the Grade 12 Compulsory English textbook, centred on the Curriculum Development Centre (CDC) in Nepal. The research focuses on empirical insights, students’ experiences, the textbook’s strengths, limitations, and future policy decisions concerning English language education. Materials and Methods: This study adopted an Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) design to explore participants' lived experiences of using the Grade 12 Compulsory English textbook and their interactions with it to understand challenges, relevance, influence, and usefulness. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with five secondary-level English teachers and three Grade 12 graduates. We obtained detailed accounts of participants’ experiences, interpretations, and perceptions to acquire meaningful information about the use of the Grade 12 Compulsory English textbook. Results: Researchers identified maj…

title: The Impact of Conducive Learning Environments on Learners’ Attitudes Towards Geometry: A Null Relationship
abstract: Geometry remains a critical component of mathematics education due to its role in developing spatial reasoning, logical thinking, and problem-solving skills essential for STEM-related fields. However, persistent negative learner attitudes toward geometry continue to hinder achievement and engagement, particularly in under-resourced educational contexts. While existing literature suggests that conducive learning environments positively influence learner attitudes, limited research has explored this relationship specifically within geometry or examined contexts where such relationships may be inconsistent or complex. Therefore, this study investigated the relationship between conducive learning environments and learners’ attitudes toward geometry. Guided by the Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework, the study adopted a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were collected through questionnaires and analysed using chi-square tests and contingency coefficients to determine the strength of association between variables. Qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with mathematics teachers and analysed thematically, with findings interpreted through the lenses of teaching, cognitive, and social presence. The quantitative results revealed a statistically significant and moderately strong relationship between learning environments and learners’ attitudes toward …

title: Motivational Influences of Detective Conan on Thai Undergraduate Psychology Students' Intentions to Pursue Advanced Studies in Forensic Psychology
abstract: Background and Aim: Popular culture may shape students’ academic engagement and career aspirations. This study examined associations between engagement with Detective Conan and undergraduates’ motivation to pursue advanced study in forensic psychology and criminology. Materials and Methods: A questionnaire was completed by 182 psychology undergraduates in Bangkok, Thailand, from 200 invitees (91.0% response rate). Hierarchical cluster analysis using Ward’s method and squared Euclidean distance classified participants into high-, moderate-, and low-engagement groups. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) identified motivational dimensions, while two-way ANOVA compared factor scores by engagement group and academic year. Ethics approval and informed consent were obtained. Results: 90.34% of participants had read or watched Detective Conan, 72.89% reported applying concepts or skills from the series to psychology studies, and 41.67% retrospectively associated the franchise with their interest in forensic psychology. EFA yielded four factors: intrinsic interest in justice, pop-culture-driven motivation, professional advancement, and academic application. Sampling adequacy was confirmed (KMO = .84), and Bartlett’s test was significant, χ² (66) = 915.42, p < .001.
