title: A graph-based iterative strategy for solving the all-line transmission switching problem
abstract: Abstract The transmission switching problem aims to determine the optimal network topology that minimizes the operating costs of a power system. This problem is typically formulated as a mixed-integer optimization model, which involves big-M constants that lead to weak relaxations and significant computational challenges, particularly when all lines are switchable. In this paper, we propose a twofold approach: first, using graph theory to derive tighter big-M values by solving a relaxed longest path problem; second, introducing an iterative algorithm that incorporates a heuristic version of the switching problem to efficiently generate low-cost feasible solutions, thereby accelerating the search for optimal solutions in the integer optimization solver. Numerical results on the 118-bus network across 100 demand scenarios demonstrate that the proposed methodology reduces the number of unsolved instances within 1 h by 57% and decreases the average computational time by 44% compared to conventional approaches in the literature.

title: DEMOGRAPHIC PROFILING AND MARKET SEGMENTATION OF SCUBA DIVERS ACROSS MALAYSIAN DIVING DESTINATIONS
abstract: SCUBA diving has shown a notable surge in popularity as a recreational pursuit within the Malaysian context. Tourism Malaysia and Malaysia SCUBA Diving Association highlighted SCUBA diving as one of the essential activities in promoting tourism destinations in Malaysia, and they advocate for SCUBA dive operators to actively promote their products and services to the respective market segments. Nonetheless, the absence of significant statistical data challenges SCUBA diving operators to strategize their marketing initiatives effectively. Thus, the main aim of this study is to identify the segmentation of demographic variables among SCUBA divers across Malaysian diving destinations. The researcher adopted the quantitative method by using an online survey of SCUBA divers who had visited diving destinations in Malaysia. The online survey was distributed via social media and the SCUBA divers’ association. The usable responses were 321, and the data were coded and analysed using descriptive analysis in SPSS software. The implications of the research contribute to the empirical research on SCUBA divers' demographic profile, which helps in providing inputs for the stakeholders. This will also help the stakeholders, such as the government and diving businesses, in planning their marketing strategies and ensuring that these strategies are aligned and suitable with their target market.

title: OPERATING OPTIMISATION FOR A DIRECT-CONNECTED GREEN-ELECTRICITY HYDROGEN-AMMONIA PARK BASED ON MIXED-INTEGER AND CONTINUOUS LINEAR PROGRAMMING
abstract: This paper studies the operation optimisation of a direct-connected wind-photovoltaic hydrogen-ammonia park and evaluates how production flexibility, energy storage and islanded operation affect power balance, renewable-electricity indicators and operating cost. Some applications have been developed for full-load operation, discrete production scheduling, continuous power regulation, islanded dispatch, storage sizing and grid-connected comparison. The park has 40 MW of wind power, 64 MW of photovoltaic power, and hydrogen-ammonia loads for 36 t/d and 72 t/d production. At a 36 t/d full-load baseline, the self-consumption, green-electricity and export ratios are 28.16%, 69.21% and 35.92%, respectively; 54 t/d is the lowest-cost feasible output in discrete scheduling, and the unit cost is 4591.27 yuan/t. The total annual cost of continuous regulation is 1.9005 million yuan, and all three indicators have been achieved in 210 of the 360 weighted days. In islanded operation, 5000 MWh of storage increases the annual output to 25920 t, but the unit cost is still higher than that of grid-connected systems. Flexible production and storage increase the utilisation of renewable energy; however, economic feasibility requires integrated planning of production, storage and grid operation.

title: Tumor-node response heterogeneity: Exploring the “spatial biology” of neoadjuvant therapy response in rectal cancer and its clinical implications
abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy - the combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy administered before surgery - followed by total mesorectal excision is the foundation of treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer. Pathological assessment of the primary tumor commonly uses tumor regression grading, which quantifies the extent of tumor response to treatment and provides prognostic value. However, a growing body of evidence reveals profound inter- and intra-patient heterogeneity in treatment response between the primary tumor and its associated lymph nodes. This review explores the concept of ‘spatial biology’ - the study of how distinct anatomical compartments within a patient, such as the primary tumor site and nodal basins, show unique biological behaviors and distinct responses to therapy. We will synthesize current evidence from single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies, explore the dynamic remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment at the primary site, and contrast this with the unique (and often discordant) response within lymph nodes that may serve as immunological sanctuaries for resistant clones. The combination of a novel lymph node regression grading system, which specifically assesses treatment response in lymph nodes, with traditional tumor regression grading is proposed here to more accurately reflect this spatial variation. abstract: BACKGROUND Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies, and chemotherapy remains the main treatment option for patients with unresectable disease. Reliable prediction of chemotherapy response is therefore critical for individualized treatment planning. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) provides high-resolution, tumor-specific imaging that may be well suited for deep learning-based prediction of chemotherapy response. AIM To develop and validate an EUS-based deep learning model for predicting first-line chemotherapy response in patients with unresectable PDAC, and to evaluate its prognostic value for overall survival (OS) stratification. METHODS In this retrospective, single-center study, 190 patients with histologically confirmed PDAC diagnosed between February 2016 and March 2025 were included. All patients were deemed ineligible for upfront surgical resection based on formal multidisciplinary team evaluation, including those with locally advanced or metastatic disease and those considered medically or personally unsuitable for surgery. title: Role of Microstructures on Bubble Detachment and Electrochemical Response in Wicking Electrodes
abstract: Abstract Gas bubble evolution at electrode surfaces reduces the electrode–electrolyte interfacial area and limits the efficiency of gas-evolving electrochemical reactions. While structured electrodes have been widely shown to improve bubble management, the independent contribution of individual geometric parameters to bubble nucleation, detachment, and electrochemical behavior remains poorly understood. Here, bubble-templated electrodeposition is used as a model fabrication platform to systematically vary structural width and height across two morphologically distinct electrode families, stochastic pillar arrays and circular-wall structures, while characterizing double-layer capacitance, current density, bubble detachment diameter, and bubble number density. Three-dimensional wicking architecture is shown to outperform a flat hydrophilic electrode in both electrochemical characterizations and bubble management. At constant height, increasing structural width raises double-layer capacitance but reduces current density and increases detachment diameter─a decoupling attributed to reduced structural unit density and reproduced across both morphological families. title: Structural–Response Consistency Evaluation of a Jiulong Coking Coal Molecular Model Based on Multi-Characterization Constraints
abstract: Abstract The evaluation of coal molecular models commonly relies on individual criteria, such as structural parameter matching, density agreement, or consistency in adsorption behavior. However, these indicators are usually considered independently, and a unified quantitative framework for integrating different evaluation dimensions is still lacking. In this study, an average organic molecular model of Jiulong (JL) coking coal was constructed based on ultimate analysis, 13C NMR, FTIR, and XPS characterization, and a structure–response consistency evaluation framework was established by integrating structural constraints and multiresponse analysis. Based on aromatic carbon fraction, XBP, C–O/C═O ratio, and pyrrolic N/pyridinic N ratio, the molecular formula of the JL coal model was determined as C205H144O30N4. Five indices, including the structural constraint consistency index (SCI), density consistency index (DCI), adsorption response consistency index (ACI), dynamic wetting trajectory consistency index (WCI), and multiresponse consistency index (MCVI), were proposed to quantify structural constraint satisfaction and response consistency. The results indicate that the model effectively retains the structural features derived from multicharacterization, with an (SCI) value of 0.981. title: Design of a Book Sales Management Information System to Support Business Process Digitalization at Sidosari Wunut Tulung, Klaten
abstract: This study aims to design and implement a web-based book sales management information system to support business process digitalization at Sidosari Wunut Bookstore, Tulung, Klaten. Book data, sales transactions, and inventory were previously recorded manually, which limited the accuracy and accessibility of information. The system was developed using the Waterfall method, which comprises requirement analysis, design, implementation, verification, and maintenance. Requirements were identified through observation of the bookstore's operational processes and documented in a Software Requirements Specification (SRS) structured according to IEEE 830-1998, while the Unified Modeling Language (UML) was used to model the system. The system was implemented using JavaScript with MySQL as the database. The main contribution of this study is a documented design and working implementation that integrates book data management, sales transactions, and automatic stock updates in a single web-based system adapted to a small-scale bookstore. The novelty of this study lies in documenting the full path from an IEEE 830-1998 requirements specification and UML models to a functionally tested implementation for a small-scale bookstore, whereas the related studies reviewed focus on online sales, recommendation, or inventory analysis. title: Architectural Dynamics of Fintech Innovations and Digital Financial Services: Empirically Understanding Consumer Trust, Perceived Risk and Financial Inclusion
abstract: Digital financial services and financial technologies have revolutionized the retail banking sector. Payments and intermediation of money has changed dramatically with the advent of these innovations. Many international development organizations have touted the power of digital financial services to promote financial inclusion. However there is still uncertainty if the rapid penetration of digital financial services leads to real financial inclusion or leads to creation of inactive bank accounts. This paper seeks to understand what drives people to adopt digital financial services and convert these services to increased financial wellbeing. Data was collected from 650 individuals across rural, semi urban and urban economies through a questionnaire. Data was analyzed using Pearson Correlations to identify correlations between variables and Multiple Linear Regression to better understand what drives digital financial service use and financial inclusion. Findings reveal that while perceived ease of use and usefulness lead to higher likelihood of adopting digital financial services consumer trust had the highest impact.

abstract: प्रस्तुत शोध अध्ययन नदी (जल) डेटा की राजनीति से संदर्भित है जो चीन की जल डेटा साझा में कमी के कारण भारत और बांग्लादेश की सुरक्षा और आपदा प्रबंधन पर प्रभाव का विश्लेषणात्मक अध्ययन करता है। इस शोध का प्राथमिक लक्ष्य, ऊपर तटवर्ती वाले देशो पर निचले तटवर्ती वाले देशों की नदी (जल) डेटा साझा हेतु निर्भरता को समझना है। भारत और बांग्लादेश, चीन की तुलना में नीचे तटवर्ती अर्थात् दक्षिण एशिया में आते हैं और चीन द्वारा जल डेटा साझा में कमी करने के कारण इन देशों पर बाढ़ जैसी बड़ी प्राकृतिक आपदा का खतरा बना रहता है। ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी बेसिन और इसकी सहायक नदियाँ भारत, चीन और बांग्लादेश से होकर बहती हैं। ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी विश्व की सबसे बड़ी नदियों में से एक है जिसका आरंभिक क्षेत्र चीन है। चीन के द्वारा इन नदियों का डाटा साझा न करने पर भारत के पूर्वी क्षेत्र और बांग्लादेश जैसे निचले तटवर्ती वाले देशों पर विशेषकर मानसून के महीने में नदियों के जल स्तर का कोई भी डाटा उपलब्ध नहीं होता है जिसके कारण अचानक आने वाली बाढ़ से भारत और बांग्लादेश के क्षेत्र में बड़ी हानि पहुँचाती है। इस अचानक आने वाली बाढ़ से भारत और बांग्लादेश दोनों देशों के आपदा प्रबंधन की क्षमता पर नकारात्मक प्रभाव पड़ता है। भारत और चीन के बीच इन नदियों के डेटा साझा करने हेतु 2002 में डवन्े समझौता हुआ इस समझौते के तहत् चीन अपने क्षेत्र से भारत की ओर बहने वाली नदियों का डाटा भारत को साझा करेगा। जिसमें ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी और उसकी सहायक नदियों से संबंधित यह डाटा प्रत्येक वर्ष मई से अक्टूबर तक का देने के लिए चीन ने सहमति जताई। भारत और चीन के बीच हुए इस सम…

title: TALABALARNING IJTIMOIY FAOL KOMPETENSIYALARINI SHAKLLANTIRISHDA KOMMUNIKATIV YONDASHUVNING PEDAGOGIK MEXANIZMLARI
abstract: Maqolada talabalarning ijtimoiy faol kompetensiyalarini shakllantirishda kommunikativ yondashuvning pedagogik mexanizmlari nazariy jihatdan asoslangan. Kommunikativ kompetensiya, kommunikativ harakat, dialogik va hamkorlikda o‘qitish nazariyalarining qiyosiy tahlili asosida ijtimoiy faol kompetensiyaning kognitiv, aksiologik va faoliyatli komponentlarining kommunikativ jihatlari ochib berilgan. Kommunikativ yondashuvning oltita pedagogik mexanizmi - dialogik o‘zaro ta’sir, argumentatsiya va kelishuv, rolli identifikatsiya, hamkorlikdagi faoliyat, tashqi ijtimoiy muloqot va ijtimoiy refleksiya ajratilgan. Mexanizmlarni amalga oshirish bosqichlari, pedagogik shart-sharoitlari va kompetensiyaning kommunikativ jihatlarini baholash mezonlari taklif etilgan.

title: MEASUREMENT OF MUNICIPAL NEW-QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES AND REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
abstract: Guided by the policy of developing new-quality productive forces in light of local conditions, this paper takes panel data (2015-2024) of five core cities in Jiangxi including Nanchang, Ganzhou, Jiujiang, Shangrao and Yichun as research samples. An evaluation system for municipal new-quality productive forces is constructed covering scientific-technological, green and digital dimensions. The entropy-weight improved AHP-TOPSIS model is adopted for comprehensive measurement, so as to analyze its temporal evolution and regional differentiation. The results show that the overall level of new-quality productive forces of the five cities presents a fluctuating upward trend, which can be divided into three stages: steady accumulation, accelerated improvement and adjustment-divergence. Obvious echelon gaps exist among cities. Nanchang takes the lead, Ganzhou ranks second, Shangrao shows strong late-comer momentum, while Jiujiang and Yichun suffer from remarkable fluctuation and decline. Green productivity enjoys sound intra-provincial balance yet meets promotion bottlenecks; inter-city gaps are prominent in scientific-technological and digital productivity. Most cities are confronted with insufficient S&T investment, weak digital industrial foundation and heavy pressure of industrial transformation. title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence in human resource management for sustainable workplaces a bibliometric and literature review
abstract: Abstract This study explores the evolving role of Human Resource Management (HRM) in managing ethical Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in workplace environments. A mixed-methods approach combining bibliometric and literature review was applied to Scopus-indexed literature. The bibliometric component analyzed publication trends, country and institutional contributions, keyword co-occurrence, and co-authorship networks, while the literature review examined conceptual insights and practical directions from the most relevant scholarly publications. The findings revealed an increasing academic interest in the intersection of HRM, AI ethics, and sustainability, with significant contributions from India, China, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Romania. Leading institutional affiliations included the Symbiosis International Deemed University and the University of Delhi. The co-occurrence of key terms highlighted central themes, including human resource management, artificial intelligence, decision-making, ethical technology, and predictive analytics. Co-authorship analysis revealed moderate research collaboration, with emerging networks indicating potential for global cooperation. Literature review of the top-cited papers indicated that HRM is evolving from an administrative function to a strategic player in guidi…

title: Mathematics for Sustainable Development: Applications, Opportunities and Educational Perspectives
abstract: Sustainable development requires the responsible management of natural resources while ensuring social and economic well-being for present and future generations. Although sustainable development is often associated with environmental science, technology and policy, mathematics plays a fundamental and often under-recognized role in achieving sustainability. Mathematics provides tools for measuring, analysing, predicting and optimizing the use of limited resources. Concepts such as statistics, percentages, ratios, probability, mathematical modelling, optimization, geometry, algebra and calculus can be applied to real-world sustainability challenges including climate change, water conservation, renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, waste management, transportation, population growth and resource allocation. The present paper explores how mathematical concepts can contribute to sustainable development and demonstrates their application through practical examples. It also discusses the role of mathematics education in developing sustainability-oriented thinking among learners. The paper argues that mathematics should be connected with real-life environmental and social problems so that learners understand mathematics not merely as a computational subject but as a powerful tool for informed decision-making and sustainable living. title: Healthcare Transaction Authorization and Management Computer Device
abstract: This technical report presents the design, functional concept, and technological significance of a registered industrial invention titled “Healthcare Transaction Authorization and Management Computer Device,” formally protected under UK Design Registration No. 6496417 and granted by the United Kingdom Intellectual Property Office on 29 January 2026 The invention is classified within International Design Classification Class 14, covering recording, telecommunication, and data-processing equipment, reflecting its role as an integrated digital platform for secure healthcare transaction processing and operational management. Assessing the Balancing Capability and Grid Integration Performance of Various Solar PV Systems
abstract: Solar photovoltaic energy production fluctuates rapidly due to sunlight and temperature. The fluctuations have to be balanced against the distribution system in which they connect. This paper examines four different types of solar photovoltaic systems; they include monocrystalline roof-top, multi-crystalline roof-top, ground mounted, and battery supported roof-top solar photovoltaic systems. A systematic comparative analysis takes into account balancing and integration indicators. Balancing efficiency is measured using the useful supply, curtailment, conversion loss, and residual imbalance energy. Integration efficiency is assessed based on voltage behavior, ramp control, power factor, controllability, and suitability. Data has been taken from research literature and other accepted references; the analysis has made use of standardized scores and not the actual field data. From the analysis, battery supported photovoltaic systems perform better with a balancing index of 90 and a grid integration score of 91. For the ground mounted systems, it is 79 and 82, respectively, while roof-top systems perform moderately well. While the type of technology affects energy production, system design affected balancing performance significantly. Inverter intelligence, prediction, storage, and coordination improved integration performance.

title: LEAN AND AGILE MANAGEMENT AND WORK ENGAGEMENT AMONG HEALTHCARE EMPLOYEES: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: Healthcare organizations face increasing pressure to improve operational efficiency while maintaining employee well-being and work engagement. Lean and Agile Management have been increasingly applied to address these challenges, yet evidence concerning their relationship with work engagement among healthcare employees remains fragmented. This systematic literature review synthesizes the existing evidence on Lean and Agile Management and work engagement in healthcare settings. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search of Scopus-indexed literature published between 2015 and 2025 identified 26 records. After removal of five duplicate and application of the eligibility criteria, 21 studies were included in the review. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and thematic analysis was conducted to synthesize the evidence. Three themes emerged: patient-centered care, healthcare efficiency, and impact on work engagement. The findings indicate that Lean Management was commonly associated with improved process flow, waste reduction, teamwork, and operational efficiency, although its relationship with work engagement varied across contexts, with some studies reporting increased workload, time pressure, and job strain. abstract: वर्तमान वैश्विक परिदृश्य मानवीय इतिहास के सबसे जटिल और परिवर्तनकारी दौर से गुजर रहा है। एक ओर जहाँ कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता और तकनीकी स्वचालन मानव जीवन के हर पहलू को पुनर्परिभाषित कर रहे हैं, वहीं दूसरी ओर जलवायु संकट, जैव विविधता का क्षरण और गहरी होती सामाजिक-आर्थिक असमानताएं हमारे अस्तित्व के लिए गंभीर खतरा उत्पन्न कर रही हैं। इन अभूतपूर्व चुनौतियों के समाधान हेतु वैश्विक शिक्षा प्रणालियों में एक बुनियादी और आमूलचूल बदलाव की आवश्यकता है। यह विस्तृत शोध पत्र इस बात का गहन और बहुआयामी विश्लेषण करता है कि 21वीं सदी की आवश्यकताओं के अनुरूप शिक्षा को कैसे पुनर्गठित किया जाए। अ/ययन मुख्य रूप से यूनेस्को द्वारा प्रस्तावित श्नव-सामाजिक अनुबंधश्, भारत की राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020 और शिक्षा में मानवकेंद्रित तकनीकी एकीकरण पर केंद्रित है। अनुसंधान यह स्पष्ट रूप से दर्शाता है कि भविष्य की शिक्षा को पारंपरिक रटंत विद्या और शिक्षक-केंद्रित दृष्टिकोण से हटकर अनुभवजन्य, योग्यता-आधारित और पूरी तरह से छात्र-केंद्रित होना चाहिए। कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता शिक्षा के क्षेत्र में असीमित अवसर प्रदान करती हैय हालाँकि, इसका अनियंत्रित उपयोग छात्रों में संज्ञानात्मक निर्भरता को बढ़ावा दे सकता है, इसलिए एक नैतिक और मानवकेंद्रित रूपरेखा का क्रियान्वयन अपरिहार्य है। इसके अतिरिक्त, वैश्विक स्तर पर योग्य शिक्षकों की भारी कमीकृजो कि वर्ष 2030 तक 44 मिलियन तक पहुँचने का अनुमान है एक ऐसा ढांचागत संकट है जिसका समाधान किए बिना किसी भी शैक्षिक सुधार की कल्पना निरर्थक है। यह पत्र निष्कर्ष निकालता है कि एक न्यायसंगत, समावेशी औ…

title: Socioeconomic Characteristics and Income Inequality among Kinnow Growers: A Comparative Study of Fazilka and Sriganganagar
abstract: This study examines the socioeconomic characteristics of Kinnow growers in Fazilka (Punjab) and Sriganganagar (Rajasthan) using primary data collected during the 2020–21 crop year from 480 growers (240 in each district). Descriptive statistics, cross-tabulation, chi-square tests, Cramér’s V, Lorenz curves, and Gini coefficients were used to compare landholding, demographic characteristics, household conditions, and income distribution. The results show that Kinnow cultivation is concentrated among medium and semi-medium farmers. These categories together account for 87.50% of sampled growers in Fazilka and 86.67% in Sriganganagar. Mean landholding is higher in Sriganganagar (6.85 ha) than in Fazilka (5.34 ha), while landholding inequality is higher in Fazilka (Gini = 0.626) than in Sriganganagar (0.510). Growers in both districts are predominantly middle-aged, married, and formally educated. Mean family size is 6.5875 members in Fazilka and 6.7208 in Sriganganagar. Mean monthly household electricity consumption is also similar at 475 and 474.16 units, respectively. Mean annual income is slightly higher in Fazilka (₹5.8125 lakh) than in Sriganganagar (₹5.525 lakh), whereas income inequality is substantially lower in Sriganganagar (Gini = 0.202) than in Fazilka (Gini = 0.352). Core Muscle Endurance and Side-to-Side Asymmetry in Club-Level Pakistani Fast Bowlers: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Lumbar bone stress injury is the most time-costly injury in cricket, and fast bowlers carry the greatest burden because the delivery stride imposes repeated, asymmetric trunk loading on a spine that is often still maturing. Pakistani club-level bowlers show a high prevalence of poor core endurance ratios, but no Pakistani study has examined core endurance asymmetry in fast bowlers in relation to side dominance, bowling workload, bowling action and low back pain history. Objective: To describe trunk flexor, extensor and side-bridge endurance, endurance ratios and dominant versus non-dominant asymmetry in club-level Pakistani fast bowlers, and to examine their associations with bowling workload, bowling action and low back pain history as potential markers of lumbar injury risk. Methods: This descriptive, multi-club, cross-sectional study will recruit 216 male hard-ball fast and fast-medium bowlers aged 15–25 years from registered clubs and academies in Lahore, Pakistan (194 required plus a 10% allowance). Core endurance will be measured with the McGill Torso Muscle Endurance Test Battery in a counterbalanced Latin-square order with 5 minutes of rest between tests. Bowling action will be classified from two-dimensional video by two independent raters, and workload will be derived from a structured 28-day recall verified against coach or club records. title: Adaptive error management for fault-tolerant quantum computing across hardware-level suppression, system-level diagnosis, and real-time decoding
abstract: Abstract Fault-tolerant quantum computing reached a milestone in December 2024 when Google’s Willow processor demonstrated below-threshold error correction on a superconducting chip, a result since reproduced on neutral-atom and alternative superconducting platforms. Yet the classical decoders needed to sustain this performance face a scaling challenge: noise becomes increasingly structured and correlated as systems grow, while decoders must respond within microsecond coherence windows. This survey asks whether error suppression, noise diagnosis, and decoding are better treated as one adaptive control problem than as three separate research programs. Drawing on a scoping review of 146 records, it organizes the field into a three-layer taxonomy. Layer 1 (Hardware-Level Suppression) integrates protection into the physical substrate; bosonic cat qubits exponentially suppress bit-flip errors, projecting up to 90% overhead reduction versus surface codes. Layer 2 (Diagnosis) employs probabilistic models and computational intelligence to characterize error sources; neuro-fuzzy architectures and the Bias–Entropy decomposition separate hardware drift from logical faults, subject to an identifiability limit that we characterize. title: A Study of CSR Practices and Environmental Sustainability Initiatives of Major Industries in Rajasthan
abstract: Rajasthan has some of India’s biggest mining, oil and gas, cement, and textile industries, each having to adhere to the mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) guidelines stipulated in section 135 of the Companies Act of 2013. This study looks at the four leading companies in the industries mentioned above—Hindustan Zinc Limited (Mining), Cairn Oil & Gas/Vedanta Limited (Oil & Gas), Shree Cement Limited (Cement), and RSWM Limited of the LNJ Bhilwara Group (Textile)—in terms of CSR expenditure and environmental sustainability practices. Using the sustainability reports and CSR reports of these companies in addition to literature on the topic, it is observed that the amount spent on CSR varies greatly among the different industries and even within an industry: Hindustan Zinc Ltd reports an expenditure of ₹273.45 crore in FY2024-25 while Shree Cement Ltd spends ₹51.34 crore on CSR in FY2023-24, while Cairn Oil & Gas’s multistate CSR expenditure decreased from ₹25.53 crore in FY2021-22 to ₹10.26 crore in FY2024-25. Similar variations have been seen in environmental initiatives: Sewage treatment and land restoration by Hindustan Zinc, Water positivity and renewable energy by Shree Cement and water conservation by RSWM through its Zero Liquid Discharge project.

title: Financial Knowledge and Financial Attitude in Mutual Fund Investment Decision-Making among Retail Investors in Thiruvananthapuram District
abstract: Financial knowledge and financial attitude are important dimensions of individual financial decision-making, particularly in investment contexts where investors need to evaluate information and make informed choices. Within this context, this study investigates the association between financial knowledge and investor confidence, as well as the relationship between financial attitude and mutual fund investment decision quality among retail investors in Thiruvananthapuram district. To evaluate the relationships between variables, this study gathered primary data from 287 retail mutual fund investors utilising a structured questionnaire through purposive sampling within a quantitative, cross-sectional, and explanatory framework. Data were examined using reliability testing through Cronbach’s alpha, exploratory factor analysis, descriptive statistics, alongside Spearman’s and Kendall’s Tau-b correlations, simple linear regression, and ordinal logistic regression. The results demonstrated a strong positive association between financial knowledge and investor confidence (ρ = 0.584, p < 0.001), where financial knowledge accounted for 34.1% of the variation in confidence. Financial attitude also showed a significant positive association with mutual fund investment decision quality (τb = 0.467, p < 0.001). title: Green Transformational Leadership and Green Innovation: The Sequential Mediating Roles of Green Human Capital Management and Work Behavior
abstract: Organizations seeking environmental improvement need to understand how leaders' environmental priorities are associated with employee capabilities, everyday conduct, and Green Innovation. This study examined the direct and indirect associations among Green Transformational Leadership, Green Human Capital Management, Work Behavior, and Green Innovation, including a sequential mediation pathway. A cross-sectional quantitative survey of 300 purposively selected company employees used a 24-item, five-point Likert questionnaire; the reported data were analyzed with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Green Transformational Leadership was positively associated with Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.406; p < 0.001) and Work Behavior (β = 0.255; p < 0.001), but not directly with Green Innovation (β = 0.041; p = 0.446). Green Human Capital Management was associated with Work Behavior (β = 0.325; p < 0.001) and Green Innovation (β = 0.292; p < 0.001), while Work Behavior was associated with Green Innovation (β = 0.326; p < 0.001). The specific indirect paths through Green Human Capital Management (β = 0.118; p < 0.001), through Work Behavior (β = 0.083; p = 0.001), and sequentially through both mediators (β = 0.043; p < 0.001) were significant. Many-objective reservoir operation optimization using NSGA-III and decision-support analysis: a sustainable management framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India
abstract: Abstract Efficient reservoir operation requires simultaneous consideration of competing goals related to hydropower generation, water-supply reliability, flood management, and storage regulation. However, deriving balanced operating policies becomes increasingly complex when several conflicting objectives are considered concurrently. This study develops a many-objective optimization framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India, considering four objectives: maximization of hydropower generation and minimization of water deficit, spill losses, and storage deviation. The reservoir operation model integrates hydrological inputs, demand characteristics, operational constraints, and reservoir continuity relationships. Five metaheuristic algorithms Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO), Multi-Objective Ant Colony Optimization (MOACO), and Multi-Objective Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (MOTLBO were comparatively evaluated using Hypervolume (HV), Inverted Generational Distance (IGD), and computational performance indicators. NSGA-III achieved an HV of 0.9234 and an IGD of 0.0338, demonstrating effective convergence and diversity for the evaluated solutions. abstract: प्रस्तुत शोध पत्र का मुख्य उद्देश्य 1920 ई. से 1957 ई. के समयांतराल में जयपुर रियासत के उपाश्रयी ;ैनइंसजमतद / हाशिए पर स्थित) वर्गों की सामाजिक और आर्थिक स्थिति का ऐतिहासिक विश्लेषण करना है। विशेष रूप से मीना जनजाति पर केंद्रित यह अ/ययन उनके पारंपरिक सामाजिक संगठन, प्रशासनिक भूमिकाओं, आर्थिक आधार संरचना तथा औपनिवेशिक व सामंती नीतियों के विनाशकारी प्रभावों को रेखांकित करता है। 1920 के दशक में लागू किए गए दमनकारी ‘जरायम पेशा कानून’ ;ब्तपउपदंस ज्तपइमे ।बजद्ध तथा चौकीदारी प्रथा के सामाजिक-आर्थिक दुष्परिणामों का गहन अ/ययन करते हुए यह पत्र स्वतंत्रता-पश्चात् (1947-1957) हुए सामाजिक सुधार आंदोलनों, पुनर्वास नीतियों, कानून निरसन एवं शैक्षणिक-राजनीतिक चेतना के उद्भव का व्यापक लेखा-जोखा प्रस्तुत करता है। ऐतिहासिक साक्ष्यों और राजस्थान राज्य अभिलेखागार (बीकानेर) के प्रशासनिक रिकॉर्ड्स के विश्लेषणात्मक अ/ययन से यह सिद्ध होता है कि 20वीं सदी के म/य में मीना समुदाय का संघर्ष केवल कानूनी मुक्ति का आंदोलन नहीं था, बल्कि यह औपनिवेशिक-सामंती उत्पीड़न से नागरिक स्वतंत्रता तथा सामाजिक पुनरुत्थान की दिशा में एक युगांतकारी ऐतिहासिक यात्रा थी।

title: Creating satisfaction and loyalty among tourists: the power of experiential tourism
abstract: Abstract The current research examines whether experiential tourism activities in the tourism industry can influence tourists’ behaviour. Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study examines how experience affects travellers’ intentions for satisfaction and loyalty among online travel agents (OTAs). Data were collected from 208 visitors across five travel destinations in India, specifically wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, to examine their lived experiences. The results were analysed using a partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) approach, indicating that experiential tourism indicators have a direct effect on customer engagement. The study suggests that experiential motivation is vital in shaping tourists’ satisfaction and loyalty. The results suggest that tourists are more likely to return to the OTA and recommend it to others if they have positive experiential motivation during their travel encounter. Moreover, the study highlights the importance of co-creation in the tourism industry. In the challenging competitive space, leveraging experiential strategies can help managers gain a competitive advantage. Travel retailers must focus on increasing tourists’ conscious participation and include certain activities that may motivate them and create enthusiasm. This study is one of the few in India to explore the relationship between exp…

title: Cancer therapy-induced intestinal injury: Mechanisms, clinical manifestations, and management strategies
abstract: As cancer treatment advances in recent years, people with cancer are living longer, but the side effects of these treatments on normal tissues remain a major challenge, particularly the intestines. Intestinal injury induced by chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and surgical intervention represents an important factor that limits the effectiveness of cancer treatment. The common symptoms are diarrhea, abdominal pain and malabsorption, which can substantially impair the patients’ quality of life and may lead to severe complications. At present, the clinical strategies for the prevention and treatment of therapy-induced intestinal injury are still relatively scarce. In this minireview, we focus on the mechanisms underlying cancer therapy-induced intestinal injury, including oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and gut microbiota imbalance, and discuss targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at reducing morbidity, improving patient outcomes, and fostering a better quality of life.

title: Analysis of Stock Price Movements of Conglomerate Groups Relative to The Jakarta Composite Index (JCI)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the relationship and influence of stock price changes within conglomerate groups on the movements of the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2019–2025 period. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing secondary data consisting of daily stock price changes and the JCI. The sample was selected using a purposive sampling technique, with the current and former constituents of the Kompas100 Index serving as the screening universe, from which stocks affiliated with conglomerate groups were identified. Based on the research criteria, 18 conglomerate groups comprising 57 companies were selected. The daily stock returns for each company were aggregated by conglomerate group and used as independent variables, while the daily return of the JCI served as the dependent variable. The analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with the assistance of EViews 13. The results indicate that for all annual models throughout the 2019–2025 period, the Prob. (F-statistic) was 0.000, demonstrating that the conglomerate group stock variables are, when taken together, statistically significant in their relationship to changes in the JCI. The Adjusted R² values ​​for each year are 67.30% in 2019, 90.81% in 2020, 76.28% in 2021, 67.33% in 2022, 65.28% in 2023, 76.20% in 2024, and 81.89% in 2025. A pooled regression for the 2…

title: FORECASTING COMPUTING RESOURCE UTILIZATION IN SERVER CLUSTERS USING A LIGHTWEIGHT TRANSFORMER
abstract: The computing resource utilization in server clusters changes dynamically and non-stationarily; thus it is critical to accurately forecast such utilization for effective resource scheduling, auto-scaling, and workload management. Existing forecasting approaches lack abilities to model complex temporal dependencies, while standard Transformers exhibit powerful long-range modeling but incur significant computational and memory overheads. In response, we propose a lightweight Transformer for computing resource utilization forecasting in server clusters. It leverages compact temporal representations and efficient feature interactions to lower computational complexity and enable multi-step forecasts of future resource utilization. We conduct experiments based on real-world server cluster traces, comparing our approach against several representative baselines: LSTM, GRU, DLinear, Transformer, PatchTST, and iTransformer. Both the forecasting accuracy and model efficiency are measured by prediction error, parameter count, computational cost, and inference efficiency respectively. Our result shows that our approach achieves good forecasting performance without significantly increasing computational overhead, which achieves a balanced trade-off between predictive accuracy and model efficiency. Thus, our framework offers an efficient solution for practical resource utilization forecasting…

TRANSMISSION LINE ICE ACCRETION PROBABILITY PREDICTION AND DE-ICING THRESHOLD OPTIMIZATION BASED ON BAYESIAN EXTREME VALUE THEORY AND MONTE CARLO SIMULATION
abstract: Transmission line icing is a rare and severe hazard; therefore, a fixed de-icing threshold cannot account for forecast uncertainty, accumulated long-term risk, and the economic trade-off between de-icing costs and tower collapse losses. Based on 30 years of annual maximum ice-thickness data, real-time weather forecasts and operating cost parameters, this paper builds a probabilistic prediction and de-icing decision model. A generalised extreme value distribution is used to obtain the prior via maximum likelihood estimation, Bayesian updating and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling generate the posterior distribution, a homogeneous Poisson process determines the long-term event frequency, and finally, Bayesian expected loss yields a dynamic de-icing threshold. The fitted GEV parameters are μ=11.95, σ=3.08, ξ=-0.19, and the 50-year and 100-year return levels are 21.5 and 23.9 mm, respectively. Under the given severe-weather condition, the posterior mean is 15.6 mm, and the probability of exceeding 15 mm is 0.84. The probabilities of at least one event within 10, 20, 30 and 50 years are 0.9030, 0.9906, 0.9991 and 0.9999, respectively. The optimal de-icing threshold ranges from 14.2 to 18.6 mm, reducing the expected total cost by about 18.7% compared with a fixed-threshold policy. This report provides verifiable statistical decision support for the construction of a high-probability …

title: The influence of sample size, modelling algorithms, and hyperparameters on bootstrap-based prediction stability in clinical prediction model development: An empirical study using the HOPE dataset
abstract: Abstract Background The stability of clinical prediction models has emerged as an important factor in model development. Models producing unstable or unreliable predictions can ultimately lead to improper clinical decisions and harm patients when applied in clinical practice. Previous studies have highlighted the role of sample size in prediction stability, with larger samples delivering increased stability. However, the role of other modelling decisions remains unclear. This study considered three modifiable factors influencing the stability of predictions: sample size, modelling algorithm (i.e., parametric regression and machine learning algorithms), and hyperparameter tuning. Methods We used the previously published HOPE dataset to develop a prediction model for anxiety at palliative care admission, incorporating 34 candidate predictors. To examine the impact of sample size, we generated seven datasets of varying sizes through random sampling. A total of 21 modelling scenarios were evaluated by combining these datasets with three modelling approaches: LASSO logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost. Models were tuned using cross-validation and assessed for discrimination (AUC) and calibration. Prediction stability was evaluated using a bootstrap-based framework, including the mean absolute prediction error (MAPE) and related instability plots. Results In this clinical …

title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
abstract: Abstract Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through…

Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing
abstract: Abstract Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that OH– forms strong chemical bonds with surface Zr atoms, thereby inducing surface hydroxylation and increasing the diffusion coefficient of Zr atoms. Adsorbed PVP molecules further regulate the softening process and transform the material from a rigid to a softened state. Simulations verify that such softening is essentially a corrosion reaction and predict the corrosion depth and corrosion rate within 60 min. Experiments combining chemical softening and magnetic abrasive finishing (MAF) show that the surface roughness of zirconia specimens decreases from Ra 0.302 to 0.057, and the material removal rate ranges from 2.29 × 10–3 μm/s to 2.93 × 10–3 μm/s. The average error between simulated and measured removal depths is only 17.02%. This composite system enables effective surface softening of zirconia. The simulation can reproduce the experimental trend, providing feasible theoretical support a…

title: FAULT PREDICTION OF FASTENER PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT VIA LIGHTWEIGHT REGRESSION MODELING WITH SCIKIT-LEARN: EVIDENCE FROM THE HAIYAN FASTENER INDUSTRY
abstract: In fastener manufacturing, an unexpected breakdown of a cold heading machine stops the entire production line, yet most small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) still maintain their equipment by rule of thumb. Targeting the SMEs in the Haiyan fastener industry cluster, this paper takes cold heading machines as the object and builds a low-cost equipment fault prediction method based on regression modeling and Scikit-learn. The remaining useful life (RUL) of key components is taken as the prediction target; four models, namely linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting regression tree (GBRT), and support vector regression (SVR), are compared, and grid search is used for parameter tuning. Since such enterprises generally lack usable historical failure data, the method is validated on real degradation data from the public XJTU-SY accelerated life test dataset of rolling bearings, which share the same data form as the key rotating components of cold heading machines. The results show that GBRT performs best (RMSE = 6.25 min, R² = 0.511), that degradation information is concentrated in a few amplitude-type statistical features such as mean amplitude, standard deviation and root mean square, and that in the early-warning replay on two test bearings, alarms are all raised ahead of failure with an average lead time of 8.0 min and no false alarm. abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of price, service quality, promotion, and trust on customers’ decisions to open Hajj savings accounts at Nano Sharia Bank, Jambi Branch, both directly and indirectly through reputation as a mediating variable. In addition, this study examines the influence of each independent variable on the bank’s reputation. This research employs an associative research design with a quantitative approach and a causal nature. Primary data were collected through a questionnaire consisting of 39 research indicators. The determination of sample size followed the minimum requirements for Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis, resulting in 195 respondents as the research sample. The results indicate that, directly, price, promotion, service quality, and reputation do not have a significant effect on customers’ decisions to open Hajj savings accounts. In contrast, trust has a significant effect on customers’ decision-making. Regarding reputation, promotion is found to have a significant influence on shaping the bank’s reputation, while price, trust, and service quality do not show a significant effect. Furthermore, the mediation analysis reveals that reputation does not mediate the effects of price, promotion, trust, and service quality on customers’ decisions to open Hajj savings accounts. title: Epitranscriptomic regulation of the COX-2/PGE2 axis by hnRNPA2B1 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression
abstract: BACKGROUND Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a highly lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic options. Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is frequently overexpressed in ESCC, yet the mechanisms leading to its dysregulation remain poorly understood. Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A2/B1 (hnRNPA2B1), an oncogenic N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, has been implicated in various cancers, but its role in regulating COX-2 expression and promoting ESCC progression has not been defined. AIM To investigate how hnRNPA2B1 promotes ESCC progression through COX-2 regulation. METHODS Expression of hnRNPA2B1 and COX-2 was analyzed in ESCC tissues and cell lines by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Stable hnRNPA2B1 knockdown and overexpression models were established to assess cellular proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth. Bulk RNA-seq, m6A RNA immunoprecipitation-qPCR and RNA immunoprecipitation-qPCR, and actinomycin D assays were used to delineate post-transcriptional regulation of COX-2. Functional and therapeutic relevance of the hnRNPA2B1-COX-2/prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) axis was evaluated using PGE2 supplementation and celecoxib treatment in vitro and in vivo . title: Sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules for the directed biosynthesis of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid in Escherichia coli
abstract: Abstract Bioconversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) confers advantages of mild conditions, high selectivity, and eco-friendliness. However, enzymatic catalysis is expensive and multi-strain microbial catalysis is limited by the transmembrane transport of intermediates between strains, restricting the efficient synthesis of FDCA and generating a byproduct. In this study, we aimed to establish sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules in Escherichia coli to precisely control the expression of hydroxymethylfurfural oxidase (HMFO) and vanillin dehydrogenase (VDH1), enabling the directed one-pot conversion of HMF to FDCA with no detectable accumulation of the measured intermediates and simplifying the operational process. At a 15 mM HMF scale, this strategy achieved a FDCA yield of 100%, significantly higher than the 78.6% yield of the dual-enzyme cascade system established by HMFO and VDH1, and the 56.73% yield from the dual-strain catalysis constructed by two engineered E. coli strains that harbor either hmfo or vdh 1(Student’s t -test, p < 0.0001). Furthermore, at a laboratory scale (production of a fermentation broth containing 100 g of FDCA), life cycle assessment demonstrated sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules represented the lowest environmental impact among the three systems (dual-strain catalysis and dual-enzyme ca…

Tunable Optical-to-THz Frequency Conversion Driven by Localized Surface Phonon Polaritons in LiNbO3 Metasurfaces
abstract: Abstract We demonstrate tunable THz generation by optical rectification in LiNbO3 rod metasurfaces supporting localized surface phonon polaritons (LSPhPs). By varying the rod length, the LSPhP resonance is tuned across the 4–5 THz range, producing a systematic red-shift of the generated THz spectral peak. THz time-domain spectroscopy and numerical calculations show that the emitted spectrum is governed by the geometry-dependent LSPhP response. Although the total far-field emission remains lower than that of the unpatterned film, numerical calculations show that the metasurfaces enhance the volume-averaged mean-square nonlinear current density and strongly localize the generated THz field near the rods. These results establish phonon-polaritonic metasurfaces as compact platforms for spectrally tailoring optical-to-THz conversion and enhancing localized THz fields.

title: Unraveling the Anti-HCV Mechanism of the Ethyl Acetate Fraction of Vitex cofassus via Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
abstract: To address the growing health burden posed by the hepatitis C virus (HCV), the present study employed computational approach to predict the medicinal properties of Vitex cofassus. Liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) analysis of its ethyl acetate leaf fraction identified 37 drug-like compounds. Network pharmacology predicted 201 biological targets, with key proteins such as STAT3, IL6, SRC, AKT1, EGFR, HSP90AA1, and TNF-α being central to the proposed mechanism of action. Functional enrichment analyses pointed to involvement in chemical response, intracellular signaling, stress, and regulated cell death, with molecular functions linked to kinase activity and ATP binding. KEGG analysis further associates targets with key pathways in cancer, viral infection, and metabolic disease. Picrocrocin and flavonoids such as isorhamnetin and apigenin were predicted as potential inhibitors of HCV-related proteins (STAT3 and SRC, respectively). While these in silico findings provide a rational basis for further investigation, the present findings remain predictive and require experimental validation to confirm actual anti-HCV efficacy.

title: BIOFLEXSHIRT: A SMA-DRIVEN SHOULDER EXOSKELETON AND ITS ASSISTED MOTION MECHANISM STUDY
abstract: Loss of shoulder mobility severely impairs upper limb function and reduces quality of life. Here we present BioFlexShirt, a wearable soft exoskeleton driven by shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators, designed to assist shoulder movements across three degrees of freedom. Inspired by the anatomy of major shoulder muscles, BioFlexShirt integrates bionic actuator alignment, a displacement amplification mechanism, and fabric-based modular design to enhance anatomical conformity and assistive performance. A coupled kinematic model was developed based on an ellipsoidal thorax approximation, while dynamic simulations using OpenSim confirmed consistency with natural shoulder–humeral rhythms. Vicon motion capture experiments revealed significant improvements in joint displacement and coordination at the GH, AC, ST, and SA landmarks. All root mean square errors remained below 5 mm, validating the system’s spatial alignment and assistive fidelity. This study demonstrates a viable pathway for SMA-based wearable exoskeletons in rehabilitation, enabling anatomically aligned, lightweight, and efficient upper limb assistance.

AN INTRA-DAY AND DAILY ROLLING ECONOMIC DISPATCHING MODEL FOR ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS IN INDUSTRIAL PARK MICROGRIDS
abstract: Aiming at the electricity-purchase-cost optimization demand of park microgrids equipped with distributed photovoltaics, two sets of energy-storage dispatching models are established for intra-day deterministic dispatching and long-term day-by-day rolling optimization. With the objective of minimizing daily total electricity-purchase cost, the intra-day dispatching model considers power balance, energy-storage charge-discharge power, capacity limits and daily cyclic constraints. Linear programming is adopted to solve electricity-purchase and energy-storage operation strategies under 10-minute time granularity, followed by feasibility verification and sensitivity analysis of key parameters. For long-term rolling dispatching, load forecasting is realized via historical same-week load weighting and deviation damping correction. A safety margin for planned electricity purchase and high-price emergency purchase penalty mechanism are introduced to realize annual-scale optimal operation of microgrid energy storage. Numerical results prove that energy-storage greatly cuts microgrid electricity-purchase expenditure. Charge-discharge efficiency dominates dispatching performance, and a 3% reserved ratio for planned purchase balances economic cost and power shortage risk. This work provides theoretical support for practical engineering dispatching of park-microgrid energy storage.

title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
abstract: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

Energysheds and the Urban Energy Transition: A Method for Assessing Spatial Imbalances in Energy Flow
abstract: Abstract Urban areas are facing the challenges of transitioning toward a low-carbon society as a response to climate change. However, the benefits and burdens of this energy transition are not evenly distributed across cities. To address this disparity, the concept of energy justice has emerged. The issue of urban energy justice can be understood as a manifestation of geographical energy disparities where energy-consuming regions enjoy significant benefits, while energy producing regions suffer from externalities. In this paper, we propose a method that utilizes the notion of “energyshed” to align city energy consumption with power plant energy generation, addressing geographical energy (im)balances. The proposed method maps the spatial supply–demand relationships between regions and power plants without relying on proprietary algorithms or territory-specific cutoff distances. Although spatial imbalance alone does not establish energy injustice, the resulting energysheds provide a diagnostic basis for identifying energy-generating regions that bear disproportionate burdens and for informing a fairer allocation of resources during the energy transition.

Education for a Changing World: Liberal Arts Education and the Case for Structural Integration
abstract: Schools are being asked to prepare young people for economies, technologies and civic conditions that nobody can describe with confidence. Estimates of how automation and generative artificial intelligence will alter work differ widely, yet most of them point in one direction: tasks built on routine procedure are the easiest to hand over to machines, while tasks that call for judgement, explanation and cooperation with others are gaining value. This conceptual paper asks what kind of education answers that situation, and it argues that the long tradition of liberal education offers a better starting point than the narrow, examination-driven specialisation that still governs much schooling in India and elsewhere. The paper first reviews labour-market and policy evidence on the changing demand for skills, drawing on Autor, Levy and Murnane, on Deming, and on Eloundou and colleagues, along with the framing documents of UNESCO and the OECD. It then traces the idea of liberal education from the classical artes liberales, through Newman and Dewey, to Nussbaum's account of democratic citizenship, and sets this history alongside the Indian precedents recognised in the National Education Policy 2020. A review of empirical studies follows. Research from the Wabash National Study and related work links particular liberal arts experiences, such as clear teaching, sustained discussion and f…

title: QR CODE MENU DESIGN AND CUSTOMER SATISFACTION IN MALAYSIAN CASUAL DINING RESTAURANTS
abstract: QR code menus are now standard in Malaysian casual dining, yet little is known about which mobile interface features are associated with diner satisfaction. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model and Menu Engineering principles, this study examines whether digital presentation, strategic item placement and visual digital prompts predict customer satisfaction in independent casual dining restaurants. A cross-sectional online survey was administered to casual dining patrons in Penang, recruited by purposive screening followed by snowball referral and required to have used a QR code menu within the preceding six months; 248 usable responses were retained. Constructs were measured on six-point Likert scales (α = .843 to .867) and analysed by multiple linear regression. The three predictors jointly explained 85.0% of the variance in customer satisfaction, R² = .850, adjusted R² = .849, F(3, 244) = 462.428, p < .001, and each was a significant positive predictor: visual digital prompts, β = .474; strategic item placement, β = .310; digital presentation, β = .178. However, the attributes proved not to be empirically separable: no construct met the Fornell-Larcker criterion, the collinearity condition index reached 37.144, and 92.5% of explained variance was shared rather than unique. Relative weights analysis accordingly returned near-equal contributions of 31.5%, 32.5% and 35.9%.…

title: Towards a competence-behaviour-design alignment for educational robotics kits: a theoretical synthesis and development principles
abstract: Abstract Educational robotics kits (ERKs) are widely used to support competence-oriented technology education, yet their design is rarely grounded in clearly prioritised technological competences and associated learning behaviours. This research, situated in China’s General Technology curriculum, addresses this gap by developing a competence-behaviour-design (C-B-D) alignment for ERKs. The research problem concerns what consistent priority competences and their operationalised learning behaviours are required to guide ERK design. A two-phase mixed-methods approach was adopted. Study 1 used a Delphi-Analytic Hierarchy Process with experienced teachers to prioritise curriculum-defined competences. Materialisation capacity and engineering thinking emerged as highest priorities; within materialisation capacity, ‘knowledge and selection of materials and tools’ and ‘making and processing capability’ were rated equally important, while ‘systems analysis thinking’ was the dominant indicator for engineering thinking. Study 2 undertook document- and artefact-based analysis to identify operationalised learning behaviours corresponding to these competences. Results show that materialisation capacity is predominantly enacted through component selection, modular assembly and basic structural testing, whereas engineering thinking is mainly elicited through functional evaluation, system-level …

De Novo Design of Catalytically Active Salen-Binding Proteins
abstract: Abstract De novo design of catalytic metalloproteins has the potential to generate enzymes that combine the efficiency of natural proteins with the reactivity of synthetic organometallic catalysts. Here, we develop a computational strategy to design enzymes with novel tertiary structures that bind metal salen complexes, classic small-molecule catalysts not found in biology. Six proteins were designed and screened for function; five of six express well, bind a Co-salen cofactor, and catalyze a transition metal hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)-mediated deallylation reaction, representing the first de novo proteins to catalyze this class of transformation. The spectroscopic properties and crystal structure of the most active sequence were in excellent agreement with the design, and the holoprotein retained its structure and activity over a broad range of pH (2–12), temperatures up to 95 °C, and aqueous/organic solvent mixtures. We suggest that the combinatorial space provided by metal ion identity, ligand substitution, and active site structure can be used to generate artificial metalloenzymes that catalyze many chemical transformations.

Solid Lipid Nanoparticles as Delivery Systems for Plant-Derived Phytochemicals in Cancer Therapy: A Systematic Review
abstract: Solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) have been investigated as lipid-based delivery systems to improve the solubility, stability, bioavailability, and delivery of plant-derived phytochemicals to tumors for cancer therapy. However, the available evidence remains heterogeneous and predominantly preclinical. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the formulation strategies, physicochemical characteristics, and therapeutic applications of phytochemical-loaded SLNs in cancer therapy. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Original research articles in English investigating phytochemical-loaded SLNs for cancer therapy were included. Data on formulation composition, preparation methods, physicochemical properties, drug release, in vitro anticancer activity, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and in vivo antitumor efficacy were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE tool for animal studies and an adapted checklist for in vitro studies. Thirty one articles were included in the qualitative synthesis. Most SLNs had particle sizes in the nanoscale range, approximately 50-350 nm, with encapsulation efficiencies of 43-99% and sustained-release profiles. Encapsulation generally improved cellular uptake and in vitro cytotoxicity in several cancer models. However, evidence of improved bioavailability, active tumor targeting, and in vivo antitumor efficacy remained limited …

title: Glycolate oxidase contributes to autophagy-associated antiviral defense against citrus leaf blotch virus
abstract: Abstract Background Kiwifruit is a high-value fruit crop but is increasingly challenged by viral diseases. Citrus leaf blotch virus (CLBV), an important viral pathogen of kiwifruit, causes vein clearing and chlorotic symptoms in leaves, severely impairing kiwifruit yield and fruit quality. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are recognized as pivotal signals in plant antiviral defense, yet the downstream pathway by which virus-induced H₂O₂ accumulation restricts viral infection remains largely unclear. Results Glycolate oxidase (GOX) expression is positively associated with H₂O₂ accumulation and autophagic activity, but negatively associated with CLBV accumulation. CLBV infection in Nicotiana benthamiana was associated with elevated H₂O₂ accumulation and marked upregulation of GOX, a key peroxisomal enzyme responsible for H₂O₂ production. GOX-mediated H₂O₂ accumulation functions as an antiviral barrier against CLBV, as NbGOX silencing enhanced viral infection and kiwi ( Actinidia chinensis ) AcGOX5 overexpression reduced viral accumulation. Further analyses revealed that among the domains in CLBV replicase, the expression of PRO and OTu domains promote H₂O₂ accumulation. Mechanistically, GOX contributes to CLBV restriction and is associated with enhanced autophagic activity and reduced accumulation of the viral movement protein. Conclusions Together, these findings reveal a mechanist…

The effects of virtual reality on learning outcomes in health professions education: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly integrated into health professions education to address limitations of traditional instructional formats. However, whether VR delivers consistent advantages across different educational constructs remains variable. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of VR-based interventions on objectively assessed learning outcomes compared with traditional instructional methods across health professions curricula. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ERIC, and Cochrane Central from inception through August 28, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing VR with traditional teaching methods. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) were calculated using Hedges’ g via DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models, with outcomes categorized into cognitive/knowledge and procedural/technical domains. Between-study heterogeneity was quantified using the I 2 statistic, and 95% prediction intervals were computed. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane RoB 2, and evidence certainty was graded using the GRADE framework. Results Twenty-three randomized controlled trials (24 independent datasets, 1,202 participants) were included. title: Community Participation in Various Stages of Non-Timber Forest Product Management in the Community Forestry Scheme in Indonesia
abstract: Community participation is a key component of sustainable forest management, particularly in social forestry schemes that utilize non-timber forest products (NTFP). However, empirical evidence on how participation varies across specific operational stages of NTFP management remains limited, especially in Indonesian Community Forest settings. Examining participation at different stages is important because involvement in nursery, planting, maintenance, and harvesting may reflect distinct responsibilities, incentives, and benefit-sharing arrangements. This study therefore aimed to analyze community participation across four operational stages of NTFP management in the Tebing Siring Community Forest, Tanah Laut Regency, South Kalimantan. A descriptive quantitative case-study design was applied to 20 purposively selected members from a population of 65 group members. Participants were selected based on their involvement in NTFP management activities and availability during data collection. Participation was assessed using a four-point ordinal rating scale, with higher scores indicating greater participation. Descriptive analysis showed mean scores of 3.20 for nursery, 2.95 for planting, 2.70 for maintenance, and 2.65 for harvesting. These results suggest greater participation in the first stages and less in maintenance and harvesting. However, the Friedman test found no statistical…

Electric Field Catalysis and the Metabolic Origin of Life
abstract: Abstract Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes. We first overview types of positive feedback relevant to the early evolution of metabolism, the theory of electric field catalysis, and its dominant role in enzyme catalysis. We then examine recent experiments and calculations highlighting the ability of external electric fields to enable nonenzymatic analogues of challenging metabolic reactions in micro- to millisecond reaction times. An underexplored mode of small molecule catalysis (reorientation catalysis) that can only operate in external electric fields is proposed to make positive feedback within prebiotic reaction networks more achievable. By embodying electrostatic catalysis, compartmentalization, and ion concentration gradients, charged aqueous interfaces prepattern three fundamental features of biology, making them a preferred environment for a metabolic origin of life. Computational Compound Prioritization Strategy Incorporating Docking Variability and Interaction Energies Identifies Putative LRH-1 Binders
abstract: Abstract Compound ranking in structure-based computer-aided drug discovery notoriously yields highly ranked false positives due to sampling and, more frequently, scoring errors. We developed a compound prioritization strategy that utilizes sampled docked poses from complementary docking approaches, i.e., targeted physics-based docking and blind docking with a generative model, into multiple conformations of the target protein to train two multilayer perceptron (MLP) models. The MLPs predict binders or activators at the orthosteric ligand-binding pocket of the nuclear receptor Liver Receptor Homologue-1 (LRH-1, NR5A2). Our approach circumvents the reliance on a single docked pose for scoring compounds or individual scoring metrics for compound ranking. In an out-of-distribution compound set, we observed that the MLPs identified compounds that are chemically dissimilar from those in the training set and are sensitive to single scaffold modifications, making the MLPs potential tools for lead optimization. We applied the MLPs on a pilot study prospective drug discovery campaign, which resulted in the identification of four putative LRH-1 binders. We found that a combination of scoring and prediction metrics enriches for hit compounds across library sizes. In all, this work presents a method to leverage structural and experimental data to aid drug discovery for a challenging protein…

title: Human Resource Accounting Information and Investment Evaluation: Evidence from Individual Retail Investors in Karnataka
abstract: Human Resource Accounting Information (HRAI) gives details about an organisation’s human resources and can provide investors with additional information for evaluating investment opportunities. However, its effective use is influenced by investors’ level of knowledge, their perception of its relevance and the ease with which the information can be accessed, understood and evaluated. The present study examines the knowledge, perceived usefulness and hindrances associated with HRAI among NSE-registered individual retail investors in Karnataka. A quantitative descriptive research design was adopted, and data were collected from 287 individual retail investors using a structured questionnaire administered through both online and offline modes. The HRAI items were classified into five dimensions through Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), namely HR Valuation, HR Composition, HR Performance, Employee Benefits and Employee Governance. The responses were analysed using descriptive statistics and one-sample t-tests. The results indicate that investors have a low level of knowledge across all five dimensions, with the mean scores of the individual knowledge items falling below the scale average. In contrast, respondents expressed a high level of perceived usefulness of HRAI for investment evaluation, with mean scores ranging from 4.33 to 4.41. HRAI was particularly perceived as useful for…

abstract: Public descriptions of digital transformation often reveal customer interfaces more readily than the systems connecting them to production and distribution. This paper develops the Digital Manufacturing-to-Market Ecosystem (DM2ME), a six-domain architecture for examining those connections while recording capability maturity separately from the evidence supporting it. A bounded documentary application to Pak Elektron Limited distinguishes corporate infrastructure from its Appliances and Power businesses. The 2025 annual report describes current enterprise resource planning (ERP) integration, manufacturing information systems, reporting tools and technology governance; these disclosures support corporate-level classifications that cannot be inferred from customer-facing websites alone. Appliances provides observable retail and service interfaces, while Power has a reported digital transformer lifecycle initiative. Dealer integration, division-specific system coverage, predictive-model use and adaptive feedback remain only partly observable. Classifications represent the highest level supported by the available documents, rather than estimates of the firm's actual capability ceiling. The contribution is a transparent procedure for stating what an external assessment can establish, how business-unit scope affects inference, and which evidence would justify a stronger claim. Projected changes in precipitation and temperature over the KKSD river basin using a machine-learning-based selective CMIP6 multimodel ensemble
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable climate projections are essential for climate-risk assessment and planning. Yet, uncertainty in Global Climate Models (GCMs) and ensemble construction remains a major challenge. This study developed a machine learning-based selective multimodel ensemble framework to project precipitation, maximum temperature (Tmax), and minimum temperature (Tmin) over the Kangsabati, Keliaghai, Silabati, and Dwarkeswar (KKSD) river basin in eastern India. India Meteorological Department gridded observations were combined with statistically downscaled and bias-corrected NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 simulations. Multiple machine-learning algorithms were evaluated, and Extra Trees was adopted because of its strong predictive performance. A parsimonious four-GCM subset was evaluated against conventional multimodel approaches. Future projections for 2025–2098 under different SSP indicate an overall decline in annual precipitation, ranging from approximately −2.45% to −9.16% relative to 1991–2014, along with strong seasonal redistribution characterised by increased winter precipitation and persistent reductions in monsoon precipitation. Annual Tmax increases from approximately 0.39–0.44 °C in 2025–2039 to 1.53, 2.16, and 2.98 °C in 2085–2098 under SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5, respectively, while corresponding Tmin increases reach 1.40, 1.85, and 2.32 °C. The proposed framework therefore prov…
