THE NEW KITCHEN CLASSROOM: ASSESSING BLENDED LEARNING ACCEPTANCE IN CULINARY ARTS EDUCATION
abstract: Blended learning is a pedagogy that combines practical, hands-on, and online learning and is gaining popularity in TVET education because it offers flexible learning, enhances practical training by integrating theoretical concepts through online classes, and helps build technical and digital workplace skills among TVET graduates. However, the success of this pedagogical integration relies on students' acceptance. In blended learning, a lack of acceptance can reduce learning engagement, academic performance, motivation, and satisfaction, which can widen learning gaps. This research investigates factors such as learning flexibility, openness to new technology, attitude towards online learning, and basic technological skills on students' willingness to adopt blended learning in culinary arts education. A quantitative survey was administered to 253 diploma and degree culinary arts students at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) campuses across Malaysia. SPSS version 29 was used to conduct a hierarchical regression analysis to identify the significant factors that explain students’ acceptance of blended learning. The findings reveal that factors such as openness to new technology play a dominant role in students' acceptance of blended learning. Attitude and basic technological skills are also highly correlated, indicating that students with a positive attitude toward blended learning a…

title: KOMIK DIGITAL DENGAN MODEL PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN LITERASI VISUAL DAN BERPIKIR KREATIF SISWA KELAS VIII
abstract: ABSTRACT Informatics learning, particularly in the topics of functions and data structures, requires instructional strategies that help students understand visual representations while developing creative approaches to problem-solving. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of digital comics integrated with the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model in improving the visual literacy and creative thinking skills of eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 61 Surabaya. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design was employed, involving 60 students divided equally into an experimental class and a control class, with 30 students in each group. The experimental class learned through PBL-based digital comics, whereas the control class received conventional instruction. Data were collected through pretests and posttests and analyzed using descriptive statistics, normality and homogeneity tests, paired-samples t-tests, and independent-samples t-tests. The experimental class’s mean visual literacy score increased from 56.67 to 80.93, while its mean creative thinking score rose from 52.07 to 79.67. Between-group tests revealed significant posttest differences in visual literacy (t = 10.231, p < .001) and creative thinking (t = 7.736, p < .001). These findings support the use of PBL-based digital comics as an alternative for Informatics instruction to facilitate visual understan…

DEEP LEARNING BASED DETECTION OF ANOMALOUS INVENTORY FLUCTUATIONS IN INDUSTRIAL SUPPLY CHAINS
abstract: Fluctuations in inventories across industrial supply chains are caused by interplay between demand, ordering, replenishment, and production which makes it challenging to detect anomalies with just one threshold or simple distributional rules. In this paper we introduce an anomaly detection approach based on four synchronized time series (inventory, demand, ordering, and replenishment). Our model captures normal operating patterns through sliding windows and computes the difference between actual and estimated inventory level as an anomaly score. We tested our model over a 240-step simulated sequence including sudden inventory drops and persistent inventory surpluses; for this sequence the multivariate model obtained an F1 score of 0.897 and an AUC of 0.951, surpassing Isolation Forest, LSTM, GRU, and baseline Transformer models. Detected anomalies matched the injected anomaly events. Results indicate potential use of multivariate time-series modeling for inventory anomaly screening, however, further validation is needed on real-world enterprise data.

title: IMPROVING EFL STUDENTS' WRITING SKILLS THROUGH DIGITAL LEARNING PLATFORMS
abstract: Writing is a complex skill for EFL (English as a Foreign Language) learners because it involves grammatical competence, vocabulary knowledge, idea organization, and the ability to convey meaning coherently. Technological developments have introduced various digital platforms that can support writing instruction, particularly through collaborative features, feedback, and assessment tools. This article aims to examine the roles and uses of digital learning platforms in EFL writing instruction based on previous research. This study employed a literature review method involving 15 scholarly publications published between 2021 and 2025. The data were analyzed thematically by categorizing the findings according to the functions of technology in writing instruction. The review identified three major themes. First, Google Docs supports collaborative writing through shared text production and editing, interaction among learners, and engagement in the writing process. Second, artificial intelligence-based technologies, particularly ChatGPT, provide alternative sources of feedback and support for writing revision, although the accuracy and relevance of their outputs still require evaluation and teacher guidance. Third, AI-based tools can serve as additional resources for writing assessment; however, differences between human and AI scoring indicate that automated assessment cannot fully r…

title: Trichrome-based deep learning for quantitative assessment of steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
abstract: Abstract Aims: This study aimed to develop and evaluate Tri-MASH, a trichrome-based deep learning model for quantitative assessment of steatosis, classic hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis, and to explore their spatial relationships. Inflammatory-cell density was evaluated as an exploratory measure. Methods and results: Tri-MASH was trained using 161 training specimens and internally evaluated on 30 randomly selected, nonoverlapping specimens. External evaluation comprised 39 biopsies independently scored by four pathologists and 524 baseline and week-72 biopsies from 262 clinical-trial participants. Internal-validation F1 scores ranged from 78.9% for inflammatory-cell detection to 99.2% for sinusoidal fibrosis. In cohort 1, associations with median pathologist assessments were very strong for steatosis (Rs = 0.85) and fibrosis (Rs = 0.87–0.88) and moderate for ballooning (Rs = 0.55). In cohort 2, exploratory pooled analyses showed moderate associations for steatosis (Rs = 0.52), ballooning (Rs = 0.54), and total and portal-septal fibrosis (Rs = 0.50); confidence intervals and p values were unadjusted for repeated observations within participants. Inflammatory-cell density correlated poorly with lobular inflammation grade (Rs=-0.01 to 0.14). title: EMBEDDING SDG 12 THROUGH COMPETITION-BASED LEARNING IN VOCATIONAL CULINARY EDUCATION FOR PASTRY STUDENTS
abstract: This paper presents a qualitative case study of how a Diploma in Pastry Arts program operationalises United Nations Sustainable Development Goal SDG 12 through a structured, plant-based competition cooking initiative called the Plant-to-Plate Challenge. Embedded within the “Essential Cookery Skills” course at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Cawangan Pulau Pinang, the initiative unfolds across three progressive stages: plant-based component development, full plant-based meal design, and a judged team competition, followed by digital e-portfolio documentation. Drawing on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) competency frameworks and the literature on competition-based learning and reflective e-portfolios, this paper analyses the pedagogical design and implementation. Respondents were semester one students (n=32) of the March 2026 cohort. As a single-semester, non-comparative case, the findings indicate that the competition format generated short-term but meaningful gains in student engagement, technical problem-solving and understanding of ingredient substitution, while the e-portfolio provided visually mediated documentation of sustainability practice. The paper argues that pastry arts education, historically anchored in animal-derived and refined ingredients and under-represented in sustainability scholarship, can meaningfully advance SDG 12 competencies when experienti…

title: Transforming AI chatbots into metacognitive partners: Culturally grounded mathematics learning in LMS-based environments
abstract: The utilization of AI chatbots in mathematics education is on the rise, with these bots often serving as the primary providers of answers, potentially limiting learners’ engagement in reflective and metacognitive reasoning processes. The present study examines how AI chatbots can function as metacognitive partners within a culturally contextualized mathematics learning framework implemented through a learning management system (LMS). Using an embedded multiple-case study design, the data were collected from 33 preservice teachers enrolled in the Department of Mathematics Education during their seventh semester. The data were collected from several sources: chatbot interaction logs, participatory observations, metacognitive reflective journals, and semi-structured interviews. Four participants were purposively selected for in-depth analysis. Thematic analysis revealed two distinct patterns in the interaction of pre-service mathematics teachers with the AI chatbot when completing assignments: an iterative interaction pattern and a linear interaction pattern. The iterative pattern involves repeated exploration, whereas the linear pattern follows a straightforward path with minimal verification. The two patterns yield different metacognitive outcomes, depending on the degree of regulation. When iterative interaction is well regulated, it fosters metacognitive success; however, when…

title: Reduced attenuation of neural activation during fear extinction learning in patients with anxiety disorders: a delayed fear extinction fMRI study
abstract: Abstract Clarifying the patterns of neural activation during fear extinction in anxiety disorders (ADs) is essential for advancing our understanding of inhibitory learning. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly characterized in large, heterogeneous cohorts of patients. Utilizing a delayed fear extinction fMRI paradigm, this study examined neural responses in 280 patients with ADs — comprising panic disorder, agoraphobia, panic disorder with agoraphobia, social anxiety disorder, and multiple specific phobias — compared to 103 healthy controls (HC). The attenuation of neural activation to conditioned fear (CS+) and safety (CS−) stimuli from early versus late extinction was compared between groups. Subjective ratings of US-expectancy, arousal, and valence were also collected. In a whole-brain voxelwise analysis, patients showed significantly reduced attenuation of neural activation across both CS+ and CS− relative to HC from early compared to late phases of extinction learning. This pattern was observed in a broad network, encompassing the insular cortex (IC) and bilateral supplementary motor area (SMA), among other regions. No interaction between group and stimulus type was observed. Region-of-interest analysis of the left anterior insular cortex confirmed that reduced attenuation in this region represents a robust neural signature of altered extinction learning in ADs…

title: Professional Competence of Madrasah Teachers in the Digital Era: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Develop Islamic Learning Media at MTs Miftahul Jannah
abstract: The development of digital technology, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), requires madrasah teachers to have adaptive professional competence in developing contextual learning media that embody Islamic values. Teachers at MTs Miftahul Jannah still face limitations in digital literacy, understanding of how to use AI, and skills in designing innovative learning media. This community service program aims to describe the process and outcomes of strengthening teachers’ professional competence through training and mentoring in the use of AI to develop Islamic learning media. The activity used a descriptive qualitative approach with a participatory method involving 20 teachers. The implementation stages included observation and needs analysis, training, hands-on media development practice, mentoring, and reflection. Data were collected through observation, interviews, documentation, and analysis of media products, then analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with source and technique triangulation to ensure data validity. The results show changes in three aspects: improved teacher understanding of the wise and ethical use of AI, growing skills and confidence in designing learning media, and the creation of Islamic learning media products that are ready for classroom use. These findings indicate that training based on hands-on practice and continu…

title: Implementing Cooperative Learning to Enhance Fifth-Grade Students’ Science Learning Outcomes: A Classroom Action Research Study
abstract: This study aimed to describe the implementation of the cooperative learning model, students’ learning activities, science learning outcomes, and the challenges encountered, together with the efforts made to address them, in Grade V at UPTD SD Inpres Lasiana, Kupang City. This study employed Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles, each consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 30 fifth-grade students, comprising 17 boys and 13 girls. Data were collected through classroom observations and written tests. The observational data were used to examine students’ learning activities and the teacher’s classroom management, while the written tests measured students’ learning outcomes. The findings revealed an improvement in students’ learning outcomes following the implementation of cooperative learning. The proportion of students achieving the minimum mastery criterion increased from 50% in Cycle I to 90% in Cycle II, representing a 40-percentage-point improvement. Student participation was also reflected in increased engagement in observation, experimentation, and group work, with the frequency of these activities rising from 23 occurrences in Cycle I to 30 in Cycle II. Nevertheless, the implementation initially encountered challenges related to student participation, group collaboration, and classroom management. These challeng…

title: Akses Green Finance bagi UMKM di Indonesia: Hambatan Struktural, Kesesuaian Instrumen, dan Strategi Penguatan melalui Narrative Literature Review
abstract: Aims: This study aims to analyze access to green finance among micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia by identifying structural barriers, enabling factors, and the suitability of green financing instruments for MSMEs’ characteristics and stages of green practice adoption. It also develops a conceptual framework to explain the interaction between MSMEs’ internal readiness, financial institutions’ assessment mechanisms, and policy ecosystem support in expanding access to green finance. Method: This study employs a narrative literature review approach. Relevant literature was retrieved through Google Scholar and GARUDA, while publication metadata were cross-checked through Crossref. A critical thematic analysis was conducted on relevant scholarly articles, regulations, and institutional reports to identify recurring barriers, evaluate the suitability of financing instruments, and synthesize strategies for strengthening MSMEs’ access to green finance in Indonesia. Results: The findings indicate that barriers to green finance access emerge from the interaction of three dimensions. First, the internal MSME dimension includes limited financial and environmental literacy, inadequate financial record-keeping, administrative constraints, and limited capacity to bear the upfront costs of green investment. Second, the financial institution dimension involves collat…

title: Machine Learning-Based Screening and Rationalization for Aromatic Guest Inclusion into MOF Crystals
abstract: Abstract The exploration of metal–organic framework (MOF) properties arising from guest inclusion, particularly for less-volatile molecules incorporated through solution processes, remains time-consuming and data-intensive compared with framework synthesis, leaving much of the existing MOF library unexplored. We report a machine-learning (ML)-based guest screening approach that predicts favorable guests from a library of ∼19,000 aromatic compounds, trained on 42 inclusion experiments for a single MOF. The ML model, constructed using relevant molecular features extracted from feature sets, predicts guest inclusion amounts across low to high values, with performance superior to models containing irrelevant features. The predictions successfully identify suitable guests that can be accommodated through soaking, enabling selective inclusion from mixed solutions and facilitating crystalline sponge analysis. In the absence of inclusion crystal structures, extensive structural search calculations using a neural network potential provide insights into guest alignment and noncovalent interactions, complementing the ML outcomes. This approach substantially reduces the experimental time and cost required to explore guest-inclusion-based MOF properties.

title: Structured Exponentiation Dot Product Attention-based Vision Transformer with Coordinated FuseNet Transfer Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: The number and intensity of cyberattacks have grown exponentially with the explosive growth of cloud computing,Internet of Things (IoT), and high-speed networks. According to recent reports, more than 70% of the contemporary networks intrusions are either stealthy or low-rate intrusions, which are proven to be hard to detect with the traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs). Despite their extensive implementations in signature-based and rule-based IDS, these methods have weaknesses in terms of being slow to adapt to zero-day attacks, a high number of false alarms, and a lack of scalability when dealing with vast data volumes and high-dimensional network traffic data. To overcome these issues, this research proposes a Structured Exponentiation Dot product-based Network Intrusion Detection System (SED-NIDS) to facilitate the determination of accurate and robust cyberattacks. The proposed system is end-to-end, unlike single-model IDS methods, which perform feature learning and decision fusion independently, leading to better generalization of the system to various attack scenarios. The proposed SEDNIDS achieves an accuracy of 98.6%, 93% precision, 94% recall, and an F1-score of 93.5%. abstract: Abstract Purpose We retrospectively compared 2 strategies for adalimumab biosimilar conversion at an academic medical center to better understand the effects of each strategy. Methods The formulary for our institution is managed by physician- and pharmacist-led task forces, in collaboration with our specialty pharmacy and pharmacy benefit manager. We implemented 2 phased strategies to increase adalimumab biosimilar utilization. First, we added preferred biosimilars to the formulary at parity to reference product and relied on prescribers to promote conversion. Second, we added an interchangeable biosimilar and removed reference product from the formulary while leveraging specialty pharmacy workflows for prescription conversions, streamlined facility inventory, and minimized dependence on prescriber workflows. For both strategies, we evaluated prescribing trends, dispensing data, and pharmaceutical spend for all medical center patients, specialty pharmacy patients, and patients with the top 3 specialty pharmacy payers. Results During phase 1 (quarter [Q] 2 of 2023 [2Q23] to 1Q24), reference product dispensing remained largely unchanged (<5% reduction). title: Fostering equitable access to palliative care for people experiencing homelessness and serious illness: a multi-method, citizen science study using a theory of change approach
abstract: Abstract Background In Germany, there are currently over 531,000 people experiencing homelessness (PEH), with a high burden of physical illness, mental illness and substance use, often occurring simultaneously as trimorbidity. PEH face substantial barriers to healthcare and frequently access palliative care (PC) late or not at all. These challenges require approaches that account for complex health and social needs and fragmented care structures. However, co-produced, practice-ready, and transferable approaches remain rare. This study aims to identify current issues and needs in PC provision for PEH in Münster, Germany and to develop a Theory of Change (ToC) to inform future improvements in care. Methods This is an investigator-initiated, multi-method study conducted in Germany. Citizen Scientists and frontline staff co-designed the study, co-facilitated the empirical research and joined analysis and workshops. Association of pre-transplant right ventricular function parameters with long-term cardiovascular outcomes following kidney transplantation
abstract: Abstract The hemodynamic effects of end-stage kidney disease and associated pulmonary hypertension may impair right ventricular (RV) function and influence cardiovascular (CV) outcomes after kidney transplantation (KT). We aimed to evaluate the association between pre-transplant echocardiographic RV function parameters, including RV strain, and long-term CV outcomes following KT. In this retrospective cohort study, we included adult KT recipients at a single Midwest academic center from 2015 to 2024 who had adequate-quality pre-transplant echocardiograms and follow-up at our institution. RV function parameters included tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S′), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), fractional area change (FAC), RV index of myocardial performance (RIMP), and RV free wall strain measured by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, heart failure hospitalization, coronary revascularization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmias. Among 371 patients (mean age 53.5 ± 13.1 years; 56% male) followed for a median of 4.9 years (IQR, 3.1–6.4), 79 (21.2%) experienced MACE. On univariable Cox analysis, RIMP and RV strain parameters were associated with MACE, whereas S′, TAPSE, and FAC were not…

abstract: Purpose of Study: This study examined the effect of work-life balance on employee performance in insurance companies in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Specifically, the study assessed the influence of flexible teleworking, wellness programs, family-friendly policies, and reasonable workloads on employee performance, addressing existing knowledge gaps concerning workplace practices and organizational productivity outcomes. Methodology: The study adopted a descriptive research design targeting 520 employees across 65 insurance companies in Nairobi City County, Kenya. A sample of 226 respondents was determined using Yamane's formula. Primary data were collected through semi-structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis to establish relationships between variables. Findings: The findings revealed that work-life balance practices positively and significantly influenced employee performance in insurance companies. The regression model demonstrated strong explanatory power (R² = 0.837), accounting for 83.7% of employee performance variation. Flexible teleworking exhibited the highest unstandardized coefficient (B = 0.462), followed by reasonable workloads (B = 0.378), family-friendly policies (B = 0.376), and wellness programs (B = 0.345). All four predictors were reported as statistically significant (p < 0.05). The findings indicat…

Assessment Reform for Introduction to Sociology from the Perspective of the Field Classroom: A Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Framework
abstract: Assessment reform is central to turning the field classroom from an occasional activity into a durable mechanism of sociological learning. Drawing on the reform of Introduction to Sociology, this article explains how process-based field assignments and summative examination tasks can be aligned around knowledge, competence, and value formation. It then introduces a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation framework whose indicators and weights come directly from the assessment scheme. The framework converts cohort-level score distributions into membership vectors and returns diagnostic evidence to teaching. The reform shows that field-based questioning and assignments help students connect theory with everyday life, strengthen research awareness, and make value-oriented education concrete. Experiential learning, constructive alignment, and transparent evaluation should therefore be designed as one system.

The Determinants of Audit Quality in an Emerging Market: Evidence from Cambodian Auditors
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the impact of auditors’ skepticism, competence, motivation, time budget pressure, and audit tenure on audit quality in Cambodia. It also examines the indirect effects of auditors’ skepticism, competence, and motivation on audit quality, mediated by time budget pressure. Six latent constructs, or unobserved variables—auditors’ skepticism, competence, motivation, time budget pressure, audit tenure, and audit quality—are developed in the Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) using observed or manifest variables. The data are collected from 107 independent auditors in both local and international accounting firms in Cambodia. Path analysis within the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework is utilized to evaluate the influence of these constructs on audit quality, with auditor experience designated as a control variable. The study found that auditor competence and tenure significantly enhance audit quality, while skepticism, motivation, and time budget pressure showed no direct effect. However, skepticism, competence, and motivation significantly influenced time budget pressure. Despite this, it did not impact audit quality and therefore does not serve as a mediating variable. These results indicate that, although certain auditor traits contribute to perceived time pressure, such pressure does not affect audit outcomes. Overall, the model highlights au…

abstract: The increased use of skincare products has raised growing global concerns as regards exposure to heavy metal contaminants andmicrobes. The aim of this research study was to assess microbial contamination, heavy metals and associated health risks in skincareproducts from different market sources. A total of forty skincare products were randomly sourced and analyzed. Microbial contamination was assessed using standard microbiological methods. Heavy metal contaminations were analyzed for manganese, lead, nickel, copper, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, cobalt and zinc using atomic absorption spectrophotometry. Human health risk assessment for skin exposure was conducted using hazard index, carcinogenic risk models and hazard quotients. The result from this study showed variations in microbial counts as regards organism, product type, and source: online products showed high total bacterial counts and the highest reported Salmonella and Shigella counts, supermarket oil had the highest total fungal count, and open-market products showed high coliform and E. coli counts in selected products. All sources contained measurable concentrations of the assessed metals. Powders had comparatively high concentrations of several metals, including copper (6.09 mg/kg) in online products, lead (1.55 mg/kg) in open-market products, and chromium (3.22 mg/kg) in supermarket products; however, the highest c…

Law and Economic Performance: An Analysis of Regulatory Frameworks and Market Efficiency
abstract: This study examines the drivers of sustainable regional economic growth and economic performance through two complementary structural models analyzed using SmartPLS. Model 1 evaluates the role of Green Infrastructure Investment (GII) in influencing Environmental Quality (EQ), Economic Performance (EP), and Sustainable Regional Economic Growth (SREG). Model 2 explores how Regulatory Framework Quality (RFQ), Legal Certainty (LC), and Market Efficiency (ME) affect Economic Performance. A quantitative approach based on Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) is employed to assess both measurement and structural relationships. The results indicate that all constructs demonstrate strong reliability and convergent validity. The structural model demonstrates strong explanatory power, with -square values exceeding 0.98 across endogenous variables in Model 1, and ranging from 0.898 to 0.966in Model 2. In Model 1, green infrastructure investment has a strong positive impact on environmental quality and economic performance, while environmental quality significantly enhances sustainable growth. However, economic performance and the direct effect of green investment on sustainable growth show negative relationships, indicating short-term trade-offs. In Model 2, regulatory framework quality strongly influences legal certainty and indirectly improves economic performance …

title: Product Substitution and Comparative Dynamics in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market
abstract: Pharmaceutical product substitution has become a central structural mechanism reshaping pricing, competition, and firm strategy within the Indian pharmaceutical market under an increasingly regulated healthcare environment. This study examines the regulatory, economic, and institutional determinants of generic and therapeutic substitution in India, with particular emphasis on how policy-driven mechanisms shape substitution outcomes across public and private healthcare systems. Using an analytical secondary-data design, the study draws on evidence from the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), Health Management Information System (HMIS), National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM), Competition Commission of India (CCI), and international benchmarks from the OECD and WHO. The findings show that generic medicines account for approximately 97% of pharmaceutical sales by volume in India (AIOCD-AWACS), yet represent only around 38% of total market value, yielding an Effective Substitution Efficiency Ratio (ESER) of 0.39, substantially lower than the OECD average of 0.77. While generic entry results in 30–50% revenue erosion for branded products and generics priced 50–80% lower rapidly gain substantial volume share, economic substitution remains incomplete. Institutional procurement systems achieve significantly greater price efficiency, with procurement prices nearly 1.9 …

title: INSTALLATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SOLAR PANELS AS AN ALTERNATIVE ELECTRICITY SOURCE FOR POWERED SYSTEMS IN AUTOCAD LABORATORY FOR TEACHING, LEARNING AND TRAINING
abstract: Unreliable electricity supply remains a major constraint to practical training in technical education institutions across Nigeria, with the AutoCAD Laboratory a digitally intensive facility being especially vulnerable to power interruptions. This study is on design, installation, and maintenance of a solar panel photovoltaic (PV) system as an alternative electricity source for an AutoCAD Laboratory. An electrical load audit established a total daily demand of approximately 72.2 kWh, against which an 15.44kWp solar array (8 × 580W JA-Solar Panels double side), a 11.7 kVA, 48V/60-battery Leoch Lithium, MPPT charge controllers, and a 5 kVA pure sine wave hybrid inverter were sized, procured, and installed. Postinstallation testing over a two-week period under varied weather conditions showed the system delivering 96.6% of its design output, sufficient to power all computers, lighting, and the projector for a full 8-hour training day without interruption. Cost analysis showed a total installation cost of approximately N6,600,000:00 with a projected payback period of 3-4 years against Ikeja Electricity, Petrol, and diesel-generator alternatives, and an expected system lifespan of 20-25 years. The findings confirmed that solar PV technology is a technically reliable and economically justifiable alternative to grid electricity for powering technical education laboratories in Nigeria. …

Beyond Free Certification: Administrative Burdens and Market Inclusion in Indonesia’s 2026 Halal Transition
abstract: This qualitative documentary study examines how Indonesia’s halal-certification transition distributes administrative responsibilities and subsidized access across micro and small enterprises and public institutions. A purposive case analysis compares enacted regulations, technical decrees, January and April 2026 SEHATI allocation schedules, a dated October government announcement, and relevant peer-reviewed studies. Findings distinguish waived application charges from eligibility checks, documentation, facilitator work, and enforcement review. The original 1,350,000 SEHATI allocation was formally revised to 1,090,891 places on 8 April 2026; these are budgeted facilitation slots, not measured certifications. On 16 October, the government announced an extended compliance schedule for selected categories, but the operative amending government regulation could not be independently authenticated by the evidence cut-off. We propose a bounded burden-incidence framework linking information clarity, procedural usability, facilitation capacity, assurance quality, and reviewability. The evidence establishes policy design and administrative assignments, not applicant costs, realized market inclusion, causal business effects, or equitable provincial access. The contribution is a time-specific institutional diagnosis and an auditable agenda for subsequent firm- and agency-level evaluation.

title: Laser‐Architected Hierarchical Wood Evaporator for Salt‐Resistant Solar Desalination and Dual‐Mode Water–Electricity Cogeneration
abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater scarcity and intermittent solar irradiation motivate the development of technologies for freshwater production and electricity generation. However, salt accumulation limits the long‐term operation of solar interfacial evaporators. A laser‐architected delignified balsa wood evaporator (DBW/LCC) with a 3D cylindrical array and laser‐carbonized surfaces is fabricated through delignification, laser engraving, and in situ laser carbonization. The array enhances light trapping and exposes additional sidewall area. Vertically aligned hydrophilic channels sustain capillary water supply and, together with the hydrophobic top surface, establish asymmetric wettability. DBW/LCC achieves an average absorptance of 99.46% over 250–2500 nm. The wetted surface exhibits a valley–plateau temperature difference of ∼1.2°C. Thermo–solutal Marangoni circulation may contribute to brine redistribution. The evaporator maintains stable evaporation for 150 h in 20 wt.% brine without visible salt deposition. Under 1 sun, it achieves a mass‐loss rate of 5.09 kg m −2 h −1 normalized to its horizontal projected area, with an apparent evaporation efficiency of 99.85% calculated using an effective enthalpy. Coupled with a thermoelectric module, it generates voltages of 86.3 mV under 1 sun and 79.8 mV at a wind speed of 9.6 m s −1 without illumination. This platform offers a route to decentra…

Geographic Pricing and Cross-Market Tariff Spillovers in a Differentiated Bertrand Duopoly
abstract: This paper studies how third-degree price discrimination impacts the Nash equilibrium of a duopolistic Bertrand model in differentiated markets. The model looks at two automobile producers, one based in the UK and the other based in the EU, competing in two different markets–Ireland and Britain market. The European Union producer faces a tariff only in the British market, while the United Kingdom producer faces no tariff in either of the markets. By calculating both firms’ best-response functions, this study compares the equilibrium prices and quantities under geographic price discrimination and a uniform price system. The results show that price discrimination results in the tariff increasing both producers' equilibrium prices in Britain, while leaving prices in the Irish market unchanged. This leaves the cost shock isolated in the British market. Additionally, the tariff increases the British producer’s equilibrium quantity demanded while reducing the EU producer’s quantity demanded. However, under uniform pricing, the tariff results in a cross-market spillover, increasing equilibrium prices in Ireland, set by both producers, despite the absence of a tariff in that market.

Chest pain risk-stratification tools used or trialled in Ambulance Health Service settings: A Scoping Review
abstract: Introduction Patients with chest pain account for a significant proportion of ambulance attendances and Emergency Department (ED) presentations. Rapid identification of life-threatening aetiologies and differentiation from benign causes enables timely interventions and efficient utilisation of healthcare resources. Chest-pain risk-stratification tools are used throughout healthcare; their implementation into Ambulance Health Services (AHS) (i.e. Emergency Medical Services) may support ambulance clinicians with clinical decisions to safely divert patients to alternative care pathways. Objectives This scoping review maps literature describing the use and/or evaluation of chest-pain risk-stratification tools within AHS. It (1) identifies and describes tools used or trialled in adults with chest pain to stratify risk of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or major adverse cardiac event (MACE); (2) reports key characteristics and resource requirements; and (3) describes whether tools have been validated for AHS use. Methods This scoping review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and presented using PRISMA-ScR. Searches of CINAHL, MEDLINE Complete, and Scopus were performed, with grey literature searches through Google Scholar and Trove. Data was extracted using a structured data-charting approach and summarised descriptively, including frequency mapping where…

title: Impact of a pharmacist-led pharmacogenomic service on test capture rates in oncology: A retrospective pre-post cohort study, 2024-2026
abstract: Background Pharmacogenomic (PGx) testing can support clinical decision-making to reduce toxicity associated with commonly used oncology therapies. However, PGx testing remains underutilized in oncology practice due to lack of personnel to coordinate testing. We evaluated whether the implementation of a pharmacist-led PGx service increased PGx testing among oncology patients. Methods We used a retrospective cohort study to compare outcomes from the pre-and post-intervention periods following implementation of a pharmacist-led PGx service within our Duluth oncology clinic, Minnesota-USA. EHR/laboratory data were extracted on adult cancer patients with planned/receiving 5-fluorouracil, capecitabine, or irinotecan between September 1, 2024, and March 31, 2026. The primary outcome was PGx capture, defined as the rate of patients who received PGx testing prior to chemotherapy initiation. Secondary outcomes included tests with actionable results and the proportion leading to therapy modification. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square test, Mann-Whitney U test, and adjusted (age and sex as covariates) logistic regression were used. All analyses were performed using SPSS (IBM 29.0) and RStudio (2025.09.1 + 401) with a statistical significance at ≤0.05. title: Stakeholders Involvement, Project Performance, and Service Delivery in Kenya's Water Flagship Projects: A Three-Construct System, Competing Structures, and Cross-Sectional Versus Temporal Coherence
abstract: Stakeholder involvement, project performance, and service delivery are usually studied as links in a presumed causal chain, but their joint structure, the alternatives to the chain, and the agreement between project-level and portfolio-level evidence are rarely examined. This study analyzes the three constructs as a system in Kenya's water flagship projects.Survey data from 208 usable questionnaires (65.62% response; stratified sample of 317 of 1,804 projects) were analyzed with partial correlations, maximum-likelihood fit of competing three-variable structures with information criteria, Monte Carlo mediation, dominance and commonality analysis, a Gaussian conditional-independence graph for the four constructs including tendering strategy, and a comparison with recorded annual performance and service delivery indices (2015-2019; n = 5) using correlations, first differences, lags, gap series, and a domain cross-correlation matrix. With tendering strategy added, involvement became a leaf of the conditional-independence graph: its partial correlations with performance (-.031) and service delivery (-.014) were non-significant, and only its link to tendering (.451) survived. title: Meeting the demand to teach mathematics using technologies – a Cross-Sectional analysis of In-Service and Pre-Service teachers’ Technology-Related professional knowledge
abstract: Mathematics teachers are required to effectively integrate technology into mathematics teaching. Meeting this demand draws on their technology-related professional knowledge. While standards specify competencies teachers should develop, little is known about the extent to which pre- and in-service teachers actually meet such demands. Based on a sample of N = 409 German pre- and in-service secondary mathematics teachers, this study aims (i) to investigate differences between in-service and pre-service teachers regarding their technological content knowledge (TCK) and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPCK), and to characterize the range of teachers’ TCK and TPCK by describing which demands different shares of the sample can meet. Using item-response-theory methods, we found no significant overall differences between pre- and in-service teachers in TCK or TPCK. However, group-specific strengths emerged: in-service teachers performed relatively better on demands involving dynamic geometry software, whereas pre-service teachers showed advantages in spreadsheet-related tasks. Characterizing the range of TCK, demands successfully addressed by 75% of the sample include identifying suitable technology to solve a mathematical task. In comparison, only 25% of the sample demonstrated basic spreadsheet skills. Teachers’ TPCK ranges from knowledge that allows them to identify sin…

title: Pain Characterization: Presentation Patterns, and Multidimensional Assessment in Women with Advanced Gynecologic Cancer in a Palliative Care Service
abstract: Abstract Background Pain in advanced cancer is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon extending beyond intensity to include biological, psychological, and social components. In women with advanced gynecologic malignancies, pain is highly prevalent yet often undercharacterized, particularly in resource-limited settings where disparities in access and delayed integration of palliative care may influence its presentation and management. Objective To characterize multidimensional pain features and identify distinct descriptive pain patterns in women with advanced gynecologic cancer receiving palliative care. Design Observational study. Setting/Subjects Electronic medical records of women aged ≥18 years with advanced gynecologic cancer and documented pain, treated at a tertiary cancer center in Mexico between 2013 and 2023, were reviewed. Measurements Sociodemographic and clinical variables were collected. Pain assessment included location, intensity, time of onset, and characteristics (somatic, visceral, neuropathic, or mixed). Psychosocial factors, including anxiety and depression, were also evaluated. Descriptive statistics were used to explore multidimensional pain patterns. Results A total of 1,015 women were included (median age 56 years; most had≤12 years of education). Cervical and ovarian cancers predominated (43.4% and 32.3%). Pain was mainly pelvic or abdominal (81.0%)…

title: The Effect of Taste, Service Quality, and Omnichannel Experience on customer Satisfaction and Loyalty at Tomoro Coffee Surabaya
abstract: Tomoro Coffee has grown rapidly in Surabaya, but intense competition among coffee shops makes it easy for customers to switch if they encounter dissatisfaction with the product or service. This study focuses on Tomoro Coffee customers in Surabaya and examines the effects of taste, service quality, and omnichannel experience on Customer satisfaction and loyalty. Questionnaire data were collected from 130 respondents and analyzed using covariance-based Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with statistical software, through the stages of measurement model, structural model, and model modification. The study aims to obtain an influence model and its simultaneous equations. The results show that the modified model fits well. The independent variables taste (X1), service quality (X2), and omnichannel experience (X3) have a positive and significant effect on Customer satisfaction (Y1) and Customer loyalty (Y2). Meanwhile, Customer satisfaction (Y1) has a positive but non-significant effect on Customer loyalty (Y2). Taste has the largest total effect on Customer satisfaction, while omnichannel experience has the largest total effect on Customer loyalty. Aging Service Organizational Capacity to Deliver Evidence-Based Depression Programs: A National Survey
abstract: Background Integration of mental health programs within community-based, social or aging service organizations has been recommended to serve more older adults with depression. Objective The purpose of this study was to obtain input from aging service organizations across the United States regarding their consideration and resource needs for implementing a lay-led program for depression ( “Do More, Feel Better,” DMFB). Methods An online survey distributed via email inquired about perceived need and consideration regarding DMFB, existing resources, and resource needs. Results Among 242 respondents across 42 states, perceived need for community-based depression services was high (8.7/10), and almost all reported they would consider implementing DMFB (94%). Most had some resources in place to support DMFB (e.g., technology, staff, experience with other evidence-based programs), but most indicated need for key program-specific resources, with the most critical resource needs being funding, dedicated personnel, and training (e.g., depression identification, DMFB delivery, and emergency management).

title: Exploring Pre-Service Biology Teachers’ Anxiety Levels In the University of Education, Winneba
abstract: This study explored the levels and sources of anxiety among Level 100 pre-service biology teachers at the University of Education, Winneba, Ghana, with a focus on how gender influences anxiety experiences during lessons and assessments. Employing a mixed-methods research design, the study integrated a descriptive survey and a qualitative descriptive design to collect both quantitative and qualitative data. The study involved the entire cohort of 81 level 100 pre-service biology teachers (51 males and 30 females). Data were gathered via a structured questionnaire (adapted from the Betz MAR-S scale, 1978) to measure biology-specific anxiety and semi structured interviews. The quantitative findings revealed that while many students reported low to moderate levels of anxiety, significant anxiety was triggered by conceptual difficulty and cognitive overload rather than test-related stress. Inferential statistical testing revealed that male students reported significantly higher levels of anxiety specifically related to conceptual confusion and cognitive overload, though general test anxiety did not differ by gender. Qualitative data further illuminate the impact of anxiety on academic performance, highlighting themes such as cognitive interference, self-doubt, study avoidance, and reduced classroom engagement. These findings underscore the need for targeted pedagogical interventions…

title: Is the association between Arabic, Somali, and Russian maternal origin and exclusive breastfeeding mediated by health service use and peer support?
abstract: Aims: To examine differences in maternal and child health service utilization between Somali-/Arabic-speaking, Russian-speaking, and Finnish-speaking mothers, and to explore whether health service use and breastfeeding peer support mediate the association between maternal origin and exclusive breastfeeding (EBF). Methods: We used data from the FinChildren 2020 survey. The analysis included 5348 mothers with infants aged 4–5 months: 78 Somali-/Arabic-speaking, 123 Russian-speaking, and 5147 Finnish-speaking mothers. Mediation analysis was used to examine the potential mediating role of health service use and breastfeeding peer support in the association between maternal origin and EBF. Results: Among the infants born to Somali-/Arabic-speaking mothers, 23% had not attended routine child health clinic visits, compared with 1.7% of Russian-speaking and 0.4% of Finnish-speaking mothers ( p < 0.005). Somali-/Arabic-speaking mothers were less likely to be offered postpartum nurse home visits (50% vs. 62% and 72%, respectively; p < 0.005) and to report adequate breastfeeding peer support (50% vs. 57% and 69%, respectively; p < 0.005). In unadjusted mediation analyses, breastfeeding peer support and the offer of a postpartum nurse home visit showed the largest indirect effects (−0.013 and 0.002, respectively). Utilisation of diverse healthcare providers: Virtual health service engagement and geographic barriers among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adults with chronic disease
abstract: Background Virtual Health Services (VHS) may improve healthcare access for rural Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, but little is known about whether active engagement is associated with more diverse providers or reduced geographic barriers to primary care. This study examined whether active VHS engagement was associated with provider diversity and moderated geographic distance effects on primary care access. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included 74 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander adults enrolled in the Goondir Health Services VHS program in rural Queensland. VHS status (active versus inactive in the past 2 weeks) was the primary exposure, with outcomes being provider diversity across 27 types and visit frequency to 12 services over 12 months. Negative binomial regression, adjusted for sociodemographic, lifestyle and health factors including chronic disease burden examined VHS associations with provider diversity, and interaction terms tested whether active engagement moderated distance effects on Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS) visits. Results Of 74 participants, 47 (63.5%) were active VHS users. title: The Taxation of Non-Resident Digital Service Providers Without Physical Presence In Tanzania: Jurisdictional and Enforcement Challenges
abstract: The study examines the jurisdictional and enforcement challenges associated with taxing non-resident digital service providers without physical presence in Tanzania. The rapid growth of the digital economy has enabled non-resident providers to supply digital services to Tanzanian consumers without establishing conventional physical premises in the country, creating challenges for traditional tax rules based on physical presence. The study adopts doctrinal and non-doctrinal legal research methodologies. The doctrinal approach analyses relevant tax legislation, subsidiary legislation, policy documents, international tax materials and scholarly literature, while the non-doctrinal approach draws on empirical information obtained from selected respondents and interviews with Tanzania Revenue Authority tax officials. The study is guided by the Ability to Pay Theory, Benefit Theory and Neutrality Theory. The findings indicate that jurisdictional challenges include difficulties in establishing a taxable nexus, determining the location of digital transactions and consumers, accessing information held outside Tanzania, and exercising taxing authority over providers operating across borders. The study further finds that enforcement is constrained by difficulties in identifying and monitoring non-resident providers, obtaining reliable transaction information, reliance on voluntary complian…

title: Assessment of the Cybersecurity Posture of the Federal Inland Revenue Service Against AI-Assisted Threats Using NIST, MITRE and ACGF Frameworks
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how attackers target national institutions, yet most cybersecurity assessments still check whether controls exist without asking whether governance can cope with AI-assisted threats. This study assesses the cybersecurity posture of the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) in Nigeria against AI-assisted threats using an integrated model that combines the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the MITRE adversary knowledge base and the AI Cybersecurity Governance Framework (ACGF).

title: Patterns and Factors Associated With Contacting a Children and Young People’s Mental Health Crisis Service
abstract: Background In recent years, there has been a notable increase in the number of children and young people (CYP) experiencing mental health crises. Objective This study aimed to explore the demographic and clinical characteristics of CYP who engaged with a mental health crisis service in Northwest England. Method A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data collected from CYP accessing the crisis service between January 2022 and December 2023. Results A total of 1,940 individuals were identified as having contact with the crisis team. Approximately 75% were female, and nearly half lived in the two most deprived socioeconomic quintiles. The majority were aged between 13 and 15 years. The number of contacts per individual ranged from 1 to 186, totaling 7,711 contacts overall. The primary reasons for contact included self-harm (50%) and suicidality (30%). Notably, 29% were not in education, and 28% were also receiving therapy from CYP mental health services. Contact rates peaked during weekdays and during May, September, October, and November. Conclusions The findings highlight the need for multi-agency preventative interventions, particularly targeting females and those from deprived communities, with attention to times of high service demand.

Comparing self-regulation, anxiety, and willingness to communicate across blended, face-to-face, and online instruction in female EFL learners
abstract: Abstract Technology-enhanced language instruction has expanded the range of instructional options available to EFL learners, yet evidence comparing blended, online, and face-to-face modes across multiple cognitive and affective outcomes remains limited, particularly among advanced EFL learners. This study compared self-regulated learning strategies (SRLSs), foreign language classroom anxiety (FLCA), and willingness to communicate (WTC) in English writing across these three instructional modes. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was conducted with 360 advanced female EFL learners in Iran (120 per group), selected through two-stage cluster sampling from language institutes. Learners participated in 10 instructional sessions delivered through blended, online, or face-to-face modes. Pre-test and post-test measures of SRLS, FLCA, and WTC were collected using self-report questionnaires. One-way ANCOVAs were conducted for each outcome, controlling for the corresponding pre-test score, followed by Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. After adjustment for baseline scores, statistically significant between-group differences were observed for SRLS, FLCA, and WTC. title: Hand-washing frequency, gastric histopathology, and depressive symptom burden in adults undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: a structural equation modeling study
abstract: Abstract Depressive symptoms are common among patients referred for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, but their relation to mucosal pathology is unclear. We examined whether gastric histopathological severity links lifestyle exposures to depressive symptom burden in 442 adults undergoing endoscopy at two tertiary care hospitals in Pakistan, 320 of whom had gastric biopsies. Depressive symptom burden (five DSM-5-derived items) and gastric severity (four Updated Sydney System markers) were modeled as latent variables using structural equation modeling. An abrupt shift in patient characteristics and histology grades during recruitment was identified and adjusted for. In the primary model (CFI = 0.971; RMSEA = 0.040), less frequent hand washing was associated with higher depressive symptom burden (β = 0.23, 95% CI 0.06–0.39) but not with gastric severity (β = −0.11, 95% CI − 0.25 to 0.03). Gastric severity was not associated with symptom burden (β = 0.14, 95% CI − 0.06 to 0.35), and the indirect effect through gastric severity was null. The hand-washing association persisted in all six sensitivity analyses, whereas an apparent hand-washing–pathology association appeared only without adjustment for recruitment period. Depressive symptom burden in these patients was unrelated to mucosal pathology but tracked reduced self-care, supporting symptom screening irrespective of endoscopic f…

title: Frequency of transcalvarial brain matter herniation in depressed skull fractures and its association with clinical, hematological, and injury-related radiological factors
abstract: Objective: To assess the frequency of transcalvarial herniation of brain matter in depressed skull fractures (DSF), and to evaluate the clinical, radiological, and hematological factors associated with such herniation. Methodology: This retrospective observational cohort study included patients who presented with depressed skull fractures between January 2024 and April 2026 at the Department of Neurosurgery, Unit-I, Punjab Institute of Neurosciences, Lahore, Pakistan. Chi-square tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U tests were used to assess the association with transcalvarial brain matter herniation in DSF. Results: Among 60 cases of DSF, brain herniation was present in 36.70% (22). The mean age of the cohort was 25.65±13.11 years, with male predominance (78.30%, 47). The median presenting GCS was 14 (14-15). Radiological signs of raised ICP were present in 51.70% (31). The most common mechanism of injury was road traffic accident (RTA; 78.30%, 47). Brain herniation along the DSF was present in 36.70% (22). The most common locations were frontal (53.30%, 32). In the brain herniation group, the median depth of the fragmented segment was 20.0 (19.7-28.5), and the fractured segment median diameter was 39.5 (30.0-40.0). The presenting Glasgow Coma Scale score (GCS) was higher in patients with transcalvarial herniation (p-value 0.026). Whereas the midline shift (MLS; p…

The transcriptional regulation of specialized terpenoid biosynthesis and its regulation by jasmonic acid
abstract: Abstract All plants produce terpenoids for their general metabolism but most, if not all, also produce terpenoids in their specialized metabolism. These specialized metabolites play an essential role in the interaction of plants with their environment, in particular with other organisms. They are also of great economic value to us as they are used as medicine, in our food and as perfumes. The regulation of terpenoid biosynthesis has received much attention as it is costly for the plants to produce even though they only contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Some terpenoids are constitutively produced but most of them are induced upon biotic stress with a key role for the phytohormone jasmonate-isoleucine (JA-Ile). It has become clear that the regulation is mostly at the level of transcription with an important role for basic-helix-loop-helix (bHLH) and MYB transcription factors in the JA-Ile inducible pathways. This review summarizes recent breakthroughs with examples of specific mono-, sesqui- and diterpenoids, describing the complex molecular network regulating their biosynthesis in certain model systems with other phytohormones involved as well. It also points out that several other avenues of regulation need more attention to understand the fine tuning of the regulation. This will help optimizing the production of these specialized metabolites in our crops.

Molecular Mechanism of Proline-Mediated Regulation of Graphene–Bacterial Membrane Interactions: A Balance between Dispersion Stabilization and Membrane Disruption
abstract: Abstract Graphene nanosheets have attracted considerable attention as antibacterial nanomaterials due to their ability to directly damage bacterial membranes. However, the poor dispersion of graphene in aqueous environments limits its practical applications. Recently, natural amino acids [Mao, T.; et al.Nature2025, 645, 915–921].have been proposed as biocompatible stabilizers for nanomaterials. Nevertheless, how amino acid concentration affects graphene-membrane interactions remains unclear. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the regulation of monomeric proline on graphene insertion into bacterial membranes. Three systems containing 0, 1, and 2 M proline were constructed to reveal the influence of proline on graphene transport behavior, membrane perturbation, and molecular interactions. The results show that graphene can spontaneously insert into bacterial membranes under all investigated conditions, indicating that proline cannot completely eliminate graphene-membrane interactions. However, introducing proline significantly delays graphene penetration by enhancing graphene stabilization in the aqueous environment. The average insertion time increases from 22.3 ± 6.8 ns without proline to 95.3 ± 22.4 ns and 102.7 ± 29.1 ns under 2 and 1 M proline conditions, respectively. After insertion, graphene still induces membrane deformation, alte…

title: Hybrid piezoelectric-electromagnetic energy harvesting from ultra-low-frequency human motion via magnetic frequency up-conversion
abstract: Efficiently harvesting ultra-low-frequency vibration energy from human motion to power electronic devices remains challenging. This study presents a compact magnetically coupled energy harvester (MCEH) that integrates piezoelectric (PEH) and electromagnetic (EEH) modules through a shared reciprocating center magnet. The center magnet simultaneously produces electromagnetic induction and excites the piezoelectric cantilevers through nonlinear magnetic repulsion, enabling dual-path energy conversion and magnetic frequency up-conversion from excitation below 10 Hz. A coupled lumped-parameter electromechanical model was established and evaluated using numerical simulations and experiments, including frequency-response, load-matching, human-motion, and sensor-powering tests. At 6.5 Hz, the PEH reaches an RMS voltage of 3.56 V with magnetic coupling, versus only 0.0383 V for the no-center-magnet reference, showing an approximately 93-fold enhancement. Under the matched loads, the system delivers a total output of 1,147.88 μ W and a normalized power density of 31.89 μ W/ cm 3 . The prototype also powers a temperature-humidity sensor under the tested motion conditions, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed approach for low-power wearable sensing.

title: Sesame Oil Cake as a Partial Soybean Meal Substitute in the Practical Diets of Juvenile Asian Seabass ( Lates calcarifer ): Nutritional Performance, Physiological Responses and Nutrigenomic Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing reliance on imported soybean meal (SBM) in aquafeeds has intensified the search for locally available and sustainable alternative protein ingredients. This study evaluated sesame oil cake (SOC), an underutilized agro‐industrial by‐product in Bangladesh, as a partial replacement for imported SBM in diets for juvenile Asian seabass, Lates calcarife r. Five approximately isonitrogenous and isolipidic diets containing 0%, 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% SOC were formulated with progressive reductions in SBM. Juveniles (4.25 ± 0.27 g) were distributed among 15 tanks, with 20 fish per tank and three replicate tanks per treatment and fed for 60 days. Growth performance remained comparable with the control up to 15% SOC, whereas 20% SOC reduced final weight, weight gain, specific growth rates, and survival rate, while impairing feed conversion and protein utilization. Whole‐body crude protein was significantly lower in all SOC‐fed groups than in control. Higher SOC inclusion reduced haemoglobin, haematocrit and mean corpuscular haemoglobin, although most leukocyte indices remained stable. Fish fed 20% SOC also exhibited lower circulating total protein and lipase activity and elevated cholesterol, triglycerides, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT), indicating altered metabolic and hepatic function. Liver architecture was largely preserved at …

title: Synergistic Crystallization Regulation and Defect Suppression via Dual‐Site Molecular Coordination for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long‐term stability. Herein, (1H‐benzo[d]imidazol‐2‐yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual‐site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH 3 + ) and electron‐rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl‐modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non‐radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy‐level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. Consequently, the champion PSC achieves the conversion efficiency of 26.50% while demonstrating excellent operational and damp‐heat stability, retaining 87.49% and 80…

title: Regulating Resonance‐Related Dynamic Magnetic Response through In Situ MnO Formation in FeCoNiCr 0.4 Mn 0.6 High‐Entropy Alloy for Low‐Frequency Microwave Absorption
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient microwave absorption in the S–C band requires the strength and frequency distribution of resonance‐related magnetic loss to be regulated while sufficient permeability is retained. The key is therefore to balance control of the resonance‐related dynamic magnetic response with preservation of the magnetic contribution from the ferromagnetic matrix. Here, FeCoNiCr 0.4 Mn 0.6 high‐entropy alloy (HEA) powders were subjected to wet milling and low‐temperature annealing to produce anisotropic flakes while enabling controlled in situ oxidation of the intrinsic Mn. The resulting MnO/HEA interfaces were accompanied by changes in the local strain state and magnetic anisotropy environment of the adjacent ferromagnetic matrix, providing a structural basis for the evolution of resonance linewidth and effective damping. At 300°C, limited MnO formation produced a moderate effective damping state while maintaining relatively high permeability and sufficient ferromagnetic‐phase contribution, enabling effective absorption over 3.2–4.9 GHz at a thickness of 3.5 mm. At 400°C, further MnO formation increased the fraction of the non‐ferromagnetic phase and weakened the microwave magnetic response. These results demonstrate that controlling the oxidation degree of intrinsic alloying elements can balance interfacial regulation, dynamic magnetic relaxation, and ferromagnetic‐phase ret…

title: The Influence of Government Regulation on Tourist Motivation in Indonesia's Religious Tourism: The Mediating Role of Marketing Communication Strategies
abstract: Religious tourism is a significant economic sector in Indonesia, yet how government regulation and marketing communication jointly shape tourist motivation remains underexplored. Grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior, this study treats government regulation as an exogenous antecedent linked to perceived behavioral control and institutional credibility, and marketing communication as the proximal lever acting on attitudes and subjective norms. Government regulation was operationalized through policy implementation, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder engagement; marketing communication through advertising, publicity, word-of-mouth, on-site interpretation, and direct and interactive marketing; and tourist motivation through cultural interest, spiritual significance, and recreational opportunity. An online survey was completed by 402 non-pilgrim visitors who had visited an Indonesian religious heritage site in the previous 12 months; 81.9% reported one of five focal sites (Borobudur Temple, Istiqlal Mosque, Tanah Lot Temple, Uluwatu Temple, and Jakarta Cathedral). Ordinary least squares regression showed that government regulation predicted marketing communication ($\beta = 0.676$, $p < .001$), while marketing communication ($\beta = 0.385$) and government regulation ($\beta = 0.355$) both predicted tourist motivation, together explaining 45.8% of its variance. The Sobel t…

title: Regulation of IL ‐13 Signaling by Retinoic Acid in Airway Epithelial Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Dysregulated vitamin A signaling, characterized by reduced all‐trans retinoic acid (ATRA), is associated with asthma severity, and restoration of ATRA signaling may alleviate asthma symptoms. However, the molecular changes induced by inflammatory cytokines such as IL‐13 that are central to asthma pathology and the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) agonists in airway cells are not well established. This study investigates the effects of IL‐13 and RAR agonists on lung epithelial cells using a mass spectrometry‐based proteomics approach. A549 alveolar and BEAS‐2B bronchial epithelial cells were treated with IL‐13 in the presence of vehicle, ATRA (pan‐RAR agonist), or CD1530 (RARγ agonist). Proteomic profiling revealed significant changes in proteins relevant to asthma pathogenesis in IL‐13‐treated cells. IL‐13 upregulated pro‐inflammatory signaling kinases JAK1 and AXL, cytoskeletal‐associated proteins CLDN2 and ACTN4, and inflammatory proteins CD44 and HLAs in A549 cells. In BEAS‐2B cells, IL‐13 upregulated barrier dysfunction‐related proteins P‐Cadherin and α‐catenin, immune activation marker ICAM‐1, and pro‐fibrosis marker TGF‐β. Notably, IL‐13 significantly reduced ATRA biosynthesis enzymes RDH10 and ALDH1A1 which were accompanied by reduced ATRA levels and reduced ATRA biosynthesis in A549 cells as quantified by liquid chromatography‐multistage‐tandem mass spectrometry. title: Doping in Sport: Health Risks, Psychosocial Drivers, and the Evolving Anti-Doping Response
abstract: Doping in sport is often discussed as a problem of prohibited drugs, positive tests, and sanctions. That framing is incomplete. Contemporary anti-doping governance also addresses prohibited methods and conduct that undermines testing and investigation, while effective prevention must account for health risks, athlete decision-making, team cultures, medical practice, and the commercial pressures surrounding sport. This narrative review synthesizes selected peer-reviewed literature and official anti-doping instruments to examine four connected questions: how doping is defined and regulated; what is known about health consequences; why athletes may consider prohibited performance enhancement; and how detection and prevention can be combined more effectively. The evidence indicates that health risks vary by substance, dose, duration, route, combinations, and the population studied, so findings from non-athlete users should not be generalized uncritically to elite athletes. Research on athlete attitudes identifies perceived performance benefits, social influence, recovery concerns, and financial or career pressures as relevant factors, although attitudes do not directly establish actual use. The World Anti-Doping Code and the annually updated Prohibited List provide a harmonized framework, but testing alone cannot address every source of risk. A more credible response combines risk-…

title: Mechanical Response of EPDM Composites Partially Replacing N550 Carbon Black With FGD Gypsum‐Derived Calcium Sulfate Whiskers: Effects of Replacement Ratio and CSW Characteristics
abstract: ABSTRACT To investigate the potential of FGD gypsum‐derived calcium sulfate whiskers (CSW) as a partial substitute for N550 carbon black in EPDM rubber, CSW were incorporated by mass replacement of N550. The replacement ratio was first evaluated by tensile strength, elongation at break, and Shore A hardness. The highest measured tensile strength was 12.96 MPa at 7% replacement, but it was not statistically different from the 0%, 5%, 9%, 11%, and 13% formulations. At 15% replacement, high‐aspect‐ratio CSW (HRCSW), anhydrous CSW (ACSW), and surface‐modified CSW were compared. HRCSW showed the highest tensile strength (12.68 MPa), while CSW‐Ti1 exhibited the highest elongation at break (489.39%). CSW‐Si and ACSW showed relatively high hardness. Surface modification altered the apparent water wettability and surface chemical environment of CSW without obvious bulk‐phase transformation. SEM observations suggested contributions from whisker bridging, pull‐out, crack deflection, and stress concentration. Overall, the mechanical response depends on the combined effects of replacement ratio, whisker geometry, crystalline state, and surface characteristics.

CD3ε F(ab’)₂ PET imaging captures systemic and intratumoral T-cell response to immune checkpoint blockade
abstract: Abstract Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet only a subset of patients achieve durable responses. Because the spatial distribution of T cells within tumors and lymphoid tissues shapes therapeutic outcomes, noninvasive methods capable of monitoring these populations could improve the evaluation of antitumor immune responses. Here, we report the validation of a CD3ε-targeted F(ab’) 2 positron emission tomography (PET) probe for noninvasive mapping of T-lymphocytes across tumors and lymphoid tissues and characterize its effects on endogenous T-cell biology. Relative to the full-length IgG construct, the F(ab’) 2 format demonstrated more rapid blood clearance, enabled high-contrast imaging within 24 h, produced limited changes in endogenous T-cell populations, and did not measurably impair T-cell activation at imaging-relevant concentrations. CD3ε F(ab’) 2 PET detected tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and lymphocytes within the tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLN) across multiple syngeneic tumor models and in a genetically engineered mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma. In a combination immunotherapy study, tumor uptake distinguished responding from non-responding lesions and detected treatment-associated changes across peripheral lymphoid tissues. These results support CD3ε F(ab’) 2 PET as a noninvasive imaging approach that enables assessment of T-cell distributi…

title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavi…

title: Predictors of Response to Neoadjuvant Systemic Therapy and Survival in Patients with cN1 Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with clinically node-positive (cN1) breast cancer represent a heterogeneous population with evolving axillary management strategies. We evaluated whether extent of axillary nodal involvement is associated with survival in cN1 disease. Methods A retrospective study of patients with cT1-4N1M0 breast cancer and biopsy-proven axillary metastasis (2012–2018) was performed. All patients underwent axillary ultrasound (AUS) prior to neoadjuvant systemic therapy (NST) and again before surgery. Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used for statistical analysis. Results Among 825 patients, most had cT2-3 (75.6%), hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2−; 73%), ductal (89.7%) carcinoma. 64.1% (529) had 1–3 abnormal nodes on pretreatment AUS, whereas 35.9% had > 3 abnormal nodes. Definitive axillary surgery consisted of axillary lymph node dissection in 83.3% and sentinel node biopsy or targeted axillary dissection in 16.7%. Pathologic complete response (pCR) rate (breast and nodes) was 22.7%; breast-only and nodal-only pCR rates were 6.4% and 11.8%, respectively. At median follow-up of 5.6 years, 5-year overall survival, breast cancer-specific survival, and event-free survival were 92%, 94%, and 91%, respectively.
