Integrating machine-learning-based landslide susceptibility and vulnerability for slope-unit risk assessment
abstract: Landslide susceptibility identifies terrain associated with landslide occurrence, whereas risk prioritization also requires information on the vulnerability of threatened elements. This letter presents a slope-unit framework linking machine-learning susceptibility prediction, SHAP-based interpretation, and vulnerability-based relative risk classification. Four models were evaluated using a regional test dataset, and the selected model was applied to 393 slope units. XGBoost achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.952), followed by random forest (0.904), logistic regression (0.662), and support vector machine (0.600). Paired DeLong tests indicated significant differences between XGBoost and logistic regression (LR) and support vector machine (SVM), but not random forest (RF). SHAP analysis identified slope, relief, and elevation as the leading predictors, accounting for 62.83% of normalized grouped importance. High and very high relative risk occupied 21.34% of the mapped slope-unit area. Of 69 very-high-susceptibility units, only 13 were classified as very high risk after vulnerability integration. The framework supports the identification of priority slope units for targeted field investigation, monitoring, and mitigation planning.

The Power of Behavioral Antecedents in Predicting Supply Chain Performance of Crop Seed Enterprises
abstract: This study examined whether opportunistic behavior, supply chain collaboration, social bonds (supply chain socialization) and human resource practices predict supply chain performance, measured as quality, response time, productivity and financial/cost performance, in crop seed enterprises in Kenya. Guided by social exchange and systems theories, a quantitative survey was conducted of 143 crop seed enterprises registered in Kenya as of 2024. Data were collected from supply chain heads, operations officers or their equivalents in public and private seed companies and analyzed using structural equation modeling, with each driver tested in a separate prediction model. Each hypothesis was partially supported, with one performance dimension significantly related to each driver. Opportunistic behavior significantly lowered quality (b = ?0.40, p = .036). Supply chain collaboration (b = 0.225, p = .040) and human resource practices (b = 0.225, p = .033) were positively associated with productivity, while social bonds were associated with shorter response times (b = ?1.024, p = .034). No driver significantly predicted financial/cost performance at the .05 level. title: Transformación digital en la gestión de cobros electrónicos a través de una aplicación móvil
abstract: La transformación digital representa en una pieza clave para modernizar los procesos que involucran a la gestión de cobros electrónicos dentro de las microempresas. A este respecto la presente investigación tuvo como objetivo desarrollar un proceso para la gestión de cobros electrónicos a través de una aplicación móvil. Para esto se realizó una revisión científica en base de datos recomendados, por consiguiente, se desarrolló una herramienta tecnológica el mismo que se puso a prueba en una cadena de restaurantes en Ecuador y se evaluó mediante la aplicación del instrumento modelo de aceptación tecnológica a dueños de cada negocio. Los resultados arrojaron que la propuesta del aplicativo ayuda a controlar y de mejor manera el registro de los cobros electrónicos brinda confiabilidad al momento de uso y atiende a las necesidades de un negocio.

title: Design and Implementation of a Zero Trust API Gateway for Secure and Risk-Aware API Access
abstract: APIs connect clients, applications, and services, but perimeter-based controls alone do not provide sufficient protection when credentials are compromised or traffic crosses distributed environments. This paper describes the design and implementation of a Zero Trust API gateway developed as an inline policy-enforcement layer for protected services. The prototype is implemented with FastAPI and combines password-based authentication, OAuth sign-in, JSON Web Tokens, time-based one-time-password multi-factor authentication, scoped API keys, refresh-token rotation, and role- and scope-based authorization. Its request pipeline includes IP blocking, request logging, adaptive risk scoring, sliding-window rate limiting, and a rule-based web application firewall. The gateway also provides a reverse-proxy component that resolves registered upstream services, applies destination checks, forwards permitted requests, and records request identifiers and timing information. Additional detection components evaluate behavioral signals, impossible-travel indicators, and per-user anomalies using an Isolation Forest model when the required machine-learning dependency is available. Functional verification covers successful and rejected authentication, authorization boundaries, rate-limit responses, malicious-input detection, and proxy behavior. title: Construction and Empirical Analysis of a Multi-Source Assessment System for Theoretical Mechanics under an Outcome-Based Education Framework
abstract: To overcome the limitations of using a single aggregate score to distinguish differences in knowledge mastery, engineering application, and learning-process performance in Theoretical Mechanics, this study developed a multi-source assessment framework based on outcome-based education (OBE). The framework links course outcomes, assessment components, evidence sources, and instructional improvement. Data were collected from two intact classes of Mechanical Design, Manufacturing and Automation in the first semester of the 2025-2026 academic year and included stage tests, homework, learning-management-system (LMS) quizzes, an integrated project, and item-level final-examination scores. The mean final-examination score was 51.17 ± 22.89. The cohort attainment levels for Course Outcomes 1, 2, and 3 were 0.513, 0.436, and 0.553, respectively. Mean stage-test and LMS-quiz scores showed moderate positive correlations with final-examination performance (r = 0.461 and 0.406, respectively; p < 0.01). Project scores were high with limited dispersion and were not significantly correlated with final-examination scores. The multi-source assessment identified kinematics and multi-step calculation tasks as the main learning bottlenecks and revealed insufficient discrimination in project scoring. title: QRIS CROSS-BORDER AS DIGITAL SOFT POWER SUPPORTING SUSTAINABLE SHOPPING TOURISM: EVIDENCE FROM BATAM, INDONESIA
abstract: The rapid expansion of cross-border digital payment systems has transformed shopping tourism by enhancing transaction efficiency, convenience, and accessibility for international visitors. This study examines the role of Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) Cross-Border in supporting sustainable shopping tourism in Batam, Indonesia, while exploring its function as an instrument of Indonesia's digital soft power. Employing an exploratory qualitative case study design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 25 purposively selected participants comprising policymakers, tourism stakeholders, micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSME) operators, Malaysian and Singaporean tourists, and Batam residents. The study was further supported by non-participant observations at major shopping destinations and netnographic analysis of publicly available digital content related to cross-border payment experiences. The data were analysed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal four major themes. First, QRIS Cross-Border enhances tourists' shopping experiences by reducing cash dependency, minimising currency exchange concerns, and facilitating seamless transactions. Customer Engagement and Lead Conversion in Automotive Retail
abstract: This exploratory research paper examines customer engagement and lead conversion at a private Škoda dealership in Pune, India. The study draws on a confirmed aggregate activity summary of 52 walk-in customers observed during a three-month internship, together with an anonymised 24-record enquiry extract. Of the 52 walk-ins, 45 completed a test drive, six booked within the internship period, and three additional bookings were known to occur later. The enquiry extract shows interest concentrated in the Slavia and Kylaq models, although the extract is not a complete cohort and cannot represent the dealership or market as a whole. Field observations from both authors inform a process-level interpretation of needs discovery, product explanation, test-drive coordination, and follow-up. The analysis is descriptive: it does not estimate causal effects, compare dealerships, or attribute booking outcomes to a single intervention. The findings suggest that a dealership should treat the test drive as an intermediate engagement stage and maintain a consent-aware, structured follow-up process that distinguishes in-period bookings from later conversions. The paper contributes a carefully bounded practitioner account of how customer-journey concepts can be applied to automotive retail while preserving the limits of a small, private operational dataset. Multimodal Emotion Detection in Distributed Data Streams: Deep Transformer Ensembles, Cross-Modal Attention Fusion, and Benchmark Evaluation
abstract: Emotion detection represents a vital frontier at the inter-section of affective computing, artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction (HCI). While traditional uni-modal systems—relying solely on text, speech acoustics, or static facial photographs—have established founda-tional benchmarks, they remain fundamentally fragile in real-world conversational dialogues characterized by lex-ical ambiguity, acoustic sarcasm, and visual occlusions. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end, publication-grade deep learning architecture for Multimodal Emo-tion Detection in Distributed Big Data Streams. Our framework synchronizes three specialized foundation models: a linguistic contextual transformer (RoBERTa-Large), a self-supervised acoustic representation encoder (Wav2Vec 2.0), and a spatiotemporal Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) integrated with Facial Action Unit (FAU) tracking. To resolve temporal granularity discrepancies and inter-modal information imbalance, we formulate a novel Hierarchical Cross-Modal Attention Fusion (HCAF) network. The HCAF module leverages bidirec-tional multi-head cross-attention to project acoustic and vi-sual features into the linguistic latent subspace, selectively attending to emotional cues across communicative chan-nels. Strategic Hotel Location and Customer Repurchase Intention: Insights from Hotel sector

The perception of hotel customers towards these practices while assessing and organizing the decisions for repatronizing a hotel. title: Did the Removal of Stock-Price Floors Improve Short-Run Price Discovery? An Event Study of the Dhaka Stock Exchange
abstract: This study examines whether the January 2024 removal of stock-price floors improved short-run price discovery and reduced price rigidity in the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE). An event-study technique was applied to 338 securities: 306 firms in the main removal cohort, 20 firms in the second-stage cohort, and 12 firms that retained their floors. Market-adjusted abnormal returns were used as the primary specification, while a market model and complete-window samples were used for robustness. Cross-sectional one-sample t-tests assessed abnormal returns, paired-sample t-tests compared pre- and post-removal zero-return rates and intraday high-low ranges, and Welch tests compared treatment cohorts with the retained-floor benchmark. The main cohort recorded a cumulative average abnormal return (CAAR) of -6.77% over [-5, +5], while the second-stage cohort recorded -18.87% over [-3, +3]. Zero-return rates fell from 49.84% to 5.36% in the main cohort and from 97.85% to 3.50% in the second-stage cohort, while intraday ranges increased significantly. The findings are robust for the shorter event windows but sensitive to sample completeness over the longest window. Abnormal returns, zero-return frequency, and the high-low range are proxy indicators rather than comprehensive measures of market efficiency.

title: Arrival Time Occupancy Forecasting for Electric Vehicle Charging Recommendations Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Queueing Models
abstract: A highway driver choosing where to charge needs to know whether a charger will be free when the car arrives, not whether it is free when the trip starts. Amplyt is a charging advisor built around that need. For each station it forecasts connector occupancy at the predicted arrival time and passes the forecast through a finite-capacity queueing model and an isotonic calibration layer. A data audit early in development showed that the original wait-time target could be rebuilt from availability recorded at the same moment, so the target was redefined and the affected workbook withdrawn. The cleaned corpus holds 463 observations of sixteen stations, and the gradient-boosted model was trained on 724 connector-level trials from thirteen of them. In date-blocked rolling-origin evaluation it scored a Brier of 0.1965 against 0.2183 for a station-hour baseline, but most of the gain comes from quiet stations: at the five busiest the improvement is 1.9 percent and statistically indistinguishable, and leave-one-station-out tests are worse at unseen stations. The end-to-end wait pipeline does not beat an always-zero baseline, so forecast minutes are withheld. Arrival-time availability can be shown honestly as bands with confidence tiers, but the data does not yet support wide deployment. abstract: This study compared traditional time-series and machine-learning methods for the monthly forecasting of government expenditure of Cambodia with dataset. The study employed a natural logarithm of the monthly flows of government expenditure from January 2009 to March 2016. The dataset has 207 observations and was divided into train set, where the general model training took place (80%) and test set out of sample (20%). Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) are the metrics that are used to evaluate forecasting performance. The study compares the benchmark against the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and four machine-learning approaches: Hybrid ARIMA-Random Forest, Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The ARIMA model detects a statistical significant seasonal autoregressive behaviour and a drift, indicating that government expenditure is characterized by long-run growth and seasonal dynamics. Nevertheless, the forecasting accuracy using the traditional method is outmatched by results of machine-learning models in general. In particular, XGBoost outperforms all the other models with the lowest MAE, RMSE and MAPE metrics indicating that it is the best forecasting technique. Longitudinal prediction of biological aging: replication and extension of DunedinPACNI
abstract: Abstract DunedinPACNI is a new brain-based aging biomarker derived from cross-sectional MRI data. This study extended previous work by testing whether DunedinPACNI predicts multisystem composites of biological aging in two midlife cohorts. Replicated results indicated that less education was associated with faster DunedinPACNI in both cohorts; novel findings demonstrated that faster DunedinPACNI was associated with higher biological aging in midlife and with accelerated biological aging over 7–15 years from mid-to-later life.

title: Prediction of Subsequent Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure After a 24-Hour Landmark in Cirrhotic Patients With Variceal Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background: Some cirrhotic patients admitted with variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding experience clinical deterioration during hospitalization and develop acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a critical event strongly associated with short-term mortality. Since ACLF may be reversible in its early stages, risk stratification prior to overt ACLF is clinically important. Methods: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study (2015–2025) involving cirrhotic patients admitted for esophagogastric variceal bleeding. A 24-hour landmark analysis was performed among patients who remained ACLF-free during the first 24 hours after admission, with subsequent ACLF before discharge as the primary outcome. Predictors were identified using LASSO and best-subset selection procedures. Logistic regression and random forest models were developed and compared with the available AIMS65 and Glasgow–Blatchford score (GBS) risk categories. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (AUC), calibration (CITL and calibration slope), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis with integrated net benefit). External validation was performed using an independent cohort. Results: Of 1,787 screened patients, 555 were included in the derivation cohort and 240 in the external validation cohort after application of the 24-hour landmark. title: Development of a Maintenance Management Cost-Effectiveness Prediction Model for Ageing Bridge Infrastructure: A Case of TARURA, Tanga Region, Tanzania
abstract: Bridges managed by the Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA) in Tanga Region are maintained largely reactively. About 78% of the annual bridge maintenance budget of TZS 850 million is spent on emergency repairs that cost 2.5 to 4 times more than equivalent preventive work. Existing bridge prediction models mostly predict condition rather than cost, require long inspection histories or large datasets, and omit institutional factors such as budget adequacy. This study therefore developed a maintenance management cost-effectiveness prediction model for ageing bridges in Tanga Region. It adopted a pragmatic philosophy and a convergent parallel mixed-methods design within a single case study of TARURA Tanga. Data were collected through document review, field observation and a structured questionnaire administered to 80 TARURA staff and contractors selected by stratified random and purposive sampling. Factors were ranked with the Relative Importance Index (RII). A multiple linear regression (MLR) model of annual maintenance cost was then estimated from the records of 80 bridges and benchmarked against a Random Forest. Seven of fourteen candidate factors met the RII threshold of 0.74, led by budget adequacy and allocation methods (0.970) and coastal exposure and corrosion (0.945). abstract: Agricultural productivity in India is strongly affected by weather variability, soil degradation and the over- or under-use of fertilizers. Farmers still tend to rely on personal experience when choosing a crop, estimating its yield and deciding how much fertilizer to apply. This paper presents an integrated, web-based decision-support system that performs three tasks within a single framework: crop recommendation, fertilizer recommendation and crop yield prediction. The system takes soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium), temperature, humidity, soil pH, rainfall, soil moisture, soil type and crop type as inputs. The pipeline consists of data acquisition from public repositories, cleaning and normalisation, correlation-based feature selection, and model training using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Random Forest (RF). Model performance is evaluated with cross-validation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and correlation-based measures. In the reported experiments, the ANN model for yield prediction reached an accuracy of 94.70% and the Random Forest model for fertilizer recommendation reached 93.94%, and the crop recommendation model [insert accuracy] was the best performer for its task. The models are packaged in a Java (JSP/Servlet, Weka, MySQL) web application that lets farmers obtain all three recommendations from one input form..

title: Microbiome‐Informed Genomic Prediction of CH4:CO2 Ratio in Holstein Dairy Cattle Using 16S rRNA Profiles and SNP Markers
abstract: ABSTRACT Ruminant animals produce methane as a by‐product of microbial fermentation in the rumen, with cattle being the largest contributors among ruminants. Methane emissions may be influenced directly by the host's genetics and indirectly through host‐mediated effects on rumen microbiome composition. In this study, we investigated whether modelling both direct and indirect genetic effects could improve the genomic prediction of breeding values for methane emissions. We used genotype, methane CH 4 :CO 2 ratio and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing data (16S), including 16S genus (16S‐G), 16S species (16S‐S) from Danish Holstein cows. A conventional genomic best linear unbiased prediction (GBLUP) model was used as a benchmark and compared with a microbiome‐informed GBLUP approach based on three linked linear mixed models for the prediction of breeding values. In GMBLUP, the first model regresses methane emissions on three random animal effects (archaeal 16S, bacterial 16S and polygenic effects) using corresponding microbiome and genomic relationship matrices. The second and third models separately regress archaeal and bacterial 16S on random animal effects defined by the genomic relationship matrix. We evaluated prediction accuracy using five‐fold cross‐validation. The GBLUP model, which used only genomic marker information, achieved a mean accuracy of 0.20 across the five folds…

title: A Comprehensive Review of AI and IoT-Based Water Pipeline Leakage Detection, Prediction and Monitoring Systems
abstract: Water pipeline leakage is a major challenge in water distribution and supply systems because undetected leaks can result in water loss, infrastructure damage, economic losses, and inefficient water management [5], [13]. Conventional leakage inspection methods often depend on manual inspection, periodic maintenance, or specialized equipment, which may not provide continuous real-time monitoring [5], [13]. Recent developments in the Internet of Things (IoT), sensor technology, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) have created opportunities for automated and intelligent pipeline monitoring [9], [11]. This review presents a study of recent techniques used for water pipeline leakage detection, localization, prediction, and monitoring. Different sensing approaches, including flow, pressure, acoustic, and vibration measurements, are reviewed along with machine-learning and deep-learning methods [1], [3], [4], [8], [12], [13]. Existing research demonstrates that pressure and flow measurements are widely used for hydraulic anomaly detection, while vibration and acoustic measurements can provide additional information about leakage events [5], [6], [7]. KUSp, a novel oral spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma cell line with epithelial-mesenchymal transition features and high invasive capacity
abstract: Abstract Spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma (SpSCC) is a rare and aggressive variant of squamous cell carcinoma characterized by biphasic histopathology and epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated features. The scarcity of well-characterized experimental models, particularly those derived from metastatic lesions, has limited investigation of its biology. Here, we established KUSp, a cell line derived from a cervical lymph node metastasis of oral SpSCC, and characterized its pathological, phenotypic, and functional features. The primary tumor showed conventional squamous and spindle cell components, whereas the metastatic lesion predominantly contained spindle-shaped tumor cells expressing both epithelial and mesenchymal markers. KUSp displayed a pronounced EMT-like phenotype characterized by a spindle-shaped morphology, loss of cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and E-cadherin expression, and expression of vimentin, N-cadherin, and α-smooth muscle actin. Functionally, KUSp showed significantly greater Matrigel invasion than the established oral SCC cell lines examined, including HOC313, together with robust migratory activity. title: Capacity Building and Performance of Agricultural Program in Rural Kenya
abstract: Climate-smart agricultural programs require effective monitoring and evaluation (M&E) systems supported by adequate human capacity to achieve sustainable development outcomes. This study examined the role of capacity building in the relationship between M&E tools and the performance of Climate-Smart Agricultural Programs in Rural Kenya. A mixed-methods approach employing descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational research designs was adopted. Data were collected from 246 respondents drawn from project beneficiaries and staff through structured questionnaires and key informant interviews. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and hierarchical multiple regression analyses were used to analyse the data. The findings revealed that respondents perceived capacity building, measured through level of training, technical skills, and technical competence, as highly implemented (overall mean = 4.24, SD = 0.61). Capacity building exhibited significant positive correlations with program performance, with level of training (r = 0.786, p < 0.001), technical skills (r = 0.753, p < 0.001), and technical competence (r = 0.631, p < 0.001) showing strong associations. Hierarchical regression analysis demonstrated that incorporating capacity building substantially increased the explanatory power of the model from 61.1% to 70.5% of the variance in program performance. abstract: Organizations increasingly use machine learning to identify customers, transactions, suppliers, and projects that require attention. Yet a high predicted risk does not establish that an intervention will help, that its benefit exceeds its cost, or that the underlying evidence permits action. This paper develops an analytical framework that connects prediction, intervention value, evidence verification, and limited managerial capacity. The framework combines temporally governed data, calibrated risk estimates, bounded intervention effects, constrained optimization, and selective human review. Its central object is a decision record linking each proposed action to the information available at the decision time, the assumptions behind its expected value, and the authority required for execution. Analytical propositions establish when risk ranking agrees with value ranking, how uncertainty changes the intervention threshold, and when additional review has positive expected value. A fully specified six-case worked example demonstrates the distinction. With capacity for two interventions, risk ranking produces an assumed expected net value of −1 unit, whereas value-based selection produces 54 units. A common uncertainty allowance of 0.10 reduces the optimized lower-bound value to 34 units. These quantities are arithmetic consequences of stated assumptions, not estimates from an organ…

title: Is histone H2B deubiquitylation via ATXN7L3-dependent enzymes a new mechanism disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders?
abstract: Abstract Neurodevelopmental disorders are lifelong debilitating conditions that affect cognition and originate during embryonic development. Being heterogeneous and with a variety of etiologies, most of these disorders have no targeted treatment or cures, due to our lack of knowledge on the underlying molecular mechanisms disrupted in their pathogenesis. An emerging epigenetic mechanism recently associated with neurodevelopmental disorders is ubiquitylation of histone H2B. This posttranslational modification controls gene expression during neurodevelopment, where histone H2B ubiquitylation levels are tightly regulated by multiple deubiquitylase protein complexes ensuring correct gene expression. Components of deubiquitylase complexes regulating histone H2B ubiquitylation are the protein scaffolds ATXN7L3 and ENY2, and the deubiquitylating enzymes USP22, USP27X, and USP51. Recent clinical studies have highlighted a potential role of H2B ubiquitylation in human neurodevelopment, including the identification of neurodevelopmental disorders associated with gene variants in the ATXN7L3 , USP27X and USP51 genes. Here, we summarize our knowledge of the functions of deubiquitylase complexes that regulate histone H2B ubiquitylation and their components in neurodevelopment, and describe ATXN7L3 , USP27X , and USP51 -associated disorders, proposing future directions on the required resear…

abstract: Abstract Background Digital tools can prepare patients for decisions, but effects on clinical dialogue are uncertain. We synthesized review-level evidence on shared decision-making and examined the role of timing and workflow. Methods We rapidly reviewed systematic, meta-analytic, and scoping reviews identified through targeted PubMed, publisher-platform, and citation searches to 17 July 2026. One reviewer selected, extracted, and appraised reports and revisited eligibility after extraction. We synthesized outcomes descriptively and developed an interpretive model. Results Eleven reviews were included. Knowledge, decisional conflict, and preparation generally improved; evidence for interpersonal processes was less extensive. Preconsultation aids increased reported decision discussion (68.6% versus 50.2%), whereas separate in-consultation trials, mostly of paper aids, improved observer ratings (mean difference 12.14; 95% confidence interval 8.12–16.16). The trial sets were not directly compared. The five proposed links were decision recognition, patient preparation, clinical visibility, deliberative interaction, and decision closure and follow-through; downstream safety evidence was sparse. Conclusion Digital preparation alone does not establish improved deliberation or safety. The model is interpretive and unvalidated. Comparative studies should test information flow and outcom…

title: Research on the Innovation of Financing Methods and Operation Mechanism of Low-Altitude Economy Enterprises
abstract: As an important carrier of new-type productivity, the low-altitude economy generally faces financing difficulties such as “high R&D investment, lagging profitability, and few collateral assets.” Traditional bank lending, which focuses on fixed asset collateral and stable cash flow as its core evaluation logic, is inherently mismatched with the asset structure of low-altitude enterprises, which is mainly composed of intangible assets such as patents and flight data. This paper takes the “first national low-altitude economy ABS” and the first national dual “cross-border” intellectual property securitization project as core cases to systematically analyze the operation mechanism of two innovative financing methods: financial leasing ABS and intellectual property securitization. The study found that financial leasing ABS, through the transmission chain of “leasing receivables packaging - asset pool construction - structured stratification-exchange listing,” transforms the future cash flow of low-altitude equipment leasing into tradable standardized securities. The first product issued by Science City Leasing reached a scale of 584 million yuan, with a priority A1 tranche interest rate of only 1.9%. MERIT: Mechanism-Driven Model Predicts Drug Outcomes and Nominates Indications for Failed Drugs
abstract: Abstract Drug development depends on efficacy and safety, but many trial-outcome prediction models incorporate trial design, prior development history, or compound identity, enabling compound memorization and inflating apparent performance. We developed MEchanism-Resolved Inference of Trial outcomes (MERIT), a model that predicts trial outcomes from molecular and disease features without using information on similar-compound success. MERIT integrates the disease and drug of interest with large-scale drug–protein, protein–metabolite, and immune interaction maps to link a drug’s intended and potential off-target effects to tissue-specific efficacy and safety. Across 753 small-molecule drugs and 3,133 trials, MERIT achieved an overall AUROC of 0.770 (0.765 for efficacy and 0.784 for safety) under structure-holdout evaluation, outperforming two published methods retrained on the same trials and folds. Scored by a mechanism-fit profiling, MERIT ranked the approved indication above the failed one for 83% (50 of 60) of a preselected set of 60 cohort compounds that failed one indication but are approved for another. Finally, we registered locked, outcome-blind predictions for 55 drug-indication pairs in ongoing phase III trials for prospective evaluation.

abstract: استهدف البحث دراسة الأحكام المنظمة للرقابة القضائية على أحكام التحكيم من خلال دعوى بطلان حكم التحكيم في نظام التحكيم السعودي، عبر بيان مفهوم الطبيعة القانونية لدعوى البطلان وخصائصها وإجراءاتها والآثار المترتبة على الحكم به. بالاعتماد على المنهج التحليلي في دراسة النصوص النظامية، وتم تقسيم البحث إلى مقدمة وأربعة مباحث، ونتائج. المبحث الأول: مفهوم الرقابة القضائية على حكم التحكيم. المبحث الثاني: دعوى بطلان حكم التحكيم: خصائصها وإجراءاتها. المبحث الثالث: أسباب الرقابة القضائية على حكم التحكيم من خلال دعوى البطلان. المبحث الرابع: آثار الرقابة القضائية على حكم التحكيم من خلال دعوى البطلان. وخلص البحث إلى أن الرقابة القضائية على أحكام التحكيم تقتصر على التحقق من سلامة الحكم النهائي في حدود الأسباب التي حددها النظام حصراً، بما يكفل عدم مخالفتها للنظام العام، كما أن دعوى البطلان تعد دعوى مستقلة ذات طبيعة خاصة وليست طريقا تقليديا من طرق الطعن، وأن الأحكام الجزئية أو التمهيدية الصادرة أثناء إجراءات التحكيم لا يجوز الطعن فيها استقلالاً، وإنما تثار أوجه الاعتراضات المتعلقة بها ضمن دعوى بطلان الحكم المنهي للخصومة.

title: The influence mechanism of AIGC-driven “learning-thinking-applying-creating” integrated animation instructional design on college students’ cognitive load and creative thinking
abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence has entered animation classrooms faster than research has been able to describe what it does to learning. This study developed a “Learning-Thinking-Applying-Creating” (LTAC) integrated teaching model built on an open-source AIGC toolchain and evaluated it in a twelve-week quasi-experiment with second-year animation students, two intact classes being allocated to an experimental or a control condition. Cognitive load was measured with a three-subscale instrument adapted from Paas and from Leppink and colleagues, and divergent thinking with an abbreviated Torrance-type battery scored for fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration by two trained raters who worked blind to group and occasion (intraclass correlations 0.86 to 0.91). Data were collected at pretest, mid-test, and posttest. Analysis of covariance indicated that the intervention lowered extraneous load and raised germane load while leaving intrinsic load unchanged. Repeated-measures analysis revealed selective gains: originality and elaboration improved more in the experimental group, whereas fluency and flexibility rose in both. title: Modulation mechanism of L-tryptophan and phosphate to the chicken extracellular calcium-sensing receptor via downstream G protein-coupled signaling cascades and their binding modes
abstract: Abstract Laying hens undergo dynamic bone turnover and have a high demand for calcium due to the daily egg-laying cycle. The chicken extracellular calcium-sensing receptor (cCaSR) plays an important role in calcium homeostasis. This study investigated the modulatory effects and mechanisms of L-tryptophan (L-Trp) and inorganic phosphate (PO₄³⁻) on cCaSR-mediated signaling. A stable Flp-In™-293 cell line expressing cCaSR was established and used in a completely randomized in vitro cell culture design. Individual cell culture wells served as the experimental unit, with at least three technical replicates per experiment and at least three independent experiments. cCaSR activation was evaluated using luciferase reporter assays and a cAMP assay to assess Gαq-, Gβγ/Gαi-, Gα12-, and Gαi-mediated signaling. Dose-response curves were fitted by nonlinear regression, and data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s or Tukey’s multiple-comparison test (P < 0.05). L-Trp enhanced Ca²⁺-mediated cCaSR activation, shifting the Ca²⁺ EC50 by 12.88%, 5.18%, and 1.02% in the Gαq, Gβγ/Gαi, and Gα12 pathways, respectively, whereas the Ca²⁺ IC50 for cAMP shifted by 10.15% in the Gαi pathway. The calcimimetic R568 was used to partially substitute for Ca²⁺ to minimize Ca²⁺-phosphate interactions. Enhanced rock weathering for sustainable carbon capture: advances, challenges, and future prospects in terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) is a carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy that accelerates mineral dissolution in terrestrial systems to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), with the potential for co-benefits across managed and natural ecosystems. This review evaluates ERW’s real-world effectiveness through the lens of measurable carbon fluxes and storage permanence. We synthesize evidence across geochemical kinetics, hydrology, mineralogy, particle size distributions, and biological mediation, showing that the wide range of reported field-scale carbon removal rates (approximately 0 to 9 t CO 2 per ha −1 yr −1 ) reflects diverse site-specific environmental conditions and complex geochemical, biological, and hydrological processes that cannot be explained by intrinsic mineral reactivity alone. Widely used proxies, such as total cation dissolutions, soil pH changes, or crop yield gains, are less reliable indicators of field-scale CDR than alkalinity export or cation mass balance. Furthermore, estimates of net CDR should account for both the efficiency of converting weathering products into durable carbonate storage and full lifecycle emissions. Lifecycle assessments consistently identify energy for grinding and logistics as the dominant sources of cost and emissions, implying an optimal particle fineness for maximizing net removal. title: Chitosan-Derived Carbon Dot/Polypyrrole/Hybrid Biomembrane Assembly for Photoresponsive DNA Delivery
abstract: Abstract DNA condensation, extracellular shielding, and intracellular release impose competing requirements on nonviral polyplexes. Here, chitosan-derived cationic carbonized domains, an in situ polymerized polypyrrole phase, and a protein-bearing hybrid biomembrane shell were spatially organized into a hierarchical plasmid carrier. Carbonization and PPy hybridization retained most fluorescamine-accessible amines while introducing intrinsic fluorescence and NIR responsiveness. Membrane coverage progressively reversed the surface charge and reduced model-protein adsorption, with an intermediate membrane/carrier/DNA ratio providing the optimal balance between interfacial shielding and cellular interaction. The resulting HEV-coated assemblies maintained approximately 84% DNA encapsulation and exhibited pH- and NIR-regulated release. Optimized assemblies achieved 93.38% uptake and 56.66% GFP expression in HeLa cells, while excessive irradiation reduced expression through photothermal cytotoxicity. These findings establish a hierarchical structure−property framework for coupling biopolymer-derived DNA-binding domains, a conjugated polymer phase, and a biological macromolecular interface.

title: From Carbon Trading to Transition Finance: Institutional Alignment in Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia’s carbon exchange and sustainable-finance taxonomy evolved along distinct regulatory pathways in 2023–2026. This qualitative documentary study examines when carbon-unit records can corroborate transition-finance disclosures without being mistaken for evidence of taxonomy eligibility. It compares national carbon-pricing legislation, amended exchange rules, the Carbon Unit Registry regulation, and successive Indonesian sustainable-finance taxonomies. Passage-level coding distinguishes binding legal requirements, regulator guidance, institutional announcements, and proposed causal mechanisms. The findings identify separate evidentiary objects: issuance and disposition of carbon units, mitigation-use authorisation, technical screening of financed activities, entity and portfolio classification, and financial disclosure. The July 2026 registry rule differentiates registry functions and carbon-unit uses, while the March 2026 taxonomy update highlights version-specific screening and safeguards. Neither set of instruments establishes successful migration, improved market liquidity, lower verification costs, or financing additionality. The article advances a provisional bounded-alignment framework based on scope-specific traceability, dated classifications, claim reconciliation, and accountable correction. Its economic implications remain testable propositions rather than meas…

Research of robustness of the cluster-variation method for identification of radio emission sources to anomalous and missing measurements in multi-position systems
abstract: A study of the robustness of the cluster-variation method for identifying radio emission sources intended for use in multi-position triangulation systems under conditions of significant a priori uncertainty is carried out. The influence of anomalous measurements, data omissions, asynchrony of observations and unfavorable geometry of direction finders on the accuracy and reliability of coordinate measurement is considered. Quantitative indicators of robustness are introduced that characterize the probability of correct identification of a source, the root-mean-square estimation error and the maximum permissible levels of degradation of measurement information. Based on the results of numerical simulation, the dependences of accuracy on the proportion of gross errors and the number of available channels are obtained. It is shown that the cluster-variation approach ensures operability under conditions in which classical statistical methods become unstable.

abstract: ABSTRACT Developing soft and conformable materials with enhanced charge generation and retention capabilities remains a critical barrier for next‐generation flexible triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). Here, we report a polarization‐coupled tribo‐negative film fabricated by integrating a room‐temperature ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (FNLC) material (FNLC‐1571) into an electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) mat. In contrast to traditional rigid fillers, the optimally engineered ferroelectric nematic phase (N F ) of FNLC‐1571 microdomains assists spontaneous soft polar ordering in the nanofibrous PVDF matrix. This facilitates the integration of dipolar interactions with the fluorinated ends of PVDF, thereby synergistically promoting the crystallization of the electroactive β‐phase, enhancing dielectric behavior, modulating surface potential, improving interfacial charge‐trapping ability, and increasing contact area for superior charge generation while maintaining mechanical flexibility. When paired with a polyethylenimine (PEI)‐coated polyamide‐6 (PA‐6) tribo‐positive counter layer, the optimized 1 wt.% FNLC/PVDF‐based TENG delivers stable electrical output under low‐amplitude mechanical periodic contact‐separation excitation (8N, 10 Hz), with a peak‐to‐peak open‐circuit voltage of ∼395 V, a short‐circuit current of ∼40 µA, and a transferred charge of ∼167 nC. title: Nonlinear Ozone-Phytoplankton-Sea-Ice Coupling Regulates Fine-Scale Gaseous Elemental Mercury Enhancement in the Arctic Marginal Ice Zone
abstract: Abstract Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. Multiscale spatial statistics, machine learning, and quantile regression were applied to MOSAiC in situ observations (June-September 2020). GEM exhibits strong fine-scale spatial autocorrelation at 10 km (Moran’s I = 0.876). Random forest model (R2 = 0.85) with SHAP attribution identified ozone (O3), chlorophyll a (Chla), and open water fraction (OWF) as dominant GEM predictors. Quantile regression revealed that nonlinear coupling among OWF, Chla, and O3 strengthens under high GEM concentrations. By further combining spatial analysis with quantile regression modeling, a GEM-sensitive region was identified (OWF = 0.156–0.404, Chla = 1.17–1.57 μg/L, O3 = 9.2–19.7 ppb); within this region, both the O3 × Chla and O3 × OWF interactions exhibited significant positive correlations. The positive effect of O3 × Chla persists across all regions, while the O3 × OWF coupling varies dynamically with the retreat of sea ice. O3 indirectly favors GEM accumulation via regulating phytoplankton, and sea-ice melt exerts stage-dependent modulation of atmospheric oxidizing capacity. This study identifies O3 as a critical MIZ mercury regulator, and embedding O3-mediated pathways in models improves GEM projections under Arct…

title: RADIAL ONE-DIMENSIONAL HEAT AND MOISTURE COUPLING MODEL FOR THE PREHEATING STAGE OF HOT-AIR DRYING OF CYLINDRICAL MEDICINAL MATERIALS
abstract: This paper focuses on the preheating equilibrium stage in the hot-air drying process of cylindrical medicinal materials. A radial one-dimensional unsteady heat and moisture coupling model is established under the assumptions of axisymmetric and isotropic material. Heat transfer inside the material follows Fourier’s law, moisture migration follows Fick’s law, and the surface exchanges heat and moisture with the drying environment through convective transfer, which is described by third-kind boundary conditions. The measured drying-room temperature and moisture content are processed by piecewise linear interpolation and adopted as time-varying boundary conditions, and the governing equations are solved by an explicit finite difference scheme. During 0–1800 s, the material is heated as a whole while pre-drying occurs mainly in a thin surface layer. At 1800 s, the surface and center temperatures reach 36.79°C and 33.58°C, respectively. The surface moisture content decreases from 2.55 to 1.45 kg/kg on a dry basis, whereas the center moisture content remains close to its initial value. Convergence tests and parameter sensitivity analysis show that the surface temperature is most sensitive to the convective heat transfer coefficient, while the surface moisture content is most sensitive to the convective mass transfer coefficient and the diffusion pre-exponential factor.

title: Meteorological Drivers of Outdoor VOC Exposure at a Repurposed Brownfield Site: Coupling Subsurface Emissions with Atmospheric Dispersion
abstract: Abstract Redevelopment of brownfield sites into open public spaces can expose people to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted from subsurface contamination. Conventional risk assessments rely on low-frequency sampling and static average concentrations, which systematically miss the transient peak-exposure episodes that define the reasonable maximum exposure. To address this gap, we developed a daily resolution, meteorologically driven modeling framework to assess outdoor VOC exposure at a repurposed industrial brownfield site in northern China over a full annual cycle. Simulated VOC concentrations varied by approximately one to two orders of magnitude and were validated against bimonthly field measurements. Results showed that subsurface VOC emission fluxes are governed jointly by soil temperature and soil moisture; once the volatilized vapors reach the ground surface, their atmospheric dispersion and dilution are further controlled by local wind speed. Using the daily resolution record, we then identified distinct meteorological precursor patterns that reliably precede extreme exposure events, and captured them with a logistic regression model built on four forecast-available predictors: air temperature, cumulative rainfall, wind speed, and the 2-day change in wind speed. Preferentially sampling these meteorologically identified episodes can provide representative data for…

title: Ad libitum eating and reduced exercise resolve impaired bone integrity after prolonged reductions in energy availability in mature female rodents
abstract: Reduced energy availability (EA) results in loss of bone mass and disruption of endocrine regulators of bone integrity, even in very active individuals. Our aim was to determine whether 12 weeks of less exercise and ad libitum eating would enable recovery of deficits incurred during 12 weeks of reduced EA, hypothesizing recovery would be improved in exercising rats. Female rats (n=64, 5 months old) were randomized to sedentary (SED) or exercise (EX) conditions and, within each group, to adlib-fed (ADLIB) or severe energy restriction (SEV-ER). Energy intake was restricted in all SEV-ER rats and exercise volume in SEV-ER EX rats calculated to produce equivalent 30% reductions in EA. After 12 weeks, SEV-ER EX rats exhibited no losses in lean/fat mass and total bone mass (DXA), metaphyseal %BV/TV, and distal femur and femoral neck vBMD (by pQCT), and higher values for osteoblast activity than observed in SEV-ER SED animals. EX did not protect against declines in serum leptin and IGF-I. Half of each group recovered for 12 weeks, eating ADLIB and (in EX rats) reducing running volume by 50%. After 4 weeks recovery, body weight and energy availability for all SEV-ER rats matched those of ADLIB rats. By 12 weeks, there were no significant differences among groups for all variables. These results demonstrate that bone mass/microarchitecture and osteoblast activity observed in SED animals…

title: Differentiated Interfacial Proton Delivery for Durable CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton‐coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high‐rate CO 2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic‐and‐gap‐confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)‐modified Bi (Bi‐PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near‐surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen‐bond environment, while slow‐growth proton‐transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton‐delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to * OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential‐dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate‐related pathway response. Bi‐PDMS‐30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm − 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface‐deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO 2 ‐to‐formate electrosynthesis.

title: Effects of Shading Strategy on daylight illuminance and energy consumption for southern facades of Office Buildings
abstract: This study investigates the effects of exterior shading strategies on annual average daylight illuminance and electricity consumption for the southern façade of a two-story office building in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Using eQUEST, four cases were simulated: a baseline without shading, horizontal overhangs only, vertical fins only, and a combination of overhangs and fins. The results show that all shading configurations reduce electricity consumption compared with the baseline, while horizontal overhangs perform more effectively than vertical fins. The combined strategy achieves the lowest annual electricity consumption and the largest reduction in daylight illuminance. However, excessive shading also reduces the hours during which daylight illuminance remains above the setpoint, increasing electric lighting demand and limiting additional energy savings. The findings indicate that shading design should balance solar heat-gain reduction and daylight availability, with parameters adjusted according to climate, orientation, material, and building conditions.

title: Coordinated Economic Growth and Decarburization in Jiangsu Using an Integrated MOO–CCD Framework
abstract: Economic growth, carbon reduction, and environmental stewardship may all be achieved at once via the use of an optimization technique that takes trade-offs and multiple target progressions into account. Without fully grasping the complex interplay of financial, climatic, environmental, and resource implications, many current regional MOO studies aim for compromise solutions. The creation of a MOO and CCD framework in the Jiangsu Province, China, is the main subject of this study. From 2018 to 2030, we can see potential pathways for energy transition and company reorganization by analyzing eleven indicators: GDP, employment, water consumption, CO2, sulfur dioxide, NOx, PM, CO2, chemical oxygen demand, ammonia nitrogen and solid waste rounding it off. The study's basis is an input-output model with 47 components. Numerous factors are considered, including electricity-related situations, resource and emission coefficients from the past, and more. As a starting point for coordination, CCD ranks and evaluates potential MOO solutions once the optimal-point method has standardized the reduction and maximization objectives. All three scenarios put yearly GDP growth at 6.8%, with the precise number falling anywhere from 6.7% to 7.0%. We need to be more transparent about the moral judgments and assumptions that drive these changes because of the potential impact they have on the environm…

title: Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm −2 . The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.

title: Non‐Planar Chlorine‐Coordinated Activation of Triatomic Ruthenium Sites for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru‐based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen‐containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement‐pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine‐doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru 3 ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru 3 ON 6 Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru 3 ClNC delivers a high alkaline half‐wave potential ( E 1/2 ) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc‐air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru 3 ON 6 Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non‐planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d ‐band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate‐determining step of Ru 3 NC and OH * desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept…

Engineering Intraframework Energy Transfer in Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Luminescent Discrimination of Bisphenol Pollutants
abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent sensing relies on the generation, migration, and dissipation of excited‐state energy modulated by analytes. However, the contribution of intraframework energy transfer processes to sensing performance remains insufficiently studied. Owing to the highly tunable structures and designable energy transfer pathways, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide an ideal platform for dissecting detailed processes. Herein, a series of isostructural lanthanide MOFs were constructed from 2,5‐furandicarboxylic / 3,5‐pyridinedicarboxylic acid, enabling independent regulation of metal‐to‐metal and linker‐to‐linker energy transfer. Direct comparison of chemically integrated frameworks and their physical mixtures using bisphenol pollutants as probes reveals that metal‐to‐metal energy transfer dominates sensing performance, while linker‐to‐linker energy transfer contributes marginally. Mechanistic analyses indicate the impacts originate from the different energetic characteristics. Rigid lanthanide energy levels in Eu‐Tb systems create an “energy reservoir” that strongly regulate luminescence responses, whereas highly environment‐sensitive linker states in mixed‐linker systems give rise to self‐compensating energy transfer, resulting in a diminished influence. Moreover, the additional energy transfer pathways introduced by chemical integration can partially compensate for analy…

title: Entropy Generation Analysis of Unsteady Magnetohydrodynamic Buoyancy‐Driven Nanofluid Flow in a Porous Vertical Channel With Thermal Radiation and Chemical Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates entropy generation in an unsteady magneto‐hydrodynamic nanofluid flow with the influence of buoyancy forces embedded in a vertical porous channel. The simulation is carried out to assess the impact of thermal radiation and chemical reaction; the transport domain is bounded by a left‐cooled plate and a right‐heated plate. The schematic transport field reflects operating conditions commonly encountered in practical thermal and energy systems. The governing equations describing momentum, energy transfer, and nanoparticle concentration are nondimensionalized and solved numerically using a finite‐difference approach (FDA) to ensure stability across the computational domain. The study focuses on assessing the influence of physical parameters on the transport field and the features of the thermodynamic system. The involved parameters are velocity slip at the walls, magnetic field strength, porous medium permeability, thermal and solutal buoyancy parameters, radiation intensity, chemical reaction, Schmidt number, Brownian motion, thermophoretic, Biot number, and effects of viscous dissipation. Detailed analysis is carried out to assess the effects of varying these multi‐physical parameters on nanofluid velocity profiles, energy profiles, concentration profiles, entropy generation, as well as the Bejan number. The findings reveal that Navier slip and the…

title: Land Surface Temperature-Aware Optimization of Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Systems for Enhanced Energy Yield: A Comparative Assessment of Metaheuristic Algorithms in Adamawa State, Nigeria
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) energy-yield estimation in thermally variable environments requires consideration of spatial differences in environmental conditions beyond conventional solar-resource assessment. This study developed and comparatively evaluated a land surface temperature (LST)-aware optimization framework for grid-connected PV systems across seven locations in Adamawa State, Nigeria: Yola North, Yola South, Mubi North, Mubi South, Gombi, Numan, and Michika. Global horizontal irradiance, ambient temperature, wind speed, and satellite-derived LST were integrated within a temperature-coupled PV performance model in which LST was treated as a thermal indicator rather than being directly equated with module temperature. PV tilt angle, azimuth orientation, and installed capacity were optimized using Parametric Sweep, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Performance was evaluated using specific energy yield, improvement relative to baseline configurations, convergence behaviour, and solution stability. The optimized configurations exhibited tilt angles of 12–16°, azimuth angles of 165–180°, and installed capacities of 100–108 kWp, demonstrating spatial variation in the preferred PV configuration. At the algorithm level, PSO achieved the highest average specific yield of 2,550 kWh/kWp and a 7.6% improvement over its corresponding baseline, followed …

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in the Assessment of Low Energy Availability and Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) in Athletes Without Diabetes: A Critical Narrative Review
abstract: Background: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been proposed to support assessment of low energy availability (LEA) and Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), but its diagnostic value is uncertain. Aim: To critically evaluate CGM evidence relevant to LEA and REDs in athletes without diabetes. Material and methods: Two PubMed searches on 1 October 2026 yielded 145 unique records. AI-assisted assessment informed a purposive narrative synthesis of experimental, clinical, observational and measurement-agreement studies, supplemented by previously identified sources. Results: Severe short-term energy restriction reduced sensor glucose in one experiment, whereas studies of controlled LEA, nutritional intervention and clinically diagnosed REDs did not consistently identify differences in aggregate glucose metrics. Dietary composition, training, recovery and measurement conditions complicated interpretation. No reviewed study established a validated CGM threshold for identifying or excluding REDs. Conclusions: CGM remains an investigational adjunct. Low readings do not confirm LEA or REDs, and an unremarkable profile does not exclude them. Prospective validation must establish whether CGM adds information beyond nutritional and clinical assessment.

title: Living with family discord: a qualitative exploration of anxiety experiences
abstract: Purpose: to explore anxiety experiences among individuals experiencing family disharmony, focusing on emotional manifestations, family-related triggers, impacts on everyday life, and coping strategies. Method: this study used a descriptive qualitative approach with three participants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and non-participant observation, then analyzed using thematic analysis to identify patterns and themes related to participants' anxiety experiences. Findings: revealed that anxiety associated with family disharmony manifested as fear, persistent worry, restlessness, and emotional insecurity. These experiences affected participants' academic concentration, emotional well-being, sleep, and social interactions. Participants used various coping strategies, including emotional expression, personal activities, conflict avoidance, and seeking social support. Implications: the findings highlight the importance of emotional support, healthy family communication, and appropriate coping strategies in addressing anxiety associated with family disharmony. They may also inform the development of more sensitive psychological counselling and support services for individuals experiencing family-related distress. title: Fully Roll‐to‐Roll Coated Large‐Area Perovskite Solar Modules on Indium‐Free Microgroove Substrates
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low‐cost, low‐carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll‐to‐roll coated, large‐area back‐contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm 2 achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm 2 . The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll‐to‐roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS‐compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x‐ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real‐world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.

Design and Preliminary Performance Evaluation of a SIMON–LWE Hybrid Encryption Scheme for Cloud-Based IoT
abstract: Cloud-based Internet of Things (IoT) networks have transformed data collection, processing and communication across a wide variety of industries, including healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, smart cities, transportation, and environmental monitoring. But, most of the resource constrained IoT devices have limited battery power, memory, storage and processing power, which make it hard to implement conventional cryptographic algorithms such as Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), Rivest–Shaumir–Adleman (RSA), and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) in them. Moreover, standard cryptographic systems are vulnerable to quantum computing attacks. In this work, we propose a resource-efficient encryption framework called SIMON-LBA, combining the SIMON block cipher with a key-generation scheme based on LWE lattice cryptography to achieve quantum resistance and compromise minimal resources. Numerical experimentation with the model was carried out in a simulated cloud-IoT environment using Python in a quantitative experimental approach. Over 100 iterations, the representative sensor data was assessed, such as PM2.5, temperature, and humidity data. Encryption and decryption times, throughput, energy usage, CPU usage and memory usage were measured and compared with a 100 iterations for each of the following algorithms: AES, RSA, ECC, DES, ChaCha20, SIMON, SPECK, Attribute-Based Signcryption…

title: Design and Atmospheric Application of a Large-Volume UV-Irradiated FEP Chamber for Mercury Redox Chemistry Studies
abstract: Abstract Understanding the atmospheric redox chemistry of mercury (Hg) is critical for accurately predicting its global transport, deposition, and environmental impacts. However, large uncertainties remain with respect to reaction mechanisms and oxidation rates that convert elemental mercury (Hg0) to its oxidized forms (HgI, HgII). In this study, we present the design, construction, and characterization of a 40 m3 UV-irradiated fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) environmental chamber developed to investigate Hg oxidation under controlled, atmospherically relevant conditions. The chamber is equipped with a suite of analytical instruments, including a dual-channel Hg analysis system with SI-traceable calibration, a heated Reactive Mercury Active System (RMAS), broadband cavity-enhanced absorption spectroscopy (BBCEAS) instruments, and additional gas analyzers for monitoring oxidants and trace gases. Characterization experiments were conducted to quantify residence time, mixing, and wall loss rates for key atmospheric constituents. The system provides a flexible platform for studying Hg oxidation mechanisms involving compounds such as hydroxyl radical (OH), ozone (O3), and bromine radicals (Br). Vigorous characterization of the atmospheric simulation chamber will allow determination of uncertainties in atmospheric Hg chemistry and improve global chemical transport models.

Reconstructing literary space using artificial intelligence-enhanced architectural representation methods: Georges Perec and the Plassaert Apartment
abstract: Positioned at the intersection of literature and architecture, this study explores how abstract spaces constructed in literary texts can be reconstructed using architectural representation tools and artificial intelligence technologies. The focus of the research is the Plassaert apartment in Georges Perec’s Life: A User’s Manual, which details the space through everyday objects and lists, and the users of this space across different periods. The object-human relationships, hoarding tendencies, and the psychological weight of the space described in the text have been transformed into architectural representations through artificial intelligence (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot). The study’s methodology is based on a spatial accumulation model constructed around the parameters of Actor, Space, and Time. The 5-Level Prompt Model has transformed these literary data into a visual language, producing the spatial counterpart of each actor in their own time. Within the scope of the findings, the layering created by the material concerns, psychological and social states of space users through objects has been concretised through spatial indicators. The narrative structure in Perec’s literature (chess and jigsaw puzzle metaphors) has been represented through conceptual collages. Chromosome-level reference genome assemblies and annotation of four diploid Aegilops
abstract: Abstract Background Aegilops species represent an important reservoir of genetic diversity for agronomic and end-use quality traits as well as resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses for wheat improvement. However, the limited availability of high-quality reference genomes has impeded the effective use of these wild relatives in breeding programs. Results Here, we present chromosome-level reference genome assemblies of four diploid Aegilops species: Ae. comosa , Ae. markgrafii , Ae. umbellulata and Ae. uniaristata . Using a hybrid strategy combining Pacific Bioscience (PacBio) HiFi sequencing, BioNano optical mapping and Hi-C scaffolding, we generated contiguous assemblies ranging from 3.58 to 4.48 Gb characterized by BUSCO completeness score ranging from 97.9 to 98.4%. RNASeq and IsoSeq data from multiple tissues were integrated to facilitate gene annotation. The annotation yielded a total of 47,246 to 51,203 protein-coding genes across the four species, while also characterizing the repeat element composition of these diploid Aegilops . Collinearity analyses identified conserved colinear blocks and revealed multiple intra- and inter-chromosomal rearrangements. Orthogroups shared among the Aegilops and Triticum species were used to perform a phylogenetic analysis that clarified evolutionary relationships among the genomes of this Aegilops/Triticum complex, where the diploid …

title: IDENTIFICATION OF PLANT-SPECIFIC YABBY TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR GENE FAMILY IN FALSE FLAX (CAMELINA SATIVA L.) AND IN SILICO EXPRESSION PROFILING
abstract: Camelina sativa is a hexaploid oilseed crop with remarkable agronomic resilience and industrial value; however, the YABBY transcription factor gene family remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive genome-wide identification and in silico characterization of the YABBY gene family in C. sativa, providing insights into its evolutionary relationships, structural organization, and potential regulatory functions. Seventeen YABBY genes (CsYABBYs) were identified through conserved-domain-based screening and systematically characterized for physicochemical features, evolutionary relationships, exon–intron architecture, conserved motifs, chromosomal locations, cis-regulatory elements, and evolutionary selection pressure. Comparative phylogenetic analysis with Arabidopsis thaliana and Theobroma cacao separated the CsYABBY proteins into five clusters (FIL/YAB3, YAB2, YAB5, CRC, and INO), indicating strong evolutionary conservation and functional similarity in each subfamily. Gene structure analysis showed that exon–intron organization was highly conserved in every clade. In contrast, MEME-based motif analysis identified ten conserved motifs, including the characteristic C2C2 zinc-finger and YABBY domains. Promoter analysis uncovered abundant cis-regulatory elements associated with various regulatory functions, suggesting extensive involvement of CsYA…

Advances and Paradigms in Modern Plant Bioinformatics: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Plant bioinformatics has undergone a paradigm shift from simple gene discovery and sequence alignment to AI-driven multi-omics integration, graph pangenomics, and precision molecular breeding. The intrinsic hyper-complexity of plant genomes—characterized by high polyploidy, extensive heterozygosity, massive repetitive element burdens, and dynamic structural variations—has mandated the invention of specialized assembly algorithms, statistically robust annotation pipelines, and high-dimensional deep learning architectures. This comprehensive review synthesizes core computational methodologies across de novo polyploid sequence assembly (Overlap-Layout-Consensus vs. De Bruijn Graphs), structural and evidence-based functional annotation, epigenomic landscape mapping (WGBS, ATAC-Seq), graph-based pangenomics, single-cell multi-omics resolution, and transcriptomic network modeling. Furthermore, we evaluate state-of-the-art transformer-based Genomic Language Models (GLMs), structural biology integrations (AlphaFold3/ESMFold), and specialized plant databases. Finally, key computational bottlenecks, infrastructure scaling considerations, and actionable computational frameworks for accelerating climate-resilient crop breeding are critically evaluated.

abstract: Abstract Purpose Plant-derived hydrolates are aqueous co-products of hydrodistillation that remain underexplored despite their potential as sustainable ingredients for topical formulation design. This study comparatively evaluated two topical semisolid platforms for hydrolate valorization: a thermoresponsive gel containing Anacardium occidentale L. hydrolate and an emulgel containing Pectis brevipedunculata hydrolate associated with babassu oil. Methods Both systems were based on Pluronic F127 and Carbopol 974P and were characterized by physical stability assessment, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, scanning electron microscopy, and semiquantitative antimicrobial screening against Escherichia coli , Staphylococcus aureus , and Candida albicans . Results Incorporation of the whole hydrolate-containing aqueous fractions into the complete formulations was associated with formulation-dependent changes in matrix organization and resazurin-based metabolic activity scores. The A. occidentale hydrolate-loaded gel showed a visually observed temperature-associated change in physical form, spectroscopic evidence compatible with non-covalent hydrolate–polymer interactions, reduced crystallinity, compact lamellar morphology, and a lower resazurin score at the highest tested formulation condition.​ The P. brevipedunculata hydrolate-loaded emulgel pr…

Do floral traits associated with pollination concurrently increase vulnerability to seed predators?
abstract: Abstract Floral traits associated with floral display that likely enhance pollinator attraction may inadvertently increase attractiveness to antagonists such as pre-dispersal seed predators, yet direct tests of this trade-off within closely related species remain scarce. We investigated this relationship in three threatened grass aloes - Aloe albida , A. craibii , and A. chortolirioides - that differ markedly in floral colour, display, morphology, and flowering ecology. We quantified fruit and seed damage, identified predator and parasitoid assemblages, and tested whether independently measured floral and plant traits predicted fruit and/or seed utilisation within each species. Substantial reproductive loss occurred in all three species, with fruit utilisation ranging from 45 to 79% and seed utilisation from 20 to 55%. The chalcid wasp Eurytoma aloineae was the most abundant seed predator across species. Species-level predation was lowest in the smaller, white-flowered A. albida and higher in the more conspicuous A. craibii and A. chortolirioides ; however, within-species model selection provided little support for a general effect of floral display size on predation. In A. craibii , seed utilisation increased with perianth tube depth, whereas the corresponding relationship with fruit utilisation was marginal. These results indicate species-specific associations between floral …

title: Ultra‐High Ionic Conductivity Sulfide‐Based Composite Membranes Paired With Stable Interfacial Layer Enables High‐Energy‐Density All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsic properties of sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SEs) are crucial for achieving all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with high safety and high energy density, yet it is challenging to fabricate high‐performance sulfide SE films in a scalable approach. Furthermore, the inevitable side reactions between sulfide SE and lithium metal anodes exacerbate interfacial incompatibility, causing degradation in the cyclic stability. Here, a high‐performance sulfide SE (Li 5.4 PS 4.4 Cl 0.8 Br 0.8 ) was selected as the base phase to compensate for the loss of electrochemical performance during the dry film‐forming process. It was then combined with Polytetrafluoroethylene binder to prepare a high‐ionic‐conductivity composite membrane (HICCM). To mitigate side reactions between HICCM and the anode, a LiF‐rich interfacial layer forms in situ on the lithium metal surface, and the assembled symmetric cell achieves a high critical current density of 1.3 mA cm −2 and stable cycling for 2000 h (0.2 mA cm −2 ). For electrochemical performance, HICCM exhibits fast ion transport kinetics and electrical insulation, allowing the ASSB configured as FeS 2 //HICCM//LiF‐Li to achieve an energy density of 416.5 Wh kg −1 at a high loading of 3.4 mAh cm −2 . This work demonstrates that by combining HICCM with a stable interface design, ASSBs can achieve longevity and high cell‐level energy densi…
