title: Rational Terminal‐Group Engineering of Guest Acceptors for 20.7% Efficient Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy‐level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active‐layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S‐SMA and AS‐SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8‐BO with a weaker electron‐withdrawing 2‐(3‐ethyl‐4‐oxothiazolidin‐2‐ylidene)malononitrile (CN‐Rh) unit. This terminal‐group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8‐BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid‐to‐solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S‐SMA, asymmetric AS‐SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap‐assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8‐BO:AS‐SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal‐group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy‐level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and mor…

Integrated model of financial literacy, digital trading platforms, and behavioural biases (FL–DT–BB): A comprehensive review of retail investors’ investment decisions
abstract: The rapid digitalisation of financial markets has increased retail investor participation, particularly in emerging economies such as India. However, existing literature largely examines financial literacy, digital trading platforms, and behavioural biases independently, limiting an integrated understanding of their combined influence on retail investors’ investment decision-making. This study examines the investment behaviour of retail investors by synthesising prior research on financial literacy, digital trading platforms, and behavioural biases. Specifically, the study investigates how financial literacy and digital trading platform characteristics interact through behavioural biases to influence retail investors’ investment decision-making and develops an integrated Financial Literacy–Digital Trading Platforms–Behavioural Biases (FL–DT–BB) conceptual framework. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review methodology guided by the PRISMA framework. Academic literature was collected from Scopus, Web of Science, JSTOR, ProQuest, SSRN, ResearchGate, and Google Scholar. A total of 122 records were identified, of which 71 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis after screening. The results show that financial literacy improves investors’ understanding of risk–return trade-offs but does not independently ensure rational investment decision-making in digital trading c…

title: Structural Evolution of State-Dependent Kinetics during Potassium Storage in Layered CrSe2
abstract: Abstract Layered CrSe2 reversibly accommodates approximately one potassium (K) per formula unit, but the structural origin of its rate-dependent capacity remains unresolved. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) reveals the sequential P-3m1-R3m-C2/m phase pathway during cycling at different current rates. The P-3m1/R3m transformation exhibits the lattice discontinuity and becomes incomplete when increasing the current rate, as directly observed by operando SXRD. Chemical K deintercalation and state-resolved impedance measurements provide complementary evidence for sluggish kinetics near the fully deintercalated regime. Restricting the upper cutoff voltage will sacrifice some capacity but will improve electrochemical cycling capacity retention. These findings identify a particularly rate-sensitive structural region and show how phase-resolved characterization can guide voltage-window selection for layered potassium-storage electrodes.

title: Element-Selective Surface Reconstruction of Stainless Steel Anodes Governed by the Electrolyte Environment: Insights from High-Throughput Experiments
abstract: Abstract In neutral and mildly alkaline water electrolysis, electrolytes are primarily viewed as media controlling macroscopic solution properties such as pH and ionic conductivity. Beyond this conventional role, electrolyte species can interact with metal ions and dynamically reconstruct electrode surfaces through dissolution and reformation. Although such reconstruction is widely recognized, the extent to which operating surfaces retain the initial oxidation history or are governed by the electrolyte environment remains unclear. Here, a high-throughput electrochemical platform evaluated cell voltages under 108 conditions using 304 stainless steel anodes, independently varying anodic pretreatment, electrolyte pH (9.5, 10.5, and 11.5), phosphate concentration (1 and 3 M), and electrolysis regime. Analysis of variance showed that pH accounted for 70–81% of cell-voltage variation, whereas anodic pretreatment accounted for only 6–7%, demonstrating the dominant influence of the electrolyte environment on the electrochemical response. Surface analyses revealed widespread nickel depletion and heterogeneous chromium-rich films under lower-pH, high-phosphate conditions. Iron behavior was consistent with the equilibrium solubility trend, whereas nickel depletion did not follow the equilibrium solubility trend, indicating the involvement of processes beyond equilibrium thermodynamics. To…

title: Elastic‐Invisibility‐Enabled Metastructure With Mechanically Programmed Nonlinear Resonators for Vibration Attenuation and Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical programming provides a simple way to tune embedded nonlinear resonators without redesigning the host structure. Here, seven magneto‐elastic piezoelectric resonators are integrated into elastically reconstructed openings of a host beam. The removed stiffness, mass, and inertia are restored. The dynamics of the intact beam are therefore recovered over the investigated frequency range. Programming is performed by changing only the spacing between repulsive magnets. Each resonator can be set independently. This creates uniform, nonuniform, and graded combinations of monostable and bistable states. Experiments and simulations show marked changes in both vibration attenuation and harvested power. Different programs favor different functions. One configuration reaches 1.82 times the reference attenuation bandwidth. Another reaches 1.57 times the reference harvesting performance. Assuming nine admissible states per resonator, the seven‐resonator system spans possible configurations. Model‐selected candidates improve both numerical references simultaneously, reaching 1.16 times the attenuation bandwidth and 1.11 times the harvesting metric. The prototype also delivers up to 10.67 of total AC load power near resonance. The result is a structurally integrated platform with programmable nonlinear functionality and largely preserved host dynamics.

title: Natural Beeswax-Seed Oil Coatings for Shell Eggs: Effects on Physicochemical, Functional, and Microbiological Quality during Chilled Storage
abstract: Abstract Shell eggs lose quality rapidly during storage because the porous shell allows moisture and carbon dioxide to escape, allowing air and bacteria to enter. Beeswax is an effective natural barrier against moisture transfer; however, it possesses limited intrinsic antimicrobial activity. In this study, the effectiveness of beeswax-based coatings enriched with cold-pressed sesame oil or black cumin oil at concentrations of 3% and 5% (w/w) was evaluated for preserving the quality and microbial stability of grade A table eggs during 5 weeks of refrigerated storage at 4 °C. Uncoated, water-washed, and pure beeswax-coated eggs were included as control treatments. Quality attributes were assessed at weekly intervals and included weight loss, air-cell height, Haugh unit, yolk index, shape index, component weights, CIE color parameters, albumen and yolk pH, soluble solids content, foaming capacity, and emulsion stability. Microbiological quality was evaluated by enumerating total aerobic mesophilic bacteria, coliforms, and molds and yeasts. Coating treatment significantly affected weight loss, air-cell height, yolk index, albumen and yolk pH, albumen and yolk color, foaming capacity, emulsion stability, and all microbial counts (P < 0.05), whereas Haugh unit, shape index, shell thickness, and yolk weight were not significantly affected. Storage time and the treatment × time int…

Performance and Security Challenges in Cloud-Based Data Storage Systems: A Secondary Empirical Analysis of Object-Storage Latency, Throughput, Availability, and Cyber Risk
abstract: Cloud-based data storage offers elastic capacity, geographic redundancy, and pay-per-use access, but organizations must balance performance variability with security exposure. This study synthesizes secondary evidence from three performance studies, official reliability documentation from Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, and authoritative threat reports from NIST, the Cloud Security Alliance, Verizon, and ENISA. The analysis examines request latency, throughput, concurrency, durability, availability, misconfiguration, identity and access management, vulnerability exploitation, ransomware, and data exfiltration. In a one-million-request experiment using 1 KiB objects, S3 Standard recorded median read and write latencies of 27 ms and 40 ms, compared with 5 ms and 8 ms for S3 Express, representing reductions of 81.5% and 80.0%. An eight-week object-storage study reported per-object bandwidth of approximately 25–95 MiB/s and aggregate throughput of 75–90 Gbit/s under high concurrency. Security evidence identifies misconfiguration, weak access control, vulnerability exploitation, and ransomware as major risks. The study proposes a performance-security co-optimization framework combining workload-aware storage selection, bounded asynchronous I/O, least-privilege access, encryption, immutable recovery copies, continuous configuration assessment, and centralized …

abstract: The research work describes a unified battery management technique that involves a digital twin-based method that encompasses practically validated theory, data-oriented state evaluation, embedded management, and Internet of Things supervision. The task employs two connected phases of experimentation. The first phase consists in the analysis of a six-cell lithium-ion battery pack 3S2P 18650 in twelve operation modes, which consists of using both 0.5C, 1C, and 2C discharges under ambient temperatures of 25°C, 35°C, and 45°C with dynamic loading. The data obtained in the analysis of the voltage, current, temperature, capacity, and energy indicators will serve as calibration data for a second-order Thevenin equivalency circuit digital twin in MATLAB. Phase II benchmarks Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM models on 9,742 records from the NASA lithium-ion battery dataset and integrates the selected Random Forest model with an ESP32-based BMS prototype. The embedded platform combines dual INA219 current sensors, a 2-channel relay module, local LCD monitoring, MQTT communication, a Flask-SocketIO dashboard, and a staged voltage-protection strategy. The digital twin reproduces the measured voltage response with RMSE below 0.08 V and R² above 0.98 across the reported constant-current validation cases. In the AI benchmark, Random Forest reaches R² = 0.976, compared with 0.951 for XGBoost a…

Coordination Geometry Reconstruction Mitigates α‑Dihedral Angle Restriction of Polyanionic‐Type Cathodes for Ultrafast Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries have attracted extensive attention for large‑scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of sodium resources. However, the near‑coplanar structure geometry of polyanionic‐type cathodes causes in‑plane stress and electrostatic barriers, which lead to blocked Na + transport kinetics and hinder their practical application. Herein, an α‑plane, defined by the transition metal and its coordinating dangling anions, is identified as the critical structural bottleneck for Na + diffusion. By screening and tuning the dangling anions, a coordination geometry reconstruction is achieved that twists the α‑plane into α1‐ and α2‐planes. This twisting behavior breaks α‑plane restriction and relieves the in‑plane stress, thereby lowering the Na + migration barrier. Concurrently, the geometry reconstruction enlarges the Na2‑centered polyhedral volume and increases the Na2 site occupancy from 0.56 to 0.62. Thus, the modified cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 130 mAh g −1 and outstanding rate capability, with 80% retention at 30 C and 83 mAh g −1 at 50 C. It also exhibits excellent wide‐temperature operability (−40°C to 55°C) and stable full‑cell performance. The universality of this strategy is validated on several polyanionic cathodes. This work reveals the α‑plane as a tunable structural parameter, offering a geometry‑electronic synergy para…

title: In Situ Plasma Upcycling of Spent-Battery Graphite into Active WO3/Graphene Oxide Heterointerfaces for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution: Experimental and DFT Insights
abstract: Abstract Converting waste materials into high-value electrocatalysts through advanced synthesis technologies represents a sustainable strategy for resource recycling and clean hydrogen production. Herein, a one-step plasma-assisted electrochemical strategy, followed by ultrasonic dispersion, was developed to synthesize WO3-decorated graphene oxide heterostructures directly from spent battery graphite and tungsten rods. Among the investigated compositions, the optimized catalyst synthesized using one graphite cathode rod and three tungsten cathode rods exhibited excellent hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) performance in 0.5 M H2SO4, requiring an overpotential of 156 mV to achieve 10 mA cm–2 with a Tafel slope of 65 mV dec–1. The superior activity is attributed to strong electronic coupling at the WO3@GO heterointerface, which promotes accessible oxide–carbon interfaces and facilitates interfacial charge transfer. Density functional theory calculations further revealed interfacial charge redistribution, W 5d–O 2p–C 2p orbital hybridization, and increased electronic states near the Fermi level. The catalyst also achieved a Faradaic efficiency of 95% and sustained HER operation for 48 h with only a slight increase in overpotential and minor morphological changes after stability testing. This work demonstrates an efficient plasma-assisted route for simultaneously upcycling spent bat…

title: Interplay of Janus Polarization and Interfacial Electric Fields Governing Carrier Dynamics in MoS2/MoSSe Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract It is crucial to understand the role of polarization and the built-in electric field in heterostructures of two-dimensional materials, as these factors significantly affect carrier dynamics, interfacial properties, and device performance. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the electronic structure and excited-state carrier dynamics of MoS2/MoSSe heterostructures. We show that the interplay between the intrinsic polarization of Janus MoSSe and the interface-induced electric field strongly modulates interlayer charge transfer. This dual-field coupling drives a transition between type-I and type-II band alignments and switches the dominant carrier relaxation pathways from intralayer recombination to interlayer charge separation. Carrier relaxation is further governed by the interplay between nonadiabatic coupling and phonon-assisted transitions. These results identify polarity reversal as an effective strategy for tuning charge-transfer pathways and excited-state dynamics in van der Waals heterostructures, and provide guidance for designing two-dimensional optoelectronic and photocatalytic materials.

title: Review and analysis of tools for designing autonomous ground vehicle control systems
abstract: For the successful development of self-driving vehicles, as well as advanced driver-assistance systems, specialized programs are required. The purpose of this article is to provide an overview of the main tools for programming and virtual testing of autonomous driving systems for agricultural and road vehicles. Such tools as Autoware Foundation, Baidu Apollo, Siemens Simcenter Prescan, CARLA, MathWorks, Epic Games Unreal Engine, DSpace AURELION, Unity, Foretellix Foretify platform, IPG CarMaker, Cognata, Vector DYNA4, Nvidia Drive Sim, Vires Virtual Test Drive, VehicleSim, LG SVL Simulator are considered. The features and capabilities of each program are described, and a comparison is made according to the following parameters: distribution scheme – contractual or free, full and partial cycle programs, programming and visualization. The available operating systems for each program are listed. Among domestic companies, Sberbank (SberAutoTech) and Yandex (Yandex Self-Driving Group) stand out, which do not offer software as a product.

title: Digitalization of Specialist Modification Workshop Services Through a Customer Relationship Management Approach for Transparency in Vehicle Work Stages
abstract: Digitalization of specialist modification workshop services is needed to address scattered records and limited information regarding vehicle work stages. This study aims to build a web-based information system with a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) approach to integrate customer service and increase transparency of work progress. The study uses an applied research type with a descriptive approach and Prototype development method. Data were collected through observation, interviews, documentation, and literature studies, with owners or admins, mechanics, and customers as informants. The number of samples was not specifically stated. Analysis was carried out through business process identification, needs analysis, implementation of the Acquire, Enhance, and Retain stages, and Black Box Testing. The results show that the system integrates customer data, vehicles, orders, progress, documentation, consultations, complaints, and service history. Testing shows that the tested functions run according to the scenario. This system can support operational digitalization and transparency of workshop services

title: Dual Solar AC Charging System: A Review of Solar Photovoltaic Integration, Power Conversion and Electric Vehicle Charging Technology
abstract: The increasing demand for electric vehicles (EVs) and sustainable transportation has created a need for reliable, economical and environmentally friendly charging infrastructure. Solar photovoltaic (PV) energy provides a promising solution by utilizing renewable solar power for electric vehicle charging. This review paper presents an overview of a Dual Solar AC Charging System, in which two solar photovoltaic sources are integrated to provide electrical power for AC charging applications. The system can be designed with solar panels, solar charge controllers, maximum power point tracking (MPPT), power conditioning circuits, an inverter and suitable protection devices. The paper reviews existing solar-powered EV charging technologies, AC charging configurations, power electronic converters, energy management techniques and the challenges associated with solar energy utilization. It also discusses the possible integration of battery energy storage and grid backup to improve charging reliability during low solar irradiance and nighttime conditions. The dual-solar concept aims to improve solar energy utilization, reduce dependence on conventional grid electricity and support sustainable electric mobility

title: Effects of capacitive-resistive electric transfer therapy integrated with active rehabilitation on pain, sensorimotor function, and functional performance in subacute lateral ankle sprain: A randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Evidence on capacitive-resistive electric transfer (TECAR) applied concurrently with exercise in subacute lateral ankle sprain (LAS) is limited. Objective To evaluate the short-term effects of adding concurrent TECAR to exercise in subacute LAS. Methods Forty-two participants (20–40 years) with grade I-II LAS (10–21 days post-injury) were randomly allocated to exercise plus concurrent TECAR (EG; n = 21) or exercise alone (CG; n = 21). Both groups completed identical 20-min supervised sessions twice weekly for six weeks; TECAR did not extend session duration. Co-primary outcomes were pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale; NPRS) and Y-Balance Test (YBT) composite score ( α = 0.025). Secondary outcomes were joint position error (JPE) and Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM). Results All 42 randomized participants were analyzed; both groups improved on all outcomes ( p < 0.001). Versus exercise alone, TECAR was associated with greater improvements in pain (MD = 1.60, 95% CI 0.84–2.36, p < 0.001; below the 2-point minimal clinically important difference [MCID]), YBT composite (MD = 5.29%, 95% CI 1.44–9.14, p = 0.009), JPE (MD = 2.58°, 95% CI 2.03–3.13, p < 0.001), FAAM-ADL (MD = 10.39, 95% CI 7.72–13.06, p < 0.001), and FAAM-Sports (MD = 13.24, 95% CI 8.50–17.98, p < 0.001). Directional YBT differences did not survive multiplicity correction. Conclusion Adding TECAR was associ…

title: Almost-decoupling active control of in-wheel motors-driving 5DOF vehicle via complementary acceleration-difference feedback force control strategy
abstract: By incorporating the vertical–pitch dynamic coupling, the primary mechanism underlying motion sickness mitigating, we propose an almost-decoupling active control framework for a five-degree-of-freedom (5DOF) semi-vehicle powered by in-wheel motors (IWMs) grounded in frequency response analysis. A novel complementary acceleration-difference feedback (CAF) force control strategy is theoretically derived to suppress pitching angular acceleration and achieve almost-decoupling between vertical and pitch motions. The CAF force control law synthesizes suspension force from spatially differentiated vertical acceleration measurements acquired at the chassis–front and chassis–rear suspension interfaces. Root-mean-squared (RMS) values and frequency responses of key performance metrics, including vehicle-body acceleration, pitch angular acceleration, and related dynamic quantities are evaluated for the IWM-equipped 5-DOF semi-vehicle model subjected to stochastic road excitation conforming to ISO 8608 Class C. Results demonstrate that, across the speed range of 5–50 m/s, the proposed CAF force control strategy reduces the RMS pitch angular acceleration by up to 47.8% and attenuates its dominant frequency-domain peak amplitude by up to 41.1% at 20 m/s. The novelty of the proposed CAF force control strategy lies in its practical realizability and underlying almost-decoupling framework, not i…

title: Cation-Effect-Driven Modulation of Interfacial Solvation Structures Enables Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes. With benzyltriethylammonium serving as a model cationic regulator, we show that it accumulates near the polarized graphite surface and forms a cation layer that alters the local electric field. This cation-mediated interfacial regulation promotes PF6– accumulation at the interface, redirects early solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation toward anion-derived pathways, mitigates solvent decomposition, and accelerates Li+ desolvation and transport. As a result, graphite-based pouch cells deliver ∼88.2% state of charge within 6 min, maintain stable cycling for 2000 cycles with ∼71% capacity retention, and provide ∼218.2 Wh kg–1 with 10 min charging. Beyond LiPF6-based electrolytes, this cation effect also promotes reduction of the anions in other lithium-salt systems. This work bridges electrocatalytic cation effects and battery interfacial chemistry, offering a prac…

title: Data-centric Simulation Model for Electric Vehicle Charging Station Load Profiling and V2G Controls
abstract: The Electric Vehicle (EV) ecosystem significantly benefits from simulations that provide precise operational insights grounded in real-world data. This research proposes a data-centric simulation paradigm to generate 24-hour load profiles of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS). Specifically designed to serve as high-fidelity inputs for real-world simulators and digital twins, these profiles model charging execution, queuing delays, user responses to varying conditions, EVCS operational metrics, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) interactions. The paradigm utilizes an engineered real-world dataset derived from public charging operations within the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) grid regions. The framework integrates five interdependent stochastic modules: (i) an extended Non-Homogeneous Poisson Process (NHPP) utilizing cubic spline-interpolated thinning to model continuous diurnal arrival variations; (ii) a capacity-constrained M / G / c queuing system incorporating balking and reneging mechanisms to model user decisions better; (iii) an hourly method-of-moments bounded log-normal formulation preserving charging dynamics, time-sensitive variations, and skewness with greater fidelity than static fits; (iv) an empirical power rate formulation constrained by EVCS capacities for Grid to Vehicle (G2V) charging ; and (v) introducing scenario based V2G control models enfo…

title: Oficina educativa de primeiros socorros para estudantes: estratégia interprofissional nas escolas
abstract: Objetivo: descrever o processo de desenvolvimento de uma Tecnologia Educativa (TE) do tipo oficina de aprendizagem em Primeiros Socorros (PS) para estudantes no contexto escolar. Método: estudo metodológico, composto das seguintes etapas: revisão da literatura, diagnóstico situacional e desenvolvimento da TE, abrangendo a universidade, escola pública de Ensino Fundamental e o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU). Resultados: a TE constituiu-se em uma oficina composta por quatro matrizes: programática, conceitual, metodológica e operativa, as quais estruturaram a abordagem aos temas apontados pela pesquisa: PS e acionamento do SAMU; parada cardiorrespiratória; quedas, queimaduras e engasgo. A TE desenvolveu um modelo de competências baseado em conhecimento, habilidades e atitudes visando que os estudantes reconheçam as principais situações de urgência/emergência, executem ações básicas de PS e acionem a equipe especializada para a realização de manobras básicas de atendimento. Conclusão: o processo colaborativo, interprofissional e interinstitucional entre os sistemas de saúde e educação envolveu técnicos, docentes e acadêmicos na proposição de práticas de educação em saúde sobre um tema complexo, como os PS, com potencial impacto para sua replicação na rede escolar, por meio da implementação da TE.

title: Multiplex Determination of Pathogens via a Dual-Mode Microfluidic Platform Integrated with a Universal Sensing Strategy
abstract: Abstract Multiplex determination of pathogens is crucial for precise medical treatment of infectious diseases. To address this challenge, here we propose a CRISPR/Cas-assisted microfluidic multiplex sensing platform (CAMMSP) based on a nucleic acid amplification-free, universal, and modular sensing strategy. This strategy leverages the synergistic action of Cas12a and nanoporous materials to construct a target-responsive indicator release/enrichment system and achieve cascade signal amplification without nucleic acid amplification. By virtue of the programmability of the CRISPR system, this strategy is readily extended to different targets by replacing crRNA only. With the aid of a spatially divisional microfluidic platform, four common reproductive tract pathogens were synchronously detected as a proof-of-concept. The signal property of the methylene blue indicator was utilized to achieve electrochemical and optical signal cross-validation, guaranteeing the detection reliability at the readout level and offering flexible options for different scenarios. The developed CAMMSP exhibits broad linear ranges across 6 orders of magnitude and sub-femtomolar detection limits, with outstanding specificity in complex samples. Clinical sample analysis further validates its potential for practical applications, establishing a promising laboratory proof-of-concept and reliable technical fou…

title: Teachers’ Perception of Learning Action Cell (LAC) as a Strategy for Continuous Professional Development in Elementary Schools
abstract: This study examined teachers’ perceptions of the LAC as a strategy for continuous professional development in elementary schools during the 2025–2026 school year to inform a professional training plan. A descriptive survey research design was employed to describe teachers’ perceptions of LAC implementation before, during, and after sessions, their level across variables, and the challenges encountered. Using total enumeration, all teachers from selected elementary schools in Dumanjug District II participated, and data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and standard deviation based on an instrument adapted from the DepEd LAC Policy. Findings revealed that teachers perceived LAC implementation across three phases as fully implemented. In terms of specific areas, LAC was fully implemented in learner diversity and student inclusion, content and pedagogy, and assessment and reporting, but only implemented in 21st-century skills and ICT integration, as well as curriculum contextualization, localization, and indigenization. Challenges were generally slightly serious, with time constraints due to heavy workload identified as the most critical concern affecting participation. It is concluded that teachers have a positive perception of LAC as an effective professional development strategy that strengthens instructional practices, although improvements are needed in…

title: AYURVEDA AS A COMPLEMENTARY STRATEGY AGAINST ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF EVIDENCE, MECHANISMS INSIGHTS, AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
abstract: Introduction: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) a growing worldwide concern for health, requires an alternative and mechanistically heterogeneous treatment approaches. Ayurveda with its broad spectrum of therapeutic herbs and phytoconstituents, is a potent alternative to antibacterial and resistance-modulating treatments. Methodology: Research and review articles published from 2015 to 2026 were selected through PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Using Rayyan, 90 records screened of which, 13 duplicates were removed and 13 Articles were excluded and 64 articles were included in the qualitative synthesis. Results and Discussion: As per the reviewed evidence Ayurvedic plant phytoconstituents demonstrate an antibacterial, antibiofilm, antivirulence, resistance-modulating, and antibiotic-adjuvant effects against clinically relevant resistant pathogens. Several substances such as thymol, carvacrol, cinnamaldehyde, piperine, and quercetin, may increase the therapeutic value of conventional antibiotics by using complimentary processes. However, formulation variability, poor standardization, mechanistic gaps, a lack of pharmacokinetic and safety evidence, possible drug-herb interactions, and regulatory heterogeneity contribute as a barrier to clinical translation of ayurvedic formulation. Conclusion: Rather than taking the place of traditional antibiotic medication, Ayurv…

title: Práticas Integrativas e Complementares em Saúde como estratégia de promoção do bem-estar e autonomia dos idosos
abstract: As Práticas Integrativas e Complementares em Saúde (PICS) são ofertadas no Sistema Único de Saúde a uma população que envelhece, mas a evidência sobre bem-estar e autonomia da pessoa idosa está dispersa. Esta revisão integrativa, com dados públicos e abertos, sintetizou estudos de 2021 a 2026 sobre PICS em idosos. Seguiu o PRISMA 2020, com questão PICO, lista do Joanna Briggs Institute e níveis de evidência de Melnyk e Fineout-Overholt. As buscas de 31 de outubro de 2026, em motor de busca acadêmico e páginas de periódicos, retornaram 83 registros, e 18 estudos foram incluídos (seis de nível I, cinco de V, seis de VI e um de VII). Emergiram três categorias: práticas corpo-mente e exercício terapêutico (n = 7); música, dança e aromaterapia (n = 7); e políticas, serviços e visões panorâmicas (n = 4). Metanálises indicam benefício de Tai Chi, Qigong, ioga e musicoterapia sobre depressão, ansiedade, sono e função física, com certeza baixa a muito baixa e alta heterogeneidade; estudos brasileiros qualitativos apontam pertencimento e prazer, e um estudo com Lian Gong não mostrou efeito sobre o medo de quedas. Nenhum estudo avaliou a autonomia com instrumento específico, e o relatório nacional de monitoramento não apresenta dados por faixa etária. Propõe-se o modelo AURORA-PICS, teórico e não validado, e uma agenda de pesquisa. As bases indexadas não foram consultadas.

title: A General Strategy to Control Lifetime-Resolved Polarity Quantification of Push−Pull Fluorophores
abstract: Abstract Cellular polarity is important for physiological and biological conditions. Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) provides a quantitative approach for resolving microenvironmental polarity in living cells, and a variety of fluorophores have been developed for lifetime-based sensing. However, achieving tunable and quantitative polarity responses in fluorescence lifetime remains challenging, particularly when the range of polarity changes is wide. Herein, we establish a molecular design strategy that enables push−pull fluorophores to exhibit a linear response of their lifetime to environmental polarity in a wide range of polarity variations (dielectric constants from 5.30 to 32.70 or to 70.85). Theoretical calculations demonstrated that the tetrahydroquinoxaline−piperidine (THQP) unit exhibited an appropriate twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) tendency, enabling effective modulation of the excited-state dynamics associated with environmental polarity. This strategy provides broad applicability across multiple push−pull fluorophores including coumarins, difluoride-boron complexes, rhodols, and boranil-derived fluorophores. Notably, THQP−coumarin probes enable quantitative mapping of polarity variations in proteins and subcellular compartments both in vitro and in living cells via FLIM. Owing to their high brightness and photostability, these probes fu…

title: Research on the Financing Status, Dilemmas, and Optimization Paths of Low-Altitude Economy Enterprises under the Digital Economy
abstract: As a vital carrier of new quality productive forces and a nationally strategic emerging industry, the low-altitude economy is entering a critical window of scale-up development; however, its financial supply system significantly lags behind the pace of industrial expansion. Against the backdrop of deep integration between the digital economy and the low-altitude economy, this paper adopts a mixed-methods approach combining literature review, policy text analysis, and semi-structured interviews to systematically examine the financing status of low-altitude economy enterprises, analyze their dilemmas and underlying causes, and propose optimization paths. The study finds that the financing of low-altitude economy enterprises exhibits a structural feature of “debt-financing dominance, insufficient direct financing, and high policy dependence.” The mismatch between asset-light structures and collateral logic, the absence of rights confirmation, valuation, and disposal mechanisms for data assets, and the dual uncertainty of policy and technology jointly constitute the core causes of financing constraints, while the financing pain points of the three enterprise types—R&D-oriented, operation-oriented, and infrastructure-oriented—show significant heterogeneity. The digital economy can build a tiered and classified financing model, open the transformation channel of “data resources—data …

title: Germinate-to-Exterminate: Precrop Stimulation of Verticillium dahliae Microsclerotia Germination by Root Exudates as a Novel Strategy for Sustainable Control of Verticillium Wilt
abstract: Verticillium wilt (VW) is an important soilborne disease caused by Verticillium species. VW has been reported in nearly 400 plant species from various families, including but not limited to Solanaceae, Brassicaceae, Cucurbitaceae, Fabaceae, Rosaceae, Caprifoliaceae, Malvaceae, Lamiaceae, and Sapindaceae. Potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.), belonging to the Solanaceae family, is one of the most important staple crops globally and can be greatly impacted by VW, resulting in more than 40% yield losses in heavily infested commercial fields. VW in potatoes can be caused by infections with Verticillium dahliae (the most damaging species), V . albo-atrum , V . tricorpus , and others. V. dahliae produces microsclerotia (MS), resting structures that can persist in the soil for more than 10 years, even without a host crop, making effective field management challenging. Additionally, the incidence and severity of VW can be increased when root-lesion nematodes and V. dahliae coinfect potato crops. Root exudate metabolites facilitate plant-microbial communication, which is also essential for the pathosystems adaptation to environmental change. These can also provide important signals to plant pathogens; for example, to facilitate stimulation of V. dahliae MS germination. A thorough understanding of how root exudates drive plant–pathogen interactions and how this knowledge can be applied to dise…

title: Ukraine’s digital heritage diplomacy in China and Indonesia: Soft power visions in comparative perspective
abstract: This article addresses gaps in scholarship on Ukraine’s digital cultural diplomacy in Asia by examining how Ukraine’s Embassies communicate its national identity and heritage in China and Indonesia, major actors in the region and the world. The study asks how the Embassies of Ukraine in China and Indonesia communicate Ukraine’s national identity and cultural heritage through digital diplomacy, and how these communications align with or diverge from the soft power visions of their host countries. The analysis draws on data collected from the Embassies’ digital platform between January and May 2025, encompassing Ukraine’s Cultural Diplomacy Month. Focusing on Ukraine’s digital diplomacy towards China, the findings show that almost half of the Embassy’s heritage communication simultaneously documents Russia’s actions against that heritage, challenging depoliticised local media framing. Focusing on Ukraine’s digital diplomacy towards China, the findings show a strategic communication priority assigned to the narratives of Ukraine’s heritage destruction by Russia, challenging depoliticised local media framing. Bilateral cultural positioning is largely absent, while strong Weibo engagement reflects visibility within, but not influence over, a highly controlled information environment. In the case of Ukraine’s digital diplomacy with Indonesia, by contrast, the Embassy of Ukraine focus…

title: A Firefly‐Inspired Biomimetic Multispectral Cascade Framework for Transient Thermal Mitigation and Tissue Protection in High‐Power Laser Surgeries
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐power laser systems remain indispensable in modern clinical surgeries owing to their superior cutting precision and structural blood occlusion capabilities. However, collateral thermal damage manifesting as rapid localized carbonization, tissue scarring, and secondary peripheral cell death remains a major complication due to unmitigated macroscale heat accumulation. Traditional mechanical methods, such as air‐flow cooling or liquid cryogen sprays, suffer from structural latency and block critical intraoperative visualization fields. To resolve this photothermal bottleneck, this study introduces a novel theoretical framework: an active, firefly‐inspired biomimetic coaxial optical buffering shielding engine designed for transient millisecond‐scale spatial–temporal thermal mitigation. By engineering a hardware‐native cascaded energy transport model, localized high‐energy thermal photons generated during target tissue cutting are captured by a peripheral spectral absorption layer. This system dynamically shifts the localized photon energy across a multispectral cascade grid, mimicking the cascading energy transfer topologies observed in bioluminescent mechanisms to dissipate structural thermal waste as nondestructive, minimized‐thermal luminescent output. Multiphysics numerical co‐simulations demonstrate that this biomimetic cascading network restricts peripheral tiss…

The Power of Collective Efficacy: Sources, Interventions, and Outcomes for Diverse Students
abstract: Although self-efficacy theory has emphasized individuals’ beliefs in their capabilities, collective efficacy may operate through similar processes. Understanding these mechanisms may be particularly important for promoting equitable pathways into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) careers among students from underrepresented groups. Using a deductive qualitative analysis approach, this study examined how the four sources of self-efficacy (i.e., performance accomplishments, vicarious experiences, social persuasion, and physiological and emotional states) contribute to the development of collective efficacy during collaborative STEM learning. Focus groups with diverse eighth-grade students and semistructured interviews with their teachers explored students’ experiences working collaboratively on a multimedia STEM project. Findings indicated that all four sources of self-efficacy contributed to students’ shared belief in their groups’ ability to accomplish collective goals. Furthermore, proximal contextual supports, including peer collaboration and teacher support through problem-solving, modeling, and tolerance for mistakes, helped students navigate barriers, facilitating persistence toward shared goals and skill development. Findings extend the application of self-efficacy theory and social cognitive career theory by highlighting collective efficacy as a po…

title: Retail Sales Promotion and Consumer Conversion of Wellness-Oriented Food Products: An Exploratory Field Study of Nutrica at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi
abstract: Purpose: This study examines how point-of-sale promotion and need-based personal selling are used to engage shoppers and support purchase conversion for Nutrica wellness-oriented food products at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi. It focuses on the practical selling process, customer questions and objections, and the role of product knowledge in retail interactions. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts an exploratory, descriptive single-site case-study design based on a two-month sales internship conducted from 1 June to 31 July 2026. Evidence comprises the trainee’s field observations, customer-facing selling activities, an internship activity diary and a summary of outlet-level records supplied in the source report. No structured questionnaire, probability sample or controlled experiment was reported. Findings: The field account indicates that concise, customer-centred communication, active listening, product familiarity and responses tailored to specific objections were central to the selling process. The source report records 247 customer interactions and 192 conversions. If these counts use consistent definitions and refer to the same observation period, the implied descriptive conversion ratio is 77.7%; this should be treated as provisional because the underlying transaction-level records and operational definitions were not included. The report also lists 1,014 L as units sold…

title: O SILÊNCIO COMO ESTRATÉGIA NARRATIVA EM VARANDAS DA EVA DE MILTON HATOUM: LACUNAS, AMBIGUIDADES E A IMAGINAÇÃO DO LEITOR
abstract: Este estudo acadêmico se dedica à narrativa curta Varandas da Eva (2009), escrita por Milton Hatoum, com objetivo de dar atenção especial ao uso do silêncio e das omissões narrativas como estratégias estéticas indispensáveis. Entende-se que Hatoum, uma figura do cânone da literatura brasileira contemporânea, utiliza o não dito para gerar tensão, aumentar a profundidade psicológica dos personagens e envolver ativamente o leitor no processo interpretativo de construção de significado. A pesquisa analisa o silêncio corporal de figuras como Tarso e da Mulher Anônima, assim como as elipses temporais e as ambiguidades que marcam a narrativa. A partir das teorias formuladas por pesquisadores como Hans Robert Jauss e Wolfgang Iser, a crítica visa esclarecer de que modo as indefinições textuais incitam o leitor a interagir imaginativamente com os vácuos, colocando-os, portanto, como coautores da obra literária. A metodologia é adotada de uma abordagem bibliográfica qualitativa e parte dos pressupostos teóricos dos autores citados. A conclusão é que, o silêncio, em Varandas da Eva, vai além da simples ausência; ao contrário, ele se manifesta como uma presença potente que aprimora a experiência estética e a natureza polissêmica do texto.

Engineering Acid Adaptability of Zearalenone Lactonase Guided by an Integrated Structural and Computational Strategy
abstract: Abstract Zearalenone (ZEN) lactonases are promising biocatalysts for detoxifying ZEN-contaminated food and feed. However, their poor activity and stability under acidic conditions limit practical applications. Here, we establish an integrated computationally/structurally guided hydrophobic microenvironment engineering as a paradigm for improving the acid adaptability of ZEN lactonases. Constant pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) simulations revealed that acidic conditions suppress proton abstraction by altering catalytic-residue protonation and destabilizing key structural regions. Structure-guided engineering introduced Pro and Phe residues to stabilize acid-sensitive regions, while hydrophobic microenvironment engineering promoted substrate repositioning and the formation of near-attack conformations. The engineered M4 mutant exhibited a 111.7-fold enhancement in acid stability. Validation with 5Z-7-oxozeaenol supported a hydrophobic gating mechanism, in which the hydrophobic microenvironment governs substrate positioning, aligns catalytic residues, and stabilizes reactive conformations. M4 degraded approximately 70% of ZEN under simulated gastrointestinal pH conditions, demonstrating its potential for ZEN detoxification.

title: Anxiety Experience and Coping Strategies of Students Facing Test-Based University Entrance Exams: A Phenomenological Study
abstract: Anxiety when facing university entrance selection remains a persistent issue in Indonesia, even as the selection scheme has changed name from SBMPTN to UTBK-SNBT and undergone several structural revisions. Most existing studies rely on quantitative-correlational designs and tend to focus on prospective test-takers, leaving the lived experience of those who have already passed through the process underexplored. This study aimed to understand university students' experiences of anxiety when facing test-based university entrance exams and the coping strategies they used to manage it. A qualitative phenomenological design was employed, with data analyzed using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis. Five informants who had previously taken the exam were selected through purposive sampling and interviewed using a semi-structured, in-depth approach. Findings revealed that anxiety stemmed primarily from fear of failure linked to the absence of alternative plans, alongside negative self-evaluation of preparedness, further shaped by contextual factors such as access to learning facilities. To manage this anxiety, informants combined problem-focused strategies, such as additional study efforts, with emotion-focused and social strategies, such as cognitive reframing and peer support. These findings enrich phenomenological understanding of entrance-exam anxiety and remain relevant for cu…

abstract: Objective: Mapping learning preferences at entry into the MBBS course may help faculty design teaching sessions that are more responsive to learner diversity.The present study aims to evaluate the VARK learning preferences among first-year MBBS students. Methods: This cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among 235 first-year MBBS students The VARK questionnaire version 8.02 was administered using an online Google Form. The data was analysed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square/Fisher’s exact test, Mann–Whitney U test, Friedman test and Spearman’s correlation. Results: Of the 238 students recorded, 164 (68.9%) were females and 74 (31.1%) were males. The mean age was 19.30±1.41 years. Complete VARK data were available for 235 students. Multimodal learning was predominant [157/235 (66.8%)], with bimodal learning being the single most frequent mode [85/235 (36.2%)]. The distribution of learning modes did not differ significantly by gender (p=0.983). The highest mean component score was observed for Kinesthetic learning (8.98±3.89), followed closely by Aural learning (8.83±3.86), and the four VARK component scores differed significantly within participants (p<0.001). title: Uncertainty-Aware Face Anti-Spoofing with Epistemic and Aleatoric Referral Under Unseen Attacks
abstract: Face anti-spoofing, or face presentation attack detection (PAD), must often decide on attack types absent from training. Existing uncertainty-aware PAD methods use a single confidence or uncertainty score, which cannot show whether an unreliable decision comes from an unfamiliar attack or a poor-quality capture. This study proposes a lightweight Bayesian framework on MobileNetV3-Large that combines Monte Carlo dropout with a heteroscedastic logit head to estimate epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty separately, and uses both in an ACCEPT, REJECT or REFER rule with thresholds fixed on validation data containing only known attacks. Unseen attacks, defined as attack types excluded from training and validation, were tested on SiW Protocol III in both directions and on SiW-Mv2 Protocol II, which holds out each spoof type in turn. Over five seeds, the complete configuration reduced the average classification error rate (ACER) from 4.01% for the deterministic model to 2.61% at 97.09% coverage, with ACER of 2.91% and 3.46% on the two Protocol III directions and 2.68% on SiW-Mv2. Two re-implemented baselines reached lower ACER (1.31% and 1.94%) but do not separate uncertainty sources. Expected calibration error remained high (0.2983). The contribution is reason-coded referral rather than lower error.

title: A container architecture for migrating interoperable applications using weight adaptive temporal CNN and secretary bird optimization algorithm in cloud computing
abstract: Virtualization in cloud computing enables multiple virtual servers to be deployed on a single physical infrastructure. The increasing number of cloud applications also increases resource overload during service execution. However, the main challenge with the migration of interoperable applications is the process of establishing optimal resource allocation, performance, quality of service, the tradeoff between cost-effectiveness and satisfying the requirements of service level agreement. Deep learning methods are useful for load balancing because they can identify noisy workload fluctuations. In this paper, Weight Adaptive Temporal CNN and Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (WATCSBOA)-based container architecture is proposed for predicting the workload, which optimizes the degree of resource utilization and reduces the overload during the process of executing the migrated interoperable applications. This container architecture uses Weight Adaptive Temporal CNN (WATCNN) to determine long-term sequence dependencies for deciding the actual workload thereby improving the accuracy and response speed of container clusters. It mainly helps enhance the capabilities of feature extraction when the deep learning model is employed to address long sequences. It uses the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA), which helps in parameter optimization to maximize resource allocation and …

MgO-Biochar for Selective Orthophosphate Removal from Swine Wastewater: Optimization and Environmental Assessment
abstract: Abstract Excess dissolved reactive orthophosphate (DRP) from swine wastewater drives eutrophication, yet its selective removal remains challenging. This study develops a magnesium oxide (MgO)-modified pine biochar for efficient DRP capture and recovery. MgO-PB, CaO-PB, and MgO/CaO-PB were produced by co-pyrolyzing <1 mm pinewood with 2% Mg, Ca, or combined Mg/Ca hydroxides at 450 °C. All Mg-containing biochars exhibited high DRP removal capacities (∼20–24 mg/g) across three simulated orthophosphate systems (10–100 mg/L, pH 5–9), achieving up to ∼99% removal. MgO-PB outperformed MgO/CaO-PB, with a Langmuir maximum capacity of 36.34 mg/g for the mixed H2PO4–/HPO42 system. Removal was then optimized directly in pretreated real swine wastewater by central composite design and validated in quintuplicate. Under the optimum (0.3 g, pH 6.82, 6.5 h), the predicted removal (91.44%) was confirmed experimentally (93.04 ± 0.77%, n = 5), reducing DRP from 28.36 mg/L (after pretreatment of the raw wastewater from 79.63 mg/L) to 1.97 ± 0.22 mg/L, an overall reduction of 97.5%. Mg leaching was limited (∼9%), and the PAH content (1.40 × 10–3 mg/kg BaP-equivalent) was below the US EPA soil screening level, supporting the phosphate-loaded adsorbent as a potential material for soil amendment, pending long-term stability and agronomic confirmation.

abstract: Cassava-processing wastewater can introduce cyanogenic contaminants into soils receiving untreated discharges. This study evaluated laboratory-scale hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) oxidation of cyanide-contaminated soils from three cassava-processing-impacted locations in Ozoro and its environs, Delta State, Nigeria, and optimized the process using response surface methodology. Baseline soil pH, moisture content, electrical conductivity, organic matter and cyanide were determined. Cyanide was analysed by an acid-distillation/colorimetric procedure using copper chloride, sodium hydroxide trapping, chloramine-T and pyridine-barbituric acid, with spectrophotometric measurement at 578 nm. A randomized three-factor, three-level Box–Behnken design comprising 17 runs was executed in Design-Expert 13.0.1.0. The factors were H₂O₂ load (0.5–1.5%), water content (20–100%) and reaction time (24–96 h), while cyanide reduction was modelled separately for Leo, Oroledo and Erovie soils. Baseline pH ranged from 6.32 to 6.81, organic matter from 15.00 to 48.54%, and the cyanide concentrations were 853, 614 and 1041 mg CN⁻ kg⁻¹ dry soil, respectively. All the fitted quadratic equations were significant (p < 0.0001) and the R² values obtained were 0.9911, 0.9934 and 0.9922 for Leo, Oroledo and Erovie respectively. title: Integrated Prenatal Cardiopulmonary Assessment Using Fetal Echocardiography in Isolated Left‐Sided Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective Prenatal severity assessment in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) primarily relies on lung‐based parameters such as the observed‐to‐expected lung‐to‐head ratio (o/eLHR) and liver position; however, these markers do not fully reflect fetal cardiopulmonary adaptation. We investigated the prognostic significance of fetal echocardiographic parameters and integrated these in prenatal prediction models in left‐sided CDH. Methods This nationwide multicenter retrospective study included fetuses with prenatally diagnosed isolated left‐sided CDH. Gestational age‐adjusted Z‐scores were generated for fetal cardiac dimensions. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance for survival. Results A total of 363 fetuses were included, with an overall survival rate of 74.9%. Non‐survivors demonstrated significantly smaller right pulmonary artery and mitral valve dimensions than survivors. Among fetal echocardiographic parameters, the mitral‐to‐tricuspid valve ratio (MTR) demonstrated the strongest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.77. In fetuses evaluated at ≤ 29 weeks’ gestation, an exploratory model combining MTR with o/eLHR and liver‐up status achieved an apparent AUC of 0.827. Conclusion Fetal echocardiographic parameters were associated with survival in CDH. Integrated prenatal cardiopulmonar…

abstract: Este trabalho apresenta o desenvolvimento da L.I.L.Y., uma aplicação web voltada para a automação e a gestão de orçamentos em oficinas mecânicas especializadas em radiadores. O problema central reside na falta de padronização e de agilidade nos orçamentos elaborados manualmente, o que compromete a precisão financeira e a rentabilidade do negócio. A metodologia caracteriza-se como pesquisa aplicada, com estudo de caso em uma oficina de radiadores e desenvolvimento iterativo de um protótipo funcional construído com React, Vite e TypeScript, persistência em nuvem por meio do Firebase, serviços de retaguarda em Java com Spring Boot e um motor de inteligência artificial em Python integrado aos modelos de linguagem Gemini e Groq, com interação por texto e por voz. Os resultados mostraram que a parametrização dos custos e a automatização do cálculo de venda, custo e lucro eliminaram a variação entre orçamentos de um mesmo serviço, com concordância de 100% em relação aos valores de referência em 10.000 casos de teste, centralizaram o histórico de contas por usuário e permitiram ao assistente virtual converter comandos em linguagem natural em ações na aplicação, com taxa de acerto de 90% em 40 execuções e nenhuma ação indevida. A Multi-Stage AdSS-NARX-LSTM Approach for Enhanced State-of-Charge Estimation in Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Accurate state of charge (SoC) estimation is essential for the reliable operation, energy management, and safety of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. However, accurate estimation remains challenging due to battery nonlinearities, measurement uncertainties, and changing operating conditions. This study proposes a hybrid AdSS-NARX-LSTM framework integrating Adaptive State Smoothing (AdSS), Nonlinear Autoregressive with Exogenous Inputs (NARX), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for SoC estimation. Battery voltage and current are used as primary inputs. The AdSS stage generates a temporally consistent SoC trajectory through an adaptive smoothing process, reducing the influence of measurement noise and short-term signal fluctuations while preserving the overall state evolution trend. In parallel, the NARX model exploits historical input-output relationships to capture nonlinear temporal dynamics associated with battery behavior. The AdSS and NARX outputs are fused with measured variables as auxiliary features before being fed into the LSTM network. This integration enables the LSTM to exploit complementary information while learning long-term temporal dependencies from sequential data. The framework improves estimation stability and robustness without requiring complex electrochemical or equivalent-circuit models. The effectiveness of th…

title: Finlet AI: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Financial Intelligence Platform Using Model Context Protocol and Deterministic Risk Governance
abstract: Standalone conversational language models struggle to satisfy audit and compliance standards in institutional equity research. When an equity analyst prompts an ungrounded model to evaluate a listed company, three operational defects appear almost immediately: the model quotes outdated share prices from its pre-training cutoff, invents page or footnote numbers when summarizing regulatory filings, and produces inconsistent numerical risk ratings when executed repeatedly on identical inputs. This paper presents Finlet AI, a twelve-layer multi-agent financial intelligence platform that decouples quantitative market arithmetic and primary-source retrieval from neural text synthesis. Once an analytical query is submitted through our asynchronous FastAPI gateway, a stateful LangGraph supervisor triggers concurrent parallel fan-out across three specialized domain workers covering historical price series, live financial news feeds, and statutory annual reports isolated behind standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool interfaces. Technical price action, 20-day volume momentum ratios, and 30-day annualized volatility (σ ) are computed directly from three-month 30d Open-High-Low-Close-Volume (OHLCV) series fetched via Yahoo Finance. Real-time news catalysts are gathered through Google News RSS syndication and sanitized of HTML markup, while balance-sheet debt and liquidity disclosure…

title: Multi-scale modeling of continent-wide tracking data confirms the importance of landscape mosaics for the European wildcat
abstract: Abstract Context Land use change is a major threat to the persistence of wildlife in human-dominated landscapes, making the knowledge of the amount and spatial configuration of suitable habitat essential for conservation. The European wildcat ( Felis silvestris ) currently persists in fragmented populations and faces ever increasing human pressure. Objectives We modeled and mapped suitable wildcat habitats at the continental scale, to identify opportunities and constraints for its conservation. Methods We compiled a large telemetry dataset comprising 200 wildcats across Europe and developed multi-scale habitat suitability models using Maxent. Habitat selection was analyzed at two hierarchical levels: home-range placement within the wider landscape and selection within the established home ranges. Results At both levels, wildcats selected broadleaved forests, mixed forests, and grasslands, while avoiding landscapes dominated by large continuous forests. For home-range placement, they preferred lower terrain ruggedness and less intensive agriculture. Within the home ranges, wildcats selected forest edges and small woody features. Conclusions Our results highlight the importance of heterogeneous forest–grassland mosaics habitats. More than half of the predicted suitable habitat occurred outside protected areas, highlighting the need for effective conservation strategies beyond the…

title: Farmer Risk Management Protocol, Community Support and Small-Scale Irrigation Performance: Empirical Evidence from Migori County, Kenya
abstract: Irrigation is adduced to delink food production from rainfall, and the contribution of small-scale irrigation to world food security cannot be overstated. However, despite the potential of small-scale irrigation to mitigate against food insecurity, this study posits that inadequacy of empirical data on factors that influence post construction performance inhibits performance in the sector. Therefore, using cross-sectional and correlational design, and descriptive and inferential statistics, the study examined the influence of farmer risk management protocol and community support on small-scale irrigation performance. The results show that farmer risk management protocol explains 61.1% of variation in the model, and that while mitigation is the most preferred protocol, avoidance significantly influences small-scale irrigation performance. Consequently, the study recommends policy guidelines that require project proposals in small-scale irrigation to incorporate risk management protocols. Further, with regard to practice, in order to entrench farmer risk management protocol in small-scale irrigation, the study recommends transfer of governance in small-scale irrigation from government agencies to community organisations. In addition, the study recommends training of small-scale irrigation farmers on risks management and mobilisation of insurance providers to implement agricultura…

title: From Financial Access to Productive Finance: A Comparative Institutional Analysis of MSME Financing in Indonesia’s Conventional and Islamic Banking Systems
abstract: This study examines how financial-access priorities are represented in governance, product design and risk-allocation arrangements in Indonesian conventional and Islamic banking, and what public disclosures can establish about productive MSME finance. Using comparative qualitative document analysis, we purposively review source-located passages and selected administrative tables from BRI, Bank Mandiri, BSI and Bank Muamalat, with annual-report coverage framed around 2023–2025 and contextual regulatory and sustainability disclosures. All 12 bank–year annual reports were identified and checked selectively; comprehensive full-report coding and independent recoding were not conducted. The analyzed excerpts support three interpretive dimensions—governance translation, financing architecture and prudential allocation—while exposing non-equivalent product categories and reporting measures, including unresolved differences among BSI report versions and arithmetic tensions in Mandiri tables. Product labels and administrative balances do not establish realized productive use. Originality/value: The study develops a bounded institutional-alignment reading that connects observable organizational arrangements to the measurement limits of MSME financing, without asserting comparative system superiority, policy causality or borrower-level impact.
venue: Journal of Economic Studies and Analytics

title: Sectoral heterogeneity in the digital transformation–financial performance nexus: evidence from Korean manufacturing firms
Financial Constraints, Wages, and Macroeconomic Implications
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates how firm‐level financial constraints affect individual wages and aggregate labor market dynamics during financial recessions. We derive testable predictions from competing theoretical mechanisms and assess them empirically using German administrative worker data matched to firm balance sheets. Embedding these microlevel estimates in a macroeconomic model with labor and financial frictions, we demonstrate how small ceteris paribus effects align with large aggregate dynamics. Tighter financial conditions amplify wage and unemployment volatility, weakening the tight link between wage rigidity and the volatility of unemployment discussed in the literature. Financial constraints reduce the effectiveness of hiring subsidies during recessions.

title: Organizational preparedness for extreme events: mindfulness and the measurement, management and avoidance of risk in the financial sector
Impact of Financial Inclusion Schemes on Socio-Economic Status of Housekeeping & General Maintenance Staff of Higher Education Institutions
abstract: Financial inclusion has emerged as a critical policy strategy for improving the socio-economic conditions of marginalized populations by expanding access to formal banking, insurance, and pension services. Despite significant government initiatives in India, many low-income occupational groups continue to experience limited awareness and utilization of financial services, which restricts the potential socio-economic benefits of financial inclusion schemes. This study investigates the impact of awareness of and access to selected financial inclusion schemes Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), and Atal Pension Yojana (APY) on the socio-economic status of housekeeping and general maintenance staff working in higher education institutions in Rajasthan, India. The study employs primary survey data collected from 121 respondents using a structured questionnaire and applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the relationships among awareness, access to financial services, and socio-economic status. The reliability and validity of the constructs were confirmed, with Cronbach's alpha values ranging from 0.846 to 0.944, composite reliability between 0.862 and 0.951, and average variance extracted values exceeding the threshold of 0.50. The structural mod…

title: Aedes -borne febrile exanthems in UK dermatology: lessons from European transmission
abstract: The first documented breeding of Aedes aegypti in the United Kingdom creates a new diagnostic context for dermatologists. European transmission data show that locally acquired arboviral disease may circulate for weeks before recognition and that early recognised cases can present with febrile eruptions. This letter translates those lessons and WHO evidence into a practical framework for distinguishing dengue chikungunya and Zika and for deciding when arboviral testing should extend beyond travel history.

title: DE-RISKING AND FINANCIAL INCLUSION IN INTERNATIONAL REMITTANCES: A SCOPING REVIEW OF BANKING ACCESS AND RISK-BASED APPROACHES
abstract: De-risking, that is, the restriction or termination of banking relationships in order to avoid, rather than manage, risks associated with certain customers or sectors, creates tension between the financial integrity and financial inclusion agendas, and international remittance providers are among the most affected segments. This scoping review, conducted under the Joanna Briggs Institute framework and reported according to PRISMA-ScR, mapped the drivers, consequences and alternatives to de-risking described in the 2021–2026 literature on these providers, with emphasis on the United States. Twenty-three documents were included, comprising peer-reviewed articles, a book chapter, working papers and reports by regulators and international bodies. Profitability emerges as the main driver, mediated by due diligence costs, banks' limited visibility into providers' operations, supervisory expectations perceived as uncertain and fragmented supervision; this convergence, however, partly stems from interdependent sources. Reported consequences involve costs, market concentration and fragile settlement, but causal evidence is scarce, and displacement to informal channels is presumed rather than measured. Individualized risk assessment, proportionate due diligence, advance notice of termination, sharing of supervisory information and safe corridors are proposed without any published effecti…

title: Effects of face gear tribocorrosion depth on the nonlinear dynamics of a worm-face gear two-stage transmission system
Intermediação financeira 3.0: a reconfiguração dos custos de transação na era da tokenização
abstract: Este artigo analisa as promessas e os limites da tokenização à luz da Teoria dos Custos de Transação (TCT), com o objetivo de oferecer uma interpretação pragmática dos ganhos e das novas fricções geradas por essa tecnologia emergente. Argumenta-se que, embora a tokenização reduza diversos custos associados à intermediação tradicional — como liquidação, custódia e reconciliação —, ela também reconfigura os custos de mensuração, monitoramento e enforcement, deslocando-os do plano ex post para o ex ante. A partir dos conceitos clássicos de Coase, Williamson e North, demonstra-se que as principais disfunções observadas nos modelos tokenizados — incluindo rigidez contratual, captura de governança, fragmentação de liquidez e persistência de intermediários informacionais — são previsíveis em termos transacionais. Conclui-se que modelos baseados em tokenização, especialmente no âmbito das finanças descentralizadas (DeFi), representam uma transformação institucional promissora, sobretudo para países com instituições frágeis, ao permitir novos arranjos de confiança em contextos de insegurança jurídica. Propõe-se, por fim, uma agenda de pesquisa voltada à modelagem dos trade-offs institucionais e ao desenho de governanças adaptativas para infraestruturas descentralizadas.

title: Green Credit, Financing Constraints, And Corporate Green Transformation: A Financial Resource Allocation Perspective
abstract: Green credit has become an important policy instrument for promoting sustainable development and integrating environmental considerations into financial resource allocation. As environmental concerns and climate-related risks increasingly influence economic activities, commercial banks are expected to play a greater role in supporting environmentally sustainable projects while maintaining financial stability. Where economic development and environmental sustainability are important policy priorities, green credit provides a potential mechanism for directing financial resources toward environmentally responsible industries. Drawing on financial intermediation theory and credit risk management perspectives, this study explores the channels through which green credit may influence commercial banks' credit risk. Green credit may reduce credit risk by encouraging banks to incorporate environmental factors into borrower assessments, strengthen lending standards, and identify potential risks associated with environmental regulations and unsustainable business practices. By directing financing toward environmentally responsible enterprises, banks may reduce their exposure to borrowers vulnerable to environmental and regulatory changes, thereby improving loan portfolio quality. These factors suggest that the relationship between green credit and credit risk may depend on banks' lending …
venue: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies

title: Design Vulnerabilities and Design Assumptions in Automated Systems: The Case of the B737 MAX Original MCAS Design
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate how formal modeling of human-machine systems can uncover design vulnerabilities. Two fatal accidents involving the Boeing B737 MAX raised substantial safety concerns about the aircraft’s design and led to the worldwide grounding of the MAX. These accidents involved design vulnerabilities, design assumptions about human performance that proved unwarranted, and an operational context that differed from what the designers assumed. The two accidents also involved the operation of the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS) that was introduced into the pitch trim system of the B737 MAX. We use the case of the MAX to show that by building a formal model of this system including MCAS and examining it with an analytical methodology, the vulnerabilities in the design become visible. By comparing this model with a model of the MAX’s predecessor, the B737NG, we highlight discrepancies between the design assumptions about how pilots would act when faced with system failures and the crew actions observed in the first accident. Using a formal approach to describing human interaction with automated systems to identify design vulnerabilities can be productively employed in the design of automated systems, regulatory assessment, and accident investigation.
venue: Journal of Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making

abstract: هدفت الدراسة إلى الكشف عن اتجاهات طلبة تقنيات المعلومات بكلية التربية - جامعة تعز نحو البرنامج التعليمي الرقمي، والتعرف إلى طبيعة العلاقات بين التحصيل العلمي، ومهارات التصميم الرقمي، والتفكير الإبداعي، والاتجاهات نحو البرنامج. ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة، اعتُمد المنهج الوصفي (الارتباطي)؛ لملاءمته طبيعة الدراسة وأهدافها المتمثلة في استكشاف الاتجاهات وفحص العلاقات بين المتغيرات، كما استُعين بتصميم المجموعة الواحدة ذي القياسين القبلي والبعدي. وتمثلت أدوات جمع البيانات في اختبار التحصيل العلمي، وبطاقة ملاحظة مهارات التصميم الرقمي، واختبار التفكير الإبداعي، ومقياس الاتجاهات، وذلك لتحديد مقدار التحسن وفحص العلاقات بين المتغيرات والكشف عن اتجاهات الطلبة نحو البرنامج التعليمي الرقمي. أظهرت النتائج أن اتجاهات طلبة عينة الدراسة نحو البرنامج التعليمي الرقمي جاءت إيجابية وبمستوى مرتفع، بمتوسط حسابي بلغ (4.08)، مع وجود فرق دال إحصائيا بين المتوسط الحسابي والمتوسط الفرضي عند مستوى الدلالة (α ≤ 0.05). كما أظهرت النتائج عدم وجود علاقات ارتباطية ذات دلالة إحصائية عند مستوى (α ≤ 0.05) بين متغيرات الدراسة، المتمثلة في التحصيل العلمي ومهارات التصميم الرقمي والتفكير الإبداعي والاتجاهات نحو البرنامج، سواء في القياسات البعدية أم في مقادير التحسن الناتجة عنها.
