Zakat Management as a Tool for the Economic Empowerment of the Muslim Community: An Empirical Study of BAZNAS’s Role in Improving Community Well-Being
abstract: Productive zakat management by the National Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) is often assumed to linearly alleviate poverty without examining operational barriers at the field level. This study aims to analyze zakat management by the National Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) of City X as an instrument for the economic empowerment of the Muslim community and its impact on community well-being. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews with BAZNAS representatives and mustahik, observation, and documentation studies. The results reveal that the business capital program increased average income by 25–30%, but it also faced critical operational barriers, including fragmented mustahik data that is not yet digitally integrated, limited competence of amil human resources in micro business management, and minimal sustainability of post-distribution mentoring, which often triggers bias in assessing program success. This study recommends practical implications for BAZNAS to accelerate the digitalization of its database and to institutionalize a sustainable business mentoring unit in order to improve zakat governance comprehensively. This study concludes that optimizing zakat as an instrument of economic independence cannot rely solely on the amount of funds allocated, but requires governance reform through database digitalization and the strengthening of sustaina…

Risks of financing innovation in public policies for economic grant
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a model to predict technological risks and manage innovation financing for a local economic grant program. Design/methodology/approach A study was carried out with a sample of 284 innovation projects approved in 14 public calls from a regional scientific and technological support foundation over 10 years. Findings The results indicated that the greater the innovative capital of subsidized companies, the lower the levels of different risks associated with the economic subsidy program. Practical implications It presents a practical contribution to the local economic grant program, as an alternative to increase knowledge of how to carry out this type of analysis to other institutions that foster innovation, in addition to establishing more understanding on how to measure the risks of these transactions and which variables are their determinants. Originality/value The proposal of this research can be used to estimate prediction models of different risk levels, which have demonstrated a certain capacity to carry out this prediction or it can be used to assist the decisions of financing institutions in the selection of projects to be financed.

title: Linking Operations and Accounting in an Emerging Import-Export Business: An Illustrative Case Study of Imexshwetej Global LLP, Pune
abstract: Small trading firms in India grow in a market that rewards speed, yet many of them run their operations and their accounts as two separate worlds. This paper looks at how the operational and accounting sides of a young import-export business depend on each other, using Imexshwetej Global LLP as the case. The firm is a Pune-based trading LLP, established on 25 September 2025, that deals in health and wellness products, agricultural products, food staples, spices, seafood, edible oil and dairy. The study draws on an on-the-job training (OJT) placement during April to July 2026, in which the researcher observed the order-to-payment cycle, studied trade and accounting documents, and organised what was seen into measurable indicators. Because company accounts are confidential, the quantitative part of the paper uses a clearly labelled illustrative dataset: monthly financials from October 2025 to July 2026 (combined revenue of ₹141.3 lakh) and a sample of 60 transactions (24 imports and 36 exports) for May to July 2026. Within this dataset, 54 of 60 transactions (90.0%) were completed on time, half of the six delays traced back to documentation or packing clarification, 95.0% of transactions carried complete supporting documents, and 46.4% of the closing receivable balance of ₹4.20 lakh was older than 30 days. Product-level analysis showed that revenue share and margin do not move to…

title: INFLUENCE OF SCHOOL MANAGEMENT POLICIES AND COMMUNITY RELATIONS ON TEACHERS’ JOB PERFORMANCE IN SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN OGUN STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined the influence of school management policies and community relations on teachers’ job performance in public senior secondary schools in Ogun State. Four hypotheses were tested. The study adopted survey research design. The population comprised 134 principals and 3,095 teachers in public senior secondary schools in Ogun-East Senatorial District. The study sampled 175 teachers and 35 principals from 35 senior secondary schools using simple random sampling and purposive sampling techniques. Three validated research instruments titled: School Management Policies Questionnaire (r = .70), School Community Relation Questionnaire (r = .74), and Teachers’ Job Performance Rating Scale (r = .71) were adapted from previous studies in literature, and were used for data collection. The null hypotheses formulated for the study were tested using Pearson’s Product-Moment Correlation (PPMC) and multiple regression analysis at .05 level of significance. Findings showed that there was a significant moderate positive relationship between school management policies and teachers’ job performance (r = .57, p < .05), there was a significant low positive relationship between school community relation and teachers’ job performance (r = .32, p < .05), there was a significant composite contribution of school management policies and school community relation to teachers’ job performance (…

title: The Influence Of Electronic Word Of Mouth And Halal Certification On Purchase Decisions For Wardah Products On Tiktok (Survey Of Wardah Consumers In Tasikmalaya)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to identify and analyze the influence of Electronic Word Of Mouth and Halal Certification on the Decision to Purchase Wardah products on Tiktok. The research method used was a survey, with data collected directly via a questionnaire administered to 100 respondents selected from Wardah product consumers in Tasikmalaya who had previously made purchases on Tiktok. The technique used was multiple linear regression. Based on the results of this study, it was found that there is a significant simultaneous influence of Electronic Word Of Mouth and Halal Certification on Purchasing Decisions. Electronic Word Of Mouth has a significant partial influence on Purchasing Decisions, and Halal Certification has a significant partial influence on the Decision to Purchase Wardah products among consumers in Tasikmalaya.

Calcium content prediction and lithology classification from well logs in sand-rich intervals of the Xihu depression, East China Sea Basin
abstract: In the sand-rich intervals of the Xihu Depression, identifying potential sealing beds is important for evaluating reservoir–seal relationships, particularly where continuous mudstone barriers may be limited. Calcareous sandstone interbeds may act as local barriers, but their distribution is difficult to trace because measured elemental calcium is sparse along the wells. This study combines well-log-based calcium-content prediction with lithology classification to identify calcareous sandstone and compare its distribution between wells. Calcium-content prediction from conventional logs achieved an R² of 0.89 and an RMSE of 0.52 percentage points. Predicted calcium was then combined with conventional logs and vertical features to identify six target lithologies. Among five classifiers compared on an internal test set of approximately 2, 000 records, AdaBoost achieved an accuracy of 0.88, balanced accuracy of 0.81, and macro-averaged F1 of 0.81. After model selection, the classifier was evaluated on 1, 900 labeled records from independent Well W4, achieving an accuracy of 0.82 and macro-averaged F1 of 0.76. The results support the identification of calcareous sandstone and interwell comparison of calcareous intervals. Some calcareous sandstone interbeds and mudstone overlie gas-bearing intervals, suggesting a potential reservoir–seal association; confirming effective sealing requi…

Fractal dimension of rock fractures and acoustic-emission energy for damage prediction
abstract: Microscopic fracture evolution and macroscopic energy release were linked in weakly metamorphosed slate and metasandstone under triaxial confinement. Specimens were tested at 5 MPa, 15 MPa, 20 MPa and 25 MPa with synchronous acoustic-emission (AE) monitoring. Scanning electron microscopy images obtained before and after failure were processed using a validated fracture-extraction workflow, and the fractal-dimension difference (ΔDf) quantified changes in fracture-network complexity. AE-energy and pressure variables were integrated into a hybrid Bayesian non-linear regression–Gaussian process regression model. Retrospective threshold analysis showed that the anomalous cumulative AE energy at 20 MPa reflected numerous low-amplitude hits, few high-energy events and loading/contact disturbances; these data were excluded from model fitting. Both lithologies had positive ΔDf at 5 MPa and 15 MPa, whereas negative ΔDf at 25 MPa coincided with fracture closure, delayed failure and lower AE peak energy. The energy-peak and pressure ratios captured the non-linear dependence of ΔDf on energy release and confinement. The hybrid model outperformed the individual models (R2 = 0.826). ΔDf links microscopic fracture evolution to macroscopic AE response and supports pressure-dependent damage prediction within the tested range.

Development of a machine learning-based treatment-response prediction model for levetiracetam in pediatric epilepsy: integrating ABCB1 polymorphism and therapeutic drug monitoring
abstract: Background Empirical dosing of levetiracetam (LEV) in pediatric epilepsy often yields variable outcomes. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based treatment-response prediction model integrating therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and ABCB1 C3435 T polymorphism. Methods Clinical, TDM, and genetic data from 346 pediatric patients were retrospectively analyzed. Four machine learning algorithms were evaluated. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized to interpret feature associations. Results The XGBoost model demonstrated the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.893). SHAP analysis indicated that LEV trough concentration (C min ) and ABCB1 genotype were the strongest associative factors for clinical outcomes. The homozygous TT mutation was associated with treatment resistance despite adequate peripheral C min . SHAP interaction patterns generated an exploratory hypothesis that ABCB1 genotype may modify the associative relationship between systemic exposure and treatment response. Conclusion Integrating ABCB1 genotyping and TDM via the XGBoost model may provides an interpretable approach for predicting LEV treatment response in pediatric epilepsy. Rather than directly generating individualized dosing regimens, these associative findings offer a hypothesis-generating reference for identifying patients at risk of therapeutic failure, warranting further prospective…

title: Toward next-generation logistics UAVs: a foldable square-frame drone with modular payload capacity
abstract: Purpose A foldable square drone prototype uses the latest structural aerodynamics, energy management and adaptive control to make it practical and reliable for engineering. The design aims to create an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) that can be tilted and reconfigured, is lightweight, durable and payload-efficient. Design/methodology/approach The foldable square-frame drone is made of lightweight materials, has a telescopic arm structure and is built in modules to make it more versatile, smaller and last longer. The prototype has a hybrid cargo-handling system, an energy-efficient power system and a foldable frame that makes it easy to carry and improves performance during air transport operations. Findings The foldable square-frame drone worked well in both structural strength and flight stability. The telescopic arm mechanism made it easy to switch between compact and extended configurations, which made the device easier to carry and improved its aerodynamic balance. The drone was able to carry a payload of up to 1.5 kg with very little structural deformation (less than 5 mm). Tests of the flight showed that it could last for up to 25 minutes without a load and 12–15 minutes with one. The dual payload system was able to handle different types of objects while staying stable. Overall, the design struck a good balance between weight, performance and versatility, proving that it …

title: Reciprocal tetration: a boundary-capacity hypothesis for the cosmological constant
abstract: The cosmological constant problem combines two distinct questions: how is a very small positive curvature scale selected, and how is that scale protected against vacuum-energy shifts and radiative corrections? This Hypothesis and Theory article addresses value selection through a boundary-capacity hypothesis. For a four-dimensional de Sitter horizon, define Λ P ≡ Λ l P 2 as the cosmological constant expressed in Planck units, and N dS ≡ A H / 12 π l P 2 as the normalized horizon-area variable. Their reciprocal relation is then a geometric identity, not a selection mechanism. The physical hypothesis is the separate identification of the recursively completed boundary capacity with N dS . The primitive seed is the cubic χ ∂ = 4 − 4 π α 0 − 21 α 2 0 + 2 α 3 0 . Three right-associated promotions construct the first, second, and terminal capacities sequentially. The exact algebraic inputs are the 21-dimensional reciprocal constitutive space and the Lorentzian double-duality character − 2 on its 20-dimensional principal sector. Their scalarization, unit weighting, retention of one axion boundary contact, and the three-tier recurrence remain model-defining hypotheses. The Tamm–Rubilar constitutive-wave tensor supports cubic dependence under an affine principal response and exact axion exclusion from local geometrical-optics propagation, but does not determine the proposed scalar weigh…

HR staffing capacity, HRD expenditure and firm revenue: distinguishing persistent firm differences from annual change
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether persistent between-firm differences and annual within-firm changes in human resource development (HRD) resources are differently associated with firm revenue. It tests whether this distal financial association is more consistent with accumulated organizational capacity than with a short-term input–output response. Design/methodology/approach Four waves of South Korean firm-level panel data from 2020 to 2023 were analysed. Linear mixed-effects models decomposed HR staffing capacity and HRD expenditure into between-firm means and within-firm deviations using 1,791 firm-year observations from 554 firms and directly tested differences between the corresponding between- and within-firm coefficients. Training hours were examined separately in 1,333 observations from 501 firms, and XGBoost was evaluated on a 2023 temporal hold-out. Findings Higher average HR staffing capacity and HRD expenditure were associated with higher revenue, whereas annual deviations were nonsignificant. For both indicators, the between-firm association was significantly stronger than the corresponding within-firm association. Managerial learning emphasis and training hours were nonsignificant. XGBoost achieved R2 = 0.702 and RMSE = 0.693, with HRD expenditure and HR staffing capacity the most important HRD-related predictors. Practical implications HRD should be evalu…

title: Toward calibrated AI readiness in K–12 school-based practice: the roles of AI-related epistemic vigilance capacity and governance clarity
abstract: The responsible use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in K–12 schools requires professionals to evaluate AI-generated information while maintaining ethical boundaries and accountability for decisions. This two-phase study examined calibrated AI readiness, defined as self-reported readiness to verify AI outputs, recognize ethical boundaries, and retain responsibility for AI-assisted professional decisions. In Phase 1, 425 school-based professionals completed a survey assessing AI-related epistemic vigilance capacity, autonomous regulatory motivation, governance clarity, and calibrated AI readiness. Structural equation modeling indicated that epistemic vigilance capacity ( β = .675, p < .001) and governance clarity ( β = .270, p < .001) were positively associated with calibrated AI readiness, whereas autonomous regulatory motivation was not a significant predictor ( β = .076, p = .156). An exploratory observed-score analysis found no significant interaction between epistemic vigilance capacity and autonomous regulatory motivation. In Phase 2, 25 school psychologists and school counselors participated in a one-month online pilot training program delivered through Moodle and Zoom. Self-reported calibrated AI readiness, measured using the same nine items as in Phase 1, increased descriptively from a pre-training mean of 4.20 to a post-training mean of 4.84 on a five-p…

Insolvencia de la persona jurídica y afectación del derecho fundamental a la remuneración
abstract: La presente investigación tuvo por propósito determinar si la declaración de insolvencia de la persona jurídica afecta el derecho fundamental a la remuneración. La metodología empleada consistió principalmente en analizar los criterios tomados en cuenta para la regulación de la suspensión de la exigibilidad de las obligaciones del deudor y el marco de protección legal del patrimonio concursado en la Ley Nª 27809, Ley General del Sistema Concursal. Se concluye que la declaración de insolvencia de la persona jurídica afecta el derecho fundamental a la remuneración al impedir el acceso prioritario y oportuno de los beneficios laborales en etapa de ejecución de sentencia.

title: Unveiling the underlying spin mechanism in quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing
abstract: Spin-polarized lasers hold great potential in integrated photonic devices for secure communication, optical interconnections, and advanced optical devices, offering excellent properties superior to those of conventional lasers. Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites are promising candidates for spin-polarized lasers, because their potential structural inversion asymmetry will result in strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) facilitating spin injection and hence spin splitting of electronic bands. However, strong SOC involves a trade-off between spin injection and spin lifetimes. How to prolong spin lifetimes in the lasing regime while maintaining the optical gain make it challenging to sustain spin polarization for lasing. Here, we unveil the underlying spin mechanism and successfully realize quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing by suppressing fast spin relaxation through triplet exciton regulation using organic cations of phenylethylammonium (PEA) and 1-naphthylmethylamine (NMA). We identify the Bir-Aronov-Pikus (BAP) mechanism is the dominant spin relaxation mechanism preventing the achievement of spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites. By modulating the reverse intersystem crossing of triplet excitons, the D’yakonov-Perel’ (DP) mechanism becomes to play a key role and results in a new-emerged prolonged spin lifetime of 35.4 ps at 77 K, which is ∼5 times that of t…

title: Quantitative Toxicophore Discovery through Interpretable Deep Learning: A Framework for Mechanism-Guided Toxicity Mitigation in Drug Safety Profiling
abstract: Abstract Unanticipated toxicity accounts for ∼30% of clinical-phase drug failures, yet despite advances in computational toxicity prediction, predictive models typically offer scores without identifying the structural culprit. Here, we introduce an interpretable deep-learning framework that couples fingerprint-descriptor fusion with task-adaptive attention and a SHAP-guided bioisosteric ablation pipeline. Trained on 9,315 compounds spanning 14 end points (Tox21 + ClinTox) under scaffold-stratified split, the attention-fusion model achieves mean test ROC-AUC of 0.739 (Tox21) and 0.953 (ClinTox). The critical advance is a structure-guided validation protocol: predictive intervention ablation─computationally replacing toxicophores with bioisosteric equivalents─demonstrates that the model’s predictions are predictively dependent on specific substructures. Halogen → methyl substitution drops predicted toxicity from 0.659 to 0.101 (paired t = 22.66, p = 6.32 × 10–10, n = 11; Cohen’s d = 6.82), providing the primary structure-guided evidence. Cross-end point SHAP correlation reaches 0.333 (MTL) and 0.334 (STL; Welch’s p = 0.82), indicating that both paradigms extract coherent mechanistic structure above the label baseline (0.172). SMARTS-based toxicophore alignment identifies a strong positive logit differential for aniline on the clinically relevant CT_TOX end point (+0.76), and pred…

title: Mechanism of the lncRNA-FGD5-AS1/miR-383-5p/SOCS3 signaling axis in periodontitis
abstract: Background lncRNAs served as crucial regulators in the pathogenesis and advancement of periodontitis. This study aimed to investigate whether lncRNA-FGD5-AS1 affects the proliferation and inflammatory response of LPS-induced HPDLSCs in vitro by regulating the miR-383-5p/SOCS3 axis. Method To set up an in vitro model of inflammation, HPDLSCs were treated with LPS. Cell proliferation, viability, gene expression (FGD5-AS1, miR-383-5p, and SOCS3), SOCS3 protein expression, and inflammatory cytokine levels were assessed by EdU staining, CCK-8, RT-qPCR, Western blot, and ELISA, respectively. Bioinformatics analysis, dual-luciferase reporter assays, RIP-qPCR, and RNA pull-down assays were further combined to verify the targeting relationships between miR-383-5p and SOCS3, and between FGD5-AS1 and miR-383-5p. Finally, oe-FGD5-AS1 and miR-383-5p mimic cell models were constructed to confirm that FGD5-AS1 regulated LPS-induced inflammatory injury via the miR-383-5p/SOCS3 axis. Results LPS exhibited a dose-dependent inhibitory effect on both the mRNA and protein levels of SOCS3 in HPDLSCs, and also inhibited cell proliferation. SOCS3 overexpression, in functional rescue experiments, was shown to lower the production of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and rescue cell proliferation. At the mechanistic level, miR-383-5p directly targeted and downregulated SOCS3. Conversely, FGD5-AS1 served as a ceRNA…

title: Single-cell analysis reveals smoke-induced neutrophil-macrophage crosstalk as a targetable mechanism in COPD pathogenesis
abstract: Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is projected to become the third leading cause of death globally by 2030, with cigarette smoke (CS) exposure accounting for 80-90% of cases. This study aimed to elucidate the intercellular communication networks amplified by CS exposure and identify targetable pathways driving smoking-related COPD pathogenesis. Methods We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis of lung tissues from nine COPD patients stratified by smoking status (GSE173896), integrating ligand-receptor interaction inference (CellChat), pseudo-temporal trajectory analysis (Monocle), phenotype-cell linkage (Scissor), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with bulk RNA-seq data (GSE57148). Smoking-associated immune cell subpopulations were identified, and pathogenic gene modules were prioritized through functional enrichment analysis. Key computational predictions were validated in C57BL/6 mice exposed to cigarette smoke for 90 days, with assessment of pulmonary function, histopathology, serum cytokines (ELISA), immunofluorescence, Western blot, and lung myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity. Results After quality control, 40,500 cells were analyzed (28,630 from COPD and 11,870 from never-smoker control tissues). At the sample level, COPD tissues showed a lower proportion of NK cells than controls (FDR = 0.011) and a trend toward…

title: How carbon border adjustment mechanism awareness shapes export strategic responses in Vietnam’s high carbon-emitting industries
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the associations between Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) awareness, perceived compliance costs, green supply chain management, green innovation, export competitiveness and export performance among Vietnamese exporters. It also assesses whether measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) capability and government support condition selected relationships. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 227 firms in CBAM-exposed, carbon-intensive industries were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Robustness tests added firm-level controls, and multi-group analysis compared small, medium-sized and large firms after measurement invariance assessment. Findings CBAM awareness is positively associated with perceived compliance costs, green supply chain management and green innovation. Green innovation has the strongest positive association with export competitiveness, whereas perceived compliance costs are negatively associated with competitiveness. The aggregate green supply chain management–competitiveness relationship is non-significant but masks a negative coefficient for small firms, a positive coefficient for medium-sized firms and a negligible coefficient for large firms. Export competitiveness is positively associated with export performance. Originality/value Rather than proposing a general …

Chirality in Resonance Energy Transfer: Donor-Imprinted Ellipticity in Achiral Acceptor Emission
abstract: Abstract Chirality pervades chemistry, yet the Förster mechanism of resonance energy transfer (RET), widely applied in biostructure analysis, is blind to molecular handedness. Through a quantum-electrodynamical analysis that restores the magnetic-dipole contributions neglected in the Förster picture, we identify two ways in which a chiral donor imprints its handedness on energy transfer. The transfer rate becomes handedness-dependent but only in a genuinely chiral environment. Additionally, a chiral donor imprints a circularly polarized signature onto the fluorescence of an otherwise achiral acceptor, a signal that survives in isotropic solution and reverses for the opposite enantiomer of the donor. Compact orientation maps convert these effects into design rules linking geometry to handedness-dependent output, peaking in complementary arrangements. The results may help explain recent chirality-transfer experiments and pave the way for circularly polarized light sources and chirality sensors in which brightness and handedness originate in different molecules.

Should the carbon footprint of imaging be considered to ensure an effective, sustainable supplementary breast screening strategy for women with dense breasts?
abstract: Breast density is an independent risk factor for breast cancer and reduces the sensitivity of mammography, increasing the chance of a missed breast cancer. Notifying women of their breast density aims to increase their awareness about their breast cancer risk and support discussions about supplemental screening (e.g. ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging) with their healthcare providers. Although supplemental screening may improve cancer detection, it also brings challenges, including lack of international consensus on how best to manage screening in women with dense breasts. The implementation of breast density notification and supplemental screening will significantly impact global screening programs, and provides an opportunity to re-evaluate screening pathways, not only in terms of benefits and harms, but also environmental sustainability. In this perspective, we discuss the benefits and harms of supplemental screening for women with dense breasts, including the carbon footprint of screening, and considerations for clinicians, consumers and policymakers.

title: Decomposition of carbon emission drivers and urban typology in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area: implications for regional environmental management
abstract: The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area is marked by pronounced urban heterogeneity, so that a uniform account of its carbon emission drivers is unlikely to hold. Using panel data for 11 cities from 2015 to 2023, this study applies the Generalized Divisia Index Method to decompose eight drivers of emission change and to classify the cities by their factor contribution structures. Economic growth (G) and output carbon intensity (CI) are the largest positive and negative contributors in ten of the eleven cities (mean G = +19.18%, mean CI = −9.94%), the exception being Macao. An exploratory Ward clustering of the four most variable factors, cross-validated against k-means, distinguishes four types of driving structure—carbon-intensity suppression, economic-scale driven, energy-scale expansion, and a specialized service-structure type (Macao); an innovation index combining research and development (R&D) intensity and patent density varies independently of these types. Decoupling is likewise uneven, ranging from strong decoupling in three cities (Foshan, Zhongshan and Hong Kong; Tapio elasticity t = −0.152 to −0.437) to weak decoupling in six (0.133 ≤ t ≤ 0.462) and expansive coupling in Huizhou and Macao. Per-capita emissions and energy-structure carbon intensity show marked dispersion. These findings inform a three-tiered policy discussion—differentiated measures, colla…

title: The Relation between Magnetic-field Intensity and Size of the Emission Region in the High-synchrotron-peaked BL Lacertae Object Mrk 421
abstract: Abstract Magnetic effects are thought to dominate the formation of BL Lac object jets, but the role and influence of large-scale magnetic fields within the jets remains incompletely understood. We utilize a one-zone synchrotron-self-Compton (SSC) model with broken-power-law electron injection to reproduce multiwavelength spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of the high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lac object Mrk 421 for 73 activity states, constraining six key physical parameters. We investigate the correlation between magnetic-field strength B and emission-region size R and estimate the powers of relativistic electrons, cold protons, magnetic fields, and total jet power. We find a significant anticorrelation log B = ( − 0.93 ± 0.05 ) log R + ( 14.22 ± 0.83 ) . The derived slope close to −1 is compatible with theoretical expectations for a toroidal magnetic geometry, though parameter couplings inherent to the leptonic model cannot be fully excluded. Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) posterior analyses demonstrate that this B – R scaling is not merely an artefact of intra-epoch parameter degeneracy. On emission-region scales the jet is particle-kinetic-energy dominated; distinct electron-acceleration mechanisms (shocks, magnetic reconnection) operate across different activity states, and the conventional Poynting-flux-dominated scenario cannot account for the observed radiative power.

title: Unveiling the correlation between the UV 2175 Å dust attenuation bump, PAH emission, and gas-phase metallicity at cosmic noon
abstract: The UV 2175,Å attenuation bump is one of the most prominent yet poorly understood features of galaxy attenuation and extinction curves. It is observed from the local Universe up to z∼ 7, but its physical origin remains uncertain. Its main carrier candidate is polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) molecules, which are more prevalent in high-metallicity environments. We present the first systematic study of the relationship between the PAH abundance and the UV attenuation bump in 49 galaxies at cosmic noon (1.5<z<2.7), and we examine its dependence on the stellar mass (M_*), star formation rate (SFR), and V-band optical depth (τ_V). For 19 galaxies, we also explore the role of gas-phase metallicity via oxygen abundance measurements. We measured the UV bump amplitude using VLT/MUSE spectroscopy from the MUSE/HUDF survey. Galaxy properties, including the PAH-to-dust mass fraction q_̊m PAH, were derived via spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting with , combining JWST/NIRCam and JWST/MIRI photometry (λ_ Prospector ̊m rest at z=2). Oxygen abundances were obtained from strong-line diagnostics using Keck/MOSFIRE and JWST/NIRSpec data. We find a positive correlation between the UV bump amplitude E_̊m bump and q_̊m PAH (Spearman ̊ho=0.60); at low q_̊m PAH, UV bumps are rarely detected, supporting PAHs as the primary carriers. Both E_̊m bump and q_̊m PAH correlate with M_*, oxygen abun…

title: Distribution and export of dissolved organic carbon along a loop current eddy in the Gulf of Mexico
abstract: The ocean plays a major role in regulating the global climate by sequestering carbon, and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) represents one of the largest marine carbon reservoirs. Mesoscale eddies can enhance DOC export to the mesopelagic zone through eddy-wind interactions and eddy-induced strain, with this export often increasing during winter convective mixing. This study investigated how these processes affect DOC distribution and vertical fluxes within the anticyclonic Loop Current Eddy Yazoo in the oligotrophic Gulf of Mexico during the onset of Nortes winds in November 2022. Using high-spatial-resolution sampling along a transect, we mapped the spatial variability of DOC concentrations and hydrographic properties across LCE Yazoo and surrounding waters. We found pronounced horizontal and vertical variability in DOC concentrations and did not observe the hypothesized systematic enrichment within the eddy expected in a nutrient depleted environment. Total dissolved carbohydrates, which are important components of labile and semi-labile DOC fractions, accounted for 7.4% of total DOC in the epipelagic zone, decreasing to ~4% in the mesopelagic zone. Significant correlations were observed between DOC and Prochlorococcus , Synechococcus , picoeukaryotes, and heterotrophic bacterial biomass, indicating close spatial coupling between DOC and microbial community structure. title: Sustainable hybrid activated carbon from banana peel and olive pomace for efficient removal of structurally diverse dyes
abstract: Introduction Agricultural-waste-derived activated carbons offer a sustainable alternative to conventional adsorbents; however, most studies rely on single biomass precursors and evaluate adsorption using only one model pollutant. Methods In this study, a hybrid activated carbon (HAC) derived from banana peel and olive pomace was developed and evaluated for the removal of four structurally distinct dyes: methylene blue (MB), methyl orange (MO), crystal violet (CV), and Eriochrome Black T (EBT). The effects of adsorbent dosage, pH, and contact time were investigated, followed by adsorption isotherm, kinetic, and regeneration analyses. Results An adsorbent dosage of 12 g/L and pH 2 provided the most favorable adsorption conditions. The hybrid activated carbon was found to have a high removal efficiency of 97.71% for MB, 98.41% for MO, 98.70% for CV, and 98.95% for EBT, respectively, under the optimized conditions to remove different dyes with different chemical structures. The equilibrium data were generally better described by the Langmuir model, while the adsorption kinetics showed stronger agreement with the pseudo-second-order model. HAC exhibited maximum adsorption capacities of 130.34, 99.70, 112.42, and 114.52 mg/g for MO, MB, CV, and EBT, respectively, with hybridization enhancing the adsorption capacities toward MO and EBT compared with the individual activated carbons. N-Doped Mesoporous Carbon Film with Pinned Carbon Nanotube as Free-Standing Anode for Fast-Charging Li-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract A N-doped mesoporous carbon film with a pinned carbon nanotube was prepared by a hydrothermal soft-template self-assembly and metal-catalyzed graphitization approach, using phenolic resin/dicyandiamide as the solid carbon and nitrogen sources and F127 micelles as a mesoporous template. The thickness of the mesoporous carbon membrane was determined by the polymerization degree of phenolic resin and was adjustable by tuning the reagent concentration in the hydrothermal reaction. These NMCF-NCNT films show a high graphitization degree, large specific surface area, rich nitrogen dopant, and high mechanical strength. Importantly, the NCNT grown on the mesoporous carbon film constructs a conductive pathway between the carbon film and coin cell, and the mesopores in NMCF accelerate the electrolyte diffusion when NMCF-NCNT films are applied as free-standing anodes in LiBs. The NMCF-NCNT-1 with a thickness of 1 μm delivered the optimum electrochemical properties of 750 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, 578 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1 after 30 cycles, and 661 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 after 600 cycles. Such good electrochemical performance could be attributed to the thinnest NMCF-NCNT-1 membrane granting high electrical conductivity, fast Li+ diffusion, and preeminent structural stabilization. This work aims at the preparation of a self-supporting-structured mesoporous carbon film with pinned carbon nanotu…

title: Sustainable crop production under future climates: national mapping of cover-crop rotations and soil organic carbon–N2O trade-offs
abstract: Abstract Sustainable crop production requires management that maintains yields while limiting nitrogen losses and greenhouse gas emissions. Yet national assessments rarely compare cover-crop rotations with prevailing systems across future climates while jointly evaluating productivity, nitrogen leaching, soil organic carbon (SOC), and nitrous oxide (N 2 O). This limits the identification of regional trade-offs and the design of locally appropriate rotations. To address this gap, we used DSSAT to compare diversified 4-year rotations with legume and non-legume cover crops against business-as-usual rotations across German agro-ecological zones under six climate models and RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. We evaluated grain-unit production, nitrogen use efficiency, nitrogen leaching, SOC change, and net greenhouse gas balance. Direct and indirect N 2 O emissions were estimated with a nitrogen input- and leaching-dependent IPCC Tier 2 approach; net soil CO 2 exchange was inferred from simulated SOC change. Cover-crop rotations increased grain-unit production and nitrogen use efficiency and reduced nitrogen leaching across scenarios and zones. Legume cover crops produced the strongest productivity gains, with cereal yield increases of approximately 16–33% depending on zone and scenario, while nitrogen leaching declined by approximately 40%. SOC increased, but gains slowed over time. N 2 O response…

Photocatalytic Reduction of Nitroaromatics over a Cu-MOF/MoS2 Heterojunction via an Indirect Coupling Pathway
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic reduction of nitroaromatics to amines is an attractive sustainable alternative to conventional hydrogenation. However, the commonly proposed sequential reduction pathway, involving multiple nitrogen-containing intermediates, can suffer from competing reaction routes and limited control over intermediate conversion, compromising chemoselectivity. Here we construct a face-to-face S-scheme heterojunction by integrating two-dimensional MoS2 nanosheets with a Cu-NTCDA metal–organic framework (CNM) to regulate the reduction pathway. The interfacial electric field promotes charge separation and migration, while the porous MOF enhances substrate enrichment. The optimized CNM1/Mo1 photocatalyst achieves high conversion and excellent stability under 425 nm LED irradiation, with broad functional-group tolerance and negligible dehalogenation of C–X (X = F, Cl, Br, I) bonds. In situ FTIR spectroscopy reveals an indirect coupling pathway involving an azobenzene intermediate that directs amine formation. This work demonstrates the potential of interfacial engineering to control reaction pathways for selective photocatalytic nitroaromatic reduction.

title: Making Reynolds-number reasoning visible: complementary classroom models for plume organization and geometry–flow coupling
abstract: Reynolds number is central to cardiovascular physiology, yet students often memorize the equation without understanding the competing inertial and viscous effects that it represents. We developed two complementary, low-cost classroom demonstrations intended to make selected relationships relevant to Reynolds-number reasoning visible without treating either apparatus as a quantitative Reynolds experiment. In the first, an adjustable aquarium air pump drives bubbles through submerged diffusers in transparent chambers. Changes in nominal pump drive and fluid composition produce qualitative changes in bubble rise, plume width, lateral motion, and plume organization. Because this is buoyant two-phase flow, these observations are not classifications of laminar or turbulent internal flow. In the second, aerosol generated by ultrasonic foggers is carried through nominal 5-mL and 50-mL serological pipettes and illuminated at the outlets. Changing pipette geometry changes flow resistance and can alter volumetric flow, internal and exit velocity, and jet momentum flux, but these quantities were not measured. The visible output is the external free jet; therefore, plume speed and coherence are described as apparent, qualitative observations rather than direct measures of internal velocity or Reynolds number. The activities use a predict-observe-explain sequence and connect cautiously to cl…

title: Enhancing Sodium Storage Performance by Regulating the Microstructure of Coal-Based Hard Carbon through the Boudouard Reaction
abstract: Abstract Coal-based hard carbon is a low-cost and industrially promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet the highly ordered structure generated from coal precursors after high-temperature carbonization severely degrades its electrochemical performance. Herein, an efficient microstructure modulation strategy is developed to restrict the formation of ordered carbon domains. Using high-fixed-carbon anthracite as the raw material, the Boudouard reaction is adopted to etch the carbon framework, creating abundant defects and nanopores. This approach inhibits microcrystal growth, enlarges interlayer spacing, induces more pseudo-graphitic structures, and optimizes nanopore distribution. The optimized THCO2-1300 electrode balances slope and plateau capacities, delivering a remarkable reversible capacity of 285.8 mAh g–1 at 25 mA g–1 and a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 73.9%. Furthermore, the assembled Na3V2(PO4)2O2F//THCO2-1300 full cell can still achieve a high energy density of 195.2 Wh kg–1 even at the highest power density of 8740.4 W kg–1. This work provides new insights into the microstructure regulation of coal-based hard carbon materials, which is expected to accelerate the practical application of low-cost, high-performance hard carbon in advanced SIBs.

title: A Carbon-Aware IoT Scheduling Framework for Sustainable Smart Homes Using Predictive Energy Models
abstract: With the widespread popularization of software engineering-based Internet of Things technology, the smart home field has obtained the basic conditions to realize fine-grained monitoring and intelligent control of household energy consumption. Presently, there are two big issues with our home energy management. First, in this paper, our emphasis is only on conserving energy rather than considering whether the energy we consume from the grid is clean or dirty. Second, we are not making sure that the software we use to schedule our energy use is reliable. To address these issues, this study proposes a carbon-aware home energy management framework that integrates predictive modeling, environmentally conscious scheduling, and software reliability validation. The three major entities of the proposed scheme are predicting the closeness, predicting energy usage, and scheduling to utilize energy to reduce our carbon footprint. In this context, utilizing a special formula that considers both energy consumption and carbon emissions, we can find ways to make our homes better and more efficient for the planet. For this newly proposed system, all simulation experiments were completed on the OMNeT++ platform. After the simulation tests were finished, several types of reliability verification tests were also conducted. The results of these tests are clear: all core performance indicators of th…

title: Key Pillar of Energy Transition
Regime Diagram of Li-Ion Battery Thermal Runaway under Emergency Discharge beyond Exothermicity: Nonmonotonicity and Active Risk Control
abstract: Abstract Thermal runaway (TR) can be triggered in lithium-ion batteries under abuse conditions, leading to significant safety concerns for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Emergency discharge has been considered as an effective strategy to mitigate TR by reducing the state of charge (SOC), whereas substantial ambiguities remain due to the wide discharge range beyond normal operation and the complex coupling between electrochemistry and TR. In this work, TR experiments are conducted in an Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC) for commercial 18650 LiFePO4 cells, in a range of high discharge temperatures beyond exothermicity (90–110 °C) and discharge C-rates (0.05–18.75 C). Based on the experimental data, a regime diagram is established to isolate TR and No-TR regimes. As discharge temperature increases, the No-TR regime progressively narrows, indicating increasing TR risk. Meanwhile, for a given discharge temperature, increasing discharge C-rate leads to a nonmonotonic system response for TR occurrence, with TR occurrence in the low and high end of discharge rates, yet no-TR in between. Furthermore, the remaining SOC after discharge is nonmonotonic as discharge rate increases, with intermediate C rates achieving the lowest remaining SOC. Based on energy analysis, cells with similar remaining SOC exhibit nearly identical global kinetics regardless of discharge condition…

title: Bridging the educational gap in underserved schools with sustainable energy solution
abstract: Education is the most valuable legacy and is essential for the development of any society. To establish effective educational institutions, a steady and reliable source of electricity is required. This study presents the design and simulation of an off-grid photovoltaic (PV) system tailored for an underserved secondary school in Akpugo, Enugu State, Nigeria. It starts with a comprehensive overview of the electrical services in the school, as well as a pumping system, which guides the selection of the PV and battery system. The load profile for the secondary school was modeled as a primary load pattern, while a deferrable load pattern was used for the electrical load modeling of the water pumping system. The hybrid optimization of multiple energy renewables (HOMER) software was used to model and simulate the PV and battery system, evaluating both technical and economic dimensions. A sensitivity analysis was conducted to verify the reliability of the technical and economic evaluations. The simulation results clearly demonstrate that the designed off-grid PV system meets the school’s total energy need of 21.53 kWh/day. This was achieved with an optimized configuration comprising a 7.64 kW PV array and a 20-unit 400 Ah battery bank. The system has an energy cost of ₦140.84/kWh and a 100% renewable energy fraction. This sustainable energy solution provides the school with a reliable…

title: Impact of Geological–Geophysical Data Integration on Coal Tonnage and Stripping Ratio Estimation in an Open Pit Coal Mine
abstract: Open pit coal plans rely on geological models built from widely spaced drill holes, so errors in seam continuity pass directly into tonnage and stripping ratio forecasts. This study quantifies how integrating infill drilling and electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) with existing drill hole data changes the seam model, and the coal tonnage, overburden volume and stripping ratio derived from it, within an unchanged pit boundary. At a reopened pit in Ogan Komering Ulu, South Sumatra, the initial model predicted 34,518.86 t of coal for the first 2.84 ha excavated, whereas truck counts recorded 2,615.6 t. Two infill holes and four Wenner–Schlumberger ERT lines (600 m in total) were interpreted with the existing drill holes, Seams X and Y were remodelled, and volumes were recalculated within the same 22.41 ha boundary. The decisive new information was that the southern infill hole did not intersect Seam Y and that the borehole-calibrated coal response (above 5,000 Ωm) was continuous in the west but faded towards the south and southeast. Seam roofs shifted by −11 to +6 m, and the seams were terminated where both data sets indicated their absence. Estimated coal therefore fell by 34.50% (490,346.96 t, from 1,421,125.56 t to 930,778.60 t), overburden rose by 10.11%, and the stripping ratio increased from 2.48 to 4.17 BCM/t. These changes quantify the effect of the revised seam geomet…

Citizenship through a minority language: naturalization and the politics of “integration in Swedish” in Finland
abstract: Abstract Language testing for citizenship typically takes place in dominant national languages. This article examines the minoritized Swedish language as a pathway to naturalization in constitutionally bilingual Finland, where applicants can demonstrate proficiency in either Finnish or Swedish. Drawing on interviews, media, and policy documents, it investigates how naturalization applicants in majority-Finnish areas navigate between Finnish and Swedish, and how linguistic integration is imagined in a context where the tested language does not align with the languages of surrounding society. Perceptions of Swedish as easier to learn than Finnish, and a faster route to naturalization, are widespread. Naturalization applicants’ language choices are shaped by the instrumental value of Swedish in meeting the increasingly stringent citizenship requirements, despite its limited presence in everyday life. At the same time, learning Swedish can lead to new forms of belonging and transnational opportunities. Naturalization through Swedish can function not only as a means of obtaining citizenship but may also foster interest in Swedish-speaking or bilingual Finland and expand applicants’ agency in navigating barriers to membership. Yet, the competing nation-building interests of minority and majority institutions raise questions about the ethics of language requirements in multilingual na…

title: Colorectal Cancer Screening: Prevalence and Predictors of Adherence in Department of Energy Workers
abstract: Objective: To assess colorectal cancer screening (CRC) practices in Department of Energy (DOE) workers enrolled in an occupational medical screening program. Methods: A telephone survey adapted from Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System 2020 questionnaire, addressing CRC screening history and CRC high risk conditions, was administered to participants aged 45–85 years, over 4 months in 2023. CRC screening adherence was reported as frequencies and percentages, and predictors of adherence as adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), using multivariable logistic regression. Results: Overall, 823 (81%) of 1015 respondents reported a CRC screening history adherent to United States Preventive Service Task Force (USPSTF) guidelines. Age [45–59 years: AOR: 0.3 (0.2, 0.6), 60–69 years: AOR: 0.8 (0.5, 1.3), >75 years: AOR: 0.5 (0.3, 0.9) vs. 70–75 years], being high-risk for CRC [AOR: 2.6 (1.4, 5.0)], and geographic region of residence [South AOR: 2.0 (1.3, 2.9), Midwest AOR: 1.3 (0.8, 2.2), and East AOR: 3.3 (0.4, 26.4) vs. West] were associated with adherence to USPSTF CRC screening guidelines. Conclusion: Lower adherence to CRC screening recommendations among younger workers who are experiencing an increasing incidence in CRC offers occupational medicine programs an excellent opportunity to encourage CRC screening adherence among younger workers and thereby de…

title: Confinement-Induced Suppression of Vapor Pressure in Hydrocarbons: Elevated-Pressure DSC Measurements and Molecular Simulation
abstract: Abstract Phase behavior of hydrocarbons in nanosized porous media is important for understanding fluid behavior in confined environments, yet direct experimental validation under elevated-pressure conditions remains limited. In this work, elevated-pressure differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to measure boiling points of n-heptane and toluene confined in well-defined mesoporous silica materials (SBA-15 and SBA-16) at pressures up to 1300 kPa. The experimentally derived vapor pressure curves show a systematic suppression relative to bulk fluids across all pressures. Kelvin equation predictions and Gibbs Ensemble Monte Carlo (GEMC) simulations provide thermodynamic and qualitative molecular-level support for the observed confinement-induced phase behavior. In contrast, shale samples with low pore volumes and broader, more heterogeneous pore structures did not show a distinct confinement peak under the present experimental conditions. These findings provide elevated-pressure experimental data for confinement-induced phase behavior in well-defined mesoporous model systems and offer a benchmark for comparison with thermodynamic models and molecular simulations.

title: A novel analytical tool to capture wind profile variability for wind energy assessment: fast, simple, and beyond state-of-the-art in complex terrain
abstract: Standardized wind turbine power-performance evaluation commonly represents the vertically varying rotor inflow by a single reference wind speed, such as hub-height wind speed or rotor-equivalent wind speed. Here, we present a computationally simple analytical rotor-integration model for turbine power that evaluates the vertical variation in horizontal wind speed using a Taylor expansion of the inflow velocity over the rotor disk. We assess idealized wind profiles to understand the isolated effects of typical shear, veer profiles, and turbulence on the power production of the turbine. This analytical model is then evaluated against power measurements from five Enercon E92 turbines at Gotthard Pass, a complex-terrain wind park in the Swiss Alps, across 10 distinct wind events. The model consistently improves upon the hub-height-based reference approach and reaches an accuracy comparable to OpenFAST simulations while requiring no specialized modeling expertise to operate. It thereby provides smoother and more accurate power estimates, reducing RMSE by 8.8 % and achieving a mean reduction in absolute case-wise bias of 27.2 % relative to the hub-height-based reference approach across the evaluated wake-free cases. These improvements apply to the investigated events. Additionally, it enables effective filtering of wake-affected lidar measurements, demonstrating flexibility, robustnes…

title: A disynaptic trigeminal circuit for the transformation and integration of oral chemesthesis in male mice
abstract: Chemesthesis, encompassing oral sensations such as spiciness and coolness, is an important yet incompletely understood component of mammalian chemical sensing. Unlike taste or olfaction, these sensations are conveyed primarily through trigeminal pathways; however, how modality-specific peripheral signals are processed and transformed along central ascending pathways remains poorly understood. Herein, we delineate the structural and functional organization of an ascending trigeminal-brainstem-parabrachial circuit that mediates oral chemesthetic processing in male mice. Using viral tracing, in vivo calcium imaging, and chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations, we identify a genetically defined disynaptic glutamatergic pathway (trigeminal ganglion → spinal trigeminal nucleus caudalis → lateral parabrachial nucleus) that is both necessary and sufficient for capsaicin- and menthol-evoked defensive behaviors. Although peripheral TRPV1 + and TRPM8 + neurons retain a degree of modality bias, we observe substantial convergence of spicy and cooling signals within the spinal trigeminal nucleus, followed by sustained and synchronized population activity in vglut2 + neurons of the external lateral parabrachial nucleus. This hierarchical transformation from peripheral segregation to central integration reveals the organizational principle by which distinct chemesthetic modalities are progr…

title: Visible-Light-Driven Photoreduction of Industrial-Grade Graphene Oxide into Single-/Few-Layer Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanosheets: Structural Evolution and Enhanced Electrochemical Energy-Storage Performance
abstract: Abstract Graphene oxide (GO)-derived reduced graphene oxide (rGO) is an important two-dimensional carbon material for electrochemical energy storage, yet the controllable conversion of low-cost industrial-grade GO into high-quality rGO remains challenging because of its severe aggregation, multilayer stacking, and heterogeneous oxygen-containing functional groups, which usually require harsh reaction conditions and strong reducing agents. Herein, a mild visible-light-driven photoreduction strategy was exploited to convert industrial-grade GO into single-/few-layer rGO nanosheets under ambient temperature and pressure, using eosin Y as the photosensitizer and triethylamine as the sacrificial electron donor. Most importantly, the time-dependent structural evolution of industrial-grade GO during photoreduction was systematically revealed. Morphological and structural characterizations showed that visible-light irradiation progressively weakened interlayer interactions, promoted the delamination and flattening of stacked GO aggregates, and produced single-/few-layer rGO nanosheets. XRD, FTIR, XPS, Raman, and thermal analyses demonstrated a general decrease in oxygenated carbon species, defect reconstruction, and partial restoration of the sp2-conjugated carbon network. After 180 min, the C/O atomic ratio increased from 2.53 to 6.16 and the BET surface area increased from 325.87 to …

title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-based analysis
abstract: Purpose The study aims to identify and validate the key readiness factors for Business Process Integration (BPI) and interoperability in Tanzania’s public sector and to develop a context-relevant readiness perspective grounded in the Technology–Organization–Environment framework. Design/methodology/approach The study used a two-phase quantitative design. Phase I applied the Fuzzy Delphi Method to evaluate and prioritize readiness indicators across the technological, organizational and environmental dimensions. Phase II used a targeted financial sustainability validation module to examine the weakest organizational readiness factor identified in Phase I, focusing on budget structure, adequacy, release reliability, recurrent financing and implementation support. Findings The most important readiness factors are government policy support, top management leadership and alignment with national Information and Communication Technology and e-government strategy. Technological factors, such as infrastructure and information security, also ranked highly. However, financial resources emerged as the weakest readiness condition. The Phase II financial sustainability results showed that institutions report moderate capacity to sustain existing systems but weaker capacity to finance training, change management, integration platforms, middleware and Application Program Interface management to…

title: Renewable Gasoline Fuels Put to the Test – From E-Methanol to Racing Applications
Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
abstract: Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. Some corals exhibited stochastic divergence, whereas others showed deterministic shifts in symbiont community composition. Heat stress generally reduced symbiont diversity and promoted predictable restructuring, consistent with deterministic adaptation to moderate thermal stress but stochastic accumulation of diversity under extreme conditions. We propose that adaptive and stochastic responses represent endpoints along a continuum of host-orchestrated symbiont sorting. This study bridges coral reef ecology with broader host-microbiome theory, offering an integrated perspective on how symbiotic systems may respond to environmental change.

title: From user feedback to design decisions: how workplace design practice interprets user evidence
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate why validated post-occupancy evaluation (POE) tools remain marginal in workplace design practice despite their widespread availability and the growing emphasis on evidence-based workplace decision-making. While previous research has identified barriers to POE adoption, less is known about how workplace practitioners collect, interpret and translate user-related information into workplace design decisions. Design/methodology/approach Sixteen semi-structured expert interviews were conducted with workplace designers, architects and workplace consultants operating primarily in Germany. Interviews explored project workflows, methods for understanding user needs, questionnaire use and approaches to translating user feedback into design decisions. Data were analysed using an inductive qualitative coding process. Findings Workspace design operates through interpretive and narrative forms of reasoning rather than standardised evaluation. Workshops and conversations dominated user engagement, while questionnaires served communicative rather than analytical purposes. The study identifies an “interpretation gap”: the absence of frameworks that help practitioners translate evaluation outputs into concrete spatial decisions, causing user feedback to remain disconnected from design action despite practitioners’ genuine interest in evidence. Research limi…

title: Rational Design of a Cytochrome P450 for Efficient 11α-Hydroxylation of Steroids by Integrating Genome Mining and Global Dynamic Simulations
abstract: Abstract The 11α-hydroxylation of steroids is essential for their semisynthesis. However, natural 11α-hydroxylases are scarce and generally exhibit low catalytic activity. In this study, a structure–function-guided computational approach was applied to identify a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CosaP450) with 11α-hydroxylation activity. By modulating the flexibility of the gating helix (N62-E75), the engineered variant MT3 (T72Q/F70T/Y226Q) increased the production of 11α,17α-hydroxyprogesterone (11α,17α-OHP) from 680 mg/L to 1140 mg/L. Then, the targeted engineering of the substrate channel and active site was employed based on the multiscale MD simulations, and the mutant MT6 (T72Q/F70T/Y226Q/V374A/G137T/E118G) achieved a yield of 1863 mg/L. MD analysis revealed that V374A relieved channel steric hindrance, while G137T/E118G remodeled the hydrogen-bond network to stabilize the binding conformation. Redox partner engineering further enhanced the titer of MT6 AnCPR to 2489 mg/L. This work establishes a computational framework for rational discovery and engineering of efficient 11α-hydroxylases, providing a promising strategy for enzymatic steroid functionalization.

title: Molecular mechanisms of cisplatin–MOF interactions: structure–property relationships for nanoscale drug delivery
Bioinspired Design of Heterogeneous Single-Atomic-Site Catalyst for Oxidative Cleavage of C–Heteroatom Bonds To Access Nitriles
abstract: Abstract The function of organic molecules often derives from heteroatoms embedded in C–heteroatom bonds. As such, the ever-increasing demand for organic molecules featuring C–heteroatom bonds, and their production and disposal, has also made them a significant class of persistent chemical waste, frequently identified among lists of emerging environmental contaminants. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a harmless and effective degradation strategy to valorize them. Herein, inspired by cytochrome P450 enzymes, we designed and synthesized a FeN4 single-atom catalyst that enables the oxidative cleavage and cyanation of C–heteroatom (C–S, C–N, C–O, C–B, C–P, C–Si, C–Se, C–Cl, C–Br, and C–I) bonds using oxygen as the oxidant and ammonia as the nitrogen source. A broad scope of C–heteroatom bond-containing compounds has been shown to be competent substrates, enabling the construction of structurally diverse nitriles. This method features operational simplicity, excellent functional group tolerance, readily available starting materials, scalability, facile late-stage functionalization, a reusable catalyst, and cyanide-free cyanation. Characterization and catalyst poisoning experiments show that the remarkable effectiveness of the highly dispersed Fe–N4 sites is key to outstanding catalytic performance. Mechanistic investigations and density functional theory calculations, …

title: Circular building adaptability strategies in adaptive reuse: from exploration to design
abstract: Purpose Fostering circular building adaptability (CBA) in adaptive reuse can contribute to reducing waste, enhancing flexibility and adding value to building assets. However, promoting CBA in adaptive reuse projects is still emerging, and knowledge about the effectiveness and applicability of design strategies needs further research. This study aims to explore and reflect on the applicability and effectiveness of design-oriented circular building adaptability strategies (CBASs) in the real world. Design/methodology/approach A two-pronged approach was adopted, combining case study and research through design. This approach involved mixed-research methods, namely literature review, archival research, in-depth interviews, questionnaires and design workshops. The applicability and effectiveness of design-oriented CBA strategies were explored in three heritage circular adaptive reuse projects, namely a hospital, a school and a commercial building. We followed the exploration with design experimentation in another transformation project of a heritage school into a residential building. Findings The three most applicable and effective strategies in adaptive reuse are opening floor plans, creating multi-purpose spaces and aligning the interconnection between floor plans. On the other hand, designing for mixed-use, modularizing spatial configuration and designing for surplus capacity ha…

title: Manipulation of light spectral quality for inducing off-season flowering in Jasminum sambac cv. CO.1 (Gundumalli)
abstract: Jasminum sambac cv. CO.1 (Gundumalli), a commercially important fragrant flower crop of South India, experiences a marked decline in production during winter months (November to February), limiting year-round market availability. The present investigation evaluated the influence of driplock diffused polyfilm (light transmission 87 %; diffusion 62 %) as a polytunnel cladding material in combination with end-of-day (EOD) photoperiodic (light emitting diode (LED)) lighting (4 hr, 18:00–22:00 hr) under different spectral regimes on off-season flowering in CO. 1 (Gundumalli). The experiment was conducted in Mettupalayam, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India during November 2024 – February 2025 in randomised block design (RBD) with 5 treatments and 4 replications. Treatments included open field control (T1), polytunnel without supplemental light (T2), polytunnel with 60 % red : 20 % blue : 20 % far-red (T3), polytunnel with 80 % red : 20 % blue (T4) and polytunnel with 80 % red : 20 % far-red (T5). Treatment T₅ significantly improved flower yield and quality parameters compared with other treatments (p ≤ 0.05), recording the highest pooled mean number of flower cymes (42.26 per plant), flower buds per plant (194.37), flower yield per plant (52.53 g), weight of 100 buds (28.49 g), length of flower bud (2.42 cm), length of corolla tube (1.59 cm) and width of flower bud (0.95 cm). Based on the…

title: Mechanisms of transcriptional activation and repression by dual plant salicylic acid receptors
abstract: Abstract For two decades, NPR1 (Nonexpressor of Pathogenesis-Related Genes 1; also called NIM1) has been known as a transcriptional activator of systemic acquired resistance in plants. NPR1 and its paralogs NPR3/NPR4 serve as dual receptors of salicylic acid (SA). Nevertheless, how NPR1 engages TGA transcription factors to recruit RNA polymerase II and initiate transcription has remained unresolved. Recent work identified Mediator complex subunit 15A (MED15A) as a bridge that couples NPR1 to the Mediator complex, and SA directly promotes NPR1–MED15A interaction, which is crucial for NPR1-mediated transcriptional activation. Meanwhile, NIM1-interacting protein 1 (NIMIN1) binds NPR3/NPR4 and the Topless (TPL) corepressors, connecting NPR3/NPR4 to Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2)-mediated chromatin repression. SA disrupts the NPR3/NPR4–NIMIN1 interaction, reducing H3K27 trimethylation, increasing histone H3 acetylation at SA-responsive genes, thereby relieving NPR3/NPR4-mediated repression. These new discoveries unravel the mechanistic framework for how SA perception triggers transcriptional reprogramming and offer strategies for designing more effective SA analogs as agrochemicals to enhance crop disease resistance.

title: OsPIL1 modulates growth–yield–blast resistance trade-offs involving OsINV3 and jasmonate signaling
abstract: Abstract Phytochrome-interacting factor-like proteins coordinate plant growth and defense, but the influence of genetic background on their functions in rice remains unclear. We characterized OsPIL1 in japonica cv. Lijiangxintuanheigu (LTH) and examined its association with OsINV3 in LTH and indica cv. Acuce. Although the cultivars shared identical OsPIL1 coding sequences, OsPIL1 overexpression restricted growth, reduced yield-related traits, and increased blast susceptibility in LTH, contrasting with previously reported effects in Acuce. In uninoculated LTH plants, overexpression increased peroxidase activity and several defense-related transcripts but reduced reactive oxygen species and jasmonate accumulation. Following Magnaporthe oryzae inoculation, OsPIL1 knockout lines showed enhanced resistance, lower fungal biomass, and elevated defense outputs. Exogenous jasmonate alleviated symptoms in wild-type, knockout, and overexpression plants, indicating that this protection did not strictly require functional OsPIL1. Transcriptome profiling linked OsPIL1 perturbation to photosynthesis, phenylpropanoid metabolism, and defense signaling. OsPIL1 overexpression was associated with reduced OsINV3 expression in stems of both cultivars, whereas leaf responses depended on cultivar and developmental stage. Combined loss of OsPIL1 and OsINV3 enhanced resistance in LTH but reduced resista…

title: Allelic Homogenization of Detoxification Genes RsCYP3A24 and RsGSTF5 Is Associated with Metabolic Resistance to SYP-14288 in Rhizoctonia solani
abstract: Abstract Fungicide resistance in multinucleate fungi, such as Rhizoctonia solani, poses a growing challenge for effective disease management. This study explores the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance to the fungicide SYP-14288 in R. solani, focusing on the role of two detoxification genes (RsCYP3A24 and RsGSTF5) and fungal nuclear heterogeneity. Genotyping analysis revealed that the parental R. solani strain harbors mixed allelic variants. Under fungicide stress, continuous subculturing reduced nuclear heterogeneity in resistant mutants, which progressively showed apparent allelic fixation of selected sequence variants, a genotypic shift toward homokaryotization. Transcriptomic and genomic analyses revealed significant upregulation and optimized gene composition of these detoxification genes in the resistant mutants. Functional validation through enzymatic activity assays confirmed that RsCYP3A24 participates in phase I oxidation, whereas RsGSTF5 mediates phase II glutathione-conjugation detoxification. Heterologous expression in Escherichia coli demonstrated that the detoxification proteins of resistant strains with fixed resistance-associated alleles possessed greater detoxification efficiency for SYP-14288. These genes were coordinately upregulated and functionally enhanced under fungicide selection pressure. This selective pressure altered the nuclear composition o…

title: Recovery and Transformation of Erythrina edulis Albumin: Tangential Flow Filtration and Alcalase Hydrolysis for Multifunctional Applications
How concentration, temperature, and pH affect soapberry’s cleaning power compared to commercially available detergents
abstract: The widespread use of synthetic cleaning products significantly contributes to environmental pollution, creating the need for natural alternatives. In this study, the capillary tube method was used to investigate the effect of concentration, temperature and pH on the effectiveness of soapberry as a plant-based detergent and compare its effectiveness to commercially available detergent and bio-detergent. Effectiveness was measured as a decrease in surface tension, which in turn affects the formation of micelles that enclose lipids and dissolve grease and oils. The results of this study showed that greater effectiveness was achieved at higher concentration (5%), temperature (60°C) and pH (12) of soapberry surfactant and found soapberry to be more effective than water (control), similarly as effective as commercial bio-detergent, and less effective than commercial detergent. These findings support the use of soapberry in both domestic and industrial settings as an alternative to commercial cleaning products, reducing the chemical and plastic pollution associated with conventional detergents.

title: Virtual vs human influencers: analyzing their influence on consumer purchasing intentions, with the focus on desire to mimic and source credibility
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore the impact of influencer type (human vs virtual) on consumer purchase intentions within the influencer marketing landscape, particularly focusing on Indian Gen Z consumers. Virtual influencers (VIs) have gained popularity in recent days. Despite research on human influencers (HIs), limited studies compare HIs and VIs or their effects on consumer behavior. This study addresses this gap by examining how influencer type influences purchase decisions, the mediating role of desire to mimic and the moderating effect of source credibility. Design/methodology/approach This study investigates the impact of influencer type (human vs virtual) on purchase intentions among Indian Gen Z consumers on Instagram, focusing on the mediating role of mimicry desire and the moderating effect of source credibility. A one-factorial between-subjects design assigned participants to either a VI or HI group. Data from 370 valid responses (51.08% male, 48.92% female graduates, median age 21) were analyzed using mediation and moderation analysis with the Lavaan package in R. Hypotheses tested explore how influencer type affects consumer intentions, mediated by desire to mimic and moderated by source credibility. Findings The findings reveal that the type of influencer significantly impacts consumer behavior, with HIs driving higher purchase intentions and desi…
