Bacterial community dynamics associated with Pinus massoniana across progression stages of pine wilt disease
abstract: Abstract Aims Plant microbiomes display distinct spatial compartmentalization, yet their responses to disease disturbance across host compartments and disease stages remains largely unexplored. Methods This study characterized bacterial communities in five compartments of Pinus massoniana (needles, stems, roots, rhizosphere soil and bulk soil) across four stages of pine wilt disease (PWD; healthy, early, intermediate and late) using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and functional prediction. Results The results showed that bacterial community dynamics were significantly influenced by compartment and disease stage. Notably, the stem compartment exhibited substantial changes: Chao1 index significantly increased at the intermediate stage, whereas Chao1, Shannon and Shannoneven indices declined at late stage. Also in stem compartment, the late stage was characterized by marked enrichment of the phylum Proteobacteria, accompanied by elevated relative abundances of the genera Pseudomonas and Methylobacterium . In contrast, the phylum Actinobacteriota and its affiliated genus Acidothermus decreased markedly. Additionally, functional prediction revealed enhanced chemoheterotrophy and aromatic compound degradation pathways as disease progressed ( P < 0.05). By comparison, bacterial communities in needles remained stable across all stages. In roots, Mycobacterium was significantly enric…

title: From orchestrated resources to supply chain performance: the indirect role of power
abstract: Purpose The study applied resource orchestration and resource dependency theories to examine how firm resources affect supply chain performance in Ghana's food and beverage industry, as well as the mediating role of power. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach and explanatory design were employed using survey data collected from firms in Ghana's food and beverage sector. Out of the 427 questionnaires distributed, 395 usable responses were obtained. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling to assess direct and specific indirect effects. Findings The results indicate that human, financial and innovation resources significantly enhance supply chain performance, whereas relational and structural resources do not exert direct effects. Power positively influences performance and serves as a critical mechanism, with both partial and full mediation observed across resource categories. The findings reveal that resource value is heterogeneous and context-dependent, and that performance gains are realised when resources are effectively translated into influence that aligns with partner behaviour. Originality/value The study advances the literature by moving beyond the composite view of firm resources and demonstrating that resource effects are not uniform but context-specific. It further positions power as a central mechanism …

title: Characteristics of suicide cases among indirect disaster-related deaths after the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant accident following the Great East Japan Earthquake
Differential effects of neutral and alkaline salt stress on wheat photosystem II photochemistry
abstract: Soil salinization poses a major threat to global crop productivity, yet the differential effects of neutral (NaCl) versus alkaline (NaHCO 3 ) salts on photosystem II (PSII) thylakoid reactions remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we systematically compared the photosynthetic responses of two wheat cultivars (Xinong 388 and Linhan 6) to equimolar concentrations (100 mM) of NaCl and NaHCO 3 stress, using both OJIP transient and PAM chlorophyll a fluorescence analyses. Specifically, we investigated the effects of these two salt types on thylakoid reactions, and explored the associated photoinhibition sensitivity and nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ)-mediated photoprotection. The results indicated NaHCO 3 stress was associated with greater reductions in shoot and root biomass than NaCl in both cultivars. This growth inhibition coincided with a pronounced impairment of PSII function. This was indicated by significant decreases in the maximum quantum yield of PSII photochemistry (Fv/Fm) and the performance index (PIabs). Energy flux analysis indicated electron transport flux per reaction center (ETo/RC) was reduced under NaHCO 3 in both cultivars. In contrast, dissipated energy flux per reaction center (DIo/RC) increased only in Linhan 6. Moreover, Linhan 6 failed to increase NPQ under stress, which exacerbated photoinhibition. title: ALKALINE-EXTRACTED SUGARCANE BAGASSE AS A PLANT-BASED COAGULANT FOR CATTLE SLAUGHTERHOUSE WASTEWATER
abstract: Effluent from the Banda Aceh municipal slaughterhouse, Indonesia, receives only bar screening, and a single grab sample exceeded the national chemical oxygen demand (COD) limit. Plant-based coagulants are proposed alternatives to metal salts; sugarcane bagasse has been studied as an adsorbent and activated-carbon precursor but, to our knowledge, not as a coagulant for slaughterhouse effluent. We screened a crude alkaline bagasse extract (2% NaOH, hotplate set to 120 °C, 2 h, open beaker) as a coagulant for cattle slaughterhouse wastewater. Three stock concentrations (0.1–0.3% w/v) were each dosed at four volumes (5–20 mL; nominal doses 5–60 mg/L) in single-run jar tests, with a settling-only control. Raw COD was 1,422 mg/L, and settling alone reduced it by 53.3%. The lowest COD (155 mg/L; 0.2% stock, 20 mg/L nominal dose) was 76.7% lower than the control and below the 200 mg/L COD limit; pH stayed within 6.5–6.8, but other regulated parameters were not measured. Over-dosing increased COD, and in one treatment (0.3% stock, 60 mg/L) it exceeded the control. Three conditions met the COD limit (0.2% stock at 20 and 30 mg/L; 0.3% stock at 15 mg/L). Because equal nominal doses from different stock concentrations gave inconsistent results and each treatment was run once, these results identify conditions for further testing rather than an optimum. Replicated jar tests with a control i…

title: PmiREN3.0: a multi-omics integrated and AI-assisted encyclopedia for plant microRNA research
abstract: Abstract MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators in gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Comprehensive research on miRNAs increasingly requires the integration of large and heterogeneous datasets, together with more efficient approaches to knowledge exploration. Here, we present PmiREN3.0, a major update of the Plant MicroRNA Encyclopedia. Compared with PmiREN2.0, species/subspecies coverage increased from 179 to 340, adding 22 orders, 51 families, and 108 genera. Using the same standardized workflow and annotation criteria as previous releases, high-confidence miRNAs were identified from 5319 small RNA sequencing (sRNA-seq) datasets, with miRNA loci increasing from 39 751 to 87 667 and miRNA families from 7838 to 18 389. Resources and tools from previous releases were extensively updated, while six new modules were added for primary transcripts, DNA methylation, RNA modifications, stress-responsive expression, metabolic pathways, and core GRNs. PmiREN3.0 also introduces miRai+, a knowledge service powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that combines a language model fine-tuned on miRNA knowledge with retrieval augmented generation. Evaluation yielded scores of 0.910 for answer relevance, 0.965 for faithfulness, and 0.906 for factual correctness. Together, PmiREN3.0 provides an expanded plant miRNA dataset and an integrated platform combining multi-omics data an…

title: Genomic and functional characterization of quorum sensing and plant growth-promoting traits in Pseudomonas sp. P77
Comparative transcriptome analysis reveals candidate genes and defence pathways associated with resistance to potato cyst nematodes in potato (Solanum tuberosum)
abstract: Globodera rostochiensis and Globodera pallida are two nematode species responsible for are potato cyst nematode (PCN) that significantly reduce potato (Solanum tuberosum) productivity worldwide. To elucidate the molecular basis of PCN resistance, we compared transcriptomic responses of the highly resistant potato breeding clone SM/11-120 with the susceptible cultivar Kufri Jyoti following simultaneous infection with both PCN species. Nematode penetration assays showed that SM/11-120 completely restricted nematode invasion up to 7 days post-inoculation (dpi), whereas Kufri Jyoti was susceptible to nematode penetration within 24 h post-inoculation (hpi) and supported juvenile development at 72 hpi and 7 dpi. RNA-sequencing (RNA-Seq) generated 18–27 million high-quality paired-end reads per library, of which 51.6–68.3% mapped uniquely to the potato reference genome. Comparative transcriptome analysis identified 724, 795, 694, and 899 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between SM/11-120 and Kufri Jyoti at 0 hpi, 24 hpi, 72 hpi, and 7 dpi, respectively. The resistant genotype exhibited enhanced expression of genes involved in immune signalling (NRC1, NBS-LRR), transcriptional regulation (WRKY, MYB), calcium signalling, pathogenesis-related proteins (PR1), hormone and defence metabolism (ACO1, geraniol 10-hydroxylase), and cell wall reinforcement (HRGP, XTH3, pectinesterase, β-exp…

title: Processing Technologies for Designing Micro- and Nano-Structured Plant-Based Dairy Alternatives: Structure–Function and Stability Relationships
Transition pathways of coal mining and coal-based power generation industries
abstract: This research investigates the strategic directions of a sunset industry sector, coal-based power. Drawing on the literature on sustainable business model innovation (SBMI), dynamic capabilities, and transition pathways, we take an exploratory approach to analyze how large coal-based businesses are developing transition pathways to reduce their environmental footprints. Analysis of secondary data on the environmental performance of 167 large companies over the period 2014–2023 is followed by an in-depth strategic analysis of five coal mining companies and five coal-based power generation companies to derive insights. The results show that leading firms in downstream businesses, specifically those involved in coal-based power generation, have identified superior transition pathways than their upstream counterparts in coal mining. We attempt to explain the phenomenon through the lens of institutional role in transition, dynamic capabilities, leveraging organizational slack, and structural limitations in pursuing SBMI. Consequently, the synthesis recommends a pragmatic approach to the fossil fuel industry for finding transition pathways. The research provides novel empirical evidence on the transition pathways of fossil fuel industries, contributes to theoretical concepts of business model innovation, and offers actionable insights for practice.

title: Quality characteristics of frozen horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus) treated with starch–glycerol coatings containing plant extracts
Entornos virtuales en la comprensión lectora de idioma inglés en estudiantes de una universidad pública en Trujillo
abstract: El objetivo de este estudio fue determinar la influencia de los entornos virtuales de aprendizaje en la comprensión lectora del idioma inglés en estudiantes del primer ciclo de la Escuela Profesional de Ciencias Matemáticas de una universidad pública de Trujillo durante el año 2024. Se realizó un estudio de enfoque cuantitativo, de tipo aplicado y diseño preexperimental con un solo grupo, utilizando mediciones antes y después de la intervención. La muestra estuvo conformada por 48 estudiantes seleccionados mediante muestreo censal. La comprensión lectora se evaluó mediante una prueba estructurada validada por juicio de expertos y con adecuada confiabilidad (α > 0,80). Los datos fueron analizados mediante estadística descriptiva e inferencial utilizando la prueba t de Student para muestras relacionadas con un nivel de significancia de 0,05. Los resultados evidenciaron que el porcentaje de estudiantes con nivel bajo de comprensión lectora disminuyó de 90 % a 0 %, mientras que el nivel alto aumentó de 0 % a 94 % después de la intervención, observándose diferencias estadísticamente significativas entre el pretest y el postest (t = 15,32; p < 0,001). Se concluye que la implementación de un programa basado en entornos virtuales de aprendizaje se asoció con una mejora significativa de la comprensión lectora del idioma inglés en los estudiantes evaluados.

title: Cladosporium BF-F promotes rice growth and yield by enhancing nutrient uptake and reshaping rhizosphere microbial communities
Extending the range of photosynthetically active radiation (PAR): the significance of far-red photons for photosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) for oxygenic photosynthesis has traditionally been defined as the 400–700 nm wavelength range. However, recent studies revisiting the Emerson enhancement effect, an early demonstration of wavelength synergy in photosynthesis, have provided compelling evidence that longer-wavelength far-red (FR; 700–750 nm) photons contribute to plant photosynthesis far more effectively than previously thought when combined with shorter-wavelength photons. Nonetheless, the reported magnitude of this contribution varies among studies, prompting ongoing debate over whether the definition of PAR should be expanded to include FR photons. In this review, we (i) synthesize recent advances in our understanding of the photosynthetic role of FR photons and the physiological mechanisms underlying their synergistic interactions with shorter-wavelength photons; (ii) critically evaluate the factors contributing to differences among studies in the estimated photosynthetic contribution of FR photons, and (iii) discuss the implications of these findings for redefining PAR and improving the measurement and modeling of photosynthesis under both sunlight and electric lighting.

title: Multifaceted alfalfa improvement through FTO overexpression facilitated by an efficient MsPep1-based transformation platform
abstract: Abstract Alfalfa (Medicago sativa) as one of the most important leguminous forages globally, plays an irreplaceable role in the development of animal husbandry and ecological conservation. However, its low genetic transformation efficiency severely constrains molecular breeding progress. In this study, the application of elicitor peptides MsPep1 significantly increased the genetic transformation efficiency of alfalfa by 1.61 times and shortened the transformation cycle by 20 days. Using this improved transformation system, we investigated FTO, an m⁶A RNA demethylase gene that regulates plant growth and stress responses. In the greenhouse, overexpression of FTO in alfalfa significantly enhanced plant height, root length, the number of lateral roots, as well as drought and salt tolerance. Under field conditions, it substantially increased fresh weight per plant by 24.98%, relative feed value (RFV) by 10% and hundred-seed weight. Through transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq), we inferred that the FTO gene promotes alfalfa growth by regulating auxin, optimizes forage quality by enhancing secondary metabolite synthesis and enhances salt-drought tolerance by activating oxidative stress pathways. FTO mediates large amounts of m6A demethylation in plant RNA, altering chromatin composition and transcriptional activation. In summary, these findings provide molecular breeding support for dev…

title: Association between sports participation and psychological capital among college students: the moderating role of active-passive sports participation patterns
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to examine the association between sports participation and psychological capital (PsyCap) among college students and to assess whether this association varies between active and passive participation patterns. Methods Questionnaire data were collected from college students. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, and regression analysis were performed using SPSS (version 26.0). The moderating role of participation pattern was assessed using Model 1 of the PROCESS macro, and separate partial correlation networks were estimated in R for the active, balanced, and passive groups to examine the conditional association between sports participation and four dimensions of PsyCap. Results Sports participation was significantly and positively associated with PsyCap. Using the active participation pattern as the reference group, the interaction term between sports participation and the passive pattern reached statistical significance ( β = −0.186, 95% CI [−0.291, −0.080]), indicating that the positive association between sports participation and PsyCap was weaker in the passive group relative to the active group. Conversely, the interaction between sports participation and the balanced pattern failed to reach statistical significance ( β = −0.062, 95% CI [−0.15, 0.026]). In the network analysis, self-efficacy exhibited the strongest…

title: Active commuting to school and physical activity participation in children and adolescents: evidence from a large cross-sectional study in Greece
abstract: Introduction Active commuting to school, such as walking or cycling, represents an accessible opportunity for children and adolescents to incorporate physical activity into their daily routines. This study examined the prevalence of active, mixed, and passive commuting to school and the demographic, behavioral, and contextual correlates of commuting mode among school-aged students in Greece. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted between early 2024 and April 2025 among school-aged students (N = 20,932) recruited from public schools in the metropolitan regions of Attica and Thessaloniki, Greece. Data were collected using structured questionnaires assessing commuting mode, organized and non-organized physical activity, perceived barriers to active commuting, and home-to-school distance. Multinomial logistic regression was used to examine the independent associations of demographic, behavioral, and contextual characteristics with commuting mode, with active commuting as the reference category. Results Among participants with valid commuting data, 68.8% were classified as active commuters. Active commuters reported higher levels of non-organized physical activity than passive commuters (p < .001). Home-to-school distance showed the strongest association with commuting mode, with the odds of mixed and passive commuting increasing progressively across distance categories. …

title: Implementation strategies for warehouse management systems in cold storage: Evidence from phased and big-bang approaches
abstract: Background: Warehouse management system (WMS) implementation in cold storage environments presents technical, organisational and human challenges that are amplified by perishability, seasonality, traceability requirements and operational disruption risks. Empirical evidence comparing implementation methodologies in this context remains limited. Objectives: This study compared phased rollout and big-bang WMS implementation methodologies in the Western Cape fruit export sector, focusing on implementation challenges, critical success factors (CSF), post-implementation benefits and long-term support and sustainability. Method: A quantitative survey was administered to 40 respondents directly involved in WMS implementation in cold storage operations in the Western Cape fruit export sector. Respondents were drawn from two companies employing different implementation methodologies: phased rollout (n = 20) and big bang (n = 20). Data were analysed using Cronbach’s alpha, independent-samples t-test, effect sizes (Cohen’s d) and principal component analysis. Results: Phased rollout respondents reported significantly stronger outcomes than big-bang respondents for all CSF and post-implementation benefits, with large effect sizes across all 16 items (Cohen’s d ≥ 0.83). The largest differences were observed for quality of vendor support (d = 2.47), data visibility improvement (d = 2.37), cu…

title: Behavioral pathways to hospitalization: physical exercise, social participation, and healthcare utilization in China
МНОГОКРИТЕРИАЛЬНАЯ МОДЕЛЬ ОПТИМИЗАЦИИ ПОВЫШЕНИЯ ЭНЕРГОЭФФЕКТИВНОСТИ И ОБЕСПЕЧЕНИЯ БЕЗОПАСНОСТИ
abstract: В исследовании разработана многокритериальная модель оптимизации промышленно-энергетических систем, объединяющая показатели энергопотребления, производственного риска и эксплуатационных затрат. Безопасность рассматривается не как фиксированное ограничение, а как самостоятельный оптимизируемый критерий наряду с энергопотреблением и эксплуатационными затратами. Функциональная структура системы формализована с использованием методологии IDEF0 и математического моделирования. Для формирования множества Парето-оптимальных решений применён алгоритм NSGA-II, итоговое решение выбирается методом нормированной взвешенной суммы. Вычислительный эксперимент на синтетических данных (10 независимых запусков) показал снижение энергопотребления на 25,2 ± 4,3% и уровня риска на 38,9 ± 9,4% по сравнению с традиционным режимом при росте эксплуатационных затрат на 8,0%. Однокритериальная оптимизация обеспечила более значительную экономию энергии, однако уровень риска приблизился к допустимому порогу. Научная новизна заключается в интеграции критериев энергоэффективности и безопасности в едином адаптивном оптимизационном контуре с обратной связью.

title: Investigation of kinetic energy of .308 projectiles of different masses
abstract: Projectile kinetic energy is a useful metric in ballistics that allows for the understanding of the magnitude of chemical potential energy that is transferred to projectiles in firearms. The purpose of this report is to investigate the effect that .308 projectile mass has on the kinetic energy of projectiles at muzzle exit of a .308 target rifle. Velocity was measured with the use of a radar chronograph, which was used to calculate the kinetic energy of the projectiles at that point in time. It was found that although velocity decreased as mass increased, kinetic energy increased as mass increased. The kinetic energy increased from approximately 3275J at 155 grains to 3962J at 220 grains. This was explained by the greater opportunity for work to be done on projectiles of greater mass due to slower volume expansion behind the projectile. This acts as a demonstration of Newton’s Second Law and variables that influence projectile behaviour in ballistics such as pressure evolution over time.

title: Towards Sustainable Cloud Infrastructure: Energy Optimization and Resource Management
abstract: Cloud computing has transformed the delivery of computing, storage and software services, but the concentration of workloads in large data centres creates a significant sustainability challenge. This paper proposes an Energy-Aware Green Cloud Computing Framework (EGCCF) that combines workload-aware virtualization, carbonsensitive resource allocation, renewable-energy preference, intelligent cooling coordination, storage optimization and responsible hardware lifecycle management. The framework extends conventional green-computing practices by treating energy, carbon intensity, service quality and hardware utilization as related decision variables rather than isolated objectives. A conceptual architecture is presented in which a Green Resource Broker receives workload requirements, estimates the energy and carbon implications of candidate resources, and selects an allocation that satisfies service constraints while reducing environmental impact. The paper also identifies practical benefits, implementation challenges and evaluation measures suitable for educational institutions, enterprises and cloud providers. The proposed framework is intended as a conceptual model for future experimental implementation and does not claim measured performance results.

title: Factores de la experiencia del cliente y comportamiento de compra del distribuidor minorista de baterías automotrices
abstract: La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo determinar la relación entre los factores de la experiencia del cliente y el comportamiento de compra del distribuidor minorista de baterías automotrices. Se realizó un estudio de enfoque cuantitativo, con diseño no experimental, alcance descriptivo-correlacional y corte transversal. La información fue recolectada mediante la técnica de la encuesta, utilizando un cuestionario aplicado a una muestra de 84 distribuidores minoristas ubicados en Piura, Lambayeque, La Libertad y Chimbote, seleccionados a partir de la base de datos de la empresa en estudio. Los resultados evidenciaron una correlación positiva baja y estadísticamente significativa entre la experiencia del cliente y el comportamiento de compra (Rho de Spearman = 0,293; p = 0,007). Asimismo, el 67,9 % de los participantes percibió un nivel bueno de experiencia del cliente, mientras que el 91,7 % presentó un nivel alto de disposición del comportamiento de compra. Se concluye que la incorporación de una cultura centrada en el cliente fortalece las relaciones comerciales, incrementa la disposición de compra de los distribuidores minoristas y contribuye a la sostenibilidad del negocio.

title: Orbital-Enabled Intrinsic Defect Healing via Charge Compensation toward Accelerated Sodium Storage in Mn-Rich Composite Phosphates
abstract: Abstract Manganese-rich composite phosphate cathodes, represented by Na4Fe1.25Mn1.75(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP), offer high energy density for sodium-ion batteries. However, their limited electrochemical durability and sluggish kinetics hinder practical application. In this work, we first identify abundant intrinsic oxygen vacancies, which are determined to be responsible for the occurrence of Mn/Na antisite defects and deteriorate electrochemical performance of NFMPP. Building on the new insight, we design a trace V-doped Mn-rich composite phosphate cathode, Na4Fe1.25Mn1.65V0.1(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP-V). Different from other dopants (Cr3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Nb5+), the unique empty eg*0 orbitals and modest charge compensation (Δz = +1) of V3+ effectively reduce the oxygen-vacancy defects in the NFMPP structure. This reduction leads to a more uniform strain distribution and a lower concentration of in situ formed Mn/Na anti-site defects, ultimately accelerating Na+ kinetics and enabling more complete utilization of the intrinsic low-voltage Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reaction. Consequently, NFMPP-V can deliver an energy density of 421.1 Wh/kg, relating to a reversible capacity of 125.7 mAh g–1 with an enhanced initial Coulombic efficiency of 97.0% (105.8 mAh g–1, 87.0% for the NFMPP), outperforming most Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes reported to date. Notably, a full pouch cell paired with a hard-carbon …

Exploring factors that influence human peer reviewers' acceptance of AI peer review as a teammate
abstract: Purpose Academic publication is one of the significant parts of higher education (HE). Given the pressures on the traditional peer-review system with the increasing number of submitted manuscripts, the rapid advancement of AI attracts interest in AI adoption in the peer review process. There is growing concern that AI has transformed the peer review process, which requires efforts to explore and establish human–AI hybrid collaboration for the peer review ecosystem. To better understand the fundamental questions about AI peer review regarding the quality and ethics of reviewers' reports for manuscript evaluation, and to further understand the human reviewers' acceptance of AI as a teammate, this paper develops a conceptual framework from the perspectives of technology acceptance and team trust for a comprehensive analysis. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a theory-building approach that integrates literature on technology acceptance and team trust. A conceptual framework is proposed, which extends physical, psychological, technological and ethical factors that reflect the characteristics of human reviewers' acceptance of AI in the peer review process. The framework also integrates the exploration of team trust in human–AI collaboration, which sheds light on how human reviewers recognize AI peer review. Findings Drawing from the unified theory of acceptance and use of…

title: From Detection to Operativity: Defeater Propagation in Hybrid AI–Human Peer Review
abstract: Hybrid AI–human review systems are evaluated through model accuracy, reviewer agreement, transparency, citation verification, and human oversight. These properties leave a further issue unresolved: whether detected evidence against an initial assessment receives appropriate treatment in the eventual decision. This paper introduces a formal framework for measuring that transition. It models review as a sequential process in which a candidate defeater must be detected, transmitted, taken up, and connected to a reasoned disposition. Defeater Propagation Adequacy (DPA) measures the weighted proportion of detected candidate defeaters receiving traceable downstream disposition; the Presence-to-Operativity Gap (POG) is its complement. Three structural results follow under stated assumptions. Downstream bottlenecks bound the benefit of improved detection. Additive scoring can dilute a severe minority objection as panel size increases. Mandatory escalation improves transmission when other transition rates remain fixed, but cannot alone secure substantive uptake. An exact parameter sweep illustrates these relations without estimating any platform’s performance. The publicly documented review architecture of the Institute for Complexity Science and Advanced Computing serves as a motivating case. Its citation checks, disagreement flags, review-quality audit, and requirement for human curat…

title: Effects of Alfvénicity on the compressible energy cascade in magnetohydrodynamic solar-wind turbulence: Evidence from Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, and WIND observations
abstract: The compressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) energy cascade in the solar wind is shaped by Alfvénicity, plasma fluctuations, and proton temperature, yet how they regulate the relative contributions of compressible and incompressible energy transfer across heliocentric distances remains poorly understood. We aim to investigate how Alfvénicity, plasma fluctuation amplitudes, and proton temperature regulate the compressible and incompressible MHD energy cascade rates in the solar wind and how the two components of the compressible cascade, the Yaglom-like term and the purely compressible term, respond to changes in plasma conditions. We applied compressible and incompressible exact relations to a large statistical sample of two-hour intervals from WIND (1 au), Parker Solar Probe (PSP; $<0.25$ au), and Solar Orbiter (SolO; 0.3--1 au), classifying intervals as Alfvénic ($|σ_c|>0.75$) or non-Alfvénic ($|σ_c|<0.25$) based on the normalized cross helicity and further separating them by solar-wind speed. The velocity-fluctuation amplitude is found to be the strongest predictor of the compressible cascade rate, łangle|ɛ_c|̊angle, among the variables examined, followed by density and magnetic-field fluctuations. łangle|ɛ_c|̊angle and łangle|ɛ_i|̊angle are tightly correlated across all regimes, with their ratio organized by Alfvénicity and wind speed---non-Alfvénic and Alfvénic fast winds cl…

title: Experimental Study of the Dynamic Response and Energy Dissipation Characteristics of Silica Sand and Sandy Soil under Multi-impact Loading
abstract: To investigate the dynamic behavior of granular materials under repeated impact loading, repeated compression tests were conducted on sandy soil and silica sand using an improved Φ40 mm split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) setup. The study systematically examined the evolution of material density, particle breakage, stress wave propagation, stress–strain response, and energy dissipation characteristics. The results indicate that the density of both materials increases gradually with the number of impacts and eventually stabilizes. The median particle size of sandy soil decreases by only approximately 25 %, whereas that of silica sand reduces by up to 65.6 %. After five impacts, the relative breakage indices of sandy soil and silica sand are 0.05 and 0.23, respectively, indicating a more pronounced particle refinement effect in silica sand. Wave velocity measurements show that both the compression wave and peak stress velocities of sandy soil are more sensitive to densification, while silica sand exhibits limited increases in wave velocity due to severe particle breakage. Regarding stress–strain behavior, both materials undergo elastic, plastic, yielding, and strain-hardening stages, with overall stress levels shifting upward as the number of impacts increases. However, due to particle breakage, silica sand exhibits greater energy dissipation, resulting in lower stress levels und…

title: Core-engineered plasmonic tuning in Au nanoshells: solar-weighted SOI and APF analysis across air, SiO₂, TiO₂, and GaP cores for solar energy applications
Bridging talent gaps for a sustainable green hydrogen ecosystem: lessons from Chile
abstract: Purpose The transition towards green hydrogen requires more than technological innovation and renewable resources; it also depends on governance mechanisms capable of developing, coordinating and sustaining the human capabilities needed for emerging industrial ecosystems. This study aims to examine the human talent governance challenges affecting the sustainable development of the green hydrogen ecosystem in Chile’s Tarapacá Region and investigates how coordinated action among government, industry, educational institutions and other regional stakeholders can strengthen human capital as a strategic enabler of the energy transition. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods research design was adopted, integrating descriptive analysis of secondary data from official reports, educational databases and labour market information with qualitative evidence obtained through intersectoral workshops, stakeholder surveys and semi-structured interviews conducted within the corporación de fomento de la producción (CORFO) project Development of the Green Hydrogen and Derivatives Ecosystem in Tarapacá (Project 24BP-272099). Methodological triangulation and stakeholder triangulation enhanced the robustness and credibility of the findings. Findings The analysis identified 18 critical human talent governance gaps, consolidated into six interrelated governance domains: training and certificatio…

title: The evolution of legitimacy discourse in corporate social responsibility reporting: evidence from a state-owned Irish energy company (2003-2025)
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how legitimacy is discursively constructed and stabilised over time in corporate social responsibility (CSR) reporting in a state-owned enterprise (SOE) and what these legitimacy dynamics reveal about how an SOE responds to evolving sustainable-development expectations. Design/methodology/approach The CSR sections of the Electricity Supply Board’s annual reports from 2003 to 2025 are analysed using a theory-informed computerised content analysis based on Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count categories mapped to Suchman’s (1995) legitimacy framework. To assess the mapping’s interpretive validity, the authors incorporate several robustness analyses. Findings Over the 23-year period studied, the reports increasingly and consistently used language that conveyed a sense of the ESB as a natural, accepted part of everyday life. While the report language reflected pragmatic and moral legitimacy, cognitive legitimacy was prominent. This prominence is observed across multiple analytical approaches, suggesting a stable discursive orientation. This finding suggests that in SOE contexts, legitimacy depends less on actively persuading stakeholders and more on being perceived as taken-for-granted in society. Sustainable-development transitions occur through organisations whose historically embedded societal roles can both support continuity and require continui…

title: Mechano-electrochemical energy harvesting and self-powered sensing via dynamic liquid metal–electrolyte interfaces
abstract: Wearable devices, stretchable sensors, and soft electronics benefit from harvesting ambient energy using compliant materials, yet existing approaches often face limitations in power density, scalability, and electrode adaptability. Here, we report a liquid metal mechano-electrochemical energy harvester (LMMEEH) that converts mechanical stimuli into electricity through dynamically regulated electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Mechanical motion changes the interfacial area and drives asymmetric Faradaic reactions associated with dynamic oxide formation and dissolution, generating electrical output. The fluidity, high surface tension, and self-renewing surface chemistry of liquid metals enable rapid interfacial reformation, large reversible deformation, and stable cyclic operation. The device achieves a power density of 140.2 microwatts per square meter and scales to a 40-unit array producing 2 volts. Spatial and temporal programming of the liquid metal interfaces further enables synchronized three-phase alternating-current generation. We demonstrate wave-driven emergency lighting, self-powered pressure sensing, and real-time physiological monitoring. This work establishes dynamic liquid metal electrochemical interfaces as a scalable strategy for soft mechanical energy harvesting and self-powered electronics.

title: Operation and maintenance capabilities for effective energy efficiency interventions in Klang Valley office buildings
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how operation and maintenance (O&M) capabilities influence the effectiveness of energy efficiency (EE) interventions in office buildings of Klang Valley. It moves beyond treating O&M as a set of isolated maintenance activities by examining the technical, monitoring, organisational and manpower conditions required to sustain EE outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design was adopted using semi-structured interviews with ten facilities management professionals involved in managing office buildings in Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Putrajaya. The interview data were analysed using thematic analysis and compared with the literature to refine the themes and develop a conceptual framework. Findings The findings indicate that inspection-based and time-based maintenance remain dominant, while condition-based, predictive and occupancy-responsive practices are less widely adopted. EE outcomes were stronger where O&M practices were supported by energy monitoring, management commitment, staff capability and sustainability-oriented culture. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to Klang Valley office buildings and interview-based qualitative evidence. The proposed O&M capability framework should be tested through wider quantitative and longitudinal studies using building-level energy data. Originality/value The study contributes…

How STARA-enabled technological readiness shapes intrapreneurial behaviour and digital competence in China's electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing sector
abstract: Purpose This study examines how employees' perceptions of STARA (smart technologies, artificial intelligence, robotics, and algorithms) influence their intrapreneurial behaviour (IB) and digital competence (DC), and how digital dynamism (DD) conditions this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Sociotechnical Systems Theory, and the Antecedents–Decisions–Outcome framework, the study develops an integrated model explaining how employees' perceptions of STARA shape behavioural responses and digital capability development. Data were collected from full-time employees in China's electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing sector, a context characterized by extensive use of STARA technologies, using an online survey and stratified purposive sampling, resulting in 193 valid responses. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was applied to test the proposed model. Findings The results show that positive perceptions of STARA are associated with higher levels of IB and DC. IB serves as a key mechanism through which perceived STARA relates to DC. This highlights the role of employee behaviour in capability development. DD weakens the positive relationship between perceived STARA and DC, suggesting that high environmental turbulence may constrain employees' ability to translate perceived technological opportunities into DC. title: Invention of a new device to optimise air quality for vehicle occupants in Sydney’s tunnels: the Car Canary
abstract: Traffic-related air pollutants (TRAP) present a risk to vehicle occupants (VO) when driving in tunnels. Recirculating vehicle cabin air (RVCA) is the current recommended strategy to protect motorists from TRAP exposure. TRAP and carbon dioxide (CO2) concentrations were hypothesised to be higher in tunnels, with RVCA reducing TRAP but increasing exposure to CO2. Air quality testing in tunnels confirmed the presence of TRAP and that CO2 accumulates in a passenger vehicle when two VO use RVCA. The measured levels of CO2 indicate poor ventilation and a build up of re-breathed air, which may increase the risk of transmission of airborne viruses when an infectious person is present, along with fatigue or drowsiness that may be relevant to driving behaviour. Three scenarios were tested using different combinations of RVCA and window use. Testing indicated a trade-off: particulate matter 2.5 μm or less in diameter (PM2.5) exposure was highest with windows open and lowest with windows closed and RVCA enabled, while CO2 exposure was highest when RVCA was enabled. Driving with windows closed and RVCA disabled reduced CO2 exposure but slightly increased PM2.5 exposure. To help manage this tradeoff, a prototype device known as the Car Canary was developed to alert VO when PM2.5 reaches a set point, indicating when to enable RVCA. These preliminary findings from the WestConnex M4–M8 tunnel s…

Modulating Sulfur Composition toward Ultralow Dielectric Loss Polymers: A Miscible Blending Strategy with Poly(phenylene oxide)/Poly(phenylene sulfide) Alternating Copolymers
abstract: Abstract In recent high-speed communications (i.e., 5G and 6G), insulating polymers exhibiting both a minimized dielectric constant (Dk) and dissipation factor (Df) have been extensively used to reduce dielectric loss, although the empirical Dk–Df trade-off relationship has prevented further reductions in these values. Here, we describe a rational approach for the simultaneous reduction of both Dk and Df through simple polymer blending, wherein a low-Dk ether polymer is hybridized with a low-Df sulfide polymer. Specifically, upon mixing poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene sulfide) (PMPS) or poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) (PPO) with their alternating copolymer, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms of the resulting polymer blends revealed their miscibility, as verified by shifting of glass-transition temperatures, allowing for the successful film preparation and the tuning of their dielectric properties without compromising other material properties (e.g., thermostability). In particular, the observed enhancement in free fractional volume for the polymer blends suggests a reduction in Dk, finally minimizing dielectric loss (Dk = 2.43, Df = 0.00081 at 10 GHz). Specifically, those dielectric losses are significantly lower than the empirical limits defined for single-component polymers. title: AHP-Based Prioritisation of Development Strategies for Semi-Intensive Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) Farming in a Mining-Affected Area, Central Halmahera Regency
abstract: Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) farming is a growing livelihood in Central Halmahera Regency, where nickel mining raises fish demand but may also threaten shared water resources. Choosing among development strategies requires weighing economic, technical, environmental, and institutional considerations, yet such multi-criteria priorities have rarely been quantified for mining-affected smallholder farms. This study aimed to prioritise development strategies for semi-intensive tilapia farming and to test how robust the ranking is to changes in criteria weights. From January to April 2026, 40 purposively selected farmers in the Weda Tengah and Weda Selatan sub-districts and ten experts were surveyed. Eighteen strategy alternatives, derived from a strengths–weaknesses–opportunities–threats analysis reported elsewhere, were grouped into four operational strategies and ranked with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) under four criteria. Production improvement ranked first under every criterion and overall (global weight 0.532), followed by institutional strengthening (0.231), water-quality management (0.160), and production cost efficiency (0.077); consistency ratios were below 0.10. In recalculated weight scenarios, production improvement stayed first, and the second rank changed only when the environmental criterion exceeded about 66% of the total weight. Simulating 80% survi…

title: Dedicated Transient Operating Strategy for Hydrogen Engines
The AI-ification paradox: the challenge of AI delegation in healthcare
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces the AI-ification paradox and explains why organizations that invest in increasingly autonomous AI often keep it in advisory rather than delegated roles. We examine the paradox in healthcare services, where the promise of AI is high but autonomy is tightly bound. Design/methodology/approach The article develops a conceptual model by integrating servitization and task-delegation literature with an illustrative synthesis of 11 interviews from healthcare settings, supplemented by two subsequent expert interviews used for model refinement. Findings AI is most readily delegated to reversible, auditable tasks such as documentation, information retrieval, drafting and second-opinion support. Delegation stalls when verification remains costly, tasks require socio-emotional alignment or professional judgment, and organizational risk, liability, and workflow integration are unresolved. The result is a gap between AI capability and delegated authority that can trap value and weaken return on AI investment. Resources and costs also shape the scope and value of delegation. Originality/value The paper extends research on digital servitization by identifying delegation, rather than technical capability alone, as the next bottleneck in AI-enabled service delivery. It offers a managerial framework for governed autonomy in services.

title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation
abstract: Abstract The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this dire…

title: Do corporate governance and strategy matter in corporate goodness decisions?
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how governance mechanisms and corporate strategy jointly influence corporate goodness in an emerging market characterized by concentrated ownership and mandatory corporate social responsibility regulations. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel of 397 listed firms from an emerging market (India) between 2010 and 2023, this study analyzes the impact of governance mechanisms (ownership, boards and management) and strategic investments on corporate goodness, specifically evaluating the complex interactions among these internal governance structures. Findings Advancing the governance-environment, social and governance (ESG) literature on principal-principal conflicts, the authors find promoter-dominated ownership negatively influences corporate goodness. However, strong board and management governance actively drives corporate goodness, interactively offsetting these negative ownership impacts. Furthermore, aligning with compliance-cost perspectives, corporate goodness acts primarily as a regulatory burden without complementary strategic investments. Practical implications This study reframes corporate goodness as a strategic resource, dynamically shaped by the interactions among internal governance mechanisms rather than mere regulatory compliance. It demonstrates that the interdependent relationship among ownership, boards and management ser…
venue: Corporate Governance: The International Journal of Business in Society

title: Efecto de estrategia didáctica en el nivel de desarrollo de habilidades investigativas en estudiantes de educación secundaria
abstract: El objetivo del estudio fue determinar el efecto de una estrategia didáctica centrada en la indagación en el desarrollo de habilidades investigativas en estudiantes de educación secundaria de una institución educativa del distrito de Laredo. Se adoptó un enfoque cuantitativo aplicado con diseño preexperimental de un solo grupo (pretest–postest). La muestra estuvo conformada por 120 estudiantes. Se utilizó un cuestionario tipo test de 10 ítems, interpretado mediante una rúbrica de evaluación; la consistencia interna fue adecuada (α = 0,794). Los resultados del pretest mostraron 15,8% en nivel alto, 40,8% en nivel medio y 43,3% en nivel bajo. En el postest, el nivel alto aumentó a 43,3%, el nivel medio se ubicó en 23,3% y el nivel bajo disminuyó a 33,3%. La prueba de Kolmogorov–Smirnov evidenció no normalidad (p < 0,001), por lo que se aplicó Wilcoxon, encontrándose diferencias significativas (Z = −9,515; p < 0,001) con tamaño del efecto grande (r ≈ 0,87). Se concluye que la estrategia didáctica influyó de manera significativa y relevante en el desarrollo de habilidades investigativas.

title: The AI throwaway economy: when organizations stop revising and start replacing
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces the AI Throwaway Economy, a framework explaining when a still-usable knowledge-based output becomes economically disposable because generating a replacement is expected to cost less than refining what already exists. It also considers what may be lost when replacement becomes the default. Design/methodology/approach The article develops a conceptual framework through an integrative synthesis of research on generative AI, automation and augmentation, knowledge management, and the knowledge-based view of the firm. Findings Generative AI can reverse the economics of preservation when the total cost of regeneration falls below the total cost of refinement at comparable quality and risk levels. Both options may use AI. Regeneration is most attractive for codified, standardized, context-light, and readily verifiable outputs. Preservation remains advantageous when outputs embody tacit knowledge, proprietary context, institutional memory, or high integration and error costs. Repeated replacement may also weaken organizational learning. Practical implications Leaders should compare full lifecycle costs, classify outputs by preservation value, retain provenance and decision context, and invest in verification. They should also ask: What will our people stop learning or practicing if we routinely replace rather than refine their work? Originality/value This f…

title: Enhancement of a Closed-loop Recycling by Converting Rejected Coal Fly Ash into Coagulants for Desulfurization Wastewater Treatment in a Coal-Fired Power Plant
Do US apparel retailers absorb or pass through tariff costs? Evidence from US apparel import and retail prices, 2015–2025
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how changes in US apparel import tariff rates were transmitted through the apparel import-to-retail pricing chain, focusing on their effects on import prices, retail prices and the timing of these adjustments. Design/methodology/approach A reduced-form vector autoregression model was estimated using monthly US apparel data from January 2015 to December 2025. Findings Tariff shocks had only a limited influence on US apparel import prices, with import prices remaining largely driven by their own dynamics. Meanwhile, although US apparel retail prices exhibited a moderate positive response to tariff shocks after a lag of approximately two months, this effect was temporary and relatively small. Taken together, the findings suggest that US apparel retailers and their supply-chain partners absorbed a substantial share of additional tariff costs rather than fully passing them on to consumers in the short to medium term. Originality/value This study provides some of the first apparel-specific empirical evidence on how tariff shocks were transmitted through the US apparel import-to-retail pricing chain covering the latest wave of US tariff increases, extending existing research that has focused primarily on macroeconomic effects of tariffs.
venue: Research Journal of Textile and Apparel

title: Behavioral overtrading, bot filtering and retail performance in centralized cryptocurrency markets: transaction-level evidence from anonymized exchange data
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how investor overconfidence shapes trading behavior and realized performance in cryptocurrency markets. Specifically, it examines whether overconfident trading leads to systematic return penalties, and whether these effects intensify under high-volatility conditions and for less experienced investors. Design/methodology/approach Using 77 million transaction records from 405,000 investors across four major cryptocurrency exchanges over 2014–2024, this paper proxies overconfidence by trading frequency and portfolio concentration (HHI). To strengthen causal interpretation, it exploits quasi-exogenous variation in trading frictions – exchange outages and fee-tier resets – as instruments for trading intensity, supplemented by extensive robustness checks and alternative concentration measures distinguishing benchmark (BTC/ETH) holdings from altcoin-dominant portfolios. Findings Both overconfidence proxies are robustly associated with significantly lower realized and risk-adjusted returns, indicating economically meaningful welfare losses for retail investors. The penalty is strongly state-dependent, becoming substantially larger during high-volatility regimes and among novice traders. Instrumental-variable results confirm that intensified trading causally contributes to performance deterioration rather than merely reflecting unobserved investor heterog…

title: The Effect Of Liquidity And Profitability On Financial Distress In Retail Companies Listed On The IDX 2015 – 2024 Period
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of liquidity and profitability on financial distress in retail companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2015–2024 period. This study employed a quantitative method with an associative approach. The sampling technique used purposive sampling with secondary data in the form of financial reports, resulting in a sample of 10 retail companies. Data analysis was performed using panel data regression with the help of EViews 13, and hypothesis testing was performed using F-tests and t-tests at a significance level of 0.05 or 5%. The results indicate that liquidity and profitability simultaneously have a significant effect on financial distress. Partially, liquidity has no effect on financial distress, while profitability has a effect. Therefore, optimal corporate financial management is essential to maintain financial stability.

title: Omnichannel integration in fashion retail: privacy barriers to customer retention
abstract: Purpose Focusing on fashion retail, this study investigates how customer-perceived channel integration (CPCI) influences privacy concerns (PC) and customer retention (CR), specifically testing whether PC mediates the link between integration and retention. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the “Stimulus–Organism–Response” model and privacy calculus theory, this study explores omnichannel retail consumer behaviour (ORCB). Data were collected via in-person surveys from 600 Generation Y customers in Ankara. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling was employed to examine the direct and indirect pathways within the model. Findings The results indicate that retail CPCI is positively associated with CR and negatively associated with PC. PC partially mediates the CPCI–CR relationship, indicating that integrated omnichannel experiences relate to retention both directly and indirectly through lower privacy-related anxieties. Research limitations/implications Generalisability is bounded by the focus on a single metropolitan area. Future research should incorporate diverse demographic cohorts and cross-cultural settings to extend these findings. Practical implications Fashion retailers should transition towards “privacy-by-design” frameworks. By implementing transparent consent mechanisms and consistent service delivery, retailers can alleviate PC and strengthen long-term …
venue: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management: An International Journal

title: Tax is a Double-Edged Sword: Transfer Pricing Opens the Door to Tax Avoidance, Moderated by CEO and Foreign Ownership
abstract: Background: Transfer pricing remains a persistent tax-governance concern because related-party arrangements may shift taxable income across jurisdictions, while governance and ownership characteristics can alter executives’ incentives to pursue aggressive tax positions. Objective: The study investigates the relationship between transfer pricing and tax avoidance and evaluates whether CEO narcissism, CEO financial expertise, and foreign ownership change the strength of that relationship among Indonesian energy-sector companies. Methods: The research used a quantitative explanatory approach with 70 firm-year observations obtained through purposive sampling. Secondary financial and corporate-governance information was processed using PLS-SEM in WarpPLS 8.0, and an alternative proxy for tax avoidance was applied as a robustness assessment. Results: Transfer pricing was significantly associated with tax avoidance (β = −0.381; p < 0.001). CEO narcissism (β = −0.186; p = 0.018) and foreign ownership (β = −0.332; p < 0.001) significantly moderated this relationship, whereas the robustness model indicated that the strength of selected effects depends on the tax-avoidance proxy. Conclusion: The findings show that the transfer-pricing–tax-avoidance relationship is contingent on executive and ownership characteristics, supporting the need for risk-based monitoring that jointly considers re…

title: Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections
abstract: Abstract Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections Re and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers’choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of Re and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate Re in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health perspective. In contrast, deep…

title: AI in Clinical Research: Understanding Statistics and Machine Learning
Self-efficacy, engagement, attitudes, and perceived learning in AI-assisted STEM education
abstract: Introduction The rapid advancement of AI technologies is reshaping educational practices, offering new ways to support learning activities. This study examines the interrelationships among self-efficacy, engagement, attitudes, behavioral intentions, and perceived learning in secondary STEM education. Methods The study was based on real-world classroom teaching involving 710 students, who engaged with an AI learning companion that provided personalized guidance and support during STEM laboratory courses. Using a single-group, post-test-only design and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), the study examined concurrent associations among students' self-reported perceptions. Results Attitude had the largest estimated direct association with perceived learning (β = .306), followed by engagement ( β = .275), intention ( β = .176), and self-efficacy ( β = .119). Discussion Among students who used the AI learning companion, higher reported engagement was associated with higher perceived learning. These findings describe concurrent associations and do not establish that changes in learning are attributable to the AI learning companion.

title: A hybrid approach using lattice Boltzmann and machine learning for predicting the transient dynamics of slug flow in non-Newtonian fluids
abstract: Slug flow is a prevalent and crucial flow regime in many industrial applications, such as petroleum and chemical processing, where accurate modeling and prediction are essential for optimizing system performance and ensuring operational stability. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of two-phase slug flow (Newtonian and non-Newtonian) in a horizontal channel using the Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM). A color-gradient model is employed to capture slug formation, and a non-Newtonian power-law model is used to represent the shear-thickening behavior of one of the fluids. The simulations explore the influence of key parameters, including the flow index (n) and inlet velocities, on slug formation, propagation and pressure drop. Results show that increasing the power-law index (n) — indicating higher shear-thickening behavior — significantly modifies the velocity profile, reduces apparent viscosity near the wall, and leads to a positive pressure drop compared with Newtonian cases. Additionally, this study introduces a hybrid machine learning approach combining Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for predicting transient slug flow behavior. The POD method reduces the high-dimensional LBM data by capturing the dominant flow dynamics, while LSTM predicts the temporal evolution of these modes with minimal error. The POD[…
venue: International Journal of Modern Physics C

title: Penerapan Model Experiential Learning Berbantuan Praktik Hastakarya Untuk Meningkatkan Keterampilan Menulis Teks Prosedur Siswa Kelas V Sekolah Dasar
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menggambarkan pelaksanaan pembelajaran menulis teks prosedur dengan model experiential learning berbantuan praktik hastakarya, keterampilan menulis teks prosedur setelah pembelajaran serta faktor pendukung dan penghambat pelaksanaannya. Penelitian ini dilaksanakan di SD Muhammadiyah Plus Kota Probolinggo dengan melibatkan 17 siswa kelas V. penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dalam bentuk refleksi pembelajaran, data diperoleh melalui catatan refleksi, pengamatan dan dokumentasi LKPD, hasil karya dan nilai siswa. Data kemudian di analisis melalui kondensasi data, penyajian data dan penarikan kesimpulan dengan triangulasi sumber dan teknik. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian dan uraian tersebut dapat disimpulkan pelaksanaan pembelajaran menulis teks prosedur dengan model experiential learning berbantuan praktik hastakrya pada siswa kelas V berlangsung melalui 4 tahap : Siswa membuat hastakarya dirumah sebagai pengalaman konkret, mencatat peoses secara berurutaan sebagai bentuk pengamatan, kemudian menyusun teks prosedur pada LKPD sesuai struktur yang telah ditetapkan. Selain itu dari 17 siswa, 15 siswa menunjukkan pemahaman yang baik terhadap struktur teks prosedur dengan tulisan yang lengkap dan runtut. Terdapat faktor pendukung salah satunya dari antusiasmen siswa, konsep tugas yang dekat dengan kehidupan sehari-hari, hastakarya sebagai…

title: Globalising higher education in Africa through artificial intelligence: student acceptance of ChatGPT in an open distance and e-learning context
abstract: Introduction Higher education is increasingly globalised through digital technologies, Open Distance Learning, e-Learning, and emerging generative AI. In the absence of research examining the acceptance and use of ChatGPT by students in an Open Distance and e-Learning higher education setting, this study evaluated a UTAUT2 model comprising seven standard predictors and Personal Innovativeness, as well as moderating variables age, gender, work status, and year of study. Methods Data collected from 294 students at the largest distance education institution in Africa were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Results Four relationships with Behavioural Intention were significant, with Habit emerging as the strongest predictor, followed by Facilitating Conditions, Personal Innovativeness, and Performance Expectancy. Effort Expectancy was found to be negatively associated with Behavioural Intention. Social Influence and Hedonic Motivation were not significantly associated with Behavioural Intention. For Use Behaviour, Habit was once again the strongest predictor, followed by Facilitating Conditions, with Behavioural Intention negatively associated. Neither Social Influence nor Hedonic Motivation returned a significant relationship with Behavioural Intention. The interaction between Year and Hedonic Motivation was the only significant moderator of Behavi…
authors: Thomas Mc Donald van der Merwe

title: Federated learning for IoMT-enabled predictive healthcare and remote patient monitoring: a systematic review
