title: Effects of Saturated Steam Softening on Radial Gradient-Dependent Hygrothermal Deformation and Compressive Response of Bamboo
abstract: Bamboo’s inherent radial gradient gives rise to heterogeneous hygrothermal deformation and mechanical responses, yet the effects of saturated steam softening across the radial thickness of the bamboo culm remain unclear. Eight radial layers of untreated bamboo (UB) and hygrothermally softened bamboo (HSB) were subjected to tests of anatomical structure, water absorption, hygrothermal deformation, and longitudinal and transverse compression in this study. The fraction of the vascular bundle area decreased from 67.67% in the outer layer to 10.08% in the inner layer, and water uptake in UB increased from 19.80% to 77.55%. Softening increased water absorption by 4.30–18.21 per hundred. Tangential and radial swelling coefficients generally decreased inwards, whereas dimensional swelling strains showed different radial trends, and the tangential-to-radial swelling ratio dropped from 1.70 to 0.62 in UB and from 1.46 to 0.59 in HSB; thus, the main direction of swelling had shifted. The most prominent adjacent-layer swelling mismatch occurred at L2–L3, and after softening, the radial mismatch increased by 52.40%. The largest dimensional swelling differences occurred between L1 and L2. Temperature-dependent deformation also varied with direction and radial position. Effects of sustainable packaging cues on perceived sustainability, purchase intention and price acceptance of cosmetic products
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractSustainable cosmetic packaging is increasingly important as consumers use packaging-related cues to evaluate the environmental attributes and value of products. However, empirical evidence on consumer responses to different sustainable packaging configurations and communication cues remains limited in Central and Eastern Europe. This study examines perceived environmental sustainability, purchase intention and price acceptance across cosmetic packaging configurations featuring conventional plastic, biodegradable plastic and glass, as well as consumer evaluations of Vegan and Cruelty-Free labels and QR-code cues. A quantitative within-subject study was conducted among 204 adult Slovak consumers using an online questionnaire with nine visual stimuli. Data were analyzed using the Friedman test, Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient. Significant differences were identified across packaging configurations in perceived sustainability (χ²(2) = 8.21, p = 0.016), purchase intention (χ²(2) = 16.09, p &lt; 0.001) and price acceptance at the premium price level (χ²(2) = 28.48, p &lt; 0.001). Perceived sustainability was strongly and positively associated with purchase intention (ρ = 0.686, p &lt; 0.001). title: Call Option Price using Pearson Diffusion Processes
abstract: This study introduces a framework for pricing European call options using Pearson diffusion processes with linear drift and quadratic squared diffusion. This class of diffusion processes follows Pearson type IV distribution as its invariant distribution which can effectively capture skewness and excess kurtosis, key empirical features of financial returns. We verify the Novikov condition for risk-neutral measure, and establish the existence of a unique strong solution of stock prices under this measure. We apply the method to Nifty 50 index options and find encouraging results compared to the Black-Scholes and Heston models.

title: Measurements of longitudinal flow decorrelations in p p and Xe + Xe collisions with the ATLAS detector
abstract: Measurements of longitudinal flow decorrelations in 13-TeV p p and 5.44-TeV Xe + Xe collisions with the ATLAS detector are presented. The measurements are performed using the two-particle correlation method, combining charged-particle tracks within | η | < 2.5 with either calorimeter energy clusters or towers within 4.0 < | η | < 4.9 . A template-based subtraction procedure is used to remove nonflow effects in both the p p and the Xe + Xe analyses. The dependence of the longitudinal flow decorrelations on the pseudorapidity separation between the particles is characterized via the slope parameter F n for the elliptic ( n = 2 ) and triangular ( n = 3 ) harmonic moments. The results are reported as a function of charged-particle multiplicity for the p p and Xe + Xe collision systems. Comparing the data to a color string-based model of the initial geometry indicates that in p p and peripheral Xe + Xe collisions, subnucleonic structure, and fluctuations in longitudinal energy deposition are needed to describe the data.

title: A lag-informed deep learning framework for real-time downstream water-level forecasting and flood decision support in the Kalu Ganga Basin, Sri Lanka
abstract: Floods are among the most damaging hazards in Sri Lanka's wet-zone river basins, where short warning lead times constrain preparedness and physically based hydrodynamic models are often impractical under limited data. This study develops a lag-informed deep-learning framework for 10-h-ahead downstream water-level forecasting in the flood-prone Kalu Ganga Basin, Sri Lanka. Flood-wave travel times between Rathnapura, Ellagawa, Millakanda, and the downstream target station Putupaula were estimated from hourly records covering 2021–2024 using event-based peak matching, rising-limb timing, and cross-correlation. Selected travel times were 18 h for Rathnapura–Ellagawa, 23 h for Ellagawa–Putupaula, and 24 h for Millakanda–Putupaula. These lags were used to align upstream water-level inputs, while rainfall remained in its original chronological order. No-lag and lag-informed Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Bi-LSTM models were evaluated using chronological training, validation, and independent testing. Lag-informed inputs reduced Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) from 0.317 to 0.288 m for LSTM and from 0.339 to 0.286 m for GRU, while Bi-LSTM performance decreased. The lag-informed GRU also outperformed persistence and ARIMA baselines. title: Pricing and Coordination of a Dual-Channel Supply Chain Considering Price Reference Effect and Return Service
abstract: With the development of dual-channel supply chains, consumers have more purchasing options, and reference price effects have become increasingly important in shaping their purchasing decisions. To attract consumers, some suppliers and retailers need to adjust their pricing strategies and provide measures such as return services to gain more profits. To address these problems, considering that the reference price effect and return service level are important factors affecting the supply chain, we construct game-theoretic models for a manufacturer-dominated dual-channel supply chain comprising one manufacturer and one retailer, use them to examine the optimal decisions, and analyze the effects of the reference price effect and return service level on the supply chain. Then, a two-part pricing contract is developed. The results show that, within the feasible parameter region, a higher return service level improves the total supply chain profit. In the parameter regions examined, a stronger reference price effect increases the manufacturer’s online channel demand and revenue, whereas the retailer’s offline channel demand and revenue tend to decrease when the return service level is relatively low. Furthermore, the manufacturer’s profit increases, while the retailer’s profit may decline at relatively low return service levels. A sufficiently high return service level can mitigate th…

title: Multiscale Quantum-Enhanced Forecasting Framework for Photovoltaic Power Output and Electric Load
abstract: Accurate day-ahead forecasting of photovoltaic (PV) power and electric load is essential for reliable power system operation under growing renewable penetration and demand complexity. Both series, however, are strongly nonstationary, with multiscale dynamics driven by external factors. This study develops a multiscale quantum-enhanced forecasting framework integrating rolling variational mode decomposition (VMD), feature attention (FA), and bidirectional quantum temporal modeling. Rolling VMD separates slower trends from rapid fluctuations, FA weights weather and calendar inputs, and the bidirectional quantum module encodes nonlinear dependencies within the observed history to represent irradiance-driven PV variability and temperature- and calendar-related load dynamics. Historical context is combined with the corresponding previous-day target for direct day-ahead forecasting. Using the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC) photovoltaic dataset and the GEFCom2014 load dataset, the seasonal reference comparisons cover four seven-day intervals per task. Across the 672 hourly evaluation points per task, the five-run mean RMSE and R2 are 2.0299 kW and 0.9618 for PV and 7.5385 MW and 0.9633 for load. PV evaluation includes nighttime zeroing based on observed irradiance. Ablation results confirm the complementary contributions of the three modules, supporting a unified appr…

title: Bridging Climate Resilience and Travel Demand Forecasting: State-of-Practice Review
abstract: Statewide travel demand models (TDMs) are essential tools for long-range transportation planning, policy evaluation, and infrastructure investment. As climate-related disruptions such as floods, wildfires, and extreme heat events become more frequent, there is growing interest in integrating climate resilience into these models. However, little is known about how this integration is currently being pursued in practice. This study investigates the state-of-practice in incorporating climate and hazard considerations into statewide TDMs. It draws on a nationwide survey of transportation agencies, targeted interviews with selected practitioners, a thematic analysis of agency approaches, and an evaluation of 47 publicly available climate and hazard data resources and analytical tools. Together, these methods offer a comprehensive understanding of current implementation efforts, technical and institutional barriers, and emerging opportunities for more resilient travel modeling. The findings indicate that while many agencies are conducting hazard assessments and scenario planning, few have operationalized this work within TDMs. Data compatibility, institutional fragmentation, and lack of standardized workflows remain major challenges. Liquidity Contagion and Price Discovery: Evidence from Cryptocurrency Markets
abstract: Do exchanges that transmit liquidity shocks also lead price discovery? We examine this question across fragmented cryptocurrency markets using high-frequency limit order book and transaction data. Liquidity contagion is measured through a directed network of lower tail dependence in limit order book depth. We find that stronger liquidity contagion is associated with weaker price discovery after accounting for exchange heterogeneity and common market conditions. The evidence is strongest for contemporaneous specifications and persists under alternative definitions of liquidity contagion, price construction and sampling frequency. Information share provides the most consistent evidence across these alternative measurement choices. The estimates attenuate when sparse systems are excluded, particularly in the most demanding and predictive specifications. The findings suggest that liquidity shock transmission and information leadership capture distinct dimensions of market importance: exchanges that play a central role in propagating adverse liquidity conditions tend to contribute less to permanent price formation.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FETAL MEDICINE: APPLICATIONS IN DIAGNOSIS AND GESTATIONAL RISK PREDICTION
abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence into obstetric care has expanded the possibilities for image processing, pattern recognition, and integrated analysis of clinical information, with particularly relevant applications in fetal medicine. Machine learning and deep learning algorithms have been investigated for automating ultrasonographic measurements, identifying anatomical structures, detecting fetal anomalies, and estimating the risk of gestational complications. In this context, the ability to analyze large volumes of data and identify complex relationships may complement traditional methods of maternal-fetal assessment and contribute to greater precision and earlier stratification of risk. This review aimed to analyze the main applications of artificial intelligence in fetal medicine, with emphasis on image-based diagnosis and the prediction of adverse gestational outcomes. This is a narrative literature review, guided by a structured question based on the PICo strategy and directed at studies on artificial intelligence, machine learning, fetal ultrasound, and predictive models applied to pregnancy. The evidence points to applications in the automated identification of ultrasonographic planes, fetal biometry, assessment of anatomical structures, and recognition of cardiac and other organ abnormalities, in addition to the development of models to estimate the risk of…

An Interval Type‐3 Fuzzy Elman Neural Network Model for Chaotic Time‐Series Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Chaotic time series prediction plays a crucial role in various fields, including economics, meteorology, and nonlinear control. However, the strong nonlinearity and high sensitivity to initial conditions make this problem difficult. In this study, we propose a new predictive model based on an Elman neural network combined with interval Type‐3 fuzzy Elman neural network (IT3FENN). The IT3FENN structure is designed to leverage the dynamic state memory capability of the Elman network while enhancing its ability to handle uncertainty and noise through the membership function mechanism of interval Type‐3 fuzzy logic. An adaptive learning algorithm optimizes the system parameters to ensure fast convergence and low forecast errors. Simulation results on benchmark chaotic time‐series datasets as well as a real‐world traffic dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the T1FLS‐ENN and IT2FLS‐ENN models in terms of forecasting accuracy and noise robustness. The results demonstrate the potential application of IT3FENN in complex nonlinear forecasting problems.

title: Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for TT-POCUS Based Prognostic Prediction of Did-Not-Finish and First-Treatment Failure Cattle Diagnosed with Bovine Respiratory Disease
abstract: Bovine respiratory disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in feedyard cattle and is associated with substantial economic and animal welfare consequences. Prognostic tools remain limited, but combining objective diagnostic measures with predictive modeling may improve clinical decision-making. This study evaluated the performance of machine learning models incorporating targeted thoracic point-of-care ultrasound (TT-POCUS)-derived variables to predict did-not-finish (DNF) and first-treatment failure (FTF) outcomes in feedyard cattle diagnosed with bovine respiratory disease (BRD). First-treatment cattle were evaluated for both FTF and DNF outcomes, whereas chronic cattle were evaluated for DNF outcomes following enrollment. A prospective cohort observational study was conducted in cattle receiving either first treatment or chronic treatment for BRD. TT-POCUS examinations were performed at enrollment to assess pulmonary abnormalities, including lung consolidation, pleural irregularities, B-lines, and lesion scores. A total of 1422 first-treatment cattle and 150 chronic cattle were enrolled. Six supervised machine learning algorithms were trained using TT-POCUS variables and demographic data. For FTF prediction, logistic regression demonstrated the highest AUC (0.71). For first-treatment DNF, logistic regression again achieved the highest AUC (0.80). In chron…

title: Multi-physics coupled simulation of a 110 kV three-phase gas-insulated switchgear busbar and its temperature-rise prediction based on machine learning
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to investigate the temperature distribution of a 110 kV three-phase gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) busbar by multi-physics coupled numerical simulation. This study analyses the influences of different factors on the temperature field of the busbar. The study aims to provide an efficient formula to predict the temperature rise of the contact area based on the numerical results through machine learning. The findings can be used for the over-temperature warning of the hot spot in the GIS busbar equipment. Design/methodology/approach A multi-physics coupled numerical simulation is performed in the ANSYS software, which aims to study the effects of different factors, such as the contact resistance, solar radiation and ambient temperature, on the temperature field of the busbar. Based on the data set from the simulation, an empirical formula is fitted to quickly predict the contact temperature. In addition, the Random Forest (RF) algorithm is used for the training of the obtained temperature data set, which is used for the over-temperature prediction. Findings The results reveal that the temperature of the contact area is mainly affected by the contact resistance, while the temperature of the GIS enclosure is more sensitive to the solar radiation and the ambient temperature. The fitted empirical formula can quickly predict the contact temperature,…

title: CONCEPTUAL MODEL FOR GENDER PREDICTION BASED ON USER INPUT
abstract: The present study examines an approach to the synthesis of a conceptual model for gender prediction based on user input. The predictive capability of the model is grounded in statistical differences observed within specific datasets and in the applicability of a machine-learning classification model. The predictive analysis is governed by a set of parameters, including language, the specifications of the peripheral input device, sample size, and biological indicators. It should be noted that reliable classification of a user's gender is a function of predefined key indicators.

title: From language awareness to critical multilingual language awareness: Chilean pre-service EFL teachers’ knowledge for diverse contexts
abstract: Abstract It has become imperative for English language teacher education (ELTE) programmes to prepare pre-service teachers (PSTs) for the pedagogical and sociopolitical complexities of multilingual classrooms in linguistically and culturally diverse contexts such as Chile. This study explores critical multilingual language awareness (CMLA) as a framework for addressing language ideologies, power dynamics, and the sociopolitical dimensions of English language teaching. Through in-depth semi-structured interviews, data were collected from eight PSTs at different Chilean universities. The study examined their perceptions of the role and status of English in Chile, the knowledge they consider necessary for teaching in culturally and linguistically diverse contexts, and the changes to ELTE curricula they envisage. Analysis revealed that while all eight participants valued language awareness and knowledge about language, some also questioned the strong ‘linguistics’ orientation of their preparation and called for greater attention to Anglocentric ideologies of power and to cultural and linguistic diversity, views partly consistent with principles of CMLA. These findings suggest considerations for ELTE and directions for further research on how programmes might support PSTs’ CMLA.

title: ЯКІСТЬ ДОГОСПІТАЛЬНОЇ МЕДИЧНОЇ ДОПОМОГИ ПАЦІЄНТАМ ІЗ ГОСТРИМ ІНФАРКТОМ МІОКАРДА В ЗАКАРПАТСЬКІЙ ОБЛАСТІ: РЕЗУЛЬТАТИ ОПИТУВАННЯ ПРАЦІВНИКІВ ЕКСТРЕНОЇ МЕДИЧНОЇ ДОПОМОГИ
abstract: Purpose: to determine the opinions of EMS personnel in the Zakarpattia region regarding the quality of prehospital medical care provided to patients with AMI. Materials and Methods. A sociological survey was conducted among 297 EMS workers. Primary data were analyzed using a systematic analysis method. The results are presented as relative indicators. Statistical analyses were performed using RStudio 2025.05 and LibreOffice Calc version 7.6.4.1. Results. The study identified both strengths and shortcomings in the provision of prehospital medical care for patients with AMI provided by EMS teams in the Zakarpattia region. Among the main strengths, EMS teams demonstrated a high level of availability of medical equipment, medications, consumables, and vehicles, with more than 90 % of respondents rating these resources as sufficient or high. Most respondents (73.06 ± 2.57 %) reported arriving within the standard response time to emergency calls. Furthermore, 80–100 % of EMS personnel highly rated their capacity to perform key diagnostic and therapeutic interventions, including establishing venous access, monitoring oxygen saturation, blood pressure, and ECG, providing oxygen therapy, pharmacological blood pressure control, and conducting telemedicine consultations during the prehospital care of patients with AMI. The main shortcomings included delays in reaching patients due to poor…

title: E-Service quality and customer satisfaction in online shopping: Implications for sustainable digital commerce
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified competition among online retailers, making e-service quality increasingly important for building customer trust, satisfaction, and sustainable customer–platform relationships. This study examines the relationships among e-service quality, customer trust, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty using a second-order Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework. The five SERVQUAL dimensions such as empathy, responsiveness, reliability, assurance, and tangibles were modeled as first-order constructs reflecting the higher-order construct of service quality. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 402 respondents with prior online-shopping experience. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and SEM were employed to assess the measurement and structural models. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and overall model fit. The structural results showed that service quality significantly and positively influenced customer trust and customer satisfaction, while customer trust significantly enhanced satisfaction. Trust also partially mediated the relationship between service quality and satisfaction, indicating that e-service quality improves satisfaction both directly and through increased customer confidence. title: Multi-domain contracting of the non-physician primary care workforce and per-domain service output: a nationwide cross-sectional analysis of Polish National Health Fund data, 2022–2023
abstract: Abstract Background Combining community nursing, midwifery, and school medicine within a single provider organisation is widely advocated as a route to more comprehensive primary care, yet whether multi-domain provision is accompanied by differences in per-domain service output remains untested at population scale. Economic theories predict opposing effects: economies of scope favour joint provision, while specialisation may yield higher per-unit throughput. Methods A nationwide cross-sectional analysis was performed using administrative data of the Polish National Health Fund (NFZ) covering all contracts for community nursing (N), midwifery (M), and school medicine (S) in 2022 and 2023. The unit of observation was the unique provider-year ( n = 16,574; 8,302 in 2022 and 8,272 in 2023) from 8,511 providers across all 16 NFZ regional branches. Providers were classified into seven mutually exclusive service-domain combinations. Two primary outcomes were specified ex ante: nurse services per 1,000 nurse declarations and midwife services per 1,000 midwife declarations. Adjusted associations were estimated by negative binomial regression (NB2, dispersion estimated by maximum likelihood) with log(declarations) as offset, fixed effects for regional branch and year, mono-domain providers as reference categories, and standard errors clustered at the provider level. title: Stroke disability burden and rehabilitation service-capacity proxies in China, 1990–2023: A population-based analysis using GBD 2023 and national service statistics
abstract: China’s stroke burden is increasingly shaped by survival with disability, population ageing, and demand for rehabilitation and long-term support. Yet the extent to which stroke disability burden has shifted towards older-old and oldest-old adults, and how this burden relates to community and elder-care service capacity, remains insufficiently quantified. We conducted a population-based secondary analysis of Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for China from 1990 to 2023, focusing on ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage. We examined disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), YLD share of DALYs, age-specific patterns among adults aged 50 years or older, estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs), and three-factor decomposition of absolute DALY changes. We also linked 2023 stroke YLDs with national community health and elder-care service indicators as descriptive capacity proxies. From 1990 to 2023, the YLD share of DALYs increased from 10.5% to 22.3% for ischaemic stroke and from 1.8% to 3.3% for intracerebral haemorrhage. The crude all-age ischaemic stroke YLD rate increased by 2.75% per year (95% CI 2.68 to 2.82), while the crude all-age intracerebral haemorrhage DALY rate declined but its YLD rate and YLD share increased. Crude all-age rates were interpreted as population-level burden indicators influenced by population age…

title: Profile der Alltagsbegleitung
abstract: Zusammenfassung Hintergrund Die Mehrheit der Pflegebedürftigen (PB) in Deutschland wird ambulant gepflegt. Niedrigschwellige Leistungen zur Unterstützung der PB und deren pflegenden Angehörigen können als Angebote zur Unterstützung im Alltag (AUA) über Leistungen nach dem Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB) XI finanziert werden. Alltagsbegleitung (AB) ist eine Form der AUA, die sozialer Isolation entgegenwirken und die Selbständigkeit von PB erhalten soll. Bislang fehlen empirische Befunde zu den Merkmalen der Personen, die Alltagsbegleitung erbringen, sowie zu deren Tätigkeiten. Ziel Explorative Beschreibung der AB sowie der im Rahmen der Alltagsbegleitung erfolgten Aktivitäten. Methodik Online-Befragung von 165 in Bayern tätigen AB sowie semistrukturierte Interviews mit neun AB. Ergebnisse Die meisten Teilnehmenden der Online-Befragung (TN) waren weiblich, zwischen 40 und 65 Jahre alt und gaben an, Alltagsbegleitung als ehrenamtliche Tätigkeit auszuüben. Rund ein Drittel war oder ist in einem Gesundheits- oder sozialen Beruf tätig. Die AB betreuen überwiegend ältere PB ab 65 Jahren mit psychischen Einschränkungen. Psychosoziale und aktivierende Aktivitäten wurden am häufigsten berichtet. Daneben wurden auch hauswirtschaftliche Aktivitäten umgesetzt. Diskussion Das Spektrum der in der Alltagsbegleitung erbrachten Aktivitäten zeigt das Potenzial, Mobilität, geistige Fähigkeiten und psychoso…

title: Structural insights into West Nile virus programmed ribosomal frameshifting reveal coordinated regulation by RNA, ribosome, and nascent peptide
abstract: ABSTRACT Programmed −1 ribosomal frameshifting (−1 PRF) is essential for West Nile virus (WNV) gene expression and generates NS1′, a protein implicated in viral replication and pathogenesis. However, the structural pathway by which translating ribosomes traverse the WNV frameshift signal remains poorly understood. Here, we combined cryo-electron microscopy, RNA structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and functional analyses to investigate the mechanism of WNV −1 PRF. We resolved a pre-frameshift ribosomal complex together with four translocation intermediates, including a previously uncharacterized semi-rotated state in which the 40S subunit undergoes partial rotation while tRNAs remain in near-canonical A/A–P/P configurations. This intermediate is accompanied by remodeling of conserved peptidyl-transferase-center nucleotides, suggesting that active-site rearrangements can precede canonical tRNA movement during translocation. Structural modeling and simulations further suggest that the WNV frameshift-stimulatory RNA exists as a compact but conformationally heterogeneous ensemble capable of adopting multiple stable or metastable pseudoknot architectures. In addition, we identified direct interactions between the nascent viral peptide and the ribosomal exit tunnel, and disruption of the tunnel-occupying peptide reduced frameshifting efficiency. Together, our findings…

title: Leukocyte Regulation by Exercise and Complementary Lifestyle Factors in Cardiovascular Health
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of death worldwide, underscoring the need for effective preventive and therapeutic strategies. Chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation contribute to CVD development, with leukocytes linking systemic immune responses to vascular and myocardial injury. Regular exercise is a cornerstone of non-pharmacological cardiovascular prevention and exerts immunomodulatory effects beyond conventional risk-factor control by regulating leukocyte production, trafficking, immunometabolism, and effector functions. Diet, sleep, circadian rhythms, and psychological stress also influence leukocyte-mediated immune regulation through interconnected metabolic, neuroendocrine, and microbiota-related pathways. This review integrates mechanistic evidence on how these lifestyle factors shape leukocyte-mediated immunity in cardiovascular health and disease. Acute exercise induces transient catecholamine-mediated leukocyte mobilization and redistribution, with responses generally increasing with exercise intensity and duration, whereas regular training may produce more sustained changes in hematopoiesis, immunometabolism, and inflammatory function. These adaptations are influenced by cumulative training load and recovery, with experimental studies implicating adipose-derived leptin signaling and myeloid metabolic reprogramming as potential mechani…

title: Metadata for Metacognition: Supporting Self-Regulation Capabilities in Soar
abstract: Metacognition, the ability to represent, monitor, and modulate cognitive processing, is realized in the Soar cognitive architecture through the interaction of metadata and standard architecture mechanisms for reasoning, now applied to reasoning (metareasoning). To explore enabling the wider range of self-regulatory metacognitive capabilities reported in humans, we examine what metadata is required and the current support (or lack thereof) in Soar for this metadata. We propose an approach where metadata is produced by appraisal processes that evaluate agent state in the context of current tasking. We present an initial investigation, where we implement a limited set of appraisals that signal agent progress (or lack thereof) in a troubleshooting domain, facilitating agent strategy change when it is unable to make progress.

title: Optically Controlled Hybrid Metasurface for Efficient Terahertz Frequency Modulation
abstract: Abstract Terahertz waves exhibit considerable application value in fields such as high-speed wireless communication, nondestructive testing, and biomedical imaging owing to their broadband transmission and low photon energy characteristics. However, existing hybrid metasurfaces integrated with active materials suffer from the inherent electromagnetic response of the structure and limited reconfigurability, making broadband frequency modulation difficult to achieve. To address these challenges, this work proposes a terahertz metasurface frequency modulation device based on a composite structure of double-opening square split-rings and metal patches, and systematically investigates how the geometric parameters and the incidence angle govern the resonance characteristics. Numerical simulations show that adjusting the structural parameters and incidence angle can produce significant resonant frequency shifts and enable flexible modulation of the number and distribution of resonant peaks. On this basis, two germanium-based optically controlled hybrid metasurface schemes are further proposed. By embedding germanium in the key structural regions, dynamic frequency regulation is numerically demonstrated under optical pumping, with a maximum tuning range of 0.8 THz, exhibiting excellent dynamic modulation performance. The proposed metasurface combines the advantages of static regulation…

title: University Students’ Perceptions of Artificial Intelligence Regulation in Business Decision-Making
abstract: This study aims to examine university students’ perceptions of artificial intelligence (AI) regulation in business decision-making, focusing on the roles of perceived risks, trust, transparency, legal liability, and the effectiveness of regulatory measures in shaping acceptance of AI-based decisions. Understanding these perceptions is crucial, as students represent the next generation of professionals, managers, and policymakers who will interact with AI in organisational and societal contexts. A structured questionnaire was administered to 304 students across multiple faculties, capturing data on perceived AI risks, trust, transparency and audit practices, legal liability, regulatory effectiveness, and AI acceptance in business. The study applied PLS-SEM to assess the measurement and structural models, supported by exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and normality tests. Results indicate that transparency and audit practices significantly enhance trust, while perceived liability and regulatory effectiveness demonstrate stronger relationships with AI acceptance. Although trust represents an important theoretical dimension of AI governance, its direct effect on acceptance was not statistically significant in this study. Perceived risks negatively affect adoption, whereas the perceived effectiveness of legal and regulatory measures indirectly reduces risk perceptions, thereby foste…

title: Hierarchical cross-temporal frequency network for remote sensing building change detection
abstract: Building change detection (BCD) using remote sensing images has become a crucial technique for urban planning. Although deep learning-based methods for BCD have made significant progress in the field of remote sensing imagery, they still encounter several challenges, including unclear detection of boundaries of buildings, susceptibility to noise interference, and missed detection of subtle changes. To address these issues, we propose a hierarchical cross-temporal frequency network (HCTFNet) to achieve more precise and refined building change detection. Specifically, we design a frequency-channel enhancement model, which incorporates a frequency-guided spatial attention block to capture different frequency components of input features, thereby enabling more accurate extraction of textural details and building edges, and a residual channel attention block to assign weights to features from a channel-wise perspective, which suppresses invalid channel features and enhances the model’s capability to detect change regions. We further introduce a cross-attention fusion block to establish spatial correlations between the two temporal phases, strengthen the representation of change regions, and fuse the features to highlight areas with the most significant changes. Experimental results show that HCTFNet achieves F1-scores of 92.10% on the LEVIR-CD dataset, 89.58% on the WHU-CD dataset, …

Two-stage robust optimization for formulating regulation curves of smart building clusters considering multiple regulation characteristics
abstract: Accurate formulation of smart building regulation curves is essential for exploiting building-side flexibility and supporting supply–demand interaction in new power systems. However, existing methods often insufficiently consider the multiple regulation characteristics of adjustable loads, scenario-specific response requirements, and response-capability uncertainty, resulting in underused response potential and poor curve executability. This paper proposes a two-stage robust formulation method for smart building cluster regulation curves. First, five response characteristics, including response capacity, maximum response duration, minimum response interval, maximum response count, and response speed, are represented by a unified characteristic matrix to describe heterogeneous smart buildings. Second, response-demand characteristic matrices of typical scenarios are extracted from historical data, and response periods and weights are embedded into resource aggregation to obtain scenario-oriented cluster response-capability curves. Finally, a two-stage robust optimization model for regulation curves considering response-capability uncertainty is proposed. The first stage determines cluster regulation curves and response states, while the second stage adjusts individual building response quantities under different realizations of response capability. title: Protocolo Hints na emergência: frequência de uso na síndrome vestibular aguda
abstract: Introdução: A síndrome vestibular aguda é um desafio diagnóstico comum em emergências, e o protocolo HINTS é uma ferramenta importante para diferenciar causas centrais e periféricas, porém, sua aplicação ainda é limitada na prática clínica. Objetivo: Avaliar a frequência de aplicação do protocolo HINTS em pacientes com síndrome vestibular aguda na emergência, comparando a realização entre equipes de clínica médica e otorrinolaringologia. Metodologia: Estudo observacional, analítico, longitudinal e retrospectivo realizado em hospital terciário em São Paulo, com pacientes acometidos por síndrome vestibular aguda atendidos entre 2021 e 2025. Foram coletados dados clínicos, demográficos, aplicação do protocolo (Head Impulse, Nystagmus e Skew Test) e exames complementares. Análises estatísticas incluíram testes exatos de Fisher, qui-quadrado e coeficiente Kappa de Cohen. Resultados: O protocolo acima foi aplicado em 98,6% dos casos pela otorrinolaringologia e em 30,4% pela clínica médica, com diferença estatisticamente significativa (p<0,05). A análise dos componentes individuais (nistagmo espontâneo, semi-espontâneo, teste do impulso cefálico e desalinhamento vertical) evidenciou maior realização por parte da otorrinolaringologia, especialmente dos testes mais técnicos, como o Head Impulse Test e o teste do desalinhamento vertical (Skew Test). Conclusão: O protocolo HINTS ainda é s…

title: Effectiveness of Occupational Therapy in Enhancing Emotional Regulation and Therapeutic Alliance Among Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) is a therapeutic approach designed to enhance individuals’ independence, functional abilities, and participation in meaningful daily activities, including self-care, education, play, and leisure. It may play an important role in supporting children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) by addressing challenges related to emotional regulation, adaptive functioning, and social participation. However, further investigation is needed to understand its effects on selected psychological variables among children with ASD. The present study aims to examine the impact of occupational therapy interventions on expressive suppression, cognitive appraisal, and therapeutic alliance among children with ASD. A pre-test–post-test research design was employed to assess changes in these variables following occupational therapy sessions. The collected data were analysed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and mean-rank comparisons to evaluate differences between pre-intervention and post-intervention scores. The findings revealed statistically significant post-intervention improvements across all the variables examined. These results suggest that occupational therapy may have a beneficial role in supporting selected emotional and therapeutic outcomes among children with ASD. The study highlights the importance of further research into the psychological dimensions of occupat…

Axial compressive behavior and capacity reduction of circular CFST stub columns with internal discrete voids
abstract: Abstract To investigate the influence of internal discrete voids on the axial compressive behavior of circular concrete‐filled steel tubular (CFST) stub columns, 24 specimens were tested under axial compression. Regularly distributed spherical voids were introduced using thin‐walled hollow stainless steel spheres. The effects of nominal void volume ratio χ , tube wall thickness t , and column height L on failure mode, axial capacity, secant stiffness at 0.4 N u , and steel‐tube strain response were examined. Internal voids promoted local buckling near the hollow spheres and between adjacent voids, accompanied by localized crushing and circumferential cracking of the core concrete. Increasing χ generally reduced axial capacity and secant stiffness at 0.4 N u , whereas increasing t improved structural resistance and delayed local deformation. For the tested specimen dimensions and nominal void‐ratio range ( χ = 0%–12%), a linear capacity reduction factor kr = 1 − 0.0221 χ was established based on the normalized capacity ratio and combined with the GB 50936‐2014 reference capacity. The full‐dataset calibration and leave‐one‐out cross‐validation gave MAPEs of 4.45% and 4.66%, respectively.

title: Nurses' Coping Capacity for Nursing Interruptions During Medication Administration in Clinical Nursing Practice: A Concept Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Nursing interruptions during medication administration (NIMA) occur frequently, often leading to medication errors and workflow delays that threaten patient safety. While previous studies primarily focused on preventive interventions, many interruptions remain unavoidable in dynamic clinical environments. Nurses' active capacity to cope with these unavoidable events is critical, yet it lacks a clear conceptual definition. Aim To develop a conceptual definition of nurses' coping capacity for NIMA. Methods Walker and Avant's eight‐step approach to concept analysis was used to identify the defining attributes, antecedents, consequences and empirical referents of nurses' coping capacity for NIMA. Eight databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and SinoMed, were searched from inception to May 2026. Ultimately, 46 publications met the inclusion criteria. Results Five defining attributes were identified: anticipatory preparation, cognitive appraisal, emotion regulation, strategy selection and task recovery. Coping capacity for NIMA was defined as a dynamic professional ability to prepare for and appraise interruptions, regulate emotions, select responses and safely resume medication tasks. Antecedents included work environment, organizational support, medication‐task characteristics, interruption‐event characteris…

Human Resource Management and Teacher Work Capacity in Kazakhstani Schools
abstract: This study examines how school-level human resource management (HRM) practices shape teachers’ work capacity in Kazakhstan. Based on 10 semi-structured interviews with teachers, deputy heads and school directors, it explores how workload, material resources, staffing, professional development, performance evaluation, leadership support and teacher voice affect teachers’ daily work. The findings suggest that teachers’ ability to work effectively depends not only on their qualifications and professional commitment but also on organisational conditions at the school level. Large classes, limited classroom space and unequal access to technical resources increase job demands and constrain opportunities to provide individualised feedback. By contrast, mentoring, developmental appraisal, collegial exchange, professional development and supportive leadership serve as important job resources. Drawing on the Job Demands–Resources framework, the study illustrates how these demands and resources are experienced by teachers and school leaders. It offers practical recommendations for school management in Kazakhstan.

title: Breaking the Capacity‐Reversibility Linear Trade‐Off in Li–O 2 Batteries via Amorphous Non‐Precious High‐Entropy Alloy Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries suffer from sluggish reaction kinetics and rely on precious metal‐based catalysts to facilitate the reaction process. Despite being effective, these costly catalysts would inevitably introduce a critical trade‐off between capacity and reversibility, compromising the high energy density advantage of Li–O 2 batteries. In this study, we have designed an amorphous non‐precious MnFeCoNiCu high‐entropy alloy (A‐HEA) catalyst via a mild liquid‐phase reduction strategy to break the above inherent linear trade‐off. The amorphous and porous structure of A‐HEA could provide a large electrochemical active surface area, diluting the local current density to promote the solution‐mediated discharge pathway. This enables the growth of large‐sized Li 2 O 2 to deliver a discharge capacity reaching 10.8 mAh cm −2 . Additionally, the multielemental synergistic electron redistribution of A‐HEA optimizes the d ‐band center to strengthen the LiO 2 adsorption and weaken the O─O bonding, reducing the overpotential to 0.75 V and extending the battery lifetime by 4−5 times compared to the crystalline counterparts. Importantly, the A‐HEA can be produced at a scale of over 100 g and works well in Li–O 2 pouch cells with a rate capability up to 400 mA and an energy density of 754 Wh kg −1 (560 Wh kg −1 even at −30°C).

title: Optimizing open space capacity under heritage constraints in the ancient city of Suzhou: a multi-scale recursive approach
abstract: Abstract Optimizing open spaces in historic urban areas presents a unique challenge: balancing macro-level planning objectives with the preservation of irreplaceable heritage. This study introduces a multi-scale recursive optimization framework that integrates assessment, prediction, and configuration to address these conflicts. Using the ancient city of Suzhou, China (a UNESCO World Heritage site), as a case study, we applied the framework at city, community, and plot scales. Comprehensive assessment identified critical challenges, including insufficient per capita open space, uneven spatial distribution, and pronounced quality–quantity mismatches. Recursive optimization refined initial macro-level capacity targets, derived from national standards, by incorporating micro-scale heritage constraints. A potential–constraint model quantified regeneration potential, while spatial-cultural rules, such as water proximity, directed capacity allocations along river corridors. The proposed framework achieves synergy between capacity enhancement and historic character preservation. By shifting spatial governance from static blueprinting to dynamic, multi-scale optimization, our findings provide transferable methodologies and actionable strategies to support sustainable regeneration in heritage cities facing conservation–development conflicts.

title: From legal mandate to operational capacity: evaluating river basin committees under Thailand's water resources act
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical summary of the study context, mixed-methods evaluation, four RBC performance dimensions, and key finding that D3 scored highest and D4 lowest. Often, river basin committees are established to coordinate water governance across administrative, sectoral, and stakeholder boundaries. However, their legal creation does not necessarily ensure effective implementation. This study evaluated the performance of Thailand's 22 River Basin Committees (RBCs) under the Water Resources Act B.E. 2561 (2018), focusing on their operation during the 2022–2024 implementation period. A mixed-methods institutional evaluation was conducted in 2025, combining documentary analysis, meeting observation, semi-structured interviews, and questionnaire surveys. Thirteen statutory-duty indicators, reviewed through expert consultation, were grouped into four dimensions: planning alignment, basin management, legal and regulatory execution, and innovation, public awareness, and support for Water User Organizations (WUOs). Based on the results, there was moderate overall performance, with a mean score of 3.29 out of 5.00. Legal and regulatory execution recorded the highest score (4.33), while innovation, public awareness, and WUO support recorded the lowest score (2.05). The findings showed that Thailand's RBCs have established an important procedural foundation for basin-level water governance…

title: Creative adaptation or ceremonial compliance? Senior leadership agency and institutional capacity building under hybrid governance
Acid-Treated Cotton Linter-Derived Mesoporous Activated Carbon for Textile Dye Removal: Effect of Hydrothermal Temperature on Pore Structure and Adsorption Mechanism
abstract: Activated carbons were prepared from acid-treated cotton linter waste, an industrial by-product, by hydrothermal carbonization at 160 and 200 °C for 12 h, followed by phosphoric acid activation and pyrolysis at 500 °C under nitrogen. The two carbons were tested against three dyes of different molecular size: Reactive Black 5, Basic Red 2, and Methyl Violet. The sample carbonized at 160 °C had the higher surface area (about 1156 m2 g-1), yet the more mesoporous sample carbonized at 200 °C (about 93% mesopores) removed the bulky Reactive Black 5 far more effectively (99.8% against 85.5%). Pore accessibility therefore mattered more than surface area for the large dye. All three dyes were removed by at least 97.6% within 90 min. Basic Red 2 and Methyl Violet followed the Freundlich isotherm, while Reactive Black 5 was taken up completely at every concentration tested. A moderate rise in carbonization temperature is thus a simple way to build mesopore-rich carbons for polishing dilute textile effluents.

title: Mechanism of Delayed Polarization Saturation Induced by B‐Site Zr Doping for Enhancing Energy Storage Performance in Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 ‐ Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 TiO 3 Ceramics
abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, Zr 4+ ions are introduced into the B‐site of 0.67Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 ‐0.33Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 TiO 3 relaxor ferroelectric ceramics, leading to a significant improvement in energy storage performance. On one hand, Zr 4+ doping suppresses grain growth, increasing the breakdown electric field from 250 to 470 kV cm −1 . On the other hand, it tailors the phase structure by reducing the fraction of the strong polar rhombohedral phase, refines polar nanoregions (PNRs) into discrete micro‐nano polar clusters with reduced size and weakened cooperative switching, and notably alters their morphology and distribution, thereby reducing the local polarization intensity. These micro‐nano polar clusters exhibit reduced switching cooperativity under an electric field, resulting in a marked delay of polarization saturation—the electric field required to achieve a comparable polarization value is increased. Finally, the recoverable energy storage density ( W rec ) and efficiency ( η ) of the 0.67Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 Ti 0.94 Zr 0.06 O 3 ‐0.33Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 Ti 0.94 Zr 0.06 O 3 samples are significantly improved, reaching 7.2 J cm −3 and 88.1% under 470 kV cm −1 . It also exhibits stable performance from 30–160°C, with the fluctuation of W rec lower than 5%. Moreover, it possesses a high power density of 140 MW cm −3 and an ultrafast discharge time. The proposed “delayed polarization satura…

title: Constraint Mechanism Design for Fast Dielectric Elastomer Actuator-Driven Capsule Robots
abstract: Dielectric elastomer actuator (DEA)-driven capsule robots convert periodic excitations into net translation through passive constraints, yet a systematic study on optimal constraint design remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we present a comparative numerical study of six passive constraint families that range from linear and bistable springs to limit stops and polynomial shapes and encompass 2447 configurations under a reference condition. The best configuration of each family spans more than an order of magnitude in speed, from 2.62 mm/s (linear spring) to 33.86 mm/s (asymmetric bistable). We find that the sign of the constraint-force derivative at the rest position separates every family with negative rest-position stiffness from every family with positive stiffness, whereas the second derivative (curvature) shows no correlation with speed. Building on this observation, we formulate a library-based inverse-design framework that treats velocity as a specification and minimizes the peak driving force. The comparisons reported here are made under one reference condition, and the ranking is therefore a property of the library as sampled rather than a general design rule. For example, relaxing the target velocity from 25 mm/s to 23 mm/s reduces the peak force from 0.31 N to 0.19 N. These results move passive-constraint design from empirical trial-and-error toward a r…

title: Investigation of the physical mechanism of wall hollowing based on laser acoustic-vibration non-destructive testing
abstract: Abstract Existing laser vibrometry-based inspection techniques primarily focus on defect localization and vibration visualization, whereas the quantitative determination of internal defect geometry remains challenging. This study develops a physics-based nondestructive evaluation framework by integrating acoustic excitation, scanning laser Doppler vibrometry, and a mechanical impedance model. Three geometric parameters are considered: defect area, overlying-layer thickness, and cavity thickness. The proposed method identifies the equivalent stiffness, mass, and damping of defect regions from measured vibration responses and investigates their relationships with defect geometry, with quantitative inversion primarily focused on defect area. Systematic experiments were conducted on gypsum and C35 concrete specimens containing prefabricated internal cavities with different geometric configurations. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves quantitative inversion of defect area, with mean absolute relative errors of 8.62% for eight gypsum specimens and 7.66% for five selected concrete specimens. The effects of overlying-layer thickness and cavity thickness on resonance behavior were also investigated through theoretical analysis, experiments, and three-dimensional finite element simulations. Compared with conventional SLDV-based defect imaging approaches that main…

Engineering a Porous CoMn2O4/PANI Conductive Nanohybrid for High-Performance Oxygen Evolution: From Rational Architecture to Electrocatalytic Mechanism
abstract: Efficient, durable, and low-cost electrocatalysts for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction (OER) are essential for the improvement of Alkaline Water Electrolysis and sustainable hydrogen production. In this work, a conductive CoMn2O4/polyaniline (CoMn2O4/PANI) nanohybrid was successfully synthesized via a simple hydrothermal method to overcome the drawbacks of low conductivity and nanoparticle aggregation of pristine CoMn2O4. The successful incorporation of the crystalline spinel CoMn2O4 nanoparticles into the conductive PANI matrix was confirmed by structural and physicochemical characterization using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), resulting in a porous, interconnected architecture with uniformly distributed catalytic active sites. The synergistic coupling between CoMn2O4 and PANI greatly improved electrical conductivity, active-site accessibility, electrolyte penetration, and charge-transfer kinetics. It was found that the CoMn2O4/PANI nanohybrid had a low overpotential, 373 mV at 10 mA cm−2, a small Tafel slope, 57 mV dec−1, a remarkably low charge-transfer resistance, 0.12 Ω, and a sevenfold increase in electrochemically active surface area, 350 cm2, compared with pristine CoMn2O4. In addition, the nanohybrid also proved to be extremely durable for operatio…

title: Graded-twist TPMS metamaterial with twist-locking mechanism and non-monotonic stiffness
Is Oxidative Stress a Shared Mechanism Linking Autism Regression, Late Diagnosis, and Sex-Disparate Diagnostic Timing?
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) research has largely treated early regression, late decline after a period of stability, gradual increases in symptom severity, late diagnosis, and the sex difference in diagnostic timing as separate topics. These phenomena differ in definition, evidence, and plausible mechanism, and diagnostic and recognition processes may explain much of the late-diagnosis and sex-timing findings. This narrative, hypothesis-generating review asks whether a cumulative oxidative and inflammatory burden, arising from environmental chemical exposure, infection and autoimmune activity, and chronic psychosocial stress, and modified by genetic susceptibility, one-carbon metabolism, the gut microbiome, and individual buffering capacity, could contribute to some of these trajectories. We grade the evidence for each link in four tiers (human ASD data, other human data, experimental models, and our hypotheses). Most links rest on associations with ASD risk or on experimental data; no study has linked these exposures to regression or late diagnosis, and oxidative stress may be a consequence or correlate rather than a cause. We therefore define operational terms, derive predictions that could refute the model, and outline the prospective, sex-stratified evidence needed to test it.

title: Investigation of Dynamic Failure Mechanism and Microscopic Rupture Mechanism of Shale Rock Using Dynamic Three‐Point Bending Test
abstract: ABSTRACT Shale gas extraction relies on understanding reservoir rock fracture. Focusing on Longmaxi shale, this study conducted dynamic three‐point bending tests using a split Hopkinson pressure bar, combined with digital image correlation (DIC) and scanning electron microscopy, to investigate the effect of bedding angle ( α ) on dynamic fracture characteristics. Results show significant anisotropy in failure modes, fracture toughness, energy dissipation, and crack propagation velocity (CPV). Except for the C0 group (Divider) exhibiting pure tensile failure, all other angles display tensile–shear composite failure. Fracture toughness and energy first decrease, then increase, and finally decrease with rising α , whereas CPV shows an opposite trend. DIC reveals stress concentration at the notch tip and captures secondary shear crack propagation at α = 30°. Microscopically, all fractures are mixed transgranular and intergranular; as α increases, the dominant mode shifts from transgranular to intergranular fracture. These findings support hydraulic fracturing design in shale gas reservoirs.

title: Temporal Dynamics of Soil Organic Carbon Contents in Long‐Term Monitored Arable Sites in Lower Saxony, Germany
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Temporal changes in soil organic carbon (SOC) contents in agricultural soils are variable, and underlying drivers are not sufficiently understood. Aim The objectives were to describe the long‐term dynamics of SOC contents at 41 sites in Lower Saxony, Germany, and to analyze the relationships between estimated long‐term changes of SOC contents and climate, soil, and agricultural management data. Methods Mixed‐effects regression models with observation weights were calculated for each site to estimate long‐term SOC changes (ΔSOC), and the long‐term ΔSOC values were then described using climate, soil, and agricultural management variables. Results The fitted regression lines for the temporal trajectories of SOC dynamics fell within the 95% confidence intervals of the annual mean SOC values in 96% of the observations, consistent with the expected coverage under a well‐fitting model. Multiple linear regression modeling for the estimated long‐term ΔSOC values explained the estimated ΔSOC variation satisfactorily (coefficient of determination R 2 = 0.77) and identified four variables with significant contributions: the initial SOC content with a negative regression coefficient and the initial pH, initial proportion of years with catch crops, and the clay content with positive regression coefficients. Conclusions The results suggest that initial soil properties (SOC…

title: Molecular Conductance Orbital Origins of Anti-resonance Peaks in Six-Carbon Polyene Molecular Junctions
abstract: Abstract In single-molecule electronics, electron transport through a molecular junction is governed by quantum effects owing to the molecular dimensions being comparable to the electron de Broglie wavelength. In this study, we systematically investigate the quantum transport properties of a polyene containing six carbon atoms with different bond orders and connection sites using molecular conductance orbitals (MCOs) within the Hückel model in the wide-band approximation. The transmission spectra exhibit anti-resonance peaks characteristic of destructive quantum interference (DQI), which remain largely unaffected by the bond order within the nearest-neighbor approximation. Under specific configurations, however, bond order affects the number and location of the anti-resonance peaks. The interaction between the two closest conducting orbitals frequently dominates the DQI. In particular, when the molecule is connected through the central two carbon atoms, the nearest-neighbor and second-nearest-neighbor conducting orbitals have the most significant effects on DQI away from the Fermi level. Furthermore, for certain connected sites, none of the conductive orbitals can be ignored. The dominant conductive mechanism is elucidated using MCO phases, MCO-electrode coupling strengths, MCO energy-level alignments, quantum interference maps, and projected transmissions. These findings advan…

title: Investigating a Two-Dimensional Carbon Cost Control Method Based on “Carbon Flow–Value Flow”
abstract: Achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality requires coordinated action across macro, meso, and micro levels. For Chinese firms, reducing carbon emissions and controlling carbon costs are important challenges. Using Nanjing Iron and Steel Co., Ltd. (NJ Steel) as a case, this study proposes a two-dimensional “carbon flow–value flow” cost control method that traces carbon-containing material and energy inputs, transformation, and emissions through steel production, maps these flows to internal resource transfer costs and external environmental damage costs, and identifies process-level control points and optimization measures. Carbon flow analysis indicated that coking, ironmaking, and steelmaking are high-emission processes. Value flow analysis showed that these processes also incur high carbon costs and are therefore key control points. Within the process-level quantitative boundary and simulated optimization scenarios, internal resource transfer costs and external environmental damage costs were RMB 1,176 million and RMB 1,442 million lower than baseline, respectively. After accounting for technical retrofit investment and key parameter uncertainty, carbon cost reductions ranged from approximately RMB 1,879 million to RMB 3,941 million across the sensitivity scenarios. The findings provide practical guidance for enterprises seeking to strengthen carbon emissions management,…

title: Integrating recycled concrete carbonation and calciner electrification for low‐carbon cement: Techno‐economic assessment
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the techno‐economic feasibility of integrating a recycled concrete fines (RCF) wet carbonation process into an electrified‐calciner cement plant focusing on energy consumption, CO 2 avoidance, and cost implications at an industrial scale. The proposed system is compared with a stand‐alone electrified calciner, an electrified‐calciner plant using non‐carbonated RCF directly in the cement blend, and an electrified‐calciner plant equipped with monoethanolamine (MEA)‐based capture. Results show that the RCF carbonation process is energy‐intensive (3.35 MJ el /kg) and provides limited decarbonization compared to MEA capture. Under the European energy mix, the CO 2 avoidance rate reaches 61.7%, only slightly higher than calciner electrification alone and largely driven by clinker substitution rather than by CO 2 uptake during carbonation. Economically, the increased cement production and lower capital expenses associated with carbonation result in a modest improvement in CO 2 avoidance cost (200.7 €/t) compared to the MEA‐based capture option (217.4 €/t).

title: The Pollen-Reward Strategy: The Paradoxical Realities of Trading Gametes for Sex
abstract: Pollen-rewarding plants face a fundamental tension: Pollen serves simultaneously as the male gametophyte and pollinator reward. Despite this apparent paradox, pollen is the second most common floral reward and the sole reward for an estimated 20,000 angiosperm species. We review the ecology and evolution of the pollen-reward strategy, synthesizing literature encompassing pollen chemistry, floral morphology, and sex allocation. We find that this reward strategy is unevenly distributed among plant families, that the resource costs of pollen rewards remain poorly characterized, and that this reward strategy may influence plant sexual-system evolution. We offer hypotheses regarding the evolution and maintenance of the pollen-reward strategy and examine the ecological and evolutionary consequences associated with its expression. We suggest that floral rewards are not isolated traits, but key elements of plant reproductive strategies, and that this perspective allows comparison among strategies and can advance our understanding of the evolutionary ecology of plant reproduction.

Multivariate Linear Response Estimates of Solar Wind–Magnetosphere Coupling
abstract: Solar wind forcing and magnetospheric evolution contribute to the timing of geomagnetic disturbances. A central question is how estimated response lags depend on the chosen observable and preprocessing. We analyzed eight selected intervals of one-minute OMNI observations using multivariate covariance-based response estimates for the symmetric disturbance index in the horizontal component (SYM-H). The state contains electric field, dynamic pressure, and index levels at the current time and four preceding samples. Causal exponential high-pass filtering defines the primary analysis. Within a 0–40 min search window, the electric-field response of SYM-H increments has a median eventwise peak lag of 20 min and an interquartile range (IQR) of 10.5 min; its ensemble-mean curve peaks at 35 min. The pressure response peaks at 4 min in both summaries. Individual increment-response peak lags are unchanged across four preprocessing schemes at common timestamps. Extending the search to 120 min shifts the electric-field median to 41 min, while ensemble peaks remain at 35 and 4 min. These descriptive estimates are consistent with rapid compressive and slower convective contributions, but window dependence, model approximation, and interpolated inputs limit their interpretation as physical transport delays.

title: Multiparametric cardiomyocyte profiling with single‐LED excitation reveals subtype‐specific electromechanical coupling in LQTS in vitro
abstract: Abstract Cardiac excitation–contraction coupling (ECC) is an essential and tightly regulated process that links action potentials to intracellular calcium release and mechanical contraction. At the whole‐heart level, ECC is captured by integrative evaluation of electrical and mechanical components of the cardiac cycle through parameters termed electromechanical delay (EMD) and electromechanical window (EMW). Alterations in the EMD or EMW reflect impaired electromechanical coupling and have been associated with increased arrhythmic risk across multiple cardiac diseases. However, it is currently unclear whether and how equivalent metrics can be derived and interpreted in vitro or meaningfully applied to patient‐specific human disease models. Here, we implement ECC profiling in vitro using a single‐LED optical imaging system that enables simultaneous measurements of membrane voltage, intracellular calcium and contractility. This approach allows quantification of individual transients and their temporal relationships. To investigate distinct perturbations of ECC, we applied this platform to human‐induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC‐CMs) representing three mechanistically distinct ECC perturbations: a repolarization defect (LQT2, KCNH2 p.A561V), a calmodulin‐associated calcium‐handling defect (CALM‐LQTS, CALM1 p.F142L) and pharmacological contractile uncoupli…

Assessing the Influence of Ocean-Wind-Wave Coupling on Marine Boundary Layer Wind Dynamics
abstract: Abstract Understanding and accurately forecasting marine boundary layer dynamics in coastal areas is essential for resource management and strategic planning. These areas are characterized by intricate air–sea–land interactions, which pose challenges to predictability. Traditional high-resolution models treat wave–ocean effects through parameterization in stand-alone simulations, potentially overlooking fine-scale processes and simultaneous feedbacks. In this study, we employ the Coupled Ocean–Atmosphere–Wave–Sediment Transport (COAWST) system to investigate the impacts of ocean–wind–wave interactions on coastal processes and marine boundary-layer winds. Focusing on the Mid-Atlantic Bight, simulations from July 2021–June 2022 are validated against available buoy observations. Compared to stand-alone atmospheric simulations, the fully coupled system reduces wind-speed and direction errors within the lowest 50 m of the atmosphere above sea level. Targeted experiments are conducted to isolate the contributions of (i) sea-surface temperature (SST) and (ii) wave-dependent surface roughness, with specific emphasis on land–sea-breeze dynamics and high-wave conditions. SST feedbacks improve prediction of land–sea-breeze-driven low-level jets (LLJs), by enhancing skill in occurrence rates, jet-nose speed, and nose height at diurnal timescales. title: Energy-saving policy and economic performance in Kazakhstan: A structured systematic-narrative review
abstract: This article examines the conditions under which energy-saving and energy-efficiency policies can improve economic performance in Kazakhstan. It applies a structured systematic-narrative review to 29 substantive peer-reviewed studies published from January 2021 to July 2026 in journals indexed in Scopus and/or the Web of Science. Three methodological sources informed the review design and reporting, while six official and institutional sources established the national energy and policy baseline. Candidate studies were identified through documented keyword combinations across publisher platforms and digital object identifier metadata, assessed against explicit eligibility criteria, and coded by research design, sector, outcome, evidential status, limitation, and relevance to Kazakhstan. The synthesis distinguishes causal results, associations, modelled effects, and untested mechanisms across six channels: production costs and productivity; investment and innovation; employment and skills; competitiveness and structural change; household welfare and distribution; and fiscal, environmental, and energy-security effects. Evidence generally links higher energy productivity to stronger firm performance and identifies potential employment and welfare gains, but effect sizes vary across sectors and institutions. title: B(N 5 ) 3 : Stabilized Boron Pentazolates with Promising Performance as High–Energy–Density Material
abstract: In this work, we identify two high–pressure boron pentazolate phases, P2 1 −B(N 5 ) 3 and P1−B(N 5 ) 3 , via ab initio evolutionary searches. These phases contain cyclo-N 5 − units arranged into distinct one-dimensional and layered B–N frameworks. Both phases are thermodynamically metastable at their respective predicted pressures, and P1–B(N 5 ) 3 remains thermodynamically metastable under ambient pressure after decompression. Electronic–structure and bonding analyses indicate that the stability of these phases originates from the combined effects of aromatic stabilization of the cyclo–N 5 − units, moderate charge transfer from boron, and strong covalent B–N interactions. After including zero–point energy and thermal corrections, the calculated energy densities at 0 GPa and 300 K are 6.24 kJ/g for P2 1 –B(N 5 ) 3 and 7.59 kJ/g for P1–B(N 5 ) 3 . These values exceed those of several representative energetic materials, including TNT and HMX, and are also competitive with previously reported nitrogen–rich high–energy–density compounds. These results demonstrate a boron-based stabilization strategy for crystalline pentazolate frameworks and provide insights into the relationship between B–N bonding and the stabilization of nitrogen-rich structures.

title: Integration of metabolomics and transcriptomics identifies pathways involved in arginine vasopressin-mediated brown adipose tissue thermogenesis and glucose tolerance improvement in type 2 diabetes mice
abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D), a global epidemic, is a metabolic disease often accompanied by impaired glucose tolerance and insulin resistance. Arginine vasopressin (AVP), a key neuroendocrine hormone regulating fluid balance and vascular tone, has attracted increasing attention for its association with metabolic disorders, particularly T2D. Concurrently, brown adipose tissue (BAT) has emerged as an important peripheral target for mitigating T2D; however, data on the role of AVP in improving glucose tolerance via enhancement of BAT thermogenesis remain limited. Moreover, no combined multi-omics studies have investigated the associated metabolic pathways and mechanisms. This study aimed to examine the therapeutic effect of AVP on glucose intolerance through BAT activation and to explore the related pathways using multi-omics approach. We used db/db mice, a classic T2D model, to induce impaired glucose tolerance and insulin resistance. During AVP administration, mice had ad libitum access to chow and water. Our results demonstrated that AVP enhanced BAT thermogenesis and improved glucose tolerance in T2D mice. Metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed that AVP modulated inositol phosphate metabolism, the pentose phosphate pathway, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, alleviating glucose tolerance impairment through BAT thermogenesis via inflammatory and insulin secretion pathways. Benchmarking Scheelite Oxides XTcO 4 (X = Li, K, Rb, Cs) via First-Principles Calculations: Stability, Band Gaps, and Thermoelectric Performance for Sustainable Energy Technologies
abstract: This study investigates the structural, optoelectronic, and thermoelectric properties of scheelite oxides XTcO 4 (X = Li, K, Rb, Cs) using first-principles ab-initio calculations. The results reveal that CsTcO 4 is the most stable compound among the studied oxides, with the lowest ground state energy. Within the PBE+U framework, the calculated direct band gaps of LiTcO 4 , KTcO 4 , RbTcO 4 , and CsTcO 4 are 2.30, 2.34, 2.27, and 2.37 eV, respectively, indicating their potential for visible/near UV photovoltaic applications. These materials exhibit significant photon absorption in the visible and UV regions, with XTcO 4 (X = Li, K, Rb, Cs) showing superior thermoelectric performance. The analysis of thermoelectric properties confirms the thermal performance of these compounds, while KTcO 4 and CsTcO 4 exhibit positive Seebeck coefficients indicating p-type semiconducting behavior. Conversely, the Seebeck coefficient (S) values for the LiTcO 4 and RbTcO 4 compounds decrease with increasing temperature, suggesting a transition in the material’s semiconductor type from p-type to n-type behavior. The calculated electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties of CsTcO 4 indicate interesting intrinsic characteristics from a fundamental materials-science perspective. However, the radioactive and artificial nature of technetium presents substantial practical limitations for experimen…

title: TGF-Net: Tri-Gated Fusion Network for Coarse-to-Fine Unsupervised Deformable Medical Image Registration
abstract: Abstract Medical image registration aligns anatomical structures by spatially transforming images within the same modality. However, existing deformable registration methods often struggle to accurately model large anatomical deformations and complex local structural variations, limiting registration accuracy in clinically challenging scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose TGF-Net, a Tri-Gated Fusion Network for unsupervised deformable medical image registration. TGF-Net employs dual encoders with non-shared weights to extract multiscale features from the moving and fixed images, followed by a coarse-to-fine decoder for progressive deformation estimation. The core of the proposed framework is a tri-gated fusion module that explicitly models complementary interactions among decoder, fixed-image, and warped-image features to progressively refine deformation fields. Furthermore, an adaptive multi-branch pooling strategy aggregates fine-scale structural responses from each feature stream and generates feature-specific gating weights, enabling more effective preservation of local anatomical details during refinement. The proposed framework was trained and evaluated on three publicly available datasets, including the Laboratory of Neuro Imaging Probabilistic Brain Atlas (LPBA), AbdomenCT, and Information eXtraction from Images (IXI). title: Design and Implementation of Secured Electronic Health System Using Pin and Barcode Technology
abstract: The healthcare sector increasingly relies on electronic systems to manage patient information, improve service delivery, and enhance operational efficiency. However, the digitization of medical records has introduced significant security and privacy concerns, including unauthorized access, data breaches, and identity misuse. The aim of this study is to design and implement a secured electronic health system using Personal Identification Number (PIN) and barcode technology. This work was motivated on the basis of finding a solution to the security concerns of patients about their Electronic Health Records (EHR). The replacement of paper processes in our hospitals with Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system has neither ended the problem of continued manual and repeated processes in gathering health history of patients, nor the security problem with the patients’ health information, hence, the need for the research. The methodology used is the Object Oriented Analysis and Design Methodology (OOADM). The expected result of this new system is a two-level authentication security technique, as the hybrid model that will solve the bottlenecks identified in this work. Some of the hardware, programming and scripting languages, and application packages that were used for the development of this hybrid software are barcode reader, php, java scripts, CSS, ajax, and Adobe Photoshop - CS6.
