title: From Membranes to Catalyst Layers: Molecular and Interfacial Design of Anion-Exchange Polyelectrolytes
abstract: Conspectus Sustainable electrochemical energy conversion relies on functional materials that enable efficient transport while withstanding demanding operating environments. Anion-exchange membrane fuel cells (AEMFCs) and anion-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs) are attractive platforms because their alkaline environments enable the use of nonprecious-metal catalysts and hydrocarbon-based polymer electrolytes. Anion-exchange polyelectrolytes (APEs) are central to these devices, serving as both free-standing anion-exchange membranes (AEMs) and catalyst-layer anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs). Although AEMs and AEIs share related polymer chemistries, their distinct operating environments and functional roles impose different requirements on molecular design. Our work on AEMs has focused on the coupled requirements of hydroxide transport, chemical stability, dimensional control, and mechanical durability. We first examined how polymer architecture and chain packing affect the formation of ion-conducting domains and confined transport environments. As conductivity improved, chemical degradation and mechanically induced failure became increasingly relevant, leading us to investigate cation stability, local electronic environments, dimensional constraints, and molecular-level stress dissipation. These studies showed that AEMs cannot be optimized on the basis of a single perfo…

title: Trust Without the Word: Object-Scoped Evaluation and the Case for an Operational Design Domain for Trust Metrics
abstract: Assurance frameworks increasingly treat user trust as a form of evidence. The instruments that produce it are multidimensional in why a system is trusted (performance, process, purpose) but not in what it is trusted for. Nearly every item asks about the system as a whole. We report two measurements from a corpus study of naturalistic AI discourse across 17 online communities and 38 months. Among items expressing a trust or distrust evaluation, 96.97% contain no trust vocabulary. Of these evaluations, 84% attach to a specific object as measured, and approximately 89% after correction for a one-directional coding error (Section 4.3), rather than to AI as a category. A word-list detector built from the definition of explicit trust vocabulary reaches only κ= 0.464 against hand codes, and about two thirds of its positive calls are false. We argue that an unscoped trust score aggregates over distinctions its respondents are making and so has no clear referent. Trust evidence used in assurance should therefore carry a scope specification, as safety claims for driving automation carry an operational design domain. This paper reports Phase 1 of a two-phase project and is exploratory throughout.

An Enzyme-Mediated Duplex Exponential Amplification Assay for Rapid Detection of Plasmodiophora brassicae
abstract: Clubroot, caused by the soilborne obligate biotrophic protist Plasmodiophora brassicae , substantially reduces the yield and quality of cruciferous crops worldwide. In this study, an enzyme-mediated duplex exponential amplification (EmDEA) assay was developed for rapid detection of P. brassicae in extracted DNA. By comparing the P. brassicae strain 3A genome with representative bacterial, fungal, and oomycete genome assemblies, we identified 157 candidate regions that showed no detectable matches in the selected non-target genomes under the specified alignment criteria. Pbspec1, a fragment within the annotated locus PBTT_08698, was selected based on computational non-target screening, within-species conservation, and suitability for assay design. PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing were used to validate the target fragment. Six forward primers, six reverse primers, and six RNA probes were screened, and F2–R4–RNA2 was selected for subsequent EmDEA experiments. Using serial dilutions of purified recombinant plasmid DNA, the F2–R4–RNA2 combination consistently detected template concentrations of 1.0 × 10 3 copies/μL and above. No amplification was observed from the 12 non-target fungal or bacterial organisms. The assay detected P. brassicae in DNA extracted from four infected root samples and three naturally infested soil samples. All tested positive samples produced detectabl…

title: The Effect of Early Season Alternate Row Middle Fungicide Application on Spray Coverage and Scab Severity in Tall Pecan Trees
abstract: Scab (caused by Venturia effusa ) is the major yield-limiting factor of pecan in the southeastern United States. Control is typically achieved using conventional fungicides applied using an air-blast sprayer. Generally, sprays are applied to both row sides simultaneously by traveling up and down the center line of consecutive rows (every row middle, ERM). Early in the season, some growers have used alternate row middle (ARM) spray applications. However, the impact of early season ARM on scab control and fruit weight has not been explored. In this study, ARM every 7 and 14 days and ERM every 14 days for the first 6 weeks (and ERM in all treatments thereafter) were compared with nontreated controls in the 2018 and 2019 seasons. There were some effects of spray date and tree side on spray coverage that were likely due to canopy development after bud break, and the ERM application had at least twice the spray coverage in both seasons compared with the ARM applications. In 2018, scab severity on young leaflets was least on the ARM14 treatment compared with the other treatments, but in 2019, all three treatments had less severe scab when compared with the control (but were not different from each other). For the older leaflet assessment, in both seasons, there was more severe scab on leaflets of the control compared with the ARM7 treatment and in 2019 compared with the ERM treatment …

Feasibility and Acceptability of Virtual Reality for Pain Relief During Vaso-occlusive Episodes in Sickle Cell Disease: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Behavioural interventions are increasingly studied as adjunctive treatments for vaso-occlusive episodes (VOEs) among patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). Objective To assess the feasibility of virtual reality (VR) and changes in VOE-related pain among adults with SCD, with secondary assessment of acceptability, perceived distraction, and side effects. Design Prospective pilot pre-post study. Participants Twenty adult individuals with SCD (mean age 35 years; 90% identifying as non-Hispanic Black/African American; 50% identifying as female; 10% assessed as having low electronic health literacy). Interventions A VR application delivered via Meta Quest 3 headset as an adjunctive, non-pharmacologic intervention for patients experiencing VOEs. Main Measures Feasibility and acceptability were assessed via self-reported distraction from pain and simulation sickness symptoms. Changes in pain were assessed using a 0–10 pain scale immediately before and immediately after VR use, with paired t -tests evaluating mean post- vs. pre-intervention pain scores. Key Results Most participants (75%) reported that VR at least somewhat helped distract them from pain, and 85% experienced mild to no simulation sickness symptoms during VR wear. Participants had a statistically significant reduction in pain following the intervention (mean pre, 7.25 vs. mean post, 6.35; p = 0.002)…

Cadmium tolerance and distribution patterns in three perennial herbaceous plant species: Implications for phytostabilization potential
abstract: Abstract To evaluate the phytostabilization potential of perennial herbaceous species in cadmium (Cd)‐contaminated soil, Cd tolerance and distribution were assessed in a 90‐day pot experiment under 0–100 mg/kg Cd. Crested wheatgrass ( Agropyron cristatum (L.) Gaertn.), orchardgrass ( Dactylis glomerata L.) and Siberian wildrye ( Elymus sibiricus L.) were tested. The final germination percentage, shoot length, root length, and root‐shoot ratio of A. cristatum did not differ significantly among the control and Cd treatments. In D. glomerata , germination, growth, chlorophyll content, and root activity decreased significantly at 50 and 100 mg/kg Cd. By contrast, E. sibiricus displayed trait‐specific positive responses: germination percentage, shoot length, root length, and root biomass increased significantly at 50 mg/kg Cd, while root volume, shoot biomass, chlorophyll content, and root activity increased significantly at both 50 and 100 mg/kg Cd. Based on the root‐length tolerance index, Cd tolerance ranked as E. sibiricus > A. cristatum > D. glomerata . Malondialdehyde (MDA) content, relative conductivity, and Cd concentrations in shoots and roots increased with increasing Cd stress and were significantly higher at 100 mg/kg Cd than in the control, indicating high‐Cd injury. title: Evaluation of ITS copy number variation among Clarireedia jacksonii isolates using single-copy genetic markers cam and hsp60
abstract: Molecular tools are widely used for plant pathogen detection and quantification. Recent quantitative PCR applications for the turfgrass disease causal agent Clarireedia jacksonii were developed targeting the ITS region and showed potential utility in improved disease management. However, accurate and consistent pathogen quantification is contingent on stable copy numbers of the target genes across populations. In this study, we evaluated the genomic copy number of molecular markers in C. jacksonii using in silico analyses, quantitative PCR, and digital PCR. Calmodulin ( cam ), elongation factor 1-alpha ( ef1α ), and minichromosome maintenance protein 7 ( mcm7 ) were consistently identified as single-copy loci, whereas ITS exhibited multiple copies in two out of nine assemblies. Digital PCR confirmed that cam and heat shock protein 60 ( hsp60 ) closely followed theoretical single-copy expectations across a genomic DNA dilution series of C. jacksonii isolate HRS10. In the analysis of 27 C. jacksonii isolates, ITS was consistently detected as a multicopy locus, with copy number estimates ranging from 33 to 48 copies per genome when normalized using cam and from 34 to 52 copies per genome when normalized using hsp60 . These results demonstrate that ITS copy number variation among C. jacksonii isolates was consistently observed, independent of the single-copy reference locus used fo…

title: Medicinal plants, lessons from mushrooms and the power of smell: Books in brief
Plant autoinhibited Ca2+-ATPases: shaping calcium signals for growth, stress adaptation, and crop improvement
abstract: P-type ATPases are conserved ATP-driven ion transporters that maintain cellular ion homeostasis. Plant P-type IIB Ca 2+ -ATPases, known as autoinhibited Ca 2+ -ATPases (ACAs), are key regulators of Ca 2+ signaling networks. This review summarizes the structural features, Ca 2+ /calmodulin-dependent regulation, evolutionary diversification, and biological functions of plant ACAs. By contributing to cytosolic Ca 2+ clearance and the restoration of basal Ca 2+ levels, ACAs may modulate stimulus-specific Ca 2+ dynamics and participate in diverse physiological processes, including plant growth, development, stomatal movement, immunity, and abiotic stress adaptation. Comparative analyses across plant species highlight functional specialization of ACA isoforms and their potential value for crop improvement. We further discuss current challenges in ACA functional characterization, particularly the complexity of Ca 2+ signaling networks and the limited understanding of ACA-associated genetic variation. Emerging approaches integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and precision genome editing provide new opportunities for identifying and designing ACA alleles for climate-resilient crop breeding.

title: Critical dynamics of a scalar field near four spatial dimensions
abstract: A bstract The critical dynamics of a non-conserved order parameter is generally expected to become overdamped at long distances, even when propagating modes occur at microscopic or intermediate scales. We investigate the critical dynamics of a scalar field theory in thermal equilibrium which, in addition to local friction and noise, also contains a time-dependent second-order kinetic term. We show how to build a supersymmetric field-theory formulation. Using a two-loop expansion about four spatial dimensions, we show that the propagating and strictly overdamped limits share the same static Gaussian and Wilson-Fisher fixed points but realize distinct dynamical scaling regimes. The overdamped limit reproduces Model A. On the surface where local friction and noise vanish, the theory instead supports an interacting propagating fixed point whose dynamic exponent receives corrections at two loops. We demonstrate that coarse-graining does not generate a local dissipative operator on this surface, which therefore remains invariant under the RG flow. Local dissipation is nevertheless relevant at the propagating fixed point: an arbitrarily small equilibrium friction-noise perturbation drives the flow away from propagating scaling. Propagating critical dynamics thus defines a consistent but fine-tuned regime that is unstable to local equilibrium dissipation.

title: Sistema fotovoltaico para la sostenibilidad energética del Palacio Municipal del cantón La Libertad
abstract: La incorporación de generación fotovoltaica en edificios públicos requiere relacionar el recurso solar con el consumo, las condiciones de conexión y la capacidad de aprovechar la energía producida. La investigación tuvo como objetivo desarrollar una propuesta de prefactibilidad para el Palacio Municipal del cantón La Libertad mediante el reanálisis de seis registros mensuales de marzo a agosto de 2025, el dimensionamiento analítico y una revisión técnica complementaria. El consumo acumulado fue de 23.393 kWh, con una media de 3.898,83 kWh/mes y un coeficiente de variación muestral del 26,08 %. Adoptando el rendimiento específico de 4,97 kWh/kWp/día consignado en la información de partida, la cobertura del 60 % del consumo medio requiere al menos 29 módulos de 550 Wp; se desarrolló una alternativa de 30 módulos y 16,50 kWp para estudiar dos cadenas equivalentes y un inversor candidato de 15 kW. Su producción de referencia sería de 29,93 MWh/año, mientras que dimensionar para el 60 % del mes de mayor consumo requiere 36 módulos y 19,80 kWp. Con fracciones hipotéticas de autoconsumo del 60 al 100 %, la alternativa de 16,50 kWp sustituiría entre 17,96 y 29,93 MWh/año de electricidad de red y representaría entre 2,00 y 3,33 t CO₂eq/año de reducción operacional, utilizando el factor oficial del SNI de 2025. title: APPROACH TO MODELING PHOTOVOLTAIC ENERGY YIELD USING CHEBYSHEV POLYNOMIALS
abstract: Photovoltaic energy yield varies in response to changes in meteorological conditions. The main factors affecting the amount of electricity generated include solar irradiance and air temperature, as well as seasonal and daily variations. This paper examines the relationships between these factors and photovoltaic energy yield and presents an approach to modeling those using orthogonal Chebyshev polynomials. The main input variables, data-preprocessing steps, and structure of the approximation model are defined.

title: From the 2026 Hormuz disruption to renewable resilience: energy security and decarbonization governance in import-dependent economies
abstract: Import-dependent economies face a systemic governance challenge: a small number of fossil-fuel chokepoints and centralized fossil assets concentrate macroeconomic, health, and water-security risks that conventional energy-security framing systematically underprices. Using the 2026 disruption of the Strait of Hormuz as an illustrative stress test and Israel as a semi-arid, security-sensitive case, this Perspective develops a four-component analytical framework—chokepoint-exposure assessment (distinguishing physical supply, global price, infrastructure-concentration, and cross-sector cascade exposure), quantification of domestic fossil-fuel externalities, mapping of fossil-fuel–water infrastructure couplings, and security-oriented governance instruments—and applies it to governmental, OECD, and epidemiological evidence. The analysis shows that Israel’s fossil-centric paradigm couples exposure to distant chokepoints with the concentration of domestic gas supply in three offshore platforms, a total ambient air-pollution burden of 4,641–6,166 premature deaths annually (over USD 7.2 billion in economic costs), to which fossil-fuel combustion is a major though not exclusive contributor, and a desalination system exposed to low-probability, high-impact maritime oil-spill scenarios. We argue that distributed renewable generation, energy storage, and transport electrification warrant des…

SuperDelta: Improving the Compression Ratio in the Fine-grained Deduplication Storage Systems
abstract: As a complement to data deduplication, delta compression further reduces the data volume by compressing non-duplicate data chunks relative to their similar base chunks in backup storage. However, we find that existing delta compression approaches suffer from several limitations that prevent them from achieving higher compression ratios. Specifically, (1) First-fit problem. They directly select the first-fit similar candidate chunk among several, which may miss a better candidate. (2) Old-compress-new problem. The similar base chunk is usually selected from older-version backups, since once a chunk in the new version has been delta-compressed, it can no longer be used as a base chunk. However, new chunks may be more suitable for compressing subsequent backups due to the locality of shorter “modification distance”. (3) One-to-one problem. The compression scope of delta encoding is restricted to only one base chunk and one delta chunk, which wastes opportunities to compress against other similar chunks. To address these problems, we propose SuperDelta, which exploits higher compression ratios in delta compression storage. It incorporates several techniques: (1) A chunking-boundary-assisted similarity detection method, which leverages the observation that highly similar chunks tend to share the same chunk boundaries with high probability, thereby enabling the system to select bette…

title: ALT-index+: An Efficient Hybrid Learned Index for Concurrent Memory Systems
abstract: The learned index technique has been widely explored as a strong competitor to traditional indexes. However, frequent retraining is required when it comes to insertion scenarios, and the read-write performance of the learned index still falls short of expectations, especially in concurrent conditions. In this paper, we first propose a novel hybrid index scheme that combines a read-efficient learned index with an insert-efficient Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) to realize high read-write performance. However, it is not trivial due to expensive model prediction errors, complicated retraining process, redundant node traversals, and slow bulkload speed. Therefore, we introduce ALT-index, an efficient hybrid learned index structure with a delicate two-tier architecture, a compact pointer buffer, and an efficient segment algorithm to address these issues. Nevertheless, its performance is still limited by blocking retraining process, and the bulkload time cannot exploit multithreading. To address these limitations, we present ALT-index+ with two major extensions. First, we develop a stepped lazy eviction scheme to support a non-blocking retraining process. Second, a parallel recursive construction scheme is designed to accelerate bulkloading in both layers. Experimental results show that ALT-index+ achieves 1.4x–2.5x throughput improvement in read-write-balanced scenarios, with a maximum 80…

Degradation Regime Discovery for EIS-Based Lithium-Ion Battery SOH Estimation Using Equivalent-Circuit and Vision-Based Features
abstract: Accurate State of Health (SOH) estimation is essential for the safe and reliable operation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), yet most electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)-based approaches fix a single equivalent circuit model (ECM) topology and measurement state without testing whether that choice is actually the most degradation-sensitive one, and rarely cross-check circuit-based findings against an independent, model-agnostic representation of the same impedance data. This study addresses both gaps through a physics-constrained framework applied to four commercial Li-ion cells cycled to end of life, with EIS spectra acquired at nine states in a cycle. Six ECM topologies (1R to 2RCPEW) were fitted at each state, and the Pearson Correlation Coefficient was used to jointly rank topology–state combinations by their sensitivity to capacity fade. The best-ranked ECM parameters were then used as input to a left-to-right Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to segment battery aging into ordered latent degradation regimes, with results compared against an HMM applied to DINOv2 embeddings of Nyquist and DRT plots. Finally, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was used to estimate SOH with and without the HMM-derived regime label as an auxiliary feature. Results show that State V (reached after a post-charge rest) yields the highest degradation sensitivity for most ECMs, with ohmic and charge-…

title: Fiscal Federalism and the Determinants of State Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) in Nigeria
abstract: This study empirically examines the impact of fiscal federalism on state Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) in Nigeria over the period 1999–2024. The study evaluates how the fiscal instruments such as revenue-sharing arrangements, grants and transfers, sub-national debt levels, and vertical and horizontal revenue allocation formulas affect IGR across Nigerian states with heterogeneous economic structures. Specifically, the study seeks to: (i) assess the impact of revenue-sharing arrangements on state IGR; (ii) examine the effect of grants and transfers on state IGR;. Adopting an ex post facto and analytical research design, the study utilizes secondary data sourced from the National Bureau of Statistics and other official publications. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model is employed to estimate both short-run and long run dynamics, with inflation rate incorporated as a moderating variable. The study applies a comprehensive set of econometric techniques, including unit root tests. The empirical findings reveal that revenue-sharing arrangements exert a statistically significant effect on IGR, leading to the acceptance of the alternative hypothesis (H₁). Similarly, grants and transfers demonstrate a statistically significant relationship with IGR, supporting the acceptance of (H₂). title: Interfacial Bond Fabricated From High Entropy MOFs Facilitates Electric Field Modulation for Boosted Photoelectrochemical DHA Formation on BiVO 4
abstract: ABSTRACT BiVO 4 (BVO) photoanodes are promising for photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation (PEC GOR), but their performance is limited by sluggish hole extraction, V 5+ dissolution, and poor control over selective C 3 oxidation. Herein, we develop an in situ surface‐confined topological transformation strategy to construct an amorphous FeCoNiCuMn high‐entropy MOF interfacial layer on BVO (BVO‐H MOF). The high‐entropy layer acts as a catalytically coupled interface rather than a passive coating: it induces a Ni–V–O X activation layer to suppress V 5+ leaching and establishes an interfacial electric field that promotes directional hole extraction. In situ XPS, Raman, ATR‐SEIRAS, and DFT calculations indicate that electron‐deficient Ni sites favor adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol and promote the DHA‐forming pathway. As a result, BVO‐H MOF achieves a DHA formation rate of 361.5 mmol m −2 h – 1 and a selectivity of 69.8% at 1.0 V (vs. RHE), outperforming previously reported catalysts. More importantly, the Ni–V–O X activation layer generated by in situ conversion enabled stable operation for 120 h in an unbiased integrated PEC system. This work establishes high‐entropy MOF‐derived interfacial activation as a promising strategy for coupling solar‐driven biomass valorization with pollutant conversion.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Electrolyte Additive Discovery for Ultrafast Charging of Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract Sodium metal batteries hold immense promise for large-scale, high-power storage systems, yet their fast charging is severely constrained by sluggish Na+ transport across unstable electrode–electrolyte interphases. Conventional fluorine-donating additives suffer from inefficient self-decomposition, inevitably generating resistive organic byproducts. Herein, we propose an active machine learning framework based on Gaussian process regression to develop an innovative additive-triggered anion decomposition pathway. Guided by iterative screening of key physicochemical descriptors, a trace-level (0.02 M) sodium chlorodifluoroacetate (NaCDFA) additive is successfully identified. Theoretical calculations combined with in situ characterizations reveal that the NaCDFA thermodynamically promotes the targeted and continuous decomposition of the PF6– anion, enabling the construction of robust and highly conductive NaF-rich interphases, which substantially reduces the Na+ migration barrier. Consequently, the Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cell achieves ultrastable cycling over 50,000 cycles at an extreme rate of 200 C. Furthermore, outstanding performance is retained under rigorous practical conditions, including high-mass-loading cathodes and limited sodium excess or anode-free architectures. This work establishes a cost-effective trace-level electrolyte additive strategy for engineering fast-cha…

Proportional Spacing Tracking Control for Connected Vehicle Platoons Under Semantic Deception Attacks
abstract: Connected vehicle platoons rely on intervehicle information to regulate longitudinal spacing and attenuate downstream disturbance propagation. This dependence also exposes the platoon to semantic deception attacks that falsify communicated gap and relative speed information while preserving kinematic consistency. This paper investigates proportional spacing tracking and velocity string stability for a predecessor-following platoon of third-order vehicles with first-order actuator dynamics under such attacks. A vehicle-dependent proportional spacing policy is developed in which the proportional factor acts exclusively on the desired spacing without scaling the leader state. The semantic falsifications are mapped through the distributed controller into an equivalent attack-induced input while their kinematic coupling is retained in the closed-loop model. Internal stability is characterized using the Routh–Hurwitz criterion, and verifiable sufficient conditions for nominal velocity string stability are derived through frequency-domain analysis. A weighted transfer-gain inequality is further established to characterize the propagation of finite-energy semantic deception. By applying Parseval’s relation, the frequency-domain bound is converted into an explicit L2 energy recursion relating link-wise attack energy to downstream velocity-deviation energy. title: The Next‐Generation Layered Hydroxide Electrocatalysts Based on High‐Entropy Strategy: Synthesis, Characterization, and Electrochemical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy layered hydroxides (HE‐LHs) with five or more metal elements have drawn great attention because of their unique properties and scalable synthesis. Equipped with a tunable interlayer of two‐dimensional infrastructure, considerable atomic diversity, and promising industrial applications. These HE‐LHs have significantly higher mixed entropy and more complicated multiorbital hybrid effects than conventional hydroxides, which allows them to gain a customizable catalytic microenvironment, ideal conductivity, and thermodynamic stability. Although the high‐entropy strategy has been widely discussed in alloy and oxide systems, its immense potential in layered hydroxides remains undervalued. This review provides a comprehensive summary of the latest progress of layered hydroxides modified with the high‐entropy strategy, from the synthetic methods to electrochemical applications. The versatile synthetic strategies, including hydrothermal reaction, solvothermal reaction, co‐precipitation, and electrodeposition methods, are summarized. Besides, a thorough discussion of characterization methods for analyzing the basic structure of HE‐LHs is given and their electrochemical performance is assessed. Ultimately, this review briefly outlines the application of HE‐LHs in fields of oxygen evolution reaction, hydrogen evolution reaction, organic‐molecular oxidation reaction, an…

title: Pharmaceutical Salt Formation as a Strategy to Enhance In Situ Drug Loading into Apatite-Based Materials
abstract: Abstract Water-based loading is attractive for pharmaceutical and industrial applications and helps prevent damage to drug carriers; however, the poor aqueous solubility of many APIs, such as ciprofloxacin (CIP), limits their incorporation into these systems. To overcome these limitations, this work explores the use of a ciprofloxacin–dexketoprofen (CIP–DKT) pharmaceutical salt to improve API solubility and in situ loading into sensitive apatite platforms, including biomimetic apatite nanoparticles (Ap) and apatite-mineralized eggshell membranes (ApESM). Computational and solid-state characterization rationalized the improved aqueous solubility and drug loading observed with CIP–DKT. CIP showed higher affinity for the negatively charged apatite surface, whereas DKT displayed lower affinity and, due to its acidic nature, altered the synthesis pH, affecting apatite morphology and ESM mineralization. Interestingly, CIP–DKT enabled the simultaneous incorporation of CIP and DKT while preserving the biomimetic apatite morphology and the mineralization of the ESMs, likely due to the buffering effect of CIP. Final HPLC and antibacterial assays confirmed pH-dependent API release and sustained antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, with improved diffusion from ApESM–CIP–DKT. Overall, these results demonstrate that pharmaceutical salt formation is an efficient strategy to enhanc…

title: THE EVOLUTION OF THE “ALTERNATIVE FOR GERMANY” PARTY’S COMMUNICATIONS STRATEGY (2013–2026)
abstract: The article analyzes the evolution of the information strategy of the “Alternative for Germany” party in the context of the development of modern German political history. The aim of the article is to study the causes and consequences of the rise in popularity of the “Alternative for Germany” party in an open information society. The research methods used are: analytical, comparative, problem-chronological, critical. The scientific novelty of this article lies in the systematization and analysis of the origins of the “Alternative for Germany” party, the strengthening of the party’s position in the eastern and western federal states, and the information and political countermeasures against the strategy of its opponents, which was aimed at isolating “Alternative for Germany” from power at the state and federal levels. The conclusions indicate that the strengthening of the political positions of the “Alternative for Germany” party is due to the systemic socio-economic and moral-psychological problems of the Federal Republic of Germany. Initially, the German establishment did not take this party seriously. As a result, the opportunity to ban its legal activities was lost. The AfD party has become the main opposition political force. title: Sustainable Value Creation and Board Gender Diversity in Multinational Enterprises: The Moderating Role of Degree of Internationalisation
abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores the empirical relationship between sustainable value creation (SVC), board gender diversity (BGD) and the degree of internationalisation (DOI) in multinational enterprises (MNEs). Using an unbalanced panel of 285 MNEs across 22 countries over the period 2016–2025 and employing high‐dimensional fixed effects (FE), system GMM and entropy balancing techniques, we find that the individual effects of BGD and DOI on SVC are negative and insignificant, respectively. However, the interaction term (BGD × DOI) has a positive and significant effect on SVC. Theoretically, our findings suggest that the rigorous monitoring associated with gender‐diverse boards shifts from being a coordination cost to a value‐enhancing asset as MNEs face the heightened complexity and information asymmetry of global operations. This study contributes to Sustainability, Corporate Governance and International Business literature by synthesising stakeholder and legitimacy perspectives to explain the contingent role of corporate governance in MNE sustainable value creation.

title: Strategic Sustainability Management Through Dynamic Integration: A Systems Framework for Business Model Innovation and Competitive Advantage
abstract: ABSTRACT Strategic sustainability management (SSM) has become central to competitive strategy, yet the field remains fragmented across the Resource‐Based View, Stakeholder Theory, and Systems Theory, each illuminating different aspects while leaving integration mechanisms unspecified. This fragmentation creates strategic tensions: sustainability capabilities may fail to generate legitimacy, stakeholder engagement may lack operational substance, and systemic adaptation may proceed without supporting capabilities. This study develops a Dynamic Integration Framework positioning the three perspectives as interdependent dimensions connected through three reinforcing dynamics: adaptive integration strengthens legitimacy through credible commitment signaling; legitimacy facilitates capability development through resource access and protection from imitation; and capability development enables further adaptation through learning and resource generation. Business model innovation is identified as the activation mechanism enabling simultaneous progress across all three dimensions. The framework advances SSM theory by specifying the mechanisms linking the three perspectives and offers managers a roadmap for integrating business model innovation into competitive strategy.

title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
abstract: ABSTRACT Red organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non‐PAH merocyanine with pure π‐π* transition character (NBMCy‐B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P . Meanwhile, a dual‐locking strategy featuring molecular‐engineered double intramolecular H ‐bonds and a new quasi‐planar benzocycloketone (5‐methoxytetralone, 5M‐TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy‐B4/5M‐TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy‐B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual‐mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet‐yielding pathways. When doped in 5M‐TL, analogous merocyanines with different N ‐Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy‐B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short‐lived NBMCy‐B2 (green) and long‐lived B4 (red) in 5M‐TL afforded an unconventional and color‐tunable time‐dependent afterglow ma…

title: La modulación como estrategia de innovación en la vivienda contemporánea en México.
abstract: La arquitectura contemporánea ha evolucionado hacia una disciplina que busca responder con mayor precisión a las necesidades sociales, tecnológicas y ambientales de nuestro tiempo. Lejos de limitarse a propuestas estéticas, se ha convertido en una práctica crítica e innovadora que incorpora nuevas formas de habitar, materiales más eficientes y herramientas digitales que permiten mejorar los procesos de diseño y construcción. Se desarrolla una investigación documental exploratoria para analizar la aplicación de la modulación en la arquitectura contemporánea, para ello se consultaron diversas fuentes tales como libros académicos, revistas y artículos científicos. Los resultados indican que la modulación ofrece diferentes ventajas significativas, como lo son la reducción de tiempos de construcción, así como la disminución de desperdicio de material. El principal aporte del estudio consiste en integrar una perspectiva histórica, técnica y ambiental que permite comprender el potencial de la modulación como herramienta clave para la arquitectura contemporánea.

title: Projection-Based Microsurgical Strategy for Anterior Communicating Artery Aneurysms: Comparative Analysis of the Fronto-Orbitozygomatic and Pterional Approaches
abstract: Abstract Anterior communicating artery (ACoA) aneurysms with superior or posterior projection present significant microsurgical challenges due to limited exposure and complex vascular relationships. To compare the fronto-orbitozygomatic (FOZ) and pterional approaches in the microsurgical treatment of ACoA aneurysms with superior or posterior projection. The present retrospective single-center study included patients treated with microsurgical clipping between 2016 and March 2025. Only aneurysms with superior or posterior projection were included. Cases were stratified according to surgical approach and rupture status. Among 168 unruptured ACoA aneurysms, 28 (16.7%) had superior or posterior projection, 17 (60.7%) of which were treated using the FOZ approach and 11 (39.3%) using the pterional approach. Among 121 ruptured aneurysms, 19 (15.7%) had this projection, with 16 (84.2%) treated via FOZ and 3 (15.8%) via the pterional approach. The FOZ approach provided wider surgical exposure, improved visualization of bilateral A2 segments, facilitated proximal control, and reduced the need for frontal lobe retraction, particularly in complex and ruptured cases. The pterional approach remained effective in selected cases with favorable anatomy. The FOZ approach appears to be more suitable for ACoA aneurysms with superior or posterior projection, particularly in ruptured cases. Surgical…

title: The Scale Length of Electron Cyclotron Harmonic Wave Power by MMS Satellites
abstract: Abstract Using four MMS satellites from 2015 to 2021, we statistically investigate Electron Cyclotron Harmonic (ECH) wave power scale lengths. These waves are categorized into three distinct populations based on the background magnetic field topology: equatorial, off‐equator, and near the magnetopause. Generally, the observed scale lengths range from several kilometers to 100 km, with a typical value of ∼10 km. For the equatorial population, the typical parallel and perpendicular scale lengths are ∼14 and 24 km, respectively. For the off‐equator population, the parallel and perpendicular scale lengths are typically 20.8 and 19 km, respectively. For the population near the magnetopause, the parallel and perpendicular scale lengths are 19 and 13.7 km, respectively.

title: Overheating Characteristics of Contact Defects in the Transition Circuit of Oil-immersed Power Transmission Equipment On-Load Tap Changer
abstract: Abstract To address the local overheating and ablation problems of fastening connection structures in the transition circuit of oil-immersed power transmission equipment on-load tap changers (OLTCs), this paper proposes a contact-defect simulation method based on Joule-heating energy equivalence. According to the short-duration high-current characteristics during tap-changing operation, the current-carrying process of the transition circuit is equivalently converted into a laboratory current-carrying condition of 258 A for 2 s. A temperature-rise test platform consisting of a programmable AC constant-current source, prototype connection specimens, and an infrared thermal imager is established. Typical contact-defect conditions, including insufficient tightening torque, foreign-particle inclusion, abnormal anti-loosening coating, and uneven contact end surfaces, are designed to investigate the temperature-rise characteristics of the connection structure. The experimental results show that contact defects change the contact state of the conductor-connector interface, reduce the real contact area, increase the contact resistance, and intensify local temperature rise. Furthermore, an electro-thermal coupled simulation model is developed, in which an equivalent contact heat flux is used to characterize the additional interfacial heating caused by contact degradation. The results sho…

title: The infrastructural state: Evaluative power, socio-technical architectures, and stratification under digital-ecological conditions
abstract: Sociological analyses of the state have traditionally emphasized bureaucratic hierarchy, governmental techniques, and market-oriented managerial reforms. This article argues that contemporary governance increasingly depends on socio-technical infrastructures that embed evaluation within operational systems. Herein, the author proposes the concept of the infrastructural state as a conceptual refinement that captures this development without abandoning classical insights. The concept differs from Mann’s infrastructural power, which is concerned with the state’s ability to reach into society and carry out its decisions. Here, the focus is on how administrative judgment is shaped by the databases, scoring systems, and environmental models through which institutions increasingly work. The argument is illustrated through anticipatory social protection in northern Kenya, where biometric identification is linked with satellite-based drought monitoring. The case is useful because digital administration and ecological measurement come together within the same process. It shows how authority can become partly embedded in system design, calibration, and maintenance while administrative judgment remains important. The article further considers how these arrangements mediate stratification by shaping who becomes legible, eligible, and prioritized within governance systems.

High-power radiofrequency ablation with optimized pulsing algorithm for renal tumors: initial clinical experience and safety profile
abstract: Abstract Incidental diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma is increasing. While surgery remains the standard treatment for localized T1b or larger lesions, image-guided percutaneous ablation represents a valid alternative for T1a cases. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is effective but limited by smaller ablation volumes and sensitivity to the heat-sink effect. Microwave ablation and cryoablation have emerged to address these limitations, although the first is susceptible to thermal injury to adjacent structures and the second requires multiple, larger probes and longer procedures. High-power RFA (HP-RFA) is a recent development that delivers higher energy (370 versus 200 W), enabling faster and larger ablations. This study evaluated the feasibility and safety of a novel HP-RFA system incorporating an impedance-controlled pulsed algorithm and internally cooled electrodes. Five patients with small renal tumors (mean diameter 2.3 cm) unsuitable for surgery underwent ultrasound- or computed tomography-guided HP-RFA. Technical success, safety, and early tumor control were assessed. All procedures were technically successful. No major complications occurred; one minor perirenal hematoma was managed conservatively. Follow-up imaging at 6 months demonstrated complete tumor ablation without local recurrence. These preliminary findings suggest that HP-RFA is feasible and safe for treating small…

Work-Related Musculoskeletal Complaints Among Male Retail Butchers: Multisite Pain, Upper-Extremity Disability and Burnout
abstract: Background/Objectives: Butchering combines repetitive forceful knife work, sustained standing and heavy manual handling, yet data on musculoskeletal complaints in this trade are scarce. We examined the seven-day prevalence of musculoskeletal pain in male retail butchers and the factors associated with multisite pain and upper-extremity disability. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 99 of 112 male butchers affiliated with the Istanbul Chamber of Retail Butchers (participation 88.4%) completed a sociodemographic form, the Standardised Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (seven-day recall), the QuickDASH and the Maslach Burnout Inventory in face-to-face interviews. Multisite pain was defined a priori as pain in three or more of nine regions. Given marked group imbalance, it was modelled with Firth penalised logistic and Poisson regression; QuickDASH with linear regression. Results: Mean age was 38.69 ± 7.53 years; mean experience 16.10 ± 7.36 years. Pain was most frequent in the upper back (66.7%), shoulders (63.6%) and hand/wrist (59.6%); 88.9% (95% CI 81.2–93.7) reported three or more painful regions. Age was the only variable independently associated with multisite pain (OR 1.17, 95% CI 1.05–1.30) and with region count (IRR 1.022, 95% CI 1.010–1.036). No statistically significant association was detected between any burnout dimension and any outcome, but the confidence in…

Feasibility, Safety, and Preliminary Effect Estimates of an Ultrasound‐Informed Hybrid Joint‐Sparing Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Prospective Non‐Randomized Proof‐of‐Concept Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and PurposePhysical rehabilitation is recommended as an adjunct to pharmacological treatment in rheumatoid arthritis (RA); however, exercise prescription remains challenging when synovitis is active. Musculoskeletal ultrasonography (MSK‐US), particularly power Doppler (PD), provides a sensitive assessment of synovial inflammatory activity and may help inform rehabilitation planning. The primary objectives were to describe the feasibility and safety of a 12‐week ultrasound‐informed hybrid joint‐sparing rehabilitation protocol in patients with RA. Pain intensity (VAS) was the designated primary outcome for generating preliminary effect estimates, with ultrasonographic indices as secondary outcomes. No feasibility criteria were prespecified. Methods This prospective non‐randomized proof‐of‐concept study, reported according to the TREND statement, enroled 60 consecutive patients fulfiling the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria between February 2024 and January 2025. Participants were allocated by clinic attendance order (sequential recruitment) into a rehabilitation group ( n = 30) or a control group ( n = 30). The rehabilitation group received a 12‐week ultrasound‐informed hybrid protocol (supervised outpatient sessions plus a structured home programme) comprising weekly paraffin wax baths and baseline ultrasound‐stratified exercise progression, alongside stable pharmacol…

title: The Impact of Geopolitical Risks on Digital Innovation Among Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Beijing
abstract: Against the backdrop of an increasingly complex geopolitical environment, geopolitical risks have become a key external variable influencing digital innovation among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Focusing on SMEs in Beijing, this study employs a questionnaire survey to explore the internal mechanisms through which geopolitical risks affect corporate digital innovation. The questionnaire survey of 102 SMEs in Beijing reveals that geopolitical risks exert a dual impact on corporate digital innovation-both inhibiting and driving it. Although enterprises have implemented self-help measures, their risk-resilience varies significantly. Enterprises have an urgent need for subsidy and financing policies, yet gaps remain in the current policy offerings. Based onfindings, these this paper develops a self-assessment tool for corporate geopolitical risks and offers practical insights from three dimensions: corporate risk assessment, government public services, and social science research and practice.At the same time, the paper objectively analyzes research limitations-such as sample distribution and analytical methods-to provide a reference for the digital development of Beijing’s SMEs and for subsequent related empirical studies.

title: Investigating Associations Between Media Sentiment Surrounding Climate Change Engagement (SDG 13) and Performance Measures: A Study of FTSE 100 Listed Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether media coverage of climate change action (SDG 13) by FTSE 100 firms is associated with business performance in the following year. Drawing on 406,052 news articles published between 2013 and 2022, the study adopts a novel bibliometric keyword‐extraction approach to identify the valence of SDG 13‐related coverage of these firms. A dynamic panel model estimated by the generalized method of moments estimator shows that adverse SDG 13 media coverage of a firm is negatively associated with its sales, net profit, and Tobin's Q . In contrast, positive coverage is associated with improved sales and Tobin's Q . Viewed through the lens of integrated thinking as a holistic framework linking institutional and stakeholder theories, the findings suggest that SDG 13‐related media coverage is associated with corporate reputation and performance. Several implications are extracted from the study and avenues for future research.

title: When and How the Implementation of Green HRM Analytics and Open Eco‐Innovation Collaboration Improves Firm Net‐Zero Performance?
abstract: ABSTRACT The understanding of how manufacturing companies can successfully incorporate collaborative eco‐innovation strategies to reach challenging environmental objectives represents one of the main challenges in sustainable operations management. Given this lack of knowledge, the present study aims to research the mechanisms by which Open Eco‐Innovation Collaboration (OEIC) can be used to develop circular learning capability (CLC) and, in turn, improve net‐zero performance (NZP). Further, the moderating influence of green human resource management analytics (GHRMA) is examined and the challenging relationship between them is reinforced. This study presents and empirically tests a new conceptual model, based on the theoretical frameworks of open innovation and natural‐resource‐based view (NRBV). The model assumes that the relationship between OEIC‐NZP is mediated by CLC, which is also a positive moderator for the relationship between the firm's proficiency in GHRMA‐CLC. The data were gathered from 274 manufacturing companies in Pakistan through structured questionnaire and analyzed by partial least square structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM). The results demonstrate the important role of OEIC in improving a firm's CLC, which in turn is an important determinant of NZP. In addition, the findings show that the positive impact of OEIC on NZP through CLC is significantly enhanced…

title: Strategy for ensuring the competitiveness of Ukrainian energy enterprises in the conditions of sustainable development
abstract: The article examines the theoretical, methodological, and applied principles for developing a strategy to ensure the competitiveness of Ukraine’s energy enterprises in the context of sustainable development. The study is relevant because the domestic energy sector must adapt to structural transformations in the energy market, the consequences of military challenges, increased requirements for energy security, decarbonization, digitalization, and Ukraine’s integration into the European energy space. It has been established that the competitiveness of energy enterprises in modern conditions is determined not only by the level of economic efficiency and the ability to provide stable energy supply, but also by innovative and technological potential, investment attractiveness, environmental responsibility, energy efficiency, and the ability to quickly adapt to changes in the external environment. The study’s methodological basis includes general scientific and specialized methods, including a systematic approach; methods of analysis and synthesis; induction and deduction; comparison and generalization; and statistical and structural-dynamic analysis. The study’s results identify significant structural changes in Ukraine’s energy sector. Electricity production fell from about 157,7 billion kWh in 2021 to 96,9 billion kWh in 2024, reflecting the scale of transformations in the industr…

title: Regulatory uncertainty in management of individuals with intersex traits in Italy: A medico-legal and bioethical perspective
abstract: Individuals with intersex traits continue to experience a significant lack of protection within the Italian legal and healthcare system. The absence of specific legislation and standardized clinical guidelines contributes to practices that vary across regions and institutions, generating uncertainty in the medico-legal sphere and raising bioethical concerns about autonomy, non-maleficence, and justice. In particular, the persistence of early surgical interventions without the individual's consent remains controversial, especially when contrasted with the consent-based frameworks emerging in other European states. This article provides an in-depth analysis of the Italian normative vacuum, highlighting its consequences for clinical practice and the medico-legal landscape, with reference to the risk of future claims of biological damage resulting from physical and psychological harm. By situating the Italian scenario within a broader European context, including reforms in Malta, Germany, Portugal, Greece, Iceland, and Spain, the article demonstrates how Italy lags behind in recognizing and protecting the rights of individuals with intersex traits. The conclusion calls for urgent legislative and clinical reform that integrates international human rights principles and ensures the consistent application of bioethical standards in intersex healthcare.

title: Multi-hazard road-network criticality from earth observation data using spatial graph attention networks with conformal uncertainty
abstract: Coastal deltaic road networks in India experience compounding hazards of monsoon flooding, prolonged soil-moisture saturation, and heat stress. However, many graph-learning approaches to network vulnerability assessment validate with random train–test splits that do not account for spatial dependence between adjacent road segments leading to insufficient quantification of failure probability without any spatially calibrated uncertainty. This study attempts to address these gaps by developing a spatially aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) that estimates road-segment failure probability from multi-hazard exposure and network-topological covariates. Due to the lack of geocoded road-closure records, multi-hazard threshold rules were used to generate training labels, with model predictions interpreted as disruption susceptibility rather than observed failure probabilities. Model performance was evaluated using random and spatial-block cross-validation, while split-conformal prediction was used to quantify predictive uncertainty. The framework was applied to the East Godavari–Krishna deltaic corridor of coastal Andhra Pradesh using multi-source climate, satellite, terrain, road-network and population data (i.e., IMD, NASA SMAP, ERA5-Land, CHIRPS, Copernicus DEM, Sentinel-2, OpenStreetMap, and WorldPop) from 2016 to 2025. The GAT achieved an area under the receiver operating characte…

title: The moderating role of country-specific uncertainty in the cross-border banking–financial stability relationship
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe purpose of this study is to examine whether country-specific uncertainty modifies the relationship between cross-border banking exposure and financial stability. The analysis uses an annual panel covering 53 countries over 2005–2024, with 788 country-year observations in the baseline estimation sample. Financial stability is measured by the ratio of bank non-performing loans to total gross loans, cross-border banking exposure by BIS consolidated cross-border claims relative to GDP, and uncertainty by the country-specific World Uncertainty Index. The empirical strategy employs country and year fixed effects with standard errors clustered at the country level and includes an interaction between cross-border banking exposure and uncertainty. Formal triple-interaction tests are used to assess heterogeneity across exchange-rate regimes, levels of economic development, and financial depth. Robustness checks include lagged explanatory variables, placebo leads, country-specific linear trends, bias-corrected dynamic estimation, alternative transformations of cross-border exposure, and sample checks. The results show that higher uncertainty makes the relationship between cross-border banking exposure and non-performing loans more positive, indicating a less favorable association with financial stability as uncertainty rises. Refusal, Confidence, and Explanation: A Cross-Modal Audit of Uncertainty-Expression Failures in Small Open-Weight Language and Vision-Language Models
abstract: Safety evaluations usually test refusal, abstention, and stated confidence separately. We treat them as one property, appropriate uncertainty expression, and audit it in text and vision across six small open-weight LLMs and five vision-language model (VLM) configurations. On a 240-item Korean benchmark, judged refusal is higher for harmful than for benign-looking requests in every model and under every labeling rule, but model-level orderings depend on the rule (primary rule: zephyr-7b-beta refuses harmful requests least, 42.5%, and benign ones most, 18.8%). Against 150 blinded labels from one annotator, the judges agree on refusal (κ=0.63) but overstate benign-prompt refusal (10.4% vs. 3.6%). Replacing sensitive words in benign prompts did not lower refusal (−1.9 pp [−5.4, 1.7]). Two VLMs abstain far more on out-of-distribution images, yet their stated confidence when they answer is equivalent within ±5 points to that on in-distribution images. On six MedMNIST v2 tasks, VLM accuracy is near chance (13.2–15.6% vs. 14.6% expected; ConvMixer reference on the same images: 67.8%) at ≈80% stated confidence, and stated evidence locations match CNN saliency only at chance level. Scaling from 2B to 8B shrinks the confidence gap without improving accuracy. At a fixed generation budget, only a step-by-step instruction to assess intent and risk raised benign-prompt refusal (+9.0 pp); gene…

title: Predictive–Prescriptive Workforce Scheduling Under Absenteeism Uncertainty: A Computational Proof of Concept with Saudi-Relevant Logistics Scenarios
abstract: Absenteeism-related workforce uncertainty complicates logistics scheduling. This study evaluates a leakage-aware predictive–prescriptive proof of concept, using 740 observations from 36 workers in the Brazilian UCI Absenteeism at Work dataset. The measured outcome is whether recorded absence duration exceeds two hours, not future shift nonattendance. Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost were assessed with worker-disjoint testing, grouped tuning, calibration and cluster bootstrap uncertainty. Holdout ROC-AUC values were 0.4959, 0.4765 and 0.5243, respectively, indicating weak discrimination. A scheduling layer evaluated hypothetical availability-risk scenarios, using CP-SAT and mixed-integer programming with shortage, overtime, rest and fairness constraints. The solvers agreed on a small verification instance, and CP-SAT returned feasible schedules for 100 workers over 14 days and 200 workers over 30 days, with 200-worker optimality gaps near 19–21%. Across five replicated scenarios, shortage priority raised modelled coverage over greedy scheduling by 0.01408, whereas overtime priority reduced it by 0.07901. A value-of-prediction test on identical rosters compared forecast, uninformative, permuted and oracle risk inputs: the Logistic Regression forecast raised the modelled coverage by 0.0115 over an uninformative input (about 20% of the oracle gain), but this was not d…

title: Certified Rankings of Laminate Magnetoelectric Composites under Declared Parameter Uncertainty: Materials, Geometries, Modes and Electrodes
abstract: Abstract Reported magnetoelectric voltage coefficients of laminate composites span more than three orders of magnitude, and recomputing them on one engine makes them comparable without saying which comparisons are settled. Each figure of merit is therefore enclosed by two-sided bounds over a declared parameter box, and each comparative claim is decided by a bound on the RATIO of two configurations with the nuisance parameters they share held tied. The piezomagnetic coefficient and the interfacial coupling enter through the numerator only, so they cancel identically at fixed magnetic phase and structural claims survive an order-of-magnitude ignorance about the material. Five magnetostrictive phases (Terfenol-D, Galfenol, CoFe2O4, Ni, Metglas) and three piezoelectrics (PZT, BaTiO3 and LiNbO3 in four cuts) are compared across disk, bar and ring geometries and two electrode topologies. Fifteen of thirty-three headline claims are certified, two pairs certified indistinguishable, fourteen undecidable and two model-dependent: structural choices are settled by the evidence, rankings between materials are not. Blind validation on four published configurations, nothing calibrated, misses exactly the two devices with segmented electrodes, which the proper longitudinal-longitudinal circuit then contains. title: Statistical Model Checking of Ethical Autonomous System Under Uncertainty
abstract: Artificial intelligence-based systems are omnipresent in our daily lives. Thus, it is imperative automated systems perform decision-making ethical. The model abstraction for the evaluation of ethical decision-making of automated systems is limited because of limited data. Further, the model abstraction often do not account for environmental fluctuations during operation. In this work, we create a formalism based on internal discrete-time Markov chains to incorporate system uncertainty with integration of Deontic logic-based ethical rules. Statistical model checking is performed on a prototype to demonstrate computational feasibility and address epistemic uncertainty in the model. Experiments are conducted on a prototype of unmanned aerial vehicle on runaway using temporal logic queries and effectiveness of the results are discussed.

title: Impacts of national adaptation plans on water security under future climate uncertainty: system performance and internal dependency in the Seomjin River Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT Four-panel summary diagram showing: (top left) maps of national adaptation plan locations in the Seomjin River Basin, (top right) boxplots of changes in reliability, resilience, and vulnerability across four water-use sectors, (bottom left) choropleth maps of internal dependency under baseline and difference scenarios for each sector, and (bottom right) scatter plots of RRV metrics against internal dependency with LOWESS trend lines. Climate-induced hydrological variability poses increasing challenges to basin-scale water security, highlighting the need to evaluate the effectiveness of climate adaptation strategies under future uncertainty. This study assesses how national adaptation plans influence water security in the Seomjin River Basin using an integrated modelling framework that couples the Soil and Water Assessment Tool and the Water Evaluation and Planning system. Water security is evaluated through system performance indicators, including reliability, resilience, and vulnerability, together with an internal water dependency metric based on the water footprint concept. The results show that adaptation measures improve recovery capacity and reduce localized supply stress, particularly for domestic and industrial water uses. In contrast, agricultural water supply and instream flow remain largely governed by hydrological variability and show limited response to ad…

Time-Asymptotic Behavior of the Boltzmann Equation with Random Inputs in Whole Space and its Stochastic Galerkin Approximation
abstract: Abstract. We consider the Boltzmann equation with random uncertainties arising from the initial data and collision kernel in the whole space, along with its stochastic Galerkin (SG) approximations. By employing Green’s function method, we show that the higher-order derivatives of the solution with respect to the random variable exhibit polynomial decay over time. These results are then applied to analyze the SG method for the SG system and to demonstrate the polynomial decay of the numerical error over time.

title: RP: AeroGNN: A Multi-Fidelity Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network for Aerodynamic Design Optimization of Tall Buildings
abstract: Tall buildings are subject to unsteady wind-induced lateral forces that cause vortex-induced vibrations (VIVs), leading to structural fatigue and occupant discomfort. Nonetheless, exploring the large design spaces needed to identify optimal geometries with high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) or wind-tunnel testing is resource-intensive. This study presents AeroGNN, a physics-informed multi-fidelity graph neural network for rapid aerodynamic optimization of tall building designs. To enable wide design exploration, geometries are generated across a nine-dimensional parameter space defined by the Gielis superformula and three-dimensional modifications. These geometries are evaluated with OpenFOAM Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes simulations at coarse and fine fidelity levels. The model exploits the resulting inexpensive coarse-resolution data to learn the underlying flow physics, while fewer high-resolution simulations are used to refine the predictions. Aerodynamic force coefficients are predicted alongside the pressure and velocity fields, and these coefficients are combined into a scalar aerodynamic performance score. Relative to fine-resolution CFD, the framework accelerates design evaluation by a factor of 364. The final model achieved a cross-validated R-squared of 0.849 for the aerodynamic score. Coupled with differential evolution, the model identified a geom…

title: Vibration analysis and control of oil-free process screw compressor discharge piping system
abstract: While screw compressors are widely regarded as suitable for butadiene delivery due to their liquid-injection capability and precise temperature control, severe vibration in the discharge piping system has remained a key issue threatening the long-term safe operation of such units. This paper presents a systematic study on the abnormal vibration observed in the discharge pipe of a butadiene screw compressor, including mechanism analysis, numerical simulation, and vibration reduction optimization. Vibration testing and spectrum analysis first show that the dominant vibration frequency is 395 Hz, consistent with the second harmonic of the compressor operating frequency. Based on plane wave theory and vibration principles, the gas pulsation and modal characteristics of the piping system are analyzed. It is confirmed that the abnormal vibration originates from structural resonance triggered by gas pulsation. To address the poor attenuation performance of the original two-chamber impedance composite silencer at 395 Hz, an improved three-chamber silencer is proposed. Field application shows that the vibration displacement at the silencer is reduced to less than 27 μm. The horizontal vibration across the whole piping decreases by at least 30%, while vertical vibration falls by no less than 50%. The whole pipe now operates within a safe vibration range. This study systematically explain…

title: Gene Regulatory Networks that Support Multi-fate Cellular Decisions
abstract: Abstract Cell fate decisions are driven by gene regulatory networks (GRNs). While the mutually inhibitory toggle switch effectively models binary fate decisions, fully connected inhibitory networks with more than two nodes fail to capture multi-fate decisions due to the low prevalence of “single high states”, where only a single master regulator is highly expressed. The goal of this study is to find network structures that support all single high states. We find that the only network that attains the highest possible prevalence of all single high states within the set of monotone Boolean (MB) models is completely disconnected. Since biological networks typically require connectivity, we investigate network structures that support equipotency, where all single high states have equal prevalence within MB models. Finally, we characterize the networks that support multistability between all single high states, finding that it is possible only in networks in which each node either has self-activations or is inhibited by every other network node. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for understanding the network design principles that can support simultaneous differentiation into multiple distinct cell types.

title: Coaching and Talent Retention of Selected Tertiary Institutions in Abia State
abstract: The study investigated coaching and talent retention of selected tertiary institutions in Abia State. The specific objective is to determine the relationship between coaching and talent retention of tertiary institutions in Abia State. This study adopted a mixed-methods research design. The study adopted primary source of data to collect information from the respondent. The population of this study was seven thousand five hundred and seventy-four, (7574) obtained from the three selected tertiary institutions in Abia State. The sample size is 366 staff derived from Krejcie and Morgan (1970) formula. The study adopted a stratified sampling method. ANOVA model and Pearson correlation coefficient model test were employed to test the hypotheses of the study. Three hundred and sixty-six (366) copies of questionnaire was administered to academic staff of Abia State University, Aba, Michael Okpara University Umudike, and Ogbonnaya Onu University, however, twenty-nine (29) copies of questionnaire were lost while three hundred and thirty-seven (337) copies of questionnaire were retrieved from the respondents with 92.1% retrieved which formed basis of this study. The study found out that there is a positive significant relationship between coaching and talent retention of tertiary institutions in Abia State. The study concluded that institutions that invest systematically in their employe…

title: Dynamic Target Leverage and Speed of Adjustment: Evidence from Moroccan Agricultural SMEs
abstract: This study examines whether Moroccan agricultural small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) adjust their leverage toward a target capital structure and estimates the speed of adjustment. Drawing on the dynamic trade-off perspective and the partial-adjustment framework, this study uses a balanced panel of 54 Moroccan agricultural SMEs observed from 2017 to 2022, yielding 324 firm-year observations. The empirical analysis employs the Arellano–Bond Difference Generalized Method of Moments (GMMs) estimator to account for the dynamic nature of leverage and potential endogeneity. The results reveal significant leverage persistence, with the coefficient on lagged total leverage estimated at 0.6155 (p < 0.01). The implied annual speed of adjustment is 38.45%, suggesting that firms correct approximately 38% of the deviation between observed and target leverage over one year. The corresponding model-implied half-life is approximately 1.43 years. These findings provide evidence consistent with partial adjustment toward target leverage among Moroccan agricultural SMEs and offer insights into the dynamics of their financing decisions.

title: EFFECT OF TAX SAVINGS STRATEGIES ON THE FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF LISTED MANUFACTURING COMPANIES IN NIGERIA
abstract: This study investigated the effect of tax saving strategies on the financial performance of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria. An ex-post facto research design was adopted for the study. Data were obtained from secondary sources, specifically the annual reports of three selected listed manufacturing companies over a period of ten years, resulting in 30 observations. The variables used for the analysis included Return on Assets (ROA) as the dependent variable, while Effective Tax Rate (ETR), Debt-to-Equity Ratio (DER), and Capital Intensity (CI) served as the explanatory variables. The data were analysed using regression analysis with the aid of the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS). The findings revealed that Effective Tax Rate had no significant relationship with the return on assets of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria. In contrast, thin capitalisation showed a significant relationship with return on assets, while capital intensity was found to have no significant relationship with return on assets. Based on these findings, the study concluded that tax saving strategies can influence the financial performance of manufacturing firms, although the extent of such influence varies across the different tax-related measures considered. Accordingly, the study recommended that organisations should not rely solely on tax planning as a strategy for improvin…

title: Molecular Transmission Clustering and Pretreatment Drug Resistance Among Men Infected With HIV-1 Who Have Sex With Men in Baotou, China: A Cross-Sectional Subgroup Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background In the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, men who have sex with men (MSM) have become a high-risk group for HIV transmission due to their complex, secretive sexual relationships, posing challenges to HIV-1 prevention. Objective We analyzed factors associated with molecular transmission clustering and pretreatment drug resistance (PDR) among newly reported HIV-1–infected MSM in Baotou, China, and to provide locally relevant evidence for targeted public health interventions. Methods We conducted a subgroup cross-sectional molecular epidemiological analysis of all newly reported HIV-1 cases attributed to homosexual transmission in Baotou between January 2022 and December 2024. The sample comprised 213 treatment-naïve MSM, from whom plasma samples were obtained. A 1.3-kb fragment of the HIV-1 pol gene was amplified and sequenced using next-generation sequencing. Inclusion criteria were a newly reported HIV-1 infection, no antiretroviral therapy at the time of this writing, and self-reported same-sex sexual behavior. Primary outcomes were clustering in a genetic distance–based molecular transmission network and the presence of PDR according to the Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database. title: Syncope with right bundle branch block without left hemiblock: lower risk, but not benign.
Housing insecurity, displacement, and the right to adequate housing in the Gaza Strip: a mixed-methods study amid protracted conflict
abstract: Background: Housing insecurity is a critical humanitarian concern in conflict-affected settings, where home destruction, repeated displacement, overcrowding, and disrupted services affect health, dignity, and recovery. In the Gaza Strip, the war that began in October 2023 has intensified housing and shelter insecurity among displaced and war-affected households. This study examined the extent, patterns, correlates, and perceived consequences of housing insecurity. Methods A convergent mixed-methods design combined a household survey with semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were collected from 420 households across the five governorates of the Gaza Strip within the study period (2 April−4 August 2026). Qualitative data were obtained from 34 displaced household members and 10 key informants. Differences in severe housing insecurity, measured with a study-specific six-component index, were expressed as crude prevalence ratios, while qualitative data were thematically analyzed and integrated with the quantitative findings. Results Of the sampled households, 88.6% had been displaced at least once, and 33.6% of displaced households reported four or more displacement episodes. Complete home destruction was reported by 42.9% of households and severe damage by 28.3%. Current shelter conditions were frequently inadequate: 78.1% reported overcrowding, 72.6% lacked sufficient wat…

title: ROLE OF ELECTRONIC TAX INVOICE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS IN ENHANCING TAX COMPLIANCE AMONG SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN NAIROBI CITY COUNT, KENYA
abstract: Purpose of Study : This study examined the role of electronic tax invoice management systems in enhancing tax compliance among small and medium enterprises in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Specifically, it assessed the effects of electronic tax registers, enterprise resource planning integration, point-of-sale integration, and electronic tax return filing on tax compliance among SMEs. Methodology: The study adopted a descriptive research design targeting 33,701 registered SMEs in Nairobi Central Business District. A sample of 394 respondents was selected through stratified and simple random sampling techniques. Primary data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis in SPSS. Findings: The findings revealed that electronic tax invoice management systems positively and significantly influenced tax compliance among SMEs. Electronic tax registers (β=0.286, p<0.001), enterprise resource planning integration (β=0.241, p=0.001), point-of-sale integration (β=0.318, p<0.001), and electronic tax return filing (β=0.297, p<0.001) demonstrated significant positive effects on tax compliance. Point-of-sale integration exhibited the strongest influence, followed by electronic tax return filing, electronic tax registers, and enterprise resource planning integration. The regression model expl…
