title: The moderating role of money laundering risks according to corporate charter and by-laws: A study of services marketing and financial sustainability
abstract: This study examines the relationship between services marketing and financial sustainability, with money laundering risk as a moderator, integrating marketing and financial crime perspectives to explain how regulatory and risk conditions influence sustainable financial outcomes. A quantitative analysis of 432 organizational survey responses, with 429 valid cases after outlier filtering, assessed measurement reliability and validity through exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses (CFA). A structural equation model (SEM) tested hypothesized relationships among services marketing, financial sustainability, and money laundering risks, while moderation analysis examined interaction effects. The results show that services marketing significantly improves financial sustainability. The efficiency of services marketing in improving financial sustainability is weakened or conditioned by increasing levels of money laundering concerns, which considerably temper this relationship. The findings show good model fit, reliability, and construct validity, confirming the measurement and structural models’ robustness. Results suggest firms should integrate services marketing with anti-money laundering (AML), governance, and risk management to achieve financial sustainability. Policymakers should strengthen frameworks to support sustainable performance and protect investment returns. This stud…

title: Host plant species modulate whitefly‐mediated transmission of tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus and viral effects on vector performance
abstract: Abstract Background Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV) is an emerging bipartite Begomovirus primarily transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci , causing severe yield losses in cucurbit and solanaceous crops. Despite its rapid spread, the differential susceptibility of these crop families and the vector–virus–host interactions driving transmission disparities remain poorly characterized. Results Our field surveys revealed widespread ToLCNDV infection, with high prevalence in cucurbits although infection in solanaceous crops was much less frequent. Subsequent vector transmission experiments demonstrated that B . tabaci efficiently acquired ToLCNDV from infected melon, tomato and tobacco plants, and that transmission efficiency and viral accumulation were significantly higher in melon plants. Whitefly host adaptability ranked melon > tomato > tobacco, aligning positively with transmission efficiency. Notably, ToLCNDV infection exerted a graded mutualistic effect on whitefly fitness across different plants: survival and reproduction were significantly enhanced on the non‐adaptive host tobacco, reproduction was promoted on the moderately adaptive host tomato, and no significant fitness effects were observed on the highly adaptive host melon. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that differential ToLCNDV transmission on cucurbits versus solanaceous crops is collectively sh…

title: Acute Right Heart Failure Following Left Coronary Myocardial Infarction in Left Ventricular Assist Device–Supported Patients: A Case Series and Mechanistic Insight
abstract: Right heart failure (RHF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs). While right coronary artery infarction is a recognized cause of acute RHF, the ventricular consequences of left coronary system infarction in LVAD-supported patients are not well characterized. We describe two patients supported with HeartMate III LVADs who developed acute RHF within 24–48 hours after successful revascularization of acute left coronary system occlusions (mid-left anterior descending artery and left main coronary artery). Both had previously stable LVAD function and no evidence of advanced RHF. After revascularization, each developed hypotension, rising central venous pressure, reduced LVAD flows, and echocardiographic evidence of severe right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction with septal shift toward the left ventricle. Hemodynamic deterioration reversed with inotropic support, diuresis, and LVAD speed adjustment, without mechanical RV support. These cases suggest left coronary acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may precipitate acute RHF in LVAD-supported patients through septal ischemia with impaired ventricular interdependence, acute increases in RV afterload, and relative RV ischemia despite patent right coronary arteries. Heightened surveillance and early echocardiographic assessment after left-sided AMI in…

title: Toward cognitively informed instructional design
DECODE: Detecting Structural Obfuscation in HLS based DSP Designs using Machine Learning Framework
abstract: Structural obfuscation has been a widely used hardware security technique that is used to transform the internal structure of a high-level synthesis (HLS) digital signal processing (DSP) intellectual property (IP) design such that it becomes unobvious and obscure. The intent is to thwart deobfuscation/reverse-engineering (RE) attempts. These transformations in structurally obfuscated DSP designs are elusive and non-intuitive, making them arduous to identify and detect from an attacker's perspective. In this article, we for the first time, present a novel strategy for detecting structural obfuscation in HLS based DSP designs using machine learning (ML) frameworks. This article presents a novel technique called ‘DECODE’ : DE tecting Stru C tural O bfuscation in HLS based D SP Designs using Machine L E arning Framework . The presented approach introduces a set of unique/distinct features that can successfully classify between structurally obfuscated HLS DSP designs and its non-obfuscated versions. The article also presents a novel ML database consisting of several instances of structurally obfuscated and un-obfuscated DSP HLS designs that can be fed into our ML framework (logistic regression and random forest classifier). Results of the proposed approach revealed successful detection of structurally obfuscated DSP designs with high accuracy.

Crystal Structure and Enhanced Physicochemical Properties of a Famotidine−Saccharin Salt
abstract: Abstract A hydrated salt crystal comprising famotidine (FMT) and saccharin (SAC) was synthesized via liquid-assisted grinding and solvent evaporation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction results revealed that the FMT−SAC salt crystallized in the triclinic space group P-1, comprising an FMT cation, SAC anion, and water molecule in each asymmetric unit. The structure features a distinct layered packing motif, stabilized by a hydrogen bonding network with R22(8), R22(10), and R44(34) motifs, while water molecules function as bridges. FMT−SAC exhibited significantly improved physicochemical properties with 5- and 9-fold higher aqueous solubility and intrinsic dissolution rates, respectively, than pure FMT. Tableting performance of FMT−SAC was remarkably enhanced. Moreover, the FMT−SAC tablet prevented capping under strong compaction forces. These improvements were attributed to the exposure of a hydrophilic surface of the salt with low attachment energy and a slip plane owing to the presence of lattice water molecules. This study establishes a structure−property relation, highlighting the utility of salt formation and hydrate engineering for enhancing the solubility and mechanical performance of poorly compressible drugs.

title: Design and Implementation of a Regional Culinary Community Platform with AI-Assisted Question Answering: A Case Study of Xunwei Zhanjiang
abstract: Digital platforms for regional culinary culture need to connect information about local dishes and places with community participation and accessible exploration services. This study presents the design and implementation of Xunwei Zhanjiang, a community-oriented web platform that integrates regional food discovery, user interaction, and AI-assisted culinary enquiry. Built with Next.js, React, Drizzle ORM, and MySQL, the platform organizes culinary information through district-based displays and structured food cards, alongside community features for sharing posts, commenting, bookmarking, and following users. A server-side integration with Dify enables natural-language enquiries about local cuisine and suggested food itineraries. The system incorporates standardized API responses, input validation, cookie-based authentication, and database uniqueness constraints to support consistent interactions and prevent duplicate social relationships. Preliminary functional checks confirmed successful operation of selected content retrieval endpoints, user login and profile retrieval, access restrictions, and the integrated AI enquiry interface. These observations support the feasibility of bringing structured culinary content, community interaction, and conversational assistance together within a regional web application. However, they do not establish improvements in recommendation qual…

title: Distributionally Robust Bidding Strategy for Co-Located and Integrated Wind–PV–Storage Hybrid Resources in Day-Ahead and Real-Time Electricity Markets
abstract: With the growing demand for flexibility in emerging power systems, hybrid-resources characterized by the coordinated deployment of renewable generation and energy storage have become an increasingly important form of renewable-energy development and market participation. However, in a day-ahead–real-time dual-settlement electricity market, uncertainties in wind and photovoltaic (PV) generation not only affect day-ahead bidding revenues but also influence revenue realization through real-time deviation settlement and energy-storage dispatch. Focusing on price-taking hybrid resource operators, this paper compares two representative market participation models: co-located hybrid resources (CHRs) and integrated hybrid resources (IHRs). Separate two-stage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) models are developed for the two configurations. In the first stage, day-ahead bidding schedules are determined based on wind and PV generation forecasts. In the second stage, real-time recourse decisions and energy-storage dispatch are implemented according to the actual available renewable output, thereby coordinating day-ahead revenues, real-time deviation revenues, and deviation-penalty risks. An initial set of representative scenarios is constructed using Latin hypercube sampling combined with a Wasserstein-distance-based scenario reduction method. A scenario-probability confidence se…

title: Predictive Electricity Price Forecasting for Generative AI: Anticipating Future Energy Costs for Proactive Computational Scheduling
abstract: The increasing computational requirements of generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems have made electricity expenditure an increasingly important component of inference infrastructure management. Large language model (LLM) inference, proactive response preparation, model loading, speculative computation, and other GPU-intensive operations may be performed across different time periods, during which electricity prices can vary substantially. Although existing economic-aware predictive computing approaches consider dynamic electricity pricing when selecting computational execution periods, incorporating electricity prices into scheduling decisions is not equivalent to predicting future electricity prices with sufficient temporal and probabilistic accuracy. Without explicit forecasting of future energy costs, computational schedulers may rely on historical averages, currently observed prices, or externally supplied pricing information, potentially overlooking future price fluctuations and the opportunities they create for advance computational preparation. This paper introduces Predictive Electricity Price Forecasting for Generative AI (PEPF-GAI), a specialized framework that investigates the prediction of future electricity prices and their integration into proactive computational scheduling. Unlike conventional price-aware scheduling, which primarily evaluates the cost of…

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Degradation-Aware and Coordinated Control of Virtual Power Plants
abstract: Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) coordinate distributed energy resources (DERs) under forecast uncertainty and multi-time-scale constraints, while battery and generator wear can erase short-term trading gains. This paper proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) controller that matches aggregator practice: a slow-time-scale manager issues location-level power subgoals together with a continuous autonomy signal, and fast-time-scale workers dispatch devices under local physics. Battery and generator degradation enter the training reward through a three-phase curriculum that activates a throughput-budget penalty and a cycle-depth surcharge, so the policy optimizes profit net of wear rather than arbitrage alone. On a 100-day shared-seed benchmark against two decentralized RL controllers, an open-loop stochastic mixed-integer programming (MIP) day-ahead optimizer, and a closed-loop model predictive control (MPC) baseline that reoptimizes hourly over an 8-h horizon, HRL attains an average daily profit of \$50,264─3.1× MPC and 4.0× MIP─at 50–170 ms per simulated day. HRL is the only method whose throughput-to-cycle-depth ratio exceeds unity (1.18), and it incurs only \$24.6 of cycle-depth-aware wear per \$1,000 of profit (2.5× better than MPC). These results indicate that degradation-aware hierarchical control can outperform both open-loop stochastic optimization and receding-ho…

title: Development of a Vibrio natriegens -Based Plate-Clearing Assay for Rapid Screening of PET-Hydrolyzing Enzymes
abstract: Abstract Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a major contributor to plastic waste. Enzymatic PET degradation offers a sustainable recycling approach, but screening for effective enzymes remains challenging. Herein, we established an experimental plate-clearing assay using Vibrio natriegens, exploiting its protein secretion system to rapidly identify catalytic activity without time-consuming downstream processing. To validate the assay’s robustness, we tested variants of Fusarium solanipisi cutinase (FsC) and found that one variant, T45P, exhibited 3-fold higher PET-film degradation yield than the wild type and favored the production of terephthalic acid. As a further test case, we screened an error-prone polymerase chain reaction (PCR) library of FsC using the assay, obtaining a 25% hit rate after screening 150 colonies. This demonstrates the scalability of the method to large enzyme libraries.

title: Response to discussion: Sensitivity analysis of post-disturbance roll stability for a high-speed planning craft
Trust gained, trust lost: how service robot anthropomorphism shapes consumer trust in tight and loose cultures
abstract: Purpose This paper aimed to examine the dual pathways through which service-robot (SR) anthropomorphism shapes consumer trust in service robots (CTSR), specifically the positive serial mediating effect of perceived warmth (WA) and perceived competence (CO) and the negative serial mediating effect of perceived identity threat (TH) and discomfort (DI). It further explored cross-cultural differences in consumer attitudes and their underlying reasons from the perspective of cultural tightness-looseness. Design/methodology/approach Five scenario experiments were conducted across three sets of SR picture stimuli, two service settings (hotel and hospital) and two cultures (China and the United States). Findings Both study 1 and study 2 found that anthropomorphism had a double-edged sword effect on CTSR across different sets of SR picture stimuli, service settings and cultures. An exploratory analysis in study 1 further revealed that among Chinese consumers, CTSR and its antecedents did not show significant differences across different service settings. Study 2 results further indicated that Chinese (versus. American) consumers had higher WA, CO and CTSR, along with lower TH and DI and that region-level cultural tightness influenced CTSR and its antecedents, potentially explaining these cross-cultural differences. Practical implications For hospitality managers, this paper offers insig…

title: Housing insecurity and cancer in South Australia: artificial intelligence-enabled insights from a statewide cancer support service
abstract: Objective This study demonstrates the use of a locally hosted, offline artificial intelligence approach to identify, quantify, and describe housing-related needs documented in routine case notes from a statewide cancer support service. Methods In this retrospective, exploratory service evaluation, a locally hosted, offline large language model screened 25,031 staff-generated case notes recorded between December 2020 and December 2025 for housing-related interactions and grouped confirmed interactions into categories based on a predefined framework. Flagged records and categorisation were independently verified by at least two reviewers, and confirmed interactions were summarised descriptively. Results Of 25,031 interactions, 308 (1.23%) were confirmed as housing-related interactions. The most prominent categorisations were lack of support from health and social services (44.16%), financial barriers to housing stability (37.66%), and homelessness or reliance on emergency or crisis housing (36.04%). In more than half of confirmed interactions, housing was not the initial reason for contact and emerged only during discussion. Conclusions Findings highlight the utility of a privacy-preserving artificial intelligence approach to identify, quantify, and describe community needs at the intersection of housing and cancer care within large-scale, routinely collected service data. title: Spatially Programmed Water Access Reconciles Service Stability with Triggered Post-Use Degradation in Biobased Multilayer
abstract: Abstract Sustainable packaging plastics often face a fundamental paradox: the material must resist moisture and remain stable during service, yet undergo controlled disassembly after disposal. Therefore, sustainable materials should not be evaluated solely based on their service performance or degradation rate, but rather on their ability to undergo effective functional transitions at critical stages throughout the lifecycle. Here, we developed a spatially programmed design strategy that addresses these conflicting requirements by regulating not only when and where water enters the material, but also how the degradation proceeds. The film consists of a hydrophilic, pectin-based inner layer, a hydrophobic polylactic acid (PLA) outer layer, and a hydrogen-bonded interface formed via hydrogen bonding. During packaging service, the PLA layer acts as a moisture-shielding skin, maintaining wet stability, barrier performance, and mechanical integrity. A key conceptual advance of this work lies in turning an inherent weakness into a lifecycle-regulating function, where water sensitivity serves as a trigger rather than a limitation. After use, assisted by mechanical damage, water activates the pectin/deep eutectic solvent (DES) phase. The acidic, water-rich microenvironment generated by the pectin/DES supports preferential cleavage near the PLA chain ends, promoting progressive molecula…

title: Integrated Marketing Communication for Trust Building: Wuling Motors in Indonesia's Automotive Market
abstract: This study examines how Wuling Motors employs integrated marketing communication (IMC) to build consumer trust and strengthen its market presence in Indonesia's automotive industry despite the long-standing dominance of Japanese brands. A qualitative case study approach was employed using purposive sampling, in-depth interviews, and thematic analysis. The findings reveal that Wuling's market penetration was achieved through trust-building strategies integrating local legitimacy, consumer experience, and adaptive marketing communication. This study contributes to the existing literature on integrated marketing communication, market penetration, and country-of-origin effects by explaining how IMC strategically reconstructs consumer trust and brand legitimacy for an emerging Chinese automotive brand in a market dominated by established Japanese manufacturers. The findings suggest that managers should prioritize integrated marketing communication to build consumer trust and strengthen market penetration, while policymakers should promote policies that support fair competition and innovation in the automotive industry

title: Public service crisis caused by the influx of Ukrainian refugees from the perspective of the job demands resources model
abstract: Purpose This study examines the well-being of public servants by utilizing the Job Demands-Resources model during a crisis, contributing to research on human resources management in public institutions. Design/methodology/approach The research investigates the potential moderating roles of Public Service Motivation (PSM) and resilience relative to demanding jobs, available resources, and adverse outcomes in an unprecedented scenario-a situation of adversity. The survey was conducted among civil servants directly involved in serving refugees in main provincial offices that had established crisis centers for Ukrainian refugees in Poland between March and May 2023, when demand for work permits rose due to the protracted war. A total of 138 complete responses were collected. The regression models were supplemented using Johnson's Relative Weight Analysis (RWA). Findings Results indicated that respondents faced heightened job demands and limited job resources, leading to significant stress and extended fatigue; however, the anticipated moderating effects of PSM and resilience were not evident. Originality/value The research advances management scholarship by identifying factors that shape mental health and performance measures in public-sector employees operating in extreme conditions. It offers empirical insights into how crisis-induced workloads challenge human resource management…

Intelligent service systems and value co-creation in hotel frontlines
abstract: Purpose Drawing on service-dominant logic, this study examines how mechanical- and feeling-intelligent service systems contribute to value co-creation through distinct customer-engagement pathways and how these effects change over time and following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Design/methodology/approach Using a large-scale dataset of hotel information and online reviews, we conduct text mining to measure key variables and regression analyses to examine the proposed relationships and their changes over time and following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Findings The results show that mechanical-intelligent service systems contribute to co-created value through functional engagement, whereas feeling-intelligent service systems contribute through emotional and social engagement. Additionally, value co-creation driven by both types of intelligent service systems strengthens over time, with a notable surge observed following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Originality/value This study advances understanding of how intelligent service systems participate in frontline value co-creation in hospitality and provides practical guidance for service firms seeking to deploy such systems strategically in service frontlines.

title: Effect of income trajectory on dental service utilization patterns during the transition from childhood to adolescence: a 10-year cohort study
abstract: Abstract Objectives This study aimed to investigate the influence of income trajectories on dental service utilization patterns during the transition from childhood to adolescence in a Southern Brazilian birth cohort. Materials and methods Children were followed over 13 years (T1, T2, and T3). Income trajectories (stable low/decreasing vs. stable high/increasing) were identified using group-based trajectory modeling based on finite mixture models. Outcomes included frequency of dental visits and reason for the last visit (preventive vs. curative). Socioeconomic disparities were explored using the non-linear Blinder–Oaxaca decomposition method. Results From 639 children at baseline (T1), 449 were followed at T2 and 429 at T3 (67.1% retention). Adolescents from stable high or increasing-income trajectories had a lower prevalence of dental visits for curative reasons (OR = 0.29; 95% CI 0.09–0.90). Decomposition analysis showed that maternal education (9%) and skin color (12.5%) explained only a small portion of these inequalities, suggesting an independent effect of income over time. Conclusions Individuals with increasing income were less likely to use dental services for curative purposes, regardless of race, dental caries, and maternal education, highlighting the impact of economic stability on oral health behaviors. Clinical relevance Income trajectories over time influence th…

title: Pembuktian Digital dan Pertanggungjawaban Pidana Pelaku Penjualan Akun Streaming Premium Ilegal: Perspektif Hak Cipta serta Batasnya terhadap Terms of Service dan UU ITE
abstract: The rise of subscription-based streaming services has been accompanied by the unofficial sale of premium accounts through social media and digital marketplaces in Indonesia. Although such practices are commonly labelled illegal, the label does not automatically establish criminal liability. This study addresses two issues: first, how difficulties in digital evidence and offender anonymity constrain criminal enforcement, and the standing of electronic evidence in linking offenders, accounts, transactions, and copyright-related objects; second, how criminal liability of sellers of illegal premium streaming accounts is constructed under the Copyright Law, and where its limits lie in relation to Terms of Service violations and offences under the Electronic Information and Transactions Law. Using normative legal research with statutory and conceptual approaches, the study analyses primary legal materials and secondary literature through descriptive-analytical qualitative analysis. The findings show that digital infringement leaves no physical trace, so proof depends on authentic, intact, and relevant electronic evidence supported by digital forensics. Criminal liability under the Copyright Law arises only when the act is committed without right or permission, relates to economic rights over protected works, including computer programs, is carried out for commercial use, involves fau…

title: Consumer acceptance and market viability of artisanal granadilla wine in Puno, Peru: a concept test using the marketing mix and purchasing behavior approach
abstract: Background Fruit wines from non-traditional sources offer opportunities to add value to underutilized agricultural resources and generate economic alternatives in regional contexts. In the Puno region of Peru, granadilla ( Passiflora ligularis ) production faces limited profitability due to lack of processing infrastructure and commercial channels. Objective This study analyzes consumer acceptance and market viability of DIVINO artisanal granadilla wine in Puno, Peru, using the marketing mix framework to understand how product, price, place, and promotion elements influence purchasing behavior. Method A concept test was conducted with 50 potential consumers in Puno. Data were collected using a structured 24-item questionnaire measuring marketing mix perceptions and purchasing behavior on a five-point Likert scale. Analysis included descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, and exploratory multiple linear regression. Results Results show favorable product concept perception: availability via WhatsApp and social media reached 83.0% acceptance; personal recommendations, 81.6%; and price of S/27.00 (approximately 8.00 USD), 78.7%. Correlational analysis revealed a significant relationship between Marketing Mix Strategies and Purchasing Behavior (Rho = 0.834, p < 0.01), with Product (Rho = 0.844) and Promotion (Rho = 0.745) dimensions exerting the greatest influence. In thi…

title: Revisiting the efficient market hypothesis for ten sub-sectors of the Istanbul Stock Exchange (BIST): new evidence from non-linear unit root tests with Fourier function
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine the efficient market hypothesis (EMH) for ten sub-sector indices in BIST (Istanbul Stock Exchange) including Services Index (XUHIZ), Food Index (XGIDA), Holding Index (XHOLD), Chemicals Index (XKMYA), Metals Index (XMANA), Technology Index (XUTEK), Banks Index (XBANK), Financials Index (XUMAL), Industrial Index (XUSIN). Design/methodology/approach To analyse the EMH for ten subsector indices in BIST, the ADF, Fourier KPSS (FKPSS) (2006), Fourier ADF (FADF) (2010), KSS (2003), Fourier KSS (FKSS) (2010), Sollis (2009), Omay (2015), Fourier Sollis (FSOLLIS) (2018), Kruse (2011), Fourier Kruse (FKRUSE) (2019) unit root tests are applied. Findings The results of the Fourier KPSS (2006) stationarity test confirm that the EMH is not valid for the variables XMANA, XUTEK, XBANK and XUMAL. Furthermore, the results of the KSS (2003), Sollis (2009), Fourier Sollis (2018), Kruse (2009) and Fourier Kruse (2019) unit root tests also revealed that the EMH is not valid for the variable XMANA. Finally, the results of the Fourier-Sollis (2018) and Fourier-Kruse (2019) unit root tests imply that the EMH is not valid for the variables XKMYA and XBANK. Originality/value This study is a comparison of the results of traditional unit root tests without structural breaks and linear with the results of current unit root tests with structural breaks and non-…

title: Overview of food service hygiene and sanitation at islamic boarding schools in Tasikmalaya
abstract: Food service management in Islamic boarding schools (pondok pesantren) plays a crucial role in supporting the nutritional status and health of students; however, suboptimal hygiene and sanitation practices may increase the risk of foodborne disease. This study aimed to describe the hygiene and sanitation of food service management in two Islamic boarding schools in Tasikmalaya in 2025. The study employed a descriptive qualitative design using observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation. Informants consisted of eight food handlers and two nutritionists. Data were analyzed through editing, coding, classifying, verifying, and concluding stages. Results showed that food handler hygiene practices met the standards at 81% in Boarding School A and 91% in Boarding School B. Kitchen sanitation facilities met the standards at 86% in both schools. Location and building conditions met the standards at 75% in Boarding School A and 92% in Boarding School B. The application of the six principles of food hygiene and sanitation met the standards at 78% in Boarding School A and 92% in Boarding School B. Main deficiencies were found in the use of light-colored clothing, gloves, kitchen door design, waste separation, and food storage. It is concluded that hygiene and sanitation practices in both boarding schools largely met the standards, yet improvements are still needed in personal hygie…

title: The symbolic divide: how human and robotic service rituals shape perception of brand symbolism
abstract: Purpose The rapid adoption of service robots in tourism and hospitality raises questions about their ability to generate brand-related meaning compared to human-led service rituals. Drawing on interaction ritual theory, this study aims to examine how human and robotic service rituals influence perception of brand symbolism through emotional energy and memory and how these effects differ for customers with varying levels of social phobia. Design/methodology/approach Using a multistudy design, this research uses five experiments across airports, hotels and restaurants to test the hypotheses. The inclusion of both Asian and Western respondents across varying service contexts provides preliminary evidence regarding the generalizability of the findings. Findings Human-led service rituals create a stronger perception of brand symbolism than robot-led rituals, with emotional energy and memory as sequential mediators. For high-social-phobia customers, perception of brand symbolism did not differ significantly between the two ritual types, although human-led rituals generated higher emotional energy; for low-social-phobia customers, human-led rituals produced greater perception of brand symbolism and higher emotional energy. Originality/value This study contrasts human and robotic service rituals, identifies sequential mechanisms (emotional energy and memory) and extends interaction rit…

title: Regulatory governance, digital payment systems and tourism service delivery: a comparative study of Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how different regulatory governance configurations are associated with the functionality of digital payment systems, providing valuable insights for tourism and hospitality service performance. It aims to fill the gap regarding the role of financial regulation in building digital service interactions within tourism contexts. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative comparative policy analysis was conducted across three Southeast Asian countries, including Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. These cases represent innovation-facilitating, controlled and precautionary regulatory models. The analysis is grounded in the proposed Regulatory–Payment–Service Interaction Framework, focusing on three key dimensions, transaction flexibility, cross-border interoperability and user trust and compliance assurance. Findings The results suggest that different regulatory configurations are associated with variations in the functionality of digital payment systems. In particular, innovation-facilitating frameworks are associated with higher transaction flexibility and cross-border interoperability. Controlled models foster widespread adoption under structured conditions, while precautionary approaches lean toward stability but limit cross-border integration. These differences reflect service efficiency, accessibility and customer experience in tourism and hospita…

title: Reused over Refurbished: Exploring Smartphone Life Extension in Thailand’s Informal Market
abstract: The rapid turnover of smartphones has created a growing electric waste challenge globally, particularly in emerging economies where formal recycling infrastructure remains limited. Circular economy strategies, such as reuse and refurbishment, offer potential pathways to extend smartphone lifespans, yet consumer preferences and market structures strongly shape their adoption. This study explores the dynamics of smartphone life extension in Thailand’s informal economy, focusing on Bangkok’s second-hand smartphone market. Data were collected through structured interviews with 110 kiosk operators in Bangkok, complemented by stakeholder insights from recyclers and used-phone providers. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted to examine business pathways, purchasing behavior, and factors influencing smartphone life extension. The findings demonstrated that reuse, rather than refurbishment, constitutes the dominant life-extension pathway. Most kiosks preferred smartphones that could be resold with minimal repair, while warranty provision emerged as the strongest enabling factor supporting consumer trust. Inferential analyses showed that prolonged smartphone circulation was significantly associated with product value, reflected in brand and price, whereas external condition and technical functionality were not significantly associated with smartphone age. The Issue of Legal Regulation of the Increase of a Joint-Stock Company’s Authorized Capital by the Amount of Subsidies Received for Capital Investments in Capital Construction Projects
abstract: The paper considers the problem of increasing the authorized capital of a joint-stock company, 100% of which is owned by the state, by the amount of a subsidy received for the purpose of capital investments in capital construction facilities. The problem of increasing the authorized capital at the expense of property (own funds) is characterized, when the latter is understood as components of equity in the sense of accounting, for example, additional capital. It is determined that the budget subsidy has a dual nature: "earmarked budget funding" and "contribution to property", and therefore, for accounting purposes, it is proposed to qualify it as additional capital as part of the organization's own funds.

title: Emergent Roles of RVLMC1 Neurons in Cardiovascular Homeostasis and Systemic Physiological Regulation
abstract: Abstract Purpose of the Review Adrenergic C1 neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM C1 ) have long been recognized for their role in regulating sympathetic activity and arterial blood pressure (BP). However, novel approaches such as genetic targeting, optogenetics, fiber photometry, among others, allowed us to study the biology of these neurons in deeper detail and in non-anesthetized preparations, unraveling previously underappreciated or unrecognized functions. Here we will discuss recent studies that explored the function of RVLM C1 neurons for the sympathetic regulation of BP and also the emergent roles of these cells for other processes involved in systemic physiological regulation. Recent Findings Using selective methods of manipulation and recording of neuronal activity in conscious animals, it was demonstrated that RVLM C1 neurons play a critical role in BP stability across multiple behaviors, including sleep-wake state and postural changes. Besides cardiovascular control, recent evidence shows that these neurons play a critical role in different homeostatic functions such as thermoregulation, immune response, glycemia and in complex behaviors such as anxiety. Summary RVLM C1 neurons are a key hub that integrates interoceptive signals from peripheral systems to regulate BP and other basic physiological functions. Along with their role in cardiovascular regul…

title: Psilocybin modulates nucleus accumbens activity via astrocytic transcriptional regulation
abstract: Abstract Psilocybin is a serotonergic hallucinogen that acts primarily through 5-HT₂A receptor signaling, yet the mechanisms by which it regulates mesolimbic inhibitory tone remain poorly understood. Here we investigated how psilocybin and structurally related synthetic tryptamines modulate inhibitory signaling in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and whether astrocyte-associated mechanisms contribute to this process. Psilocybin-like tryptamines that generalized to the psilocybin cue increased NAc neuronal activity while reducing extracellular GABA levels, identifying diminished NAc GABAergic tone as a neurochemical correlate of psilocybin-like behavioral responses. Consistent with this interpretation, local pharmacological modulation of NAc GABA receptor signaling altered psilocybin-appropriate responding. We next examined the cellular and molecular basis of this GABAergic regulation. Ex vivo whole-cell recordings revealed that psilocin, the active metabolite of psilocybin, reduced tonic GABA current in NAc medium spiny neurons without affecting miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents, indicating preferential modulation of tonic rather than miniature synaptic inhibition. Cell-type-specific analyses further showed that psilocybin selectively reduced intracellular GABA levels in astrocytes, but not neurons. Psilocybin increased astrocytic NFATc4 and ALDH5A1 protein expression toget…

title: Am I Dependent in Order to Be Perfect? A Serial Mediation Model Linking Academic Perfectionism to AI Dependency Through the Impostor Phenomenon, Writing Anxiety, Self-Regulation, and Academic Procrastination

title: From Digital Attendance to Discipline Transformation: An Empirical Study of Behavioral Visibility, Moral Surveillance, and Religious Self-Regulation
abstract: Digital transformation in education is advancing rapidly, yet empirical understanding of how technology contributes to student discipline development in Islamic education remains relatively limited. This study aims to examine the relationship between the QR-Code Attendance System, Behavioral Visibility, Parental Digital Engagement, Digital Moral Surveillance, Religious Self-Regulation, and Student Discipline Transformation. The study used a quantitative explanatory survey design involving 436 madrasah students who have used a QR-code-based attendance system. Analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares. The results indicate that the QR-Code Attendance System increases Behavioral Visibility, which in turn strengthens Parental Digital Engagement. Parental Digital Engagement is positively associated with Digital Moral Surveillance, which fosters the development of Religious Self-Regulation. Religious Self-Regulation, in turn, contributes to Student Discipline Transformation. All mediation pathways showed strong significance, including full serial mediation from the digital attendance system to student discipline transformation. These findings expand our understanding of the relationships among digital educational governance, family engagement, moral surveillance, and religious character formation, and highlight the importance of integrating techn…

title: Legal Regulation of the Principles of Bioethics and Biolaw in India
abstract: The author provides the analysis of the evolution of the regulation of biolaw and bioethics in India in 1985–2025 (as of early 2026) in the context of socially significant cases of ethical violations (organ trade, abuses in clinical trials, commercial surrogacy), and assessment of the impact of adopted changes on further regulation. Legal regulation of bioethics and biolaw in India has developed in a predominantly reactive manner – in response to practical crises, unlike the directive model of planned codification characteristic of the European Union. The historical core of the system combined the judicial constitutional doctrine of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and delegated regulation by specialized agencies, supplemented since 2021 by parliamentary sectoral legislation; a unified bioethics law remains absent. The research results may be used in Russian doctrine of biolaw and medical law in developing models of comprehensive regulation of bioethical relations.

title: Molecular Insights into Gene Expression Changes in Apoptosis Immune Response and Cellular Regulation Pathways in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients
Composition, frequency, and severity of future rain-on-snow floods in Germany
abstract: In Germany, severe widespread winter floods are often generated by rain-on-snow (ROS) phenomena. Under suitable conditions, when rain falls on the snow cover, the snow can melt and produce extreme amounts of runoff. In a warming climate, the frequency of ROS events is expected to change locally depending on elevation and regionally based on the general climate conditions. Consequently, the characteristics of ROS-driven winter floods are also anticipated to change. To investigate these changes, streamflow for multiple gauge stations in Germany was simulated using an ensemble of Long Short-Term Memory models based on an ensemble of downscaled climate projections. Germany, as a representative mid-latitude country with a considerable portion of historical floods generated by ROS, offers extensive spatial and temporal coverage of hydrological observations spanning long temporal scales, and hence warranting efficient training of the deep learning model. We used an explainable artificial intelligence method, integrated gradients, to examine flood-generating processes, focusing primarily on ROS, for every simulated flood peak. Changes in frequency, feature importance, and a ranking based severity of ROS flood events were assessed for individual streamflow gauges and for widespread floods affecting multiple catchments across four major river basins in Germany. We found that with regard …
venue: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF PRESIDENTIAL REGULATION NUMBER 32 OF 2024 ARTICLE 7 ON THE COOPERATION BETWEEN DIGITAL PLATFORMS AND PRESS COMPANIES
abstract: Background. Digital platforms such as Google and Facebook now control the dissemination and visibility of news, leaving small and independent publishers economically dependent on them and earning revenue that does not reflect the true value of their content. Indonesia has responded by introducing Publisher Rights through Presidential Regulation No. 32 of 2024, which is grounded in Copyright Law No. 28 of 2014. Research Purpose. This study aims to analyze Google’s approval mechanisms and policies in managing and distributing PorosJakarta.com news content, and to examine how the regulation protects the economic rights of online news publishers, including the challenges of its implementation. Research Method. This qualitative empirical juridical study collected primary data through in-depth interviews with two informants selected through purposive sampling: the Head of Creator Management at PorosJakarta.com and the Chair of the Publisher Rights Committee (KTP2JB), chosen for their positions and direct involvement in news content distribution and Publisher Rights implementation. Secondary data came from legislation, academic literature, official reports, and institutional documents on Publisher Rights. Findings. Google’s control over content visibility limits publisher oversight and reduces potential revenue. Small publishers still have difficulty accessing royalties because they d…

title: Posthumous Reproduction in Russia: Debatable Aspects of Legal Regulation and Law Enforcement
abstract: Based on an analysis of judicial practice and domestic and international theoretical approaches, this article examines controversial issues of postmortem reproduction in the Russian Federation: subjects eligible for this procedure, ethical and legal issues of establishing written consent during one’s lifetime for reproduction during infertility treatment, and the absence of such consent (implied consent) in cases of postmortem biomaterial collection.

title: The Relationship between Need for Cognition and Chemistry Learning Interest among Senior High School Students: A Chain Mediation Model of Chemistry Self-Efficacy and Self-Regulation
abstract: Abstract Chemistry learning interest plays a crucial role in sustaining students’ engagement with chemistry and supporting their long-term development in science learning. Need for cognition is regarded as an important intellectual investment trait that may be associated with students’ willingness to engage in effortful thinking and complex problem solving. Although previous studies have provided evidence for the association between need for cognition and academic interest, the psychological mechanisms underlying this relationship in the context of chemistry education remain insufficiently examined. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the multiple mediating pathways involving chemistry self-efficacy and self-regulation in the relationship between need for cognition and chemistry learning interest. A multiple-mediation model was constructed by drawing on intellectual investment theory and social cognitive theory, with Social Cognitive Career Theory specifically informing the self-efficacy–interest pathway and research on interest development informing the conceptualization of interest. Data were collected from grade 10 students in China (N = 3,431) using scales to measure need for cognition, chemistry learning interest, chemistry self-efficacy, and self-regulation. The results indicated that (1) need for cognition was significantly and positively associated with students’ …

title: Conflicts of Law in the Regulation of State Duties in Summary Proceedings When Applying Tax Benefits
abstract: The article discusses a conflict in Russian law concerning the payment of state duty in writ proceedings before courts of general jurisdiction. The focus is on claims for alimony and unpaid wages, where the law provides both general rules on court fees and special tax benefits. The author shows that these rules may contradict each other in practice, creating uncertainty for courts and claimants. The article examines this issue through alimony and labor disputes, reviews relevant court positions, and suggests ways to make the legislation more consistent.

title: Legal Regulation of the Inclusion of Royalties in the Customs Value of Goods
abstract: The work is devoted to topical issues of legal regulation of the inclusion of royalties in the customs value of goods. The authors conducted a detailed analysis of the regulatory framework of the EAEU and the Russian Federation governing such issues. Criteria have been established according to which a decision is made to include royalties in such a cost of goods. The authors pays special attention to the analysis of the regulatory framework for determining the customs value when importing raw materials. Based on the analysis, contradictions of the current legislation regarding the inclusion of royalties in the customs value were revealed. It has been established that in the current legislation there are legal conflicts associated with such a definition of customs value.

title: Salud intercultural en Pastaza: regulación del uso de plantas medicinales y de la ayahuasca
abstract: Las plantas medicinales y la ayahuasca forman parte de la medicina ancestral amazónica, pero su uso fuera del contexto comunitario plantea riesgos para la salud y dudas sobre su regulación. El artículo analizó el marco jurídico y la evidencia científica sobre el uso de plantas medicinales y de ayahuasca en Pastaza, desde la salud intercultural. Se realizó una revisión documental de normas, instrumentos internacionales y literatura arbitrada etnobotánica, farmacológica y clínica. El análisis, organizado en tres ejes, mostró que el reconocimiento constitucional de la medicina ancestral no se acompaña de criterios específicos de seguridad, dosificación ni protección del conocimiento, y que los riesgos de la ayahuasca derivan de su uso descontextualizado. Se concluye que se requiere una regulación intercultural, elaborada con los sabios y las comunidades. No se recogieron datos primarios.
venue: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales

title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma
abstract: Purpose Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression. Methods RNA-sequencing and clinical data from 80 UM patients were obtained from TCGA. Thirty highly connected hypoxia-related genes were prioritized through protein-protein interaction analysis and evaluated using five complementary survival-based machine learning approaches: LASSO-Cox, CoxBoost, random survival forest, XGBoost-Cox, and Survival-SVM. Genes supported by at least three of the five methods were defined as core candidates and further evaluated by multivariable Cox regression to construct the prognostic model. The prognostic relevance of the model was evaluated in the dependent GSE22138 cohort using metastasis-free survival (MFS) as the clinical endpoint. Survival analysis, ROC, PCA, GSEA, and immune microenvironment analyses were performed. PFKP was further examined for its associations with immune features and experimentally validated through in vitro and in vivo assays. Results Multi-algorithm consensus identified PFKP, ENO3, and FOXO3 as core candidate genes. PFKP showed the stro…

title: Fabrication, characterization, and reliability analysis of 3D printed high frequency, wideband, and flexible carbon-nanotube and graphene-oxide based rectangular patch antennas deployable on curvilinear and deformable surfaces
abstract: In this paper, we extensively report the additive fabrication and characterization of carbon-nanotube and graphene oxide-based 3D printed rectangular patch antennas that can be integrated on curvilinear and deformable surfaces. Our fabricated antennas can be as thin as few microns and demonstrate reflection coefficient ( S 11 ) values that confirm their super-high-frequency (in tens of GHz) and ultra-wideband characteristics. For example, the measured result of S 11 is below −10 dB in the frequency range of 12 GHz–39 GHz (7 GHz–22 GHz or 5 GHz–25 GHz) for printed patch antennas on flat FR4 substrates (or on curvilinear, bendable PLA substrates). In addition, we quantify other characteristics of these printed antenna structures (e.g., radiation efficiency and gain) and also demonstrate good robustness and reliability (in terms of maintaining the performance) of the antenna structures after being subjected to long-term temperature cycling. Additionally, we measure the radiation efficiency of the printed CNT-GO patch antenna on flat FR4 substrates and also obtain simulation results for quantifying the S 11 and the gain of the antenna.

title: A Gap in the Legal Regulation of Jurisdiction in Criminal Cases Involving Jurors
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the issue of jurisdiction in criminal cases before a jury. It has been established that the Criminal Procedure Code of the Russian Federation has a gap in the legal regulation of the rules of jurisdiction in cases where there are circumstances indicating the need to change the jurisdiction at the stage of trial of a criminal case before a jury. As a result, of the conducted research, the author has proposed legitimate options for overcoming the legislative gap, including through the development and implementation of legal mechanisms for changing the composition of the court.

title: YEASTRACT+: the 2026 update with focus on global quantitative transcription regulation data and metabolic engineering applications
abstract: Abstract YEASTRACT+ (http://yeastract-plus.org/) is a tool for the analysis, prediction, and modelling of transcription regulatory data at gene and genomic levels in yeasts. It incorporates three integrated databases: YEASTRACT, PathoYeastract, and NCYeastract, focused on Saccharomyces cerevisiae, pathogenic yeasts, and non-conventional yeasts of biotechnological relevance, respectively. In this release, YEASTRACT+ offers upgraded information on transcription regulation for 13 yeast species, extending the database to two additional yeasts of the basidiomycota phylum, the pathogenic yeast Cryptococcus neoformans, and the biotechnologically relevant Rhodotorula toruloides. A dramatic upgrade in the quality of the data provided occurred, as regulatory associations between transcription factors (TFs) and target genes are now associated with quantitative assessment. Quantitative impact of TFs on gene expression levels enabled the construction and release of two additional analytical tools: quantitative rank by TF, for the prediction of the most relevant TFs underlying a given transcriptomics dataset; and metabolic engineering based on integrating the quantitative impact of TF expression into genome-scale metabolic models. Altogether, this release of YEASTRACT+ provides unparalleled access to massive, curated, quantitative data associated with gene expression control in 13 yeast spec…

title: Frequency of Adherence to Obstetric Anesthesia Best Practices for Cesarean Delivery: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Analysis
abstract: Background: Increasingly, protocols have been developed to optimize obstetric anesthesia care. However, there is a paucity of data on adherence to these guidelines. The primary aims of this study were to utilize the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group (MPOG) database to estimate (1) the rate of adherence to best practice guidelines for cesarean delivery, (2) the association of case- and hospital-level factors with adherence, and (3) the percentage of variability in adherence attributable to the patient-, case-, and hospital-level factors. Methods: The authors performed a multicenter observational cohort study utilizing the MPOG database to review all cesarean deliveries in women age 15 to 44 yr. Best practices were defined based on societal guidelines and included timely antibiotic administration, postspinal systolic blood pressure (SBP) maintenance greater than 90 mmHg, general anesthesia avoidance, prevention of perioperative hypothermia, use of low-dose neuraxial morphine, postspinal vasopressor infusions, and spinal needles 25-gauge or smaller. Covariates of interest included patient-, case-, and hospital-level factors. Results: The authors analyzed 289,047 cesarean delivery cases in the MPOG database from 2015 to 2022. The following adherence outcomes were observed: timely antibiotic administration, 86.2% (99% CI, 86 to 86.3%); postspinal SBP maintenance, 96.7% (99% C…

Integrating AI with BIM for enhanced construction cost and schedule forecasting: a machine learning model with barrier analysis
abstract: Purpose This research identifies the barriers in BIM-AI adoption and demonstrates how the combination of building information modeling (BIM) and artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to improve construction project schedule and cost forecasting through an integrated framework. Design/methodology/approach This study was conducted using a combination of different research methods. The questionnaire survey measured the 43 barriers by means of the relative importance index (RII) and Pareto analysis. A Python-based BIM-AI forecasting framework was developed based on the findings. Random forest, gradient boosting and XGBoost were benchmarked using 5-fold group cross-validation (GroupKFold) with project-level grouping to prevent data leakage. Findings The results indicate that random forest and gradient boosting showed more stable performance in duration prediction (R2 = 0.806), while random forest achieved the highest accuracy in cost forecasting (R2 = 0.909) and was therefore selected for integration into the final BIM–AI framework. In the applied case study, the model achieved a duration R2 of 0.7886 and a cost R2 of 0.4368, reflecting forecast variance due to project uncertainties rather than realized cost savings. The barrier adjustment factor was 1.0857 (8.57%), consistent with FIDIC Sub-Clause 13.8, which limits contractual adjustments to 10%. Research limitations/implicatio…

title: Mitigating systematic underestimation in short-term wind speed forecasting via time-dependent weighted quantile loss (TDWQLoss)
abstract: Abstract Accurate short-term wind speed forecasting is critical for wind power integration. Although deep learning models exhibit strong predictive capability, their performance is often limited by systematic underestimation when optimized with conventional symmetric loss functions. This issue arises from the right-skewed Weibull distribution of wind speed, where the scarcity of high-wind-speed samples induces pronounced data imbalance and leads to biased learning, particularly under longer forecast lead times. To address this problem, we propose a lightweight Time-Dependent Weighted Quantile Loss (TDWQLoss), which introduces a time-dependent quantile weighting mechanism that adjusts penalty strength according to forecast horizon, enabling a more appropriate representation of increasing uncertainty with lead time. We evaluate the proposed method using three representative spatiotemporal models (Conv3D, SimVP, and MFWPN). Experimental results show that TDWQLoss consistently reduces systematic negative bias and improves overall forecasting accuracy across all models and lead times. In addition, it improves performance in event-based metrics, including Probability of Detection (POD) and Critical Success Index (CSI), without requiring any modification to model architectures. These results demonstrate that TDWQLoss provides a simple, architecture-agnostic, and effective strategy for…

title: A physics-guided uncertainty calibration framework for reliable probabilistic rainfall forecasting under heavy and extreme rainfall conditions
abstract: Reliable rainfall forecasting requires not only accurate point predictions but also well-calibrated estimates of predictive uncertainty, particularly during heavy and extreme events where forecast errors carry the greatest operational consequence. Deterministic machine learning models provide point forecasts without quantifying uncertainty, while existing probabilistic methods generally derive uncertainty from statistical relationships in the available data without explicitly conditioning it on the physical state of the atmosphere. This study presents a physics-guided uncertainty calibration framework for probabilistic rainfall forecasting. A two-stage architecture employs gradient-boosted regression to estimate the conditional mean and a separate heteroscedastic model trained on out-of-fold residuals to estimate the predictive variance. An interpretable Atmospheric Instability Score, constructed from moisture, thermodynamic, synoptic, and dynamic indicators weighted by variance-model feature importance, then scales the predictive variance on a per-sample basis. The framework is evaluated on the WeatherAUS dataset (145,460 daily observations, 49 stations) for next-day rainfall using rolling-origin validation across five expanding windows. Physics-guided calibration is found not to improve average probabilistic skill, as the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) achieves it…

title: Gated Hybrid Network Using CRNN and RNN Models for Time-Series Forecasting and Case Studies
abstract: Time-series forecasting is a critical challenge in industrial applications such as inventory management and energy planning. This paper proposes a gated hybrid network for time-series forecasting that combines feature vectors obtained from convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) branches. Unlike conventional CRNN models, the proposed model feeds the original time-series sequence in parallel to both CRNN and independent RNN branches, enabling each branch to extract complementary temporal features. A squeeze-and-excitation-inspired gating mechanism then adaptively weights and integrates the two feature vectors. Experiments were conducted using six real-world datasets, including automotive sales, electricity consumption, and solar energy data. The proposed model achieved lower mean relative squared error and relative absolute error values averaged across four forecasting periods than autoregressive (AR), autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), Holt–Winters, gated recurrent unit (GRU), and long short-term memory (LSTM) baseline models on most of the datasets, while also demonstrating superior prediction stability. These results suggest that the proposed architecture is suitable for practical industrial forecasting tasks.

title: Dual-branch graph neural network with spatio-temporal fusion for traffic flow forecasting
abstract: Reliable traffic flow forecasting is fundamental to intelligent transportation systems. Existing spatio-temporal models often emphasise either localised variation or long-range dependency, rely on spatial relations that respond too slowly to traffic changes, and fuse multi-branch features in a relatively shallow way. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-branch spatio-temporal fusion graph neural network (DB-STFGNN). The first branch captures localised coupled dynamics through multi-scale temporal convolution and a hybrid diffusion dynamic graph convolution (HDGCN) module with iterative interaction updates. The second branch employs spatio-temporal multi-head attention to model broader dependencies across nodes and time steps. To strengthen collaboration between the two branches, the authors further introduce a bidirectional cross-attention fusion module (CAFM), which performs cross-branch interaction and feature refinement before prediction. A non-autoregressive prediction head then maps the fused representation to future traffic flow values. Experiments on real-world benchmarks, including PeMS03, PeMS04, PeMS07 and PeMS08, show that DB-STFGNN achieves competitive performance under mean absolute error, root mean square error and mean absolute percentage error compared with traditional spatio-temporal models and mainstream graph-based baselines.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Transport

title: Machine learning prediction of 1-year thrombosis risk in membranous nephropathy: integration of renal pathology and early longitudinal trajectories
abstract: Introduction Patients with membranous nephropathy (MN) have an increased risk of thrombotic events. Existing prediction approaches primarily use clinical and laboratory measurements obtained at a single time point and rarely incorporate renal pathology or early longitudinal changes. This study integrated multiple types of information to predict the occurrence of thrombosis from 4 weeks after discharge to 1 year after being diagnosed with MN. Method This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1,070 patients with MN. Patient characteristics, laboratory findings, renal pathological features, and follow-up data were collected. Patients were randomly divided into training and validation sets at an 8:2 ratio. Latent class trajectory modeling identified longitudinal classes from measurements obtained during the index hospitalization for MN diagnosis and at 2 and 4 weeks after discharge. Predictors were selected using LASSO regression. Seven machine learning algorithms were used, including logistic boosting, adaptive boosting, generalized linear model, weighted k-nearest neighbors (kknn), naive Bayes, random forest, and support vector machine. Result Thrombotic events occurred in 150 patients (14.0%). LASSO selected 10 predictors: hypertension history, stroke or myocardial infarction history, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, D-dimer, cystatin C, estimated glomerular filtratio…

title: Advanced parametric inference and prediction for censored data using standard omega distribution: applications to tensile strength and failure time analysis
abstract: Purpose This study presents a framework for parametric inference and prediction of censored data modeled by the standard omega (SO) distribution under progressively Type-II censored sampling schemes. It focuses on developing accurate estimation methods, predicting future failure times, and constructing prediction intervals using classical and Bayesian approaches. Real-world engineering datasets are analyzed to demonstrate the practical applicability of the proposed methodologies to address challenges in engineering involving censored data. Design/methodology/approach Unknown parameters are estimated using MLE, expectation-maximization, product spacing, least squares, and weighted least squares methods, with rigorous demonstration of the existence and uniqueness of MLEs. Confidence intervals are derived using the Fisher information matrix. Bayesian estimation with gamma priors and MCMC methods is applied to compute credible intervals. Prediction methods include best unbiased, conditional median, and Bayesian approaches, with prediction intervals constructed using pivotal, conditional, and HPD techniques. Simulations and optimality criteria guide the selection of sampling schemes, and the methodology is illustrated with two real engineering datasets. Findings The proposed framework proves effective in addressing engineering problems involving censored data. Simulations validate t…

title: Graph-Aware Controlled Continuous Dynamics Network for Information Diffusion Prediction
abstract: Information diffusion prediction aims to infer future user activations from observed cascade prefixes in social networks, where diffusion unfolds as a complex, irregular, continuous-time process. Existing methods typically model dynamic user preferences by discretizing diffusion into temporal graph or hypergraph snapshots. As a result, these methods produce hidden states only at discrete timestamps and do not capture the continuous dynamics between cascade events. Although neural ordinary differential equations provide a natural framework for modeling temporal dynamics, their trajectories are determined by the initial condition and cannot incorporate subsequent observations as direct controls along the evolving path. To address these limitations, we propose CoDyNet, a graph-aware Controlled continuous Dynamics Network for microscopic information diffusion prediction. CoDyNet first learns graphaware user representations from multi-source static relations and dynamic diffusion hypergraphs. It then constructs timestamp-aware control paths that drive a neural controlled differential equation for observation-guided continuous propagation modeling. We further introduce a cascade-aware graph contrastive regularizer that enforces consistency between clean and perturbed static user representations while avoiding co-activated false negatives. The resulting continuous diffusion context an…

title: Hybrid ANN–metaheuristic models for EWQI prediction and hydrochemical assessment in drinking water distribution systems
Summability Methods for Noisy Industrial Reliability Data and Failure Prediction
abstract: Purpose: Industrial reliability records contain impulsive noise, drift, missing intervals, maintenance resets, regime changes, and right censored lifetimes, which complicate the estimation of degradation trends and the prediction of failures. This study examines how classical summability ideas, especially Cesàro averaging and Abel type regularization, can be integrated with robust preprocessing, survival analysis, and prognostics. Research Methodology: The study uses a methodological design that specifies a hybrid workflow of data quality screening, time aware normalization, parallel smoothing at multiple scales, reliability or degradation modeling, blocked temporal validation, uncertainty calibration, and cost aware maintenance decisions, supported by mathematical definitions and generated illustrations. Results: The illustrations show that short windows leave noise, long windows delay warnings, and the cumulative Cesàro mean recovers only about half of a regime shift after 100 cycles, whereas trailing and Abel type means reach about 90% within 18 cycles. In a pump example, smoothing removed two false alarms at the cost of about two days of warning. Conclusions: Summability should be treated as a transparent, tunable preprocessing and diagnostic layer rather than as a substitute for a physically meaningful failure model. Limitations: All numerical illustrations are synthetic, …

title: Prediction of lncRNA–cervical cancer associations using a multi-view collaborative variational autoencoder with knowledge distillation transfer learning
abstract: Introduction Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play critical regulatory roles in the pathogenesis of cervical cancer, and accurate identification of lncRNA–cervical cancer associations is important for understanding the molecular mechanisms of the disease and discovering potential therapeutic targets. However, the extreme scarcity of cervical cancer-specific lncRNA association data constitutes a major bottleneck limiting the performance of existing computational prediction methods. Methods To address this challenge, we propose a Multi-View Collaborative Variational Autoencoder based on Knowledge Distillation Transfer Learning (MVCVAE), which integrates multi-source heterogeneous data fusion and cross-disease knowledge transfer in a task-oriented manner. The multi-view collaborative variational autoencoder constructs dual-view feature representations of lncRNA and disease similarities and employs a symmetric encoder–decoder architecture to learn complex lncRNA–disease association patterns in the latent space. The knowledge distillation transfer learning framework adopts a teacher–student network design: a teacher model is pre-trained on a large-scale dataset containing 12,865 lncRNA–disease associations to learn general association patterns, and the resulting prior knowledge is effectively transferred to a student model targeting 92 cervical cancer associations through feature dist…

Response Inhibition in an Affective Context and Its Relation to Psychopathic Traits
abstract: Background: Psychopathic traits are associated with affective deficits and elevated impulsivity levels, such as those measured by Go/No-go tasks. Previous research assessing the combined effects of psychopathic traits and emotional processing on response inhibition has focused on low cognitive load task designs and found little evidence of valence-dependent effects. Objective: To investigate whether assessing affective response inhibition under low and high cognitive load manipulations reveals interactive effects between psychopathic traits and valence processing on response inhibition. Methods: We assessed 146 student and community participants using the Psychopathic Personality Inventory—Revised (PPI-R). Response inhibition was measured under low and high cognitive load using the parametric Go/No-go task (PGNG) alongside positive, negative, and neutral distractor images. Results: Cognitive load and valence affected performance. Response times were faster and accuracy rates were higher for the low-load (easier) task stage. Negative and positive trials slowed response times and reduced response inhibition performance compared with neutral trials. In terms of psychopathic traits, the PPI-R Self-Centered Impulsivity factor and two of its subscales, Machiavellian Egocentricity and Blame Externalization, correlated negatively with response inhibition across valences and load. Corre…

title: Optimization of Verbascoside Extraction from Jasminum subtriplinerve Blume Collected in Quang Tri Province Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Abstract: This study optimized the ultrasound-assisted extraction of verbascoside from Jasminum subtriplinerve Blume using an ethanol–water solvent system. Verbascoside content under various conditions was determined by HPTLC- Scanning. Key variables and their ranges were initially screened using the one-factor-at-a-time approach and subsequently optimized via response surface methodology with a Box–Behnken design. Ethanol concentration (10–40%), extraction temperature (50–80°C), and extraction time (15–45 min) were selected as independent variables, while verbascoside yield and total extract yield were responses. Under the optimal conditions (33% ethanol, 76°C, 43 min), the verbascoside yield reached 60.12% and total extract yield was 24.46%, with RSD values of 1.77% and 1.49%, respectively. This result provides a scientific basis for the production of a highly concentrated extract of verbascoside from the medicinal plant, opening up applications in medicine and pharmaceuticals. Keywords: Verbascoside, Optimization, Jasminum subtriplinerve.

abstract: Background: Delaying surgery following neoadjuvant concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) may permit continuing tumor cell death and regression over time. This exploratory pilot study examines the influence of extending the time interval from completion of CCRT to surgery on achieving a pathological complete response (pCR) across a rectal cancer cohort. Methods: This pilot analysis reviewed data from 64 patients with Stage II–III rectal cancer who completed neoadjuvant protocols were reviewed. Patients were stratified based on the real-world resting interval between CCRT completion and total mesorectal excision (TME) into Shorter Interval group (<8 weeks, n = 10) and an Extended Interval group (≥ 8 weeks, n = 54). Univariate logistic regression analyzed the impact of resting intervals, alongside clinical stage, tumor grade, and histology on pCR and overall response rates (ORR). Primary outcome included analyzing if a prolonged interval between the completion of CCRT and radical surgery yields superior tumor regression without escalating surgical morbidity, Secondary outcomes included factors influencing pCR. Results: Surgery executed ≥8weeks weeks post-CCRT demonstrated a prevailing, non-significant trend toward significantly higher odds of achieving a pCR compared to shorter intervals (OR = 3.250, 95% CI: 0.369–28.650, P=0.289).

abstract: Purpose: We evaluated whether student and item representations learned from response correctness provide information about examinee and item characteristics, including item response theory (IRT) estimates, and whether this information translates into better response prediction.Methods: We analyzed Korean Medical Licensing Examination (KMLE) responses from 3,259 examinees to 360 items. We froze 64-dimensional representations learned by cyclic dual latent discovery (CDLD) and assessed IRT prediction using nested cross-validation. Exploratory analyses compared the addition of CDLD, 64-dimensional representations based on singular value decomposition (SVD64), or random inputs to augmented response summaries. Across 5 splits, response prediction was compared with Rasch and 2-parameter logistic (2PL) models; 0–40 responses from new examinees were used for adaptation.Results: In exploratory comparisons, adding CDLD to augmented response summaries increased R2 from 0.9289 to 0.9843 for 2PL ability and from 0.8759 to 0.9216 for log discrimination. The increment for log discrimination was 0.0458 (95% confidence interval, 0.0163 to 0.0842), exceeding the increment with SVD64 by 0.0267 (0.0091 to 0.0457).
