Fermi-Level Modulation in Graphene Sensors Revealed by Voltage-Dependent Raman Spectroscopy and 3D Waterfall Response Mapping
abstract: Abstract The electronic properties of graphene sensors are governed by the position of the Fermi level, which determines the carrier concentration and consequently controls the electrical conductivity and sensing performance. Although Fermi-level modulation is widely recognized as the fundamental mechanism of graphene-based sensing, its direct experimental correlation with the dynamic sensing response has remained insufficiently explored. In this work, we demonstrate that Raman spectroscopy provides a direct, nondestructive method for quantifying the relative Fermi-level modulation through systematic shifts of the G and 2D Raman bands associated with changes in carrier concentration. The Raman analysis reveals reversible electrical tuning of the graphene electronic structure under source-drain voltage without introducing structural defects, allowing quantitative estimation of the Fermi-level relative displacement. To investigate the dynamic behavior of the same electronic states during sensor operation, low-frequency time–frequency waterfall spectroscopy was employed under chemical and optical stimulation. The results demonstrate that external stimuli induce transient perturbations of the graphene Fermi level, producing characteristic conductivity fluctuations that depend on the magnitude and kinetics of carrier-density modulation. The combination of static (Raman spectroscopy)…

title: Dynamic Response and Vibration Signature of Single Degree of Freedom Steel System
abstract: Introduction/Objective Civil engineering structures face major challenges, particularly earthquakes, which are random phenomena in their intensity and frequency content. The seismic response of structures depends largely on the intensity of an earthquake and especially on its frequency content. The assessment of the dynamic behavior of structures subjected to seismic excitations is therefore essential for understanding their performance. The main objective of this study is the experimental identification of the vibration signature of a single-degree-of-freedom SDOF steel system. Methods Based on the laws of similarity, a 1:6 reduced-scale steel model is developed. In this context, dynamic experiments using the shaking table of the RISAM laboratory (Risk Assessment and Management: University of Tlemcen) are carried out to determine the structural dynamic parameters of this steel system. This is achieved through experimental determination of natural frequency and damping. Acceleration and displacement measurements are also established. The experimental estimation of damping is established using the logarithmic decrement method. Several dynamic analyses are carried out based on the finite element model of the reduced-scale steel system. title: Criticizing the Methodological Realisability of the Value-Free Ideal: A Response to Sikorski
abstract: Abstract The value-free ideal (VFI) has recently been the subject of renewed interest with some authors attempting to defend it in the face of ongoing criticism. A particularly ambitious project is that of the methodological vindication of realisability, which attempts to vindicate the VFI through arguments aimed at scientific methodology and how research practice can be amended to avoid the influence of non-epistemic values. I shall critically review the debate around the strategy of methodological vindication and respond to the attempts at vindicating the VFI. Thereby, I will draw a distinction between two aspects of the classic argument against the VFI usually referred to as the argument from inductive risk (AIR) and show why a distinction between a problem of context-sensitivity and a problem of translation is relevant. Utilizing this distinction, I shall demonstrate why the methodological vindication is ultimately unsuccessful.

Engineered Dielectric Response of Liquid-Filled Interfacial Bubbles in van der Waals Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract Interfacial bubbles in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are typically regarded as unavoidable byproducts of stacking. Here, we show that they can be repurposed as engineered dielectric nanocavities by intentionally trapping selected liquids during assembly. A simple prewetting step before stamp transfer forms liquid-filled bubbles at hBN/graphite interfaces containing acetone, ethanol, H2O, and NaCl(aq), alongside untreated reference bubbles. Electrostatic force microscopy (EFM), crosstalk correction, and finite-element modeling enable quantitative extraction of the effective dielectric constant (εeff) of individual bubbles, revealing higher εeff for all liquid-filled bubbles than for untreated ones. To estimate the apparent core permittivity of the confined contents, each bubble is modeled as a liquid core enclosed by an hBN shell. Simulations of the tip–bubble–substrate geometry yield core dielectric constants (εcore) larger than εeff yet physically consistent with the trapped media. Acetone and ethanol exhibit εcore values close to their expected dielectric properties, whereas water shows a reduced εcore consistent with nanoconfined pure water. Notably, NaCl(aq) shows a larger εcore than pure water, suggesting distinct electrolyte dielectric behavior under nanoscale confinement. This work establishes vdW bubbles as versatile platforms for engineering local elect…

title: Anomaly detection of asset data in power monitoring systems based on knowledge graph reasoning
abstract: Abstract Edge computing nodes face severe constraints on both computing and storage resources, and the dynamic correlation of asset data remains complex within power monitoring systems. To address this challenge, this study proposes an anomaly detection framework that is based on knowledge graph reasoning and tailored for asset data in such systems. The framework first constructs a lightweight embedding method for knowledge graphs, then introduces a time-sliding window mechanism that builds a sequence of dynamic subgraphs, thereby adapting to the dynamic evolution of the network topology. Following this, the approach combines relational attribute modulation with low-rank matrix decomposition, thereby reducing both the model’s global parameter count and its memory overhead. It then proposes a relation-aware lightweight graph attention network. Within this network, a differential projection decoupling mechanism separates the coupling effects between target nodes and relational features. In addition, the approach introduces a sparse attention truncation selection strategy to filter out low-frequency background noise. Based on real datasets collected from substations and distribution networks, the results show that the proposed model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.982 on dataset A and an accuracy of 0.949 on dataset B. The low-rank…

title: Spatial dynamics of tourism and human capital: spillover effects on environmental sustainability
abstract: Purpose This study examines the spatial dynamics of environmental quality in 213 Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics (NUTS)-2 regions across 23 European countries during 2016 and 2020. It evaluates the impact of tourism activity and human capital on environmental sustainability, challenging traditional assumptions about economic growth and environmental quality. Design/methodology/approach A spatial econometric modeling approach is applied to assess the interdependencies between regions. The study incorporates spatial lag and spatial error models to capture spillover effects. The Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis is tested using an alternative specification, while the spatial relationships among environmental quality, tourism, and human capital are analyzed through spatial regression techniques. Findings The results contradict the conventional EKC hypothesis, revealing a convex relationship between economic growth and environmental quality. The study highlights three key findings: (1) environmental quality in a given region is significantly influenced by its neighboring regions, (2) human capital generates positive spillover effects, enhancing sustainability across regional boundaries, and (3) tourism activity produces negative externalities, contributing to environmental degradation beyond local jurisdictions. Research limitations/implications The study…

A Prompt-Optimized Vision-Language Model System for Fine-Grained Fashion Style Recognition
abstract: With the accelerated digital transformation of the fashion industry, accurate clothing style recognition has become essential for intelligent e-commerce retrieval, personalized outfit recommendation, and fashion trend analysis. Vision-language models (VLMs), with their cross-modal semantic alignment and zero-shot inference capabilities, offer an efficient technical pathway for this task. However, when applied to the fashion domain, general-purpose VLMs face several challenges, including vague prompt semantics, insufficient fine-grained discrimination, difficulty in capturing composite style characteristics, and high deployment costs. To address these issues, this paper presents a comprehensive clothing style recognition system based on Qwen3-VL-Plus. A four-level structured prompt template—comprising style definitions, visual feature guidance, and confidence distribution constraints—is introduced to direct the model's attention toward fine-grained attributes such as silhouette, fabric, color, and decoration. A confidence distribution modeling mechanism based on Softmax normalization is proposed to convert cross-modal similarity scores into interpretable confidence distributions, enabling quantitative representation of composite styles. Furthermore, INT8 quantization and inference pipeline optimization are employed to achieve lightweight deployment, allowing the system to operat…

Sistema agroforestal para el uso racional del suelo en Sacrifrancia, Pastaza, Ecuador: estudio de caso
abstract: La degradación del suelo por monocultivo, agroquímicos y deforestación amenaza la producción y la biodiversidad amazónicas. El estudio analizó un sistema agroforestal para el uso racional del suelo en una finca de la zona de Sacrifrancia, en Pastaza. Se empleó un enfoque cualitativo con revisión documental de artículos científicos y una entrevista semiestructurada de once preguntas al propietario, quien dirige la finca desde hace dieciocho años. Según su relato, la finca combina maderables, frutales, aromáticas y cacao bajo manejo orgánico, con una poda que deja el material vegetal como abono, mejor calidad del cacao y mayor presencia de fauna silvestre; el apoyo institucional se percibe como limitado. Se concluye que el caso es coherente con lo que la literatura atribuye a la agroforestería, aunque, al tratarse de un solo testimonio sin mediciones, no permite afirmar que el modelo sea replicable.

title: Implementation drivers of blockchain technology for payment processes of construction projects in South Africa: a quantitative analysis
abstract: Purpose Innovative technologies such as blockchain are changing the modus operandi of construction contract execution and project actualisation. Implementing blockchain technology for the payment process seeks to proffer solutions to conventional challenges facing construction contract execution. This study aims to explore the drivers of implementing blockchain technology for the payment process in construction contract administration from a developing economy perspective. Design/methodology/approach The study used a quantitative approach aided by a well-structured questionnaire for data collection from the target respondents. The retrieved data was analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, namely, the Kruskal-Wallis h-test, Student Newman Kauls (post hoc) test and exploratory factor analysis. Findings The principal components extracted from the analysis portrayed three main drivers of implementing blockchain technology for the payment process in the construction industry: automation functionality, enhanced security and transparency and trust. Also, it was revealed that there are diverging viewpoints among the respondents on some of the identified drivers. Practical implications The study’s findings unravel practical insights that can assist in driving the digital transformation of payment processes of construction projects for effective contract administration. title: Evaluating the Circular Economy Performance of Construction and Demolition Waste Management in Taiwan: A DEA and Malmquist Index Approach
abstract: Construction and demolition waste (CDW) is a major industrial waste stream in Taiwan. Conventional indicators such as recycling rates and treated volumes describe throughput, without directly measuring how efficiently regional systems transform resource inputs into reusable products while limiting residual waste. This study evaluates regional CDW circular-economy performance using an input-oriented data envelopment analysis (DEA) framework and the Malmquist productivity index. The original database covered 19 geographic units for 2023–2025; excluding observations with all-zero outputs, the static DEA dataset contained 53 county-year observations for 18 counties and cities. A common pooled frontier was estimated using three inputs (CDW received, licensed treatment/reuse capacity, and estimated treatment cost) and three outputs (treated/reused CDW, recycled product output, and a reciprocal transformation of residual waste). For 2023–2025, the mean Charnes-Cooper-Rhodes (CCR) efficiencies were 0.509, 0.455, and 0.461 and mean Banker-Charnes-Cooper (BCC) efficiencies 0.639, 0.598, and 0.573, respectively. Input correlations were moderate ( r ≤0.578). Slack analysis identified frequent treated-/reused-output shortfalls and input excesses. title: Managing material cost overruns in industrial building projects using a system dynamics approach
abstract: Purpose Material cost overruns remain a persistent challenge in industrial construction projects, driven by interconnected risks such as price volatility, supply chain disruptions and changes in material specifications. This study aims to enhance cost risk management by analysing the dynamic relationships among these key contributing factors. Design/methodology/approach A system dynamics modelling framework was developed to investigate feedback mechanisms and temporal dynamics among nine critical material-related risk factors. These factors were identified through an extensive literature review and expert input, and structured into interconnected sub-models representing core risk domains, including material price volatility, distribution inefficiencies and impacts of specification changes. Findings Nine interconnected material risks collectively drive cost deviations through reinforcing and balancing feedback mechanisms. Baseline simulations showed a 135% cumulative deviation, reduced to 122% through preventive measures, a 10.66% improvement. Procurement optimisation achieved the largest reduction, while improved material planning and warehouse management also strengthened cost control. Originality/value This study proposes an empirically grounded system dynamics framework to examine the interdependent and temporal effects of material-related risks on cost overruns in industria…

Battery-Side Energy Efficiency of Wirelessly Connected Robots Using the Joint Offloading, Compression and Scaling Offloading and Scheduling Policy
abstract: Battery capacity is the binding constraint on how long a fleet of mobile robots can work between charges. In wirelessly connected fleets, the robot battery is shared between three competing consumers: locomotion, onboard computation, and the radio. All energy figures in this paper refer exclusively to the robot battery; the edge server is mains-powered and outside the optimisation scope. Offloading perception to the edge server removes computation from the battery, but it consumes airtime on a shared wireless medium and a late result forces the robot to slow down, lengthening the mission and increasing locomotion energy drawn from the same cell. We develop a battery-side energy model that prices a missed perception deadline in joules through its effect on mission duration, derive the penalty in closed form as λ = 5.18 J, and propose joint offloading, compression and scaling (JOCS), a decentralised per-epoch policy that jointly selects the offloading decision, payload compression level, transmit power, and processor frequency for each pipeline stage. JOCS admits offload requests in decreasing order of battery energy saved per second of airtime consumed, subject to a feasibility test on the self-induced congestion. Simulated over 30 independent channel realisations, JOCS reduced robot battery energy by 22.6% relative to run-to-deadline local execution at eight robots per access p…

title: Conception d’un système spatial d'aide à la décision pour la collecte et la surveillance des maladies animales au Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, Tchad
abstract: Contexte : La province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, située au Tchad, est une zone pastorale importante mais qui demeure vulnérable aux épizooties en raison de la densité et de la diversité de son cheptel. Pour combler le manque d'outils numériques destinés à la surveillance sanitaire animale, un système d'aide à la décision spatiale (SDSS) a été développé dans le cadre du projet Géo Santé, sous la forme d’une application mobile innovante. Objectif : Cette étude avait pour objectifs de présenter la conception et la mise en œuvre du SDSS Géo Santé, et d'évaluer ses contributions effectives dans la province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest. Méthodes : Conçue en collaboration avec les acteurs locaux, l'application a été expérimentée dans treize cantons et a permis d'enregistrer 160 cas sanitaires dans le cadre d’une phase pilote. Les données ont été collectées par des vétérinaires et des techniciens communautaires à l’aide de formulaires numériques géolocalisés intégrant des informations zootechniques, cliniques et spatiales ; les cas recensés correspondent à des suspicions cliniques non confirmées biologiquement. Résultats : Les résultats ont montré une amélioration de la traçabilité des maladies animales suspectées et du suivi des risques sanitaires. Process mining in humanitarian procurement: a scoping review
abstract: Purpose Despite its strong potential to optimize business processes, process mining remains largely unexplored in humanitarian operations. Therefore, this study aims to systematically examine the state of research across process mining in procurement and humanitarian procurement analytics and identify complementarities between the two streams. Design/methodology/approach A scoping review methodology was applied to systematically analyze peer-reviewed studies published between January 2015 and August 2025. Following a structured search and screening procedure, 43 studies were analyzed across two themes: process mining in procurement and humanitarian procurement analytics. Findings The study reveals a clear methodological divergence between the two themes. Process mining studies mainly provide descriptive and diagnostic insights using real event-log data, yet rarely extend to predictive or prescriptive analytics. In contrast, humanitarian procurement research advances prescriptive models but mainly relies on simulated or parameterized data. Predictive applications remain underdeveloped across both themes, while prescriptive models in humanitarian procurement are rarely validated using operational data. The comparison shows that process-mining capabilities, including compliance checking, bottleneck analysis, anomaly detection and process-variant analysis, could provide empirical e…

title: Life cycle management for improving sustainability effectiveness in area-based infrastructure projects: lessons from Thailand
abstract: Purpose Life cycle management (LCM) is increasingly recognized as a strategic approach for improving infrastructure sustainability; however, evidence remains limited on how perceived implementation of LCM practices is associated with perceived sustainability effectiveness across the life cycle of area-based infrastructure projects (AIPs), particularly in developing countries. This study examines these associations in Thai local administrative organizations (LAOs). The Sufficiency Economy Philosophy (SEP) and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) provide the policy context; they are not measured as separate empirical constructs. Design/methodology/approach Literature synthesis and expert screening were used to develop the questionnaire. A total of 645 valid questionnaires from Thai LAOs were analyzed using SPSS Version 28, exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, correlations and multiple regression. Qualitative consultations supported item refinement and interpretation; because participant counts and a formal qualitative coding record were unavailable for this revision, they are not presented as an independently validated mixed-methods strand. How review environments shape review voting: the roles of competition intensity and attention intensity
abstract: Purpose Most platforms feature online reviews with voting functions that act as peer-based social feedback. Beyond prior research that examines how review and reviewer characteristics shape voting outcomes, this study investigates how two environmental factors, competition intensity and attention intensity, affect voting outcomes. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on communication models and uses Poisson Pseudo Maximum Likelihood regression with high-dimensional fixed effects, using 293,670 Yelp reviews from 29,842 reviewers across 11,436 US restaurants to empirically test our communication-based framework. Findings We find that competition intensity reduces the number of votes a review receives, whereas attention intensity increases it. We also show that review deviation and reviewer status mitigate the negative effect of competition; review deviation amplifies, whereas reviewer status weakens, the positive effect of attention. Practical implications Our findings demonstrate that the environment surrounding a review meaningfully shapes how it communicates with readers, guiding users' attention allocation and engagement. The results offer practical implications for reviewers seeking to strategically improve voting outcomes and for platforms aiming to manage information overload and enhance user engagement efficiency. title: Integration of Solar PV and Wind Power into Modern Power Grids: A State-of-the-Art Review
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation now supply a rising share of electricity in many countries, and the systems built around coal, gas, and hydro were not designed for them. Both resources are weather-driven, both connect to the network mostly through power electronics, and both are often located far from load centres. This review examines how these characteristics affect network operation and how the research and industry communities have responded. It covers generation and conversion technologies, the main operational problems (voltage and frequency regulation, falling inertia, power quality, fault behaviour, congestion, and curtailment), and the main remedies: grid-forming converter control, energy storage, hybrid plants, flexible transmission, demand-side flexibility, and data-driven forecasting. The paper adds worked equations, simulated illustrations, and side-by-side comparisons of technologies, control methods, forecasting approaches, and documented system events. Open research problems are identified for networks that must run with very high shares of inverter-based generation. The review is intended as an organized starting point for researchers and engineers working on renewable-rich power systems.

title: Isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant glioma in the post-INDIGO era: advances in classification and management
abstract: Purpose of review Recent advances have reshaped the classification and management of IDH-mutant glioma. Updated molecular diagnostic frameworks, evolving multidisciplinary treatment strategies, and the emergence of mutant IDH inhibitors have introduced new therapeutic opportunities while also raising important unresolved clinical questions. This review summarizes recent developments and ongoing controversies in the post-INDIGO era. Recent findings Recent cIMPACT-NOW recommendations further refine molecular classification and grading criteria for IDH-mutant glioma. Increasing evidence supports maximal safe resection and, in select cases, supramaximal resection, particularly in astrocytoma. Questions regarding the optimal timing and modality of radiation therapy remain unresolved. Comparative studies of chemotherapy regimens continue to demonstrate tradeoffs between efficacy and toxicity. The INDIGO trial established mutant IDH inhibition as a new treatment paradigm, and ongoing studies seek to optimize patient selection and explore new types of IDH-directed therapies. Summary Management of IDH-mutant glioma is becoming increasingly individualized and molecularly driven. Although mutant IDH inhibitors represent a major therapeutic advance, their integration with existing treatment paradigms remains uncertain. Ongoing studies will continue to refine prognostic stratification and m…

title: Human–AI interaction in academic knowledge co-creation: a typology based on a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to knowledge co-creation in academic writing, focusing on systematic literature reviews (SLRs) as a representative and consequential form of structured knowledge production. It develops a typology of human–AI interaction that reveals how intellectual responsibility, decision-making and dialogue are distributed between human researchers and AI systems. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review of 120 publications from Scopus and Web of Science was conducted to analyse applications of AI in SLRs. Studies were coded along two dimensions derived from human–AI interaction theory: (1) decision-making delegation and (2) iterative dialogue between humans and AI. Using deductive thematic analysis, the research identified distinct interaction types and synthesised empirical patterns into a transparent framework. Findings The analysis reveals three types of human–AI interaction: AI-Supported, Collaborative and Partner-like. The AI-supported type treats AI as an assistive tool for automating repetitive tasks while preserving full human control. The collaborative type represents dialogical co-creation, where humans and AI engage in iterative prompting and feedback cycles. The partner-like type reflects hybrid partnership and partial delegation, where AI contributes analytical reasoning and interpretation u…

Enhancement mechanism of high temperature stability for in-situ oxide scale on high-entropy carbide coatings induced by rare earth
abstract: Abstract For ultra-high temperature ceramic (UHTC) coatings used in aerospace thermal protection systems, enhancing the oxygen barrier capability and thermal stability of in-situ oxide scale during ablation is crucial for stable service. Herein, a high-entropy design strategy is proposed to boost the compactness and phase stability of oxide scales by leveraging multi-component synergistic effects. Three high-entropy carbide coatings, (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Sm)C (HEC-Sm), (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Er)C (HEC-Er) and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Lu)C (HEC-Lu), with better ablation resistance than ZrC, (Hf-Zr-Ti)C, and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y)C coatings,were designed. HEC-Lu delivers optimal ablation resistance, featuring a linear ablation rate of -0.173 ± 0.012 μm·s-1, superior to HEC-Sm (-0.111 ± 0.032 μm·s-1) and HEC-Er (-0.144 ± 0.022 μm·s-1). This superior performance is correlated with higher Ti retention and stronger calculated Ti-O bonding, increasing Ti content in the oxide scale by 53.85 % and 33.33 % compared to HEC-Sm and HEC-Er, thereby inhibiting volatilization. Rare-earth (Sm, Er, Lu) incorporation can reduce the diffusion coefficients of Ti and O atoms in oxide scales by one order of magnitude at 2573 K compared with TiO2. title: Synergistic Absorption Mechanism in Flexible Polymer Composites Reinforced with Rare Earth Cobaltite and Molybdenum Carbide for EMI Shielding Applications
abstract: Abstract The sudden growth of digital devices and fifth-generation (5G) communication systems has generated increasing concerns regarding electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding in advanced technological applications, due to the high necessity for development of flexible, lightweight and efficient shielding materials. In this study, low thickness polymer composite films based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) polymer that is incorporated with gadolinium cobaltite and molybdenum carbide fillers were successfully fabricated through a solution casting technique. The chemical, structural, and morphological characteristics of the composite films were investigated using XRD, FTIR, FESEM, HR-TEM, tensile strength and contact angle. Thermal stability was assessed through thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and electromagnetic properties were evaluated in terms of complex permittivity and permeability across the X-band frequency range. The EMI shielding was examined in terms of shielding effectiveness due to absorption, reflection, and transmission and further validated using CST software. The selected composite film with an ultralow thickness of ∼0.15 mm exhibited a maximum EMI shielding efficiency of ∼49 dB in the X-band region with the absorption dominant shielding as the primary attenuation mechanism. The composite films displayed an enhanced mechanical strength and hydrophobicity beh…

title: A multi-mechanism partial counterbalancing approach for multi-session esports performance research in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
abstract: Esports performance research increasingly relies on repeated-measures designs, in which each player serves as their own control. Such designs are efficient, but they are vulnerable to order effects: participants improve with practice, tire within a session, and carry the influence of one condition into the next. Competitive gaming makes this problem unusually acute, because skill acquisition in digital games is rapid and session fatigue develops quickly. The conventional remedy, complete counterbalancing, is unattainable once a study tests more than a handful of conditions. This article describes and evaluates a partial counterbalancing strategy that layers four mechanisms: category-level Latin square sequencing, randomisation of values within categories, forward–reverse distribution of sequences across participants, and temporal spacing with session truncation. The strategy was implemented in an 18-week laboratory study of 170 South African Counter-Strike: Global Offensive players, testing six categories of hardware and in-game settings at three values each. Three independent checks were used to evaluate whether order effects had been controlled. Conditions were evenly distributed across testing positions in every setting category. Performance at the first testing position did not differ from performance at later positions on any of five metrics, with all effect sizes below th…

Algorithmicized Administrative Discretion in the Mechanism of Administrative Law Protection of Property: The Normative Nature, Concept, and Procedural Guarantees
abstract: The article examines algorithmised administrative discretion as a mode of exercising the general legal institution of administrative discretion in the digital environment of public administration. It defines the concept and identifies three mandatory elements: a legally established scope of choice, prior digital formalisation and a legally significant impact of the system rule on an individual decision. The concept is distinguished from automation of bound powers, technical error and hidden rulemaking. Using property-related administrative procedures as examples, the article substantiates requirements for reasoning, reconsideration by an authorised official, a legal regime for system parameters, preservation of a digital audit trail and allocation of the burden of proof. It proposes incorporating these safeguards into legislation on administrative procedures and administrative acts.

title: Regulated Remuneration Autonomy in Zambia’s Public Universities Under the Emoluments Commission Act No. 1 of 2022
abstract: The enactment of the Emoluments Commission Act No. 1 of 2022 reshaped Zambia’s public-sector remuneration context, raising questions about the extent to which its provisions qualify the authority of public university councils under the Higher Education Act No. 4 of 2013. This article examines how the two statutes allocate remuneration authority and how national regulatory coherence can be reconciled with the distinct workforce needs of public universities. The article employs doctrinal legal analysis, purposive and contextual statutory interpretation, and documentary analysis, informed by a strategic human resource management perspective. The analysis finds that the Emoluments Commission Act prevails over inconsistent provisions of the Higher Education Act only to the extent of the inconsistency and within the Commission’s statutory jurisdiction over emoluments. It does not displace university councils’ governance and employment responsibilities where these remain legally compatible with the Emoluments Commission Act No. 1 of 2022. The article distinguishes remuneration determination from collective bargaining, job evaluation, workforce planning, implementation and institutional evidence generation. It further argues that harmonisation does not necessarily require uniformity: justified differentiation may be considered where credible evidence demonstrates specific workforce pre…

title: Exergo-energetic evaluation and predictive modeling of a double helical coil air heater for sustainable energy applications
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study in residential heating that focuses on passive and surface engineering strategies to produce significant benefits with minimal geometric modifications. The current double helical coil air heater (DHCAH) synergistically integrates geometric modification and the inherent advantages of helical coil designs. Design/methodology/approach This study experimentally investigates the energetic and exergetic performance of a DHCAH under varying geometrical and flow parameters, including helical tube diameter, fluid flow rate, air velocity and inlet temperature. Nusselt number, friction factor, JF factor, effectiveness, exergy efficiency and sustainability index are evaluated. Subsequently, artificial neural network (ANN) and adaptive physics-guided neural network (PGNN) models are developed and assessed using repeated five-fold cross-validation. Unlike the purely data-driven ANN, the PGNN incorporates experimentally derived thermofluid and thermodynamic consistency relationships through adaptive physics-guided loss terms, ensuring physically admissible predictions without directly solving governing partial differential equations. Findings Experimental results show that the tube-side Nusselt number increases with hot-water flow rate, whereas the shell-side Nusselt number decreases. The 6.4 mm helical tube generally provides higher tube-side heat transfer a…

Reform and Practice of Modern Cryptography Courses in Integrated Undergraduate–Graduate Cybersecurity Education: Science–Education Integration and AI as Dual Drivers
abstract: In order to tackle the problems that exist in integrated undergraduate–graduate cybersecurity education at provincial universities with significant differences in the level of student preparedness, lack of coherence between undergraduate and graduate programs, inability to transform the results of faculty research into instructional resources, and disjointed use of artificial intelligence, the given study uses the Modern Cryptography course which is provided to the undergraduate students, the academic master’s students and the professional master’s students in Cybersecurity at Heilongjiang University as a case study. Design-based action research methodology was employed in order to form a three-level curriculum chain of undergraduate foundations, undergraduate–graduate articulation, and advanced graduate-level research training. Moreover, a four-step mechanism for transforming research outputs into teaching resources was devised, consisting of selecting the research outcome, pedagogical adaptation, implementation in the classroom, and iterative feedback. AI-based learning diagnostics, literature assistance, and learning behavior recording were incorporated in the entire process of instruction. Five dimensions of process-oriented assessment were developed, namely: theoretical knowledge, practical skill, research-focused reading and participation in tasks, innovation capacity, an…

title: Wastewater Treatment Plants as Anchor Infrastructure for Geothermal Energy in Cold Regions
abstract: Abstract Thermal constraints in cold regions suppress biological treatment, increase energy demand, and elevate greenhouse gas emissions of existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and remain a major barrier to the deployment of adequate sanitation infrastructure in many cold-region communities. Where geothermal resources exist, low-enthalpy hydrothermal heat is well matched to this energy gap. Yet, WWTPs are underrecognized anchors for broader geothermal deployment, providing a continuous, weather-independent thermal offtake through which subsurface CAPEX can be amortized. We reframe geothermal-WWTP integration as a system-level enabler that benefits both parts. Using three cascaded configurations for a full-scale WWTP, a rapid techno-economic analysis identifies three trends: energy and carbon savings/revenues alone are insufficient under realistic policy stacks, whereas crediting the upgrade-deferral value of geothermally enhanced treatment makes the project economically favorable across most policy scenarios. Globally, this triple intersection encompasses ∼11,600 catalogued WWTPs serving ∼280 million people, with a further estimate of ∼48 million people in the same regions beyond current service radii. The opportunity is greatest in cold, remote, and underserved communities, where local geothermal resources, treatment intensification, and community-scale demand togethe…

title: Stablecoins as a Means of Payment. Prospects for Integration into the Existing Legal System of the Russian Federation
abstract: The article is devoted to the issues of legal regulation of stablecoins as a means of settlement. The foreign experience of introducing stablecoins into financial markets is analyzed, as a result of which it is concluded that approaches to regulating their circulation are different. A number of countries are creating a new legal architecture for the creation and circulation of stablecoins, while others, on the contrary, use existing legal regulation mechanisms. The Bank of Russia's approaches to the legal nature of stablecoins and the doctrinal definitions of Russian and foreign scientists were also analyzed, the comparison of which allowed the author to classify them as a type of digital financial assets from the point of view of current Russian legislation.

title: Investigating the efficiency of rural industrial integration development in China: based on the undesirable super-efficiency SBM-Malmquist model
abstract: Promoting rural industrial integration development (RIID) to boost farmers’ income is a core strategy for rural revitalization and common prosperity. A reasonable and objective evaluation of RIID efficiency that jointly accounts for farmers’ income growth and the food-security and environmental constraints entailed by integration is critical for advancing sustainable rural development. This paper applies the super-efficiency SBM model with undesirable outputs and the Malmquist index to measure China’s RIID efficiency across 30 provinces from 2012 to 2023, analyzing its spatio-temporal evolution. The results show that the national annual average RIID efficiency fluctuated between 0.423 and 0.663, exhibiting a three-stage trajectory of “steady rise—fluctuating bottoming-out—accelerated climb” alongside a descriptively observed east–central–west gradient (eastern leading, central following, western lagging) that does not attain statistical significance. The annual average Malmquist index reached 1.060, corresponding to an average annual growth rate of 6.0%, and efficiency catch-up became the dominant driver of productivity growth in the later stage. The exploratory regression further reveals that rural human capital and transportation infrastructure are significantly and positively associated with RIID efficiency. This study integrates farmers’ income growth, farmland non-grain co…

title: Collisional passing alpha energy transport in nearly quasisymmetric stellarators
abstract: Recent advances in stellarator optimisation have found nearly precise quasisymmetric configurations. These are expected to reduce the non-turbulent background plasma transport to acceptable neoclassical levels while removing nearly all collisionless direct orbit losses of alpha particles. Yet, alpha particles under resonant conditions can be very sensitive to collisions, causing concerning energy losses and damaging plasma facing components. For the passing alphas such resonances can happen near rational surfaces in the presence of helical error field departures from quasisymmetry that change the magnetic field direction and magnitude. The cancellation between streaming motion and tangential drift of the alphas enhances the effective collision frequency, allowing the formation of a collisional boundary layer and giving rise to a perturbed distribution function. We develop an analytical model to illustrate and evaluate the resonant plateau transport this mechanism causes by formulating a drift kinetic treatment. The results indicate the associated particle and energy losses can become significant in the vicinity of rational surfaces at values of q equals m divided by n q = m / n $q=m/n$ when error fields with poloidal and toroidal numbers m m $m$ and n n $n$ are present. In addition, we investigate the validity of the quasilinear approximation to the energy flux to show that it …

title: Between vision and realisation: a policy design diagnosis of SDG integration in Saudi Arabia’s higher education transformation
abstract: Purpose This study examines how Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 higher education reforms structure incentives for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) integration. It offers a diagnostic analysis of how policy design features – especially clarity and ambiguity – shape institutional responses to transversal sustainability agendas and the reform’s contribution to economic diversification. Design/methodology/approach Using qualitative analysis of 42 documents across four tiers – national policies, institutional plans, external evaluations and performance data (2016–2024) – the study applies Matland’s (1995) ambiguity–conflict framework. A hybrid deductive-inductive coding framework operationalises his dimensions, grounded in evidence of temporal, procedural and metric tensions. Findings The diagnostic reveals a policy configuration marked by high clarity on economic ends but interpretive ambiguity in operational means, with latent structural conflict between centralised accountability and professional discretion. Evidence from five universities, ministry dashboards and external evaluations aligns with Matland’s symbolic implementation quadrant: institutions prioritise demonstrable compliance over risk-intensive innovation. SDG mapping and ranking participation outweigh curriculum redesign and interdisciplinary research. Originality/value Reframing the implementation gap as a design patho…

Tuning CO2 Hydrogenation to Carbon Monoxide over Cu@SiO2: The Critical Role of Trace ZnO
abstract: Abstract Selective CO2 hydrogenation to CO via reverse water–gas shift is severely restricted by competing methanol synthesis over Cu@SiO2 catalysts, owing to stable Cu–O–Si linkages that favor formate intermediates. Herein, trace ZnO introduction is proposed to precisely tune catalytic pathways. Characterizations verify trace ZnO disrupts Cu–O–Si bonds, generating highly dispersed metallic Cu0 sites. In-situ DRIFTS demonstrates suppressed formate accumulation and accelerated formate decomposition into CO after ZnO modification. The Cu-0.02ZnO@SiO2 catalyst achieves the optimal performance with 10.4% CO2 conversion, 85.5% CO selectivity and a CO space-time yield of 11.2 mmolCO·gcat–1·h–1. Excess ZnO may induce Cu agglomeration and probable Cu–ZnO interface formation, shifting product preference back to methanol. This study offers a simple strategy using minor metal oxide additives to regulate CO2 hydrogenation selectivity for CO production.

title: DeepANFIS: an interpretable and uncertainty-aware neuro-fuzzy framework for energy disaggregation in smart microgrids
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) facilitates appliance-level energy disambiguation based on aggregate power consumption measurements and is an important facilitator of energy efficiency and demand-side management. However, state-of-the-art NILM methods tend to have low interpretability, low sensitivity to the sampling rate, and difficulty in providing reliable uncertainty information, which delay their effectiveness in practical implementations. To address these issues, we present a new deep adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (DeepANFIS) for joint appliance-state identification and power estimation with enhanced interpretability and uncertainty awareness. The proposed system comprehensively incorporates modular convolutional feature learning with multiple resolutions, fuzzy memory networks with temporal dependencies, hierarchical fuzzy inference, and evidential deep learning. Extensive experiments were conducted on both the UK-DALE dataset and REDD to illustrate the efficacy of DeepANFIS under high-frequency and low-frequency sampling schemes. On the UK-DALE dataset, DeepANFIS attained an F1-score of 0.7122 with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 25.63 W at a sampling frequency of 6 s, along with an F1-score of 0.8371 and a root mean-squared error (RMSE) of 78.03 W at a sampling frequency of 15 min. On the REDD, DeepANFIS obtained a near-perfect F1-score of 0.9869 with an ac…

title: Optimal energy storage configuration for multi-energy microgrids based on hybrid multi-stage robust optimization
abstract: The source-load uncertainty of a multi-energy microgrid shows markedly different fluctuation characteristics across operating scenarios, which makes an energy storage configuration that balances economy and reliability difficult to obtain. This study proposes an optimal energy storage configuration model for multi-energy microgrids based on hybrid multi-stage robust optimization. An electricity–heat–hydrogen multi-energy microgrid model is first established, and its objective minimizes the sum of the annualized storage investment cost and operation cost. A comprehensive-norm ambiguity set constructed from a 1- and an ∞ -norm constraint then characterizes the uncertainty of the scenario probability distribution, a box uncertainty set with an uncertainty budget characterizes the source-load fluctuation within each scenario, and a min–max–max–min hybrid multi-stage stochastic-robust storage capacity model that accounts for the worst-case scenario probability is formulated. Finally, the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm decomposes the model into a master problem and two-level subproblems that are solved iteratively, and the intra-scenario max-min bilevel problem is transformed into an equivalent single-level problem through Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions. Case studies show that the proposed method hedges against both the source-load output uncertainty and t…

title: Pore Engineering of IL@MOF-Derived Carbons via IL-Assisted Double Templating for CO2 Separation
abstract: Abstract The mitigation of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions requires adsorbent materials with tunable pore structures capable of balancing adsorption capacity and selectivity under postcombustion conditions. In this work, a proof-of-concept IL-assisted double-templating strategy is presented to engineer porosity in IL@MOF-derived carbons. The metal–organic framework (MOF) Cu-BTC was used as both carbon precursor and primary template, while the ionic liquid (IL) [C6MIM][B(CN)4] was used as a secondary sacrificial template at low loadings (1–10 wt %). IL@MOF composites with varying IL contents were prepared, carbonized, and subsequently acid-washed to remove residual copper-containing phases formed during carbonization. This enabled the evaluation of how IL loading influences the resulting carbon pore structure and adsorption behavior. Porosimetric characterization shows that IL incorporation promoted the development of additional (ultra)microporosity while simultaneously reducing total accessible pore volume at higher loadings, strongly influencing gas adsorption behavior. CO2 and N2 adsorption–desorption measurements at 303 K revealed a nonmonotonic dependence of CO2 adsorption capacity on IL loading, with a maximum at 2 wt % IL. At higher IL contents, the reduction in accessible pore volume limited adsorption capacity. In contrast, ideal CO2/N2 selectivity at 1 bar increased pro…

title: Structuring strategies for big data analytics and lean six sigma integration in circular construction supply chains
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, validate and structure strategies for integrating big data analytics (BDA) and lean six sigma (LSS) to support circular economy (CE) adoption in construction supply chains. It aims to provide a prioritised strategy framework for sequencing BDA–LSS adoption. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach. Firstly, strategies for promoting BDA–LSS integration CSCs were identified through an extensive literature review and expert consultation. Secondly, the fuzzy delphi method was applied to screen and validate the strategies based on expert consensus, reducing the preliminary list to 24 retained strategies. Thirdly, interpretive structural modelling was used to unfold the direct and hidden interactions among the validated strategies. Finally, Matrice d’Impacts Croisés Multiplication Appliquée à un Classement analysis was applied to classify the strategies into “driving”, “linkage” and “dependent” clusters. The natural resource-based view and institutional theory were used to interpret the results. Findings The findings identify “Integrate BDA–LSS into national plans” and “Top management support” as the strongest system drivers, with each strategy recording the maximum driving power of 24 and the minimum dependence power of two. “Provide targeted financial incentives” and “Advocate for collaborati…

title: Ad-Lib: An Adsorption-Energy Descriptor Library for Physically Interpretable Catalyst Informatics
abstract: Abstract A central challenge in heterogeneous catalyst informatics is developing descriptors that capture catalyst behavior while remaining physically interpretable. Catalyst–reaction-species interactions provide a basis for representing heterogeneous catalytic reactions. Here, a high-throughput density functional theory adsorption-energy library (Ad-Lib) is constructed, and designed descriptors are applied to oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) and CO2 methanation, with OCM as the principal case study. Mapping catalysts in an adsorption-energy-defined interaction space provides a landscape of catalytic performance. The utility of this representation for describing catalytic behavior is further demonstrated through machine learning and SHAP analysis. This work establishes the multidimensional adsorption-energy space as a reaction-informed, physically grounded framework for heterogeneous catalyst informatics.

title: Middle East war-driven energy supply disruptions could influence air pollution in India and China
abstract: Abstract Rapid economic growth has increased energy demand to ~ 11,000 TWh in India and ~ 50,000 TWh in China, where coal accounts for 57.5% and 54.79% of total energy consumption, respectively. Both countries also depend strongly on imported oil, with ~ 45% of India’s and ~ 54% of China’s crude-oil imports originating from the Middle East, creating vulnerability to geopolitical energy-supply disruptions. Here, we investigate whether such disruptions could influence regional air pollution by integrating energy data, sector-resolved emissions, GEOS-Chem simulations, and satellite observations. CEDS indicates SO 2 emissions of ~ 9.15 Mt yr −1 in India and ~ 10.61 Mt yr −1 in China, while GEOS-Chem simulations indicate considerable power-sector contributions to aerosol loading over major energy-producing regions. TROPOMI observations show SO 2 column enhancements of up to ~ 0.6–0.8 DU during the conflict period relative to the corresponding non-conflict reference period. Sulfate constitutes ~ 48% and ~ 42% of aerosol loading over India and China, respectively. However, these SO 2 enhancements cannot be uniquely attributed to increased coal combustion or the Middle East conflict because contemporaneous coal-generation changes were not quantified and atmospheric SO 2 is influenced by multiple emission sources and meteorological processes. The combined evidence therefore identifies a…

title: HỘI NHẬP KINH TẾ QUỐC TẾ CỦA VIỆT NAM - NHỮNG VẤN ĐỀ ĐẶT RA TRONG GIAI ĐOẠN HIỆN NAY
abstract: Sau 40 năm thực hiện công cuộc đổi mới, Việt Nam đã đạt được những thành tựu to lớn trong hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế với những chuyển biến sâu sắc cả về lý luận và thực tiễn, từ chủ trương mở cửa, phá thế bao vây sang chủ động hội nhập, hội nhập toàn diện và hướng tới tự chủ chiến lược, tham gia định hình luật chơi. Tiến trình này góp phần mở rộng không gian phát triển, thúc đẩy cải cách, thu hút nguồn lực và nâng cao vị thế quốc gia. Tuy nhiên, năng lực nội sinh, mức độ tham gia chuỗi giá trị, tính tự chủ chiến lược, chất lượng thực thi cam kết và khả năng quản trị rủi ro còn hạn chế. Bài viết khái quát bốn giai đoạn phát triển, những thành tựu, hạn chế và các vấn đề lớn đặt ra đối với hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế của Việt Nam trong giai đoạn hiện nay. Trên cơ sở đó, bài viết đề xuất chuyển trọng tâm hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế sang việc chuyển hóa kết quả hội nhập thành tiến bộ công nghệ, năng suất cao hơn, sức chống chịu mạnh hơn và vị thế quốc gia được nâng cao. Từ khóa: hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế; độc lập, tự chủ; nội lực

Design Thinking Lesson Exemplars in Basic Education Toward a Transformative Instruction
abstract: Background: Lesson exemplars (LEs) present teachers' best practices for quality instruction, serving as a benchmark for others to innovate in their own classrooms, bringing transformative experiences that foster meaningful, lifelong learning.Aims: In this study, LEs were developed and validated, aligning with the design thinking (DT) as an instructional model.Methods: Descriptive development research was used as the study design, in which three developed LEs were validated by 10 expert teachers with respect to objectives, subject matter, procedures, evaluation, and assignment/agreement/take-home activities. The developed validation tool was then further validated by three expert educators, and the results were analyzed using Kappa Statistics (CVI=1.00; excellent). Moreover, the results of the dry run conducted with ten (10) teachers were analyzed using Cronbach’s Alpha to determine the instrument's reliability (α=0.8559; good). For the analysis of the results, descriptive statistics, such as mean, standard deviation, and rank, were used.Result: The study developed and validated design thinking-based lesson exemplars, making teachers capably blend the iterative, student-centered phases of design thinking (understanding, exploring, materializing) with the structured framework of conventional lesson plans, and received strong approval from teacher-experts for fostering creativity,…

Cultural and Digital Readiness for AI-Integrated Higher Education: A C-TAM-Informed Curriculum Design Framework
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) requires higher education institutions to redesign curricula, assessments, and student support rather than merely authorize or prohibit a new tool. This article develops a Cultural-Technology Acceptance Model (C-TAM) as a theory-building curriculum framework. It integrates current studies of university students’ GenAI use with established technology-acceptance research, cross-cultural scholarship, AI-literacy frameworks, backward design, constructive alignment, and assessment reform. The revision explicitly limits the role of pre-GenAI evidence. Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2018 and World Values Survey (WVS) Wave 7 indicators are treated as contextual evidence about the digital and cultural readiness pipeline entering higher education; they are not treated as measures of GenAI acceptance, and no cross-national structural equation model is estimated from them. The synthesis identifies five mechanisms that curriculum designers should anticipate: perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and AI competence, attitudes shaped by trust and ethical risk, social and institutional norms, and culturally patterned expectations about uncertainty and authority. These mechanisms are translated through backward design into aligned learning outcomes, assessment evidence, pedagogy, and support. An AI-Ready Curriculum Reconstru…

title: Classroom physical design and the use of digital technologies: an exploratory observational study across educational stages
abstract: The integration of digital technologies (DT) in education has become a priority for education systems, yet the mere availability of devices does not guarantee their use in the classroom. This exploratory study analyzes the relationship between classroom physical design and the use of digital technologies in real educational practices, drawing on the Pedagogy-Space-Technology (PST) framework, and additionally examines whether the type of session is associated with differences in technology use. A quantitative, cross-sectional observational study was conducted through direct observation of 121 classrooms in Spain and Andorra, from early childhood to higher education. Because classrooms across these stages are not comparable units, analyses were disaggregated into three blocks, with 83 classrooms providing valid technology-use data: early childhood and primary ( n = 21), secondary and vocational ( n = 33), and higher education ( n = 29). Associations between furniture flexibility, physical environment, spatial organization and technology use were tested with Kendall's tau-b, with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment within blocks, and differences by session type with the Kruskal–Wallis test. The pattern of associations differed across blocks. In early childhood and primary education, only the quality of the physical environment was associated with technology use ( τ = 0.673). In secondar…

title: Recycling Medical Intravenous Infusion Bags into Sharps Containers: Process Design and System Implementation
abstract: In 2024, Taiwan generated approximately 130,000 metric tons (MT) of medical waste, including about 42,000 MT of hazardous waste. Despite the implementation of circular economy initiatives, most of the medical waste is still incinerated and landfilled, thereby increasing the environmental burden through dioxin emissions and secondary pollution. Current recycling practices are aimed at converting medical plastics into secondary products but face logistical and operational challenges. This study developed a circular recycling system for medical intravenous (IV) infusion bags in Taiwan. In collaboration with two medical institutions, used IV bags were collected, sorted, cleaned, and reprocessed into recycled plastic pellets via a patented recycling-and-pelletization process. The pellets were incorporated into sharps containers, which were returned to participating hospitals, thus establishing a circular material pathway within the healthcare sector. The entire process was independently verified for traceability and regulatory compliance. The containers were assessed for recycled content, safety performance, and cradle-to-gate carbon footprint. The containers complied with ISO 14021 and ISO 23907-1 and were adopted by two hospitals in northern Taiwan. The carbon footprint was estimated as 1.852 kg CO 2 -eq per container, comprising 1.587 kg CO 2 -eq from raw-material acquisition and…

Multidisciplinary collaboration and workflows on heritage building information modelling (HBIM) projects: a framework for improvement
abstract: Purpose Heritage building information modelling (HBIM) projects face significant challenges, especially in relation to multidisciplinary collaboration and project workflows. This paper aims to examine HBIM work processes, presenting a practical framework to improve HBIM workflows and multidisciplinary collaboration occurring on construction heritage projects. Design/methodology/approach An initial deductive literature review provides a foundation for the study by identifying thematic HBIM industry challenges. An inductive, interpretivist and qualitative examination of HBIM combines survey questionnaire with case study and in-depth interviews to provide a holistic understanding of the opportunities and challenges confronting practitioners. Findings Findings indicate that HBIM offers great potential for improving heritage protection, but challenges around data management, human factors, technical issues and training skills remain. A resulting framework for improvement identifies five key outcomes around which improvement depends: team coordination; sharing of knowledge; standards and industry specifications; technical tools and training/education. Recommendations are rooted to case study evidence and practitioner opinion; the paper highlights the need for further research to refine practices globally. Originality/value The research contributes to the Heritage Building Information…

title: An AI-Integrated Constructivist Learning Environment Framework for Thai as a Second Language in Higher Education: Design and Expert Review
abstract: Digital technology is now central to higher education, yet learner engagement is usually measured as an outcome after instruction rather than designed into the learning environment. This study designs an AI-integrated constructivist learning environment (CLE) framework for promoting learning engagement and creative writing, referred to here as the CLE-EW framework, for Chinese university learners of Thai as a second language. The study followed design and development research (DDR). It combined an integrative literature synthesis, a contextual analysis, a theory-driven design synthesis, and expert review. The contextual analysis took place at two universities in Yunnan Province, China, with 120 third-year Thai majors, their two writing instructors, and four support staff. The framework has seven interrelated centers: Problem Base, Learning Resources, Cognitive Tools, Collaboration, Promoting Learning Engagement and Creative Writing, Scaffolding, and Coaching. AI is used in five centers in three bounded forms (rule-based formative feedback, a retrieval-based answer system, and an external generative tool used to seek, collect, organize, and integrate information), while the Collaboration and Coaching Centers are human-led. The rule-based and retrieval-based forms run in the learner’s browser and send no learner writing to an external service. Five experts rated the framewo…

title: Design and User Evaluation of a Mobile-Based Virtual Reality Application for English Vocabulary Learning in Elementary Students
abstract: English vocabulary mastery among elementary school students in Indonesia remains limited, particularly in recognizing everyday household objects, due to conventional teaching methods that rely on passive approaches and the lack of engaging interactive learning media. Although prior work has proposed several virtual reality (VR) applications for vocabulary learning, most stop at content visualization and have not been systematically evaluated using a psychometrically validated instrument designed for child users. This study addresses that gap by designing, developing, and evaluating a mobile-based VR application for fourth-grade students, and by examining (RQ1) the extent to which the application satisfies end-user requirements across five EUCS dimensions, (RQ2) whether the child-adapted instrument is valid and reliable when applied to primary-school respondents, and (RQ3) which dimension yields the lowest score and what design implications it reveals. The application was developed using the Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) method, with content adapted from the independent curriculum and focused on household-object vocabulary. The evaluation employed User Acceptance Testing comprising alpha testing using a black-box matrix and beta testing involving 51 fourth-grade students. User satisfaction was measured using a child-adapted End User Computing Satisfaction (EUCS) instr…

title: Baculovirus-Mediated Expression and Functional Characterization of a Glycyrrhizin-Specific Single-Chain Variable Fragment in Sf9 Cells
abstract: Abstract Background Glycyrrhizin (GC) is a major bioactive saponin in licorice plants ( Glycyrrhiza spp.). A GC-specific single-chain variable fragment (GC-scFv) was constructed from anti-GC monoclonal antibody 2H2. To obtain a soluble recombinant recognition reagent for GC immunoassays, GC-scFv was expressed using a baculovirus–insect cell platform. Methods The variable heavy- and light-chain genes were amplified from 2H2 hybridoma-derived complementary DNA (cDNA) and assembled using a (Gly 4 Ser) 3 linker. The construct was transferred through pET-28a(+) and pCold I into pFastBac1Mel, which contains the honeybee melittin signal sequence for secretion in Sf9 insect cells. GC-scFv was recovered by nickel-chelate affinity chromatography and characterized using indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (icELISA). The calibration curve was analyzed by semi-logarithmic regression using triplicate wells at each concentration. Results An anti-T7-tag Western blot detected GC-scFv at approximately 29 kDa in the eluate recovered from culture medium. Free GC produced concentration-dependent inhibition, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 0.46 μg/mL and a semi-logarithmic calibration interval of 0.0488–3.125 μg/mL. The apparent limit of detection and apparent limit of quantification, defined as 10% and 20% inhibition, were 54.2 and 92.8 ng/mL, respectivel…

title: The impact of virtual reality and augmented reality on global brand transformation: insights from immersive advertising among Nepalese adolescents
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) marketing communication on consumer engagement, perceived diagnosticity, brand attitude and purchase intention in an emerging market context. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 408 consumers aged 18 years and above across five cities in Nepal who were exposed to real-world AR and VR brand marketing content. The proposed relationships were tested using structural equation modelling. Findings Perceived immersion significantly enhances consumer engagement and perceived diagnosticity. Both factors positively influence brand attitude, which in turn drives purchase intention. Brand attitude emerged as the strongest direct predictor of purchase intention. The findings indicate significant consumer responses to AR/VR marketing communications, although the effects are statistically small and should be interpreted in light of the passive exposure design. Practical implications This study suggests that AR and VR can effectively enhance consumer engagement and brand attitude by providing immersive and informative product experiences. Marketers should focus on designing interactive and easy-to-use content that clearly demonstrates product benefits. Since brand attitude strongly drives purchase intention, immersive campaigns should prioritise building positive brand perceptions.…

title: Physicochemical, microbial, and sensory characterization of quinoa-based vegan yogurt as a functional plant-based fermented product
abstract: Background This study aimed to develop quinoa-based vegan yogurt products in response to the increasing interest in plant-based diets and to evaluate their sensory, chemical, and microbiological properties. Methods In the first phase, four quinoa-based yogurt formulations were prepared using different starter culture and activation strategies, and fermented under controlled conditions. In the second phase, samples were subjected to sensory analysis by 12 trained panelists and 80 consumer panelists, evaluating appearance, taste, color, aroma, texture, flavor, and overall acceptability. Additionally, functional properties (total phenolic content [TPC] and antioxidant capacity [CUPRAC]) and proximate compositions (crude protein, total fat, and moisture content) were analyzed and compared with a commercially available rice-based vegan yogurt. Results The findings indicated that quinoa-based vegan yogurts are a promising alternative in terms of nutritional value, functional properties, and sensory acceptability. Microbiological analyses revealed viable lactic acid bacteria (LAB) counts ranging from 6.9 to 8.2 log CFU/g, confirming successful fermentation. title: Genetic diversity analysis using phenotypic and SSR markers with trait association and multivariate analysis in cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp.) genotypes
abstract: The low productivity of cowpea is primarily attributed to inadequate utilisation of genetic diversity for the improvement of local cultivars. The present study was conducted to assess genetic diversity utilising 17 yield and biochemical traits along with simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers. Fifty cowpea genotypes were assessed during summer 2024 at Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), India. Genotypes were planted with three replications in a randomised block design. Significant genetic variability was observed in the studied traits. The minimal differences between phenotypic and genotypic coefficients of variation (CV) indicated that the observed variation primarily stemmed from the genetic component. Most traits showed high heritability, with varying levels of genetic advance. Trait association revealed a positive interrelationship among yield-contributing traits, suggesting their utility for selection for cowpea yield improvement. Cluster I possessed better-performing genotypes for yield traits. Principal component analysis emphasised that pods per cluster (PCL), pods per plant (PPL) and clusters per plant (CPL) were the major contributing traits in principal component 1 (PC1). Out of 64 SSR markers screened, 40 showed successful amplification and 18 were highly polymorphic and used for diversity analysis, with an average of 2.94 alleles per mark…

A Fatigue Simulation Approach for Long-Crack Propagation Phase of Radial Tires Using Modified Virtual Crack Closure Technique
abstract: ABSTRACT Tire fatigue failure involves short-crack initiation and long-crack propagation. While the crack energy density effectively predicts short-crack propagation, the simulation of long-crack propagation requires improvement. In this study, we propose a fatigue simulation approach for radial tires using the modified virtual crack closure technique. We prefabricate cracks via hybrid submodel-composite modeling (tie constraint), calculate the strain energy release rate with the modified crack closure technique, and predict crack propagation. Groove crack experiments and finite element simulations on two all-steel radial truck tires verified the effectiveness of this approach. The approach provides a reliable tool for fatigue evaluation, aiding tire durability design and life prediction.

title: Administrative Offenses Constituting in Infringement upon Public Order and Public Safety in the Virtual Space (on the Example of the Russian Federation and the Republic of Tajikistan)
abstract: This article provides a comparative legal analysis of administrative offenses that infringe upon public order and public safety in the virtual space of Russia and Tajikistan. It argues that virtual space possesses characteristics of a public space, but is not identical to it. The fragmentary nature of Tajikistan’s legislation is highlighted, and the authors propose adopting Russian experience to improve the Code of Administrative Offenses of the Republic of Tajikistan, taking into account the principles of legality and proportionality.

abstract: The article presents a socio-philosophical analysis of pacifism and anti-pacifism in secular and religious discourses on war. It traces the evolution of conceptions of violence from its sacralization in religious tradition and its rationalization in the theory of just war to contemporary concepts of nonviolence, moral realism, and the ethical-political critique of the cult of power. Particular attention is paid to the relationship between pacifist and anti-pacifist positions in Christian thought, specifically in the Catholic and Protestant traditions, as well as their correlation with secular concepts of power, war, and political responsibility. Based on an analysis of Judith Butler’s works, the study argues that nonviolence should be viewed not as a manifestation of passivity or moral idealism, but as an active ethical-political practice capable of countering structural violence, affirming social equality, and fostering new forms of solidarity. It is shown that recognizing human vulnerability, interdependence, and the value of every life creates the foundation for rethinking the politics of peace beyond the logic of domination and coercion. The Ukrainian context is analyzed separately, in which the current war has prompted a reevaluation of the relationship between pacifism, the right to self-defense, and civic responsibility. title: Reconfiguring power, trust, and identity in early contractor involvement
abstract: Purpose Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) has emerged as a pivotal mechanism for improving efficiency, innovation, and risk management in complex construction projects, yet its theoretical and institutional foundations remain unsettled. While ECI has been embedded in national procurement reforms and digital collaboration frameworks, persistent gaps remain in cross-jurisdictional validation, governance modelling, and measurement of long-term value. Design/methodology/approach This study presents the most comprehensive systematic mapping of ECI scholarship to date, integrating an 80-paper corpus across three analytical phases spanning 2009–2025, supported by a 100-paper global construction challenge dataset used for contextual comparison. Using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-based screening, bibliometric network mapping, and thematic synthesis, the evaluation identifies how ECI research has evolved from descriptive analyses of delivery performance toward deeper theorisation of governance, identity, trust, and procurement. Findings Results reveal that ECI is consistently positioned as a corrective to chronic industry inefficiencies, such as cost overruns, schedule delays, and design fragmentation- but that empirical studies remain regionally concentrated and methodologically fragmented. title: DESIGN AND DEVELOP A PIEZOELECTRIC POWER GENERATOR AND ENERGY HARVESTER UTILIZING HUMAN FOOTSTEPS
abstract: The development of sustainable energy technologies has encouraged the exploration of alternative methods for converting mechanical energy into electrical energy. One promising approach is piezoelectric energy harvesting, which utilizes the pressure generated by human footsteps to produce electrical output. This research aimed to design and developed a piezoelectric power generator prototype and evaluate its voltage output under different human-weight conditions. An experimental research design was employed, involving five participants with body weights ranging from 56 kg to 62 kg. Each participant performed footstep pressure tests on the prototype at a consistent walking pace, with voltage measurements recorded using a digital multimeter across three one-minute trials. The results showed an increasing trend in voltage output as participant weight increased, with average outputs ranging from 10.2 V at 56 kg to 16.3 V at 62 kg. Linear regression analysis revealed a strong positive relationship between participant weight and voltage output, with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.9815. The resulting regression equation was y = 0.9991x – 45.368. These findings demonstrate the potential of the developed prototype to generate electrical voltage from human footsteps. Further improvements in material selection, circuit design, energy storage, and prototype durability are recommen…

title: Comparative assessment of freshly cultured microbial bioproducts and a seaweed-based biostimulant for plant growth promotion and root-knot nematode management in capsicum and spinach in Kenya
abstract: Summary Root-knot nematodes (RKN; Meloidogyne spp.) are among the most damaging pathogens of vegetable crops worldwide. They damage roots and reduce yield, with their management becoming challenging because of their wide host range. This study evaluated three microbial bioproducts, Mytech ® ( Purpureocillium lilacinum ), Trichotech ® ( Trichoderma asperellum ) and Regain ® ( Bacillus subtilis ) and a seaweed-based biostimulant (Maximizer ® ) for growth promotion and RKN management in capsicum and spinach. The fungal and bacterial bioproducts were cultured to provide fresh inocula for each experimental trial. In RKN-free pot experiments, Mytech ® and Trichotech ® consistently improved plant height, shoot and root fresh weight and total plant weight in capsicum, whereas Regain ® and Mytech ® enhanced plant height, shoot fresh weight and total plant weight in spinach compared with the non-treated control. In RKN-infected pot experiments, where microbial bioproducts or the seaweed-based biostimulant were applied before nematode inoculation, all treatments using bioproducts and biostimulant improved growth parameters, although responses varied between crops and repeated experiments. All bioproducts and biostimulant treatments significantly reduced nematode infection in both crops.
