Communal verification in group musical competition (douyue): peer evaluation, inter-society authority, and relational outcomes in the traditional Chinese music practice of Xi’an Guyue
abstract: This Hypothesis and Theory article examines group musical competition ( douyue 斗乐) in Xi’an Guyue 西安鼓乐, a tradition of Chinese instrumental ensemble music played by local music societies in and around Xi’an. In douyue , two or more societies perform for, and in response to, one another, either simultaneously from facing positions or in turn on a shared stage, while fellow musicians, elders, and local audiences listen, compare, and comment. The article asks how a society’s musical standing, recognized by its own members, comes to be acknowledged or questioned by other societies, and how this process may affect musicians’ relationships and wellbeing. To address this question, it introduces the concept of communal verification: a provisional, shared appraisal by a knowledgeable community of whether a specific claim made through performance, such as command of a multi-section suite, stylistic accuracy, or ensemble control, is convincing, open to question, or not yet settled. Such appraisals are more likely when performances can be compared, are assessed by what is heard against standards that participants recognize, and remain open to response and later revision. Communal verification differs from simply winning a contest or receiving a score. Under fair and respectful conditions, it may help performers feel heard and respected, whether their claim is recognized or questioned, and …

title: Renewable-Energy-Based Global Supply Chain Network Design for Greenhouse Gas Reduction: A Comparison of Different Assembly Products
abstract: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in global supply chains can be reduced by introducing renewable energy (RE) systems such as solar power generation systems. Some manufacturers commit themselves to the RE100 global initiative that encourages companies to source 100% of the electricity used in their business operations from RE. Thus, suppliers will face the risks of contract termination if suppliers fail to satisfy the target RE utilization rate to reduce GHG emissions. Besides costs, GHG emissions from electricity consumption during component production and GHG emissions from material production differ among suppliers due to differences in the availability of RE and regional energy mixes. Hence, in this study, we proposed a RE-based global supply chain network to reduce GHG emissions using an optimization model to satisfy the target RE utilization rate and GHG reduction rate simultaneously, where we considered the GHG emissions from electricity consumption and material production. In our model, the suppliers were allowed to purchase electricity generated by non-RE systems when they could not fulfill the electricity required to manufacture components from RE systems. We compared the RE utilization rate, GHG emissions, and total cost for two products (laptop and vacuum cleaner). title: AI-driven real-time control architecture for hybrid battery and supercapacitor systems to enhance frequency regulation in high renewable microgrids
abstract: A The growing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation in microgrids poses problems of fast-changing power and low inertia, which pose challenges for frequency regulation. Although traditional battery energy storage systems have the capacity for providing continuous energy supply, they might be subjected to increased stress due to the charging and discharging activities in response to high-frequency disturbances. The current paper aims at presenting an artificial intelligence-based real-time control architecture for the coordinated operation of a battery-supercapacitor hybrid energy storage system in a microgrid characterized by a high penetration of renewable energy sources. The developed architecture is able to make the necessary adjustments based on the values of frequency deviation, rate of change of frequency, renewable generation, load demands, battery state of charge, and supercapacitor voltage. The proposed scheme was simulated using MATLAB/Simulink under the conditions of moderately varying renewable sources, sudden load disturbances, highly intermittent renewables, and a combination of renewable and load disturbances. The maximum frequency deviation was lowered from 0.32 Hz to 0.18 Hz (−43.8%), and the frequency settling time decreased from 4.1 s to 2.6 s (−36.5%). title: Energy distributions of precipitating electrons in Jupiter's auroral regions from combined Juno/JADE and Juno/JEDI measurements
abstract: Jupiter's auroras are produced by magnetospheric electrons precipitating into its atmosphere. The Juno/JADE and Juno/JEDI instruments together measure these electrons over the energy range 100, However, their spectra in Jupiter's auroral regions cannot be accurately reproduced by the widely used kappa distribution, hereafter referred to as the classical single-kappa distribution. We aim to statistically characterize the energy flux distributions of precipitating electrons in Jupiter's auroral regions and to derive a new phenomenological energy distribution, referred to as the 4-kappa distribution, better suited to reproduce the combined JADE+JEDI data. We builT mean electron energy flux distributions in six auroral subregions (the polar, the main, and the outer emission regions, for both hemispheres), combining JADE and JEDI data from PJ3 to PJ35. These data were mapped to the Jovian SIII reference frame using the JRM33 magnetic field model, which accounts for the contribution of the current sheet. We fitted these distributions using MCMC in logarithmic space, testing both the classical single-kappa distribution and the 4-kappa distribution. The mean distributions show an overall monotonic power-law decay, with an energy cutoff visible beyond ∼ 500, in most subregions, although a fraction of the individual spectra depart from this behavior at intermediate energies. title: A Sub-Optimal Control of a Non-linear Vibrating System Excited by a Non-ideal Energy Source
abstract: Abstract Purpose Non-Ideal Systems (NIS) are distinguished by their unique dynamic properties, which present considerable challenges to the application of conventional control techniques. The present study examines non-ideal excitation sources with limited power. Nonlinear phenomena were observed in a range of applications, providing insights for future NIS engineering. Methods The governing equations of Non-Ideal Systems (NIS) with multiple degrees of freedom are derived, accounting for nonlinear damping, stiffness, and time-varying excitations. The implementation of a state-dependent Riccati equation (SDRE) control strategy is proposed as a means to optimise system stability and dynamic performance. Results For the ideal system (case 1, $$a_0 = 0$$ ), the proposed control strategy effectively regulates the system’s response, reducing amplitude and stabilizing the orbits, as confirmed by time-domain and frequency-domain analyses. For the non-ideal system (case 2, $$a_0 > 0$$ ), despite the increased excitation complexity, the controller successfully suppresses vibrations and mitigates nonlinear effects, demonstrating robust performance in both time- and frequency-domain measures. Conclusions The present study focuses on excitation sources that deviate from ideal conditions. Why Cannot Solid Cages Compress Water? A Computational Thermodynamic Activity Linking Hydrogen Storage to Water’s Anomalous Density
abstract: Abstract Core physical chemistry concepts, such as hydrogen bonding, Gibbs free energy, and configurational entropy, rarely appear within a unified pedagogical framework. This article presents an interactive web-based HTML module prompted by a genuine student question: if metal hydrides compress hydrogen, why do crystalline hydrates fail to compress water? The answer is explored through a simplified thermodynamic framework based on ideal configurational mixing entropy. The mathematical limits and maxima of this symmetric pedagogical model provide a unified way to discuss three seemingly disparate macroscopic phenomena: the anomalously low density of ice, the existence of liquid water’s density maximum, and water’s thermodynamic resistance to complete close-packing. Implemented in an upper-division undergraduate Energy Chemistry course (n = 14 enrolled junior chemistry and materials science majors), this 60 min interactive session provided evidence of conceptual gains. To evaluate mechanistic understanding beyond factual recall, student learning was assessed via a rubric-scored preactivity diagnostic and a formative capstone synthesis task. Results indicate a distinct shift in student reasoning, moving away from simple geometric heuristics (like mechanical squeezing) toward rigorous thermodynamic arguments based on Gibbs free energy minimization.

title: Financial feasibility of employee ownership under the Danish succession model
abstract: Purpose We examine the feasibility of employee-financed succession under Denmark's new framework, which lets owners transfer ownership to employees through a cooperative holding structure with deferred capital gains tax. Design/methodology/approach We develop a cash-flow model yielding closed-form feasibility conditions that incorporate the statutory dividend threshold and tax deferral, with simulations and a stochastic extension quantifying liquidity risk. Findings Feasibility turns on short-run liquidity rather than profitability. Because dividends are pro rata, funding a stake of any size requires the operating company to distribute its entire equity value; this “dividend leakage” to non-participating owners is the root of the constraint. The maximum sustainable multiple rises with payout and falls with leverage, leaving high-valuation firms unreachable; a smaller stake does not help, as feasibility is independent of the ownership share. Feasibility therefore hinges on concessions outside the dividend channel: tax-exempt seller gifts or employee contributions. Research limitations/implications The baseline abstracts from bargaining and from heterogeneity beyond payout and leverage; an appendix shows earnings risk tightens the feasible set. Practical implications The results clarify why employee buyouts are viable in some firm contexts but not others and inform the statutory …

title: Persistence of Staphylococcus epidermidis in Cardiopulmonary Bypass Circuits Primed with Plasma-Lyte A: Implications for Circuit Storage Following Contamination
abstract: Background There is limited evidence on how long cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuits can remain primed before use or when primed CPB circuits should be disposed of due to loss of sterility or instability of the priming solution. Understanding bacterial persistence in priming solutions is critical for patient safety and institutional protocols. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the survival of Staphylococcus epidermidis in Plasma-Lyte A-primed CPB circuits over time. Methods Three commercially available CPB circuits (Affinity, CAPIOX, and Inspire) from different manufacturers (Medtronic, Terumo, and LivaNova) were primed with Plasma-Lyte A inoculated with S. epidermidis (~1 CFU/mL) to simulate accidental contamination. Following brief recirculation, circuits were stored without circulation at 20–22°C. Samples were obtained aseptically from pre- and post-oxygenator sites on Days 0, 2, 4, 7, 9, and 11. Viable bacterial recovery was reported as colony-forming units per milliliter (CFU/mL) over time. Results Viable S. epidermidis was recovered from all three CPB circuits at both sampling sites through Day 11. Colony counts remained low, fluctuating between approximately 1 and 9 CFU/mL without a consistent increase over time. The highest observed count, 9 CFU/mL, occurred at the Inspire post-oxygenator sampling site on Day 7. Each measurement represented a single observation. Conc…

title: Impact of Tissue Storage on Bioanalytical Data and Live Tissue Science
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Precision oncology increasingly depends on accurate molecular and functional characterization of tumor tissue across genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, epigenetic, and live-cell applications. This review evaluates how commonly used tissue preservation methods, including formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE), fresh, flash-frozen, and cryopreserved tissue, affect downstream analytical fidelity and translational utility. Recent Findings Recent comparative studies demonstrate that FFPE remains effective for histopathology and a few established molecular assays but introduces nucleic acid fragmentation, crosslinking, deamination artifacts, protein modification, and loss of cellular viability. These effects can reduce sequencing efficiency, alter quantitative molecular measurements, and limit applications requiring intact proteins or viable cells. In contrast, flash-frozen and cryopreserved tissues generally provide greater molecular fidelity, while controlled-rate cryopreservation additionally preserves viable cellular populations for single-cell analysis, organoid development, functional precision medicine, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte expansion, and CAR-T manufacturing. Emerging evidence also supports the use of cryopreserved living tumor biobanks for longitudinal and functional testing. Summary No single preservation method is optimal for every appl…

Interfacial Origin of Mn Promotion in Ni/AlO x Catalysts for Methane Pyrolysis and Carbon Nanotube Growth
abstract: Abstract Commercial deployment of methane pyrolysis (MP) requires H2 to be produced at a high rate while the solid carbon is recovered as a marketable product such as multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). Various promoters have been explored for Ni-based MP catalysts, including Mn, but the origin of its effect has remained elusive. Here, Ni/AlOx catalysts containing 0 to 5 wt % Mn were used to separate the two roles that Mn plays in activity and stability. The amount of Ni exposed at an oxide boundary correlated with the apparent CH4 reaction order across the series, identifying the Ni–O–Mn perimeter as the site at which CH4 activation is promoted. The same perimeter converted weakly bound NiO into strongly interacting species that resisted encapsulation, linking the rate and the lifetime of the catalyst to a single interface. At 1 wt %, Mn the apparent activation energy fell from 93.9 to 84.2 kJ mol–1, the CH4 reaction order rose from 0.46 to 0.84, and the turnover number increased from 375 to 456 mol C mol Ni–1. At 2 wt %, MnOx began to bury the Ni surface, and above that loading it segregated into a separate phase, so the promotion was lost. Mn also improved the graphitization and conductivity of the MWCNTs formed at the start of the reaction, but this benefit faded as disordered carbon accumulated. title: Green Manufacturing of Iron Fluoride/Fluorinated Carbon Nanocomposite Cathodes from PTFE Waste and Iron Oxides via Mechanochemistry
abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste poses persistent environmental challenges due to its exceptional chemical stability. Meanwhile, the conversion of iron oxides, the major components of abundant natural iron ores, into advanced materials commonly involves multistep processing through refined iron precursors. Herein, we report a closed-loop mechanochemical strategy that integrates PTFE waste upcycling with direct iron oxide fluorination. Compared with conventional iron fluoride synthesis relying on hazardous HF-derived fluorochemicals and refined iron salts, this approach utilizes PTFE waste as a fluorine source and avoids fluoride-containing byproducts. During high-energy ball-milling, mechanochemical activation promotes stable C–F bond cleavage in PTFE and oxygen vacancy generation within the iron oxides. The released fluorine is captured by defect-rich iron oxides to form iron fluoride nanoparticles, while the residual PTFE framework evolves into electrochemically active fluorinated carbon containing reversible semi-ionic C–F bonds. The nanocomposite cathode delivers a capacity of 316.7 mAh g–1 with 70.5% retention after 1000 cycles at 0.25 A g–1, surpassing the one-electron theoretical capacity of FeF3 (237.0 mAh g–1). The enhanced electrochemical performance originates from the synergistic contributions of iron fluoride redox reactions and reversible Faradaic rea…

title: China's urban rail transit carbon peak: when and how – a dynamic life cycle assessment
abstract: China's rapidly expanding urban rail transit (URT) system faces significant environmental challenges, particularly regarding the inflexibility and structural nature of passengers’ urban transportation demands. It is a key issue to assess the carbon peak timeline and related technological roadmap for carbon peaking in China’s URT sector. This study conducts a comprehensive life cycle assessment to evaluate carbon dioxide emissions across different URT life cycle phases. Through input factor identification and scenario modelling, the authors investigate critical factors affecting life cycle emissions and project emission data from 2019 to 2035. The analysis results suggest that there was an 11% reduction in emissions in 2020, which is attributed to the shifts in transportation demand induced by COVID-19. Among various development scenarios, only the ambitious scenario, which involves the adoption of decarbonisation technologies and robust policy enforcement, achieves carbon peaking by 2030. To support emission management, the authors propose a multi-level framework that combines upstream data integration with goal decomposition methodology. This framework is based on macro-level sectoral assessments and the development of technology-specific roadmaps, thereby supporting the sustainability of the URT system in line with China's national climate objectives while maintaining transpo…

title: Does carbon assurance deter corporate greenwashing?
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates whether third-party carbon assurance deters corporate greenwashing. Motivated by competing theoretical perspectives, where assurance may either enhance accountability or provide symbolic legitimacy, we examine whether carbon assurance aligns firms' environmental disclosures with their actual performance. Design/methodology/approach Using 2,276 US publicly listed firm-year observations from 2007–2020, we analyse the association between carbon assurance and greenwashing, measured as the divergence between ESG disclosure and ESG performance. Findings Carbon assurance reduces greenwashing, supporting its monitoring and signalling roles. We document that environmental innovation is a channel for this relationship: carbon assurance is associated with greater environmental innovation, which in turn lowers greenwashing. The effect is concentrated in non-RGGI states and is stronger in less competitive product markets. The results are robust across alternative specifications and endogeneity tests, particularly for assurance level and percentage. Originality/value This study provides the first large-scale evidence that carbon assurance effectively curbs corporate greenwashing and identifies environmental innovation as the key mechanism. The findings inform regulators considering mandatory carbon assurance, and assist investors and creditors evaluating firms…

title: Study of the absorption and emission spectra of polymeric films colored with laser organic dyes
abstract: This study focuses on the absorption and emission (fluorescence) spectra of two organic dyes, Rhodamine and Fluorescein. The dyes are prepared as liquid samples dissolved in a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) polymer solution at different concentrations (0.01, 0.02, 0.03, and 0.04 mM). Solid samples in the form of PVA polymer films doped with Rhodamine and Fluorescein are also prepared using the casting method, in which the dyes are directly mixed with the polymer solution at different concentrations (0.01, 0.02, 0.03, and 0.04 mM), while maintaining a constant film thickness of 120 μm.The absorbance values of all prepared samples are measured using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer. The results indicate that increasing dye concentration affects the linear optical properties of the prepared samples, resulting in increased absorbance and decreased transmittance, consistent with the Beer–Lambert law. title: Evaluation of recovered Carbon black as a sustainable alternative to commercial Carbon black in solid tyre cushion compounds
abstract: Pyrolysis is a sustainable solution for waste tyre (WT) management. Recovered carbon black (rCB), is a second highest by-product of tyre pyrolysis process, contains a high amount of carbon, ash and inorganic impurities. In the present study, rCB derived from WTs was upgraded through magnetic separation, ball milling, and purified treating twice with 2M HCl and once with 2M NaOH at 60⁰C for one hour using 2 g/mL rCB: leachate ratio to obtain demineralized rCB(drCB). Both raw rCB and drCB were characterized by particle size analysis, proximate and ultimate analyses, TGA, ICP-OES, FT-IR, XRD, and iodine adsorption. The drCB exhibited a substantial reduction in ash content from 22.20% to 3.42 % (by weight) and an increase in carbon content up to 94.41 % (% wt). The upgraded drCB was subsequently incorporated into solid tyre cushion compounds as a partial replacement for commercial carbon black (CCB, N550) to evaluate industrial feasibility. Physico-mechanical properties of the drCB compound demonstrated improved modulus, tear strength, hardness, and other properties such as tensile strength, rebound resilience within the industrial standard limits. These findings confirm the technical feasibility of rCB as a partial replacement of the filler in industrial solid tyre cushion compounds, supporting circular economy concept in the rubber and tyre industry.

title: Improved Biomass Production via Enhanced Inorganic Carbon Availability Using Crystalline Calcium Silicate Hydrate in a Marine Oleaginous Diatom Cultivation for Sustainable Aviation Fuel Production
abstract: Abstract Microalgae are promising feedstocks for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) because of their high oil productivity and nonedible nature. In particular, Fistulifera solaris (F. solaris) is an oleaginous marine diatom that has attracted considerable attention as a potential feedstock for SAF production. However, low CO2 solubility limits biomass production. In addition, conventional carbonate-enrichment methods are often species-specific and carbon-intensive. In this study, cultivation using crystalline calcium silicate hydrate (cCSH), a low-cost and environmentally friendly material derived from concrete scrap and waste, was experimentally investigated to improve CO2 enrichment and biomass production. The addition of cCSH increased the dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) concentration in the medium, mainly through the accumulation of bicarbonate ions (HCO3–). In the presence of cCSH, the DIC concentration was approximately 1.5-fold higher, and the biomass production of F. solaris increased 1.4-fold. The impact on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions was calculated for a life-cycle microalgae-based SAF production process to evaluate the environmental impact of cCSH. With the introduction of cCSH, GHG emissions were estimated at 67.1 g-CO2eq/MJ, corresponding to an approximately 24.6% reduction compared with the conventional jet fuel. These results indicate that cCSH is a promising ca…

Size- and Time-Resolved Emission Rates of Particulate Matter Mass, Chemical Constituents, and Oxidative Potential from Indoor Sources
abstract: Abstract We quantified the time- and size-resolved emission rates of particulate matter (PM) mass, its chemical constituents, and OP (via dithiothreitol assay) from six indoor sources in a test chamber (two types of incense, candle, toaster, humidifier, and cigarette). Both the chemical composition and mass-normalized OP (OPm) varied little temporally. However, both the chemical composition and OPm varied with particle size from <0.25 to 10 μm, with quasi-ultrafine particles (Q-UFPs < 0.25 μm) showing the highest OPm. The particle size distribution of the PM emitted from these sources was mostly unimodal, with both PM10 mass and OP emission rate concentrated in the Q-UFP size range. Given the abundance of Q-UFPs in the emitted PM with their high intrinsic OP, we find that 37 ± 3% of the emitted PM10 mass and OP from these sources has the potential to deposit in the respiratory tract, 45 ± 2% of which deposits in the alveolar region. An exploratory exposure assessment suggests that for an equal dose of PM10 mass and OP originating from these indoor sources vs ambient PM, the emissions from the tested indoor sources will likely result in a 76 ± 10% higher dose of alveolar-deposited mass and OP. Collectively, these results emphasize the need to better quantify the size-resolved toxicological properties of PM from myriad indoor emission sources to reliably estimate the result…

The Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) is a prime example of machine-learning (ML) techniques efficiently enriching existing catalogues with classifications and derived physical properties that would be impractical to obtain from spectroscopy or colour selection alone. We will then use this sample to examine radio properties and redshift-dependent trends. We applied a pre-trained multi-stage ML pipeline to optical-to-infrared photometry of EMU-PS sources to derive classifications and photometric redshifts, which we used to compute additional radio properties, including luminosities. title: Assessing the Carbon Footprint of Wrap-Faced Retaining Walls: A Comprehensive Life-Cycle Evaluation in Bangladesh
abstract: In the field of geotechnical engineering, there's a growing emphasis on climate-friendly and sustainable approaches, leading to a heightened demand for solutions that integrate technical, ecological, and aesthetic considerations. In response, life cycle assessment (LCA) has become increasingly important as a method for assessing the environmental effects of geotechnical engineering projects. This paper focuses on a soil and water soil and water bioengineering construction project that utilizes geotextile to construct a wrap-faced retaining wall. The objective is to evaluate the wall's contribution to global warming potential (GWP) by evaluating its CO2 emissions. The results highlight the significant environmental advantages of soil and water soil and water bioengineering compared to conventional approaches, especially in terms of global warming potential (GWP). The selection of materials is crucial in determining this benefit, as wrap-faced walls exhibit significantly reduced carbon footprints in comparison to conventional alternatives such as reinforced concrete (RC) walls and mechanically stabilized earth (MSE) walls. The carbon footprint of soil and water soil and water bioengineering constructions is estimated to be nine times lower than RC walls and three times lower than MSE walls, indicating a notable reduction in emissions associated with their construction and utiliza…

abstract: PurposeInterstitial fibrosis is a critical histopathologic feature used in the diagnosis and prognosis of kidney diseases. However, conventional assessment using trichrome-stained slides is limited by interobserver variability and inconsistent stain reproducibility. This study evaluates whether dual-mode emission and transmission (DUET) microscopy, which generates virtual trichrome images from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) slides, can provide a practical, reproducible, and quantitative alternative for assessing interstitial fibrosis in kidney transplant biopsies.ApproachThirty-two kidney transplant biopsies were imaged using DUET to acquire pixel-registered brightfield and fluorescence whole-slide images from H&E-stained slides. A deep learning pipeline was trained on DUET-acquired images to extract collagen-positive signal from both the brightfield and fluorescence channels, which was used to generate virtual trichrome images and to compute quantitative fibrosis scores. Virtual trichrome images were compared with corresponding conventional trichrome slides. CFAP47 is involved in sperm head–tail coupling via cooperating with Septin12 and SUN5: gene knockout and protein analysis
abstract: Context Sperm head–tail linkage is essential for maintaining sperm integrity and male fertility. Although CFAP47 is associated with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella, its role in sperm head–tail coupling remains unclear. Aims This study aimed to investigate the role of CFAP47 in sperm head–tail connection. Methods A Cfap47 knockout mouse model was established to assess sperm motility and morphology. Molecular docking, co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assays were used to investigate the relationships of CFAP47, Septin12 and SUN5. Key results Cfap47 knockout mice exhibited impaired sperm motility and severe sperm morphological defects, with approximately 70% of sperm displaying abnormal head–tail connection or decapitation. Co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assays demonstrated that CFAP47 cooperates with Septin12 and SUN5. CFAP47 deficiency reduced the protein expression levels and affected their localization at the sperm head–tail junction. Conclusions CFAP47 is essential for sperm head–tail coupling. Implications These findings provide new insight into the molecular basis of sperm head–tail connection.

From policy commitment to lived professional experience: educator wellbeing and leadership values in Malta's National Education Strategy 2024–2030
abstract: This study aims to ask two questions: how does Malta's National Education Strategy 2024–2030 respond to working conditions associated with educator wellbeing, and what would need to change for its commitments to be felt in educators’ everyday work? We bring together Maltese studies from different periods, relevant international research and a structured analysis of policy documents. Across the Maltese literature, concerns recur about workload, educational reform, professional autonomy, consultation, recognition and support. Because the studies used different methods and populations, they cannot show whether these problems remained at the same level over time or what caused them. The Strategy addresses several of these concerns through commitments to wellbeing support, professional participation, recognition, development and less administration. Whether these measures have been implemented successfully remains an open question. We propose a six-level framework that distinguishes policy commitments, wider system conditions, leadership values, observable practices, educators’ immediate experiences and wellbeing outcomes, while recognising that feedback can inform future practice and policy. Trust, respect, care, fairness, recognition and empowerment are proposed leadership values, not measured outcomes. The framework offers a way to evaluate policy implementation without assuming …

title: Translanguaging as a Pedagogical Strategy in Developing Communicative Competence Among English First Additional Language Learners
abstract: Several studies in multilingual contexts reveal that translanguaging challenges linguistic boundaries and norms for social interaction in language teaching and learning. This study was guided by sociocultural theory and communicative language teaching in exploring how translanguaging enhances English First Additional Language learners’ communicative competence. The study adopted a qualitative research approach to explore how translanguaging is used as a pedagogical strategy and how learners experience its contribution to English First Additional Language (EFAL) communicative competence. Participants included one English First Additional Language teacher and twelve Grade 10 English First Additional Language learners who were sampled at a selected secondary school. The qualitative data were generated through non-participant classroom observations and semi-structured learner interviews and analysed using inductive thematic analysis. The study found that translanguaging was effective when employed strategically as temporary scaffolding to clarify meaning, support peer discussion, negotiate concepts, and develop ideas. The study recommends strategic use of translanguaging, drawing from learners’ Sepedi Home Language in facilitating understanding and developing ideas while ensuring learning opportunities in English. abstract: Abstract Background The sinus tarsi approach (STA) is a minimally invasive approach for intra-articular calcaneal fractures. Compared to the extended lateral approach (ELA), STA offers fewer wound complications and allows early operation. After obtaining a sound reduction of posterior facet and hindfoot alignment, the fixation strategy which varies from K-wire to plate can be used. In our study, we focused on Combo and perimeter plates. To evaluate the clinical results between these two plates, we conducted this retrospective clinical study. Methods From January 2022 to July 2025, 38 patients with closed intra-articular calcaneal fractures who received open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with Combo or perimeter plate via the sinus tarsi approach were recruited. All patients underwent postoperative clinical and radiological evaluation. Results Patients were followed up postoperatively. abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyze the optimization of Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies of amil (zakat institutions) in Indonesia’s regional National Amil Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) to improve the effectiveness, professionalism and transparency of zakat collection. Design/methodology/approach This research uses the Analytical Network Process (ANP) method to formulate priority strategies for managing amil human resources. ANP was selected because it can capture interdependencies and feedback loops among issues, aspects and strategies. The study’s network structure consists of clusters including Goals, Aspects, Problems and Strategies. Data were collected through pairwise-comparison questionnaires completed by 13 experts, including academics, regulators and practitioners from BAZNAS at national and regional levels, using a 1–9 scale, with consistency ratios (CR) maintained below 0.1. The analysis was conducted using Super Decisions software. Findings This study identifies three key problems in zakat human resource management (HRM): weak leadership, unprofessional recruitment, unclear employment status and low compensation. The highest-priority strategy is promoting leaders as role models of integrity and commitment, consistently rated highly by academics, regulators and practitioners. Other aligned strategies include strict recruitment based on competence (ST.1) and clarifyi…

This study aims to describe the implementation of deep learning strategies in developing early childhood problem-solving skills at TK B UMP Purwokerto through three main principles: meaningful learning (connecting learning materials with children's real-life experiences), mindful learning (fostering children's engagement and focus through simple project-based learning and small-group discussions), and joyful learning (creating an enjoyable learning environment through songs, games, and environmental exploration). The findings indicate that the three principles of deep learning were implemented through activities focusing on Healthy and Clean Living Habits and Introduction to Farm Animals. Sustainable values and consumer responses in cosmetic retailing: cross-cultural evidence
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates how environmental and ethical values shape consumer responses in the cosmetics retail context, focusing on detachment from brands that use chemical ingredients or engage in animal testing, as well as preferences for green and cruelty-free products across cultural and generational contexts. Design/methodology/approach We conducted three online survey studies in Italy (n = 310), Thailand (n = 198) and Czechia (n = 535). The first two studies examined how environmental values predict detachment from brands associated with animal testing or chemical ingredients, with brand attitude towards green and cruelty-free products tested as a mediator. The third study analysed how environmental and ethical values predict favourable attitudes towards cruelty-free cosmetics and willingness to purchase such products among Generation Z. Mediation was evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples and the bias-corrected percentile method. Findings In Italy and Thailand, environmental values predict detachment from brands associated with animal testing or chemical ingredients, and this effect is fully or partially mediated by brand attitudes towards green and cruelty-free cosmetics. In Czechia, environmental and ethical values directly predict higher willingness to buy cruelty-free products. Results support an attitude-to-behaviour pathway while revealing cross-…

Digital operational excellence in retail: a systematic review and dynamic causal framework
abstract: Purpose This study examines how digital technologies integrate with Operational Excellence (OpEx) routines, including Lean Six Sigma, in retail, identifying responsive processes, benefits, evolving KPIs, enablers, barriers, and mitigation strategies, and developing a retail-specific dynamic causal framework. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of 58 peer-reviewed articles from Q1/Q2 journals (2016–2026), following PRISMA guidelines, combined publication mapping, full-text coding, and narrative synthesis to conceptualize Digital-OpEx integration in retail. Findings Digital-OpEx is most evident in inventory, warehousing, logistics, and e-commerce. Digital technologies provide visibility, prediction, and traceability, while OpEx routines provide standardization and continuous-improvement discipline, with implications for customer experience and revenue. KPIs shift from retrospective to real-time, predictive, system-integrated indicators. Adoption depends on digital infrastructure, leadership commitment, employee capabilities, data availability, and system integration; financial, technical, organizational, and ethical barriers persist, though phased rollout and pilot testing aid implementation. Practical implications The framework helps retail managers prioritize high-responsiveness processes, align OpEx routines with digital technol…

title: Transfer Pricing, Capital Intensity, Thin Capitalization, dan Penghindaran Pajak pada Perusahaan Pertambangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2021–2024
abstract: Penerimaan pajak Indonesia masih menghadapi praktik penghindaran pajak, terutama pada sektor pertambangan yang memiliki aset tetap besar, transaksi pihak berelasi, dan kebutuhan pendanaan tinggi. Temuan penelitian terdahulu tentang transfer pricing, capital intensity, dan thin capitalization belum konsisten, dan hubungan ketiganya dengan penghindaran pajak pada periode setelah berlakunya kewajiban dokumentasi transfer pricing dan batas rasio utang terhadap modal masih perlu ditelaah. Penelitian ini menganalisis hubungan ketiga variabel tersebut dengan penghindaran pajak pada perusahaan pertambangan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2021–2024. Sampel dipilih secara purposive sebanyak 20 perusahaan (80 observasi; 75 observasi setelah lima pencilan dikeluarkan). Penghindaran pajak diukur dengan cash effective tax rate (CETR), sehingga CETR yang lebih rendah menunjukkan penghindaran pajak yang lebih tinggi, dan data dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda. Transfer pricing berhubungan negatif dengan CETR (B = −1,480; p = 0,008), yang mengindikasikan penghindaran pajak yang lebih tinggi; capital intensity berhubungan positif dengan CETR (B = 1,599; p = 0,040), yang mengindikasikan penghindaran pajak yang lebih rendah; dan thin capitalization tidak berhubungan signifikan (p = 0,345). abstract: This study was conducted based on initial observations of mathematics learning among fifth-grade students at SD Negeri 1 Jatianom. The observations indicated that students’ mathematics learning outcomes were still not optimal, particularly in addition of fractions, and the use of concrete learning media had not been optimally implemented. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effectiveness of plastic waste-based teaching aids in improving students’ mathematics learning outcomes. This study employed a mixed-method approach with a one-group pretest-posttest design for quantitative data and classroom observations for qualitative data. The participants were 20 fifth-grade students selected using total sampling. Data were collected through learning outcome tests and observations of students’ activities during the implementation of plastic waste-based teaching aids. Quantitative data were analyzed by comparing pretest and posttest scores and calculating the N-gain, while qualitative data were analyzed descriptively to describe students’ activities during the learning process. The results showed an improvement in students’ learning outcomes after the implementation of the teaching aids, with the mean score increasing from 43.4 on the pretest to 87.6 on the posttest, while the N-gain was categorized as high. The observation results also indicated that students became more active…

Equilibrium of a rapidly rotating axisymmetric magnetic mirror machine
abstract: A recent paper (Hazeltine et al. 2026 Phys. Plasmas, vol. 33, 072501) has questioned whether the standard result, (ultimately) due to Ferraro, that the plasma angular velocity is approximately constant along individual equilibrium magnetic field lines in a rotating axisymmetric magnetic mirror machine, continues to hold when the rotation becomes sonic or supersonic. In order to resolve this issue, the equilibrium of a rapidly rotating mirror is investigated, starting from first principles, using an ideal two-fluid model with anisotropic pressure. It is found that, as long as the ion gyro-radius is much less than the machine size, and the angular velocity of the plasma is much less than the ion gyro-frequency, the Ferraro result holds good.

abstract: Aim: This study examines how a madrasah principal enacts emotional intelligence, identifies its supporting and inhibiting factors, and explores the integration of dhikr and pikir within the ulul albab paradigm at MAN 1 Nganjuk, Indonesia. Method: A qualitative single-case study was conducted using three semi-structured interviews with the principal, participant observation by a researcher working as a teacher, and institutional documents. Data were analysed through condensation, display, and conclusion drawing. Results: Emotional intelligence was manifested through tabayun-based self-regulation, personal engagement and informal dialogue, and participatory, bottom-up communication. The principal understood leadership as service (khadimul ummah), delegated responsibilities according to organisational roles, and retained accountability. Enabling conditions included leadership experience, willingness to learn, clear delegation structures, and external partnerships; obstacles included resistance to change, limited cohesion, cultural differences, and unbudgeted needs. Decision-making combined verification and rational analysis with prayer, followed by spiritual consultation when reasoning reached an impasse. abstract: Deep learning in education denotes an approach through which students seek meaning, connect new knowledge with prior understanding, critically evaluate ideas and apply concepts beyond immediate assessment. It differs from surface learning centred on reproduction and memorisation. Foundational investigations distinguished qualitative differences in students’ learning approaches (Marton & Säljö, 1976), while subsequent frameworks connected deep, surface and strategic approaches with learning environments and academic outcomes (Entwistle & Ramsden, 1983; Biggs, 1987). Evidence from higher education suggests that learning approaches and study behaviours have meaningful, though not necessarily large, associations with achievement (Richardson et al., 2012).

title: Interpretable human-label-free deep learning for real-bogus classification with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Time-domain surveys generate large numbers of transient candidates, making real-bogus classification a critical step in automated discovery pipelines. Obtaining reliable human-labeled training sets is costly, while community-provided labels can be noisy and survey-dependent. We aim to develop a real-bogus classification framework for point-like astrophysical transient detections against bogus survey detections, that can be trained without human-labeled data using physically motivated injected transients and bogus-dominated survey data, that remains robust under strong class contamination, and that provides well-calibrated and reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) suitable for downstream decision-making. We combine simulated transient injections with a heavily contaminated survey class and train a dual-network model using an asymmetric co-teaching strategy for classes with different label-noise levels. We evaluate performance on a labeled benchmark subset and analyze the learned representation with latent-space visualization tools. For UQ, we compare standard approaches (Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles) and propose a low-cost hybrid strategy that exploits the dual-network setting to improve calibration. We further extend the evaluation to the light-curve domain to assess recovery of light-curve classes. The method achieves strong real-bogus performance on the labeled s…

title: Does the direct anterior learning curve persist after fellowship training? A single-center comparative cohort study
abstract: Abstract Introduction The direct anterior approach (DAA) for total hip arthroplasty (THA) has historically been associated with a learning curve affecting both operative efficiency and early complications. Whether contemporary adult-reconstruction fellowship training modifies that curve is not established. We compared 90-day complication rates and operative times between newly graduated fellowship-trained DAA surgeons and one experienced DAA surgeon at a single high-volume center. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 600 primary THAs performed via a DAA from a single institution between November 2019 and February 2025 with a minimum of 90-day follow-up. Intra- and post-operative complications were compared between the following two groups: the first 100 cases of each of three junior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons (“Junior”) and the most recent 300 cases of a senior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon (“Senior”). The study was powered to detect a 5% absolute difference in overall complication rates. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were analyzed as exploratory secondary endpoints. Results Operative complications were infrequent in both cohorts, with a numerically higher rate in the Junior group that did not reach statistical significance (Junior 27 [9.0%] vs Senior 20 [6.7%]; absolute difference + 2.3%, 95% CI − 2.0% to + 6.6%, p = 0.362). title: Environment-Aware Deep Learning for Adaptive Dissolved Oxygen Sensing: Resolving the Information Efficiency Paradox in Aquatic Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Continuous high-frequency monitoring of dissolved oxygen (DO) faces a fundamental conflict between excessive energy consumption and substantial data redundancy, whereas conventional fixed-frequency sampling risks frequency aliasing and the omission of acute transient ecological events. To resolve this dilemma, a knowledge-guided, seasonally adaptive dynamic sampling strategy coupled with bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) reconstruction is proposed. Validated via long-term datasets from two hydrodynamically distinct Yangtze River stations, this framework yields three principal findings. First, summer precipitation acts as the primary catalyst for acute hypoxic risks (DO < 5.0 mg/L), whereas winter rainfall predominantly drives reaeration, dictating the nonstationary triggers for dynamic sampling. Second, optimal data decimation exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity governed by site-specific environmental buffering capacities; high-fidelity reconstruction requires merely 22.99% data retention at the hydrodynamically stable Nanjinguan mainstream. Third, a counterintuitive information efficiency paradox is mathematically proven at the highly volatile Chenglingji lake outlet: the dynamic strategy (utilizing 50.23% of data) achieves a Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE) of 0.969, vastly outperforming the uncompressed 100% full-data baseline (KGE = 0.797). title: A Summability Assisted Machine Learning Framework for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Equipment
abstract: Purpose: Industrial Predictive Maintenance (PdM) relies on sensor streams that are noisy, irregular, and affected by changing operating regimes, which can cause machine learning models to overreact to transient spikes or miss slow drift. This study develops a summability assisted machine learning framework that converts noisy time series into stable, interpretable features before prediction. Research Methodology: The study uses a methodological design that combines a literature synthesis, mathematical definitions of finite Cesàro means, weighted means, cumulative and robust summaries, a leakage resistant evaluation protocol, a cost sensitive decision rule, and simulation based illustrations on a synthetic pump record. Results: On the synthetic record, an adjacent window difference and a clipped cumulative sum detected a slow drift that a single sample limit missed while ignoring an isolated spike. Window length governed a clear trade off between false alerts and detection delay, and a worked example showed that a calibrated failure probability of 0.18 justifies inspection when the break even probability is 0.048. Conclusions: Summability features are a low cost and interpretable complement to raw signals, but their value must be demonstrated for each asset class and decision horizon. Model-based graph reinforcement learning for robust cyber-attack defense in active distribution systems with high DER penetration
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a model-based graph reinforcement learning (MBGRL) framework for defending active distribution systems with high penetrations of distributed energy resources (DERs) against cyber-physical threats, particularly false data injection attacks (FDIAs). The proposed approach integrates a learned power-flow surrogate model with a graph neural network (GNN) policy to accelerate convergence, reduce simulator dependence, and capture the spatial structure of distribution networks. Adversarial scenario training further enhances robustness under coordinated load-altering attacks, DER-setpoint tampering, and combined multi-vector FDIAs. Evaluated on the IEEE-123 bus system, the MBGRL framework demonstrates significant improvements over existing methods: it reduces simulator interactions by 54% and training time by more than 60%, while achieving superior operational resilience—lowering voltage violations to 5 (compared with 12 for SAC and 18 for MPC) and reducing active-power losses to 89 kW (compared with 102 kW for SAC and 111 kW for MPC). abstract: Abstract Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters such as ν-DABNA have enabled highly efficient deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, their device performance is strongly governed by the electronic structure of the host matrix. Here, we demonstrate that ν-DABNA displays a distinct host-dependent reversal of charge-trapping polarity in three representative host matrices—mSiTrz, mCBP, and PhCzBCz in an identical device architecture. Specifically, ν-DABNA behaves as a hole trap in mSiTrz, an electron trap in PhCzBCz, and a bipolar trap in mCBP according to its energy level. The electroluminescence (EL) spectra of ν-DABNA-based devices exhibit nearly identical peak positions around 470 nm, and the mCBP-based device delivers the highest peak EQE at low current density, a relatively serious efficiency roll-off at high current density, and a long device lifetime, indicating the bipolar carrier-buffering effect of doping ν-DABNA. Transient EL measurements reveal a clear decoupling between charge formation and emissive decay processes. The rise dynamics strongly depend on host-dependent trap polarity, leading to a significant variation in turn-on time, while the decay dynamics remain invariant across all devices, confirming that delayed fluorescence is exclusively governed by intrinsic ν-DABNA reverse intersystem crossing (RISC). title: A social entrepreneur’s journey to heal the world: uncertainty the only certainty?
abstract: Learning outcomes At the end of this discussion, students will be able to apply key theoretical frameworks – tensions of hybridity, institutional logics and hybrid organizing archetypes – to analyze Centre for Health and Development (CHD) Group India’s strategic challenges and emerging market context; evaluate whether CHD should accept, reject or seek to modify the donor’s hybrid condition, considering the trade-offs among financial resilience, mission integrity, stakeholder legitimacy and organizational capacity; develop and justify an organizational and governance arrangement appropriate to the recommended strategic pathway. Where the recommendation includes earned-income activities, students should explain how those activities can be structured and governed without undermining CHD’s mission; and assess the role of partnerships and stakeholder engagement in supporting CHD’s chosen sustainability pathway while protecting community access, organizational legitimacy and long-term impact. Case overview/synopsis This case examines the strategic dilemma faced by Dr Edmond Fernandes, founder of CHD Group India – a public health nonprofit organization operating in underserved communities in India. Despite reporting program reached of over four million people through health-care delivery, disaster preparedness and climate-health advocacy, CHD is encountering financial stagnation. As g…

title: Multiobjective Optimization of Integrated Green Hydrogen and Biomass Supply Networks for Vacuum Gas Oil and Bio–Oil Coprocessing in Refinery Hydrocracking Units
abstract: Abstract A multiobjective optimization framework is developed for the integrated green hydrogen and biomass supply network design of vacuum gas oil and bio–oil coprocessing in hydrocracking units, to support the low-carbon transformation of refinery hydrogenation processes. A mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model is established with dual objectives of minimizing total annual cost (TAC) and total carbon emission (TCE). The ε-constraint method is adopted to generate the Pareto optimal frontier, and the evaluation function method is used to screen the optimal compromise solution balancing economic and environmental performance. Results show that the system achieves a maximum carbon emission reduction of 43.99% with only a 6.91% increase in TAC. The optimal compromise solution realizes a 39.74% TCE reduction with a negligible 0.16% TAC increase compared with the cost-optimal scenario. Green hydrogen related costs account for more than 74% of TAC, which is the dominant factor affecting the supply chain economy, while biomass transportation contributes over 60% of total emissions as the core emission reduction handle. In sensitivity analysis, the optimal supply chain configuration remains stable under fluctuations of green hydrogen price, and the effective implementation interval of carbon tax is 0–75 CNY/t CO2-eq. The proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for …

title: Unsorted Antithetic RQMC for Relaxed Barrier Optimization: Enhanced Stability and Variance Reduction
Formulation optimization, flavor formation, and quality characteristics of a seasoning paste containing a Maillard-derived flavor base
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop and characterize a compound seasoning paste containing a Maillard-derived flavor base prepared from quinoa hydrolysate and bovine bone collagen peptides. Methods The flavor base was prepared through the Maillard reaction and subsequently incorporated with beef tallow and other auxiliary ingredients. Using sensory score as the evaluation index, the formulation was optimized through single-factor experiments and an optimal mixture design. The product was characterized by amino acid analysis, multivariate statistical analysis, volatile flavor profiling, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and physicochemical and microbiological analyses. Results The optimal formulation consisted of 37% flavor base, 33% beef tallow, 12% maltodextrin, 9% corn starch, 6% sucrose, and 3% salt. The experimental sensory score was 8.75 ± 0.11, showing a relative error of 0.13% from the predicted value. A total of 17 hydrolyzed amino acids were identified in the optimized compound seasoning paste, with Pro (0.60 g/100 g), Ala (0.38 g/100 g), and Glu (0.27 g/100 g) among the most abundant. Principal component analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis, and orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis revealed that Pro, Ala, Arg, Glu, Asp, and Gly were the key differential amino acids contributing to sample discrimination. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry …

title: Balancing DOF margin and stochastic failure in high-NA EUV process
abstract: BackgroundHigh-numerical aperture (NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography delivers superior resolution, but it severely restricts the depth of focus (DOF) window. To expand this margin, the detrimental impact of stray photons leaking into unexposed areas must be mitigated. Crucially, we confirmed that increasing the photo contrast to decrease stochastic failure conversely increases sensitivity to this leakage light, thereby degrading the DOF margin.AimWe aim to maximize the functional DOF window in the High-NA EUV process by understanding the effects of the photoresist material configurations and post-exposure bake (PEB) process conditions.ApproachBased on lithographic simulations, we employed a low-contrast resist environment that exhibits low sensitivity to optical leakage in defocused condition.ResultThe DOF window was expanded by elevating the PEB temperature, reducing the polymer molecular weight, decreasing the protecting group (PG) ratio, or applying a PG with high activation energy (Ea) for deprotection. These adjustments reduced profile degradation and pattern collapse by systematically lowering the photosensitivity of the resist matrix against optical leakage in High-NA process.ConclusionThese findings expose a fundamental problem of High-NA process. Widening the DOF margin requires an insensitive resist environment, which can inherently degrade pattern uniformity.…

title: Implicit differentiation for measurement-efficient bilevel quantum-classical optimization
abstract: Quantum optimization has shown promising results for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. Real-world applications, however, often involve polynomial coefficients that depend on tunable external factors—such as demand forecasts or risk preferences—giving rise to bilevel optimization structures. We show how variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) can efficiently handle such parametric problems, thus making three contributions. First, we propose a bilevel optimization model for diagonal cost Hamiltonians where coefficients depend on a tunable outer parameter: an outer loop adjusts this parameter—reshaping the cost landscape—while an inner VQA optimizes circuit variables. Second, since derivative-free probing methods incur multiplicative overhead when each outer evaluation requires a complete inner solve, we develop correlator-reuse implicit differentiation (CR-ID), which obtains outer gradients by reusing quantum measurements already collected during inner energy estimation, thus requiring essentially no additional circuit executions. Experiments across three coefficient families show that CR-ID consistently improves budget-normalized efficiency by 4% in 1D and over 14% in multi-dimensional settings, showing a significant performance advantage compared to finite-difference methods. Third, we show that this property is architecture-dependent: the Variational Q…

title: Optimization of Proximal Balloon Edge Dilation Technique for Link-Connect Type of Stent in Coronary Bifurcation Interventions
Sustainable multi-objective topology optimization of composite hybrid tubular trusses
abstract: Purpose The construction sector significantly contributes to global CO2 emissions, underscoring the need for structural optimization methods that explicitly integrate mechanical performance, cost, and environmental criteria. However, existing composite-truss optimization studies do not simultaneously couple truss topology and member sizing with composite slab geometry and reinforcement while considering these competing criteria. This work addresses the gap by developing an integrated multi-objective formulation for hybrid composite concrete–high-strength steel trusses, featuring a concrete-filled upper chord and simultaneous optimization of slab geometry with reinforcement. Design/methodology/approach Two assessment stages were conducted: (1) single-objective optimization across spans of 8–24?m to quantify the structural and environmental benefits of pairing hybrid trusses with optimized slabs; and (2) multi-objective optimization for the best-performing span from (1), including slab capacity as an explicit objective. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithms were used to solve the single- and multi-objective problems, respectively. Findings Results show that hybrid trusses combined with optimized slabs reduce emissions by up to 24% relative to the corresponding homogeneous trusses combined with catalog-based slabs, con…

title: Multistage MP-DRA optimization across C+L and S+C+L MB-WDM transmission systems
abstract: Abstract This paper introduces an optimized multistage design approach for multipump distributed Raman amplifiers (MP-DRAs) in future multiband wavelength division multiplexing (MB-WDM) systems. Wideband system increases transmission capacity of the transmission but results in extreme nonuniformity of gain and asymmetric noise accumulation. To limit these impairments, three single-stage configurations are systematically explored in the C+L band: copropagating, counterpropagating, and bidirectional. The bidirectional configuration provides the optimum C+L performance. It has a peak gain of 17.57 dB, a minimal gain ripple of 1.97 dB, an average noise figure of 7.077 dB (average), and a transmission reach of 206 km. This was the starting point for the implementation of a dual-stage cascaded bidirectional DRA in the same system of 8 channels C+L. This configuration increased the maximum common transmission reach to 274 km, an extra 68 km. The optimization framework is then extended to 110 nm S+C+L band (1,515–1,625 nm). Two different configurations are assessed; single-stage gain-flatting filter (SS-GFF)- and dual-stage (DS-GFF)-based DRA. The SS-GFF yields a 14.12 dB peak gain, a 4.125 dB ripple, and 188 km reach. Importantly, the DS-GFF architecture extends the range of transmission reach to be 236 km, an improvement of 25.5 %. The results provided a strong, simple path toward op…

Modeling the moral account: a system dynamics framework for brand-induced moral licensing and behavioral rebound in sustainable consumption
abstract: Introduction Quantitative models of sustainable consumption typically treat consumption as exogenous, assuming that every green purchase improves environmental outcomes. Behavioral research on moral licensing, however, suggests that purchases perceived as virtuous can license compensatory indulgence that erodes some of the benefit. Recent formal work treats licensing as an environmental rebound mechanism in static consumer models; this study contributes the first dynamic stock-and-flow formalization, developed from a recent conceptual framework of brand-induced moral licensing. Methods Four communication pathways (virtue attribution, identity conferral, effort signaling, and absolution framing) feed two moral accounts with opposite mechanics: credits, which deplete when spent, and credentials, which license behavior without being consumed. The model yields closed-form steady states and a licensing-resistance condition on the rebound ratio ρ> (backfire at ρ> 1). Communication parameters were calibrated through a preregistered content analysis of 120 verbatim-archived units from eight sustainable brands, with perfect dual-coder agreement on the reliability subsample; identity internalization was calibrated from a two-country survey of 3,293 adults. The behavioral conversion parameters are literature-anchored or illustrative, so all rebound magnitudes are model-derived, orde…

title: Estimation of minimum inflow time series under reservoir system operation
abstract: ABSTRACT Frequent and severe droughts driven by climate change highlight the need for reliable reservoir operation strategies. While most studies evaluate firm yield at the scale of individual reservoirs, few explicitly consider reservoir system operation of multiple reservoirs, despite its potential to enhance downstream supply reliability. The main objectives are to develop a method to estimate the firm yield of the Seomjingang and Juam Reservoirs in South Korea under reservoir system operation and to define and estimate the minimum inflow time series for each reservoir as a basis for assessing water supply reliability during extreme droughts. Results show that reservoir system operation increases firm yield by about seven percent (+1.24 cubic meters per second [CMS]), from 17.92 CMS under independent operation to 19.16 CMS under reservoir system operation, and delays reservoir depletion, thereby enhancing water supply stability during droughts. The novelty of this study lies in developing a firm-yield estimation method that incorporates reservoir system operation and establishing the concept of a minimum inflow time series. The proposed methodology establishes a quantitative framework for minimum inflow time-series estimation and highlights how reservoir system operation can enhance the resilience and reliability of long-term water supply.

title: Financial Culture as a Legal Phenomenon and a Crucial Component in the Development of the Financial System of the Russian Federation
abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and legal significance of financial culture and its correlation with financial literacy. An analysis of strategic planning documents adopted in the financial sector from 2008 to the present day reveals a legal transition: the focus has shifted from regulating how citizens are informed and how they acquire relevant knowledge (i.e., financial literacy) toward fostering specific values and cultivating desired behavioral practices (i.e., financial culture). It is acknowledged that, from the perspective of jurisprudence, and, more specifically, the theory of financial law, the term "financial and legal culture" is more precise and better suited to the scientific and terminological framework of financial law. In conclusion, the importance of financial literacy for the development of a state’s financial system and the strengthening of its financial sovereignty is also emphasized.

title: Error de prohibición y diversidad cultural: el pluralismo jurídico en el sistema penal ecuatoriano
abstract: En un Estado intercultural, una persona puede actuar conforme a las normas de su comunidad y, sin saberlo, infringir la ley penal ordinaria. El artículo analizó cómo el error de prohibición, regulado en el artículo 35.1 del Código Orgánico Integral Penal, se relaciona con el pluralismo jurídico y la jurisdicción indígena en Ecuador. Se realizó una revisión documental de la Constitución, el Código Orgánico de la Función Judicial, el Convenio 169, jurisprudencia constitucional y doctrina penal y de pluralismo jurídico arbitrada. El análisis distinguió tres supuestos: conductas dentro de la competencia indígena, conductas fuera de ella con error culturalmente condicionado y conductas sin relación con la cultura. Se concluye que la valoración de la vencibilidad del error debe incorporar el contexto cultural, mientras la ley no ofrece criterios expresos. No se recogieron datos primarios.
venue: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales

title: Cross-model validation of large language models in English-to-Chinese consecutive interpreting assessment: a multi-dimensional comparison with trained human ratings
Long-range spectral entanglement and quantum correlations in highly nondegenerate multi-comb and ultrafast systems
abstract: Abstract Frequency combs are multimode photonic systems that underlie countless precision sensing and metrology applications. Since their invention over two decades ago, numerous efforts have pushed frequency combs to broader bandwidths and more stable operation. More recently, quantum squeezing and entanglement have been explored in single-comb systems for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum-enhanced spectroscopy. However, the production of bright quantum light across multiple nondegenerate pulses or frequency combs, a key technology for multispectral applications, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we explore a mechanism that generates a series of nonlinearly coupled bright frequency combs through cascaded three-wave upconversion and downconversion processes mediated by a single idler comb. We consider both discrete combs and broadband ultrafast pulse systems, showing how these systems generate inter- and intracomb two-mode squeezing and entanglement directly in the frequency basis, spanning a large spectral range. Furthermore, we demonstrate how these systems can be engineered to produce target cluster states and concentrated two-mode squeezing through covariance matrix optimization. Our findings uncover a new multimode quantum regime enabled by hierarchical nonlinear interactions in two frequency dimensions, unlocking applications such as entanglement-a…

title: Concurrent Multi-Level Policy Implementation and the Technology Transfer Performance of Chinese Universities
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of concurrent multi-level policy implementation on university technology transfer performance. It clarifies the moderating roles of government financial support and regional research and development (R&D) conditions. It further examines heterogeneous policy effects across university disciplinary characteristics, geographical locations, regional technology intermediary density, and industrial structure. The findings offer a refined empirical perspective for evaluating multi-level policy effectiveness and optimizing university technology transfer practices. They also provide guidance for strengthening basic research capacity and better integrating of basic and applied research in universities. Design/methodology/approach Panel data from 61 universities directly under the Ministry of Education spanning 2011–2019 were analyzed. We employed the Difference-in-Differences (DID) method to empirically test the specific impact of the concurrent implementation of local and university-level policies on university technology transfer. Additionally, moderating effect models and grouped regression are adopted to explore the underlying mechanisms. Findings The empirical results show that the concurrent implementation of local and university-level policies exerts a significantly positive impact on university technology transfer. Second, gover…
