Density functional prediction of 2D spintronic materials: magnetic doping of semiconducting 1 T-GeO 2 monolayer
abstract: Abstract The search of new two-dimensional materials, for practical usage in the emergent field of spintronics, is a very active topic due to the exceptional properties of these systems compared to their corresponding bulk phases. In the present study, we use DFT calculations to investigate the electronic structure and magnetic ordering of 1 T-GeO 2 monolayer, doped with transition metal (TM) elements: V, Cr, and Mn; at 25% doping concentration. The undoped monolayer is predicted to be an ultrawide band gap semiconductor (with 5.34 eV indirect band gap). When the ferromagnetic ordering is considered, the V-doped system is found to be a half-metal; while the Cr- and Mn-doped ones exhibit a semiconducting character. The mechanism responsible for these predicted features is also examined. This suggests that TM-doped 1 T-GeO 2 could be advantageous for spintronic applications.

title: Beyond Disease Susceptibility: Genetics, Prediction, and the Limits of Inferring Human Potential
abstract: This narrative review examines the expansion of human genetics beyond disease susceptibility to variation in human function, development, and phenotypic outcomes. In this regard, we define human potential as genetically influenced variation in what individuals may develop or achieve under different biological and environmental conditions. Its genetic architecture is highly polygenic and shaped by pleiotropy, genetic background, developmental and regulatory context, gene–environment interplay, and genetic influences on response and adaptation. Similar observed phenotypes can arise through different genetic routes, while individuals with similar baseline function may differ in their responses to environmental conditions or interventions. Genetic prediction of these traits remains incomplete and strongly dependent on population and context. Polygenic scores developed in European-ancestry populations may show systematically different score distributions in populations underrepresented in genomic discovery datasets. Between-population differences in polygenic-score means cannot be interpreted as differences in intrinsic human capacity. Such differences can produce scientifically invalid comparisons and discriminatory use of genetic prediction. Genetic information concerning human potential should be used conscientiously, particularly in education, employment, insurance, reproduction…

title: Prediction of Molecular Physicochemical Properties Using Molecular Structure and Characteristics
abstract: The prediction of molecular physicochemical properties—such as solubility, hydration free energy, and lipophilicity—plays a crucial role in multiple fields, including drug discovery and materials science. Current prediction methods predominantly fall into two categories: machine learning methods based on molecular descriptors and deep learning methods that learn representations directly from molecular structures. However, when evaluated under rigorous scaffold splitting, these methods often exhibit limited generalization capability, resulting in unsatisfactory prediction accuracy. In this study, a method named PMPP is proposed to predict the physicochemical properties of molecules, which effectively utilizes enhanced graph representations that capture molecular motif structures and optimized selection of pharmacophore and physicochemical characteristics. The framework of PMPP contains three parts: molecular structure representation extraction, molecular characteristics extraction and optimized selection, and molecular physicochemical property prediction model construction. Experimental results demonstrate that PMPP achieves superior predictive accuracy, with lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) scores on three benchmark datasets: 0.787 (ESOL), 1.875 (FreeSolv), and 0.615 (Lipophilicity). These results outperform six state-of-the-art methods, including GROVER, MGSSL, MolCLR, KANO…

title: Multiscale homogenization-based finite-element modeling of fused filament fabrication (FFF)-printed polylactic acid (PLA) components for mechanical performance prediction
abstract: This study investigates the mechanical behavior of polylactic acid (PLA) components manufactured by fused filament fabrication (FFF) through a combined experimental and homogenization-based numerical approach. The effects of raster orientation (0°, 45°, and 90°) and strain rate (10 −4 –10 −2 s −1 ) on tensile properties were evaluated. Representative volume elements (RVEs) were used to determine the effective orthotropic elastic properties of the printed material, which were subsequently implemented in macroscale finite-element simulations. Experimental validation was performed using ISO 527-2 Type 1BA tensile specimens. The results showed that raster orientation and strain rate significantly influence the mechanical response of FFF-printed PLA. The 90° raster configuration exhibited the highest stiffness and strength, whereas the 0° configuration showed lower performance due to its greater dependence on interlayer bonding. The numerical model successfully reproduced the overall mechanical trends and anisotropic behavior of the printed structures, although discrepancies remained for Young's modulus and ultimate elongation because of the assumptions of perfect interlayer bonding and the absence of viscoelastic and damage mechanisms. The proposed framework provides an efficient tool for predicting the mechanical behavior of FFF-manufactured components while reducing experimental …

High-Precision Lumped-Parameter Thermal Modeling and CNN-LSTM-Based Temperature Prediction for Optical Interconnect Modules
abstract: The increasing power consumption and intensified thermal coupling in next-generation high-speed optical interconnect modules present severe thermal management challenges. To address these issues, we propose a high-precision lumped-parameter thermal modeling method for optical interconnect modules. Building upon the constructed lumped-parameter thermal model (LPTM), a real-time transient temperature prediction framework utilizing a hybrid convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture is developed. The LPTM achieves high-precision modeling while reducing computational complexity. Compared with the simulation results from COMSOL Multiphysics 6.3, the proposed LPTM model exhibits an average mean absolute error (MAE) of only 0.52 °C and an average root mean square error (RMSE) of only 0.69 °C for the transient temperatures of key components. Furthermore, the CNN-LSTM neural network, trained on the dataset generated by the LPTM, achieves an MAE of 0.34 °C and an RMSE of 0.78 °C on an independent transient temperature testset generated by COMSOL Multiphysics. The proposed methodology successfully achieves both high-precision modeling and real-time, accurate transient temperature prediction, providing a solid theoretical foundation for thermal management in next-generation optical interconnect systems.

title: Coupled Effects of Burial Depth and Surface Double Cracks on the Uplift Bearing Capacity of Strip Anchor Plates in Red Clay
abstract: Prolonged drought can induce shrinkage cracking in near-surface clay foundations, leaving persistent defects that may affect the uplift safety of underground structures before subsequent rainfall events. This study investigates how burial depth regulates the influence of two pre-existing surface cracks on the uplift bearing capacity and failure mechanism of a horizontal strip anchor plate in red clay. A two-dimensional plane-strain model was established in Optum G2 and validated against laboratory pull-out tests under crack-free conditions. Two burial-depth ratios, H/B = 3 and 8, were examined, and 360 cases were generated by varying normalized crack depth (h/B = 0.25–3), spacing (s/B = 0.25–3), and horizontal offset (d/B = 0–6). Under shallow burial, cracks readily intersect the potential sliding zone and the maximum capacity reduction reaches 81.6%, with pronounced transitions around s/B = 1 and d/B = 1. Under deep burial, the principal failure surface remains predominantly a deep elliptical arc and capacity reduction is generally below 15%. Burial depth therefore controls the spatial overlap between the environmentally damaged zone and the anchor-bearing zone. The results provide a mechanical basis for post-drought crack inspection, uplift-safety reassessment, and burial-depth selection. Building capacity for engagement: A scoping review of informal and formal research training for Indigenous youth
abstract: Abstract Community‐based research approaches, including community‐based participatory action research (CBPAR), are a research design that engages communities as active collaborators by offering training and support throughout the research process. These approaches, including CBPAR, have gained traction in work with Indigenous youth, as they build research capacity and foster equitable partnerships between community members and researchers. As an underrepresented population in CBPAR, Indigenous youth offer critical perspectives that can deepen understanding of community needs and inform culturally responsive approaches. To explore the uptake in community‐based research approaches and youth inclusion, this scoping review analyzed 37 research articles detailing 33 research training programs for Indigenous youth engaged in research in Canada, the United States, Aotearoa (New Zealand), and Australia. Training programs ranged from providing a brief overview of the research process (42%) to teaching youth specific research skills (27%). Youth involvement also varied across training programs, from being included as study participants (15%) to extensive youth co‐researcher partnerships (48%). Key themes were extracted from the articles to highlight the limitations and strengths of the research training programs. The programs demonstrated variability in delivery and youth involvement, wi…

title: Three-Dimensional Coupling Assessment of Eco-Geological Environment in Alpine Gorge Areas Integrating the Remote Sensing Ecological Index, Ecosystem Services, and Geological Environment Carrying Capacity
abstract: Alpine gorge areas are typical regions where ecological fragility and geological hazard risk overlap strongly. Existing eco-geological assessments remain largely single- or dual-dimensional: remotely sensed indices describe surface status, ecosystem-service indices describe functional supply, and geological models are usually applied separately from ecological assessment, so each approach misses the information carried by the others. To close this gap, this study proposes a three-dimensional coupling framework for Eco-Geological Environment Carrying Capacity (EGECC) that integrates the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI), the Ecosystem Services Index (ESI) and the Geological Environmental Carrying Capacity (GECC), and applies it in Lixian County, Sichuan Province. The three indices were coupled at pixel level, and their coupling and vertical differentiation were analysed along an altitudinal gradient. Three findings are highlighted. (1) RSEI and ESI are only moderately correlated, and their altitudinal peaks are separated, so neither can substitute for the other. (2) GECC contributes the largest share of the variation in EGECC, indicating that the geological dimension carries information that is not a linear combination of the two ecological dimensions. title: AI-Enabled Teaching Capability and Sustainable Education Practice among Teachers in Mountainous China: The Roles of OER-Enabled Pedagogical Capacity and Institutional Digital Support
abstract: This study examines how teachers' artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled teaching capability and open educational resources (OER)-enabled pedagogical capacity are associated with sustainable education practice in mountainous areas of China. It also assesses the indirect role of OER-enabled pedagogical capacity and the moderating role of institutional digital support.The study describes a cross-sectional quantitative survey of 462 teachers from 54 schools in 18 mountainous counties across Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Gansu, and Qinghai, using a 24-item questionnaire and partial least squares structural equation modelling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The analyzed results report positive associations between AI-enabled teaching capability and sustainable education practice (? = .331, p < .001), between AI capability and OER-enabled pedagogical capacity (? = .550, p < .001), and between OER capacity and sustainable practice (? = .390, p < .001). The indirect association is .215 and the interaction with institutional digital support is .134. The R² for sustainable practice is .475. title: Dietary Multivitamin Supplementation in Siganus fuscescens: Integrated Effects on Growth Performance, Antioxidant Capacity, and Mitigation of Darkening Syndrome Under High-Lipid Dietary Stress
abstract: Siganus fuscescens, an economically important species in southern China, is noted for its rapid growth and high nutritional value. Nonetheless, the prevalence of darkening syndrome, a condition marked by skin discoloration and significant mortality rates, presents a challenge to aquaculture practices, with its etiology remaining largely unexplored. This study aimed to examine the impacts of varying dietary lipid levels and multivitamin supplementation on the incidence of darkening syndrome in S. fuscescens. Five experimental diets were developed: a low-fat diet containing 10% lipids; a moderate-fat diet with 13% lipids; a moderate-fat diet with 13% lipids supplemented with multivitamins; a high-fat diet containing 16% lipids; and a high-fat diet with 16% lipids supplemented with multivitamins. A 55-day feeding trial was conducted on S. fuscescens specimens. The results indicate that, in this experiment, increasing dietary fat content led to a higher cumulative incidence of darkening syndrome in S. fuscescens. Serological and histological findings suggested that in the 16% lipid diet group, S. fuscescens exhibited liver injury and oxidative stress. Notably, supplementation with multivitamins alleviated these adverse effects. Overall, we recommend using an appropriate dietary fat level and further supplementing with antioxidant multivitamins, which may represent an effective stra…

title: Transmission mechanism and identification of power pulsation signals in sucker rod pumping wells
abstract: Abstract Traditional wellbore communication technologies for sucker-rod pumping wells suffer from severe signal attenuation and poor stability under deep-well and complex operating conditions. This study investigates the transmission mechanism and signal identification of power pulsation wireless communication. A three-dimensional full-scale fluid–structure coupling dynamic model incorporating the sucker rod, centering device, wellbore fluid, and tubing is established to characterize stress wave propagation from the downhole pump to the wellhead. The model reveals that the transmission channel exhibits typical high-impedance, low-pass characteristics, with fluid viscous damping, rod–tubing friction, and material damping governing signal attenuation, while low-frequency stress waves retain superior long-distance transmission capability. The model is validated using field-measured loading data, achieving prediction errors below 10% across the full operating condition range. Based on the validated model, a joint time- and frequency-domain identification algorithm is developed by combining characteristic spectral peak recognition with time-domain waveform verification, enabling detection of power pulsation signals under strong noise. Tunable viscoelastic hydrogels for vascularization: mechanism, design and applications
abstract: Abstract Vascularization is crucial for fabricating large-scale functional artificial tissues and organs, and hydrogels are the most commonly used biomaterials for constructing microenvironments conducive to blood vessel formation. However, traditional static hydrogels lack the dynamic regulation of cell behavior similar to natural extracellular matrix (ECM) because they cannot replicate the viscoelasticity of ECM. Viscoelasticity is a key dynamic biomechanical signal for regulating the cell fate and is crucial for modulating vascular cell behavior. In recent years, tunable viscoelastic hydrogels (TVHs) based on reversible crosslinking have become highly promising biomaterials due to their capacity to mimic the viscoelasticity of ECM. Although some vascularization studies using TVHs have been conducted, and significant progress has been made, this emerging field lacks a systematic summary. Therefore, this review summarizes the recent advances of TVHs in vascularization, including the three major strategies for precisely controlling hydrogel viscoelasticity, the influence of hydrogel viscoelasticity on vascular cell fate, and the application of hydrogel viscoelasticity in regulating blood vessel formation. The prospects and challenges of TVHs are also discussed. This review aims to provide design principles for engineering TVHs capable of precisely controlling viscoelasticity an…

title: Digital Training Demand and Labor Market Alignment in Adult Continuing Education: Evidence from Slovakia
abstract: Rapid digitalization is reshaping occupational skill requirements and increasing the importance of flexible adult continuing education. This study examines expressed demand for digital and labor-market-oriented online training in Slovakia, identifies the skill domains represented in program choices, and compares the characteristics of packages selected by employed and unemployed participants. The analysis used 1,717 de-identified participant-program records from the Skills for the Labor Market project, collected between April 2024 and November 2025. Training packages were classified by thematic area and described using analytically constructed indicators of digital intensity, practical orientation, occupational market relevance, and labor-market alignment. Frequency distributions, descriptive statistics, Spearman rank correlations, and Mann-Whitney U tests with effect-size estimates were applied. Demand was concentrated in information technology, software development, data analytics, digital marketing, and related applied fields. Selected packages generally combined high digital intensity, practical orientation, and occupational relevance. Employed and unemployed participants showed broadly similar choice profiles. title: Nanomaterials in the Hydrogen Economy: A Narrative Review of Production, Storage, Carbon Capture and Commercialisation
abstract: Hydrogen is widely regarded as a key component of future low-carbon energy systems, and nanomaterials are central to improving the efficiency and performance of the technologies that will deliver it. Existing reviews typically treat hydrogen production, storage and carbon capture separately; this narrative review compares nanomaterials across these selected domains using qualitative evidence categories and, where the data permit, indicative cost benchmarks. Of the 22 classes assessed, 19 are classified on the maturity axis. Of those, 14 show laboratory evidence only, three reach prototype or pilot evidence and two reach field or commercial evidence in the reviewed application. The remaining three have industrial precedent only in other applications and are not classified on this axis. Across six unmatched storage examples, reported capacities vary substantially, but the data do not support an application-specific maturity relationship. Cost data for nanomaterial-based hydrogen storage are particularly scarce compared with production and carbon capture, where indicative but inconsistently reported benchmarks exist. Commercialisation pathways, hydrogen carrier technologies and environmental, health, safety and life-cycle considerations are also examined alongside the potential contribution to industrial decarbonisation. Key research priorities are identified, including a five-poi…

title: First-Principles Study of ScM2 (M = C and N) Monolayers as High-Performance Anode Materials for Potassium-Ion Storage
abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for sustainable energy storage technologies has driven the exploration of alternatives to lithium-ion batteries, with potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) emerging as promising candidates owing to the natural abundance and favorable electrochemical properties of potassium. Two-dimensional (2D) scandium carbide (ScC2) and scandium nitride (ScN2) monolayers were systematically investigated as potential anode materials for PIBs through first-principles density functional theory calculations performed using the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The absence of imaginary phonon modes and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations confirm the dynamical and thermal stability of both monolayers, while electron localization function analysis reveals mixed ionic-metallic bonding in ScC2 and ionic-dominant charge transfer in ScN2, with both satisfying the Born mechanical stability criteria. Electronic band structure calculations using GGA-PBE and hybrid HSE06 functionals confirm an intrinsic metallic character in both materials, ensuring efficient electron transport during charge/discharge cycling. The most favorable K adsorption occurs at the Sc top site with adsorption energies of −0.86 eV and −1.32 eV for ScC2 and ScN2, respectively, with Bader charge analysis confirming a K+-like ionic character through charge transfers of 0.85e and 0.86e. The K-ion dif…

title: A Transient Boundary Element Framework for Pressure Buildup, Injectivity Enhancement, and Reactive Permeability Evolution During CO₂ Storage in Heterogeneous Carbonate Reservoirs
abstract: Background Reactive CO₂ injection couples multiphase flow, aqueous chemistry, mineral alteration and permeability changes. Methods This paper develops a transient subdomain boundary element formulation for a reduced single-fluid pressure-diffusion model with phenomenological pressure-activated permeability feedback, and specifies a physically based two-phase compositional reactive-transport extension and a finite-radius well coupling that remain to be implemented. Results Previously reported scenario outputs and tables are preserved as illustrative legacy calculations. They do not provide matched experimental calibration, reproducible convergence or mass-balance evidence, or uniquely defined physical well injectivity. Conclusions The original model illustrates pressure–property feedback but cannot support field-scale reactive CO₂ storage or injectivity forecasting without further coupled physics and numerical validation.

title: Productive, profitable and energy-efficient Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. based vegetable intercropping system under Northern Telangana zone
abstract: Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. based intercropping systems offer considerable scope for improving productivity, profitability and resource-use efficiency (RUE) under sustainable agricultural production systems. An experiment was conducted in rabi season 2022 at the Agricultural Research Station, Adilabad, Telangana to test the efficiency of intercropping different vegetables in mustard with different row ratios. A total of 13 treatments comprising sole crops such as mustard, sole root vegetables (radish, beetroot, carrot and potato) and their combination under 2 : 2 and 3 : 3 row ratios were considered in the randomised block design (RBD) of the experiment. It was found that the highest total economic yield (24212 kg ha-1), mustard equivalent yield (5775 kg ha-1), gross returns (₹338968 ha-1), net returns (₹264526 ha-1) and benefit-cost ratio (B : C) ratio (4.55) were obtained from the monocropping of radish. While among intercropping combinations, mustard with radish under 3 : 3 row ratio yielded the highest total economic yield (13515 kg ha-1), mustard equivalent yield (3964 kg ha-1), mustard oil yield (351 kg ha-1), gross returns (₹216033 ha-1), net returns (₹160966) and B : C ratio (3.92). These results were statistically comparable with mustard with radish at ratio 2 : 2. An energetic efficiency analysis concluded that the performance of the mustard with radish (3 : 3 and 2 :…

title: Do CEO Characteristics Constrain Firm Growth? Evidence from the U.S. Energy Industry
abstract: Objectives Drawing on Upper Echelons Theory (UET), this study examines the relationship between CEO characteristics and firm growth among publicly listed U.S. energy firms. Specifically, it investigates the effects of CEO tenure, CEO compensation, financial expertise, financial education, technical education, and CEO age on firm growth, thereby extending the application of UET to firm growth in the context of the U.S. oil and gas sector. Material and Methods The study employs panel data from 26 publicly listed U.S. oil and gas companies over the period 2011–2024. Firm growth is proxied by firm size, while the explanatory variables capture selected CEO demographic, educational, experiential, and compensation characteristics. Panel-data econometric techniques are employed to examine the relationship between CEO characteristics and firm growth. Results The empirical findings indicate that CEO tenure has a negative and statistically significant effect on firm growth, suggesting that longer CEO tenure may be associated with reduced flexibility in responding to strategic change. CEO compensation is positively and significantly associated with firm growth, indicating that compensation incentives may encourage expansion-oriented managerial decisions. A Survey of Vehicle-Enabled Control of Traffic for Freeway Flow in Partially Connected Environments
abstract: Abstract Efficient freeway traffic control can alleviate congestion, improve operational efficiency, and enhance traffic safety. With the rapid development of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and connectivity technologies, Connected Vehicles (CVs), including Connected Automated Vehicles (CAVs) and Connected Human-Driven Vehicles (C-HDVs), are expected to coexist with conventional Human-Driven Vehicles (HDVs) on freeways for a considerable period. In partially connected traffic environments, CVs can provide historical and real-time Vehicle Trajectory Data (VTD) as mobile sensing sources and can also influence surrounding traffic as mobile actuators through vehicle guidance and cooperative control, thereby enabling Vehicle-Enabled Control of Traffic (VECT) for freeway flow. This paper systematically reviews recent advances in VECT under partially connected environments. The literature is organized into four categories according to the functional role of CVs and the level at which information, decisions, or control actions are generated: (1) vehicle-trajectory-enabled traffic state analysis, (2) vehicle-trajectory-enabled traffic control, (3) vehicle-guidance-enabled traffic control, and (4) collaborative vehicle–flow control. The review covers traffic state estimation, traffic state prediction, traffic anomaly detection, Variable Speed Limit (VSL) control, Ramp Metering (…

الضوابط التي تحكم عملية تفتيش السيارات في القانون العراقي والقانون الكويتي

Analog‐Tunable Nonvolatile Memristors with Self‐Compliance Behavior via a MoS x ‐Interlayer Strategy for Neuromorphic Recognition and Zero‐Trust Image Encryption
abstract: ABSTRACT The von Neumann memory wall severely restricts the performance of traditional computing systems, and memristors have emerged as premier candidates for neuromorphic computing by virtue of their ability to integrate storage and computation functions. However, conventional HfO x memristors suffer from abrupt resistive switching and lack of intrinsic self‐protection, limiting their synaptic emulation performance. Herein, a novel nonvolatile HfO x /MoS x /HfO x trilayer heterostructure memristor with intrinsic self‐compliance and analog conductance modulation was constructed. The optimized device exhibits stable cycling endurance, multilevel retention stability and fast response speed, and achieves linear and symmetric conductance potentiation and depression. Furthermore, the proposed memristor successfully emulates diverse biological synaptic plasticities, including EPSC, IPSC, PPF, and PPD. A constructed neural network based on this device achieves a high handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 93.84% on the MNIST dataset, with excellent noise immunity and device variation robustness. Furthermore, the memristor acts as an irreplaceable physical entropy source for zero‐trust XOR‐based image encryption, generating ciphertext images with near‐optimal information entropy reaching 7.978 bits. This work presents a feasible MoS x interlayer modification strategy to optimize hi…

title: Sustainability as a Mediating Construct: Connection, Evaluative Openness, and the Risk of Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Similar sustainability commitments can become organizationally consequential in markedly different ways, yet the relational architecture producing this variation remains under‐theorized. This conceptual paper theorizes sustainability as a mediating construct through representational, projective, and organizing forms. Recursive translation explains how changes within one form feed back into the others, generating varying degrees of connection. Because connection does not determine which sustainability claims retain capacity to challenge and revise mediation, the framework introduces evaluative openness as a second, analytically independent dimension. Their intersection yields four configurations: symbolic, exploratory, embedded, and captured sustainability. The embedded–captured distinction reveals the central implication: strongly connected mediation can sustain coordinated action while the range of values, actors, evidence, and possible futures capable of redirecting that mediation progressively narrows. By separating connection from evaluative openness, the framework extends research on decoupling, hybrid organizing, and performativity and explains why organizational incorporation alone does not establish transformative capacity.

title: Biopolymer-Based Biopriming Strategy with Trichoderma virens to Enhance Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) Establishment
abstract: Biopriming cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) seeds with beneficial fungi and biopolymer matrices offer a sustainable strategy to enhance crop establishment in smallholder agriculture. This study evaluated four biopolymers—sodium alginate (SA), guar gum (GG), arabic gum (AG), and maltodextrin (MAL)—as film-coating delivery systems for Trichoderma virens. We assessed biopolymer-bioagent compatibility, optimal imbibition kinetics, conidium loading efficiency via scanning electron microscopy (SEM), early seedling growth promotion, and inoculant survival over 30 days of cold storage. Results indicated that while all matrices preserved seed viability, their efficacy varied significantly. SA demonstrated the highest initial conidia entrapment capacity and provided superior protection of the conidia throughout storage, maintaining peak fungal viability and 100% seed germination. Conversely, AG exhibited a stimulatory effect on seedling development, resulting in the highest total plant and radicle elongation compared to unformulated T. virens and the untreated control. Microstructural analysis confirmed that matrix architecture directly dictates conidia binding and distribution. In conclusion, biopolymer-based seed coatings significantly modulate the biopriming efficacy of T. virens. Selecting an optimal carrier requires balancing physical loading efficiency and shelf-life viability with plant…

title: Dose- and strategy-dependent effects of anti-angiogenic therapy on tumor growth and microenvironment remodeling
Distributed Fresnel Lens–Fiber System for Solar Light Collection and Transmission: Comparable Output Power with Reduced Thermal Loading
abstract: Concentrated solar radiation can be transported through optical fibers to remote locations; however, the high thermal load at the concentrator–fiber interface can limit the operation of systems using polymer optical fibers. This work investigates whether distributing a fixed solar collection area among multiple Fresnel lens–fiber channels can mitigate localized heating while maintaining comparable transmitted optical power. Two PMMA Fresnel lens–fiber configurations with the same nominal solar collection area were numerically and experimentally evaluated: a single-channel system and a four-channel system. Non-sequential ray-tracing simulations were used to analyze the optical performance and determine the lens–fiber coupling distances, while outdoor experiments and thermographic measurements were conducted to evaluate the thermal response. The numerical model predicted total output powers of 29.24 W and 31.39 W for the single- and four-channel configurations, respectively. Experimentally, visible melting occurred at the single-fiber entrance after approximately 40 s, whereas the four-channel system operated for more than 5 min without visible fiber deformation. These results indicate that distributing the solar collection area among multiple lens–fiber channels can reduce localized thermal loading while maintaining comparable total transmitted optical power.

title: An Analytical Transient Model for Three-Phase Transformer Reclosing Considering Hysteresis Residual Magnetism and Recovery Control of Cascading Failures in Cyber-Physical Power Systems
abstract: In cyber-physical power systems (CPPS), the inrush current generated during transformer reclosing can easily cause misjudgment of protection devices and thus serves as an important trigger for cascading failure propagation. Existing studies mostly rely on black-box electromagnetic transient simulations or simplified magnetization models, lacking analytical approaches that account for hysteresis and residual magnetism, and therefore fail to accurately characterize the coupling mechanism between physical transients and information-layer dynamics. To address this issue, an analytical transient model for three-phase transformer reclosing is established based on the Jiles–Atherton theory, in which the hysteresis loop and residual magnetism are embedded into the electromagnetic transient process as a differential–algebraic equation (DAE) set, and the semi-analytical dependence of the inrush peak, harmonic characteristics, and decay law on the residual flux and closing angle is derived. On this basis, an inrush-feature-driven probability model of protection misjudgment is constructed, a CPPS cascading failure propagation model incorporating physical–information state transitions is developed, and an adaptive reclosing recovery control strategy based on the node fault-state reachability is proposed. Simulations on the IEEE 39-bus system show that the proposed model accurately reproduce…

Subjective Age Discrepancy Associates With Sleep Quality in a Large Longitudinal Sample of Middle‐Aged and Older Adults
abstract: ABSTRACT While age is typically measured in chronological terms, subjective age has also been shown to be clinically relevant. Given the clinical importance of subjective age discrepancy (the distinction between chronological and subjective age), we aimed to examine whether it was associated with another important aspect of health, sleep quality, among middle‐aged and older British adults. Data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing was analysed. We used a longitudinal approach involving a primary test sample ( N = 11,050) and an independent replication sample ( N = 1800). Subjective sleep quality, sleep duration and frequency of difficulties falling asleep, staying asleep or experiencing unrefreshing sleep were self‐reported and subjective age discrepancy was derived from items regarding chronological age and subjective age. Regression analysis was conducted cross‐sectionally within a wave of data collection and longitudinally between two data waves separated by 4 years. Better sleep quality ( β = −0.11) and longer sleep duration ( β = −0.03) were associated cross‐sectionally with ‘younger’ subjective age discrepancy and unrefreshing sleep ( β = −0.12) emerged as the sleep factor most strongly associated with subjective age discrepancy. In the test sample, but not the replication sample, sleep quality had interactions with chronological age, sex and the presence of long…

title: EVOLUTION OF TURKISH GEOPOLITICAL STRATEGY: HISTORICAL AND ECONOMIC INSIGHTS
abstract: This paper reveals the basic stages of the transformation that Turkish geopolitical strategy and foreign policy have undergone in the 20th century by analyzing Türkiye’s position in the international system. The article mainly analyzes the framework of foreign policy built around a realist perspective that was followed during the founding period of the Republic of Türkiye, evaluates the challenges that Türkiye faced when it abandoned the basic philosophy of the founding period, and explains how the Republic’s geopolitical vision can guide the challenges that Türkiye faces in the environment of global fragilities. It argues that the need to redefine the elements of the geopolitical balance between Türkiye and the global powers, as was done one hundred years ago, is the key to Türkiye’s ability to overcome the possible political and economic difficulties in the contemporary era.

title: BRANDING CORPORATIVO, ESTRUTURAÇÃO ORGANIZACIONAL, ESTRATÉGIA DE MARCA E ASSESSORIA: UMA REVISÃO BIBLIOGRÁFICA E PROPOSIÇÃO DE UM MODELO PARA A INTERNACIONALIZAÇÃO DE PEQUENAS E MÉDIAS EMPRESAS NOS MERCADOS INTERNACIONAIS
abstract: Este artigo analisa como o branding corporativo, a estruturação organizacional e a estratégia de marca podem apoiar a internacionalização de pequenas e médias empresas, propondo um modelo de assessoria orientado à construção de reputação, adaptação e competitividade em mercados internacionais. Realiza-se uma revisão bibliográfica integrativa, de natureza analítico-conceitual, com protocolo transparente de busca e seleção de estudos publicados entre 2021 e 2026. Foram consideradas publicações localizáveis em Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Emerald, SciELO e Google Scholar, combinando descritores relacionados a branding corporativo, orientação de marca, estratégia, capacidades de marketing, internacionalização, reputação, processos empresariais, redes e pequenas e médias empresas. A síntese articula branding corporativo, visão baseada em recursos, capacidades dinâmicas, internacionalização e aprendizagem, orientação para o mercado, adaptação versus padronização, estruturação de processos, redes empresariais e governança. Os resultados indicam que a marca pode funcionar como capacidade estratégica quando é traduzida em identidade, posicionamento, promessa, cultura, processos, experiências e evidências reconhecíveis nos mercados-alvo. Para PMEs, a assessoria é especialmente relevante porque reduz assimetrias de conhecimento, organiza prioridades, seleciona mercados, estrutur…

title: Biopsy-free versus biopsy-confirmed robot-assisted radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of an investigational strategy
abstract: Background Routine prostate biopsy before radical prostatectomy (RP) provides histopathological confirmation and information for risk stratification but is associated with procedure-related morbidity. Advances in multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography (PSMA PET) have prompted interest in highly selected biopsy-free pathways. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026 for randomized or non-randomized comparative studies of biopsy-free RP (BF-RP) versus biopsy-confirmed RP (BC-RP). Analyses were stratified by study design, and fixed-effect models were used for design-specific subgroup estimates when at least two studies were available. Results Three comparative studies (one randomized trial and two non-randomized cohorts) contributed 532 analyzed participants. In the randomized trial, BF-RP was associated with shorter operative time (MD −15.06 min, 95% CI −22.11 to −8.01) and lower estimated blood loss (MD −29.80 mL, 95% CI −43.77 to −15.83). In the two non-randomized studies, BF-RP was also associated with shorter operative time (MD −9.89 min, 95% CI −12.29 to −7.49; I²=0%) and lower estimated blood loss (MD −20.56 mL, 95% CI −27.03 to −14.08; I²=47%). Non-randomized evidence favoured BF-RP for study-defined continence at 3 months (RR …

title: Sustainable Innovation Management: From Knowledge Creation to Resource Efficiency
abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to uncover the internal organizational mechanisms driving sustainable innovation and to develop a unified conceptual framework. To address the theoretical fragmentation in current research, a systematic review of 128 recent empirical articles was conducted, combining conceptual mapping of keyword co‐occurrences with qualitative thematic synthesis. The findings reveal a sequential organizational architecture comprising four interdependent pillars: cognitive foundations, strategic orchestration (driven by dynamic capabilities and strategic agility), technological amplification, and sustainable materialization, all supported by a transversal human and relational substrate. Based on these insights, the study proposes the capability‐based sustainable innovation (CBSI) framework. By integrating the resource‐based view, the knowledge‐based view, and the dynamic capabilities framework, the model explicates the operational sequence required to execute the twin transformation and achieve verifiable circular economy and environmental performance. The framework provides a structured agenda for future research and offers managers a practical blueprint for appropriately aligning human capital with digital investments.

title: Development of Potent METTL1 Inhibitors Using a Nanoscale Direct-To-Biology Strategy
abstract: Abstract The RNA methyltransferase METTL1/WDR4, which catalyzes N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification in tRNA, has emerged as a key regulator of mRNA translation, and its dysregulation is associated with cancer development. Here, we report the development of a potent series of METTL1 inhibitors by combining conventional structure−activity relationship (SAR) studies with a tandem direct-to-biology (D2B) approach. Lead compound VK238 inhibited METTL1 enzymatic activity at nanomolar concentrations and exhibited selectivity across a panel of methyltransferases and kinases. In a cellular context, pharmacological METTL1 inhibition reduced m7G levels in tRNAs, leading to apoptosis-mediated cell death in several acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines. Mechanistic studies combining biophysical experiments, photoaffinity labeling (PAL), and molecular docking suggested that this inhibitor series occupies the (S)-adenosylmethionine (SAM) binding pocket of METTL1. Collectively, these findings highlight METTL1 as a tractable and pharmacologically relevant target for therapeutic intervention in AML.

title: Fairness perceptions in marketing strategy and across the marketing mix: An integrative review and call to action
abstract: Abstract Fairness is a foundational and highly consequential construct in marketing, shaping purchase intentions, brand attitudes, complaints, boycotts, and word‐of‐mouth. Yet extant consumer research has largely concentrated on price fairness, leaving fairness across the rest of marketing strategy and the marketing mix comparatively underexplored. This review makes three contributions. First, we review and integrate the field's three theoretical foundations: dual entitlement, inequity aversion, and moralized cognition. Second, we organize recent findings in the fairness literature around two managerial frameworks: strategy (segmentation, targeting, and positioning) and tactics (promotion, place, and product, in addition to price). Third, we highlight understudied areas and topics across the full range of marketing activities and issue a call to action for future research.

Concealed Groundwater Day Zero: An Uncertainty–Scarcity–Vulnerability Framework for Assessing Groundwater Unsustainability and Hydro-Social Risk in Bangladesh
abstract: Groundwater depletion is a major environmental and socio-economic challenge in Bangladesh. This study evaluates the spatiotemporal dynamics of groundwater depletion and hydro-social vulnerability using 400 Bangladesh Water Development Board monitoring wells for 1990–2019. The conceptual basis is the Reliability–Resiliency–Vulnerability (RRV) framework; operationally, it is adapted into three normalized groundwater-stress components: Uncertainty (U, the frequency of threshold exceedance and therefore a proxy for unreliability), Scarcity (S, persistence or non-recovery after a drought episode), and Vulnerability (V, severity of groundwater-level deficit). These components are combined into a Groundwater Day Zero Index (DZI), while population and irrigation layers are used separately to characterize exposure. Drought episodes are defined when standardized groundwater level falls below −1 standard deviation of the long-term mean. Results indicate widespread depletion, with reported rates of about 0.15–0.21 m yr−1 in stressed northwestern and central regions. Dhaka has a severe DZI (≈0.91; >0.75), while much of the Barind Tract falls within high-to-severe conditions (≈0.72–0.78). National mean component values (U = 0.46, S = 0.52, V = 0.57) indicate predominantly moderate-to-high stress. title: Uncertainty-aware quantum machine learning for portfolio optimization: evidence from sector and multi-asset ETFs
Financial Aspects in the Field of Activation and Prevention Aimed at the Elderly Based on the Nysa Daily Care Centre and Nysa Senior+ Clubs
abstract: Aim: The article addresses the growing problem of the ageing population, as well as the role of the state in preventing and counteracting the negative effects of this process, by activating a range of measures to improve the condition and well-being of older people. The study was based on an analysis of the Nysa Daily Care Centre (Dzienny Dom Pobytu w Nysie; Nysa DCC) and its activities in 2016−2025 and the newly established Nysa Senior+ Clubs, as an example of the implementation of measures for seniors in the region. The Nysa DCC is also taking initiatives to increase the value of its incomes by conducting additional economic activity. Senior+ Clubs, on the other hand, operate on the basis of funds obtained annually from participation in public tenders, as part of the Senior+ government programme. The aim of the study was to show how public institutions carry out preventive activities in this area, and how they raise and spend funds. Methodology: The research method used was a case study. The author employed basic methods of statistical description. Findings: The institutions in Nysa are operating properly and meeting the needs of seniors. A leading institution is the Nysa DCC which serves an average of more than 200 people per year, while three Nysa Senior+ Clubs cater for 60 people in total. title: A Modified Northern Goshawk Optimization Algorithm for Truss Design Problems
abstract: Northern goshawk optimization, one of the metaheuristic algorithms recently proposed for solving optimization problems, is an optimization algorithm inspired by the behavior of the northern goshawk in nature. In this study, a fitness distance balance (FDB) strategy was incorporated into the northern goshawk optimization algorithm to enhance its performance. This strategy strengthens the algorithm’s search capability and improves solution quality. Consequently, the algorithm developed with the fitness distance balance strategy has been named the modified northern goshawk optimization algorithm (MNGO). The performance of the proposed MNGO was analyzed using fifteen different benchmark functions, taking into account population size and the number of dimensions. The experimental results obtained are presented along with convergence plots. Furthermore, the proposed MNGO was compared with some other algorithms in the literature; convergence plots, box plots, and radar charts were used, and statistical analyses were also conducted. As a result of these analyses, it was observed that the performance of the MNGO improved as the number of dimensions increased. In addition, the performance of the proposed MNGO was examined statistically. Furthermore, the proposed MNGO algorithm was applied to challenging and complex 10-bar, 37-bar, 52-bar, 72-bar, and 200-bar truss problems, which are rea…

title: Beyond CRBN and VHL: DCAF16-Recruiting Degraders from Rational Design to Clinical Translation
abstract: Abstract Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has revolutionized modern drug discovery. However, the current clinical landscape remains predominantly reliant on CRBN and VHL, restricting the targetable proteome and increasing the risk of acquired resistance. Expanding the TPD toolbox with therapeutically tractable E3 ligases is imperative. Recently, DCAF16 has emerged as a frontrunner in this effort, underscored by the advancement of DCAF16-based monovalent degraders such as PLX-61639 and AMX-883 toward clinical evaluation. Unlike the historically serendipitous discovery of CRBN-based molecular glues, DCAF16 offers a versatile platform for the rational design of both bifunctional and monovalent degraders. In this timely perspective, we present the first comprehensive medicinal chemistry analysis of the DCAF16-mediated degradation landscape, focusing on delineating the expanding diversity of recruiting motifs and elucidating the design principles, structural basis, and SAR of representative degraders. Finally, we outline current challenges and offer insights into future design strategies and clinical translation of DCAF16-based degraders.

title: On the Kolmogorov constant explicit form in the theory of discrete-time stochastic branching systems – CORRIGENDUM
abstract: Abstract The explicit expression for the Kolmogorov constant given in Theorem 1.2 of [1] has a restricted range of validity: it gives the constant precisely for linear-fractional offspring generating functions, whereas for other subcritical offspring generating functions the constant may be strictly larger or strictly smaller than that expression. Within the class of embeddable offspring generating functions the expression is a sharp lower bound for the constant.

title: OpenGRF: prediction of ground reaction forces and moments during activities of daily living using OpenSim
abstract: Abstract OpenGRF is a new OpenSim-based tool that estimates ground reaction forces and moments (GRF&Ms) and centre of pressure (CoP) directly from joint kinematics, addressing an existing limitation of current OpenSim workflows. The approach combines calibrated foot–ground contact probes with an optimization framework derived from static optimization, and computes CoP by accounting for both kinematic and dynamic contributions. Its performance was validated against force-plate measurements. Validation involved 126 marker-based trials from seven healthy adults, each performing six trials of level walking, stair ascent and stair descent. Results showed the highest accuracy for vertical GRF, with normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) ≤ 1.5% and Pearson's correlation coefficient (ρ) ≥ 0.94, particularly during level walking. Anterior–posterior GRF was also satisfactorily predicted (nRMSE 4.4%–6.1%, ρ = 0.81–0.91). By contrast, medial–lateral GRF was less reliable, especially in stair tasks, with errors up to 11.2% and correlations as low as 0.48. Free moments were the hardest variable to estimate (nRMSE up to 28%), whereas ankle moments showed excellent agreement with force-plate data (nRMSE ≈ 1.7%, ρ ≈ 0.98). Median CoP error was 21–23 mm, with the largest discrepancies during double support. Overall, OpenGRF enables physics-consistent estimation of GRF-related variables, parti…

title: Economic Fundamentals and Short-Run Exchange Rate Prediction: A Machine-Learning Perspective
abstract: Abstract The exchange rate predictability puzzle—that fundamentals fail to forecast short-horizon exchange rate movements out of sample—has long resisted resolution. We show that fundamentals do matter, but their effects vary with global financial conditions. Using a rich set of country characteristics interacted with global state variables and machine-learning techniques to handle the high-dimensional data, we document that interactions between country characteristics and foreign exchange market volatility are particularly important, consistent with a “flight to fundamentals” during periods of financial stress. Our forecasts deliver substantial economic value and offer new insight into the carry trade.
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis

title: GECKO-A v1.0: exploring VOC oxidation trajectories through comparison with the master chemical mechanism
abstract: Numerical models are crucial tools for understanding complex chemical systems such as the atmosphere, and their sensitivity across a range of conditions. In atmospheric chemistry models, reaction mechanisms are used to represent chemical transformations and define the underlying system of equations. Building highly explicit mechanisms that capture the full complexity of organic oxidation occurring in the atmosphere remains challenging owing to the large number of intermediates involved, the breadth of reaction pathways, and the limited availability of reliable kinetic and thermodynamic data. The Generator for Explicit Chemistry and Kinetics of Organics in the Atmosphere (GECKO-A) was developed to address these limitations by enabling the systematic construction of near-explicit mechanisms. Here, we present its first open-source release (v1.0), which incorporates updated chemical protocols and structure-activity relationships, together with its companion box model for mechanism integration. GECKO-A's performance is benchmarked through systematic comparisons with the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM v3.3.1), based on simulations of the oxidation of five representative hydrocarbons (butane, octane, dodecane, toluene, and α -pinene) under environmental conditions ranging from urban to remote. The two approaches yield similar oxidation pathways for small and structurally simple compou…

title: Transformation of Human Resource Management in Islamic Education: Problems, Global Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Human resource management in Islamic education has become a strategic issue in improving the quality, competitiveness, and sustainability of educational institutions in the modern era. This article aims to analyze the transformation of human resource management in Islamic education by focusing on major problems, global challenges, and future development prospects. This study employs a qualitative approach using library research methods through the collection of books, scientific journals, academic articles, and relevant documents related to Islamic educational management and human resource development. Data were analyzed using content analysis techniques to identify important themes and concepts associated with the transformation of human resource management in Islamic education. The findings indicate that Islamic educational institutions continue to face several major problems, including limited teacher professionalism, inadequate digital competence, weak organizational leadership, and insufficient welfare systems for educators. Global challenges such as digital transformation, educational competition, technological disruption, and changing student characteristics have intensified the need for strategic reform in educational management. However, Islamic education also possesses strong future prospects through the integration of Islamic values, digital innovation, continuous pr…

title: Effects of air pollution on corporate charitable donations: evidence from China
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the impact of air pollution on corporate charitable giving by combining listing data from the China Stock Market and Accounting Research Database (CSMAR) and data on air pollution in Chinese cities. Using the instrumental variable method and regression discontinuity design, it explores the impact of air pollution on corporate charitable donations and further explores the impact of air pollution on state-owned enterprises and enterprises in high-pollution industries. Design/methodology/approach Using 2013–2019 data from Chinese listed firms and air quality indices, this study examines air pollution as a new influence factor. To address omitted variable bias, regressions include industry/year fixed effects, regional economic controls and corporate governance variables. Endogeneity concerns are mitigated via three tests: an instrumental variable (thermal inversion) for reverse causality, a regression discontinuity test and a Huai River policy placebo test – all yielding robust results. Findings Empirical results show air pollution significantly reduces corporate charitable donations: a 10% pollution increase correlates with an approximately 30% decrease in corporate charitable donations. These findings hold after robustness checks (excluding air quality index (AQI) manipulation, alternative measures and first-tier cities). Effects are heterogeneo…

title: Integrated early childhood development services in market and cross-border communities in Rwanda: a mixed-methods pre–post evaluation
abstract: Background Families working in markets and cross-border trade often have limited access to affordable and safe childcare. This study assessed the implementation, reach, and service quality of integrated early childhood development (ECD) centers established in market and cross-border communities in Rwanda. It also examined differences between baseline and endline samples in complementary feeding, nutritional status, child development, health and hygiene practices, caregiving, and child protection, while exploring stakeholder experiences, implementation constraints, and sustainability. Methods An embedded mixed-methods pre–post evaluation compared independent cross-sectional samples of child–caregiver pairs assessed at baseline ( n = 551) and endline ( n = 421). Survey-round differences were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression. Endline focus group discussions (FGDs), key-informant interviews (KIIs), and structured observations conducted at all eight centers documented service delivery, staffing, infrastructure, learning materials, safety, accessibility, and other implementation conditions. Results The eight centers provided integrated early learning, nutrition, health, hygiene, and child-protection services to 701 children. Endline survey participation was associated with higher adjusted odds of meeting minimum meal frequency (AOR = 2.66; 9…

abstract: การเพิกถอนบทความ วารสารวิชาการ มทร.สุวรรณภูมิ ขอเพิกถอนบทความ (Retracted Article) บทความเรื่อง การประยุกต์ใช้วิธีทากูชิสําหรับกระบวนการเชื่อมเสียดทานกวนแบบจุด ระหว่างอะลูมิเนียมผสม Al6061-T6 กับเหล็กกล้าความแข็งแรงสูง โดยการศึกษาค่าพารามิเตอร์ที่ดีที่สุดของเครื่องจักรในการผลิต (Silachai, A., & Prasomthong, S. 2021) ภายหลังการตีพิมพ์ ได้มีการแจ้งรายงานจากนักวิจัยมายังกองบรรณาธิการ เกี่ยวกับบทความดังกล่าวมีเนื้อหาซ้ำซ้อนกับผลงานที่ได้รับการเผยแพร่ในปี 2565 อย่างมีนัยสำคัญ ตามขั้นตอนการพิจารณาการรายงานจากนักวิจัย กองบรรณาธิการได้ดำเนินการตรวจสอบตามหลักเกณฑ์และแนวปฏิบัติด้านจริยธรรมการตีพิมพ์ของวารสาร และยินยันว่ามีความซ้ำซ้อนทางวิชาการ การตีพิมพ์ซ้ำซ้อน (Redundant Publication / Self-Plagiarism) รวมถึงการนำภาพถ่ายผลการทดลองมาใช้ซ้ำ ผลการตรวจสอบดังกล่าวทำให้กองบรรณาธิการมีมติให้เพิกถอนบทความ (Silachai, A., & Prasomthong, S. 2021) ฉบับนี้

title: The ‘invisible hands’ depicting early electricity: the careers of james mynde and john ingram at the royal society and the académie royale des sciences
abstract: Abstract While the historiography of eighteenth-century electricity has consolidated over the past fifty years, scholarly attention remains focused on natural philosophers, largely overlooking the hidden artisans behind early scientific imagery in this field. This paper addresses this gap by reconstructing the institutional trajectories of two British illustrators and engravers: James Mynde (1702–1770) and John Ingram (1721–ca 1776). Drawing upon extensive archival research at the Royal Society and the Académie Royale des Sciences, this study recovers their professional routines and institutional ties between the 1740s and 1760s, amid a rapid expansion in studies on electricity. As the primary engravers for the Philosophical Transactions and the Histoire et Mémoires, respectively, Mynde and Ingram produced virtually all electrical imagery published by these societies during this early stage of studies in electricity. This historical analysis reveals that producing these images involved diverse factors far removed from conceptual debates regarding what electricity was. Ultimately, it demonstrates how Mynde's and Ingram's work actively built a distinct iconography that underscored the empirical and captivating nature of electricity, highlighting the impact of these ‘invisible hands’ on the circulation of scientific knowledge.
venue: Notes and Records: the Royal Society journal of the history of science

title: Strategic reorientation under institutional volatility: a conceptual replication in an emerging-market fintech context
abstract: Purpose This study aims to conduct a bounded conceptual replication of McDonald and Gao’s (2019) strategic reorientation framework, examining what it retains, how stakeholder tension is contextually modified and which supporting interpretations become analytically useful in two Turkish fintech cases with varying regulatory salience. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative conceptual replication was conducted across two early-stage Turkish fintech ventures, Alpha and Beta, through nine in-depth founder interviews, documentary analysis and triangulation of secondary data. McDonald and Gao’s audience-management constructs, product framing, audience expectations and penalties and the anticipation, justification and staging of reorientation served as sensitizing concepts. Findings The framework’s broader audience-management problem remains recognizable in both cases but requires contextual qualification. Alpha provides the closer-transfer case, with predominantly market-related stakeholder tension. Beta provides the stronger contextual-modification case, where regulatory salience is more visible alongside customer-process, market and investor considerations. State-induced logic is therefore treated as an article-level interpretation most clearly evidenced in Beta, while founder-centric governance and situated legitimacy-building remain supporting interpretations. Practical implica…

title: Marketing Digitalization for Traditional MSMEs: Market Access, Digital Literacy, and Program Sustainability
abstract: Micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Cikondang Village, Cianjur Regency, face marketing challenges, including dependence on intermediaries, limited digital literacy, and the lack of integration between product information and online market access. This article describes the marketing digitalization assistance process, identifies supporting and inhibiting factors, and outlines requirements for program sustainability. The community engagement program was conducted from 15 July to 23 August 2026 using a participatory qualitative descriptive approach. Data were collected through observation, semi-structured interviews, and activity documentation involving MSME owners and village officials. Activities included coordination and data collection, socialization, and assistance with Business Identification Numbers (NIB), QRIS, Google Maps/Google Business Profile, and a village product-catalog website. The findings indicate that a combination of direct assistance, village institutional support, and youth involvement helped establish a more structured foundation for digital presence. However, limited digital skills and internet connectivity remained obstacles. As the evaluation was conducted during the program period, increases in revenue, profit margins, and competitiveness cannot be concluded as measurable impacts. Program sustainability requires the appointment of a web…

title: QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE GLOBAL HYDRAULIC MARKET DEVELOPMENT
abstract: The article provides an integrative quantitative and qualitative assessment of the global hydraulic equipment market, combining data from recent commercial reports, consulting studies and scientific publications. The analysis confirms that, despite methodological differences, all major sources predict sustained market expansion with an average compound annual growth rate of about 4% over the next decade, indicating favourable conditions for entering industrial and mobile hydraulics. Particular attention is paid to regional distribution, sectoral structure and component-level dynamics, showing the leading roles of Asia-Pacific, construction and mobile hydraulics, as well as the rising importance of energy-efficient pumps, smart systems and advanced actuators. The study identifies three key transformation drivers: electrification, digitalisation and smart hydraulics, and the green transition, which jointly shape future R&D priorities.

title: Imaging therapeutic response at brain neuroimmune interfaces in women with systemic lupus erythematosus
abstract: Purpose Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) frequently affects the central nervous system, likely via neuroimmune interfaces; how these interfaces respond longitudinally to standard therapy remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify these therapeutic dynamics. Methods This retrospective longitudinal study included 63 women with SLE who had brain MRI at baseline and after standard therapy. Enlarged perivascular spaces (ePVS), choroid plexus (CP), and gray matter (GM) volumes were segmented from 3D T1-weighted images; the diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index was computed from DTI scans. Paired t-tests compared baseline and post-therapy values. Patients were grouped into neuropsychiatric SLE (NPSLE) and non-NPSLE groups, and longitudinal deltas compared. Spearman correlations assessed associations of MRI changes with clinical measures. Results After standard therapy, all 63 patients showed clinical improvement (decreased SLEDAI-2K, increased MoCA scores). Left DTI-ALPS index increased (T = -2.475, P FDR = 0.048), and bilateral CP volumes decreased (left: T = 2.432, P FDR = 0.048; right: T = 3.330, P FDR = 0.006). ePVS volumes remained unchanged. No significant correlations emerged between MRI changes and clinical scores, and improvement did not differ between NPSLE and non-NPSLE subgroups. Conclusions Longitudinal MRI identified measurable altera…

A Supramolecular Symmetry-Breaking Strategy for Enhanced Circularly Polarized Luminescence, High-Temperature Phase Transition, and Piezoelectric Response in Chiral Manganese(II) Halides
abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) has attracted intense interest for applications in 3D displays, optical data storage, and quantum information processing. Chiral organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides (HOMHs) have emerged as promising CPL materials owing to their structural tunability, facile solution processability, and tunable photoluminescence, yet they often suffer from small luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum) and limited functionality. Herein, we report a pair of enantiomeric host–guest compounds, [18-crown-6]2[(R/S)-C3H12N2][MnCl4] (R-Mn and S-Mn; (R/S)-C3H12N2 = (R/S)-propane-1,2-diammonium), via a supramolecular assembly strategy. The resulting two-in-one structures feature strong N–H···O hydrogen bonds that lock the chiral cations and reduce the crystal symmetry from the C2 phase of the previously reported compound without 18-crown-6 to the lowest-symmetry P1 space group. R/S-Mn exhibits CPL with |glum| = 2.6 × 10–2, more than 10 times higher than the previously reported value of 2 × 10–3. Moreover, both compounds display a reversible high-temperature solid–solid phase transition at 405 K and a measurable piezoelectric coefficient of 11 pC/N. DFT calculations reveal that the band edges and emissive states are dominated by the [MnCl4]2– units. Meanwhile, the organic cations do not contribute to the electronic transitions, indicating that the CPL ari…

title: Perceptions of Trade Remedy Law and Firms’ Response Readiness in Vietnam: A Stimulus–Organism–Response Approach
abstract: This study examines the factors associated with firms’ response readiness to trade remedy measures among business owners and managers of import–export enterprises, with perceived legal effectiveness of trade remedy law and trust in the legal and enforcement system examined as mediating variables. The research model is grounded in the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework and empirically tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Data were collected from a survey of 425 business owners and managers of import–export enterprises in Vietnam, an emerging economy in Asia. The findings indicate that perceived legal fairness, legal information accessibility, and perceived government support are positively associated with firms’ response readiness through selected indirect pathways involving legal effectiveness and institutional trust. In contrast, perceived legal clarity and digital legal information quality are not significantly associated with firms’ response readiness. Furthermore, importance–performance map analysis (IPMA) identifies perceived legal effectiveness of trade remedy law and trust in the legal and enforcement system as priority factors for enhancing firms’ response readiness. The findings contribute to the empirical literature on trade remedies by extending the analysis to firms’ perceptions and behavioral readiness. They also prov…

title: Factors associated with treatment response to microwave ablation of benign thyroid nodules: a retrospective single-center study of nodule composition and vascularity
abstract: Background This study aimed to evaluate radiological and procedural factors associated with treatment response in benign thyroid nodules treated with microwave ablation (MWA). Methods Of 90 consecutive patients who underwent MWA for cytologically benign (Bethesda II) thyroid nodules, 80 who completed 12 months of follow-up were retrospectively analyzed. Pre-procedural ultrasonography was used to assess nodule volume, composition, and Doppler vascularity. All ablations were performed under ultrasound guidance using the moving-shot technique, and volume reduction ratio (VRR) was calculated during follow-up at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary outcome, treatment success, was defined as a VRR ≥75% at 12 months. Pearson correlation and multivariable logistic regression (forced-entry method) analyses were performed to determine factors influencing response. Results The mean patient age was 46.7 ± 16.6 years, and 66.3% were female. Mean baseline nodule volume was 11.75 ± 3.31 mL. Nodules were predominantly cystic in 38.8%, solid in 35%, and mixed in 26.3%. Mean VRR increased progressively during follow-up, from 26.2 ± 8.1% at 1 month to 72.5 ± 5.9% at 12 months, and treatment success (VRR ≥75%) was achieved in 35.0% of patients (28/80), whereas all nodules (100%) achieved a VRR ≥50%. Regrowth (any volume increase from the smallest recorded volume) occurred in 25.0% of patients, repe…

title: Immune Response to Hepatitis B Vaccination According to National EPI Schedule among Children Below 2 Years
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus infection is a public health burden globally. We incorporate Hep-B vaccine in our EPI schedule. There is no comprehensive data regarding the immune response of the HBV vaccine at one year in our country. The study was done to assess the immune response among HBV vaccinated children at this age group. Materials and methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at EPI outdoor of Chittagong Medical College Hospital from January to December, 2022. Blood sample from 375 vaccinated children were tested for Anti-HBs titre by ELISA technique in between 9 months to 15 months. Statistical analyses were performed with Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 23.0. Results: This study shows that older children and male tend to have better immune responses after vaccination and malnutrition is a significant risk factor for low antibody titers. This study also shows that 79.2% of children had satisfactory or high levels of anti-HBs antibodies (≥10 mIU/mL). However, 20.8% of children had low antibody titers (<10 mIU/mL) indicating inadequate immune protection. Conclusion: Most children vaccinated under the current EPI schedule develop protective immunity against hepatitis B; a small proportion remain vulnerable due to inadequate seroconversion. Key words: Anti HBs; EPI; Hep-B vaccination; One-year><10 mIU/mL) indicating inadequate immune protection. Co…

title: Parent–teacher support congruence and adolescents’ academic well-being: a response surface analysis
abstract: Background Parental support and teacher support are usually studied as separate predictors of adolescents’ academic functioning, which leaves open whether the correspondence between these two resources carries its own significance. Drawing on ecological systems theory, developmental assets theory, and person–environment fit perspectives, this study examined how the joint configuration of parental and teacher support is associated with adolescents’ academic well-being, and whether expectancy-value motivation statistically accounts for part of this association. Methods Participants were 2,492 junior high school students (1,266 girls, 1,224 boys; M age = 13.04, SD = 0.88) nested within 101 classrooms in China. Multilevel polynomial regression with response surface analysis (RSA) was estimated in 20 multiply imputed datasets. The random-effects structure was selected by likelihood-ratio tests; the retained model, which included a random classroom intercept and a random slope for teacher support, was used for all surface parameters, figures, and mediation analyses. Surface parameters were tested directly, using standard errors from the pooled covariance matrix and a classroom-level cluster bootstrap. Results Motivation and well-being were higher when parental and teacher support were jointly high than when both were low (congruence-line slopes a 1 = 0.65 and 0.69). The direction of …

title: Intermittent Demand Forecasting and Inventory Service Level Evaluation Using The TSB Method and Machine Learning: A Case Study on PT X in The Document Solutions Industry
abstract: Intermittent demand presents significant challenges in demand forecasting and inventory management, particularly in the document solutions industry, where demand is driven by both rental and sales activities. Forecasting accuracy alone does not necessarily translate into improved inventory performance. This study evaluates the forecasting performance of the Teunter–Syntetos–Babai (TSB) method and machine learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM, across total, rental, and sales demand categories and examines their implications for inventory service levels. A quantitative analysis was conducted using supply demand data for 134 stock-keeping units (SKUs) of Brand Z at PT X from August 2023 to November 2025. Demand patterns were classified using the Average Demand Interval (ADI) and the squared coefficient of variation (CV²). Forecasting models incorporated historical demand, lead times, new printer installations, and new printer sales. Forecasting performance was evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE), while inventory performance was assessed using an order-up-to-level (S) policy based on the probability of no stockout (S1), fill rate (S2), and ready rate (S3). Random Forest demonstrated superior overall performance in terms of forecasting accuracy and inventory service levels, particularly for intermittent and lumpy dem…

title: Aggregating Demand and Standardizing Supply: Instrument Choice for U.S. Small Modular Reactor Deployment
abstract: The United States leads the world in small modular reactor (SMR) designs and has yet to complete a commercial deployment. Federal awards, hyperscaler agreements, and state funds are now underwriting first units for the leading projects, but serial factory production, the basis of the SMR value proposition, has begun nowhere, because the supply chain has neither a standard to tool against nor firm orders that justify tooling. This article asks what the minimal sufficient intervention is. Comparative analysis of SEMATECH, the French and Korean nuclear programs, and five decades of American standardization and cost-share attempts yields four diagnostic dimensions, and seven candidate instruments are rated against them on a five-point scale. None is sufficient alone. The design that prevails pairs two institutions for light-water SMRs and dominates a SEMATECH-style broad-membership consortium. In consensus standards work, ASME code cases carry vessel and component design rules, an ASTM International subcommittee writes the material, fabrication, and test specifications those rules cite, and the NRC accepts the result through its existing incorporation-by-reference process. A time-limited program in the DOE Office of Nuclear Energy, holding a no-year appropriation, makes fixed milestone payments and commits to buy the unsubscribed share of each qualifying unit’s output, up to a cap,…
