title: Case Report: Durable response to lenalidomide rechallenge after azacitidine failure in myelodysplastic neoplasm with del(5q)
abstract: Lower-risk myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) with isolated del(5q) are particularly sensitive to lenalidomide, although most patients eventually lose their response and may experience disease progression. Hypomethylating agents (HMAs) are commonly used as salvage therapy after lenalidomide failure, but treatment options following subsequent HMA failure remain limited. Evidence regarding lenalidomide rechallenge after intervening HMA therapy is scarce. We report the long-term clinical course of a woman with MDS with del(5q) and multilineage dysplasia, diagnosed after prior cytotoxic therapy for colon adenocarcinoma. Lenalidomide was started for transfusion-dependent anemia (IPSS Intermediate-1; IPSS-R Intermediate) and resulted in transfusion independence and a complete cytogenetic response after four cycles. Hematologic remission was maintained for more than three years, but lenalidomide was discontinued after 41 cycles because of progressive cytopenias and cytogenetic evolution. The patient subsequently received 36 cycles of azacitidine, achieving transient hematologic improvement before disease progression with an increase in bone marrow blasts. Because the del(5q) clone persisted and no established salvage option was available, lenalidomide was reintroduced at the original starting dose and produced a rapid erythroid response together with a reduction in bone marrow blasts, wi…

title: Trap-Assisted Photoconductive Gain and Wavelength-Dependent Response of Ti 3 C 2 F MXene/GaN van der Waals Heterojunction Ultraviolet Detectors
abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet photodetection is essential for secure optical communication, environmental monitoring and early warning systems, yet conventional GaN-based Schottky detectors rely on evaporated metal electrodes that introduce interfacial defects and limited UV transmittance. Here we report a solution-processed Ti 3 C 2 F MXene/GaN van der Waals Schottky heterojunction UV photodetector formed by low-temperature drop-coating. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Raman analysis confirm the surface termination and structural integrity of the transferred MXene, and density-functional-theory calculations rationalize the tunable Schottky barrier. The device exhibits a low dark current of ~74 nA near zero bias, about 30% lower than that of conventional Ti/Au Schottky GaN detectors. Wavelength-resolved measurements at 300, 310 and 320 nm show a photocurrent ordering of 320 nm > 310 nm > 300 nm, governed by the interplay between photon penetration depth and near-surface recombination. Under 320 nm illumination at 1.91 W/cm 2 and -4 V, a responsivity of 0.58 A/W, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 212% and a specific detectivity of 3.35 × 10 11 Jones are obtained; the above-unity EQE indicates trap-mediated internal photoconductive gain in GaN. Periodic UV switching yields rise/fall times of 1.22/0.80 s with an on/off ratio of ~2.2 and <5% peak-to-peak variation over four c…

title: Understanding household food demand in Sri Lanka using a two-step budgeting framework
abstract: Purpose Sri Lanka has been affected by a severe economic crisis in recent years, which has changed food consumption behavior. Therefore, this study examines household demand for major food groups in Sri Lanka and provides evidence on how households respond to changes in food prices and expenditure. Design/methodology/approach A two-step budgeting framework combined with the quadratic almost ideal demand system (QUAIDS) was employed to estimate expenditure and price elasticities for major food groups, including cereals, pulses, vegetables, fruits, fish, meat, eggs and milk products, using data from the Household Income and Expenditure Survey (HIES). Findings The results show that cereals, pulses, eggs and vegetables all have an expenditure elasticity of less than one, while for fruits, fish, meat and milk products, the elasticity is greater than one. The estimated own-price elasticities suggest that households are more responsive to price changes for fruits, fish, eggs, meat and milk products than cereals, pulses and vegetables. Research limitations/implications This study's findings will help policymakers develop appropriate policies and targeted programs to mitigate the impact of the ongoing economic crisis and improve the overall well-being and nutrition of the Sri Lankan population. Originality/value This study provides a recent empirical evidence on household food demand in…

title: Incorporating authority perception, economic status and behavioural response in infectious disease control
abstract: Abstract We introduce a multi-population mean field game framework to examine how economic status and authority perception shape vaccination and social distancing decisions under different epidemic control policies. We conducted a survey to inform our model and stratify the population into six groups by income and perception of authority, capturing behavioural heterogeneity. Individuals choose socialization and vaccination levels to optimize objectives such as minimizing treatment costs, complying with social distancing guidelines if they are authority-followers, or reducing losses from decreased social interactions if they are authority-indifferents, alongside economic costs. Public health authorities influence behaviour through social distancing guidelines and vaccination costs. We characterize the Nash equilibrium via a forward–backward differential equation system, provide its mathematical analysis and numerically solve it. Our findings reveal a trade-off between social distancing and vaccination. Under stricter guidelines that target both susceptible and infected individuals, followers reduce both socialization and vaccination levels, while indifferents increase socialization owing to followers’ preventative measures. Adaptive guidelines targeting infected individuals effectively reduce infections and narrow the gap between low- and high-income groups, while lower vaccinat…

title: Characteristic electric-field manipulation of the optical response in monolayer graphene oxide
abstract: The flourishing research on graphene oxide (GO)-based optical sensing platforms, laser media, and optoelectronic devices calls for efficient, reversible, and spatially resolved methods to acquire and control multimodal optical information from GO. Here, we demonstrate that the optical transmission and fluorescence of monolayer GO (mGO)—two complementary optical readouts—can be reversibly manipulated by an external electric field (EEF) as low as ±1 kV/mm; the dual-channel optical responses are monitored simultaneously by a home-built scanning confocal microscope with a spatial resolution of about 300 nm, yielding spatially resolved, real-time multimodal optical information from every probed spot. Domain-resolved dual-channel imaging reveals that the absorption and emission of mGO are spatially heterogeneous and, more strikingly, that adjacent domains on a single mGO flake respond to the EEF in opposite directions: the transmission of one domain increases by more than 25% while its fluorescence is quenched almost completely, whereas the neighboring domain exhibits a ∼25% decrease in transmission together with a twofold fluorescence enhancement. We further define, for each probing spot, a characteristic electric field E c —the smallest field at which the transmission or fluorescence departs from its zero-field baseline by more than three standard deviations of the baseline noise. …

title: Stem cell mobilization with G-CSF and on-demand plerixafor in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients treated with daratumumab: a single-center experience
abstract: Introduction Daratumumab-containing induction therapy improves treatment response in transplant-eligible patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma but may impair hematopoietic stem cell mobilization. We evaluated the effect of daratumumab exposure on stem cell mobilization and collection and assessed the effectiveness of on demand plerixafor in patients with inadequate mobilization. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 215 transplant-eligible patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated at a single center between January 2022 and February 2025. Patients underwent granulocyte colony-stimulating factor–based mobilization, with plerixafor administered on demand on the fourth day of mobilization. The primary endpoint was peripheral blood CD34+ cell concentration on day 4 of mobilization. Secondary endpoints included plerixafor use, number of apheresis procedures, total CD34+ cells collected, and mobilization failure. Results Eighty-two patients received daratumumab-containing induction and 133 did not. The median peripheral blood CD34+ cell concentration on day 4 of mobilization was significantly lower after daratumumab exposure than without (9.61 vs 20.0 × 10 6 cells/L; P < 0.001). Plerixafor was required in 74.4% versus 39.8% of patients, respectively (P < 0.001). Among patients who received plerixafor, the median peripheral blood CD34+ cell concentration incr…

title: From urban digital embeddedness to management decisions: understanding innovative SMEs' digital orientation
abstract: Purpose Developed for management decision's “The Practice of Making Decisions” section, this study examines a concrete managerial dilemma: what can managers learn by considering how deeply digital technologies are embedded in the urban environment alongside their availability? We examine how urban digital embeddedness is associated with innovative small and medium-sized enterprise (SMEs') digital orientation (DO) and its four dimensions. Design/methodology/approach The study combines city- and firm-level information for 24 Italian cities and 243 innovative SMEs observed over 13 years. Urban digital embeddedness captures citizens' use of home banking, municipal applications and broadband services. SMEs' DO is derived from annual mission statements and assessed across digital technology scope, digital capabilities, digital ecosystem coordination and digital architecture configuration. Relationships are estimated using a two-way fixed-effects Spatial Durbin Panel Model. Findings The findings show that urban digital embeddedness is most consistently associated with firms' stated digital capabilities and digital ecosystem coordination, followed by digital architecture configuration, while evidence for digital technology scope is comparatively weak. Practical implications Managers should look beyond digital technologies when making digital-strategy decisions and consider how technolo…

title: Value co-creation pathways for construction waste reduction
abstract: Purpose This study aims to address the persistent challenges of fragmented collaboration and unclear value exchange in construction waste reduction (CWR). It seeks to develop a systematic understanding of how stakeholders collaborate by constructing a stakeholder value network (SVN) model. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was employed, integrating value co-creation and social exchange theory. The SVN model was developed and analyzed using data from a literature review, policy analysis and semi-structured expert interviews. The network analysis identified 45 value streams and 846 value loops, with robustness ensured through sensitivity analysis. Findings The results reveal that non-economic values, specifically knowledge sharing, policy support and social recognition, play a more critical structural role than financial incentives in sustaining collaborative networks. Furthermore, contractors, owners and designers form the triadic core of CWR governance, whereas suppliers and the public assume more peripheral roles than traditionally presumed. Originality/value This study contributes a novel, network-based analytical framework for examining multi-stakeholder cooperation in sustainability-oriented projects. It challenges the conventional overemphasis on economic drivers as the primary collaborative force and redefines core governance actors. Based on the findin…

title: The role of AI adoption in the relationship between digital self-efficacy and sustainable entrepreneurship intentions among university students in Jordan
abstract: Purpose This study investigates associations among digital self-efficacy (DSE), artificial intelligence (AI) adoption intention and sustainable entrepreneurship intentions (SEIs) among university students at a private university in Amman, Jordan – a context with high unemployment and national digital agendas. Design/methodology/approach A sequential exploratory mixed-methods design was employed. Phase 1 involved semi-structured interviews with seven entrepreneurship faculty and an incubator director at a private university in Amman. Phase 2 comprised a survey of 150 students from the same institution. The technology acceptance model (TAM) and social cognitive theory (SCT) were integrated in a mediated model tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings DSE was positively associated with perceived usefulness (PU) (β = 0.570, p < 0.001) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) (β = 0.584, p < 0.001) of AI tools. AI adoption intention (AIAI) mediated the relationship between DSE and SEI. The total indirect effect of DSE on SEI through both serial mediation paths was 0.247 (p < 0.001). The specific serial indirect effects were 0.078 (DSE → PU → AIAI → SEI, p = 0.012) and 0.093 (DSE → PEOU → AIAI → SEI, p = 0.006). The model accounted for 42.8% and 25.3% of the variance in AIAI and SEI, respectively. These findings are limited to university students at …

title: Optimizing the Role of Internal Audit Through Effective Communication with Risk Management at PT Pegadaian (Persero)
abstract: This study examined the optimization of the Internal Audit Function (Satuan Pengawasan Intern, SPI), operating as the third line, through effective communication with the Risk Management Function, operating as the second line, at PT Pegadaian (Persero). The study was grounded in the Three Lines Model developed by The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA), alongside Financial Services Authority Regulations (Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, POJK) No. 42 of 2024 concerning the Implementation of Risk Management for Financing Institutions, Venture Capital Companies, Microfinance Institutions, and Other Financial Services Institutions, and POJK No. 48 of 2024 concerning Good Governance for these institutions. Using a descriptive qualitative approach with a case study design, the research identified communication gaps that prevented internal audit findings from being systematically integrated with the organizational risk profile maintained by the second line. The findings revealed that coordination and communication between the two functions remained suboptimal. The Risk Management Function had not established a comprehensive risk register to support risk-based internal auditing, while SPI had identified 1,491 chart of accounts (CoA)-related conditions and 72 CoA-related causes that were not systematically consolidated into reports for the Board of Directors and senior management. The…

title: MANAJEMEN PEMBINAAN KEAGAMAAN DI UPT SMAN 1 BULUKUMBA MANAGEMENT OF RELIGIOUS DEVELOPMENT AT UPT SMAN 1 BULUKUMBA
abstract: Religious development in schools represents a strategic effort to cultivate student character grounded in noble morality and religious values. However, its practical implementation faces notable challenges, such as limited competent internal human resources and suboptimal motivation among educators, parents, and students. This study aims to analyze the management of religious development at UPT SMAN 1 Bulukumba examined through planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling (POAC) dimensions. A descriptive qualitative method utilizing phenomenological, psychological, and sociological approaches was conducted through in-depth interviews, participant observations, and documentation involving eight key informants. The findings reveal that UPT SMAN 1 Bulukumba administers eight structured religious development programs coordinated by Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teachers and external mentors. Planning is carried out through collaborative deliberation and program execution runs consistently, yet organizing lacks formal appointment decrees and parental monitoring at home remains limited. This study recommends sustaining the TAJDID program (Qur'anic Memorization, Congregational Zuhur Prayer, and Habituation of Dhuha Prayer), which has been officially endorsed by the principal to foster students' religious character. title: Stakeholder-Oriented Ecotourism Management and Marketing: A Sustainability Performance Evaluation of Chengyang Eight Villages in Guangxi, China
abstract: As ecotourism destinations face increasing market competition and growing sustainability pressures, destination managers must balance stakeholder interests while converting ecological, sociocultural, and economic resources into sustainable market value. Drawing on stakeholder theory, strategic management, and destination marketing perspectives, this study develops a stakeholder-oriented sustainability performance evaluation framework for ecotourism management. Fourteen indicators across economic, sociocultural, and environmental dimensions are constructed through a literature review and evaluated from the perspective of indigenous residents as core stakeholders. Using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Likert-scale survey data, and Chengyang Eight Villages in Guangxi, China as the empirical setting, the study assesses the relative managerial priorities of sustainable ecotourism development. The reported dimension weights assign the highest priority to economic sustainability, followed by sociocultural sustainability, whereas environmental sustainability receives the lowest relative weight. Discrepancies between the displayed matrices and indicator weights require reconciliation before the indicator rankings can be treated as definitive. The reported weighting structure highlights differences in the relative emphasis assigned to livelihood, cultural, and environmental conside…

title: VLT/X-Shooter spectroscopic characterisation of the Didymos system, target of the ESA Hera mission
abstract: The Didymos--Dimorphos system was the target of the NASA Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission and is also the destination of the ESA Hera spacecraft. Ground-based spectroscopy provides an insight into its overall surface composition pre- and post-impact. We aim to characterise the Didymos system by analysing ultraviolet (down to 0.32 ) to near-infrared (up to 2.40 ) m m ground-based reflectance spectra obtained before and after the DART impact, expanding the pool of available Earth-based observations of the asteroid. We present the spectra of the Didymos system over four consecutive nights (September 26--29, 2022) acquired by the X-Shooter instrument of the Very Large Telescope. We taxonomically classified the spectra and analysed their main spectral features, evaluating the characteristic band parameters of the 1 and 2 broad absorption bands, as well as the spectral slopes. m We infer the following spectral properties: an average Band I centre at 0.944 , a Band II centre at 1.995 , and a band area ratio of 0.94 , we find that the surface exhibits a degree of space weathering comparable to that of main-belt asteroids. Furthermore, a meteorite-based ordinary chondrite classification method that isolates absorption band profiles from continuum reddening favours an H-chondrite affinity for the Didymos system. Post-impact spectra show no fundamental change in mineralogy.…

title: Correction to Algorithm 2 in “The Mason-Alberta Phonetic Segmenter: a forced alignment system based on deep neural networks and interpolation”
Mechanical design and experimental performance analysis of a hybrid single-axis photovoltaic tracking system under tropical climate conditions in Nigeria
abstract: Purpose The aim of this research is to determine if fixed-tilt photovoltaic (PV) systems have lower energy harvesting efficiency in tropical climates due to changing solar irradiation, cloud cover, and high operating temperatures. However, many modern tracking systems rely on complicated and expensive control design, which limits their use in underdeveloped countries. The aim of this research is to design, fabricate, and test a low-cost hybrid single-axis PV tracking system that combines light-dependent resistor (LDR)-based active tracking with real-time clock (RTC)-based astronomical control to improve PV energy harvesting in tropical environments. Design/methodology/approach A mechanically robust single-axis tracking system was designed and fabricated using locally available materials. The system utilizes a hybrid tracking method consisting of LDR active tracking and time-controlled astronomical calculation with an RTC. A fabricated mild-steel single-axis tracking structure and an ESP32 microcontroller were installed to enable real-time tracking and recording of PV system parameters PV voltages, PV currents and temperature) with battery status notification through an Internet of Things (IoT) system monitoring. A passive temperature regulation system was used to regulate high PV array temperature resistance within a tropical environment, which remains a key factor in improving…

title: From conflict to climate: dissecting external shocks to Islamic banking stability
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how foreign geopolitical risk (FGPR) and climate risk (CR) shape the stability of Islamic banks. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 56 publicly listed Islamic banks across 16 countries from 2010 to 2024, the authors assess bank stability through the Z-score and non-performing financing ratio. The authors estimate using fixed effects, generalized least squares and two-step system generalized method of moments models and conduct several robustness checks to address endogeneity and sample consistency. Findings FGPR from export partners significantly weakens Islamic bank stability and increases credit risk, whereas import-based risks show more mixed effects. The effects of CR on Islamic bank stability are heterogeneous across climate indicators and stability measures. Practical implications The findings suggest that Islamic banks and regulators should pay greater attention to cross-border geopolitical exposure, particularly export-market exposure, when assessing banking vulnerabilities. Given the heterogeneous climate-risk results, the study does not provide sufficient evidence for specific climate stress-testing requirements. Continued monitoring of external risks may support early identification of vulnerabilities, while specific hedging, diversification and early-warning measures require further empirical investigation. title: From Needs Assessment to Instructional Design: Empirical Requirements for a DIF-PBL Model in Inclusive Numeracy Learning
abstract: Inclusive elementary classrooms require instructional approaches that accommodate substantial variation in students’ numeracy readiness, learning characteristics, and support needs. This study examined teachers’ instructional needs and preliminary learner differences as an empirical basis for designing a Differentiation-Based Problem-Based Learning (DIF-PBL) model for inclusive numeracy learning. The study was conducted as a descriptive needs assessment within a broader research and development project. Participants included 20 classroom teachers and special education support teachers from three inclusive elementary schools in Bone Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Data were collected using a 13-item four-point Likert questionnaire and structured observations of three students representing different learner profiles. Questionnaire data were analyzed using item-level means, standard deviations, and response frequencies, while student observations were treated as illustrative contextual cases. Teachers reported substantial instructional challenges, including disparities in numeracy achievement, difficulty balancing instructional support, limitations in conventional Problem-Based Learning, and practical difficulties in implementing differentiated instruction. The strongest responses concerned the need for an integrated PBL and differentiation model (M = 3.95, SD = 0.22), an oper…

title: Data-driven well-resolved aggregate-capacity screening for brackish-blending management in Kuwait under pumping and total-dissolved-solids constraints
abstract: Brackish groundwater is a strategic supply buffer for arid states reliant on energy-intensive seawater desalination, yet the operational condition of legacy well fields and the distribution-side limits on dispatchable volume remain understudied. Both are addressed here for Kuwait, where desalination supplies ∼ 92% of municipal water. A ministry-level record of 393 wells across five production fields was assembled, and a well-resolved screening linear program was formulated to maximize brackish blending subject to the 1,000-ppm upper total-dissolved-solids (TDS) limit of the applicable Gulf drinking-water standard and an aggregate pumping bound. The model resolves individual wells but represents the distribution side as a single aggregate capacity scalar; it is a screening model, not a hydraulic network model, and its optimum is an upper bound on what a station-resolved network could deliver. Current operations support 62.24MIGD of blending; all rehabilitation scenarios saturate the pumping bound at 90.70MIGD, a 1.46 × (45.7%) uplift. The binding constraint is, therefore, distribution-side aggregate capacity, not upstream well availability. This finding is robust: a zone-partitioned re-solve yields 87.8 MIGD–90.70MIGD, and crediting the standby reserve shifts the binding constraint to the TDS limit; well availability never binds. Constraining dispatch to the nine documented pump…

title: Complete remission with single agent lorlatinib in children with ALK+ anaplastic large cell lymphoma and central nervous system involvement: a case report
abstract: Therapies targeting cancer-specific mutations can result in remarkable clinical responses while reducing adverse effects. We describe the use of lorlatinib, a potent oral inhibitor of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) that crosses the blood brain barrier (BBB), in a case report of two patients with refractory and relapsed ALK+ anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALK+ ALCL) with central nervous system (CNS) involvement. In both cases, treatment with single agent lorlatinib led to rapid and durable complete remission with tolerable side effects. Furthermore, we also describe a novel application of next generation sequencing to characterize circulating immune receptor DNA sequences associated with ALCL, and tracked the molecular response to therapy with subsequent blood specimens. These cases demonstrate that utilization of an effective targeted therapy against cancer-specific driver mutations that penetrates the BBB can lead to a significant clinical response, and presents clonal tracking for molecular response assessment as a potential approach for further study.

title: Cost-effectiveness of disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab versus chemotherapy alone as first-line treatment for HER2-overexpressing advanced urothelial carcinoma: a cost-effectiveness analysis from the Chinese healthcare system perspective
abstract: Background The antibody-drug conjugate disitamab vedotin (DV) in combination with the programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor toripalimab has demonstrated favorable efficacy and a manageable safety profile in patients with HER2-expressing advanced urothelial carcinoma (AUC), as evidenced by the pivotal RC48–016 clinical trial. Nevertheless, the economic viability of this combination strategy relative to conventional chemotherapy remains inadequately characterized. This study sought to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of the aforementioned combination regimen as first-line therapy for HER2-overexpressing AUC patients within the Chinese healthcare system. Methods Leveraging clinical data derived from the RC48–016 trial, a partitioned survival model (PSM) was developed to project long-term survival outcomes and healthcare resource consumption among HER2-overexpressing AUC patients receiving either DV plus toripalimab or chemotherapy alone. Primary outcome measures encompassed total costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER). The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was established at twice China’s 2024 per capita gross domestic product (GDP), amounting to $26,889.37 per QALY. Sensitivity analyses were undertaken to ascertain the robustness of the model findings. Results The chemotherapy-alone arm incurred total costs of $80,97…

Numerical Analysis of Five-Layer Ti–6Al–4V to Inconel 825 Functionally Graded Plate Using Power-Law Distribution, Voigt Homogenization, and Finite Element Method
abstract: This​‍​‌‍​‍‌​‍​‌‍​‍‌ study uses numerical simulations to explore the mechanical behavior of a five-layer functionally graded plate. The setup features a unidirectional gradation that starts with Ti–6Al–4V on the top surface and gradually changes to Inconel 825 at the bottom. The purpose of this gradation is to allow a smooth transition between the two superalloys and thus reduce the number of abrupt material discontinuities. The study focuses on how the volume fraction in each layer affects the structure's mechanical response. The researchers use a layer-based modeling approach to conduct their investigation. In this method, the researchers adjust the metal proportions stepwise to alter the plate's composition. This gradual change results in continuous variation in key mechanical properties, such as stiffness, elastic modulus, and strength. A power-law function with a given power index represents the compositional gradation. The Voigt homogenization model is used to calculate the effective layer properties. After that, finite element analysis (FEA) is used to determine the plate’s behavior under static, modal, and buckling conditions. According to the simulations, functionally graded layering effectively relieves stress concentrations, thereby increasing structural durability. Optimized material distribution improves load-carrying capacity and resistance to mechanical failure. …

title: Evaluating the Interaction of Alzheimer Biomarker Burden and α-Synuclein Status on Cognitive Trajectories in Parkinson Disease: Methodological Challenges and Power Estimates
abstract: Background: Alzheimer disease (AD) and α-synuclein copathology frequently co-occur in Parkinson disease (PD), but whether their interaction accelerates longitudinal cognitive decline is unknown. Objective: To investigate whether the cross-sectional interaction between AD biomarker burden (CSF pTau181/Aβ42 ratio) and α-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) status translates to accelerated cognitive decline, and to estimate sample sizes for future co-pathology studies. Methods: We studied 246 dementia-free PD participants from the Parkinson Precision Medicine Initiative, including genetically enriched subgroups, across seven cognitive domains over 12.9 years. Longitudinal trajectories were modeled using inverse probability of continuation weighted generalized estimating equations with Firth penalization, confirmed by linear mixed-effects and Bayesian joint models. Results: A cross-sectional AD×SAA visuospatial synergy was replicated ( P =0.022), but no longitudinal interaction survived false discovery rate correction (all q ≥0.180). However, a nominally significant AD×SAA interaction on verbal memory was detected by subject-specific models ( P =0.018 to 0.026). Power simulations indicated that 400 to 600 participants under enriched designs, or over 1000 under naturalistic conditions, are required for 80% power. Conclusions: Cross-sectional biomarker synergies may not predict a…

title: Managing Informal Economic Activities at Sentani International Airport: An Organizational Safety Risk Management Perspective
abstract: Airport landside areas are open public spaces where passenger access, commercial services, and community activities overlap, yet little is known about how airports manage the operational risks that arise from informal economic activities there. This study examines how Sentani International Airport manages community-related operational risks associated with such activities from an organizational safety risk management perspective. A qualitative case study was conducted between January and March 2026. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with five airport personnel representing operations, safety management, aviation security, commercial management, and airport security management, and were analyzed thematically. The findings show that managing informal economic activities involved more than enforcement. Five interconnected organizational processes were identified: organizational risk recognition, risk-informed decision-making, cross-functional organizational capability, continuous operational monitoring, and safety promotion and organizational learning. Communication, local knowledge, coordination with external agencies, and continued supervision after intervention were central to these processes. Community-related operational risks in landside areas can therefore be managed as part of a continuous Airport Safety Risk Management process in which coordination an…

title: Corporate reputation in India: unveiling the role of board dimensions
abstract: Purpose The primary motive of this research is to quantify corporate reputation by developing a reputation index along with investigating the influence of governance mechanisms, specifically board characteristics, on the reputation of Indian firms. Design/methodology/approach Reputation of 249 manufacturing firms listed in the National Stock Exchange (NSE) 500 index has been analysed over the period 2015–2024 using a reputation index, and to further investigate its association with board dynamics, panel data analysis has been employed. Findings Results reveal that board dimensions at firms in India have a huge contribution in impacting their reputation. Specifically, larger boards negatively affect corporate reputation, adding credence to agency theory, while board independence enhances it. Research limitations/implications This study enriches the corporate governance literature by empirically linking board attributes with corporate reputation in the Indian context. Practical implications The findings suggest that firms should prioritise the appointment of independent directors while maintaining optimal board size to improve their reputational standing. Furthermore, the reputation index developed in this study offers investors an additional tool to evaluate potential investments by providing firms' reputation scores. Social implications The article contains valuable insights fo…

title: Iterative Development and Functional Verification of GREENESA, a Sensor-based Smart Microgreen Cultivation System with IoT Monitoring and PLC–HMI Migration
abstract: Background Microgreen production in compact controlled environments requires timely irrigation and lighting, but many small-scale systems still rely on manual observation. This study developed GREENESA, a portable cultivation prototype integrating environmental sensing, local and remote monitoring, and manual and threshold-based actuator control, while documenting its migration from an ESP32–Blynk prototype to a more robust PLC–HMI architecture. Methods An iterative engineering design was applied. The initial prototype integrated an ESP32 controller, DHT11 temperature–humidity sensor, BH1750 illuminance sensor, analogue substrate-moisture sensor, 20 × 4 LCD, 4 × 4 keypad, relay module, two cultivation lamps, a 12-VDC pump, and Blynk connectivity. Functional verification assessed I2C communication, keypad response, moisture-sensor calibration in dry, moist, and wet media, local display, automatic and manual control, and remote monitoring. The redesign introduced an aluminium-profile frame, separated 24-, 12-, and 5-VDC power rails, PLC control, an eight-page HMI, and support for rockwool, cocopeat, and paper media. Evidence was synthesized from design records, test observations, and the project progress report. Results The ESP32 prototype acquired temperature, illuminance, and moisture data; displayed measurements locally; transmitted values to Blynk; and controlled lamps and th…

Drivers of supply chain resilience: the roles of artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, blockchain adoption and radical innovation capabilities
abstract: Purpose Global supply chain dynamics have undergone significant changes due to economic uncertainty, logistical disruptions and large-scale crises. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines the relationships among artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, radical innovation capabilities, blockchain adoption and supply chain resilience. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 208 firms operating in Türkiye's foreign trade sector and analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings The results indicate that artificial intelligence facilitates knowledge sharing, which is positively associated with supply chain resilience. While knowledge sharing is significantly related to radical innovation capabilities, radical innovation capabilities do not exhibit a direct association with supply chain resilience. In addition, blockchain adoption strengthens the relationship between knowledge sharing and supply chain resilience, suggesting that blockchain enhances the effectiveness of knowledge-sharing mechanisms in fostering resilience. Originality/value This study contributes to the productivity and performance management literature by integrating digital technologies and knowledge-based capabilities within a unified framework to explain supply chain resilience from a dynamic capabilities perspective. The findings also prov…

title: A 3D robotic inspection framework for power quality monitoring in subterranean high-voltage transmission systems
abstract: The operation of underground power transmission systems is based on continuous monitoring to ensure reliable power transmission, maintain power quality, and avoid unexpected failures. However, most of the existing robotic inspection systems are mainly based on navigation and visual inspection, which have limited ability to integrate power quality monitoring and intelligent fault analysis. To overcome these drawbacks, this work proposes an intelligent robotic inspection framework that combines autonomous robotic monitoring, multimodal sensing, optimized deep learning and adaptive hyper-parameter optimization for power quality disturbance detection. The proposed framework uses a 101-layer Squeeze-and-Excitation Residual Network (SE-ResNet-101x) to classify pre-processed one-dimensional voltage signals into normal and fault classes and hyperparameters are optimized through the Self-Adaptive Sea Lion Optimization (SA-SLnO) algorithm. A set of data is generated based on simulation to mimic an actual underground inspection scenario, including the electrical, environmental, and robotic operational factors. The LiDAR data is used in isolation to provide three-dimensional localization for the robot, while the thermal and camera data provide additional inspection data. Experimental results show that fault detection performance is very good, with 99.10% accuracy, 99.97% precision, 98.94% …

title: Proton beam therapy in the treatment of adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck: a single enterprise retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background and aims Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare salivary gland malignancy with high propensity for perineural invasion (PNI) and relative radioresistance. Proton beam therapy (PBT) may improve tumor control through improved target coverage, as well as higher physical and biologic dose while limiting dose to surrounding critical structures. This single-enterprise two-site study reports outcomes and toxicity in patients with ACC of the head and neck (HN) region treated with curative-intent PBT. Methods From 2015–2025, 89 patients with HN ACC were treated with curative-intent PBT. Patients with distant metastases or prior radiotherapy (RT) were excluded. Clinical outcomes were assessed retrospectively. Toxicities were recorded prospectively using CTCAE v5.0. The Kaplan–Meier method was used to estimate local tumor control (LC), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) and overall survival (OS). Hazard ratios, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and test of association between tumor and treatment variables and outcomes were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Results Median follow-up was 3.1 years. Sixty-nine patients underwent surgery followed by postoperative PBT, while 20 received definitive PBT for unresectable disease. The 3-year LC rate was 98.3% following postoperative PBT and 82.6% following definitive PBT. Treatment approach was not signif…

title: Fair Walk-Forward Forecasting of ICE Robusta Futures: Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, Deep-Learning, and Hybrid Models
abstract: Distribution shifts can degrade nonlinear forecasting models trained on historical price levels, particularly relative to models that retain the most recently observed level. This study empirically compares 14 statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA)–recurrent hybrid specifications for the daily ICE Futures Europe Robusta Coffee benchmark, rather than proposing a new forecasting algorithm. The synchronized dataset comprises 4,603 observations from 14 January 2008 to 28 January 2026. Specifications are selected using a chronological pure-training/validation split and evaluated once on a 300-observation blind test set under a common one-step-ahead walk-forward protocol. The blind-test price distribution shifts sharply from gross training (Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic 0.955; standardized Wasserstein distance 4.274). Delta-Random Forest achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) at 83.59 USD per metric ton, whereas Khashei–Bijari ARIMA–Long Short‐Term Memory (LSTM) yields the lowest root mean squared error at 111.99. However, Delta-Random Forest improves MAE over Naive by only 0.27 USD per metric ton, and no selected pairwise comparison remains significant after Holm adjustment of the Diebold–Mariano tests. Grouped permutation importance shows that permuting lagged first-difference history increases Delta-Random-Forest MA…

title: Epidemiological patterns and surveillance-based forecasting of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome in Jiangsu Province, China, 2015–2025
abstract: Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne infectious disease with marked seasonality and geographic heterogeneity. Long-term public health surveillance and independently validated forecasting may help translate routine case reporting into targeted prevention and preparedness. Methods We analysed clinically diagnosed and laboratory-confirmed SFTS cases reported in Jiangsu Province, China, from January 2015 to December 2025. Demographic, occupational, temporal, and county/district-level spatial patterns were described, and local spatial autocorrelation was assessed. Monthly case counts from 2015 to 2023 were used for model development, while 2024–2025 data were reserved for independent temporal testing. Seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), random forest (RF), long short-term memory (LSTM), and weighted ensemble (WE) models were compared using root mean squared error (RMSE), mean squared error (MSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). Results Among 1,660 reported cases, 1,508 (90.8%) occurred in persons aged ≥50 years and 1,042 (62.8%) among farmers. Annual cases increased from 30 in 2015 to 428 in 2024 and 345 in 2025. Overall, 97.6% of cases occurred from April to October, and high-burden areas and high-high spatial clusters were concentrated in southwestern Jiangsu. In the independent testing period, ARIMA achieved…

title: From data-driven differential equations to mechanistic forecasting with machine learning
abstract: Abstract The equations of complex dynamical systems may not be identified by expert knowledge, especially if the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Data-driven discovery methods address this challenge by inferring governing equations from time-series data using a library of functions constructed from the measured variables. However, these methods typically assume time-invariant coefficients, which limits their ability to capture evolving system dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we allow some of the parameters to vary over time, learn their temporal evolution directly from data and infer a system of equations that incorporates both constant and time-varying parameters. We then transform this framework into a forecasting model by predicting the time-varying parameters and substituting these predictions into the learned equations. The model is validated on simulated susceptible–infected–recovered and consumer–resource systems, as well as on real-world greenhouse gas concentration and cyanobacteria cell count datasets. By dynamically adapting to temporal shifts, our proposed model achieved a mean absolute error below 3% for learning a time series and below 6% for forecasting up to a month ahead. We additionally compare forecasting performance against convolutional neural network–long short-term memory and gradient boosting machine, and show that our model outperforms these met…

title: Computational text indicators of epistemic norms in higher education: auditable cross-validated prediction against a weak observed household-resource baseline
abstract: Purpose This study tests whether computational text indicators of epistemic norms add out-of-sample predictive value for normalized academic results beyond a weak baseline of directly observed household/resource indicators. Design/methodology/approach Data comprise 263 students observed in two waves across five sites. Prediction uses 263 follow-up records. The baseline contains seven observed indicators. Archived epistemic counts were generated through pre-assigned mappings for closed items and LDA/topic-model-assisted processing for open responses. A deterministic 10-fold split (seed 60126) evaluated raw counts, within-fold PCA, and fixed outcome-independent ENA coordinates using pooled OOF R2, RMSE and MAE. Findings No epistemic specification reliably improved the baseline. Pooled OOF R2 was −0.009 (M0), −0.065 (M1), −0.032 (M1-PCA) and −0.008 (M2). M1 significantly worsened MAE after Holm correction; H1 and H2 were not supported. Research limitations/implications The baseline is weak, no prior-achievement variable is available, corpus-level reliability of automated epistemic variables is unknown, ENA coordinates were fixed before resampling, and program representation is imbalanced. Practical implications The indicators should not be used for high-stakes decisions without prospective measurement, subgroup-fairness and instructional-utility validation. Originality/value The s…

title: Prediction of Mode I fracture toughness of porous rocks using rheological dynamics
abstract: Purpose The aim of this paper was to define the Mode I fracture toughness of porous dry rocks based on the rheological-dynamic theory (RDT). The topic is potentially relevant in the context of constitutive modeling and damage mechanics. Design/methodology/approach The fracture toughness is defined within the fracture process zone (FZZ) as a function of the void volume fraction (VVF), which represents existing pores and newly formed voids due to loading. The problem is formulated on a standard cylindrical specimen with a ring-shaped crack under unconfined compressive strength (UCS). Due to the differently defined cohesions in the RDT and Mohr-Coulomb (MC) material, a lateral principal stress appears in the cylinder. The conventional Griffith criterion is improved by introducing this lateral principal stress. Findings The improved Griffith criterion is consistent with the RDT at zero porosity when the rock is treated as elastic. However, differences occur within the inelastic FPZ. The fracture toughness within the FPZ is a function of: VVF, UCS, damage variables, porosity thresholds, creep coefficients, dynamic Poisson's ratio, elastic modulus ratios, cylinder diameter and geometric factor. Originality/value This study uses Zhang's empirical equation to confirm the accuracy of the results obtained by RDT. Evidence for the obtained Mode I fracture toughness is related to the FPZ. …

title: A Critical Analysis of Sociology Teachers' Pedagogical Practices Through Performance Test Documents of the 2025 In-Service Teacher Professional Education Program
abstract: This study aims to (1) describe the completeness and alignment of lesson planning in the teaching modules of Sociology teachers who took the 2025 In-Service Teacher UKIN with the indications of learning practice they contain, viewed through the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, and (2) critically analyze teacher performance in the UKIN through the critical pedagogy perspectives of Paulo Freire and Henry Giroux and Stephen Ball's theory of performativity. The study used a qualitative approach, applying Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis to a purposive sample of 190 Sociology teaching-module documents from UKIN participants at one teacher-education institution (LPTK). The results show that the administrative-format completeness of the teaching modules is generally good, while the substantive depth of teachers' pedagogical competence remains variable. Lesson planning tends to target low-to-moderate cognitive levels, with lower-order thinking categories dominating most modules; assessment items misalign with Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS)-oriented learning objectives in most documents; and PowerPoint remains the dominant, often the only, technology used across most modules. Viewed through the critical lenses of Freire's banking education, Giroux's transformative intellectuals, and Ball's performativity theory, these findings suggest that the UKIN…

title: An exploratory Kano survey of community sports service demands among participating older adults in six selected Wuhan communities
abstract: Background Community sports facilities and related services may shape opportunities for physical activity, but an overall satisfaction score can obscure asymmetric responses to service provision and non-provision. This study described service demands among older adults participating in community sports in six selected Wuhan communities. Methods An exploratory cross-sectional survey with non-probability recruitment yielded 1,065 valid questionnaires, of which 825 current community-sports participants were included in the Kano analysis. Twenty-eight services across six domains were classified by the largest A/O/M/I frequency. Better (SI), Worse (DSI), and their descriptive asymmetry contrast were recalculated from item counts. Sample-specific mean coefficients defined the quadrant reference lines. A deterministic response-recoding analysis examined the sensitivity of dominant categories. Results Eight services were must-be, eight one-dimensional, seven attractive, and five indifferent. Maintenance had the largest |DSI| (0.788), and professional guidance the largest SI (0.700). The contrast SI − |DSI| was negative for maintenance (−0.326) and safety (−0.279), but positive for free facilities (0.290) and age-friendly modification (0.260). For intercommunity exchange, reallocating four of 807 nonreverse responses from the leading category to the second category removed its unique do…

title: The Effect of Product Information Quality, Last-Mile Service Quality, and Shipment Trackability on The Decision Not to Return Furniture in E-Commerce Purchases Through Customer Trust
abstract: The growth of e-commerce has made furniture purchasing more convenient for customers; however, it has also introduced risks associated with discrepancies in product information, shipping damage, unclear delivery status, and product returns. This study aims to examine the effects of Product Information Quality, Last-Mile Service Quality, and Shipment Trackability on the Decision Not to Return Furniture, both directly and indirectly through Customer Trust as a mediating variable. The study employed a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. Primary data were collected through a questionnaire comprising 46 indicators administered to 301 customers who had purchased furniture through e-commerce platforms within the preceding 12 months. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS software. The results indicate that Last-Mile Service Quality and Shipment Trackability have significant effects on Customer Trust, whereas Product Information Quality does not. Product Information Quality, Shipment Trackability, and Customer Trust significantly influence the Decision Not to Return Furniture, while Last-Mile Service Quality has no significant direct effect. Furthermore, Customer Trust mediates the relationships between Last-Mile Service Quality and the Decision Not …

title: Spatial patterns and driving mechanisms of urban carbon sequestration service flows in China
abstract: Global climate governance increasingly relies on understanding the spatial mismatch between carbon emissions and ecosystem carbon sequestration capacity. As a critical regulating ecosystem service, carbon sequestration service flows exert substantial interregional spillover effects through spatial ecological interactions. However, existing research has largely focused on static supply–demand evaluations at regional scales, while the spatial flow processes and driving mechanisms of carbon sequestration service flows across cities remain insufficiently explored. This study quantified the supply, demand, and flows of carbon sequestration service flows across 333 prefecture-level administrative units in China from 2010 to 2024 using breakpoint–field strength models and spatial flow analysis. Furthermore, the XGBoost-SHAP model was adopted to detect the nonlinear driving mechanisms behind carbon sequestration service flows. The results showed that China’s carbon sequestration service flows presented a potential west-to-east linkage pattern, indicating a pronounced spatial mismatch between carbon sequestration supply areas and carbon emission demand areas. High-supply regions were predominantly distributed in western and northern China, whereas demand regions were concentrated in eastern coastal urban agglomerations. The total volume of carbon sequestration service flows first rose a…

title: Typologies Of Political Patronage: Expert Evidence From Mongolia's Civil Service
abstract: Political patronage remains a persistent feature of civil service systems worldwide, even where formal recruitment rules are nominally meritocratic. This article examines the typological forms political patronage takes within Mongolia's civil service, addressing a gap in the comparative literature between highly institutionalized European party-government systems, where influential typologies of patronage were originally developed, and post-socialist, semi-presidential contexts, where such typologies remain largely untested. Despite two decades of civil service reform explicitly modeled on career-based meritocratic systems, official Civil Service Council statistics document a rise in unlawful personnel rotation from 5.2 percent of civil servants in 2007 to over 22 percent in 2019, indicating a persistent divergence between formal rule and administrative practice. Drawing on a two-stage expert survey and interview design involving 55 experts from academia, the civil service, and political practice, this study tests the applicability of the influential typology developed by Kopecký, Mair, and Spirova (2012)—distinguishing party-apparatus-based, technocratic, agency-based, and party-membership-based patronage—to the Mongolian case. Findings indicate that all four typological categories are unanimously or near-unanimously recognized by experts as operative, evidencing pronounced ty…

title: Before regulation: structural lock-out of mass timber in Pakistan's built environment
abstract: Purpose Existing studies explain mass timber nonadoption through regulatory; insurance and liability mechanisms derived from Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) markets. This article asks what happens when those gatekeeping institutions are weak or absent, yet low-carbon materials still fail to enter the market. It develops and empirically applies a mechanism-based diagnostic framework distinguishing formal regulatory lock-in from informal structural lock-out, using Pakistan as a critical case. Design/methodology/approach Phase One consolidated a process model of lock-in through a critical interpretive synthesis (CIS) of 22 OECD mass timber studies drawn from a 95-study scoping corpus (literature searched January 2015 to January 2026). Phase Two tested and extended it through a qualitative Pakistan case study. Data comprised 32 semi-structured expert interviews with architects, structural engineers, developers and building regulators in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad (September 2025 to February 2026), triangulated with policy documents, tariff schedules, trade statistics, procurement records and marketing materials. Inter-coder reliability: Krippendorf’s a = 0.81. Findings The three OECD mechanisms (risk categorization inertia, epistemic closure and liability lock-in) are absent or latent in Pakistan. Yet no market presence was identified; official reco…

title: Developing Students’ Self-Regulation through Active Participation in the Sang Pendakwah Community (KSP) at SMPN 48 Surabaya
abstract: This study examines how students’ active participation in the Sang Pendakwah Community (KSP) contributes to the development of self-regulation in a public school. This research employed a qualitative approach with a case study design at SMPN 48 Surabaya. Data were collected through non-participant observations, semi-structured interviews, and documentation. Ten informants were purposively selected, consisting of one community advisor, two student administrators, and seven KSP members or participants from Grades VIII and IX. Data credibility was strengthened through technique triangulation, while analysis involved data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that students’ participation in KSP provides opportunities to practice five aspects of self-regulation: discipline, responsibility, independence, self-control, and self-confidence. This process occurs through preparation and planning, fulfillment of responsibilities and peer interaction, and evaluation with feedback. These processes correspond to Zimmerman’s three phases of self-regulation: forethought, performance, and self-reflection. The novelty of this study lies in examining a student-led religious community as a space for developing self-regulation beyond formal classroom learning. Therefore, providing meaningful responsibilities and opportunities for active participat…

title: Regulation of endogenous dsRNA: strategies for self-tolerance
abstract: Abstract Cells must continuously distinguish cellular-derived RNA from pathogenic RNA to mount effective antiviral responses while avoiding harmful autoinflammation. Cytoplasmic RNA-sensing receptors, including RIG-I-like receptors, PKR, OAS-RNase L and ZBP1, detect RNA primarily through molecular features such as structure (double- versus single-stranded), modification state and subcellular localization rather than sequence. While these are characteristics of viral nucleic acids, mammalian genomes generate abundant self-derived double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), including from transposable elements, antisense transcription and RNA processing intermediates, which exist in the cytoplasm. This review describes our current understanding of how cells achieve self-tolerance through the active regulation of endogenous RNA. These mechanisms comprise epigenetic silencing of repetitive elements, RNA modifications (such as A-to-I editing and m6A), precise splicing, regulated nuclear export and decay, circRNA buffering, protein shielding and dedicated RNA degradation pathways. Insights from rare inherited monogenic interferonopathies and murine models illustrate how perturbations in these pathways lead to inappropriate activation of cytoplasmic RNA sensors and inflammatory disease when cellular dsRNA is mistakenly recognized as non-self. We highlight how dysregulated dsRNA homeostasis contribut…

title: The two-component system CrdRS mediates sub-inhibitory antibiotic-induced biofilm formation in Helicobacter pylori via bidirectional regulation of transporters PlpA and GlnP
abstract: ABSTRACT Biofilm formation by Helicobacter pylori is a major driver of antibiotic tolerance and treatment failure, yet the signaling pathways that trigger biofilm development under sub-inhibitory antibiotic pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we show that sub-MIC levels of metronidazole, amoxicillin, and ciprofloxacin potently induce dense H. pylori biofilms. Through transcriptomic and genetic analyses, we identify the two-component system CrdRS as a central signaling hub that orchestrates this response via the bidirectional regulation of two ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. Phosphorylated CrdR binds to AC-rich promoter motifs to directly activate plpA , which encodes a substrate-binding protein that drives exopolysaccharide secretion and matrix assembly. Concomitantly, CrdR represses glnP , which encodes an inner-membrane permease, thereby relieving transcriptional inhibition of the L-asparaginase gene ansB . This derepression triggers aberrant reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which promotes oxidative stress-dependent biofilm maturation. Through phenotypic analysis of c rdRS deletion mutants, phosphorylation-defective point mutants (CrdR D53A and CrdS H173A ), and exogenous hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) induction, we demonstrate that CrdRS is required for mediating antibiotic-induced stress responses in a manner genetically separable from ROS sensing. Collec…

title: Frequency of Diabetes Mellitus andHypertension among Physicians Working inSelected Medical Colleges inChattogram, Bangladesh
abstract: Background: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) and Hypertension (HTN) are important occupational-health concerns among physicians, whose work may involve prolonged sitting, irregular schedules, psychological stress, and limited opportunity for preventive care. This study assessed the frequency of DM and HTN and their associated factors among physicians working in selected medical colleges in Bangladesh. Materials and methods: A multicentre cross-sectional study was conducted from June to December 2025 among 284 physicians from seven selected medical colleges. Sociodemographic, professional, clinical, treatment, family-history and behavioural data were collected using a pretested structured questionnaire, with blood pressure, random capillary blood glucose, height, and weight recorded. Separate multivariable logistic regression models identified factors associated with DM and HTN, adjusted odds ratios (AORs) 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) and p values were reported. Results: Among 284 physicians (Mean age 40.18 ± 10.64 years; 54.9% male), 64 (22.5%) had DM and 65 (22.9%) had HTN. Sedentary physical activity was reported by 60.9%, overweight or obesity was present in 58.8% and current or former smoking in 17.6%. For DM, increasing age (AOR per 5 years 1.58, 95% CI 1.34–1.85), smoking (AOR 5.59, 95% CI 2.46–12.70) sedentary activity (AOR 2.69, 95% CI 1.24–5.86) and reported stress (AOR 2.88, …

title: Legal Regulation of Intellectual Property in the Field of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This study aimed to identify differences between contemporary approaches to protecting intellectual outputs created or used with artificial intelligence and to establish criteria connecting rights, obligations, and liability to human contributions at successive stages of the technological process. Conducted in August 2026, the study examined a purposive, non-random sample of 45 legislative, judicial, administrative, and official analytical documents from the World Intellectual Property Organization, the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Ukraine. The documentary cutoff was 27 August 2026. Documents were examined against 13 criteria encompassing input authorization, text and data mining, rights reservations, training transparency, authorship, creative control, output protection, special protection regimes, inventorship, human inventive contribution, liability, trade secrets, and remedies. European Union materials constituted 28.9% of the sample, followed by United States materials at 24.4%, United Kingdom materials at 20.0%, Ukrainian materials at 15.6%, and international institutional materials at 11.1%. The European Union instruments connect distinct mining exceptions with rights reservations and general-purpose model transparency; the United States materials emphasize fair use and case-specific analysis. United Kingdom legislation retains a computer-ge…

title: Beyond single regulation: how does green agriculture comprehensive pilot achieve fertilizer reduction? Evidence from China
abstract: Introduction Compared with single regulation, the Green Agriculture Comprehensive Pilot (GACP) is a comprehensive pilot policy promoted by China to advance agricultural green transformation. However, few questions remain unclear whether and how this policy reduce the fertilizer use. Methods Using panel data of 106 cities from 8 Chinese central and eastern provinces over 20002022, this study adopts difference-in-differences (DID) and causal mediation analysis (CMA) to evaluate GACP’s effect on fertilizer application density, identifying its underlying mechanisms and heterogeneities, and discuss its implications for food security. Results The results show that the GACP effectively reduces fertilizer use, decreasing the average annual fertilizer per unit of sown area in pilot cities by 9.9% (44.046 kg/ hm2). The reduction effect initially strengthens but then gradually weakens over time, but remains effective throughout the observation period, these results remaining robust after a series of tests. Mechanism analysis indicates that the GACP reduces fertilizer use by establishing a green agricultural support system and promoting four internal institutional incentive mechanisms: technological progress, scale operation, professional division, and industrial convergence, with respective contributions of 11.15%, 5.46%, 12.66%, and 8.12%. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the reduction …

title: Hemodialysis patients exhibit T-cell activation accompanied by an enhanced frequency of IFN-γ+CD4+/CD8+ T cells
abstract: T-cell immune dysregulation is common in end-stage renal disease (ESRD), but whether hemodialysis (HD) differentially affects T-cell immune activity remains unclear. We evaluated the peripheral T-cell immune characteristics of 96 patients with ESRD and 86 healthy controls to explore the effects of HD on T-cell immune function. T-cell subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry for phenotype, number, and function (represented by interferon-gamma [IFN-γ] secretion capacity). Compared with healthy controls, patients with ESRD showed significant reductions in the absolute number of CD8 + T-naïve (TN)/T effector memory (TEM)/T effector memory regulatory (TEMRA), CD4 + T-cell memory (TCM), CD4 + CD38 + , CD8 + /CD4 + HLA-DR + , and CD8 + /CD4 + CD28 + cells, especially in the proportion and quantity of CD4 + TN cells. Compared with nHD patients, HD patients showed significantly different peripheral T-cell immune characteristics. Phenotypically, the changes in CD4 + T-cell subsets were more significant than those observed for CD8 + T cells, with activated T cells (CD4 + CD38 + , CD4 + HLA-DR + , and CD8 + CD38 + T cells) increased and functional T cells (CD4 + CD28 + T cells) decreased in proportion and quantity. Functionally, the frequency of IFN-γ + CD4 + /CD8 + T cells was significantly higher in HD patients than in nHD patients, indicating the enhanced functional activation of T cells…

title: Integral sliding-mode current regulation for sequence-impedance shaping and oscillation suppression in virtual synchronous generators
abstract: Cascade-controlled virtual synchronous generators (VSGs), widely adopted in grid-forming battery energy storage systems (BESS), may experience low-frequency instability when connected to stiff grids characterized by relatively high short-circuit ratios (SCRs) and small equivalent grid impedances. A frequency-coupled sequence-impedance model was developed to investigate the instability mechanism. The conventional proportional-integral (PI) current regulator was replaced with an integral sliding-mode controller incorporating an integral sliding surface and a boundary-layer reaching law, while retaining the outer power and voltage control loops. Small-signal impedance analysis, MATLAB/Simulink simulations, and RT-LAB real-time simulation tests were conducted under different SCR conditions. The baseline model identified a capacitive region in the positive-sequence impedance that resulted in insufficient phase margins at converter-grid impedance crossovers. The proposed controller narrowed the capacitive region and yielded positive phase margins in the analyzed cases. Simulations and real-time tests confirmed the suppression of sustained grid-current oscillations. Compared with a fixed virtual-inductance benchmark, the proposed method shortened recovery time and reduced grid-current total harmonic distortion from 3.38% to 0.54% at SCR = 30 (Lg = 1.5 mH). The results indicate that th…

title: LAND CARRYING CAPACITY, WATER SAFETY, AND COMMUNITY HEALTH UNDER POPULATION PRESSURE: A MULTIDISCIPLINARY ASSESSMENT OF HILLSIDE SETTLEMENT IN NEGERI BATU MERAH, AMBON, INDONESIA
abstract: Background Small island cities grow on scarce, steep, and hazard-prone land. Negeri Batu Merah, a customary village in Ambon City, is classified as a heavy slum area with 66,424 people on 911 ha. Its dense settlement relies on septic tanks and shallow wells, linking land limits to water safety, and maternal and child health. This study assesses Batu Merah’s land-carrying capacity, measures how existing settlements are distributed across it, and interprets the results for engineering, water safety, community health, access, and spatial governance. Methods Nine land capability units were analyzed following Minister of Public Works Regulation No. 20/PRT/M/2007 and converted into potential, limitation, and constraint zones. Settlement from the 2018 national land cover map is overlaid on these zones and each unit. Published water quality and health studies on Ambon were compiled, and the results were interpreted from eight disciplines, including chemistry, global health, and midwifery. Results The village had moderately high (56.14%), moderate (42.87%), and low land capability (0.99%). Settlement covers 600.61 ha at about 110 persons per settled hectare. The potential zone was 96.5% built-up, and the constraint zone was almost entirely. All 97.67 ha of settlement in the limitation zone stands on land with low foundation stability, moderate slope stability, and a moderately high haza…

title: Recovery physiology: a testable systems framework for preserving the capacity to function
abstract: Living systems must restore function after perturbation while operating under finite energetic, structural, regulatory, and environmental constraints. This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes Recovery Physiology as a testable framework for studying that problem. Recovery is defined narrowly as the time-dependent response following a prospectively specified perturbation that measurably displaces one or more prespecified functional variables from a relevant reference state. Recovery Capacity (RC) is defined separately as a hypothetical latent, context-dependent property that may influence the magnitude, rate, completeness, coordination, and cost of that response; favorable outcomes are not evidence of high RC by definition. Three candidate domains—bioenergetic capacity, biological information integrity, and systems coordination—are proposed as a parsimonious but revisable architecture. The framework makes three separable claims: recovery phenotypes may contain reliable challenge-specific latent structure and possibly a higher-order cross-challenge factor; the proposed domain architecture may explain recovery beyond simpler alternatives; and dynamic trajectories may add prognostic information beyond baseline state and established constructs. Each claim is paired with competing models and falsification criteria. A standardized exercise protocol illustrates how reliability, const…

title: Processing capacity under complexity: an organizational information processing perspective on humanitarian supply chain performance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the role of processing capacity in shaping humanitarian supply chain performance under crisis conditions. Specifically, it examines how information processing capacity influences response performance and equity performance, and how environmental complexity and structural integration moderate these relationships. It also examines whether environmental complexity moderates the information processing capacity-equity performance relationship more strongly than the information processing capacity-response performance relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT) and a contingency perspective, the research model is proposed and empirically evaluated using survey data collected from 600 professionals with relevant experience working in the humanitarian supply chain across India. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS. Findings The PLS-SEM results show that processing capacity has a significant positive effect on both response performance and equity performance. The environmental complexity amplifies the impact of processing capacity on both outcomes, but results confirm that it has stronger moderating effect for equity performance compared to response performance. Similarly, structural integration also significantly streng…

title: Temperature-accelerated multiscale degradation in manganese-based blended-cathode pouch cells: evolution and origins of capacity loss
abstract: Abstract Understanding how dominant capacity-loss factors evolve under deeper cathode delithiation is critical for improving the capacity utilization and durability of lithium-ion batteries employing Mn-based blended cathodes. Here, 6.2 Ah graphite pouch cells with an NCM/LMFP/LRMO blended cathode were cycled between 3.0 and 4.3 V at 1 C at 25 and 45 ℃ and investigated using electrochemical diagnostics, ultrasonic inspection, and multiscale post-mortem characterization. The 25 ℃ cell retained 87.9% of its initial capacity after 1,200 cycles, whereas the 45 ℃ cell retained only 75.0% after 457 cycles. Electrochemical analysis indicates that capacity fading at 25 ℃ initially exhibits features consistent with reduced electrochemically accessible reaction capacity and LAM-related degradation, followed by increasingly evident LLI-related electrode slippage and ultimately a late-stage regime involving coupled LAM-related degradation, LLI, and impedance growth. At 45 ℃, this evolution is markedly compressed, with these degradation factors becoming strongly coupled within the first several hundred cycles. Multiscale characterization further links the accelerated degradation at elevated temperature to intensified interfacial parasitic reactions, cyclable-lithium and electrolyte consumption, gas generation, anode-material detachment, separator pore blockage, transport deterioration, and …

title: Bioengineered Andrias davidianus Skin Secretion Sponge: A Sustainable Hemostatic Material with Enhanced Wound Healing Capacity
abstract: Abstract The skin secretion of Andrias davidianus (SSAD) is a miraculous natural protein-based product with exceptional potential for treating bleeding wounds and has long been used in traditional folk medicine. However, its commercialization and societal benefits have been hindered by challenges in reproducibly manufacturing products with highly consistent properties and bacteria-free conditions. Here, we introduce a straightforward manufacturing method to produce a practically applicable hemostatic sponge derived from SSAD, which significantly enhances wound healing. To further improve antimicrobial properties, the antibacterial peptide ε-polylysine (EPL) was incorporated, resulting in composite sponges (SSAD-EPLs). The fabricated sponges exhibit excellent biocompatibility and are capable of degrading in vivo over a 21-day observation period. Compared to a commercial gelatin sponge (CGS), both SSAD and SSAD-EPL2 (containing 20% EPL) sponges demonstrated superior hemostatic performance, significantly reducing blood loss and clotting time. In a full-thickness skin defect model, SSAD and SSAD-EPL2 sponges showed remarkable efficacy in promoting wound healing and could be easily removed from the wound site without causing secondary injury. Our findings highlight the practical applicability of these sponges, not only due to their outstanding hemostatic and wound-healing properties…

title: Carbon Sequestration Capacity of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati City, Davao Oriental
abstract: The study was conducted to quantify the biomass and carbon storage of the vegetative cover of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati, Davao Oriental. The specific objectives of this study were to determine the total area of the vegetative cover, to determine the vegetative structures, to identify the status of the vegetation, and to provide recommendations in relation to the management of the watershed. Actual surveying of the area as to the hectarage of various vegetative covers of the area was done with the aid of a Global Positioning System (GPS). The determined hectarage was then used in extrapolating the biomass and carbon sequestration capacity of the vegetative cover of the area. The Geographic Information System software was used to come up with a vegetation map of the area. The watershed area in Brgy. Central covers 879.21 ha., comprising agroforestry farms, Tree Plantation, Secondary-growth Forest, Cogon area, and the human settlement of Purok Malipayon and Sitio Banahaw. Their extent is as follows: Agroforestry farms, occupying the largest area, covers 492.36 ha., secondary-growth forest or thickets covers 195.97 ha., tree plantation covers 178.65 ha., and cogon area with 10.02 ha.
