title: FinTech, transparency, governance and financial inclusion: channels to sustainable development goals in Gulf Cooperation Council banking
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how banking digitalization and FinTech development advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) banks, focusing on transparency, governance and financial inclusion as the channels linking FinTech to sustainability. Design/methodology/approach To explore the relationship between digitalization and SDGs in GCC banks, the authors construct a FinTech Engagement Index (FEI) and a Sustainability Engagement Index (SEI) for 69 GCC banks over 2020–2023. A GLS regression model estimates this relationship, controlling for bank-specific characteristics and macroeconomic conditions. Findings The results of this study reveal a significant positive relationship between FinTech adoption and banking sector sustainability, demonstrating that advanced digitalization enhances transparency, governance and financial inclusion while accelerating progress toward SDGs. Institutional characteristics play a meaningful role in this relationship. These results are valuable for policymakers and regulators aiming to leverage FinTech for sustainable banking development. Practical implications Policymakers should foster FinTech innovation while ensuring risk management and consumer protection. Bank leaders should use FinTech as a strategic sustainability tool, prioritizing digital platforms for green products, automated reporting and envi…

title: Out-of-pocket expenditure for neurosurgical care in Uganda: quantifying financial catastrophe and identifying policy pathways to universal health coverage
abstract: Background Out-of-pocket payments remain the primary source of healthcare financing in many low- and middle-income countries, frequently resulting in catastrophic and impoverishing expenditures. Neurosurgical care is particularly costly due to substantial direct and indirect expenses borne by patients and caregivers, typically with little or no financial protection. This study quantifies these OOP costs, estimates the prevalence of catastrophic and impoverishing health expenditures, and examines their socioeconomic impact to inform equitable surgical financing policies. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study at the two main Ugandan public neurosurgical centers - Mulago National Referral Hospital, Kampala, and Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital, Mbarara. Consecutive patients with confirmed neurosurgical diagnoses were enrolled at discharge or within two weeks post-discharge. Structured surveys captured sociodemographic, clinical and cost data. OOP health payments were direct medical plus direct non-medical payments; total economic burden added indirect costs. Catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) was OOP payments exceeding 10% of annual household consumption expenditure (World Bank) or 40% of it after food costs (WHO). Impoverishment was the change in poverty headcount against the $3.00/person/day line (2021 purchasing power parity). Data was analyzed using R 4.4.2. Ethica…

title: Sharia financial technology organizations and ethical responsibility for sustainable development: a moral economy perspective
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether the ethical responsibility of Sharia financial technology (Sharia fintech) can be normatively justified rather than assumed on the basis of its religious identity or developmental claims. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a normative–conceptual ethical analysis that evaluates Sharia fintech as a morally accountable financial system using two normative benchmarks: the objectives of Sharia (maqasid al-Sharia) and the ethical vision embedded in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Findings The analysis develops a conceptual evaluation framework structured around four ethical tension fields: inclusion versus digital exclusion, social objectives versus profit orientation, technological efficiency versus data ethics and accountability and sustainability commitments versus symbolic alignment. These tensions show that ethical legitimacy in Sharia fintech is neither inherent nor guaranteed by formal compliance, but conditionally achieved through continuous moral negotiation between innovation, market pressures and social responsibility. Research limitations/implications This study is conceptual in nature and does not empirically assess specific fintech platforms or governance practices. Future research may operationalise the proposed framework through qualitative case studies or institutional analysis to examine how Sharia fintec…

title: How financial constraints influence the preferences for tourism destinations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how financial constraints influence preferences for natural (vs cultural) destinations. It further investigates the mediating role of psychological distress and the moderating role of perceived economic mobility in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential multistudy design comprising eight studies (n = 1,874), including three main studies and five supplementary studies, was used to examine the effect of financial constraints on destination preferences and to test the underlying mechanism and boundary condition. Findings Financial constraints shape preferences for natural (vs cultural) destinations through psychological distress. Perceived economic mobility determines the direction of this self-regulatory response: financial constraints increase preferences for natural (vs cultural) destinations when perceived economic mobility is high but increase preferences for cultural (vs natural) destinations when perceived economic mobility is low. Originality/value This research advances the literature on financial conditions and destination decision-making by shifting attention from objective financial conditions to subjective financial perceptions. It identifies psychological distress as the mechanism linking financial constraints to destination preferences and perceived economic mobility as a boundary condition that determines the …

title: Financial stress and mental well-being among older adults: an extended conceptual framework of financial vulnerability, self-efficacy and social support
abstract: Purpose Population ageing has emerged as an important social and economic phenomenon, creating increasing challenges for the financial and psychological well-being of older adults. Although ageing is generally associated with retirement, declining earning capacity and increasing healthcare requirements, the financial consequences of these changes are not experienced uniformly. Existing literature has examined financial stress, healthcare expenditure, financial dependence, social support and mental well-being among older adults independently; however, the theoretical mechanisms explaining why some older adults experience stronger psychological consequences of financial stress than others remain under-theorised. This study aims to propose an integrated framework outlining various factors of financial stress and mental well being of older adults. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper combines Life Course Theory, Hobfoll theory, the Stress Process Model, Social Cognitive Theory and conservation of resources (COR) theory to propose a moderated-mediation model connecting financial vulnerability with financial stress and mental well-being with psychological and protective resources as moderators. Findings The proposed framework incorporates healthcare expenditure, retirement-income insecurity, financial dependence, debt and digital financial challenges as core sources of f…

title: Social support, financial threat, psychological distress, burnout and nursing clinical competence in mental health courses: self-efficacy and professional identity moderators
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the psychosocial factors related to burnout and perceived clinical competence among undergraduate nursing students, with particular attention to perceived social support, psychological distress and financial threat, and whether self-efficacy and professional identity moderated key associations. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 351 third- and fourth-year nursing students at Jerash University, Jordan. Perceived social support, psychological distress, financial threat, self-efficacy, professional identity, burnout and perceived clinical competence were assessed using established self-report measures. Four moderated regression models were estimated, adjusting for age, years of nursing experience, GPA, sleep and internet use. Predictors and moderators were mean-centered, interaction terms were tested and simple slopes were examined. Findings Perceived social support was negatively associated with burnout and positively associated with perceived clinical competence. Psychological distress was positively associated with burnout and negatively associated with clinical competence, while financial threat was positively associated with burnout. Four interaction terms were statistically significant. Financial threat × self-efficacy (B = 0.055, p < 0.001) and financial threat × professional identity (B =…

title: Constructing a Diversified Medical Insurance Financing System from the Perspective of Health Industry Transformation
abstract: Health industry transformation is changing the socioeconomic conditions under which medical insurance systems operate. This study examines the relationship between established financing mechanisms and evolving health service models, including digital health integration, value-based care, and the expansion of preventive and personalized interventions. A systems analysis of institutional design, fiscal sustainability, and stakeholder alignment identifies structural tensions between existing insurance arrangements and emerging health system priorities. On this basis, the study proposes a diversified financing framework that combines innovations in risk pooling, dynamic contribution mechanisms, and cross-sectoral funding instruments to strengthen equity, adaptability, and long-term sustainability. The analysis emphasizes that effective diversification requires changes in governance, accountability, and intertemporal resource allocation, as well as additional funding sources, to support health system transformation.

title: Housing Yields
abstract: Abstract We build a granular data set of residential property yields using rental and sale listings from a major German real estate platform. With more than 1.5 million property-level rent-to-price ratios, we document a novel heterogeneity puzzle. About two-fifths of yield dispersion remains unexplained after controlling for extensive observable property characteristics and postal code-level time-varying factors using fixed effects. When we absorb finer neighborhood amenities through richer fixed effects, the unexplained share remains close to one-third. This evidence points to the importance of investors’ beliefs and preferences—rather than several alternative explanations we test—as sources of heterogeneity in risk premia.

title: Digital twins for health and safety management in construction: a systematic review
abstract: Purpose Despite regulatory and technological advances, construction health and safety (H&S) management remains hindered by poor hazard visibility, fragmented information and reactive decision-making. Digital twins (DTs) offer a proactive, integrated and data-driven approach by connecting physical construction environments with continuously updated virtual representations. However, evidence remains fragmented regarding how DT applications, enabling conditions and implementation challenges interact to improve H&S outcomes. This study aims to systematically review and synthesise evidence on DT-enabled H&S management during the construction stage. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, identifying 26 peer-reviewed journal articles from the Scopus and Web of Science databases. Bibliometric analysis and qualitative content synthesis were used to examine research trends, DT applications, implementation enablers, challenges and future research directions. Findings DTs are mainly applied to workforce monitoring, hazard detection, safety training, risk prediction and decision support. Implementation success relies on technological, organisational, human and institutional enablers, but is hindered by interoperability issues, data governance gaps, skill shortages, …

Hapten Design, Antibody Engineering, and Immunochromatographic Application: A Rapid Fluorescent Strip for Acephate Residue Detection
abstract: Abstract Acephate (AP) is one of the most extensively used organophosphorus insecticides worldwide. Its high water solubility and environmental mobility result in frequent residue detection in agricultural products, posing health risks to consumers. In this study, a specific monoclonal antibody (mAb) against AP was generated through computer technology-assisted hapten design. A recombinant monoclonal antibody (R-mAb) was further obtained by gene sequencing and recombinant expression, exhibiting a higher affinity constant (7.29 × 109 L/mol) than the parental mAb (5.60 × 109 L/mol). Using R-mAb as the recognition reagent, a fluorescent immunochromatographic assay (FICA) strip was established. Matrix matched calibration curves for lettuce, orange, Flammulina filiformis, and soybean yielded IC50 values of 2.5, 2.3, 2.0, and 24.0 μg/kg, respectively. Recoveries at 5 and 50 μg/kg were 84.9%–102.5%, agreeing well with liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. The strip provides a convenient, efficient, and reliable tool for rapid screening of AP residues in agricultural products.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: THE INFLUENCE OF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND SELF-EFFICACY OF TEACHERS ON UNIVERSAL DESIGN FOR LEARNING PRACTICES IN THE ENHANCED K TO 12 CURRICULUM
abstract: This study examined the influence of teachers’ professional development and self-efficacy on the implementation of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) practices under the Enhanced K to 12 Curriculum. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were gathered from 112 public school teachers in the Division of Panabo City, Davao del Norte, who had participated in the Revised K to 12 Curriculum seminar. Adapted survey instruments measured professional development, teacher self-efficacy, and UDL practices. Data were analyzed using weighted means, Pearson product-moment correlation, and multiple regression. Teachers rated professional development as high across student variability (M = 3.80), peer support (M = 4.25), administrative support (M = 3.75), collaboration (M = 3.67), and training (M = 3.81). Self-efficacy was very high in student engagement (M = 4.33), instructional strategies (M = 4.38), and classroom management (M = 4.36). UDL practices were also very high in engagement (M = 4.23), representation (M = 4.25), and action and expression (M = 4.25). Professional development was significantly related to UDL practices (r = .643, p < .001), as was self-efficacy (r = .706, p < .001). Regression results showed that collaboration and peer support were significant predictors among professional development domains, while classroom-management efficacy was the significa…

title: Perceived mobility affordability and welfare vulnerability among Malaysia’s B40 households during targeted diesel subsidy reform
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how perceived mobility affordability and adequacy, community participation and housing affordability are associated with subjective welfare among Malaysia’s B40 households during targeted diesel subsidy reform. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional convenience sample of 400 respondents from B40 households in the Greater Klang Valley was analysed using reliability and factor analyses, Pearson correlations, ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors, demographic adjustment and vulnerability-profile comparisons. Findings The joint low/neutral mobility–low/neutral community profile represented 35.3 % of respondents and had the lowest observed mean subjective welfare. Its mean was significantly lower than those of the two profiles with favourable community participation and did not differ significantly from that of the profile combining favourable mobility with low/neutral community participation. Practical implications Mobility and community-participation indicators can complement administrative, income, transport-expenditure, compensation and accessibility records in welfare assessment and policy targeting. Originality/value The study brings perceived transport adequacy, housing affordability and community participation into a single welfare-vulnerability framework for Malaysian B40 households.

title: China’s revised Maritime Code and vessel-source oil pollution liability: innovations, gaps, and reform pathways
abstract: Vessel-source oil pollution remains a central concern in marine environmental governance because oil spills may spread rapidly, persist in the marine environment, and cause serious ecological and socio-economic harm. China has traditionally regulated vessel-source oil pollution through rules dispersed across civil, environmental, maritime, insurance, and administrative law. The revised Maritime Code of the People’s Republic of China, adopted in 2025 and effective from 1 May 2026, introduces China’s first dedicated chapter on Liability for Oil Pollution Damage from Ships. Distinct from prior scholarship that primarily analyzed draft proposals or focused narrowly on specific compensation mechanisms like the CLC vs. domestic fund models, this article offers an incremental contribution by conducting a comprehensive assessment based on the final promulgated text. It proposes a phased reform pathway to address emerging uncertainties and provides forward-looking risk assessments regarding non-spilling vessels in collisions, alternative fuels, and ecological damage valuation. By evaluating the finalized chapter against the 1992 Civil Liability Convention, as amended, the 2001 Bunkers Convention, and China’s pre-existing domestic framework, it argues that the revised Code advances systematic integration by clarifying liable parties and defences, establishing strict liability, placing co…

title: Effect of the Stock Market on Standard of Living in Nigeria. An ARDL Analysis
abstract: This study examines the effect of stock market performance on Nigeria’s standard of living over the period 1993–2023. The HDI served as a proxy for the standard of living, while Market Capitalization, Number of Listed Companies, Turnover Ratio, and Traded Value represented indicators of stock market performance. Annual time-series data were obtained from the World Development Indicators (WDI) and UNDP. The analytical techniques included descriptive statistics, Augmented Dickey–Fuller (ADF) unit root tests, Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds cointegration tests, ARDL estimation, and post-estimation diagnostics. The ADF results revealed a mixture of stationary and non-stationary variables, integrated at I(0) and I(1). The ARDL bounds test confirmed the existence of a long-run relationship between HDI and stock market performance indicators. The long-run ARDL estimates showed that Market Capitalization and Turnover Ratio had positive but statistically insignificant effects on HDI, while Traded Value exhibited a negative but insignificant effect. Conversely, the Number of Listed Companies demonstrated a statistically significant negative effect on HDI in the long run. The study concluded that the development of the Nigerian stock market has not yet translated into tangible improvements in human development, and recommended policy reforms aimed at tax incentives and procur…

title: P-80: Role of an education nurse in a low-resource health care service: challenges and observations
abstract: Abstract Introduction In low-resource health care settings, patients education is often limited due to heavy workload, staff shortages, and lack of educational tools leading to poor understanding of disease and treatment adherence. Objectives To explore the role of an education nurse in a low-resource healthcare service. Methods An observational study with purposive sampling was conducted over one month at the Mother and Child Center of the Chantal Biya Foundation. The study involved the educational nurse and type 1 diabetes patients with their families. Data was collected through direct observation of the nurse’s daily educational activities. Results The education nurse played both in-hospital and community roles. In the hospital, she provided simplified explanations of diseases, promoted preventive practices and treatment adherence, offered psychological support and trained healthcare staff. community activities focused on outreach and health education. Positive factors included the availability of educational videos, regular patient attendance, increasing participation in training, and improved health information systems. However, challenges included the lack of community health workers, community insecurity, limited time due to high patient load, staff shortages and difficulties in insulin supply. Conclusions Education nurse plays a crucial role in improving patient knowled…

title: P-165: Transforming youth diabetes care: the role of Tellmi in providing digital mental health support in Somerset National Health Service, United Kingdom
abstract: Abstract Introduction Youth with diabetes experience substantial physical and mental health challenges. Tellmi is a novel mental health app providing unlimited, anonymous, peer support moderated by AI and human oversight, with real-time counsellor intervention for high-risk content. The app was adapted to include diabetes-specific support, including direct access to the Somerset NHS Children’s Diabetes Nurses’ Helpline. Objectives To explore the lived experiences of youth with diabetes using Tellmi. Methods A mixed-methods sequential design was used. First, a diabetes-specific Tellmi survey was disseminated through Somerset paediatric diabetes clinicians, general practitioners, and local support services, resulting in responses from 32 youth with diabetes. Participants were invited to take part in interviews, with seven interviews conducted until data saturation was reached. Quantitative data were stratified by median age and analysed using chi-square and t-tests. Qualitative data were thematically analysed using Gibbs’s framework. Results Quantitative findings demonstrated high rates of mental health difficulties, including anxiety (68.8%), depression (40.6%), panic attacks (43.8%), sleep problems (43.8%), and suicidal thoughts (34.4%). Less than half (42.9%) had informed their diabetes clinic about mental health impacts. While 53.6% had attempted to access support, others had…

title: One Market, Twenty-Seven VAT Systems and Counting: Europe Simplifies Everything but Its Biggest Tax
abstract: In this Column, the author argues that VAT fragmentation remains a major obstacle to the EU single market, particularly for SMEs, which face high compliance costs from dealing with different VAT rules, registrations and digital reporting systems across Member States. She calls for much deeper VAT harmonization, ultimately proposing one EU VAT system with a single VAT number, common rules and administration, and a unified tax court, especially as the EU prepares for further enlargement.

title: The Interest Rate and Stock Market Performance in Nigeria (1981- 2024)
abstract: The study investigated the interest rate and stock market performance in Nigeria for the Period 1981- 2024. The specific objectives of the study were to analyze the impact of real interest rate on stock market performance in Nigeria, to ascertain the impact of nominal interest rate on stock market performance in Nigeria, and to examine the impact of monetary policy rate on stock market performance in Nigeria. The study adopted ex-post facto design and employed the Auto Regressive Distributed (ARDL) to estimate the model. The major finding of the study Real Interest Rate (RIR) at 5% level of significance has highly negative impact on stock market performance in Nigeria; Nominal Interest Rate (NIR) at 5% level of significance has negative impact on stock market performance in Nigeria; Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 5% level of significance has positive impact on stock market performance in Nigeria. While at 70% level of confidence we conclude that the effect is negative and significant. The policy recommendations based on the findings are; where the simple act of raising or lowering the MPR is insufficient; policymakers must manage the expectations and real economic environment that influence the RIR and NIR to ensure capital market stability. Market and Labour Opportunities as a Driving Factor? Explaining the Gendered Literacy Disparities in the Eighteenth-Century Antwerp Countryside
abstract: Abstract This article investigates regional and gender disparities in literacy in the eighteenth-century countryside of the Southern Low Countries, comparing the Campine area and the Scheldt Polder region. We explore the socioeconomic drivers behind divergent literacy rates by drawing on a rich combination of quantitative and qualitative sources – including marriage certificates, probate inventories, and school enrolment data. Contrary to prevailing narratives of widespread illiteracy in Catholic rural regions, the Campine area displayed unexpectedly high levels of literacy, particularly among women. The analysis reveals that this disparity cannot be attributed solely to the presence of schools but must also be understood through the lens of labour market structures and gendered economic roles. The study shows that in the Campine region, smallholder farming and especially dairy production created commercial incentives for women to invest in basic literacy skills, unlike the more unequal, arable farming-based economy of the Scheldt polders. By integrating both macro-level data and micro-historical insights, the article challenges traditional assumptions about rural education and highlights the critical role of gendered economic agency in shaping literacy outcomes.

title: Price Premiums for Sustainability Claims: Evidence From U.S. Food and Beverage Markets
abstract: ABSTRACT As sustainability claims proliferate on food packaging, understanding their implicit market value is important for effective policy design and competitive firm strategy. This study quantifies the price premiums of sustainability attributes in the U.S. market using product‐level data. We analyze 210,515 food and beverage product launches from the Mintel Global New Products Database (2012–2024) and document a near‐doubling in the prevalence of sustainability claims, rising from 18% of new products in 2012 to 37% in 2024. Using a hedonic price model, we present significant price premiums for both environmental (7.9%) and social (3.5%) claims. Further decomposition reveals substantial heterogeneity, with “downstream” attributes related to disposal (e.g., biodegradable) generating the highest premiums, outperforming “upstream” production claims. Additionally, premiums vary widely across product categories, with large premiums in beverages, but zero or negative premiums in several utilitarian categories such as Sauces and Seasonings. These findings inform ongoing policy discussions on third‐party certification, standardized claim definitions, and disclosure requirements for sustainability claims.

Professional by Assumption, Consumer by Behaviour: The Microentrepreneur in the Retail Electricity Market in the Light of Behavioural Economics[1]
abstract: Civil law presumes that an entrepreneur acts as a professional, while the rules protecting electricity customers rely largely on disclosure. Drawing on behavioural economics, the article argues that both assumptions fail with respect to microentrepreneurs. It evaluates statutory classification (Germany), a default rule with standardised bills (Italy), and disclosure with ex post qualification (Poland). A CATI survey of 602 customers of one supplier (402 households, 200 businesses) shows that information on switching and on the comparison tool belongs to the least-read layer of the bill, that age and financial situation are associated with self-assessed knowledge but not the perceived comprehensibility of the bill, and that microentrepreneurs do not report understanding the bill better than households. The article formulates de lege lata conclusions concerning Annex I to Directive 2019/944, Article 31g of the Polish Energy Law, and Article 385⁵ of the Polish Civil Code, and de lege ferenda proposals favouring protection that does not depend on the addressee’s own initiative.

title: Voxel-Level Forecasting of Apparent Vertebral Bone Loss from Routine CT Using a 3D Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Existing computed tomography (CT) fracture-risk models typically output one scalar score per vertebra without localising the predicted change. We built and internally validated a three-dimensional (3D) convolutional network forecasting, from one baseline acquisition, a per-voxel map of apparent inter-scan bone-mask loss per lumbar vertebra. Paired CT studies from 65 patients yielded 298 baseline-unfractured vertebra patches (L1 to L5); every patient sustained at least one reader-adjudicated incident fracture, so the cohort is outcome-enriched. The endpoint was apparent vertebral-body mask loss between scans after rigid alignment of automated masks. A multi-task 3D residual U-Net with vertebral-level conditioning was compared with a gradient-boosted classifier on the same features and folds, under five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation with clustered bootstrap intervals. Pooled precision-recall area was 0.445 vs. 0.439 for the reference (+0.005, 95% confidence interval −0.018 to +0.028) and pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.815. At matched predicted volume, the network map was less fragmented (2.3 vs. 5.3 components per 1000 voxels), and the endpoint separated incident fractures (AUC 0.865). Voxel-level forecasting of apparent inter-scan vertebral change is feasible on routine CT; the contribution is the paired-scan forecasting framework and the spatial-profile differe…

title: Volatility Risk Spillovers Across China’s Electricity Spot, Carbon and Financial Markets: Implications for Low-Carbon Transition with Evidence from BEKK–GARCH and Nonlinear Granger Causality Tests
abstract: To support coordinated risk management of electricity and carbon markets under the new power system, this paper clarifies the volatility transmission mechanism between Guangdong electricity spot prices and Guangdong carbon allowance prices, and investigates risk spillover effects among the Guangdong electricity spot market, Guangdong carbon market and power-related financial market. The results help identify regional systemic risks in the low-carbon energy transition and provide references for regional energy security and financial stability. This paper adopts the logarithmic return of day-ahead average prices in the Guangdong electricity spot market (RE), the logarithmic return of Guangdong carbon emission allowance prices (RC), and the logarithmic return of the FTSE China A600 Electricity Index (RF). A VAR(2)-BEKK-GARCH(1,1) framework is constructed to analyze risk linkages from mean and volatility dimensions. News impact surfaces, volatility impulse response functions, the Diebold–Yilmaz volatility spillover index and the Diks–Panchenko nonlinear causality test are further applied for comprehensive inference. The results show that the electricity market has significant inherent baseline volatility stemming from real-time supply-demand balance and the non-storability of electricity. Volatility persistence ranks as financial market > carbon market > electricity market. In term…

title: GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonism does not directly drive skeletal muscle atrophy or impair myogenesis in primary human myotubes
abstract: Abstract GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists produce substantial weight loss in clinical trials but significant loss of lean body mass is reported. Whether this reflects a direct pharmacological effect on skeletal muscle or an indirect consequence of caloric restriction and reduced mechanical loading is unknown. Primary myoblasts were isolated from skeletal muscle of older adults with obesity undergoing orthopaedic surgery. GIPR and GLP-1R expression was characterised by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. Differentiated myotubes were treated with semaglutide or GIP peptide and assessed for atrophy-related gene expression (qPCR), secretome perturbation (Olink Reveal), mitochondrial and glycolytic bioenergetics (Seahorse XF Real-Time ATP Rate Assay, glucose uptake, lactate secretion) and myotube morphology and myogenesis (immunofluorescence). GIPR mRNA was consistently detected across all donors; GLP-1R mRNA was undetectable by PCR, though LUXendin645 flow cytometry in a subset of three donors identified low-level surface GLP-1R protein in 51–66% of myoblasts. Neither semaglutide nor GIP altered atrophy-related gene expression or the secretome, with no proteins reaching significance. Semaglutide reduced glycolytic and total ATP production rates, accompanied by reduced lactate secretion, suggesting modest suppression of glycolytic flux; mitochondrial parameters were unaffected. title: Applicability of a modified weather research and forecasting (WRF) model to heavy rainfall information
abstract: Abstract The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) issues “Forecast Information on Linear Rainbands” (FILR; translated by the authors) approximately half a day before the expected formation of linear rainbands. A linear rainband is identified according to a set of operational criteria. A modified Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model was applied to sixteen heavy rainfall events associated with erroneous FILR decisions. Ten of these events had no FILR issued but subsequently experienced linear rainbands (missed issuance). Model results were compared with radar/rain-gauge analyzed precipitation data, with a primary focus on maximum rainfall, one of the criteria. The model reasonably simulated the occurrence of heavy rainfall in eight of the ten events and the rainfall intensity in six of those eight events. Conversely, six of the sixteen events had FILRs issued but ultimately experienced no linear rainbands (false alarm). In five of these events, the model reasonably reproduced the observed rainfall that did not satisfy the linear-rainband criteria. These results suggest that, despite several remaining challenges, the modified WRF model has the potential to complement JMA FILR decisions and contribute to reducing both missed issuances and false alarms.

title: Phagocytosis of Acanthamoeba by macrophages and neutrophils and “kiss and run” evasion by Entamoeba histolytica
abstract: ABSTRACT Phagocytosis was discovered in the 19th century and is a cornerstone of innate immunity. Although amoebae species cause over 100 million cases of severe infections annually, one long-standing dogma remained unchallenged: that eukaryotic amoebae are too large to be phagocytosed. Here, we overturn this entrenched dogma and show that human macrophages and neutrophils efficiently phagocytose Acanthamoeba polyphaga and Vermamoeba vermiformis , in a phosphoinositide 3-kinase-dependent manner. In contrast, Entamoeba histolytica utilizes a “kiss and run” evasion strategy of phagocytosis. However, formalin-killed and UV-irradiated E. histolytica are efficiently phagocytosed. Macrophages respond to E. histolytica by formation of striking F-actin fibrillar projections, in contrast to the bona fide phagocytic cups that engulf killed E. histolytica , A. polyphaga , and V. vermiformis . Remarkably, neutrophils harboring phagocytosed amoebae are efferocytosed by macrophages. These findings redefine innate immunity to amoebae, the physical and biological limits of phagocytosis, and uncover divergent evolution among pathogenic amoebae to subvert phagocytosis. IMPORTANCE Eukaryotic amoebae have been presumed to be too large to be phagocytosed. We demonstrate that human macrophages and neutrophils can efficiently phagocytose diverse amoebae species, while Entamoeba histolytica evades pha…

title: Forecasting Non-Fungible Token (NFT) Market Volatility Through Hybrid GARCH–LSTM Models
abstract: This study forecasts price volatility in the non-fungible token (NFT) digital asset market. We develop a hybrid forecasting framework that integrates long short-term memory (LSTM) networks with a set of generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (GARCH)-type models. Using daily data, we conduct a comparative evaluation of nine competing forecasting models across five representative NFT submarkets (i.e., OpenSea, Atomic, CryptoKitties, Gods Unchained, and Decentraland). Employing standard error metrics (RMSE, MSE, MAE, and RAE), a robust loss QLIKE function, and the Diebold–Mariano (DM) statistical test, our empirical results show that the hybrid GARCH-TGARCH-LSTM model achieves the lowest error metrics. Compared with the baseline LSTM model, it achieves RMSE reductions of approximately 14% for Atomic, 49% for CryptoKitties, 13% for Decentraland, 8% for Gods Unchained, and 29% for OpenSea. Furthermore, the EGARCH conditional variance specification underperforms the TGARCH counterpart in the most NFT submarkets. This finding suggests that combining the volatility clustering characteristics captured by standard GARCH models with the asymmetric volatility features captured by TGARCH models improves forecasting performance. This study contributes to research on hybrid deep learning approaches to volatility forecasting in emerging digital asset markets.

title: A Hybrid Strategy for Probabilistic Forecasting and Trading of Aggregated Wind-Solar Power: Design and Analysis in HEFTCom2024
abstract: Obtaining accurate probabilistic energy forecasts and making effective decisions amid diverse uncertainties are routine challenges in future energy systems. This paper presents the winning solution of team GEB, which ranked 3rd in trading, 4th in forecasting, and 1st among student teams in the IEEE Hybrid Energy Forecasting and Trading Competition 2024 (HEFTCom2024). The solution provides accurate probabilistic forecasts for a wind-solar hybrid system, and achieves substantial trading revenue in the day-ahead electricity market. Key components include: (1) a stacking-based approach combining sister forecasts from various Numerical Weather Predictions (NWPs) to provide wind power forecasts, (2) an online solar post-processing model to address the distribution shift in the online test set caused by increased solar capacity, (3) a probabilistic aggregation method for accurate quantile forecasts of hybrid generation, and (4) a stochastic trading strategy to maximize expected trading revenue considering uncertainties in electricity prices. This paper also explores the potential of end-to-end learning to further enhance the trading revenue by shifting the distribution of forecast errors. Detailed case studies are provided to validate the effectiveness of these proposed methods. Code for all mentioned methods is available for reproduction and further research in both industry and acad…

title: Economic evaluation and feasibility design of an electricity-hydrogen market with hydrogen-based system: Mathematical model and techno-economic analysis
Challenges and prospectives of energy storage integration in renewable energy systems for net zero transition
Congestion-Sensitive Grid Aggregation for DC Optimal Power Flow
abstract: The vast spatial dimension of modern interconnected electricity grids challenges the tractability of the DC optimal power flow problem. Grid aggregation methods try to overcome this challenge by reducing the number of network elements. Many existing methods use Locational Marginal Prices as a distance metric to cluster nodes. In this paper, we show that prevalent methods adopting this distance metric fail to adequately capture the impact of individual lines when there is more than one line congested. This leads to suboptimal outcomes for the optimization of the aggregated model. To overcome those issues, we propose two methods based on the novel Network Congestion Price metric, which preserves the impact of nodal power injections on individual line congestions. The proposed methods are compared to several existing aggregation methods based on Locational Marginal Prices. We demonstrate all methods on adapted versions of the IEEE RTS 24- and 300-Bus systems. We show that the proposed methods outperform existing approaches both in terms of objective function value error and maximum line limit violation, while exhibiting faster node clustering. We conclude that aggregation methods based on the novel Network Congestion Price metric are better at preserving the essential physical characteristics of the network topology in the grid aggregation process than methods based on Locational …

title: Integrated equilibrium model for electrified logistics and power systems
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated equilibrium model to characterize the complex interactions between electrified logistics systems and electric power delivery systems. The model consists of two major players: an electrified logistics operator (ELO) and a power system operator (PSO). The ELO aims to maximize its profit by strategically scheduling and routing its electric delivery vehicles (e-trucks) for deliveries and charging, in response to the locational marginal price (LMP) set by the PSO. The routing, delivery, and charging behaviors of e-trucks are modeled by a perturbed utility Markov decision process (PU-MDP) while their collective operations are optimized to achieve the ELO's objective by designing rewards in the PU-MDP. On the other hand, PSO optimizes the energy price by considering both the spatiotemporal e-truck charging demand and the base electricity load. The equilibrium of the integrated system is formulated as a fixed point, proved to exist under mild assumptions, and solved for a case study on the Hawaii network via Anderson's fixed-point acceleration algorithm. Along with these numerical results, this paper provides both theoretical insights and practical guidelines to achieve sustainable and efficient operations in modern electrified logistics and power systems.

title: Strategic bidding model of integrated power-to-hydrogen systems in electricity-hydrogen coupling market
Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning based demand response and energy management for heavy industries with discrete manufacturing systems
abstract: Energy-centric decarbonization of heavy industries, such as steel and cement, necessitates their participation in integrating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and effective Demand Response (DR) programs. This situation has created the opportunities to research control algorithms in diverse DR scenarios. Further, the industrial sector’s unique challenges, including the diversity of operations and the need for uninterrupted production, bring unique challenges in designing and implementing control algorithms. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods are practical solutions to the unique challenges faced by the industrial sector. Nevertheless, research in RL for industrial demand response has not yet achieved the level of standardization seen in other areas of RL research, hindering broader progress. To propel the research progress, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based energy management system designed to optimize energy consumption in energy-intensive industrial settings by leveraging dynamic pricing DR schemes. The study highlights the creation of a MARL environment and addresses these challenges by designing a general framework that allows researchers to replicate and implement MARL environments for industrial sectors. The proposed framework incorporates a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) to model energy consumption and production processes w…

title: Energy poverty and children’s subjective well-being: evidence from young lives data
abstract: This study examines the impact of energy poverty on the subjective well-being of children in four developing countries: Ethiopia, India, Peru, and Vietnam. We assess energy poverty using a multidimensional approach, leveraging data from the Young Lives study, which conducted surveys in 2006, 2009, 2013, and 2016 (Rounds 2 to 5). Our analysis focuses on the young cohort (Rounds 3 to 5) and the older cohort (Rounds 2 to 5), as these rounds include questions on children’s subjective well-being. To mitigate potential endogeneity concerns and establish causal relationships, we employ a two-stage least squares regression, using residential electricity prices at the country level as an instrumental variable. Our findings reveal that energy poverty significantly reduces children’s subjective well-being, with boys and older children more affected. Robustness checks confirm the validity of these results. Additionally, we find that health status mediates the impact of energy poverty on children’s well-being, highlighting the importance of targeted policy interventions.

title: Market-oriented operational strategy for biomass-geothermal combined power generation and hydrogen production plant
Capacity remuneration mechanisms for decarbonized power systems
abstract: Motivated by generation system adequacy concerns, many European countries have introduced capacity remuneration mechanisms (CRMs) to ensure sufficient investments in power generation . However, it is uncertain whether the existing CRMs will promote sufficient adequacy and flexibility in a decarbonized power system , where supply and demand will become more weather-dependent. We assess the effectiveness of a centralized capacity market, a strategic reserve , and a decentralized capacity market via capacity subscriptions in a climate-neutral, weather-driven power system. We develop a co-simulation of two agent-based models simulating myopia in both operational and investment decisions. We simulate weather uncertainty by running the model with 40 different weather years. Our results from a case study based on the Netherlands indicate that a strategic reserve may increase electricity price volatility in the long-term. A centralized capacity market is more cost-effective than a strategic reserve, but administratively setting its parameters is prone to over- or underprocurement. Capacity subscription allows consumers to select their desired level of reliability. Results indicate that these decentralized capacity markets may yield a clearer signal for the needed dispatchable capacity and promote demand-side response, but it may be challenging to provide long-term certainty for investo…

title: Local energy monitoring to support smart energy management and decarbonized town development
abstract: Introduction With the increase in variable renewable energy and liberalization of the electricity retail market, the integrated energy management of demand and supply has become crucial, complementing traditional energy-saving efforts. Therefore, high-resolution energy demand-side information, accounting for household attributes and owned equipment, is essential. However, previous studies have identified energy consumption based on surveys of utility bill payments; this approach does not provide detailed, hourly data on electricity demand, which changes over time owing to lifestyle patterns and weather conditions. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the actual electricity consumption in residential buildings in Shinchi Town using the developed electricity monitoring system.Material and Method In support of regional disaster recovery initiatives, we developed a regional information and communication technology (ICT) system as a network interface for residents. As part of a social experiment, network terminals of the local ICT system were distributed to approximately 100 households in the town. Power monitoring data were collected via equipment installed in home distribution boards and centrally managed by a cloud server.Results and Conclusion We analyzed electric power consumption patterns, focusing on household attributes, seasonal variations in hot-water-supply device usage, an…

title: Perspective on challenges and opportunities in integrated electricity-hydrogen market

title: Impact of Regional and Seasonal Characteristics on Battery Electric Vehicle Operational Costs in the U.S.
abstract: This study investigates the operational cost competitiveness of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) in the United States, considering regional climates, energy prices, and driving patterns. By comparing BEVs with plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), and the alternative use of BEVs and conventional vehicles (Convs), the analysis incorporates thermal dynamometer tests, real-world vehicle miles traveled (VMT), and state-specific energy prices. Using detailed simulations, the study evaluates energy consumption across varying temperatures and driving distances. The findings reveal that, while BEVs remain cost-effective for short trips in moderate climates, PHEVs are more economical for long-range trips and cold environments, due to the excessive cost of using external direct current fast chargers (DCFCs) and reduced BEV efficiency at low temperatures. HEVs are identified as the most cost-efficient option in regions like New England, characterized by high residential electricity prices. These insights are critical for shaping vehicle electrification strategies, particularly under diverse regional and seasonal conditions, and for advancing policies on alternative energy and fuels.

title: Sharing the shortfall: Algorithmic solutions for fair demand curtailment in zonal power markets
Online Multivariate Regularized Distributional Regression for High-dimensional Probabilistic Electricity Price Forecasting
abstract: Probabilistic electricity price forecasting (PEPF) is vital for short-term electricity markets, yet the multivariate nature of day-ahead prices - spanning 24 consecutive hours - remains underexplored. At the same time, real-time decision-making requires methods that are both accurate and fast. We introduce an online algorithm for multivariate distributional regression models, allowing efficient modeling of the conditional means, variances, and dependence structures of electricity prices. The approach combines multivariate distributional regression with online coordinate descent and LASSO-type regularization (absolute shrinkage and selection operator), enabling scalable estimation in high-dimensional covariate spaces. Additionally, we propose a regularized estimation path over increasingly complex dependence structures, allowing for early stopping and avoiding overfitting. In a case study using historical data from the German day-ahead market, the proposed method yields interpretable and well-calibrated joint prediction intervals for the 24-dimensional price distribution and provides robust performance across a range of proper scoring rules. The results underscore the importance of modeling the dependence structure of electricity prices. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-off between predictive accuracy and computational costs for batch and online estimation and provide a high-pe…

title: Loss-aware Pricing Strategies for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
abstract: Peer-to-peer(P2P) energy trading may increase efficiency and reduce costs, but introduces significant challenges for network operators such as maintaining grid reliability, accounting for network losses, and redistributing costs equitably. We propose a novel loss-aware pricing strategy for P2P energy markets that addresses these challenges while incentivizing participation in the cooperative energy trading market. The problem is formulated as a hierarchical Stackelberg game, where a grid operator determines network tariffs while prosumers optimize their trades based on these tariffs while guaranteeing that network constraints are satisfied. The algorithm is designed to minimize and recover their cost from the trading parties, while also minimizing the total cost of the hubs. The mechanism dynamically adjusts tariffs based on location and network topology, discouraging loss-intensive trades. Finally, the complete framework includes the computation of fair trading prices, ensuring all market participants benefit equitably. An ADMM-based hyper-gradient descent method is proposed for solving this problem. Extensive numerical simulations using the benchmark IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate significant cost reductions and improved network efficiency through reduction in network losses compared to constant tariff schemes. Results highlight the adaptability and scalability of the propose…

title: Master–Slave Game Pricing Strategy of Time-of-Use Electricity Price of Electricity Retailers Considering Users’ Electricity Utility and Satisfaction
abstract: With the establishment of a competitive electricity retail market, how to optimize the retail electricity price mechanism has become the core of all kinds of retail companies to explore. Aiming at the pricing problem of time-of-use electricity price, this paper proposes a pricing strategy based on the master–slave game model. Firstly, considering the user’s electricity utility and satisfaction factors, the comprehensive benefit function of the electricity selling company with electricity price as the decision variable and the user’s comprehensive benefit function with electricity consumption as the decision variable are established, respectively. Then, a master–slave game model is established with the electricity selling company as the leader and the user as the follower, and the reverse induction method is used to solve the model. Finally, considering the influencing factors of user response ability, different electricity price types and user types are set up for simulation. The results show that the revenue of electricity retailers can be increased by up to 170,000 yuan, and the average electricity price of users can be reduced by up to 8 yuan. It is verified that the model can effectively achieve a win-win situation for both sides and promote peak shaving and valley filling. At the same time, it is proved that the role of the model is positively related to electricity price …

title: Federated Reinforcement Learning for decentralized peer-to-peer energy trading
abstract: The rapid development of distributed energy resources has led to an increasing number of prosumers enhancing their energy utilization, thereby raising the demands on energy management technologies. As a result, the development of future smart grids is becoming increasingly important, with a particular emphasis on integrating demand-side flexibility into electricity market. To facilitate distributed interaction among prosumers, the double-side auction market enables peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading , maximizing the social welfare within the dynamic local electricity market. In this setup, prosumers can set their own bidding prices and optimize their operations and trading strategies. However, trading in double-side auction market faces limitations due to the complexity of the market clearing algorithm and the difficulty of predicting other participants’ bidding behaviors. To address these challenges, this paper models the P2P energy trading problem in the double-side auction market as a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) task. The concept of federated learning is introduced to enhance scalability among market participants while protecting the private information of individual prosumers. Additionally, the parameter-sharing framework is proposed to accelerate the learning process . To further improve the stability of MARL training, the global information of P2P energy trad…

title: Short communication: Local electricity-hydrogen market
Extrapolating the long-term seasonal component of electricity prices for forecasting in the day-ahead market
abstract: Recent studies provide evidence that decomposing the electricity price into the long-term seasonal component (LTSC) and the remaining part, predicting both separately, and then combining their forecasts can bring significant accuracy gains in day-ahead electricity price forecasting. However, not much attention has been paid to predicting the LTSC, and the last 24 hourly values of the estimated pattern are typically copied for the target day. To address this gap, we introduce a novel approach which extracts the trend-seasonal pattern from a price series extrapolated using price forecasts for the next 24 hours. We assess it using two 5-year long test periods from the German and Spanish power markets, covering the Covid-19 pandemic, the 2021/2022 energy crisis, and the war in Ukraine. Considering parsimonious autoregressive and LASSO-estimated models, we find that improvements in predictive accuracy range from 3\% to 15\% in terms of the root mean squared error and exceed 1\% in terms of profits from a realistic trading strategy involving day-ahead bidding and battery storage.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Bidding Strategies for Prosumers Trading in Double Auction-Based Transactive Energy Market
abstract: With the large number of prosumers deploying distributed energy resources (DERs), integrating these prosumers into a transactive energy market (TEM) is a trend for the future smart grid. A community-based double auction market is considered a promising TEM that can encourage prosumers to participate and maximize social welfare. However, the traditional TEM is challenging to model explicitly due to the random bidding behavior of prosumers and uncertainties caused by the energy operation of DERs. Furthermore, although reinforcement learning algorithms provide a model-free solution to optimize prosumers' bidding strategies, their use in TEM is still challenging due to their scalability, stability, and privacy protection limitations. To address the above challenges, in this study, we design a double auction-based TEM with multiple DERs-equipped prosumers to transparently and efficiently manage energy transactions. We also propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) model with distributed learning and execution to ensure the scalability and privacy of the market environment. Additionally, the design of two bidding actions (i.e., bidding price and quantity) optimizes the bidding strategies for prosumers. Simulation results show that (1) the designed TEM and DRL model are robust; (2) the proposed DRL model effectively balances the energy payment and comfort satisfaction for prosumers …

title: Expanding the economic benefits of waste gasification through carbon and green certificate markets:Optimal bidding strategies in multiple markets
The Impact of Integrating Variable Renewable Energy Sources into Grid-Connected Power Systems: Challenges, Mitigation Strategies, and Prospects
abstract: Although the impact of integrating solar and wind sources into the power system has been studied in the past, the chaos caused by wind and solar energy generation has not yet had broader mitigation solutions notwithstanding their rapid deployment. Many research efforts in using prediction models have developed real-time monitoring of variability and machine learning predictive algorithms in contrast to the conventional methods of studying variability. This study focused on the causes and types of variability, challenges, and mitigation strategies used to minimize variability in grids worldwide. A summary of the top ten cases of countries that have successfully managed variability in their electrical power grids has been presented. Review shows that most of the success cases embraced advanced energy storage, grid upgrading, and flexible energy mix as key technological and economic strategies. A seven-point conceptual framework involving all energy stakeholders for managing variability in power system networks and increasing variable renewable energy (VRE)-grid integration has been proposed. Long-duration energy storage, virtual power plants (VPPs), smart grid infrastructure, cross-border interconnection, power-to-X, and grid flexibility are the key takeaways in achieving a reliable, resilient, and stable grid. This review provides a useful summary of up-to-date research informat…

title: Deregulating Grid-Enhancing Technologies Through Financial Transmission Rights
abstract: To accommodate the increasing share of renewable energy, the transmission network needs to be upgraded. Grid-enhancing technologies (GETs) are attractive alternatives that can replace or complement grid expansion. GETs enhance grid flexibility and increase the transfer capability over the current network. A main challenge facing proliferation of GETs is the lack of proper financial incentives for their adoption and efficient operation. This paper develops a novel Financial Transmission Right (FTR) allocation mechanism to incentivize GETs installation. The model allocates maximum feasible incremental FTRs in the directions requested by investors, while keeping existing FTRs feasible. Using the concept of proxy FTRs, the investors can only obtain incremental FTRs that their investment enables through enhancing the transfer capability. The paper shows that the proposed method is revenue adequate. Two major types of GETs are presented as representative investments that are compatible with the proposed model. These include series flexible ac transmission system (FACTS) devices, such as variable-impedance FACTS and devices based on voltage-sourced converters (VSC), as well as voltage phase controllers. The proposed model is first illustrated on a 3-bus system and then implemented on the IEEE 30-bus system to show its efficiency and scalability.

title: Distributionally Fair Peer-to-Peer Electricity Trading
abstract: Peer-to-peer energy trading platforms enable direct electricity exchanges between peers who belong to the same energy community. In a semi-decentralized system, a community manager adheres to grid restrictions while optimizing social welfare. However, with no further supervision, some peers can be discriminated against from participating in the electricity trades. To solve this issue, this paper proposes an optimization-based mechanism to enable distributionally fair peer-to-peer electricity trading. For the implementation of our mechanism, peers are grouped by energy poverty level. The proposed model aims to redistribute the electricity trades to minimize the maximum Wasserstein distance among the transaction distributions linked to the groups while limiting the sacrifice level with a predefined parameter. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposal using the IEEE 33-bus distribution grid, simulating an energy community with 1600 peers. Results indicate that up to 70.1% of unfairness can be eliminated by using our proposed model, even achieving a full elimination when including a non-profit community photovoltaic plant.

title: A data-driven merit order: Learning a fundamental electricity price model
abstract: Electricity price forecasting approaches generally fall into two categories: data-driven models, which learn from historical patterns, or fundamental models, which simulate market mechanisms. We propose a novel and highly efficient data-driven merit order model that integrates both paradigms. The model embeds the classical expert-based merit order as a nested special case, allowing all key parameters, such as plant efficiencies, bidding behavior, and available capacities, to be estimated directly from historical data, rather than assumed. We further enhance the model with critical embedded extensions such as hydro power, cross-border flows and corrections for underreported capacities, which considerably improve forecasting accuracy. Applied to the German day-ahead market, our model outperforms both classic fundamental and state-of-the-art machine learning models. It retains the interpretability of fundamental models, offering insights into marginal technologies, fuel switches, and dispatch patterns, elements which are typically inaccessible to black-box machine learning approaches. This transparency and high computational efficiency make it a promising new direction for electricity price modeling.

title: Conformal Uncertainty Quantification of Electricity Price Predictions for Risk-Averse Storage Arbitrage
abstract: This paper proposes a risk-averse approach to energy storage price arbitrage, leveraging conformal uncertainty quantification for electricity price predictions. The method addresses the significant challenges posed by the inherent volatility and uncertainty of real-time electricity prices, which create substantial risks of financial losses for energy storage participants relying on future price forecasts to plan their operations. The framework comprises a two-layer prediction model to quantify real-time price uncertainty confidence intervals with high coverage. The framework is distribution-free and can work with any underlying point prediction model. We evaluate the quantification effectiveness through storage price arbitrage application by managing the risk of participating in the real-time market. We design a risk-averse policy for profit-maximization of energy storage arbitrage to find the safest storage schedule with very minimal losses. Using historical data from New York State and synthetic price predictions, our evaluations demonstrate that this framework can achieve good profit margins with less than $35\%$ purchases.

title: Bidding in Ancillary Service Markets: An Analytical Approach Using Extreme Value Theory
abstract: To enable the participation of stochastic distributed energy resources in ancillary service markets, the Danish transmission system operator, Energinet, mandates that flexibility providers satisfy a minimum 90% reliability requirement for reserve bids. This paper examines the bidding strategy of an electric vehicle aggregator under this regulation and develops a chance-constrained optimization model. In contrast to conventional sample-based approaches that demand large datasets to capture uncertainty, we propose an analytical reformulation that leverages extreme value theory to characterize the tail behavior of flexibility distributions. A case study with real-world charging data from 1400 residential electric vehicles in Denmark demonstrates that the analytical solution improves out-of-sample reliability, reducing bid violation rates by up to 8% relative to a sample-based benchmark. The method is also computationally more efficient, solving optimization problems up to 4.8 times faster while requiring substantially fewer samples to ensure compliance. Moreover, the proposed approach enables the construction of feasible bids with reliability levels as high as 99.95%, which would otherwise require prohibitively large scenario sets under the sample-based method. Beyond its computational and reliability advantages, the framework also provides actionable insights into how reliability…

title: A Bottom-Up Approach to Optimizing the Solar Organic Rankine Cycle for Transactive Energy Trading
abstract: Solar Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC)-based power generation plants leverage solar irradiation to produce thermal energy, offering a highly compatible renewable technology due to the alignment between solar irradiation temperatures and ORC operating requirements. Their superior performance compared to steam Rankine cycles in small-scale applications makes them particularly relevant within the smart grid and microgrid contexts. This study explores the role of ORC in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading within renewable-based community microgrids, where consumers become prosumers, simultaneously producing and consuming energy while engaging in virtual trading at the distribution system level. Focusing on a microgrid integrating solar ORC with a storage system to meet consumer demand, the paper highlights the importance of combining these technologies with storage to enhance predictability and competitiveness with conventional energy plants, despite management challenges. A methodology based on operations research techniques is developed to optimize system performance. Furthermore, the impact of various technological parameters of the solar ORC on the system's performance is examined. The study concludes by assessing the value of solar ORC within the transactive energy trading framework across different configurations and scenarios. Results demonstrate an average 16\% reduction in operat…

title: Catalyzing the transition to a climate-neutral industry with carbon contracts for difference
Anomaly Detection in California Electricity Price Forecasting: Enhancing Accuracy and Reliability Using Principal Component Analysis
abstract: Accurate and reliable electricity price forecasting has significant practical implications for grid management, renewable energy integration, power system planning, and price volatility management. This study focuses on enhancing electricity price forecasting in California's grid, addressing challenges from complex generation data and heteroskedasticity. Utilizing principal component analysis (PCA), we analyze CAISO's hourly electricity prices and demand from 2016-2021 to improve day-ahead forecasting accuracy. Initially, we apply traditional outlier analysis with the interquartile range method, followed by robust PCA (RPCA) for more effective outlier elimination. This approach improves data symmetry and reduces skewness. We then construct multiple linear regression models using both raw and PCA-transformed features. The model with transformed features, refined through traditional and SAS Sparse Matrix outlier removal methods, shows superior forecasting performance. The SAS Sparse Matrix method, in particular, significantly enhances model accuracy. Our findings demonstrate that PCA-based methods are key in advancing electricity price forecasting, supporting renewable integration and grid management in day-ahead markets. Keywords: Electricity price forecasting, principal component analysis (PCA), power system planning, heteroskedasticity, renewable energy integration.
venue: Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews Energy and Environment

title: The energy transition and the value of Capacity Remuneration Mechanisms
abstract: Capacity Remuneration Mechanisms (CRM) can be used in power markets to overtake market failures, reaching security of supply. However, investment in capacity is a dynamic process, that depends on the evolution of prices and costs overtime. In our paper we study the capacity remuneration value through a CRM depending on three possible different technologies that participate to the market: a Variable Renewable Energy (VRE) source; a thermal efficient plant (i.e. Combine Cycle Gas Turbine) and a brown plant (i.e. coal). We shall see that these three types of capacities can be framed by means of a common theoretical framework, whose level of complexity increases as the uncertainty rises, moving from the simplest scheme (VRE technology) to the most complex one (coal power plant). For these different technological provisions, we consider how to evaluate them focusing on their investment value by adopting a stochastica pproach; we first provide a theoretical framework and then sensitivity analysis and calibration results. We show that for all three technology considered the effect of the CRM is to cap the firm revenues and as consequence it decreases their value.

title: Forecasting Day-Ahead Electricity Prices in the Integrated Single Electricity Market: Addressing Volatility with Comparative Machine Learning Methods
abstract: This paper undertakes a comprehensive investigation of electricity price forecasting methods, focused on the Irish Integrated Single Electricity Market, particularly on changes during recent periods of high volatility. The primary objective of this research is to evaluate and compare the performance of various forecasting models, ranging from traditional machine learning models to more complex neural networks, as well as the impact of different lengths of training periods. The performance metrics, mean absolute error, root mean square error, and relative mean absolute error, are utilized to assess and compare the accuracy of each model. A comprehensive set of input features was investigated and selected from data recorded between October 2018 and September 2022. The paper demonstrates that the daily EU Natural Gas price is a more useful feature for electricity price forecasting in Ireland than the daily Henry Hub Natural Gas price. This study also shows that the correlation of features to the day-ahead market price has changed in recent years. The price of natural gas on the day and the amount of wind energy on the grid that hour are significantly more important than any other features. More specifically speaking, the input fuel for electricity has become a more important driver of the price of it, than the total generation or demand. In addition, it can be seen that System Non…

title: Optimizing electric vehicle fleet integration in industrial demand response: Maximizing vehicle-to-grid benefits while compensating vehicle owners for battery degradation
abstract: This paper addresses the integration of electric vehicle (EV) fleets into industrial smart grids to increase operational flexibility. It focuses on an extended multi-objective optimization problem that minimizes two primary objectives: (i) the electricity expenditure of a company using its employees’ EV batteries as temporary distributed energy storage, and (ii) the costs associated with the degradation of EV batteries, given the additional usage from the company’s perspective. In this paper, the utilization of an EV fleet is simulated at the individual car level over a one-year period. These optimization problems are balanced by using real-time electricity prices and the effective demand response (DR) of the company’s electrical load. The company utilizes the EVs as battery storage to offset fluctuating electricity prices, while compensating EV owners with free electricity for the costs incurred through degradation of their batteries. The extent to which a company can compensate EV owners while maintaining the viability of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) services in a non-residential scenario was explored. The results established an equilibrium point at which the financial benefits for the company resulting from V2G services was maximized against the negative financial impact of increased battery degradation for EV owners. The results showed that there is a potential mutual benefit betw…

title: A comprehensive overview of industrial demand response status in Europe
abstract: Industrial demand response (IDR) will play a crucial role in shaping future electricity systems, as it is a key element of a just energy transition and industrial development. The aim of this work is to provide an overview of the current status of IDR in a holistic perspective. First, the main benefits and potential of IDR are reviewed, together with the motivations and challenges for the industrial sector. Most recent advances in European markets and regulations with specific focus on IDR applications are explored. Then, the different resources which are currently available to help industries participate and implement IDR programmes are reviewed. In particular: 1) the (possible) tools for defining energy-aware scheduling and planning of the manufacturing systems are analysed; 2) The role of aggregators (i.e. intermediaries between industries and power markets) for facilitating explicit IDR is examined; 3) the importance of digitalisation to provide better IDR services from the manufacturing industry is highlighted, pointing out that digital twins, cyber-physical systems, Internet of Things sensors, robots, edge computing, artificial intelligence, and big data are promising technologies; and 4) most recent related research projects are reviewed. Finally, it is analysed and discussed how each of those resources can address the different challenges that are still preventing indus…

title: Online Distributional Regression
abstract: Large-scale streaming data are common in modern machine learning applications and have led to the development of online learning algorithms. Many fields, such as supply chain management, weather and meteorology, energy markets, and finance, have pivoted toward probabilistic forecasting. This results in the need not only for accurate learning of the expected value but also for learning the conditional heteroskedasticity and conditional moments. Against this backdrop, we present a methodology for online estimation of regularized, linear distributional models. The proposed algorithm combines recent developments in online estimation of LASSO models with the well-known GAMLSS framework. We provide a case study on day-ahead electricity price forecasting, in which we show the competitive performance of the incremental estimation combined with strongly reduced computational effort. Our algorithms are implemented in a computationally efficient Python package ondil.
